# Roadmap: higher topos theory

**Summary.** This roadmap extends Mathlib's coverage of ∞-category theory (`SSet.Quasicategory`) to include essentially all of Lurie's *Higher Topos Theory* and *Higher Algebra* chapter 1 (stable ∞-categories). The build starts with three foundational layers that fill in background not yet in mathlib, and overlap in part with HTT appendix A:

| Layer | Content | HTT / HA material |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [F1](#layer-f1-classical-category-theory-and-model-categories) | classical category theory and model-category theory | HTT §§A.1–A.2 |
| [F2](#layer-f2-kan-complexes-and-the-kanquillen-model-structure) | Kan complexes, their homotopy theory, and the Kan–Quillen model structure | HTT §A.2.7 |
| [F3](#layer-f3-simplicial-categories-enriched-model-categories-and-duggers-theorem) | simplicial categories, enriched model categories, and Dugger's presentation theorem for combinatorial model categories | HTT §§A.3.1–A.3.7 |

The main layers then follow:

| Layer | Content | HTT / HA material |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [L1](#layer-l1-quasicategories) | quasicategories and their homotopy categories | HTT ch. 1 |
| [L2](#layer-l2-left-fibrations-the-covariant-model-structure-straightening-over-a-point) | left and right fibrations, the covariant model structure, straightening over a point | HTT §§2.1–2.2 |
| [L3](#layer-l3-inner-and-cartesian-fibrations-the-joyal-model-structure) | inner and Cartesian fibrations, the Joyal model structure | HTT §§2.3–2.4, 2.2.5 |
| [L4](#layer-l4-marked-simplicial-sets-and-straightening) | straightening and unstraightening | HTT ch. 3 |
| [L5](#layer-l5-limits-colimits-and-kan-extensions) | limits, colimits and Kan extensions | HTT ch. 4 |
| [L6](#layer-l6-presheaves-adjunctions-inductive-limits-groupoid-objects) | presheaves, adjunctions, Ind-objects, groupoid objects | HTT §§5.1–5.3, 6.1.2 |
| [L7](#layer-l7-accessible-and-presentable--categories) | accessible and presentable ∞-categories | HTT §§5.4–5.5 |
| [L8](#layer-l8-model-categorical-presentations-of-presentable--categories) | model-categorical presentations of presentable ∞-categories | HTT A.3.7.6–A.3.7.10 |
| [L9](#layer-l9-stable--categories) | stable ∞-categories, t-structures, the derived ∞-category of an abelian category, and the Dold–Kan correspondence | HA ch. 1 |
| [L10](#layer-l10--topoi) | ∞-topoi and Giraud's theorem | HTT §§6.1–6.2 |
| [L11](#layer-l11-the--category-of--topoi-n-topoi-homotopy-theory-in-an--topos) | the ∞-category of ∞-topoi, n-topoi, and homotopy theory in an ∞-topos | HTT §§6.3–6.5 |
| [L12](#layer-l12-higher-topos-theory-in-topology) | paracompact spaces, dimension theory and proper base change | HTT ch. 7 |

## Scope and ownership

This roadmap owns the general theory of ∞-categories as HTT and HA chapter 1 develop it. A definition or result of HTT or of HA chapter 1 is in scope, and so is any Remark of those books that a definition or result depends on. The targets without a Lurie number are the foundational targets of Layers F2 and F3, and a few stated forms of Lurie's results, such as the simplicial form of HTT 1.2.4.1.

HTT's topological categories are out of scope: Definitions 1.1.1.6, 1.1.3.1, 1.1.3.2, 1.1.3.4 and 1.1.3.6, Corollary 1.1.5.12, Theorem 1.1.5.13, Proposition 1.2.4.1, Example 1.2.13.1 and Remarks 1.1.4.3 and 1.1.5.17–1.1.5.18. They are expository. Every later use of them applies a simplicial statement, which is a target: Theorem 2.2.0.1 for fibrant simplicial categories, Proposition 2.2.4.1 for `C[S]`, and the simplicial form of 1.2.4.1. Lurie himself derives 1.1.5.13 from 2.2.0.1.

It owns in particular:

- the Kan–Quillen model structure on `SSet` and the homotopy theory of Kan complexes: homotopy groups and long exact sequences, Whitehead's theorem, `Ex^∞`, Postnikov towers, Eilenberg–MacLane complexes, and the diagonal of bisimplicial sets (Layer F2);
- the classical background of HTT Appendix A (Layer F1), as far as Mathlib does not supply it;
- simplicial categories, the Bergner model structure and Dugger's theorem (Layer F3);
- joins, slices, mapping spaces, cores, functor ∞-categories, (co)limits, fibrations of simplicial sets, the Joyal model structure, straightening, Kan extensions, presentability and ∞-topoi (L1–L8, L10–L12);
- stable ∞-categories, t-structures, derived ∞-categories and the ∞-categorical Dold–Kan correspondence (L9).

Outside its scope, with stated dependencies:

- **Topology of spaces.**
  - AlgebraicTopology owns CW pairs, cofibrations of spaces and the comparison of simplicial with topological homotopy groups. Layer F2's comparison target `HTT.A.2.7/realization` uses these, and L12 §7.1 uses that target.
  - No other target uses the topology of spaces until HTT chapter 7 (L12), which takes paracompactness from Mathlib and defines covering dimension itself (7.2.3.1). The exceptions are L11's Counterexamples 6.5.4.2 and 6.5.4.5, which use Mathlib's general topology (the Hilbert cube, coherent spaces) and nothing from AlgebraicTopology.
- **Higher algebra beyond HA chapter 1.** Operads, algebras, modules, monoidal ∞-categories and spectra beyond the stabilization of L9 belong to the roadmaps that build them, which cite this one.
- **dg categories.** Tabuada's model structure on dg categories belongs to DGAInfinity. HA 1.3.1.19–1.3.1.20 cite it from there.

The roadmap is complete when every target is formalized. BordismFormalGroups, EnhancedDerivedSheaves and DerivedModuleAlgebra build on this material; they take the notions of the Conventions table from here rather than defining their own.

## Conventions

**Model.** An ∞-category is a quasicategory in Mathlib's sense, `SSet.Quasicategory`. Each target is formalized in this model. Simplicial categories and model categories are presentations, compared with quasicategories by theorems.

**Weak homotopy equivalence.** A morphism `f : X → Y` of simplicial sets is a weak homotopy equivalence when, for every Kan complex Z, precomposition with f is a bijection `π₀ Fun(Y, Z) → π₀ Fun(X, Z)` (Kerodon 3.1.7.12). This definition is combinatorial; that it agrees with "the geometric realization is a weak homotopy equivalence of spaces" is the target `HTT.A.2.7/realization`, which only L12 §7.1 uses. The weak equivalences of the Kan–Quillen model structure are these maps. "Equivalence" with no qualifier means categorical equivalence.

**The homotopy category of spaces.** `H` is the homotopy category of the Kan–Quillen model structure, equivalently the localization of `SSet` at the weak homotopy equivalences. HTT defines it through CW complexes (Example 1.1.3.3); the roadmap does not use that description. `H` is Cartesian monoidal, and `SSet ⥤ H` preserves finite products. An H-enriched category is a Mathlib `EnrichedCategory H`.

**One definition, many characterizations.** Every notion has exactly one Lean definition, given in the table below. It is HTT's definition, except where HTT's would put machinery at the root of the build that the rest does not need (weak homotopy equivalences, whose HTT definition goes through topological spaces) or where another form is markedly more usable downstream (adjunctions, Kan extensions along arbitrary maps). Every other characterization (HTT's where it differs, Kerodon's, a Mathlib-shaped form) is an `iff` or `TFAE` target, included when some target uses it or it is an HTT statement. A Tau Ceti declaration that disagrees with the table is redefined (*Redefinitions of Tau Ceti declarations*).

The choices:

| Notion | Definition | Characterizations (targets) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| categorical equivalence of simplicial sets (for ∞-categories: equivalence of ∞-categories) | `hS → hT` is an equivalence of H-enriched categories, `hS = h C[S]` (HTT 1.1.5.14); equivalently `C[f]` is a Dwyer–Kan equivalence. HTT's "equivalence of ∞-categories" is this notion between ∞-categories, not a separate definition | `hFun(T, C) → hFun(S, C)` an equivalence for every ∞-category C (HTT 2.2.5.8); for maps of ∞-categories, an equivalence in Mathlib's `SSet.QCat.bicategory`, i.e. a homotopy inverse up to natural isomorphism (Kerodon 4.5.1.10; Tau Ceti main's `SSet.QCat.IsCategoricalEquivalence`, to be renamed), and fully faithful plus essentially surjective (HTT 1.2.10.1, Kerodon 4.8.4.1) |
| weak homotopy equivalence | bijections `π₀ Fun(Y, Z) → π₀ Fun(X, Z)` for every Kan complex Z (Kerodon 3.1.7.12) | `Ex^∞ f` is a homotopy equivalence; `|f|` is a weak homotopy equivalence of spaces (used by L12 §7.1) |
| morphism space | `Map_C(X, Y)`, an object of H (HTT 1.2.2.1), with two simplicial models, both targets: the right- and left-pinched spaces `Hom^R`, `Hom^L` (HTT 1.2.2.3; Lurie's statements use these) and `Hom_C(X, Y)`, the fibre of `Fun(Δ[1], C) → C × C` (HTT §1.2.2, Kerodon 4.6.1; the user-facing space) | `Hom^R ≃ Hom_C ≃ Hom^L` (HTT 4.2.1.8); `Map_{C[C]} ≃ \|Hom^R\|` (HTT 2.2.4.1) |
| fully faithful | `hS → hT` fully faithful as a functor of H-enriched categories: each `Map_S(x, y) → Map_T(fx, fy)` an isomorphism in H (HTT 1.2.10.1), for any simplicial sets | for ∞-categories: homotopy equivalences of `Hom^R` (through HTT 2.2.4.1, L2.8) or of `Hom_C` (with 4.2.1.8; Kerodon 4.8.3.1) |
| essentially surjective | on homotopy categories (both books) | — |
| final object | strongly final: `C_{/X} → C` is a trivial fibration, that is `SSet.IsTerminalVertex` (HTT 1.2.12.3, Joyal), for any simplicial set | contractible `Hom_C(−, X)` (Kerodon 4.7.3.1, HTT 1.2.12.4); final in `hC` (HTT 1.2.12.1, 1.2.12.5). Both need C to be an ∞-category |
| limit, colimit | a final object of `C_{/p}`, an initial object of `C_{p/}` (HTT 1.2.13.4) | a cone inducing equivalences of morphism spaces (Kerodon 7.1.1.1) |
| p-Cartesian edge | the restriction `X_{/f} → X_{/y} ×_{S_{/p y}} S_{/p f}` is a trivial fibration (HTT 2.4.1.1, `SSet.Edge.IsCartesian`) | lifting against `Λ[n, n]` (Kerodon 5.1.1.1) |
| categorical fibration | a fibration of the Joyal model structure (HTT 2.2.5.1), that is, right lifting against monomorphisms that are categorical equivalences (Kerodon 4.5.6.5) | between ∞-categories: an inner fibration lifting equivalences (HTT 2.4.6.5, Kerodon 4.5.6.1) |
| adjunction | unit and counit with the triangle identities up to homotopy (Kerodon 6.2.1.1), i.e. a Mathlib `Bicategory.Adjunction` in `SSet.QCat.bicategory` | a bicartesian correspondence over `Δ[1]` (HTT 5.2.2.1), with constructions both ways; unit transformations (HTT 5.2.2.8) |
| Kan extension | along a full inclusion: pointwise (HTT 4.3.2.2 = Kerodon 7.3.2.1); along any map: pointwise over the comma objects `K_{/C}` (Kerodon 7.3.1.2) | through the mapping cylinder (HTT 4.3.3.2); the universal property (Kerodon 7.3.6) |
| localization | universal inversion of a class W (Kerodon 6.3.1.9, HA 1.3.4.1, Mathlib `Functor.IsLocalization`) | — |
| reflective localization | a fully faithful right adjoint (HTT 5.2.7.2 "localization", Kerodon 6.3.3.4, Mathlib `Reflective`) | is a localization (HTT 5.2.7.12) |
| cofinal | sections of right fibrations (HTT 4.1.1.1; Kerodon's "right cofinal" 7.2.1.1; HA's "left cofinal") | Theorem A (HTT 4.1.3.1, Kerodon 7.2.3.1), the shape of Mathlib's `Functor.Final`; needs the target to be an ∞-category |
| weakly contractible | `K → Δ[0]` is a weak homotopy equivalence | constant maps `Z → Fun(K, Z)` are a homotopy equivalence for every Kan complex Z; `Z → Fun(K, Z)` is a categorical equivalence for every ∞-category Z |
| Ind-completion | HTT's full subcategory of presheaves (5.3.5.1) | the universal property (Kerodon 9.3.1.1); κ-flat presheaves, whose ∞-category of elements is κ-filtered (Kerodon 9.3.4.7, Theorem 9.3.4.14) |
| essentially κ-small, locally small | for κ uncountable regular: a categorical equivalence to a κ-small ∞-category (HTT 5.4.1.2 (3)–(4), 5.4.1.3; Kerodon 4.9.5.1); locally small: every `Hom^R_C(X, Y)` has a small Kan model (Tau Ceti `SSet.IsLocallySmall`, `TauCeti.HasSmallSpaceModel`; HTT 5.4.1.7 (1) through 5.4.1.5 (3)). Keep κ uncountable in the definition: for κ = ℵ₀ the theory fails (Kerodon Warning 4.9.5.8) | locally κ-small with κ-small `π₀(C^≃)` (Kerodon 4.9.7.7, HTT 5.4.1.2 (1)); κ-compact in `Cat∞` (Kerodon 9.2.7.14, HTT 5.4.1.2 (5)); minimal models κ-small (HTT 5.4.1.2 (2)); locally small: every `Hom_C(X, Y)` essentially small (Kerodon §4.9.7, through 4.2.1.8) |
| accessible | `Ind_κ(C₀) ≃ C` with C₀ small (HTT 5.4.2.1, Kerodon 9.4.7.1) | κ-filtered colimits and a generating set of κ-compact objects (HTT 5.4.2.2), the shape of Mathlib's `IsCardinalAccessibleCategory` |
| filtered, κ-compact, presentable, idempotent complete | as in both books (HTT 5.3.1.7, 5.3.4.5, 5.5.0.1, §4.4.5 with 4.4.5.15 and §5.1.4; Kerodon 9.1.1.1, 9.2.5.6, 9.5.1.2, 8.5.4.1) | Mathlib's forms of "filtered" and "idempotent complete" are not correct for ∞-categories and are not used |
| left exact | `G^op` right exact (HTT Remarks 5.3.2.2, 5.3.2.10; right exact is HTT 5.3.2.1 at κ = ω) | with finite limits in the source: G preserves them (dual of 5.3.2.9) |
| groupoid object | the squares `U([n]) → U(S), U(S') → U({s})` with `S ∪ S' = [n]`, `S ∩ S' = {s}` are pullbacks (HTT 6.1.2.6 (4″), 6.1.2.7) | the other conditions of 6.1.2.6 |
| Čech nerve | an augmented simplicial object right Kan extended from `N(Δ₊^{≤0})^op` (HTT 6.1.2.11 (1)) | groupoid object with a pullback square in degree 1 (6.1.2.11 (2)) |
| effective epimorphism | a Čech nerve of f is a geometric realization, in any ∞-category (HTT 6.2.3.5 (2)) | the other conditions of 6.2.3.5 in a semitopos |
| Grothendieck topology on an ∞-category C | a Mathlib `GrothendieckTopology` on the homotopy category `hC` | HTT's sieves on slices (6.2.2.1), compared by HTT Remark 6.2.2.3 |
| coherent topological space | Mathlib `CompactSpace`, `QuasiSeparatedSpace` and `PrespectralSpace` together (HTT 6.5.4.4's coherence; weaker than `SpectralSpace`) | — |
| t-structure | Mathlib's cohomological `Triangulated.TStructure` on the homotopy category, with `C_{≥n} = le (−n)`, `C_{≤n} = ge (−n)` (HA 1.2.1.1) | HA's homological statements, through the dictionary |
| dg category | Tau Ceti's cochain-enriched `TauCeti.DGCategory`; HA's chain degree m is cochain degree −m (HA §1.3.1) | — |

The table binds every Lean definition of these notions, whichever roadmap's target introduces it; another roadmap needing one cites this table rather than fixing its own. A characterization that holds only under a hypothesis (an ∞-category target, a Kan complex source) never becomes the definition with that hypothesis dropped: it stays an `iff` stating the hypothesis.

**Model structures on one category.** A category may carry several model structures (`SSet` has Kan–Quillen and Joyal), while Lean's instance search assumes one canonical instance per type, which is why Mathlib's `ModelCategory` docstring advises local instances or type synonyms. So the Kan–Quillen structure is Mathlib's scoped instance (`open SSet.modelCategoryQuillen`, with F2.4's weak equivalences), and every other model structure lives on a `def` type synonym `T` of its underlying category `C`: never an `abbrev`, never a global instance on `C`. A category to which the roadmap gives only one model structure and which is no synonym's underlying category (`TauCeti.MarkedSSet`, L4.3) carries it as an ordinary instance. `T` receives its `Category` instance, and any other instance its statements need, explicitly by `inferInstanceAs`. Each synonym comes with:

- the bridge `T.equivalence : C ≌ T`, the identity functors (`CategoryTheory.Equivalence.refl`), named after Mathlib's `ShrinkHoms.equivalence : C ≌ ShrinkHoms C` for its own category synonyms;
- the transport lemmas `T.weakEquivalences_eq`, `T.cofibrations_eq` and `T.fibrations_eq`, of the form `(weakEquivalences T).inverseImage T.equivalence.functor = W` with W the defining class on `C` (the hypotheses of Mathlib's `ModelCategory.transport`). They are `rfl` when the instance is built from the defining classes, which it should be.

A statement that mixes two structures on one category (Kan complexes are Joyal fibrant, categorical equivalences are Kan–Quillen weak equivalences, Quillen adjunctions between synonyms) moves objects and maps with `T.equivalence.functor` and `T.equivalence.inverse`, never with `show` or a bare type ascription. Mathlib's instance `ModelCategory.over` gives `Over X` the structure induced from the category of X. So for `S : SSet`, `Over S` carries the Kan–Quillen structure over S and `Over (SSet.Joyal.equivalence.functor.obj S)` the Joyal structure over S, and every other structure on an over category (covariant, contravariant, Cartesian) is again a synonym. The synonyms: `ModelCategory.Trivial` (F1.4), `ModelCategory.WithClasses` and `ModelCategory.Transferred` (F1.6), `Reedy` (F1.8), `ProjectiveDiagram` and `InjectiveDiagram` (F3.2), `EnrichedCat.Bergner` (F3.4), `EnrichedDiagram.Projective` and `EnrichedDiagram.Injective` (F3.5), `SimplicialModelCategory.Localization` (F3.9), `SSet.Over.Covariant` and `SSet.Over.Contravariant` (L2.6), `SSet.Joyal` (L1.4; its model structure L3.8), `TauCeti.MarkedSSet.Cartesian` and `TauCeti.MarkedSSet.SharpCartesian` (L4.3), `TauCeti.MarkedSSet.CoCartesian` (L4.6), and `TopCat.OverBasis` (L12.1).

**Terms.** The roadmap uses Kerodon's names where HTT has none or uses a model-categorical phrase: *core* `C^≃` (HTT's "largest Kan complex contained in C"), *categorical pullback/pushout square* (HTT's homotopy pullback/pushout for the Joyal model structure), *locally Kan* simplicial category (HTT's "fibrant"), *oriented fiber product* `C ×⃗_E D`, *right/left-pinched morphism space*, *left/right covering map*, *covariant transport*, and *reflective localization* ("localization" alone always means universal inversion of morphisms). Two notions keep HTT's names: *categorical fibration* (Kerodon's *isofibration*) and *cofinal* (HTT 4.1.1.1). For cofinality the later sources disagree on handedness: HA calls HTT's cofinal maps *left cofinal* (HA, notation section), while Kerodon calls the same notion *right cofinal* (7.2.1.1); the roadmap uses HTT's unhanded name and records this dictionary where HA targets cite left cofinality. Kerodon's "isomorphism" of objects is called an equivalence, as in HTT and `SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence`.

**Orientation.** The join is `K ⋆ L`, with K first. `C_{/p}` is formed with `Y ⋆ K` and `C_{p/}` with `K ⋆ Y`. A right mapping simplex `Δ[n+1] → C` is constant at y on its last vertex.

**Universes.** One universe parameter u, as in HTT §1.2.15: small means in `Type u`, large means in `Type (u + 1)`.

- A small simplicial set is an `SSet.{u}`. `Kan`, `S = N(Kan)` and `Cat∞` are large: simplicial sets in `SSet.{u + 1}` whose morphism spaces are essentially u-small. Mathlib's `nerve` and simplicial nerve land in `SSet.{max u v}`, so the nerve of a large locally small category is an `SSet.{u + 1}` already.
- Local smallness means small Kan models of morphism homotopy types (Tau Ceti `HasSmallSpaceModel`), not small sets of simplices: a simplicial set has a single universe for all its simplices.
- Statements are universe-polymorphic in u, so that Lurie's "the same argument applies to large ∞-categories" is the same theorem at `u + 1`. Moving between universes goes through `SSet.uliftFunctor` and is a stated comparison, never implicit.
- A definition that quantifies over all ∞-categories, spaces or diagrams (categorical equivalence, localization, Kan extensions along all functors, the universal property of `Ind`) states the universe of the quantified objects, and comes with a target showing that testing in that universe suffices.
- Size hypotheses are stated in Mathlib's vocabulary: `Small.{w}` and `EssentiallySmall.{w}` for sets and categories, `HasCardinalLT` for cardinality bounds, `IsCardinalFiltered`, `IsCardinalPresentable` and `IsCardinalAccessibleCategory` for κ-filtered colimits, κ-compact objects and accessibility. Cardinals are `Cardinal.{u}` and regular cardinals are `Cardinal.IsRegular`; comparisons across universes use `Cardinal.lift`. An accessibility or presentability target names its cardinal hypotheses (κ regular, κ ≪ τ in the sense of HTT 5.4.2.8) explicitly.

**Sources and locators.** HTT is Lurie's *Higher Topos Theory*, author PDF of 9 April 2017 ([math.ias.edu/~lurie/papers/HTT.pdf](https://www.math.ias.edu/~lurie/papers/HTT.pdf)). Its PDF pages run 18 ahead of the printed pages, and locators give the PDF page. HA is Lurie's *Higher Algebra*, author PDF of 18 September 2017 ([math.ias.edu/~lurie/papers/HA.pdf](https://www.math.ias.edu/~lurie/papers/HA.pdf)), where the PDF page equals the printed page. Both links served these editions as of 5 November 2026. A locator names Lurie's number and the PDF page, for example (HTT Proposition 1.2.8.3, PDF p. 59). Whoever formalizes a target reads Lurie's statement and proof at the locator first. The statement binds: the target formalizes what Lurie states, and any departure is written into the target. The proof does not bind. The prescribed proof route is Lurie's unless the target names another; when it does, the formalizer reads that proof too.

**Definitions are specified exactly.** Every definition target states its Lean definition precisely enough that review can check a PR against it: the condition, its hypotheses (for example, that the target is an ∞-category), and the Lean name. A PR whose definition differs from its target's is out of spec, even if it is mathematically equivalent. [Suggested.lean](Suggested.lean) gives typechecked forms of these definitions, with `sorry` where a proof or construction is the target itself; the README is definitive.

**Prerequisite labels.** In the *Needs* lines:

- Lean names in backticks are targets of this roadmap, located by the section that states them, or are declarations of Mathlib or Tau Ceti.
- Other roadmaps are cited by name and section.
- `HTT.A.2.7/…` and `HTT.A.3.7/…` name the foundational targets of F2 and F3.
- A bare Lurie number names the target formalizing that statement.
- A layer item (L5.2) may need a later item of the same layer. The items of a layer are written in the book's order and formalized in dependency order; each layer's introduction lists its forward needs, with the statement that causes each. No item needs an item of a later layer.

**Notation.**

| Symbol | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Λ[n, i], ∂Δ[n]` | horns and boundaries (Mathlib) |
| `π_n(X, x), [K, Z]` | combinatorial homotopy groups of a Kan complex; homotopy classes of maps into a Kan complex |
| `sd, Ex, Ex^∞` | barycentric subdivision, its right adjoint, and the colimit of `Ex^n` |
| `H, Map_S(x, y)` | the homotopy category of spaces; the mapping object of a simplicial set in `H` |
| `C[S], N(C)` | the simplicial category of a simplicial set (left adjoint of the simplicial nerve); the simplicial nerve |
| `hS, π(C)` | the H-enriched homotopy category; the homotopy category of a quasicategory built from edges |
| `Hom_C(x, y)` | the morphism space: the fibre of `Fun(Δ[1], C) → C × C` over (x, y) |
| `Hom^R_C(x, y), Hom^L_C(x, y)` | the right- and left-pinched morphism spaces |
| `C^≃` | the core of an ∞-category |
| `C ×⃗_E D` | the oriented fiber product |
| `Fun(K, C)` | the internal Hom of `SSet` |
| `K ⋆ L, K^◁, K^▷` | join, left cone `Δ[0] ⋆ K`, right cone `K ⋆ Δ[0]` |
| `C_{/p}, C_{p/}` | over- and under-categories of a diagram p |
| `Kan, S` | the simplicial category of Kan complexes; its simplicial nerve, the ∞-category of spaces |

## Exact supplier contracts

The baseline is Mathlib `1b1ccf4b088b32fa3f23f2de1127433254a81e1e` and Tau Ceti `7ac4960977499bb4976656e7658c457204e14c04`. `Suggested.lean` builds against this repository's pins (Mathlib `1b1ccf4b088b32fa3f23f2de1127433254a81e1e`, Tau Ceti `2fd255d997f47c0b5d834ee416c7015d55444ce5`); Tau Ceti declarations that postdate that pin are copied locally there and marked as such.

### From Mathlib

- **Simplicial sets:** `SSet`, horns and boundaries, `SSet.Subcomplex`, `SSet.StrictSegal`, `CategoryTheory.nerve`, `SSet.hoFunctor` with `CategoryTheory.nerveAdjunction`, `SSet.Truncated` and coskeleta, `SSet.π₀`, the sd ⊣ Ex adjunction, and the simplicial-category instance of `SSet`.
- **Kan complexes and anodyne extensions:** `SSet.KanComplex`, `SSet.modelCategoryQuillen` (cofibrations and fibrations), `SSet.anodyneExtensions` with pushout-products and Moss's pairings.
- **Quasicategories:** `SSet.Quasicategory`, `SSet.InnerFibration`, `SSet.Truncated.HomotopyCategory₂`, `SSet.QCat.bicategory`, `CategoryTheory.Nerve.quasicategory`.
- **Simplicial categories:** `CategoryTheory.SimplicialCategory`, `CategoryTheory.SimplicialThickening` with its functoriality (HTT's `C[Δ^J]`), `CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve`.
- **Homotopical algebra:** `HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory`, the homotopy category of a model category with the fundamental lemma, Ken Brown's lemma, the small object argument.
- **Category theory:** `CategoryTheory.EnrichedCategory`, `CategoryTheory.Localization`, limits, Kan extensions, the Dold–Kan correspondence (`AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan`, `CategoryTheory.Idempotents.DoldKan.equivalence`), Grothendieck abelian categories and their injectives, `Bicategory.Adjunction`, `Triangulated.TStructure`, `GrothendieckTopology` and `Sheaf`, `EffectiveEpi`, `ReedyStructure`.
- **Topology:** `TopCat`, geometric realization `SSet.toTop` and singular sets `TopCat.toSSet`, for F2's comparison with realization and for L12; `CompactSpace`, `QuasiSeparatedSpace`, `PrespectralSpace`, `TopologicalSpace.Opens`, `Locale`, paracompactness and partitions of unity, for L11–L12.

**Mathlib work in progress.** Joël Riou's Mathlib development covers part of the foundational material: presentable and accessible categories and the representation theorem (mathlib4 #30847, #45545, #45562; F1.1, F1.6), proper model categories and homotopy cartesian squares (#41744, #41735; F1.5, F3), Kan fibrations, horns and subdivision preserving anodyne extensions (#43869, #45530, #45531, #45532, #45533, #44464; F2.1, F2.3), homotopy groups and the fundamental groupoid of Kan complexes (#42435, #42488, #42495, #42587; F2.2), and the accessibility of homology and derived categories (#43980, #25848; L9). The corresponding targets of this roadmap are stated in the shape of that work; once a piece of it is in Mathlib, Mathlib's declarations discharge the target and the roadmap uses them. His fundamental groupoid of a simplicial set, `SSet.FundamentalGroupoid` (#42523, #42576), is already in Mathlib at the pin and is used in F2.2.

## How to read the build

The layers are built in the order of the table. Each target sits in a layer at or after every layer it needs. The layer is the target's home section, unless one of its inputs is later, and then the layer of that input. Lurie states many results before he proves them. Those results sit in the layer of their proof: HTT 1.2.4.3, 1.2.5.1 and 1.2.9.3, for example, are in L2 and L3. Each such target's *Needs* names the later input that placed it.

## Layer F1: Classical category theory and model categories

HTT's Appendix A.1–A.2: the 1-categorical and model-categorical background the book cites. Mathlib supplies most of it:

- κ-filtered categories, κ-presentable objects, locally presentable and accessible categories, the comparison of κ-filtered categories with κ-directed posets, sharply larger cardinals and uniformization (`CategoryTheory.Presentable`);
- lifting properties, stability classes of morphisms, weak factorization systems, transfinite compositions, relative cell complexes and the small object argument (`CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty`, `CategoryTheory.SmallObject`);
- monoidal, closed and enriched categories, lax monoidal functors and change of enrichment;
- model categories with cylinders, path objects, homotopies, the fundamental lemma, Ken Brown's factorization and derivability structures (`AlgebraicTopology.ModelCategory`), and derived adjunctions (`Functor.Derived`);
- Reedy structures with the instance for `SimplexCategory`, and coends.

The targets are what is missing: weakly saturated classes as a named notion, the comparison of Lurie's poset-indexed compactness with Mathlib's, the small object argument for every small set in a locally presentable category together with its accessibility, tensored and cotensored enriched categories, trees of pushouts, the homotopy extension property, left properness and homotopy pushouts, Quillen adjunctions and equivalences, accessible subcategories, combinatorial model categories with Smith's theorem, injective and projective classes of diagram maps, and latching objects, good filtrations and the Reedy model structure.

Everything here is about ordinary categories. Where Lurie cites a statement of the main text in this appendix, the target uses a 1-categorical statement instead, so that F1 needs nothing from the main text:

- Definition 5.4.2.1 in A.1.5.10: Mathlib's `IsCardinalAccessibleCategory`;
- Lemma 5.4.6.3 in A.2.6.6: the classical back-and-forth argument (A.2.6.6 below);
- Corollary 5.3.1.10 in A.2.6.10: not needed, since Mathlib's `ModelCategory.mk'` derives the retract axiom for weak equivalences;
- Proposition 5.4.7.10 in A.2.6.8: `HTT.A.2.6/accessible-intersections`;
- Proposition A.2.9.14 (a statement about the Joyal model structure) in A.2.9.15: the classical extension argument (A.2.9.15 below).

Projective and injective model structures on diagram categories (A.2.8.2) and the results that use them sit in F3, because Lurie proves A.2.8.3 through Lemma A.3.3.3. Proposition A.2.9.14, Remark A.2.9.16 and Lemma A.2.9.18 sit in L7, and Lemma A.2.9.17 in F2; nothing in F1 uses them. No item of F1 needs a later item of F1. Proposition A.2.9.26 sits in F3.2, since its statement uses left Quillen bifunctors (Definition A.3.1.1, F3.3).

**Orientation of enrichment.** Lurie writes composition in a C-enriched category as `Map(Y, Z) ⊗ Map(X, Y) ⟶ Map(X, Z)`, and calls `(C, ⊗)` *left-closed* when every `A ⊗ −` has a right adjoint. Mathlib's `EnrichedCategory V C` composes as `(X ⟶[V] Y) ⊗ (Y ⟶[V] Z) ⟶ (X ⟶[V] Z)`, and its `MonoidalClosed` asks for right adjoints of `tensorLeft A = A ⊗ −`, which is Lurie's left-closedness. So a C-enriched category in Lurie's sense is a Mathlib `EnrichedCategory` over the monoidal opposite `Cᴹᵒᵖ`, and Lurie's right-closedness of C is `MonoidalClosed Cᴹᵒᵖ`. Every enrichment the roadmap uses (over `Type`, `SSet`, H, a Cartesian monoidal category) is symmetric, where the two orientations agree through the braiding. The targets are stated in Mathlib's orientation.

### F1.1 Presentable categories and the small object argument

**κ-filtered posets and κ-compact objects** (HTT Definition A.1.1.1, PDF p. 806). For a regular cardinal κ, a partially ordered set I is κ-filtered when every subset of cardinality < κ has an upper bound. An object X of a cocomplete category is κ-compact when `Hom(X, −)` carries colimits indexed by κ-filtered posets to colimits of sets, and *small* when it is κ-compact for some regular κ.

*Lean:* no new definitions. A κ-filtered poset is a partial order I with `IsCardinalFiltered I κ`; κ-compact is Mathlib's `IsCardinalPresentable X κ` (`Hom(X, −)` preserves colimits indexed by κ-filtered small *categories*); small is `IsPresentable X`. Provide the two comparisons:

- a partial order I is `IsCardinalFiltered I κ` exactly when every subset of cardinality < κ has an upper bound (one direction is Mathlib's `isCardinalFiltered_preorder`);
- `IsCardinalPresentable X κ` holds exactly when `coyoneda.obj (op X)` preserves colimits of shape I for every small κ-filtered partial order I.

*Proof route.* The second comparison: every small κ-filtered category J receives a final functor from a κ-filtered partial order (Mathlib `IsCardinalFiltered.exists_cardinal_directed`, Deligne's argument), and colimits along a final functor agree.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Presentable` (`IsCardinalFiltered`, `IsCardinalPresentable`, `IsPresentable`).

**Presentable categories** (HTT Definition A.1.1.2, PDF p. 806). A category C is presentable when it has small colimits, a small set of objects generates it under colimits (every object is a colimit of a small diagram of objects of the set), every object is small, and C is locally small.

*Lean:* Mathlib's `IsLocallyPresentable.{w} C` (for some regular κ, `IsCardinalLocallyPresentable C κ`: cocomplete, with a small set of κ-presentable objects of which every object is a κ-filtered colimit). Lurie's form is a characterization target: for `C : Type u` with `Category.{v} C`, `IsLocallyPresentable.{w} C` holds exactly when `HasColimitsOfSize.{w, w} C`, `LocallySmall.{w} C`, and there is a small `P : ObjectProperty C` (`ObjectProperty.Small.{w} P`) of presentable objects with every object in `P.colimitsOfShape J` for some small category J.

*Proof route.* From Lurie's form to Mathlib's: a small set of presentable objects is κ-presentable for one regular κ; a set that generates under colimits is a strong generator (Mathlib `ObjectProperty.IsStrongGenerator.mk_of_exists_colimitsOfShape`); conclude with `IsCardinalLocallyPresentable.iff_exists_isStrongGenerator`. The converse uses Mathlib's instances `IsAccessibleCategory → LocallySmall` and `IsAccessibleCategory → IsPresentable X`.

**Checks.** `Type u` is presentable, generated by the point; a presentable category in Lurie's sense is `IsCardinalLocallyPresentable C κ` for all sufficiently large regular κ (Mathlib `IsCardinalLocallyPresentable.of_le`).

*Needs:* A.1.1.1; Mathlib `IsLocallyPresentable`, `IsCardinalLocallyPresentable.iff_exists_isStrongGenerator`, `ObjectProperty.IsStrongGenerator`.

**Weakly saturated classes** (`MorphismProperty.IsWeaklySaturated`; HTT Definition A.1.2.2, PDF p. 807). In a category with small colimits, a class S of morphisms is weakly saturated when it is stable under cobase change, under transfinite composition, and under retracts.

*Lean:* `class MorphismProperty.IsWeaklySaturated.{w} (W : MorphismProperty C) : Prop` extending Mathlib's `W.IsStableUnderCobaseChange`, `W.IsStableUnderTransfiniteComposition.{w}` and `W.IsStableUnderRetracts`. No colimit hypothesis in the definition; every statement that uses it assumes C cocomplete. The weakly saturated class generated by W is `MorphismProperty.weakSaturation.{w} W`, the infimum of the weakly saturated classes containing W (propose both names).

Lurie's transfinite compositions are indexed by ordinals with a root `C ⟶ D_{<0} = C`; Mathlib's (`TransfiniteCompositionOfShape J`) are indexed by well-ordered types with a bottom element and ask for well-order-continuous functors. The two agree up to reindexing; no comparison target is needed.

**Checks.**

- `isomorphisms C` is weakly saturated, and is `weakSaturation ⊥`.
- In `Type u`, the weakly saturated class generated by `∅ ⟶ PUnit` is the class of injections.

*Needs:* Mathlib `MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderCobaseChange`, `IsStableUnderTransfiniteComposition`, `IsStableUnderRetracts`.

**Isomorphisms and composites** (HTT Proposition A.1.2.3, PDF p. 808). A weakly saturated class in a cocomplete category contains every isomorphism and is closed under composition. Composition is Mathlib's instance `IsStableUnderTransfiniteComposition → IsMultiplicative`; isomorphisms follow from identities and the stability of transfinite compositions under isomorphism of arrows.

*Needs:* A.1.2.2.

**Intersections and lifting classes** (HTT Remark A.1.2.4, PDF p. 808). Any intersection of weakly saturated classes is weakly saturated, so `weakSaturation W` exists and is the smallest weakly saturated class containing W; for every class W, `W.llp` is weakly saturated, so `weakSaturation W ≤ W.rlp.llp`. Lurie offers to take A.1.2.3 as part of the definition; the roadmap proves it instead.

*Needs:* A.1.2.2; Mathlib `MorphismProperty.llp_isStableUnderCobaseChange`, `llp_isStableUnderRetracts`, and the stability of `llp` under transfinite composition (the instance `MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderTransfiniteComposition W.llp`, in `Mathlib.CategoryTheory.SmallObject.TransfiniteCompositionLifting`).

**The small object argument** (HTT Proposition A.1.2.5, PDF pp. 808–809). Let C be presentable and A a small set of morphisms `C_i ⟶ D_i`. There is a functor `T : Arrow C ⥤` (composable pairs) carrying `f : X ⟶ Z` to a factorization `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z` whose first map lies in the weakly saturated class generated by A and whose second map has the right lifting property against A. If κ is a regular cardinal for which every `C_i` and `D_i` is κ-compact, T preserves κ-filtered colimits.

Mathlib supplies the factorization once `HasSmallObjectArgument.{w} A` holds: `SmallObject.functorialFactorizationData A κ`, built by iterating a pushout-of-coproducts step along `κ.ord.ToType` (Lurie's construction), with first map in `A.rlp.llp` and second map in `A.rlp`. Provide:

- the instance `HasSmallObjectArgument.{w} A` for `[IsLocallyPresentable.{w} C]` and `[MorphismProperty.IsSmall.{w} A]` (choose κ with every source κ-presentable; `κ.ord.ToType` is κ-filtered, Mathlib's instance);
- part (2): if every source and target of A is κ-presentable, the functor `SmallObject.iteration A κ : Arrow C ⥤ Arrow C` is `Functor.IsCardinalAccessible κ`, so both factors of the functorial factorization preserve κ-filtered colimits.

*Proof route.* For (2): the step functor is built from the sets of squares from members of A to `f`, which commute with κ-filtered colimits in `Arrow C` because sources and targets are κ-presentable, and from coproducts and pushouts; the iteration is a colimit over `κ.ord.ToType` of such steps.

*Needs:* A.1.1.1, A.1.1.2, A.1.2.2, A.1.2.4; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.SmallObject` (`HasSmallObjectArgument`, `IsCardinalForSmallObjectArgument`, `SmallObject.iteration`, `SmallObject.functorialFactorizationData`).

**The generated class is the lifting class** (HTT Corollary A.1.2.7, PDF p. 809). In a presentable category, for a small set A, `A.rlp.llp = weakSaturation A`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's retract argument: factor f by A.1.2.5; if f has the left lifting property against `A.rlp`, it is a retract of the first factor. Mathlib's `llp_rlp_of_hasSmallObjectArgument` gives the same class as retracts of transfinite compositions of pushouts of coproducts of members of A; coproducts of members of A are transfinite compositions of pushouts of members of A, so these lie in `weakSaturation A`.

*Needs:* A.1.2.4, A.1.2.5; Mathlib `MorphismProperty.llp_rlp_of_hasSmallObjectArgument`.

**Cell presentations under the source** (HTT Remark A.1.2.8, PDF p. 810). In a presentable category, for a small set S and `f : X ⟶ Y` in `weakSaturation S`: there is a transfinite sequence `Y_β` in `Under X` in which each `colim_{γ<β} Y_γ ⟶ Y_β` is a pushout of a single member of S, and Y is a retract of `colim_β Y_β` *in `Under X`*. Mathlib's statement retracts in `Arrow C` and attaches coproducts of cells at each step; provide Lurie's form by well-ordering each family of cells and by the retract argument, which fixes X.

*Needs:* A.1.2.5, A.1.2.7; Mathlib `RelativeCellComplex`, `Mathlib.CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.RetractArgument`.

### F1.2 Monoidal and enriched categories

**The Cartesian monoidal structure** (HTT Example A.1.3.1, PDF p. 811). A category with finite products is monoidal under the product, with the final object as unit. Supplied by Mathlib: `CartesianMonoidalCategory`, and `CartesianMonoidalCategory.ofHasFiniteProducts` for a category with chosen finite products.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian`.

**Closed monoidal categories** (HTT Definition A.1.3.4, PDF p. 812). `(C, ⊗)` is left-closed when every `A ⊗ −` has a right adjoint, right-closed when every `− ⊗ A` has one, closed when both. Left-closed is Mathlib's `MonoidalClosed C`; right-closed is `MonoidalClosed Cᴹᵒᵖ`; for a braided C the two agree. No new definitions.

*Lean:* no new definition: left-closed is `MonoidalClosed C`, right-closed is `MonoidalClosed Cᴹᵒᵖ`, and closed means both.

*Needs:* Mathlib `MonoidalClosed`, `MonoidalOpposite`.

**Lax monoidal functors** (HTT Definition A.1.3.5, PDF p. 812). A right-lax monoidal functor is a functor G with natural maps `G A ⊗ G B ⟶ G (A ⊗ B)` and `1 ⟶ G 1` satisfying associativity and unit coherence; left-lax is the dual; a monoidal functor is a right-lax one whose structure maps are isomorphisms; a monoidal natural transformation commutes with the structure maps. These are Mathlib's `Functor.LaxMonoidal`, `Functor.OplaxMonoidal`, `Functor.Monoidal` and `NatTrans.IsMonoidal`. No new definitions.

*Lean:* no new definition: right-lax is `F.LaxMonoidal`, left-lax is `F.OplaxMonoidal`, monoidal is `F.Monoidal`, and monoidal transformations are `NatTrans.IsMonoidal`.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Functor`, `CategoryTheory.Monoidal.NaturalTransformation`.

**Change of enrichment and underlying categories** (HTT Remark A.1.4.3, PDF p. 815). A right-lax monoidal functor `G : C ⥤ C'` turns a C-enriched category D into a C'-enriched category `G(D)` with the same objects and `Map_{G(D)}(X, Y) = G(Map_D(X, Y))`. Applied to `Hom(1, −) : C ⥤ Type`, this gives the underlying ordinary category of D. Supplied by Mathlib: `TransportEnrichment F D` and `ForgetEnrichment V D` (with `EnrichedOrdinaryCategory` comparing an ordinary category to the underlying category of an enrichment).

**Checks.** Transport along `SSet.π₀Functor : SSet ⥤ Type`, which preserves finite products and so is monoidal, turns a simplicial category into the ordinary category of its path components of mapping spaces.

*Needs:* A.1.3.1; Mathlib `TransportEnrichment`, `ForgetEnrichment`.

**Tensors and cotensors; self-enrichment** (`EnrichedCategory.HasTensors`, `EnrichedCategory.HasCotensors`; HTT Example A.1.4.5 with the definitions before it, PDF pp. 816–817). For a monoidal category V and a V-enriched category D, a tensor of `v : V` and `X : D` is an object T corepresenting `Y ↦` (the internal hom from v into `Map(X, Y)`), through a map `v ⟶ Map(X, T)`; a cotensor of v and X is an object P representing `Y ↦` (the internal hom from v into `Map(Y, X)`) for the other closed structure, through a map `v ⟶ Map(P, X)`. D is tensored (cotensored) over V when all tensors (cotensors) exist. A.1.4.5: a monoidal category closed on one side (Lurie's right-closed, `MonoidalClosed Cᴹᵒᵖ` in Mathlib's orientation), enriched over itself, is tensored over itself, and it is cotensored over itself exactly when it is also closed on the other side (Lurie's left-closed, `MonoidalClosed C`).

*Lean:* propose, for `[MonoidalCategory V] [EnrichedCategory V D]`:

- `EnrichedCategory.HasTensors V D` (with `[MonoidalClosed V]`): for all `v` and `X` there are `T : D` and `η : v ⟶ (X ⟶[V] T)` such that for every Y the map `(T ⟶[V] Y) ⟶ (ihom v).obj (X ⟶[V] Y)`, adjoint to `v ⊗ (T ⟶[V] Y) ⟶ (X ⟶[V] T) ⊗ (T ⟶[V] Y) ⟶ (X ⟶[V] Y)` (`η ▷ _` then `eComp`), is an isomorphism;
- `EnrichedCategory.HasCotensors V D` (with right adjoints to every `tensorRight v`): for all `v` and `X` there are `P : D` and `ε : v ⟶ (P ⟶[V] X)` such that for every Y the map out of `(Y ⟶[V] P)` adjoint to `(Y ⟶[V] P) ⊗ v ⟶ (Y ⟶[V] P) ⊗ (P ⟶[V] X) ⟶ (Y ⟶[V] X)` is an isomorphism;
- A.1.4.5 for `MonoidalClosed.enrichedCategorySelf`: `HasTensors V V`, and `HasCotensors V V` given right adjoints to every `tensorRight v`. Lurie defines cotensors only on the closed side, so his converse is read through ordinary representability: if every `Y ↦ (Y ⊗ v ⟶ X)` is representable, every `tensorRight v` has a right adjoint.

Lurie's statement is for his orientation (a right-closed C); in Mathlib's orientation the hypothesis is `MonoidalClosed V` (see *Orientation of enrichment* above).

**Checks.** `SSet` is enriched, tensored and cotensored over itself (it is symmetric monoidal closed, Mathlib `FunctorToTypes.monoidalClosed`), with tensors `K × X` and cotensors `Fun(K, X)`.

*Needs:* A.1.3.4; Mathlib `MonoidalClosed.enrichedCategorySelf`, `EnrichedCategory`.

### F1.3 Trees of pushouts

The section's goal is Proposition A.1.5.12: in a κ-accessible presentable category with κ uncountable, a weakly saturated class generated by its morphisms between κ-compact objects consists of transfinite compositions of pushouts of those morphisms, with no retracts needed. Corollary A.1.5.13 packages the result as a κ-good tree. Its only uses are Lemma A.2.6.9 (F1.6) and Lemma A.3.3.3 (F3). Throughout, "κ-accessible" is Mathlib's `IsCardinalAccessibleCategory C κ`, not the ∞-categorical Definition 5.4.2.1 that Lurie cites in A.1.5.10. The lemmas are formalized in Lurie's order with Lurie's proofs; the idempotent-splitting arguments of A.1.5.8–A.1.5.9 are where the uncountability of κ enters (a countable union of κ-small sets is κ-small).

**S-trees** (`MorphismProperty.Tree`; HTT Definition A.1.5.1, PDF p. 817). For a class S of morphisms in a presentable category C, an S-tree with root X consists of a well-founded partial order A, a functor `α ↦ Y_α` from A to `Under X`, and for each α a pushout square exhibiting `colim_{β<α} Y_β ⟶ Y_α` as a pushout of a member `C ⟶ D` of S. For a regular κ, the tree is *κ-good* when every such C and D is κ-compact and every `{β | β < α}` is κ-small.

*Lean:* propose `structure MorphismProperty.Tree (S : MorphismProperty C) (X : C)` with an index type `A : Type w`, `[PartialOrder A] [WellFoundedLT A]`, `Y : A ⥤ Under X`, and for each `a : A` a morphism `f_a` with `S f_a` and an `IsPushout` square with `f_a` on top and the map from the colimit of `Y` over `Set.Iio a` to `Y.obj a` at the bottom. `Tree.IsGood κ` asks `IsCardinalPresentable` of the source and target of every `f_a` and `HasCardinalLT (Set.Iio a) κ`. The colimits are taken in `Under X`; C has small colimits. The `IsPushout` square lives in C: its left map is `f_a`, and its right map is the image under `Under.forget X` of the map `colimit (Y restricted to Set.Iio a) ⟶ Y.obj a` of `Under X`.

*Needs:* A.1.1.1, A.1.1.2.

**Colimits over downward-closed subsets** (HTT Notation A.1.5.2, PDF p. 818). For a downward-closed `B ⊆ A`, the restriction to B is an S-tree, and `Y_B` denotes its colimit in `Under X`; `Y_∅ ≅ X` and `Y_{≤β} ≅ Y_β`. *Lean:* `Tree.objOfLowerSet (B : LowerSet A) : Under X` with these two isomorphisms (propose).

*Needs:* A.1.5.1.

**Change of root** (HTT Remark A.1.5.3, PDF p. 818). Pushing an S-tree with root X out along `X ⟶ X'` gives an S-tree with root X' and values `Y_α ⊔_X X'`.

*Needs:* A.1.5.1.

**Restriction to a complement** (HTT Remark A.1.5.5, PDF p. 818). For an S-tree on A and a downward-closed B, the objects `Y_{B ∪ {β ≤ α}}` for `α ∉ B` form an S-tree on `A \ B` with root `Y_B`.

*Needs:* A.1.5.1, A.1.5.2.

**Tree inclusions are saturated** (HTT Lemma A.1.5.6, PDF p. 818). For downward-closed `A'' ⊆ A' ⊆ A`, the map `Y_{A''} ⟶ Y_{A'}` lies in `weakSaturation S`; in particular so does `X ⟶ Y_A`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: reduce to `A'' = ∅`, `A' = A` with A.1.5.3 and A.1.5.5, and exhaust A by a transfinite sequence of downward-closed subsets adding one minimal element at a time.

*Needs:* A.1.5.3, A.1.5.5; A.1.2.2.

**Making a tree κ-good** (HTT Lemma A.1.5.7, PDF p. 819). If every source and target of S is κ-compact, an S-tree on `(A, ≤)` with root X admits a coarser partial order `≼` on A (α ≼ β implies α ≤ β), a κ-good S-tree `Y'` on `(A, ≼)` with the same root, and compatible maps `Y'_α ⟶ Y_α` inducing isomorphisms `Y'_B ≅ Y_B` for every `≤`-downward-closed B.

*Needs:* A.1.5.1, A.1.5.2; A.1.1.1.

**Idempotents descend to small subtrees** (HTT Lemma A.1.5.8, PDF p. 820). Let κ be uncountable and regular, `{Y_α}` a κ-good S-tree with root X, and `T_A` an idempotent of `Y_A` in `Under X`. Every κ-small `B₀ ⊆ A` lies in a κ-small downward-closed B carrying an idempotent `T_B` of `Y_B` compatible with `T_A` along `Y_B ⟶ Y_A`.

*Needs:* A.1.5.1, A.1.5.2; A.1.1.1.

**Compatible idempotents on two subtrees** (HTT Lemma A.1.5.9, PDF p. 821). With κ as above, a κ-good tree, a downward-closed B, and idempotents `T_A`, `T_B` compatible along `Y_B ⟶ Y_A`: every κ-small `C₀` lies in a κ-small downward-closed C carrying idempotents `T_C` of `Y_C` and `T_{B∩C}` of `Y_{B∩C}`, compatible with `T_A` and `T_B` along the evident maps.

*Needs:* A.1.5.8.

**Retracts of pushouts** (HTT Lemma A.1.5.10, PDF p. 823). Let C be presentable and `IsCardinalAccessibleCategory C κ`, `f : C ⟶ D` a map between κ-compact objects, g a pushout of f, and g' a retract of g in `Arrow C`. Then g' is a pushout of some `f' : C' ⟶ D'` between κ-compact objects with `f' ∈ weakSaturation {f}`.

*Needs:* A.1.1.1, A.1.1.2, A.1.2.2, A.1.2.4; Mathlib `IsCardinalAccessibleCategory`.

**Small trees come from compact roots** (HTT Lemma A.1.5.11, PDF p. 824). Let `IsCardinalAccessibleCategory C κ`, let every source of S be κ-compact, and let `{Y_α}` be an S-tree with root X on a κ-small A. There are a map `X' ⟶ X` with X' κ-compact and an S-tree `{Y'_α}` with root X' whose pushout along `X' ⟶ X` (A.1.5.3) is isomorphic to `{Y_α}`.

*Needs:* A.1.5.1, A.1.5.3; A.1.1.1, A.1.1.2.

**Saturation without retracts** (HTT Proposition A.1.5.12, PDF p. 826). Let C be presentable, κ an uncountable regular cardinal with `IsCardinalAccessibleCategory C κ`, S̄ a weakly saturated class, and S ⊆ S̄ its members between κ-compact objects; assume `weakSaturation S = S̄`. Then every `f : X ⟶ Y` in S̄ is a transfinite composition of pushouts of members of S: there is a transfinite sequence `Z_γ` in `Under X` with each `colim_{γ'<γ} Z_{γ'} ⟶ Z_γ` a pushout of a member of S and `colim_γ Z_γ ≅ Y` in `Under X`.

*Lean:* `S̄ ≤ (S.pushouts).transfiniteCompositions.{w}` in Mathlib's vocabulary, with the stronger form under X stated as above.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: A.1.2.8 gives a sequence whose colimit retracts onto Y; make the tree κ-good (A.1.5.7); push the idempotent down to small subtrees (A.1.5.8–A.1.5.9) and replace each retract of a pushout by a pushout (A.1.5.10–A.1.5.11).

**Checks.** For `C = Type u`, κ = ℵ₁ and S̄ the injections, every injection is a transfinite composition of pushouts of injections between countable sets (indeed of `∅ ⟶ PUnit`).

*Needs:* A.1.2.8, A.1.5.2, A.1.5.5, A.1.5.7, A.1.5.9, A.1.5.10, A.1.5.11.

**κ-good trees for saturated maps** (HTT Corollary A.1.5.13, PDF p. 827). Under the hypotheses of A.1.5.12, every f in S̄ is `X ⟶ Y_A` for a κ-good S-tree `{Y_α}` with root X (`Y_A ≅ Y` in `Under X`).

*Needs:* A.1.5.7, A.1.5.12.

### F1.4 Model categories and their homotopy categories

**Model categories** (HTT Definition A.2.1.1, PDF p. 828). Lurie's model categories have all small limits and colimits; Mathlib's `HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory` (Goerss–Jardine) asks for finite ones. The other axioms agree: two-out-of-three, retract stability of the three classes, the two lifting axioms and the two (non-functorial) factorizations.

*Lean:* no new definition. A model category in Lurie's sense is `[ModelCategory C] [HasLimits C] [HasColimits C]`. Trivial (co)fibrations and (co)fibrant objects are Mathlib's (`trivialCofibrations`, `trivialFibrations`, `IsCofibrant`, `IsFibrant`).

**Checks.** Any complete and cocomplete category carries the trivial model structure (HTT Example A.2.1.2: isomorphisms, all maps, all maps), as a `ModelCategory` on the type synonym `HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory.Trivial C` (propose), with the bridge `Trivial.equivalence : C ≌ Trivial C` and the transport lemmas `Trivial.weakEquivalences_eq` (`isomorphisms C`), `Trivial.cofibrations_eq` and `Trivial.fibrations_eq` (both `⊤`); the Kan–Quillen structure on `SSet` (F2) is a model category in Lurie's sense, `SSet` being complete and cocomplete.

*Needs:* Mathlib `HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory`.

**Left and right homotopy agree** (HTT Proposition A.2.2.1, PDF p. 829). For X cofibrant and Y fibrant and `f g : X ⟶ Y`, the following are equivalent: a left homotopy through every cylinder object; through some cylinder object; a right homotopy through every path object; through some path object. Lurie's cylinder objects (the map from `X ⊔ X` a cofibration, the map to X a weak equivalence) are Mathlib's `Cylinder X` with `IsGood`; his path objects are `PathObject Y` with `IsGood`. Supplied by Mathlib: `HomotopicalAlgebra.leftHomotopyRel_iff_rightHomotopyRel`, `LeftHomotopyRel.leftHomotopy` (a homotopy through any good cylinder) and `RightHomotopyRel.rightHomotopy`.

*Needs:* A.2.1.1.

**The homotopy category** (`HTT.A.2.2/homotopy-category`; HTT §A.2.2 after Proposition A.2.2.1, PDF p. 830). The bifibrant objects modulo homotopy form a category hC, and the evident functor from hC to the localization of C at the weak equivalences is an equivalence; in particular the localization is locally small (HTT Remark A.2.2.2). Supplied by Mathlib: `HomotopicalAlgebra.BifibrantObject.HoCat C` (the quotient by `BifibrantObject.homRel`, a congruence), `BifibrantObject.toHoCat` as a localization of the bifibrant objects at the weak equivalences, the instance making `BifibrantObject.ι ⋙ L` a localization functor for any localization `L` of C, and `LocallySmall` for `HoCat C`. The equivalence `HoCat C ≌ (weakEquivalences C).Localization` follows from the uniqueness of localizations.

*Needs:* A.2.2.1; Mathlib `HomotopicalAlgebra.BifibrantObject.HoCat`, `CategoryTheory.Localization`.

**Homotopy extension** (HTT Proposition A.2.3.1, PDF p. 830). Let A, B be cofibrant and X fibrant, `i : A ⟶ B` a cofibration and `f : A ⟶ X`. If a map `g : B ⟶ X` in the homotopy category satisfies `g ∘ [i] = [f]`, then g is represented by a map `g' : B ⟶ X` of C with `g' ∘ i = f`.

*Lean:* for a localization `L : C ⥤ D` at `weakEquivalences C`, `[IsCofibrant A] [IsCofibrant B] [IsFibrant X] [Cofibration i]`, `g : L.obj B ⟶ L.obj X` with `L.map i ≫ g = L.map f`: `∃ g' : B ⟶ X, i ≫ g' = f ∧ L.map g' = g` (propose `HomotopicalAlgebra.exists_extension_of_cofibration`).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: represent g (Mathlib `map_surjective_of_isLocalization`), choose a good cylinder for A, factor the induced map into `B ⊔ B` to obtain a good cylinder for B, and extend the homotopy along the trivial cofibration from the pushout of the cylinder of A with B.

*Needs:* A.2.1.1, `HTT.A.2.2/homotopy-category`; Mathlib `Cylinder`, `LeftHomotopyRel.iff_map_eq`, `map_surjective_of_isLocalization`.

### F1.5 Left properness, homotopy pushouts, Quillen adjunctions

**Left and right proper model categories** (`HomotopicalAlgebra.IsLeftProper`, `HomotopicalAlgebra.IsRightProper`; HTT Definition A.2.4.1, PDF p. 832). A model category is left proper when, in every pushout square whose top map `i : A ⟶ B` is a cofibration and whose left map `j : A ⟶ A'` is a weak equivalence, the opposite map `j' : B ⟶ B'` is a weak equivalence; right proper is the dual for pullbacks along fibrations.

*Lean:* propose `class HomotopicalAlgebra.IsLeftProper (C) [ModelCategory C] : Prop` with field `∀ {A B A' B'} {i : A ⟶ B} {j : A ⟶ A'} {j' : B ⟶ B'} {i' : A' ⟶ B'}, IsPushout i j j' i' → [Cofibration i] → [WeakEquivalence j] → WeakEquivalence j'`, and `IsRightProper` with `IsPullback`, a fibration and a weak equivalence pulled back.

**Checks.** The trivial model structure is left and right proper.

*Needs:* A.2.1.1.

**Pushing weak equivalences between cofibrant objects** (HTT Lemma A.2.4.3, PDF p. 832). In a pushout square as above with A and A' cofibrant, i a cofibration and j a weak equivalence, j' is a weak equivalence.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: j' is an isomorphism in the homotopy category because it induces bijections on homotopy classes into every fibrant object; surjectivity through A.2.3.1, injectivity by the same argument in `Over (Z ⨯ Z)` applied to a path object.

*Needs:* A.2.1.1, A.2.3.1.

**All objects cofibrant implies left proper** (HTT Proposition A.2.4.2, PDF p. 832). A model category in which every object is cofibrant is left proper: A.2.4.3 applies to every pushout square.

*Needs:* A.2.4.1, A.2.4.3.

**Homotopy pushout squares** (`HTT.A.2.4.3/after`, `HomotopicalAlgebra.IsHomotopyPushout`; HTT §A.2.4 after Lemma A.2.4.3, PDF p. 833). A cofibrant resolution of a span `A₀ ⟵ A ⟶ A₁` is a span `A'₀ ⟵ A' ⟶ A'₁` with A' cofibrant and both maps cofibrations, with a map of spans to the given one that is a weak equivalence at each of the three objects. A commutative square with corner M under the span is a homotopy pushout square when, for some cofibrant resolution, the composite `A'₀ ⊔_{A'} A'₁ ⟶ A₀ ⊔_A A₁ ⟶ M` is a weak equivalence. Homotopy pullback squares are defined dually (HTT Remark A.2.4.5).

*Lean:* propose `HomotopicalAlgebra.IsHomotopyPushout (sq : CommSq t l r b) : Prop`, the existence of a cofibrant resolution of the span `(t, l)` for which the induced map from its pushout to the corner is a `WeakEquivalence`; dually `IsHomotopyPullback`. Provide with the definition: cofibrant resolutions exist (factorization), and the condition does not depend on the resolution, so "for some" and "for every" agree.

*Proof route.* Independence is the cube lemma (Hovey, *Model Categories*, §5.2): the pushout of a weak equivalence between spans of cofibrant objects with one leg a cofibration is a weak equivalence. It follows from A.2.4.3 and Ken Brown's factorization.

**Checks.** If A is cofibrant and both legs of the span are cofibrations, the span is its own cofibrant resolution and its pushout square is a homotopy pushout square; in the trivial model structure, homotopy pushout squares are the pushout squares.

*Needs:* A.2.1.1, A.2.4.3; Mathlib `CofibrantBrownFactorization`.

**Pushouts along cofibrations are homotopy pushouts** (HTT Proposition A.2.4.4, PDF p. 834). A pushout square on a span `A₀ ⟵ A ⟶ A₁` whose leg `j : A ⟶ A₁` is a cofibration is a homotopy pushout square if either A and A₀ are cofibrant, or C is left proper. Dually for pullbacks along fibrations, with fibrant objects or right properness (Remark A.2.4.5).

*Proof route.* Lurie omits the proof. Case (i) is the cube lemma above; case (ii) compares with a cofibrant resolution and applies left properness twice (Hirschhorn, *Model Categories and Their Localizations*, ch. 13).

*Needs:* A.2.4.1, `HTT.A.2.4.3/after`; A.2.4.3.

**Quillen adjunctions, derived functors** (`HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions`, `Adjunction.IsQuillen`; HTT §A.2.5 before Proposition A.2.5.1, PDF p. 835). For model categories C, D and an adjunction `adj : F ⊣ G` with `F : C ⥤ D`, the following are equivalent: F preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations; G preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations; F preserves cofibrations and G preserves fibrations; F preserves trivial cofibrations and G preserves trivial fibrations. A Quillen adjunction is one satisfying them. Then F preserves weak equivalences between cofibrant objects and G those between fibrant objects, and the total derived functors `LF`, `RG` between the homotopy categories exist and are adjoint.

*Lean:*

- `CategoryTheory.Adjunction.IsQuillen (adj : F ⊣ G) : Prop := cofibrations C ≤ (cofibrations D).inverseImage F ∧ trivialCofibrations C ≤ (trivialCofibrations D).inverseImage F` (propose), with the four conditions as a `List.TFAE`;
- `LF` is the total left derived functor of `F ⋙ (weakEquivalences D).Q` along `(weakEquivalences C).Q` (Mathlib `Functor.totalLeftDerived`), which exists because `HomotopicalAlgebra.CofibrantObject.localizerMorphism C` is a left derivability structure and `F ⋙ Q` inverts weak equivalences between cofibrant objects (`LocalizerMorphism.Derives.hasPointwiseLeftDerivedFunctor`); dually `RG`;
- the adjunction `LF ⊣ RG` through Mathlib's `Adjunction.derived`, after checking its absoluteness hypotheses for these pointwise derived functors.

**Checks.** The identity adjunction is Quillen. Between trivial model structures every adjunction is Quillen, with `LF = F` and `RG = G`.

*Proof route.* The TFAE is formal from the lifting characterizations (Mathlib's weak factorization systems in a model category) and adjunction of lifting problems. Preservation of weak equivalences between cofibrant objects is Ken Brown's lemma, from Mathlib's `CofibrantBrownFactorization` (Hovey, *Model Categories*, Lemma 1.1.12).

*Needs:* A.2.1.1, `HTT.A.2.2/homotopy-category`; Mathlib `CofibrantBrownFactorization`, `HomotopicalAlgebra.CofibrantObject.localizerMorphism` and its `IsLeftDerivabilityStructure` instance (with the fibrant dual), `LocalizerMorphism.Derives`, `Adjunction.derived`.

**Quillen equivalences** (`Adjunction.IsQuillenEquivalence`; HTT Proposition A.2.5.1, PDF p. 835). For a Quillen adjunction the following are equivalent: `LF` is an equivalence; `RG` is an equivalence; for every cofibrant X of C and fibrant Y of D, a map `X ⟶ G Y` is a weak equivalence exactly when its adjoint `F X ⟶ Y` is. A Quillen equivalence is a Quillen adjunction satisfying them.

*Lean:* `Adjunction.IsQuillenEquivalence adj : Prop := adj.IsQuillen ∧ ∀ X Y, IsCofibrant X → IsFibrant Y → ∀ f : X ⟶ G.obj Y, WeakEquivalence f ↔ WeakEquivalence ((adj.homEquiv X Y).symm f)` (propose; Mathlib has no Quillen equivalence predicate), the third condition, which needs no choice of localization; the target is the `List.TFAE` of the three conditions, with `LF` and `RG` as above for the canonical localizations `(weakEquivalences _).Localization`.

**Checks.** The identity is a Quillen equivalence; between trivial model structures, a Quillen equivalence is an adjoint equivalence of categories.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: (1) ⇔ (2) because `LF ⊣ RG`; both say that unit and counit are isomorphisms, which unwinds to (3) on cofibrant and fibrant objects.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions`, `HTT.A.2.2/homotopy-category`.

### F1.6 Combinatorial model categories

**Combinatorial model categories** (`HomotopicalAlgebra.IsCombinatorial`; HTT Definition A.2.6.1, PDF p. 836). A model category is combinatorial (Smith) when it is presentable and there are small sets I and J with `cofibrations = weakSaturation I` and `trivialCofibrations = weakSaturation J`.

*Lean:* propose `class HomotopicalAlgebra.IsCombinatorial.{w} (C) [ModelCategory C] : Prop` with `IsLocallyPresentable.{w} C` and `∃ I : MorphismProperty C, I.IsSmall.{w} ∧ cofibrations C = I.weakSaturation.{w}`, and the same for `trivialCofibrations C`. By A.1.2.7 these are `I.rlp.llp` and `J.rlp.llp`, and then `fibrations C = J.rlp`, `trivialFibrations C = I.rlp`.

**Checks.** The trivial model structure on a presentable category is combinatorial, with `I` the maps `∅ ⟶ G` and `G ⊔ G ⟶ G` for G in a small generating set and `J = ∅` (A.2.6.13 with A.2.6.15). The Kan–Quillen structure is combinatorial (F2).

*Needs:* A.1.1.2, A.1.2.2, A.1.2.7; A.2.1.1.

**Accessible subcategories** (`ObjectProperty.IsCardinalAccessibleSubcategory`, `ObjectProperty.IsAccessibleSubcategory`; HTT Definition A.2.6.2, PDF pp. 836–837). For C presentable and κ regular, a full subcategory C₀ is κ-accessible when it is stable under κ-filtered colimits (taken in C) and a small set of its objects generates it under κ-filtered colimits; it is accessible when it is κ-accessible for some κ.

*Lean:* propose, for `P : ObjectProperty C`, `P.IsCardinalAccessibleSubcategory κ` := (`∀ (J : Type w) [SmallCategory J] [IsCardinalFiltered J κ], P.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape J`) ∧ (`∃ Q ≤ P, ObjectProperty.Small.{w} Q ∧ ∀ X, P X → ∃ (J : Type w) (_ : SmallCategory J) (_ : IsCardinalFiltered J κ), Q.colimitsOfShape J X`), and `P.IsAccessibleSubcategory := ∃ κ (_ : Fact κ.IsRegular), P.IsCardinalAccessibleSubcategory κ`. Lurie indexes by κ-filtered posets; the two agree by A.1.1.1. For a class of morphisms W, "W is accessible" means the full subcategory of `Arrow C` it spans.

**Checks.** The surjections form an ℵ₀-accessible subcategory of `Arrow (Type u)` (used in A.2.6.8). A κ-accessible subcategory is closed under retracts (a retract is a κ-filtered colimit of the idempotent indexed by `κ.ord.ToType`).

*Needs:* A.1.1.1, A.1.1.2.

**Sharply larger cardinals** (`Cardinal.PowLT`; HTT Definition A.2.6.3, PDF p. 837). For regular κ and τ, κ ≪ τ when `τ' ^ κ' < τ` for all `τ' < τ` and `κ' < κ`.

*Lean:* propose `Cardinal.PowLT (κ τ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop := ∀ τ' < τ, ∀ κ' < κ, τ' ^ κ' < τ`. This is not Mathlib's `Cardinal.SharplyLT` (Adámek–Rosický's "sharply less than", which is irreflexive): Mathlib's `Cardinal.SharplyLT.of_pow_lt` proves `κ < τ → PowLT κ τ → SharplyLT κ τ`. Provide that every regular τ₀ is exceeded by a regular τ with `PowLT κ τ` (the successor of `τ₀ ^ κ`). The definition has no regularity hypothesis, though Lurie's has; every statement using `PowLT κ τ` assumes `κ.IsRegular` and `τ.IsRegular`, as HTT does.

**Checks.** `PowLT ℵ₀ κ` for every regular κ; for uncountable regular κ, `PowLT κ κ` holds exactly when κ is strongly inaccessible (HTT Remark A.2.6.4).

*Needs:* Mathlib `Cardinal.IsRegular`, `Cardinal.SharplyLT.of_pow_lt`.

**Matching colimit presentations** (HTT Lemma A.2.6.6, PDF p. 837). Let κ ≪ τ with τ > κ regular, D presentable, and `{C_a}_{a ∈ A}`, `{D_b}_{b ∈ B}` diagrams of τ-compact objects indexed by τ-filtered posets with isomorphic colimits. For τ-small `A₀ ⊆ A` and `B₀ ⊆ B` there are τ-small κ-filtered `A' ⊇ A₀` and `B' ⊇ B₀` whose colimits are isomorphic.

*Proof route.* Not Lurie's, who deduces it from the ∞-categorical Lemma 5.4.6.3. The classical argument (Adámek–Rosický, *Locally presentable and accessible categories*, chapter 2): a back-and-forth chain of length κ, alternately enlarging the subsets on each side by τ-compactness of τ-small κ-filtered colimits of τ-compact objects and by `Cardinal.SharplyLT` (every τ-small subset of a κ-directed poset lies in a τ-small κ-directed one; Mathlib's `Cardinal.SharplyLT` API); unions along a chain of length κ stay κ-filtered by regularity and τ-small since κ < τ.

*Needs:* A.1.1.1, A.1.1.2, A.2.6.3; Mathlib `Cardinal.SharplyLT`.

**Accessibility through sharply larger cardinals** (HTT Proposition A.2.6.5, PDF p. 837). Let C be presentable and C₀ a full subcategory stable under κ-filtered colimits. C₀ is generated under κ-filtered colimits by a small set exactly when, for all sufficiently large regular τ with κ ≪ τ, the following holds (2'_τ): for every τ-filtered poset A and diagram `{X_α}` of τ-compact objects with colimit in C₀, every τ-small `C ⊆ A` lies in a τ-small κ-filtered `B ⊆ A` with `colim_{α ∈ B} X_α` in C₀.

*Needs:* A.2.6.2, A.2.6.3, A.2.6.6.

**Preimages of accessible subcategories** (HTT Corollary A.2.6.7, PDF p. 838). For a functor `f : C ⥤ D` between presentable categories preserving κ-filtered colimits and a κ-accessible `D₀ ⊆ D`, the preimage `f⁻¹ D₀` is a κ-accessible subcategory of C.

*Proof route.* Lurie gives no proof. Stability under κ-filtered colimits is immediate. For generation, use A.2.6.5: for arbitrarily large τ with κ ≪ τ, f preserves τ-compact objects (uniformization; Mathlib `IsCardinalAccessibleCategory.uniformization` proves a form of it), so (2'_τ) for D₀ gives (2'_τ) for `f⁻¹ D₀`.

*Needs:* A.2.6.2, A.2.6.5; Mathlib `IsCardinalAccessibleCategory.uniformization`, `Functor.PreservesCardinalPresentable`.

**Intersections of accessible subcategories** (`HTT.A.2.6/accessible-intersections`). The intersection of a small family of accessible subcategories of a presentable category is accessible. This is the 1-categorical case of HTT Proposition 5.4.7.10, which Lurie cites in the proof of A.2.6.8.

*Lean:* for `ι : Type w` and `P : ι → ObjectProperty C` with each `(P i).IsAccessibleSubcategory`, `(⨅ i, P i).IsAccessibleSubcategory`.

*Proof route.* Through A.2.6.5. Choose a regular κ for which every member is κ-accessible and which exceeds the cardinality of the family (raising the indices to a common sharply larger cardinal, Mathlib `Cardinal.SharplyLT.exists_of_small`), and τ ≫ κ for which every member satisfies (2'_τ). For (2'_τ) of the intersection, build a chain of τ-small κ-filtered subsets of length κ that visits every member cofinally often; its union is κ-filtered (κ regular) and τ-small (κ < τ), and its colimit lies in every member, being a κ-filtered colimit of objects of that member. Classical references: Makkai–Paré, *Accessible categories*; Adámek–Rosický, chapter 2.

*Needs:* A.2.6.2, A.2.6.3, A.2.6.5, A.2.6.6.

**Fibrations and weak equivalences are accessible** (HTT Corollary A.2.6.8, PDF p. 838). In a combinatorial model category, the fibrations, the weak equivalences and the trivial fibrations span accessible subcategories of `Arrow C`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: for each generating map `i : A ⟶ B` the functor `Arrow C ⥤ Arrow (Type _)` sending f to the map from `Hom(B, X)` to the set of squares from i to f preserves κ-filtered colimits; the preimage of the surjections is accessible (A.2.6.7); fibrations and trivial fibrations are intersections over J and I (`HTT.A.2.6/accessible-intersections`); the weak equivalences are the preimage of the trivial fibrations under the second factor of the small object argument for J, which preserves κ-filtered colimits for large κ (A.1.2.5 (2)).

*Needs:* A.2.6.1, A.2.6.2, A.2.6.7, `HTT.A.2.6/accessible-intersections`; A.1.2.5.

**Generating trivial cofibrations** (HTT Lemma A.2.6.9, PDF p. 839). Let A be presentable and C, W classes of morphisms with: C weakly saturated and generated by a small subset; `C ⊓ W` weakly saturated; W accessible (A.2.6.2); W with two-out-of-three. Then `C ⊓ W` is generated, as a weakly saturated class, by a small subset.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.A.2.6.9/good` (good subsets of a tree), `HTT.A.2.6.9/exhaust` (exhausting a tree by good subsets) and `HTT.A.2.6.9/step` (each stage is generated by small trivial cofibrations), and this entry's own target `HTT.A.2.6.9`, which writes a map of `C ⊓ W` as a τ-good tree (A.1.5.13) and assembles the parts.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: take τ with W satisfying (2'_τ), A τ-accessible and C generated by its maps between τ-compact objects, and S the members of `C ⊓ W` between τ-compact objects; write a map of `C ⊓ W` as a τ-good tree (A.1.5.13) and exhaust it by "good" downward-closed subsets (`HTT.A.2.6.9/good`, `HTT.A.2.6.9/exhaust`), each stage of the exhaustion lying in the class generated by S (`HTT.A.2.6.9/step`).

*Needs:* `HTT.A.2.6.9/good`, `HTT.A.2.6.9/exhaust`, `HTT.A.2.6.9/step` (below); A.1.5.13.

**Good subsets of a tree** (`HTT.A.2.6.9/good`, part 1 of 3 of generating trivial cofibrations above; in the proof of HTT Lemma A.2.6.9, PDF p. 840). Under the hypotheses of A.2.6.9, with τ chosen as in its proof, `C₀` enlarged (as in Lurie's proof) to all members of C between τ-compact objects, and `{Y_α}_{α ∈ A}` a τ-good `C₀`-tree with root X, call a downward-closed `B ⊆ A` good when `X ⟶ Y_B` lies in W. Then:

- the union of an increasing family of good subsets is good;
- every τ-small subset of a good B lies in a τ-small good subset of B;
- if B, B′ and B ∩ B′ are good, so is B ∪ B′.

*Proof route.* The first by weak saturation of `C ⊓ W`; the second by condition (2′_τ) of A.2.6.5; the third through the pushout square of `Y_{B∩B′}`, `Y_B`, `Y_{B′}` and `Y_{B∪B′}` (A.1.5.6) and two-out-of-three.

*Needs:* A.2.6.2, A.2.6.5; HTT A.1.5.2, A.1.5.6 (F1.3); A.1.2.2 (F1.1).

**Exhausting a tree by good subsets** (`HTT.A.2.6.9/exhaust`, part 2 of 3 of generating trivial cofibrations above; in the proof of HTT Lemma A.2.6.9, PDF pp. 840–841). In the setting of `HTT.A.2.6.9/good`, with A good:

- for a good `A′` and a τ-small `B₀`, there is a τ-small good `B ⊇ B₀` with `B ∩ A′` good;
- hence there is a transfinite sequence of good subsets `A(γ)`, continuous at limits, with union A, each difference `A(γ) \ ⋃_{γ′<γ} A(γ′)` τ-small.

*Proof route.* For the first, an alternating countable chain built with the second property of `/good`; for the second, a transfinite recursion that adds a minimal element not yet covered.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.2.6.9/good`.

**Each stage is generated by small trivial cofibrations** (`HTT.A.2.6.9/step`, part 3 of 3 of generating trivial cofibrations above; in the proof of HTT Lemma A.2.6.9, PDF p. 841). For good downward-closed `A′ ⊆ A″` with `A″ \ A′` τ-small, the map `Y_{A′} ⟶ Y_{A″}` lies in the weakly saturated class generated by the members of `C ⊓ W` between τ-compact objects.

*Proof route.* By A.1.5.5 the difference is a τ-small tree rooted at `Y_{A′}`, so by A.1.5.11 the map is a pushout of a member `M ⟶ N` of `C₀`. Write `Y_{A′}` as a τ-filtered colimit of τ-compact objects through which M factors, and use (2′_τ) to find a τ-small κ-filtered subfamily whose pushouts lie in W.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.2.6.9/good`; A.2.6.5; HTT A.1.5.5, A.1.5.11 (F1.3); A.1.1.1 (F1.1).

**Smith's recognition theorem** (`HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory.ofSmith`; HTT Proposition A.2.6.10, PDF p. 841). Let A be presentable with classes C and W such that: (1) C is weakly saturated and generated by a small subset; (2) `C ⊓ W` is weakly saturated; (3) W is accessible; (4) W has two-out-of-three; (5) `C.rlp ≤ W`. Then A has a combinatorial model structure with cofibrations C, weak equivalences W, and fibrations `(C ⊓ W).rlp`.

*Lean:* propose `def HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory.ofSmith` producing, on the type synonym `HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory.WithClasses C W` of A (propose) carrying `CategoryWithCofibrations`, `CategoryWithWeakEquivalences` and `CategoryWithFibrations` given by C, W and `(C ⊓ W).rlp`, a `ModelCategory` instance, with a theorem that it is `IsCombinatorial`. The bridge is `WithClasses.equivalence C W : A ≌ WithClasses C W`, and the transport lemmas `WithClasses.cofibrations_eq`, `WithClasses.weakEquivalences_eq` and `WithClasses.fibrations_eq` (C, W and `(C ⊓ W).rlp`) are `rfl`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's for the factorizations and lifting: the small object argument for a generating set of C, and for the small generating set of `C ⊓ W` from A.2.6.9 (with A.1.2.7). Build the structure with Mathlib's `ModelCategory.mk'` from the two weak factorization systems `(C, C.rlp)` and `(C ⊓ W, (C ⊓ W).rlp)`, after proving `C.rlp = (C ⊓ W).rlp ⊓ W` as Lurie does; `mk'` derives the retract axiom for weak equivalences, so Lurie's appeal to Corollary 5.3.1.10 is not needed.

*Needs:* A.1.2.5, A.1.2.7, A.2.6.1, A.2.6.2, A.2.6.9; Mathlib `ModelCategory.mk'`, `MorphismProperty.IsWeakFactorizationSystem`.

**Recognizing combinatorial structures** (HTT Corollary A.2.6.11, PDF p. 843). For a model structure on a presentable category whose cofibrations are generated by a small set, being combinatorial is equivalent to the weak equivalences forming an accessible subcategory of `Arrow C`.

*Needs:* A.2.6.8, A.2.6.10.

**Perfect classes of weak equivalences** (`MorphismProperty.IsPerfect`; HTT Definition A.2.6.12, PDF p. 843). For A presentable, a class W of morphisms is perfect when it contains the isomorphisms, has two-out-of-three, is stable under filtered colimits (indexed by filtered posets), and some small `W₀ ⊆ W` has every member of W a filtered colimit, in `Arrow A`, of members of `W₀`.

*Lean:* propose `class MorphismProperty.IsPerfect.{w} (W : MorphismProperty A) : Prop` with `isomorphisms A ≤ W`, `W.HasTwoOutOfThreeProperty`, `W.IsStableUnderFilteredColimits.{w, w}`, and the generation condition for an `ObjectProperty.Small.{w}` set of arrows (`colimitsOfShape` over small filtered categories in `Arrow A`). Mathlib's stability under filtered colimits indexed by categories is equivalent to Lurie's poset-indexed form (A.1.1.1); with the last two conditions it says that W spans an ℵ₀-accessible subcategory of `Arrow A`.

**Checks.** The isomorphisms of a presentable category form a perfect class (HTT Example A.2.6.13).

*Needs:* A.1.1.2.

**Preimages of perfect classes** (HTT Corollary A.2.6.14, PDF p. 843). For a functor between presentable categories preserving filtered colimits, the preimage of a perfect class is perfect. *Proof route.* A.2.6.7 with κ = ℵ₀ applied to `Arrow` of the functor.

*Needs:* A.2.6.7, A.2.6.12.

**Smith's theorem in practice** (`HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory.ofPerfect`; HTT Proposition A.2.6.15, PDF p. 843). Let A be presentable, W a class of morphisms, and C₀ a small set of morphisms such that: (1) W is perfect; (2) in a vertical composite of two pushout squares whose top map is in C₀ and whose lower left vertical map is in W, the lower right vertical map is in W (weak equivalences are stable under pushout along pushouts of generating cofibrations); (3) `C₀.rlp ≤ W`. Then A has a left proper combinatorial model structure with cofibrations `weakSaturation C₀`, weak equivalences W, and fibrations the maps with the right lifting property against cofibrations in W.

*Lean:* propose `def HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory.ofPerfect` built from `ModelCategory.ofSmith`, on `WithClasses (weakSaturation C₀) W` with the same bridge and transport lemmas, and with theorems `IsCombinatorial` and `IsLeftProper`.

**Checks.** On `SSet` with `C₀` the boundary inclusions and W the isomorphisms, (1) and (2) hold and (3) fails; no model structure has these cofibrations and weak equivalences, since every map would factor as a monomorphism followed by an isomorphism.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the class of maps along which pushouts preserve W is weakly saturated (by stability of W under filtered colimits) and contains C₀, so W is stable under pushout along cofibrations; then `C ⊓ W` is weakly saturated, using the small object argument and (3), and A.2.6.10 applies.

*Needs:* A.1.2.2, A.1.2.4, A.1.2.5, A.2.4.1, A.2.6.1, A.2.6.10, A.2.6.12.

**Transferred model structures** (`HTT.A.2.6/transfer`; not an HTT statement). Let A be a combinatorial model category with generating sets I and J, B a presentable category, and `F : A ⇄ B : G` an adjunction with G preserving κ-filtered colimits for some regular κ. If G carries every relative `F(J)`-cell complex to a weak equivalence, then B has a combinatorial model structure with generating sets `F(I)` and `F(J)`, in which a map is a weak equivalence (fibration) exactly when G carries it to one. The hypothesis holds when B has a fibrant replacement functor and functorial path objects for its fibrant objects, both created by G (Quillen's path-object argument).

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.A.2.6/transfer/structure` (the transfer theorem) and `HTT.A.2.6/transfer/path-object` (the path-object criterion), and this entry's own target `HTT.A.2.6/transfer`, which combines them: the transferred structure exists when B has a fibrant replacement functor and functorial path objects created by G.

*Lean:* the type synonym `HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory.Transferred adj` of B for `adj : F ⊣ G`, with a `ModelCategory` instance under the hypotheses above, the bridge `Transferred.equivalence adj : B ≌ Transferred adj`, and the transport lemmas `Transferred.weakEquivalences_eq` (`(weakEquivalences A).inverseImage G`), `Transferred.fibrations_eq` (`(fibrations A).inverseImage G`) and `Transferred.cofibrations_eq` (the left lifting class of their intersection), with `IsCombinatorial`, are defined in the part `HTT.A.2.6/transfer/structure`. This target adds the instance under the path-object hypothesis.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.2.6/transfer/structure`, `HTT.A.2.6/transfer/path-object` (below).

**The transfer theorem** (`HTT.A.2.6/transfer/structure`, part 1 of 2 of transferred model structures above). Let A be combinatorial with generating sets I and J, B presentable, and `F ⊣ G` an adjunction with G preserving κ-filtered colimits. If G carries every relative `F(J)`-cell complex to a weak equivalence, then B has a combinatorial model structure with generating sets `F(I)` and `F(J)`, whose weak equivalences and fibrations are created by G. This part provides the synonym `Transferred adj`, its instance, bridge and transport lemmas.
