**Checks.** In `SSet` multiplication preserves homotopy colimits (products preserve colimits and weak equivalences). In `Cat_S` for an excellent Cartesian S it does: Theorem A.3.5.15 (HTT Example A.3.6.8).

*Needs:* HTT A.2.8.2 (F3.2); A.2.1.1 (F1.4), A.2.6.1 (F1.6); A.2.5.1, `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions` (F1.5) for A.3.6.7.

**Recognizing weak exponentials through mapping spaces** (HTT Lemma A.3.6.9, Proposition A.3.6.10, Remark A.3.6.11, PDF pp. 917–918).

- A class of simplicial sets containing `Δ[0]`, closed under weak homotopy equivalence, and closed under colimits of projectively cofibrant diagrams indexed by small posets, contains every simplicial set (A.3.6.9).
- In a combinatorial simplicial model category A with a standard diagram `Z × Y ⟵ P ⟶ X` and multiplication by Y preserving homotopy colimits, the diagram exhibits Z as a weak exponential exactly when, for all cofibrant W, W' and `W' ⟶ W × Y` exhibiting W' as a homotopy product, `Map(W, Z) ×_{Map(W', Z × Y)} Map(W', P) ⟶ Map(W', X)` is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes (A.3.6.10). In that situation `Map(W', P) ⟶ Map(W', Z × Y)` is a trivial Kan fibration, so the fibre product is a Kan complex homotopy equivalent to `Map(W, Z)` (A.3.6.11).

*Proof route.* A.3.6.9: the class is closed under coproducts and homotopy pushouts, so it contains every finite-dimensional simplicial set by skeletal induction, and every simplicial set as the colimit of its skeleta (a projectively cofibrant diagram on ℕ). A.3.6.10: from (i), test against `W ⊗ K` for all K, the class of K for which `W' ⊗ K ⟶ Y × (W ⊗ K)` is a homotopy product satisfying the hypotheses of A.3.6.9.

*Needs:* A.3.6.1, A.3.6.5; A.3.1.5 (F3.3); A.2.8.2, `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3.2); `HTT.A.2.4.3/after` (F1.5); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

**Homotopy limits over `{a ≥ b}`** (HTT Lemmas A.3.6.12, A.3.6.13 and A.3.6.14, PDF pp. 919–920). Let A be combinatorial.

- For an inclusion of posets `i : B₀ ⊆ B` with a retraction r satisfying `r(b) ≤ b`, `α : X ⟶ lim F` exhibits X as a homotopy limit of F exactly when it does so for `i^* F` (A.3.6.12).
- If C has a final object and every `X ⟶ F(C)` is a weak equivalence, then `X ⟶ lim F` exhibits X as a homotopy limit of F (A.3.6.13).
- For a poset A, `B = {(a, b) : a ≥ b} ⊆ Aᵒᵖ × A` with projection `π : B ⟶ Aᵒᵖ`, and `α : π^* G ⟶ F` whose components `G(a) ⟶ F(a, b)` are weak equivalences, α exhibits G as a homotopy right Kan extension of F (A.3.6.14).

*Needs:* `HTT.A.2.8.2/injective`, `HTT.A.2.8.7/after`, A.2.8.9 (F3.2); A.2.8.1 (F1.7); A.2.6.1 (F1.6).

**Weak exponentials turn homotopy colimits into homotopy limits** (HTT Proposition A.3.6.15, PDF p. 920). Let A be combinatorial and `A = A₀ ∪ {∞}` a poset with largest element ∞, `B = {(a, b) : a ≥ b}`. Given X, `Y : A ⟶ A`, `Z : Aᵒᵖ ⟶ A` and diagrams `Z(a) × Y(b) ⟵ P(a, b) ⟶ X` functorial in `(a, b) ∈ B`, such that each exhibits `P(a, b)` as a homotopy product, those with `a = b` exhibit `Z(a)` as a weak exponential of X by `Y(a)`, multiplication in A preserves homotopy colimits, and Y exhibits `Y(∞)` as a homotopy colimit of `Y|A₀`: then Z exhibits `Z(∞)` as a homotopy limit of `Z|A₀ᵒᵖ`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: replace A by a Quillen equivalent combinatorial simplicial model category (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-simplicial`, F3.9) using A.3.6.4 for the weak exponentials and A.3.6.7 for the hypothesis that multiplication preserves homotopy colimits; then test on mapping spaces from bifibrant objects (A.3.3.12) and compare through A.3.6.14.

*Needs:* A.3.6.4, A.3.6.5, A.3.6.7, A.3.6.14; A.3.3.12 (F3.5); A.3.1.5 (F3.3); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3.2); `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-simplicial` (F3.9).

**Localizations of chunks and homotopy limits of diagram categories** (HTT Proposition A.3.6.16, Lemma A.3.6.17, Corollary A.3.6.18, PDF pp. 921–923).

- For an excellent S, a combinatorial S-enriched A and a chunk U, with `U_f` the objects of U fibrant in A and W the weak equivalences in `U_f`, `U° ⟶ U_f[W⁻¹]` is a weak equivalence (A.3.6.17).
- For S excellent with the Cartesian product, A combinatorial S-enriched, `A = A₀ ∪ {∞}` with largest element ∞, a diagram `{C_a}` of small cofibrant S-enriched categories exhibiting `C_∞` as a homotopy colimit of `{C_a}_{a ∈ A₀}`, and a small chunk U that is a `C_a`-chunk for every a: with `U^{C_a}_f` the projectively fibrant diagrams and `W_a` their weak equivalences, `{U^{C_a}_f[W_a⁻¹]}` exhibits `U^{C_∞}_f[W_∞⁻¹]` as a homotopy limit of the diagram over `A₀` (A.3.6.16).
- The same for `A^{C_a}_f[W_a⁻¹]`, without the chunk and cofibrancy hypotheses (A.3.6.18), by writing A as a κ-filtered union of small chunks (A.3.4.15). L2.8 and L4 use A.3.6.17–A.3.6.18 for the straightening comparisons.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. A.3.6.17 through A.3.4.11 and A.3.5.14. A.3.6.16 by applying A.3.6.15 to the model category `Cat_S`, whose multiplication preserves homotopy colimits by A.3.5.15 (HTT Example A.3.6.8), with the weak exponentials supplied by A.3.4.14, A.3.5.14 and A.3.6.17.

*Needs:* A.3.6.15; A.3.4.11, A.3.4.14, A.3.4.15 (F3.6); A.3.5.14, A.3.5.15 (F3.7); A.3.2.16 (F3.4); `HTT.A.2.8.2/injective`, `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3.2); A.1.1.1 (F1.1).

### F3.9 Bousfield localization and Dugger's theorem

**Local objects, local equivalences, Bousfield localizations** (`HTT.A.3.7/intro`; HTT §A.3.7 opening, PDF pp. 923–924). Two model structures on one category are related by a (Bousfield) localization `A ⟶ A'` when they have the same cofibrations and every weak equivalence of A is one of A'; then every fibration of A' is a fibration of A. For a simplicial model category A, hA is enriched over H: `Map_{hA}(X, Y) = [Map_A(X, Y)]` for X cofibrant and Y fibrant. For a class S of morphisms of hA (or of A, through its image):

- an object Z is S-local when `Map_{hA}(Y, Z) ⟶ Map_{hA}(X, Z)` is an isomorphism in H for every `f : X ⟶ Y` in S;
- a morphism is an S-equivalence when it induces such isomorphisms for every S-local Z.

*Lean:*

- `HomotopicalAlgebra.IsBousfieldLocalization (M M' : ModelCategory A) : Prop`, with M and M' as terms, by `cofibrations` equal and `weakEquivalences ≤`;
- `HomotopicalAlgebra.SimplicialModelCategory.derivedMap X Z : SSet.H` (propose), `Map_A` of a cofibrant replacement of X and a fibrant replacement of Z, independent of the choices up to canonical isomorphism;
- `SimplicialModelCategory.derivedMap.mapLeft f Z : derivedMap Y Z ⟶ derivedMap X Z` (propose) for `f : X ⟶ Y`, the functoriality of `derivedMap` in the first variable;
- `SimplicialModelCategory.IsLocal (S : MorphismProperty A) (Z : A) : Prop` (every `derivedMap.mapLeft f Z` with `S f` an isomorphism) and `SimplicialModelCategory.localEquivalences S : MorphismProperty A`, stated for S a class of morphisms of A; Lurie's S in hA is covered because every morphism of hA is isomorphic to the class of a morphism between bifibrant objects, and the conditions depend only on classes in hA (a lemma).

Mathlib's `MorphismProperty.isLocal` and `ObjectProperty.isLocal` (1-categorical orthogonality, `ObjectProperty/Local.lean`, `Localization/Bousfield.lean`) is a different, weaker notion when applied to hA, and is not used for it.

**Checks.**

- For S empty, every object is local and the S-equivalences are the weak equivalences.
- In `SSet`, for `S = {∅ ⟶ Δ[0]}`, the S-local Kan complexes are the contractible ones and every map is an S-equivalence.

*Needs:* A.3.1.5 (F3.3); `SSet.H` (F2.4); HTT A.1.1.2 (F1.1), A.2.1.1 (F1.4).

**Detecting local equivalences** (HTT Lemma A.3.7.1 and Corollary A.3.7.2, PDF pp. 924–926). Let A be a left proper simplicial model category and S a class of morphisms of hA. A cofibration `i : A ⟶ B` is an S-equivalence exactly when `Map_A(B, X) ⟶ Map_A(A, X)` is a trivial Kan fibration for every fibrant S-local X (A.3.7.1). For a simplicial adjunction `F : A ⇄ B : G` of simplicial model categories with B left proper, `(F, G)` is a Quillen adjunction exactly when F preserves cofibrations and G preserves fibrant objects (A.3.7.2).

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7/intro`; A.3.1.5 (F3.3); HTT A.2.4.1, `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions` (F1.5); `HTT.A.2.7/kan-fibrations`.

**The localized model structure** (`HomotopicalAlgebra.SimplicialModelCategory.Localization`, propose; HTT Proposition A.3.7.3, PDF p. 926). For a left proper combinatorial simplicial model category A and a small set S of cofibrations of A, the cofibrations of A and the S-equivalences form a model structure `S⁻¹A` on the same category. It is combinatorial, simplicial and left proper, and its fibrant objects are the fibrant S-local objects of A.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.A.3.7.3/replacement` (S-local fibrant replacement), `HTT.A.3.7.3/accessible` (S-equivalences are accessible) and `HTT.A.3.7.3/saturated` (trivial cofibrations of `S⁻¹A`), and this entry's own target `HTT.A.3.7.3`, which applies Smith's theorem (A.2.6.10) to them and adds simpliciality, left properness, the fibrant objects, the synonym and its transport lemmas.

*Lean:* a `def` type synonym `Localization A S := A` with `ModelCategory` and `SimplicialModelCategory` instances; the bridge `Localization.equivalence A S : A ≌ Localization A S` and the transport lemmas `Localization.cofibrations_eq` (`cofibrations A`), `Localization.weakEquivalences_eq` (`localEquivalences S`) and `Localization.fibrations_eq` (their right lifting class); `isBousfieldLocalization`, `isLeftProper`, `isFibrant_iff` (stated with `(Localization.equivalence A S).functor.obj`).

**Checks.** For S empty, `S⁻¹A = A`. For S the generating trivial cofibrations of A, `S⁻¹A = A` as well (every fibrant object is S-local).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: Smith's theorem A.2.6.10. Accessibility of the S-equivalences (`HTT.A.3.7.3/accessible`): they are the preimage of the weak equivalences under a fibrant-replacement functor T for `S⁻¹A` built by the small object argument (`HTT.A.3.7.3/replacement`), which commutes with κ-filtered colimits (A.1.2.5, A.2.6.7, A.2.6.8); the trivial cofibrations are weakly saturated by A.3.7.1, and stable under pushout along cofibrations by left properness of A (`HTT.A.3.7.3/saturated`). Simpliciality by A.3.1.7.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7.3/replacement`, `HTT.A.3.7.3/accessible`, `HTT.A.3.7.3/saturated` (below); `HTT.A.3.7/intro`; A.3.1.5, A.3.1.7 (F3.3); HTT A.2.6.1, A.2.6.10 (F1.6).

**S-local fibrant replacement** (`HTT.A.3.7.3/replacement`, part 1 of 3 of the localized model structure above; in the proof of HTT Proposition A.3.7.3, PDF p. 927). For A left proper, combinatorial and simplicial and S a small set of cofibrations, build a functor T by the small object argument on the generating trivial cofibrations of A together with the pushout-products of S with `∂Δ[n] ⊆ Δ[n]`. It is a functorial factorization `X ⟶ T X ⟶ ∗` with `X ⟶ T X` an S-equivalence and `T X` fibrant and S-local; T commutes with κ-filtered colimits for large κ; and a map is an S-equivalence exactly when its image under T is a weak equivalence.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7/intro`, A.3.7.1; HTT A.1.2.5 (F1.1); A.3.1.5 (F3.3).

**S-equivalences are accessible** (`HTT.A.3.7.3/accessible`, part 2 of 3 of the localized model structure above; in the proof of HTT Proposition A.3.7.3, PDF pp. 927–928). The S-equivalences form an accessible subcategory of `Arrow A` and have the two-out-of-three property.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7.3/replacement`; HTT A.2.6.7, A.2.6.8 (F1.6).

**Trivial cofibrations of `S⁻¹A`** (`HTT.A.3.7.3/saturated`, part 3 of 3 of the localized model structure above; in the proof of HTT Proposition A.3.7.3, PDF pp. 927–928). The cofibrations that are S-equivalences form a weakly saturated class, stable under pushout along cofibrations, and the cofibrations with the right lifting property against all of them are trivial fibrations of A.

*Needs:* A.3.7.1, `HTT.A.3.7/intro`; HTT A.2.4.1 (F1.5); A.1.2.2 (F1.1).

**Every combinatorial localization is a localization at a set** (HTT Proposition A.3.7.4 and Remark A.3.7.5, PDF pp. 928–929). For A left proper combinatorial simplicial: every combinatorial Bousfield localization of A is `S⁻¹A` for a small set S of cofibrations, and `S⁻¹A = T⁻¹A` exactly when the S-local and T-local objects of hA coincide (A.3.7.4). S may be taken to consist of cofibrations between cofibrant objects (A.3.7.5), by replacing each `f ∈ S` by the cofibration `g_f` between cofibrant objects from the proof of A.3.7.1.

*Needs:* A.3.7.1, A.3.7.3, `HTT.A.3.7/intro`; A.3.1.5 (F3.3); `HTT.A.2.7/kan-fibrations`; HTT A.1.2.2 (F1.1), A.2.4.1 (F1.5), A.2.6.1 (F1.6).

**Simplicial presheaves are the universal model category** (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal`; foundational, D. Dugger, *Universal homotopy theories*, Adv. Math. 164 (2001), the input to Lurie's citation of [19] in the proof of HTT Proposition A.3.7.6, PDF p. 930). For a small category C, `U C = Fun(Cᵒᵖ, SSet)` with the projective structure, and a functor `γ : C ⟶ M` into a model category: there is a Quillen adjunction `U C ⇄ M` whose left adjoint, composed with the Yoneda embedding, is naturally weakly equivalent to a cofibrant replacement of γ. It is obtained from a cosimplicial resolution of γ: a functor `C × SimplexCategory ⟶ M`, Reedy cofibrant in the cosimplicial direction (A.2.9.19) and homotopically constant there (every cosimplicial structure map a weak equivalence), with a natural weak equivalence from its degree-0 part to γ.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal/resolution` (cosimplicial resolutions) and `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal/realization` (realization along a resolution), and this entry's own target `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal`, which is the existence statement `ProjectiveDiagram.universal`.

*Lean:* `HomotopicalAlgebra.ProjectiveDiagram.universal` (propose): for `γ : C ⥤ M` there exist a cosimplicial resolution and `L : ProjectiveDiagram Cᵒᵖ SSet ⥤ M` with right adjoint, `Adjunction.IsQuillen`, and a zigzag of natural weak equivalences between `yoneda ⋙ L` and γ.

**Checks.** For `C = Discrete PUnit`, a cofibrant object X of M with a cosimplicial resolution `X^•` gives the left Quillen functor `K ↦ K ⊗ X^•` from `SSet` (for `M = SSet` and X = `Δ[0]`, the identity up to weak equivalence).

*Proof route.* Dugger's: cosimplicial resolutions exist by factoring in the Reedy structure on `SimplexCategory ⥤ M` (A.2.9.19; `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal/resolution`); the left adjoint is the coend with the resolution, and it is left Quillen because it sends the generating projective cofibrations to the latching maps of the Reedy cofibrant resolution (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal/realization`).

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal/resolution`, `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal/realization` (below).

**Cosimplicial resolutions** (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal/resolution`, part 1 of 2 of the universality of simplicial presheaves above; Dugger, *Universal homotopy theories*). Every functor `γ : C ⥤ M` into a model category has a cosimplicial resolution: a functor `C × SimplexCategory ⥤ M`, Reedy cofibrant and homotopically constant in the cosimplicial variable, with a natural weak equivalence from its degree-0 part to a cofibrant replacement of γ. Any two resolutions are connected by weak equivalences.

*Proof route.* Factor `∅ ⟶ γ` (as constant diagrams) in the Reedy structure on `SimplexCategory ⥤ M`.

*Needs:* HTT A.2.9.19 (F1.8); A.2.6.1 (F1.6).

**Realization along a resolution** (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal/realization`, part 2 of 2 of the universality of simplicial presheaves above; Dugger, *Universal homotopy theories*). For a resolution Γ, the coend `L(X) = ∫^{c, n} X(c)_n · Γ(c, n)` on `ProjectiveDiagram Cᵒᵖ SSet` has a right adjoint and is left Quillen, and `yoneda ⋙ L ≃ Γ(−, 0)`.

*Proof route.* The generating projective cofibrations go to latching maps of the Reedy cofibrant Γ.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal/resolution`; `HTT.A.2.8.2/projective` (F3.2); `HTT.A.2.9.25/after` (F1.8); `HTT.A.2.7/model-properties` (F3.1).

**Combinatorial model categories have presentations** (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation`; foundational, D. Dugger, *Combinatorial model categories have presentations*, Adv. Math. 164 (2001), HTT reference [19], cited in the proof of HTT Proposition A.3.7.6, PDF p. 930). For every combinatorial model category M there are a small category C, a small set S of morphisms of `U C`, and a Quillen equivalence `S⁻¹ U C ⇄ M` with left adjoint on `S⁻¹ U C`, where `S⁻¹ U C` is the localization A.3.7.3 of the projective structure (left proper, combinatorial, simplicial). If M is a simplicial model category, the adjoint functors can be chosen simplicial (Lurie: the proof in [19] shows this). L8's A.3.7.6 uses the simplicial refinement.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as five targets: the four parts that follow this entry, `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/generators` (a small generating subcategory), `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/canonical` (the canonical homotopy colimit), `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/localize` (localizing `U C`) and `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/simplicial` (the simplicial refinement), and this entry's own target `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation`, which states the theorem in its two forms.

*Lean:* `HomotopicalAlgebra.exists_quillenEquivalence_localization` (propose) in two forms, plain and for `SimplicialModelCategory M` with simplicial adjoints (the latter from `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/simplicial`) (`EnrichedFunctor` structures on both adjoints compatible with the adjunction).

**Checks.** For `M = SSet` with Kan–Quillen, the theorem holds with `C = Discrete PUnit` and S empty: `U C` is `SSet` with the Kan–Quillen structure, `S⁻¹ U C = U C`, and the identity adjunction is the Quillen equivalence.

*Proof route.* Dugger's: take C a small full subcategory of cofibrant objects generating M under λ-filtered colimits for a suitable regular λ (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/generators`); the universal property gives `U C ⇄ M`; λ-filtered colimits in M are homotopy colimits for large λ (A.2.6.8), and S is a set of maps of `U C` whose inversion identifies the derived right adjoint with an equivalence (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/canonical`, `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/localize`); A.3.7.3 (with A.3.3.2 for `U C`) provides `S⁻¹ U C`.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/generators`, `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/canonical`, `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/localize`, `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/simplicial` (below).

**A small generating subcategory** (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/generators`, part 1 of 4 of presentations of combinatorial model categories above; Dugger, *Combinatorial model categories have presentations*). For a combinatorial model category M there are:

- a regular λ such that λ-filtered colimits of cofibrant objects are homotopy colimits (A.2.6.8);
- a small full subcategory C of cofibrant λ-presentable objects such that every cofibrant object is a λ-filtered colimit of objects of C.

*Needs:* HTT A.2.6.1, A.2.6.8 (F1.6); A.1.1.2 (F1.1); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3.2).

**The canonical homotopy colimit** (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/canonical`, part 2 of 4 of presentations of combinatorial model categories above; Dugger, *Combinatorial model categories have presentations*). For C as in `/generators` and the realization `L : U C ⟶ M` of `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal`, the derived counit `L(R X) ⟶ X` is a weak equivalence for every fibrant X: X is the homotopy colimit of the canonical diagram over `C ↓ X`.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/generators`; `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-universal`.

**Localizing `U C`** (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/localize`, part 3 of 4 of presentations of combinatorial model categories above; Dugger, *Combinatorial model categories have presentations*). There is a small set S of maps of `U C` such that `L ⊣ R` induces a Quillen equivalence `S⁻¹ U C ⇄ M`; S consists of the comparisons between the canonical colimit presentations of the representables and their images.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/canonical`; A.3.7.3, A.3.7.1; HTT A.3.3.2 (F3.5); A.2.5.1 (F1.5).

**The simplicial refinement** (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/simplicial`, part 4 of 4 of presentations of combinatorial model categories above; Dugger, *Combinatorial model categories have presentations*). If M is a simplicial model category, the resolution can be taken to be `Γ(c, n) = c ⊗ Δ[n]` on cofibrant c. Then L and R are simplicial functors, and the Quillen equivalence of `/localize` is simplicial.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/localize`; HTT A.3.1.5 (F3.3).

**Combinatorial model categories are Quillen equivalent to simplicial ones** (`HTT.A.3.7/dugger-simplicial`; foundational, corollary of the previous target). Every combinatorial model category is Quillen equivalent to a left proper combinatorial simplicial model category. Users: Proposition A.3.6.15 (F3.8) and HA 1.3.4.22–1.3.4.25 (L9).

*Lean:* `HomotopicalAlgebra.exists_quillenEquivalence_simplicial` (propose): a type with a left proper combinatorial `SimplicialModelCategory` structure and a Quillen equivalence from it to the given model category (Dugger's direction: the left adjoint starts at the simplicial side).

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/localize`.

## Layer L1: Quasicategories

HTT chapter 1 introduces four models: topological categories, simplicial categories, quasicategories and H-enriched homotopy categories. This layer builds the last three; topological categories are out of scope (see Scope and ownership).

It also introduces the operations used from chapter 2 on: joins, cones, slices, subcategories, morphism spaces, final objects and (co)limits, together with the simplicial nerve and the ∞-category of spaces `S` (L1.4). Many of the chapter's results are proved in chapter 2 and sit in L2 or L3: HTT 1.2.2.3, 1.2.4.3, 1.2.5.1, 1.2.5.3, 1.2.7.3, 1.2.9.3, 1.2.11.1, 1.2.12.4, 1.2.12.5, 1.2.12.9, 1.2.13.5 and 1.2.13.8. L1 holds what can be done before them.

The layer fixes these rows of the Conventions table: *adjunction* (`HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`, L1.2) and, in L1.5, *categorical equivalence* (`SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence`), *morphism space* (`HTT.1.2.2/morphism-space`), *fully faithful* and *essentially surjective* (`HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`, `HTT.1.2.10/essentially-surjective`), *final object* (`HTT.1.2.12/final`) and *limit, colimit* (`SSet.IsLimit`, `SSet.IsColimit`). L1.1 applies the Model and Universes conventions (`HTT.1.2.15/intro`). L1.5 redefines Tau Ceti's `SSet.IsFullyFaithful`, and makes `SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence` the definition that Tau Ceti's `SSet.QCat.IsCategoricalEquivalence` becomes a characterization of.

It takes from Mathlib `SSet.Quasicategory`, `SSet.KanComplex`, `SSet.StrictSegal`, `CategoryTheory.nerveAdjunction`, `SSet.hoFunctor`, `SSet.Truncated.HomotopyCategory₂`, `SSet.QCat.bicategory`, `Bicategory.Adjunction`, `SimplicialThickening`, `SimplicialNerve` and `CategoryTheory.EnrichedCategory`; from Tau Ceti `SSet.join`, `SSet.slice`, `SSet.coslice`, `SSet.core`, `SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence`, `SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory`, `SSet.rightMappingSpace`, `SSet.IsTerminalVertex`, `HornThickening` and `EnrichedFunctor.IsDwyerKanEquivalence`; from F2 `HTT.A.2.7/anodyne`, `HTT.A.2.7/kan-fibrations`, `HTT.A.2.7/kan-weak-equivalences`, `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`, `SSet.KanComplex.ihom` and `SSet.H`; from F1 HTT A.1.4.3; and from F3.4 `EnrichedCategory.IsLocallyFibrant`, for "locally Kan".

The main results are HTT 1.1.2.2 (nerves are the quasicategories with unique inner fillers), 1.2.3.9, 1.1.5.10 with Remark 1.1.5.11, Remark 1.1.5.2, and the simplicial form of 1.2.4.1 (`HTT.1.2.4/simplicial-equivalences`, L1.6).

Departures from Lurie: adjunctions are Kerodon's unit–counit definition, with HTT 5.2.2.1 a characterization in L6 (`HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`); final objects are Joyal's strongly final vertices of any simplicial set, with HTT 1.2.12.1 a characterization in L2 (`HTT.1.2.12/final`); Dwyer–Kan equivalences keep Tau Ceti's unwound form, with HTT 1.1.4.4's a characterization (L1.5, H-enriched constructions); the core is Tau Ceti's, defined for every simplicial set (`HTT.1.2.5/core`); and 1.2.4.1 is stated for simplicial categories in place of topological ones (L1.6).

Forward needs: no subsection needs a later one. Inside L1.5, *Categorical equivalences* needs `SSet.hoEnriched` and H, and the Lean form of *Fully faithful and essentially surjective maps* uses `SSet.hoEnriched`; both are stated in the H-enriched constructions at the end of the subsection.

### L1.1 Quasicategories and Kan complexes

**Kan complexes and ∞-categories** (HTT Definition 1.1.2.1, PDF p. 26; Definition 1.1.2.4, PDF p. 32). Supplied by Mathlib: `SSet.KanComplex` and `SSet.Quasicategory`. Lurie's "∞-category" is `SSet.Quasicategory`.

*Lean:* Mathlib `SSet.KanComplex X` and `SSet.Quasicategory X`; "∞-category" means `[SSet.Quasicategory C]`.

**Nerves are the quasicategories with unique inner fillers** (`SSet.nerve_iff_uniqueInnerFillers`; HTT Proposition 1.1.2.2, PDF p. 27). A simplicial set is isomorphic to the nerve of a small category exactly when every inner horn has exactly one filler. Mathlib proves that nerves are strict Segal, and that strict Segal simplicial sets are quasicategories. Provide the converse: unique inner fillers make K strict Segal, and a strict Segal K is isomorphic to `nerve (hoFunctor.obj K)` through the unit of `CategoryTheory.nerveAdjunction`.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.1.1.2.2/strict-segal` (unique inner fillers give a strict Segal set) and `HTT.1.1.2.2/nerve-iso` (strict Segal sets are nerves), and this entry's own target `HTT.1.1.2.2`, which is `SSet.nerve_iff_uniqueInnerFillers`, combining them with Mathlib's direction.

**Checks.**

- `Δ[n]` has unique inner fillers.
- `Λ[2, 1]` has none of the inner fillers that it would need to be a nerve.
- The nerve of a groupoid is a Kan complex in which every horn `Λ[n, i] ⟶ N(G)` with `n ≥ 2` has exactly one filler.

*Proof route.* Unique fillers in dimension 2 compose the edges, and in dimension 3 make the composition associative (`HTT.1.1.2.2/nerve-iso`). Uniqueness in higher dimensions identifies each simplex with its spine (`HTT.1.1.2.2/strict-segal`).

*Needs:* `HTT.1.1.2.2/strict-segal`, `HTT.1.1.2.2/nerve-iso` (below); Mathlib `SSet.StrictSegal`, `SSet.StrictSegal.quasicategory`.

**Unique inner fillers give a strict Segal set** (`HTT.1.1.2.2/strict-segal`, part 1 of 2 of the characterization of nerves by unique inner fillers above; in the proof of HTT Proposition 1.1.2.2, PDF pp. 29–30). If every inner horn in K has exactly one filler, then K is `SSet.StrictSegal`: every simplex is determined by its spine, and every spine comes from a simplex.

*Proof route.* Induction on dimension: fillers of `Λ[n, i]` with `0 < i < n` extend spines one vertex at a time, and uniqueness makes the extension unique.

*Needs:* Mathlib `SSet.StrictSegal`, horns.

**Strict Segal sets are nerves** (`HTT.1.1.2.2/nerve-iso`, part 2 of 2 of the characterization of nerves by unique inner fillers above; in the proof of HTT Proposition 1.1.2.2, PDF pp. 28–30). For a strict Segal K, the unit `K ⟶ nerve (hoFunctor.obj K)` of `nerveAdjunction` is an isomorphism.

*Proof route.* The spine bijections in dimensions 2 and 3 define composition and make it associative, so `hoFunctor.obj K` has the edges of K as morphisms; both sides are strict Segal with the same spines.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.nerveAdjunction`, `SSet.StrictSegal`.

**Smallness** (`HTT.1.2.15/intro`; HTT §1.2.15, PDF p. 68). Fix Grothendieck universes as in the Conventions: a set or simplicial set is small when it is u-small, and essentially small when it is equivalent (as the context requires) to a small one. No new declarations: this target fixes the universe levels that `Small`, `SSet.{u}` and the later locally small and presentable targets use.

*Lean:* no new declarations. Small means `Type u` and `SSet.{u}`, large means `Type (u + 1)` and `SSet.{u + 1}`; essential smallness of ∞-categories is the notion of L7.2.

### L1.2 The homotopy category of a quasicategory

**The nerve–homotopy-category adjunction** (HTT Proposition 1.2.3.1, PDF p. 46). Supplied by Mathlib: `CategoryTheory.nerveAdjunction : SSet.hoFunctor ⊣ nerveFunctor`.

**Homotopy of edges and the category π(C)** (HTT Propositions 1.2.3.5, 1.2.3.7 and 1.2.3.8, PDF pp. 48–49; Remark 1.2.3.6, PDF p. 48). Supplied by Mathlib for 2-truncated quasicategories: `SSet.Truncated.HomotopyCategory₂`, with its left and right homotopy relations, their equivalence, and the composition law. Provide the restatement for a quasicategory C through its 2-truncation (`SSet.Quasicategory.homotopyCategory₂`). Also provide the self-duality of Remark 1.2.3.6: edges homotopic in C are homotopic in `Cᵒᵖ`, as `homotopic_op_iff`.

*Needs:* Mathlib `SSet.Truncated.HomotopyCategory₂`, `SSet.Quasicategory`.

**π(C) is the homotopy category** (`SSet.Quasicategory.homotopyCategory₂Iso`; HTT Proposition 1.2.3.9, PDF p. 50). For a quasicategory C, the functor `hoFunctor.obj C → π(C)` is the identity on objects and sends each edge to its homotopy class. It is an isomorphism of categories.

**Checks.**

- For C the nerve of a category A, both categories are A.
- For a Kan complex C, `π(C)` is a groupoid.

*Proof route.* Generators and relations: every morphism of `hoFunctor.obj C` is the class of a single edge, because 2-simplices compose edges. Homotopic edges are identified, because a homotopy is a 2-simplex.

*Needs:* Mathlib `SSet.hoFunctor`, `SSet.Truncated.HomotopyCategory₂`.

**Functor ∞-categories, named** (HTT Notation 1.2.7.2, PDF p. 57). `Fun(C, D)` is the internal Hom `(ihom C).obj D` of `SSet`. Its edges are natural transformations, and its equivalences are natural equivalences. That `Fun(K, C)` is a quasicategory when C is one is supplied by Mathlib. The invariance statement, HTT 1.2.7.3, is in L3.

*Lean:* no new definition: `Fun(K, C)` is `(ihom K).obj C` in `SSet`.

**Adjunctions** (`HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`; the Conventions definition, Kerodon Definition 6.2.1.1; HTT's own definition 5.2.2.1 is a characterization in L6). For ∞-categories C and D, an adjunction between `F : C ⟶ D` and `G : D ⟶ C` is a unit `id_C ⟶ G ∘ F` and a counit `F ∘ G ⟶ id_D`, edges of `Fun(C, C)` and `Fun(D, D)`, whose two triangle composites are homotopic to the identity transformations.

*Lean:* a Mathlib `Bicategory.Adjunction F G` in Mathlib's `SSet.QCat.bicategory`, whose hom-categories are the homotopy categories `hFun(C, D)`; no new structure. Name the predicate `SSet.QCat.IsLeftAdjoint F := ∃ G, Nonempty (Bicategory.Adjunction F G)` if one is needed.

**Checks.**

- The nerve of a Mathlib adjunction `L ⊣ R` is an adjunction.
- An equivalence in `SSet.QCat.bicategory` can be improved to an adjoint equivalence (Mathlib `Bicategory.Equivalence`).

*Needs:* HTT 1.2.7.2; Mathlib `SSet.QCat.bicategory`, `Bicategory.Adjunction`.

**Identity morphisms and equivalences** (`SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence`; `HTT.1.2.4/intro`, HTT §1.2.4, PDF p. 51). In a quasicategory C, the identity morphism of an object X is the degenerate edge `s₀ X`. An edge is an equivalence when its image in `hoFunctor.obj C` is an isomorphism, and two objects are equivalent when some equivalence joins them. Use Tau Ceti's `SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence` with its characterization through the homotopy category.

*Lean:* the identity of `x` is `SSet.Edge.id x`, and equivalences are Tau Ceti `SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence`; for a quasicategory, `SSet.Edge.isEquivalence_iff_isIso` identifies them with the edges invertible in `hoFunctor.obj C`.

**Checks.**

- Identity edges are equivalences.
- In the nerve of a category, the equivalences are the isomorphisms.
- In a Kan complex, every edge is an equivalence.

*Needs:* Mathlib `SSet.hoFunctor`, `SSet.Truncated.HomotopyCategory₂`.

### L1.3 Joins, cones and slices

**Joins** (HTT Definition 1.2.8.1, PDF p. 58; Proposition 1.2.8.3, PDF p. 59). Supplied by Tau Ceti: `SSet.join`, its monoidal structure with unit the empty simplicial set, and `Δ[i−1] ⋆ Δ[j−1] ≅ Δ[i+j−1]`. The join of quasicategories is a quasicategory.

*Lean:* no new definition: Tau Ceti `SSet.join (K L : SSet.{u}) : SSet.{u}`, with its monoidal structure (unit `⊥_ SSet`) and `Δ[i−1] ⋆ Δ[j−1] ≅ Δ[i+j−1]`.

**Cones** (`SSet.leftCone`, `SSet.rightCone`; HTT Notation 1.2.8.4, PDF p. 59). Define the left cone `K^◁ = Δ[0] ⋆ K` and the right cone `K^▷ = K ⋆ Δ[0]`, with the cone point and the inclusion of K. Provide `Δ[n]^▷ ≅ Δ[n+1]`, with K included as the face opposite the last vertex.

*Lean:* `SSet.leftCone K := SSet.join Δ[0] K` and `SSet.rightCone K := SSet.join K Δ[0]` (propose), with the cone point and the inclusion of K.

**Checks.**

- `∅^▷ = Δ[0]`.
- `(∂Δ[1])^◁` is `Λ[2, 0]`.

*Needs:* Tau Ceti `SSet.join`.

**Slices** (HTT Proposition 1.2.9.2, PDF p. 60). Supplied by Tau Ceti: `SSet.slice`. For `p : K → S`, the simplicial set `S_{/p}` represents maps `Y ⋆ K → S` restricting to p. The coslice `S_{p/}` is dual.

**Subcategories and full subcategories** (`SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory`; `HTT.1.2.11/intro`, HTT §1.2.11, PDF p. 62).

- A subcategory of a quasicategory C is the pullback `C ×_{N(hC)} N((hC)₀)` for a subcategory `(hC)₀` of its homotopy category.
- The full subcategory spanned by a set of objects is the case of a full subcategory of `hC`. It is Tau Ceti's `SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory` for the predicate "belongs to the set", and is again a quasicategory.

Provide the general (not necessarily full) subcategory, with its inclusion and the quasicategory instance.

*Lean:* for `C : SSet.{u}`, objects `P : ObjectProperty (hoFunctor.obj C)` and morphisms `W : MorphismProperty (hoFunctor.obj C)` with `[W.IsMultiplicative]`, `SSet.subcategory C P W : C.Subcomplex` (propose) is the preimage (Mathlib `Subcomplex.preimage`) of the nerve of the subcategory with objects P and morphisms the W-morphisms between them (the simplices of `nerve (hoFunctor.obj C)` whose vertices satisfy P and whose edges lie in W) under the unit `C ⟶ nerve (hoFunctor.obj C)`, which is Lurie's pullback `C ×_{N(hC)} N((hC)₀)` (PDF p. 62); it is a `[Quasicategory]` when C is one. The full case is Tau Ceti `SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory`.

**Checks.**

- For a quasicategory C, the subcategory determined by the core groupoid of `hC` is Tau Ceti's `SSet.core`.
- For a category A, the subcategories of `nerve A` are the nerves `nerve A₀ ⊆ nerve A` of the subcategories A₀ of A (a set of objects and a set of morphisms closed under identities and composition), with no closure under isomorphisms: in the walking isomorphism `x ≅ y`, the subcategory `{x}` gives the subcategory `Δ[0]`.

*Needs:* Tau Ceti `SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory`, `SSet.core`; Mathlib `SSet.hoFunctor`, `CategoryTheory.nerve`.

### L1.4 Simplicial categories and the simplicial nerve

**Simplicial categories** (HTT Definition 1.1.4.1, PDF p. 36). Supplied by Mathlib: `CategoryTheory.SimplicialCategory`. The category `Cat_Δ` of small simplicial categories and simplicial functors is Mathlib's category of `SSet`-enriched categories. A simplicial category is fibrant (locally Kan) when every mapping simplicial set is a Kan complex (F3.4's `EnrichedCategory.IsLocallyFibrant SSet C`).

*Lean:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.SimplicialCategory C`; `Cat_Δ` is the category of small `SSet`-enriched categories and simplicial functors; locally Kan is `EnrichedCategory.IsLocallyFibrant SSet C` (F3.4).

**The thickened simplices** (HTT Definitions 1.1.5.1 and 1.1.5.3, PDF pp. 38–39). Supplied by Mathlib: `CategoryTheory.SimplicialThickening J` for a linear order J, and its functoriality in monotone maps.

*Lean:* no new definition: Mathlib `CategoryTheory.SimplicialThickening J` for a linear order J, with its functoriality in monotone maps.

**The rigidification of a simplicial set** (`SSet.rigidification`, the functor `C[−]`; HTT §1.1.5, PDF p. 41). Define `C[−] : SSet ⥤ Cat_Δ` as the left Kan extension of `Δ[n] ↦ SimplicialThickening (Fin (n+1))` along the Yoneda embedding. This is the colimit-preserving extension that HTT 1.1.5.5 uses.

Provide:

- `C[−] ⊣ SimplicialNerve`;
- `C[Δ[n]] ≅ SimplicialThickening (Fin (n+1))`;
- the objects of `C[S]` are the vertices of S.

**Checks.**

- `C[∂Δ[1]]` is the discrete simplicial category on two objects.
- `C[Δ[1]]` has one nonidentity mapping simplicial set, a point.
- `C` of a horn agrees with Tau Ceti's `HornThickening`.

*Lean:* on objects, `SSet.Rigidification S`, the simplicial category `C[S]`, and on maps `SSet.rigidification.map f : EnrichedFunctor SSet (Rigidification S) (Rigidification T)` (propose), the form L1.5 uses. As functors between the model-category synonyms used by 2.2.5.1 (L3.8): `SSet.rigidificationFunctor : SSet.Joyal ⥤ EnrichedCat.Bergner SSet`, `SSet.simplicialNerveFunctor : EnrichedCat.Bergner SSet ⥤ SSet.Joyal` and `SSet.rigidificationAdjunction : rigidificationFunctor ⊣ simplicialNerveFunctor` (propose); Mathlib has `C[−]` and N on objects only.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.2.4/presentable` (F3.4, colimits in `Cat_Δ`); Mathlib `SimplicialThickening`, `SimplicialNerve`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.leftKanExtension`; Tau Ceti `HornThickening`.

**The simplicial nerve** (HTT Definition 1.1.5.5, PDF p. 40). Supplied by Mathlib: `CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve C`, whose n-simplices are the simplicial functors `C[Δ[n]] → C`.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as five targets: the four parts that follow this entry, `HTT.1.1.5.5/functor` (the functor `C[−]` of the rigidification entry above), `HTT.1.1.5.5/nerve-map` (functoriality of the simplicial nerve and its counit), `HTT.1.1.5.5/adjunction` (`C[−] ⊣ N` on the model-category synonyms) and `HTT.1.1.5.5/horn` (`C[−]` of horns and small simplices), and this entry's own target `HTT.1.1.5.5`, which is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve`.

*Lean:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve C`, with `C[−] ⊣ SimplicialNerve` from `SSet.rigidification` (`SSet.rigidificationAdjunction`, the part `HTT.1.1.5.5/adjunction`). Its functoriality `SSet.simplicialNerve.map (F : EnrichedFunctor SSet C D) : SimplicialNerve C ⟶ SimplicialNerve D` (propose), which Mathlib lacks, and the counit `SSet.simplicialNerveCounit C : EnrichedFunctor SSet (Rigidification (SimplicialNerve C)) C` (propose), used by 2.2.0.1 (L2.8), are defined in the part `HTT.1.1.5.5/nerve-map`.

*Needs:* `HTT.1.1.5.5/functor`, `HTT.1.1.5.5/nerve-map`, `HTT.1.1.5.5/adjunction`, `HTT.1.1.5.5/horn` (below); Mathlib `SimplicialNerve`.

**The functor `C[−]`** (`HTT.1.1.5.5/functor`, part 1 of 4 of the simplicial nerve above; HTT §1.1.5, PDF p. 41). `SSet.Rigidification S` and `C[−] : SSet ⥤ EnrichedCat SSet`, the left Kan extension of `Δ[n] ↦ SimplicialThickening (Fin (n+1))` along Yoneda. This part provides:

- `C[Δ[n]] ≅ SimplicialThickening (Fin (n+1))`;
- preservation of colimits;
- the objects of `C[S]` are the vertices of S.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.2.4/presentable` (F3.4); Mathlib `SimplicialThickening`, `Functor.leftKanExtension`.

**Functoriality of the simplicial nerve and its counit** (`HTT.1.1.5.5/nerve-map`, part 2 of 4 of the simplicial nerve above; HTT Definition 1.1.5.5, PDF p. 40). `SSet.simplicialNerve.map` for an S-enriched functor, and the counit `SSet.simplicialNerveCounit C : C[N C] ⟶ C`.

*Needs:* Mathlib `SimplicialNerve`.

**`C[−] ⊣ N` on the model-category synonyms** (`HTT.1.1.5.5/adjunction`, part 3 of 4 of the simplicial nerve above; HTT §1.1.5, PDF p. 41). `SSet.rigidificationAdjunction` on `SSet.Joyal` and `EnrichedCat.Bergner SSet`, with the functors `SSet.rigidificationFunctor` and `SSet.simplicialNerveFunctor`. This part also introduces the type synonym `SSet.Joyal` with its `Category` instance and the bridge `SSet.Joyal.equivalence : SSet ≌ SSet.Joyal`; the model structure on it and the transport lemmas are L3.8's.

*Needs:* `HTT.1.1.5.5/functor`, `HTT.1.1.5.5/nerve-map`; the synonym `EnrichedCat.Bergner SSet` with its bridge (HTT A.3.2.4, F3.4).

**`C[−]` of horns and small simplices** (`HTT.1.1.5.5/horn`, part 4 of 4 of the simplicial nerve above; in the proof of HTT Proposition 1.1.5.10, PDF p. 42). `C[Λ[n, i]]` is Tau Ceti's `HornThickening` as a simplicial subcategory of `C[Δ[n]]`. `C[∂Δ[1]]` is discrete on two objects, and `C[Δ[1]]` has one nonidentity mapping space, a point.

*Proof route.* Compute the colimit over the faces of the horn in `Cat_Δ`, using the description of pushouts along functors bijective on objects from `HTT.A.3.2.4/presentable`.

*Needs:* `HTT.1.1.5.5/functor`; Tau Ceti `HornThickening`.

**The simplicial nerve of a fibrant simplicial category is a quasicategory** (`CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve.quasicategory`; HTT Proposition 1.1.5.10, PDF p. 41). If every mapping simplicial set of C is a Kan complex, then `SimplicialNerve C` is a quasicategory.

**Checks.**

- For an ordinary category A, viewed as a simplicial category with discrete mapping sets, `SimplicialNerve A` is `nerve A`.
- For the simplicial category with one object whose endomorphism simplicial monoid is `Δ[1]` under max (unit 0), which is not Kan, the simplicial nerve fills every inner 2-horn but not every `Λ[3, 1]`: with `f₀₁ = f₀₃ = 1`, `f₀₂ = f₁₃ = f₂₃ = 0` and `f₁₂` either vertex, the three faces of the horn exist (a triangle on `a < b < c` exists exactly when `f_{ac} ≤ max(f_{ab}, f_{bc})`), and the missing face `[0, 2, 3]` would need `f₀₃ ≤ max(f₀₂, f₂₃)`.

*Proof route.* An inner horn `Λ[n, i] → N(C)` is a simplicial functor out of `C[Λ[n, i]]`. Extending it to `C[Δ[n]]` is one extension problem: the inclusion of the mapping object `C[Λ[n, i]](0, n)` into the cube `(Δ[1])^{n−1}` against the Kan complex `Map_C(F 0, F n)`. That inclusion is the cube minus its interior and one face, an anodyne extension.

*Needs:* Mathlib `SimplicialNerve`; `HTT.1.1.5.5/horn`; `HTT.A.2.7/anodyne`; Tau Ceti `HornThickening.exists_extension`.

**Nerves of locally Kan fibrations** (`CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve.innerFibration_map`; HTT Remark 1.1.5.11, PDF p. 42). A simplicial functor `F : C → D` that induces a Kan fibration on every mapping simplicial set gives an inner fibration `N(C) → N(D)`.

**Checks.** For `D = ∗` this is Proposition 1.1.5.10.

*Proof route.* The extension problem of 1.1.5.10, relative to D.

*Needs:* `CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve.quasicategory`; `HTT.1.1.5.5/nerve-map` (the map `N(C) ⟶ N(D)`, which Mathlib lacks); Mathlib `SSet.InnerFibration`; `HTT.A.2.7/kan-fibrations`.

**The ∞-category of spaces** (`SSet.Kan`, `SSet.spaces`; HTT Definition 1.2.16.1, PDF p. 69). `Kan` is the full simplicial subcategory of `SSet` on the Kan complexes, with the simplicial enrichment of Mathlib's `SimplicialCategory SSet` instance. `S = SimplicialNerve Kan` is the ∞-category of spaces. Provide the quasicategory instance, from 1.1.5.10 and the fact that `Fun(K, Z)` is Kan for Z Kan.

*Lean:* `SSet.Kan.{u} : Type (u + 1)`, the full subcategory of `SSet.{u}` on `SSet.KanComplex`, with the `SimplicialCategory` structure restricted from Mathlib's `SimplicialCategory SSet.{u}`; `SSet.spaces.{u} : SSet.{u + 1} := SimplicialNerve SSet.Kan.{u}`, with `[SSet.Quasicategory SSet.spaces]`. Both are large, as the Universes convention requires.

**Checks.**

- The vertices of S are the (u-small) Kan complexes.
- An edge of S is a map of Kan complexes.

*Needs:* `CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve.quasicategory`; `SSet.KanComplex.ihom` (F2.1); Mathlib `SimplicialCategory SSet`.

### L1.5 Equivalences, morphism spaces and final objects

This subsection fixes the definitions of the Conventions table that HTT states through the H-enriched homotopy category `hS = h C[S]`: categorical equivalences (1.1.5.14) and fully faithful maps (1.2.10.1) are HTT's, so they need `C[−]` (L1.4) and H with its enriched homotopy categories (the last part of this subsection). Final objects use Joyal's strongly final form (1.2.12.3), and HTT's 1.2.12.1 is a characterization in L2. Morphism spaces have two models, `Hom^R` and `Hom_C`. The forms users need for ∞-categories (the bicategorical equivalence, fully faithful through `Hom^R`) are proved early, in L2 and L3, so that downstream work does not unpack H.

**The core** (`HTT.1.2.5/core`, Tau Ceti `SSet.core`; Kerodon §4.4.3). For a simplicial set X, `X.core` is the subcomplex of the simplices all of whose edges are equivalences (`SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence`: an inverse edge with 2-simplices witnessing both composites). On main. HTT §1.2.5 (PDF p. 52) defines the core only for ∞-categories; Tau Ceti's form extends it to all simplicial sets.

*Lean:* Tau Ceti main `SSet.core (X : SSet.{u}) : X.Subcomplex`, for any X: the simplices each of whose edges satisfies `SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence`, that is `Nonempty e.InvStruct` (one inverse edge and 2-simplices for both composites). When X is a quasicategory these are exactly the edges invertible in `hoFunctor.obj X` (`SSet.Edge.isEquivalence_iff_isIso`); for a general simplicial set the condition is stronger than invertibility in `hoFunctor.obj X`.

*Needs:* HTT 1.1.2.4; HTT 1.2.3.1 (Mathlib `SSet.hoFunctor`).

**Categorical equivalences** (`SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence`; HTT Definition 1.1.5.14, PDF p. 43). A map `f : S ⟶ T` of simplicial sets is a categorical equivalence when the induced functor of H-enriched homotopy categories `hS ⟶ hT` is an equivalence, where `hS = h C[S]` (L1.4, L1.5): essentially surjective, and `Map_{hS}(x, y) ⟶ Map_{hT}(fx, fy)` an isomorphism in H for all vertices x, y. Equivalently (a lemma of this entry), `C[f]` is a Dwyer–Kan equivalence of simplicial categories. This is the class of weak equivalences of the Joyal model structure (2.2.5.1, L3.8).

Provide `SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence` with closure under isomorphism and composition, and two-out-of-three (formal from the H-enriched form).

*Lean:* `def SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence {S T : SSet.{u}} (f : S ⟶ T) : Prop := (SSet.hoEnriched.map f).IsEquivalence`, where `EnrichedFunctor.IsEquivalence` is the notion of L1.5 (essentially surjective on underlying categories and an isomorphism in `SSet.H` on each mapping object); for any simplicial sets, with no universe quantifier. The lemma of this entry is the `iff` with `(SSet.rigidification.map f).IsDwyerKanEquivalence`.

**Characterizations** (separate targets):

- for maps of ∞-categories, an equivalence in `SSet.QCat.bicategory` (Tau Ceti main `SSet.QCat.IsCategoricalEquivalence`, to be renamed, see the redefinition table), in L3;
- `hFun(T, C) ⟶ hFun(S, C)` an equivalence of categories for every ∞-category C (HTT Proposition 2.2.5.8), in L3;
- Kerodon's form (Definition 4.5.4.1: `Fun(T, C)^≃ ⟶ Fun(S, C)^≃` a homotopy equivalence for every ∞-category C). It is not an HTT statement and is not needed by any target; add it only if another roadmap asks for it.

**Checks.**

- The nerve of an equivalence of categories is a categorical equivalence.
- Isomorphisms are categorical equivalences.
- The inclusion `Λ[2, 1] ⟶ Δ[2]` is one (an instance of 2.2.5.2); the inclusion `Λ[2, 0] ⟶ Δ[2]` is not.

*Proof route.* Formal for the closure properties. For the checks, compute `C[Λ[2, 1]] ⟶ C[Δ[2]]` directly: a bijection on objects whose only nontrivial mapping space is the inclusion of a point into `Δ[1]`.

*Needs:* L1.4 (`C[−]`); `SSet.hoEnriched`, `isDwyerKanEquivalence_iff_isEquivalence_hoEnriched` (below in L1.5) and H.

**Morphism spaces** (`HTT.1.2.2/morphism-space`, `SSet.morphismSpace C x y` and Tau Ceti `SSet.rightMappingSpace`; HTT §1.2.2, PDF pp. 45–46, Kerodon Construction 4.6.1.1). HTT's mapping object `Map_C(x, y)` lives in H; it has two simplicial models, and the roadmap keeps both.

- `Hom_C(x, y)`: for a simplicial set C and vertices x, y, the fibre over `(x, y)` of `(ihom Δ[1]).obj C ⟶ C ⊗ C`, evaluation at the two vertices of `Δ[1]`. Its vertices are the edges from x to y. Functorial in C through `Fun(Δ[1], −)`. This is the space for users.
- `Hom^R_C(x, y)`: the fibre of the slice projection `C_{/y} ⟶ C` over x (Tau Ceti main), and dually `Hom^L_C(x, y)`. Lurie's statements and proofs use these (1.2.2.3, §2.4.4, §4.2.1).

Provide `SSet.morphismSpace` and the equivalence of its vertices with `SSet.Edge x y`; `SSet.rightMappingSpace` is on main.

*Lean:* for any simplicial set C, `SSet.morphismSpace (C : SSet.{u}) (x y : C _⦋0⦌) : ((ihom Δ[1]).obj C).Subcomplex` (propose), the preimage of the vertex `(x, y)` of `C ⊗ C` under `SSet.endpoints C : (ihom Δ[1]).obj C ⟶ C ⊗ C` (propose), evaluation at the two vertices of `Δ[1]`, together with `(SSet.morphismSpace C x y) _⦋0⦌ ≃ SSet.Edge x y`. `Hom^R` is Tau Ceti main `SSet.rightMappingSpace x y`; `Hom^L` is `SSet.leftMappingSpace x y` (propose), the fibre over y of the coslice projection `C_{x/} ⟶ C` (Tau Ceti `SSet.coslice`): its n-simplices are the `(n+1)`-simplices with first vertex x whose face opposite that vertex is constant at y. It is isomorphic to the opposite of `rightMappingSpace` of `Cᵒᵖ` from y to x (a lemma), since passing to `Cᵒᵖ` reverses the vertex order of every simplex.

**Characterizations** (separate targets): for a quasicategory C, both models are Kan complexes (HTT 1.2.2.3 for `Hom^R`, L2.2; HTT 2.4.7.11 for `Hom_C`, the fibre of a bifibration, L3.9), and the pinch inclusions `Hom^R_C(x, y) ⟶ Hom_C(x, y) ⟵ Hom^L_C(x, y)` are homotopy equivalences (HTT 4.2.1.8, L5.5; its dependencies are available after L3.8, see its proof route).

*Lean (characterizations):* the pinch inclusions `SSet.rightMappingSpace.toMorphismSpace C x y : rightMappingSpace C x y ⟶ morphismSpace C x y` and `SSet.leftMappingSpace.toMorphismSpace C x y` (propose), and the functoriality maps `SSet.morphismSpace.map f x y : Hom_X(x, y) ⟶ Hom_Y(f x, f y)` (the restriction of `(ihom Δ[1]).map f`) and `SSet.rightMappingSpace.map f x y : Hom^R_X(x, y) ⟶ Hom^R_Y(f x, f y)` (propose), used by the fully faithful characterizations below.

**Checks.**

- For the nerve of a category, `Hom(x, y)` is the discrete simplicial set on the morphisms from x to y, for both models.
- For `Δ[n]` and vertices `a ≤ b`, `Hom(a, b)` is a point; for `a > b` it is empty.

*Needs:* HTT 1.1.2.4, 1.2.7.2; `HTT.A.2.7/kan-fibrations`.

**Fully faithful and essentially surjective maps** (`HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`, `SSet.IsFullyFaithful`; `HTT.1.2.10/essentially-surjective`, `SSet.IsEssentiallySurjective`; HTT Definition 1.2.10.1, PDF p. 61).

- For any simplicial sets, `f : S ⟶ T` is fully faithful when `hS ⟶ hT` is a fully faithful functor of H-enriched categories: every `Map_S(x, y) ⟶ Map_T(f x, f y)` is an isomorphism in H.
- f is essentially surjective when `hoFunctor.map f` is essentially surjective (Mathlib `Functor.EssSurj`).
- So f is a categorical equivalence (L1.5 above) exactly when it is fully faithful and essentially surjective, nearly by definition.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsFullyFaithful f := ∀ x y : SSet.hoEnriched S, IsIso ((SSet.hoEnriched.map f).map x y)` in `SSet.H` (the mapping-object component of Mathlib's `EnrichedFunctor` is the field `map`), for any `f : S ⟶ T`; no quasicategory hypothesis.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsEssentiallySurjective {S T : SSet.{u}} (f : S ⟶ T) : Prop := (SSet.hoFunctor.map f).toFunctor.EssSurj`, for any simplicial sets.

**Characterizations** (separate targets): for ∞-categories, f is fully faithful exactly when the maps `Hom^R_X(x, y) ⟶ Hom^R_Y(f x, f y)` are homotopy equivalences (through HTT 2.2.4.1, L2.8; prove it there, so that users never unpack H), and equivalently for `Hom_C` (with 4.2.1.8, L5.5; Kerodon 4.8.3.1). *Lean:* `SSet.isFullyFaithful_iff_rightMappingSpace : IsFullyFaithful f ↔ ∀ x y, IsHomotopyEquivalence (rightMappingSpace.map f x y)` and `SSet.isFullyFaithful_iff_morphismSpace`, the same with `morphismSpace.map f x y`, both for `[Quasicategory X] [Quasicategory Y]`.

**Checks.**

- The nerve of a fully faithful functor is fully faithful, and the nerve of an essentially surjective functor is essentially surjective.
- For a quasicategory C, the inclusion of a full enhanced subcategory (Tau Ceti `SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory`) is fully faithful; for simplicial sets it can fail (`Λ[2, 1]` on `{0, 2}`).
- `Δ[0] ⟶ Δ[1]`, at either vertex, is fully faithful and not essentially surjective.

*Needs:* `HTT.1.2.2/morphism-space`, HTT 1.2.3.1; `SSet.hoEnriched` and `SSet.hoEnriched.map` (below in L1.5) and H.

**Final objects** (`HTT.1.2.12/final`, Tau Ceti `SSet.IsTerminalVertex`, `SSet.IsInitialVertex`; HTT Definition 1.2.12.3, PDF p. 63). A vertex X of a simplicial set C is final when every map `∂Δ[n] ⟶ C` with last vertex X extends to `Δ[n]`, equivalently when `C_{/X} ⟶ C` is a trivial fibration. Initial vertices are the final vertices of `Cᵒᵖ`. This is HTT's *strongly final*, used for every simplicial set; for an ∞-category it is HTT's *final*.

*Lean:* Tau Ceti `SSet.IsTerminalVertex`, which is stated in the boundary-extension form; the equivalence with HTT's form, `C_{/X} ⟶ C` a trivial fibration, is a lemma of this target, `SSet.isTerminalVertex_iff_trivialFibration_π` (propose), through `∂Δ[n] ⋆ Δ[0] ∪ Δ[n] = ∂Δ[n+1]` and the universal property of the slice (1.2.9.2, L1.3). `SSet.IsInitialVertex (X : C _⦋0⦌) : Prop`, `SSet.IsTerminalVertex` of X as a vertex of `Cᵒᵖ`.

**Characterizations** (separate targets): over a quasicategory, X is final exactly when every `Hom^R_C(Y, X)` is contractible (HTT 1.2.12.4, L2), exactly when it is final in the H-enriched homotopy category (HTT 1.2.12.1 with 1.2.12.5, L2); the final vertices of an ∞-category span an empty or contractible Kan complex, so final vertices are unique up to equivalence (HTT 1.2.12.9, L2).

**Checks.**

- The last vertex of `Δ[n]` is final.
- In the nerve of a category, a vertex is final exactly when it is a terminal object.
- `Λ[2, 0]` has no final vertex.

*Needs:* HTT 1.2.12.3; Tau Ceti `SSet.slice` with its universal property (1.2.9.2, L1.3).

**Limits and colimits** (Tau Ceti `SSet.IsColimit`, `SSet.IsLimit`; HTT Definition 1.2.13.4, PDF p. 65). For a quasicategory C and `p : K ⟶ C`:

- a colimit of p is an initial vertex of `C_{p/}`, which amounts to an extension `p̄ : K^▷ ⟶ C`;
- a limit of p is a final vertex of `C_{/p}`, an extension `K^◁ ⟶ C`.

*Lean:* Tau Ceti main, for `p : K ⟶ C`: `SSet.IsColimit p (c : (SSet.coslice p) _⦋0⦌) : Prop`, which is `SSet.IsInitialVertex c`, and `SSet.IsLimit p (c : (SSet.slice p) _⦋0⦌) : Prop`, which is `SSet.IsTerminalVertex c`. The definition puts no hypothesis on C; the targets assume `[SSet.Quasicategory C]`, as HTT does. Lurie's colimit is a vertex of `C_{p/}` (PDF p. 65), and the extension form is his abuse of terms (Remark 1.2.13.5): `SSet.IsColimitDiagram (p̄ : SSet.rightCone K ⟶ C)` is `IsColimit` of the vertex of `C_{p̄|K/}` determined by `p̄`.

**Characterization** (separate target; Kerodon 7.1.1.1, stated there for limits, the colimit form being dual): for a quasicategory C, `p̄ : K^▷ ⟶ C` with cone point c is a colimit diagram exactly when, for every object y, the map `Hom_C(c, y) ⟶ Hom_{Fun(K, C)}(p, const_y)` given by composing with the cocone is a homotopy equivalence. *Lean:* that map as `SSet.coconeMorphismSpaceMap p̄ y` (propose; `const_y` is `SSet.constAt K y`), and `SSet.isColimitDiagram_iff_morphismSpace : IsColimitDiagram p̄ ↔ ∀ y, IsHomotopyEquivalence (coconeMorphismSpaceMap p̄ y)`.

**Checks.**

- For `K = ∅`, a colimit is an initial object of C.
- For a small category J, a functor `F : J ⥤ A` and a cocone `c` over F, `nerve` of the extended functor `J^▷ ⥤ A` is a colimit cocone in `nerve A` exactly when `c` is a colimit cocone in A.

*Needs:* `HTT.1.2.12/final`; Tau Ceti `SSet.slice`, `SSet.coslice`; `SSet.rightCone`, `SSet.leftCone`.

#### HTT's H-enriched constructions

These targets formalize HTT's §§1.1.3–1.1.5 and Definition 1.2.2.1 as stated. L2's comparison of quasicategories with simplicial categories (HTT 2.2.0.1, 2.2.4.1, 2.2.5.1) and Layer F3 use them; the definitions above do not.

**The homotopy category of spaces** (HTT Example 1.1.3.3 and the discussion following Definition 1.1.3.4, PDF p. 34). F2.4's `SSet.H`, with `SSet.H.Q : SSet ⥤ H` and its Cartesian monoidal structure; no new definition.

*Needs:* `SSet.H` (F2.4).

**Change of enrichment and H-enriched equivalences.** H-enriched categories are `EnrichedCategory H`. A product-preserving functor of Cartesian monoidal categories transports enrichment (HTT Remark A.1.4.3, F1). An H-enriched functor is an equivalence when it is essentially surjective on underlying categories and induces isomorphisms in H on all mapping objects. Provide `EnrichedFunctor.IsEquivalence` for this notion.

*Needs:* HTT A.1.4.3 (F1); Mathlib `CategoryTheory.EnrichedCategory`.

**The homotopy category of a simplicial category; Dwyer–Kan equivalences** (`SimplicialCategory.hoEnriched`, `CategoryTheory.EnrichedFunctor.IsDwyerKanEquivalence` (Tau Ceti main); HTT Definition 1.1.4.1, Remark 1.1.4.3 and Definition 1.1.4.4, PDF pp. 36–37). For a simplicial category C, `hC` is the H-enriched category obtained by applying `Q` to every mapping simplicial set. A simplicial functor is a Dwyer–Kan equivalence when it is a weak homotopy equivalence on every mapping space and essentially surjective on homotopy categories: Tau Ceti main's unwound form, which is also Lurie's restatement in A.3.2.1 (PDF p. 875). HTT 1.1.4.4's form, that the induced H-enriched functor is an equivalence, is a characterization.

*Lean:* `SimplicialCategory.hoEnriched (C) [SimplicialCategory C]`, with the objects of C and `EnrichedCategory SSet.H` obtained by `TransportEnrichment` along the finite-product-preserving `SSet.H.Q` (HTT A.1.4.3, F1.2). A Dwyer–Kan equivalence is Tau Ceti main's `CategoryTheory.EnrichedFunctor.IsDwyerKanEquivalence F` as it stands: `weakEquivalence_map` (each `F.map X Y` a weak homotopy equivalence, F2.4) and `essSurj` (`F.mapHomotopyCategory` essentially surjective). HTT's form, `(SimplicialCategory.hoEnriched.map F).IsEquivalence` as an H-enriched functor, is the target `isDwyerKanEquivalence_iff_isEquivalence_hoEnriched`. Provide also `SimplicialCategory.hoEnriched.map F` (propose), the H-enriched functor of a simplicial functor F.

**Checks.**

- The unique functor `SimplicialThickening (Fin (n+1)) ⥤ [n]` is a Dwyer–Kan equivalence (Remark 1.1.5.2, below).
- An equivalence of ordinary categories is a Dwyer–Kan equivalence.

*Needs:* `SSet.H`; the change of enrichment above.

**The thickened simplex is a resolution of `[n]`** (`SimplicialThickening.mapping_iso_cube`, `SimplicialThickening.dkEquivalence_toCat`; HTT Remark 1.1.5.2, PDF p. 39).

- For `i < j` in `Fin (n+1)`, the mapping simplicial set `C[Δ[n]](i, j)` is isomorphic to the cube `(Δ[1])^{j−i−1}`. It is a point when `j = i`, and empty when `j < i`.
- The functor to the poset `[n]` is a Dwyer–Kan equivalence.

*Needs:* Mathlib `SimplicialThickening`; `CategoryTheory.EnrichedFunctor.IsDwyerKanEquivalence` (Tau Ceti main).

**The H-enriched homotopy category of a simplicial set** (`SSet.hoEnriched`; HTT Definition 1.1.5.14, PDF p. 43). The H-enriched homotopy category of a simplicial set S is `hS = h C[S]`; its underlying category is Mathlib's `hoFunctor.obj S`. Provide `SSet.hoEnriched`, its functoriality `SSet.hoEnriched.map f := SimplicialCategory.hoEnriched.map (SSet.rigidification.map f)` (propose; the H-enriched functor `hS ⟶ hT` that *Categorical equivalences* and *Fully faithful and essentially surjective maps* use), and that identification. The categorical equivalences of the same definition are the L1.5 target *Categorical equivalences* above, which uses this one.

*Needs:* `SSet.rigidification` (L1.4), `SimplicialCategory.hoEnriched`; Mathlib `SSet.hoFunctor`.

**Mapping objects in H** (`SSet.mapH`; HTT Definition 1.2.2.1, PDF p. 44). For vertices x, y of S, `Map_S(x, y) ∈ H` is the mapping object of `hS`. That it is represented by `Hom_S(x, y)` when S is a quasicategory combines HTT 2.2.4.1 (L2) with the morphism-space comparison above.

*Lean:* `SSet.mapH {S : SSet.{u}} (x y : S _⦋0⦌) : SSet.H := (x ⟶[SSet.H] y)` in `SSet.hoEnriched S`, for any simplicial set S.

*Needs:* `SSet.hoEnriched`.

### L1.6 Equivalences in a simplicial category

**Equivalences in a simplicial category** (`HTT.1.2.4/simplicial-equivalences`; the simplicial form of HTT Proposition 1.2.4.1, PDF p. 51). For a morphism `f : X → Y` of a simplicial category C whose mapping complexes are Kan, the following are equivalent:

- f is an isomorphism in `hC`;
- f has a homotopy inverse;
- composition with f is a homotopy equivalence `Map(Z, X) → Map(Z, Y)` for every Z, respectively `Map(Y, Z) → Map(X, Z)`;
- composition with f is a weak homotopy equivalence on every such mapping space.

**Checks.**

- In `Kan` itself, f is an equivalence exactly when it is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes.

*Proof route.* Yoneda in the H-enriched `hC` for the last implication; a weak homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes is a homotopy equivalence. The others are formal. HTT 2.2.3.6 applies this to `(Set_Δ)/S`.

*Needs:* `SimplicialCategory.hoEnriched`; `HTT.A.2.7/kan-weak-equivalences/whitehead`, `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

## Layer L2: Left fibrations, the covariant model structure, straightening over a point

HTT §§2.1–2.2, with the chapter 1 results whose proofs live there. The layer has three parts.

- **The combinatorial core** (L2.1–L2.5): left and right fibrations, Joyal's theorem on special outer horns, slices of ∞-categories, left anodyne maps, final objects. It needs L1, F2 and Mathlib's inner anodyne pushout-products; Tau Ceti main and open PRs already cover part of it.
- **The covariant model structure and categorical equivalences** (L2.6–L2.7): covariant equivalences through left cones and the categorical equivalences of L1.5, the covariant model structure (2.1.4.7), and inner anodyne maps as categorical equivalences (2.2.5.2). Lurie's routes, through `C[−]` and Bergner's model structure (F3.4). The Joyal model structure itself (2.2.5.1) sits in L3.8, since its proof uses the inner anodyne generators of §2.3.2; only its first step, `HTT.2.2.5.1/C`, is here.
- **The comparison with simplicial categories** (L2.8): straightening and unstraightening, straightening over a point, HTT's Theorem 2.2.0.1 and the mapping-space comparison 2.2.4.1. These use F3 (Bergner's model structure, enriched diagram categories) and feed the Joyal model structure (L3.8) and L4's straightening.

Items are in the book's order. Some need a later item of the layer: L2.1 needs L2.2–L2.4 (transport, 2.1.1.4), L2.2 needs L2.3, L2.5 needs L2.8 (the H-enriched forms 1.2.12.1 and 1.2.12.5 go through 2.2.4.1), L2.6 needs L2.7 (`HTT.2.2.5.1/C`), and L2.7 needs L2.8 (2.2.5.4 uses the `Hom^R` form of full faithfulness).

### L2.1 Left and right fibrations

**Kan fibrations and anodyne maps** (HTT Example 2.0.0.1, PDF p. 71). A Kan fibration has the right lifting property against every horn `Λ[n, i] ⊆ Δ[n]`; a map is anodyne when it has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration. Supplied by Mathlib: the fibrations of `SSet.modelCategoryQuillen` and `SSet.anodyneExtensions` (F2.1).

*Needs:* `HTT.A.2.7/kan-fibrations`, `HTT.A.2.7/anodyne`.

**Trivial fibrations and cofibrations** (HTT Example 2.0.0.2, PDF p. 71). A trivial fibration has the right lifting property against every `∂Δ[n] ⊆ Δ[n]`. A map has the left lifting property against all trivial fibrations exactly when it is a monomorphism. Supplied by Mathlib (the cofibrations of `SSet.modelCategoryQuillen` are the monomorphisms, generated by the boundary inclusions) and Tau Ceti (`SSet.rlp_monomorphisms_iff`).

*Needs:* Mathlib `SSet.modelCategoryQuillen`; Tau Ceti `SSet.rlp_monomorphisms_iff`.

**Left, right and inner fibrations; left, right and inner anodyne maps** (`SSet.LeftFibration`, `SSet.RightFibration`, `SSet.leftAnodyneExtensions`, `SSet.rightAnodyneExtensions`; HTT Definition 2.0.0.3, PDF p. 71). A map `f : X ⟶ S` of simplicial sets is a left fibration when it has the right lifting property against the horns `Λ[n, i] ⊆ Δ[n]` with `0 ≤ i < n`, a right fibration for `0 < i ≤ n`, and an inner fibration for `0 < i < n`. Left, right and inner anodyne maps are the maps with the left lifting property against all left, right, respectively inner fibrations.

*Lean:* for `f : X ⟶ S` in `SSet.{u}`, `SSet.LeftFibration f` is `(leftHorns).rlp f`, where the left horns are `Λ[n+1, i] ⟶ Δ[n+1]` for `i < n+1` (Tau Ceti's indexing; this is HTT's `0 ≤ i < n` with `n ≥ 1`), and dually `SSet.RightFibration` with `0 < i ≤ n+1`. `SSet.leftAnodyneExtensions := SSet.leftFibrations.llp`, where `SSet.leftFibrations` is the morphism property `SSet.LeftFibration`, and dually; inner fibrations and inner anodyne maps are Mathlib's `SSet.innerFibrations` and `SSet.innerAnodyneExtensions`. No hypothesis on X or S. Tau Ceti PR #27231 provides the left and right declarations.

Provide also: the left anodyne maps are the weakly saturated class generated by the left horns (small object argument, HTT A.1.2.5, in the form of Corollary A.1.2.7), the form used in the proofs of 2.1.2.3 and 2.1.2.6.

**Checks.**

- A map is a Kan fibration exactly when it is both a left and a right fibration.
- The nerve of the inclusion of a non-full subcategory is not a left fibration; for any functor of ordinary categories, the nerve is an inner fibration (HTT 1.1.2.2).
- `f` is a left fibration exactly when `f.op` is a right fibration (HTT Remark 2.0.0.7, used throughout for duality).

*Needs:* HTT 2.0.0.1; Mathlib `SSet.innerFibrations`, `SSet.innerAnodyneExtensions`, `MorphismProperty.rlp`, `MorphismProperty.llp`; HTT A.1.2.2 (weakly saturated classes), A.1.2.7 (F1.1).

**Categories cofibered in groupoids** (`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCofiberedInGroupoids`; HTT Definition 2.1.1.1, PDF p. 74). A functor `F : C ⥤ D` of ordinary categories exhibits C as cofibered in groupoids over D when (1) every morphism `F C ⟶ D'` of D has a preimage with source C, and (2) for every morphism `η : C ⟶ C'` of C and every object C'', the map from `Hom(C', C'')` to the pullback `Hom(C, C'') ×_{Hom(F C, F C'')} Hom(F C', F C'')` (precomposition with η, and F) is a bijection.

*Lean:* `class CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCofiberedInGroupoids (F : C ⥤ D) : Prop` with fields `exists_lift : ∀ (c : C) {d : D} (η : F.obj c ⟶ d), ∃ (c' : C) (η' : c ⟶ c'), ∃ h : F.obj c' = d, F.map η' ≫ eqToHom h = η` (condition (1)) and `isStronglyCocartesian : ∀ {c c'} (η : c ⟶ c'), F.IsStronglyCocartesian (F.map η) η` (Mathlib `FiberedCategory/Cocartesian.lean`), which is HTT's condition (2). The weak `Functor.IsCocartesian`, quantifying only over maps over the same morphism, is not the definition. Fibres are then groupoids.

**Checks.** The Grothendieck construction of a functor `D ⥤ Grpd` is cofibered in groupoids (HTT Example 2.1.1.2). The identity functor is; the inclusion of a non-full subcategory is not.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor` (fibered-category API).

**Nerves of categories cofibered in groupoids** (HTT Proposition 2.1.1.3, PDF p. 75). For a functor `F : C ⥤ D`, C is cofibered in groupoids over D exactly when `nerve F` is a left fibration.

*Proof route.* `nerve F` is an inner fibration (1.1.2.2), so only the horns `Λ[n, 0]` matter: n = 1 is condition (1), n = 2 and n = 3 are surjectivity and injectivity in condition (2), and for n ≥ 4 the horn `Λ[n, 0]` contains every 2-simplex of `Δ[n]`, so a map from it into a nerve extends uniquely.

*Needs:* HTT 2.0.0.3, 2.1.1.1, 1.1.2.2 (`SSet.nerve_iff_uniqueInnerFillers`).

**Transport along a left fibration** (HTT Lemma 2.1.1.4, PDF p. 76). Let `q : X ⟶ S` be a left fibration. Each fibre `X_s` is a Kan complex. Each edge `f : s ⟶ s'` determines a map `f_! : X_s ⟶ X_{s'}` in H, characterized by: `η' = f_! ∘ η` for classes `η : K ⟶ X_s`, `η' : K ⟶ X_{s'}` exactly when some `K × Δ[1] ⟶ X` over `K × Δ[1] ⟶ Δ[1] ⟶ S` (through f) restricts to representatives of η and η'. The assignment `s ↦ X_s`, `f ↦ f_!` is a functor `hoFunctor.obj S ⥤ H`.

*Lean:* `SSet.LeftFibration.transport q : SSet.hoFunctor.obj S ⥤ SSet.H`, with object function the fibres.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `X_s × {0} ⊆ X_s × Δ[n]` is left anodyne (2.1.2.7), which gives lifts over `Δ[1]` (definition of `f_!`) and over `Δ[2]` (the composition law). Kerodon's covariant transport (§5.2) is the ∞-categorical version, in L4.

*Needs:* HTT 2.0.0.3; `SSet.H` (F2.4); 1.2.5.1 (Kan fibres, L2.2); 2.1.2.7 (L2.4).

**Left fibrations and equivalences** (HTT Propositions 2.1.1.5–2.1.1.6, PDF p. 77). Let `p : C ⟶ D` be a left fibration of ∞-categories.

- If `p(f)` is an equivalence in D, then f is an equivalence in C (2.1.1.5).
- For an object Y of C and an equivalence `f̄ : X ⟶ p(Y)` in D, there is a morphism `f : X' ⟶ Y` of C with `p(f) = f̄` (2.1.1.6); it is an equivalence by 2.1.1.5.

Tau Ceti main has the right-fibration forms: a right fibration whose source is an ∞-category reflects equivalences (`SSet.Edge.isEquivalence_map_iff_of_rightFibration`, stated as an iff), and a right fibration lifts equivalences with prescribed source (`SSet.RightFibration.hasLift_of_isEquivalence`). The left forms follow by passing to opposites (HTT Remark 2.0.0.7, a check of 2.0.0.3).

*Proof route.* Lift a 2-simplex witnessing a homotopy inverse along the `Λ[2, 0]` lifting property: this gives a left inverse of f, then of the left inverse, and the two are homotopic.

*Needs:* HTT 2.0.0.3, 1.1.2.4; `SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence` (L1.2).

### L2.2 Joyal's theorem on special outer horns

**Equivalences and outer horns** (HTT Proposition 1.2.4.3, PDF p. 52; proof PDF p. 79). Let C be an ∞-category and φ an edge of C. Then φ is an equivalence exactly when every `f₀ : Λ[n, 0] ⟶ C` with `n ≥ 2` and `f₀|Δ^{0,1} = φ` extends to `Δ[n]`. On Tau Ceti main: `SSet.Edge.isEquivalence_iff_hornFilling_zero`, with `SSet.Quasicategory.hornFilling_zero` for the forward direction, proved by the route below.

**Checks.** In the nerve of a category, this is the statement that extensions of `Λ[n, 0]` exist when the first arrow is invertible. For n = 2 it gives a left inverse of φ; with n = 3 the left inverse is two-sided.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. If φ is an equivalence, the extension problem is a lift of an edge along the right fibration `C_{/Δ[n−2]} ⟶ C_{/∂Δ[n−2]}` (2.1.2.1); its source lies over φ through the right fibration `C_{/∂Δ[n−2]} ⟶ C`, so it is an equivalence by (the right-fibration dual of) 2.1.1.5, and the lift exists by the dual of 2.1.1.6. Conversely, fill `Λ[2, 0]` to get ψ with `ψ ∘ φ ≃ id`, then `Λ[3, 0]` to get `φ ∘ ψ ≃ id`.

*Needs:* HTT 2.1.1.5, 2.1.1.6 (L2.1), 2.1.2.1, 2.1.2.2 (L2.3); `SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence`.

**Kan complexes are the ∞-groupoids** (HTT Proposition 1.2.5.1, PDF p. 53). For a simplicial set C, the following are equivalent: (1) C is an ∞-category whose homotopy category is a groupoid; (2) C has fillers for `Λ[n, i]`, `0 ≤ i < n`; (3) for `0 < i ≤ n`; (4) C is a Kan complex.

**Checks.** The nerve of a groupoid satisfies (1); the nerve of `[1]` satisfies none.

*Proof route.* (1) ⇔ (2) is 1.2.4.3, (1) ⇔ (3) is 1.2.4.3 for `Cᵒᵖ`, and (4) is (2) and (3).

*Needs:* HTT 1.2.4.3, 1.1.2.1, 1.1.2.4.

**Right-pinched morphism spaces are Kan complexes** (HTT Proposition 1.2.2.3, PDF p. 45). For an ∞-category C and objects x, y, `Hom^R_C(x, y)` (Tau Ceti `SSet.rightMappingSpace`) is a Kan complex. Tau Ceti main has the right-horn filling for `0 < i ≤ n`; the Kan property follows by 1.2.5.1 (3) ⇒ (4).

*Needs:* HTT 1.2.5.1; Tau Ceti `SSet.rightMappingSpace`.

**The core is the largest Kan subcomplex** (HTT Proposition 1.2.5.3, PDF p. 53). For an ∞-category C, the core `C^≃` (L1.5, Tau Ceti `SSet.core`: simplices all of whose edges are equivalences) is a Kan complex, and every map from a Kan complex into C factors uniquely through it. Tau Ceti main gives the quasicategory instance and the factorization (`SSet.le_core_of_kanComplex`); provide the Kan property.

*Proof route.* A homotopy inverse of an equivalence is again an equivalence, so it lies in the core; hence the homotopy category of the core is a groupoid, and 1.2.5.1 applies.

*Needs:* HTT 1.2.5.1; `HTT.1.2.5/core`.

### L2.3 Joins, slices and left fibrations

**Pushout-joins of anodyne maps** (HTT Lemmas 2.1.2.3–2.1.2.4, PDF p. 80). For monomorphisms `A₀ ⊆ A` and `B₀ ⊆ B`, write `h` for the inclusion `(A₀ ⋆ B) ⊔_{A₀ ⋆ B₀} (A ⋆ B₀) ⊆ A ⋆ B`.

- If `A₀ ⊆ A` is right anodyne or `B₀ ⊆ B` is left anodyne, h is inner anodyne (2.1.2.3).
- If `A₀ ⊆ A` is left anodyne, h is left anodyne (2.1.2.4).

Tau Ceti main has the generating case `Λ[n, j] ⊆ Δ[n]` against `∂Δ[m] ⊆ Δ[m]` (`SSet.join.innerAnodyneExtensions_unionJoin_horn_boundary` and its dual), where h is the horn `Λ[n+m+1, j]`; the general case follows by saturation in each variable.

*Needs:* HTT 2.0.0.3, A.1.2.2; Tau Ceti `SSet.join`, `SSet.Subcomplex.unionJoin`.

**Slices along inner and left fibrations** (HTT Proposition 2.1.2.1, PDF p. 78). Let `A ⊆ B`, `p : B ⟶ X` and an inner fibration `q : X ⟶ S`; put `r = q ∘ p`, `p₀ = p|A`, `r₀ = r|A`. Then `X_{p/} ⟶ X_{p₀/} ×_{S_{r₀/}} S_{r/}` is a left fibration. If q is a left fibration, then also `X_{/p} ⟶ X_{/p₀} ×_{S_{/r₀}} S_{/r}` is a left fibration.

*Proof route.* By the universal property of slices (HTT 1.2.9.2), the lifting problems translate into extension problems along the pushout-joins of 2.1.2.3 (first claim) and 2.1.2.4 (second).

*Needs:* HTT 2.1.2.3, 2.1.2.4; Tau Ceti `SSet.slice`, `SSet.coslice` with their universal properties.

**Slices of ∞-categories** (HTT Corollary 2.1.2.2, PDF p. 79; Proposition 1.2.9.3, first assertion, `HTT.1.2.9.3/1`, PDF p. 61). For an ∞-category C and any `p : K ⟶ C`, the projection `C_{p/} ⟶ C` is a left fibration, so `C_{p/}` is an ∞-category (2.1.2.2: 2.1.2.1 with `S = Δ[0]`, `A = ∅`). Dually `C_{/p} ⟶ C` is a right fibration and `C_{/p}` is an ∞-category (1.2.9.3, first assertion; its invariance assertion is in L3). Tau Ceti main has the dual form: `SSet.slice.rightFibration_π` (`C_{/p} ⟶ C` is a right fibration) and `SSet.slice.quasicategory`; restriction of cones along a monomorphism `L ⊆ K` is a right fibration (`SSet.slice.rightFibration_map`, the case `S = Δ[0]` of the dual of 2.1.2.1).

**Checks.** For `C = nerve A` and `p` an object a, `C_{a/}` is the nerve of the under-category `a/A`. The fibre of `C_{/y} ⟶ C` over x is `Hom^R_C(x, y)`.

*Needs:* HTT 2.1.2.1; Tau Ceti `SSet.slice`, `SSet.coslice`.

**Restriction of slices along anodyne maps** (HTT Proposition 2.1.2.5, PDF p. 80). Let `π : S ⟶ T`, `p : B ⟶ S`, an inclusion `i : A ⊆ B`, and write `p₀ = p|A`, `p' = π ∘ p`, `p'₀ = p'|A`. If i is right anodyne and π an inner fibration, or i is anodyne and π a left fibration, then `S_{p/} ⟶ S_{p₀/} ×_{T_{p'₀/}} T_{p'/}` is a trivial fibration.

*Proof route.* The class of such i is weakly saturated; for `i = Λ[m, j] ⊆ Δ[m]`, the lifting problem against `∂Δ[n] ⊆ Δ[n]` is a horn `Λ[m+n+1, j]` against π.

*Needs:* HTT 2.0.0.1, 2.0.0.3, 2.1.2.1, A.1.2.2; Tau Ceti `SSet.coslice`.

### L2.4 Left anodyne maps

**Generators of left anodyne maps** (HTT Proposition 2.1.2.6, PDF p. 81). The following generate the same weakly saturated class of maps of simplicial sets, the left anodyne maps:

- the horns `Λ[n, i] ⊆ Δ[n]`, `0 ≤ i < n`;
- the inclusions `(Δ[m] × {0}) ⊔_{∂Δ[m] × {0}} (∂Δ[m] × Δ[1]) ⊆ Δ[m] × Δ[1]`;
- the inclusions `(S' × {0}) ⊔_{S × {0}} (S × Δ[1]) ⊆ S' × Δ[1]` for all monomorphisms `S ⊆ S'`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's (Joyal's combinatorics: filter `Δ[n] × Δ[1]` by its nondegenerate (n+1)-simplices, each step a pushout of a left horn; each left horn is a retract of a map of the third kind), or Mathlib's Moss pairings, which already give the analogous statements for anodyne and inner anodyne maps; Tau Ceti PR #27231 provides the left and right cases.

*Needs:* HTT 2.0.0.3, A.1.2.2; Mathlib `SSet.anodyneExtensions` (Moss pairings).

**Pushout-products with left anodyne maps** (HTT Corollary 2.1.2.7, PDF p. 82). If `A ⟶ A'` is left anodyne and `B ⟶ B'` is a monomorphism, then `(A × B') ⊔_{A × B} (A' × B) ⟶ A' × B'` is left anodyne. Immediate from the third generating family of 2.1.2.6.

**Checks.** `X × {0} ⊆ X × Δ[1]` is left anodyne for every X; `X × {1} ⊆ X × Δ[1]` is right anodyne.

*Needs:* HTT 2.1.2.6.

**Anodyne pushout-products** (HTT Remark 2.1.2.8, PDF p. 83). The pushout-product of an anodyne map with a monomorphism is anodyne. Anodyne maps are generated by the left and the right anodyne maps, so this follows from 2.1.2.7 and its dual. Also supplied by Mathlib (F2.1).

*Needs:* HTT 2.1.2.7, 2.0.0.1.

**Exponentials of left fibrations** (HTT Corollary 2.1.2.9, PDF p. 83). For a left fibration `p : X ⟶ S` and a monomorphism `A ⟶ B`, the map `X^B ⟶ X^A ×_{S^A} S^B` is a left fibration, and a trivial fibration if `A ⟶ B` is left anodyne. By adjunction from 2.1.2.7 and 2.1.2.8.

*Needs:* HTT 2.1.2.7, 2.1.2.8.

**Homotopy extension lifting** (HTT Corollary 2.1.2.10, PDF p. 83). A map `p : X ⟶ S` is a left fibration exactly when `X^{Δ[1]} ⟶ X^{\{0\}} ×_{S^{\{0\}}} S^{Δ[1]}` is a trivial fibration.

*Proof route.* "Only if" is 2.1.2.9 for `{0} ⊆ Δ[1]`. "If": by adjunction p lifts against the second generating family of 2.1.2.6.

*Needs:* HTT 2.1.2.9, 2.1.2.6.

**Sections with a fibrewise contraction are left anodyne** (HTT Proposition 2.1.2.11, PDF p. 83). Let `p : X ⟶ S` have a section s, and let `h : X × Δ[1] ⟶ X` be a homotopy over S from `s ∘ p` to `id_X` that is constant on the section: `h ∘ (s × Δ[1]) = s ∘ pr`, with `pr : S × Δ[1] ⟶ S` the projection. Then s is left anodyne. Lurie states this without the constancy condition, but his proof uses it, and without it the claim fails: for the monoid `M = {1, e}` with `e² = e`, the natural transformation from the constant functor to the identity with component e gives such an h on `nerve M` over `Δ[0]`, and the vertex is not left anodyne (a lift against the left fibration `(nerve M)_{s/} ⟶ nerve M` would be a functor `M ⥤ s/M` over M sending the object to `id`, so `e · 1 = 1`). The users, Theorem A (4.1.3.1, L5.4) and the pullback form of the groupoid condition (6.1.2.6, L6.8), apply it to homotopies that are constant on the section.

*Proof route.* Given a lifting problem of s against a left fibration q (the square below commutes because h is constant on the section), extend along the left anodyne map `(S × Δ[1]) ⊔_{S × {0}} (X × {0}) ⊆ X × Δ[1]` (2.1.2.7) and restrict to `X × {1}`.

*Needs:* HTT 2.0.0.3, 2.1.2.7.

**Left fibrations over Kan complexes** (HTT Lemmas 2.1.3.2–2.1.3.4, PDF p. 84). Let `p : S ⟶ T` be a left fibration.

- If S and T are Kan complexes and p is a homotopy equivalence, p is surjective on vertices (2.1.3.2).
- If T is a Kan complex, p is a Kan fibration (2.1.3.3).
- If every fibre `S_t` is contractible, p is a trivial fibration (2.1.3.4).

*Proof route.* 2.1.3.3: S is Kan; for anodyne `A ⊆ B`, `S^B ⟶ S^A ×_{T^A} T^B` is a left fibration (2.1.2.9) and a homotopy equivalence, hence surjective on vertices by 2.1.3.2. 2.1.3.4 (stated for right fibrations): pull back to `T = Δ[n]`, deform along `Δ[n] × Δ[1]` towards the initial vertex using the filtration of 2.1.2.6; the last step fills a `Λ[n+1, 0]` whose first edge lies in a Kan fibre, hence is an equivalence, and uses 1.2.4.3.

*Needs:* HTT 2.0.0.3, 2.1.2.6, 2.1.2.9, 1.2.4.3, 1.2.5.1; F2 (homotopy equivalences of Kan complexes, `SSet.KanComplex.W`).

**Kan fibrations among left fibrations** (HTT Proposition 2.1.3.1, PDF p. 84). A left fibration `p : S ⟶ T` is a Kan fibration exactly when, for every edge `f : t ⟶ t'` of T, the transport `f_! : S_t ⟶ S_{t'}` (2.1.1.4) is an isomorphism in H.

**Checks.** Over a Kan complex every edge is invertible in `hT`, so this recovers 2.1.3.3; a left fibration with contractible fibres has all `f_!` invertible (compare 2.1.3.4).
