Call X over `N(C)` *good* when `α_C(X)` is a weak homotopy equivalence (unmarked case), respectively when its marked version is a Cartesian equivalence (marked case). In both cases:

- good objects are closed under filtered colimits, and under pushouts in which one leg is a cofibration;
- every simplex of dimension at most 1 is good;
- in the marked case, X is good once `X^♭` is good, by attaching marked edges along `(Δ[1])^♭ ⊆ (Δ[1])^♯`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Closure: `St⁺_φ` and `F⁺_•(C)` commute with filtered colimits and preserve cofibrations (3.2.1.7, 3.2.5.15), and the projective structure is left proper. In dimensions at most 1 both sides are computed directly, and α is an isomorphism.

*Needs:* 3.2.5.10, 3.2.5.15, 3.2.5.16 (above); 3.2.1.7 (L4.4); `HTT.A.2.8.2/projective` (F3.2); A.2.4.1, `HTT.A.2.4.3/after` (F1.5); `HTT.1.1.5.5/functor` (L1.4).

**The spine of a simplex is good** (`HTT.3.2.5.17/spine`, part 2 of 2 of Lemma 3.2.5.17 in comparison with straightening above; HTT Lemma 3.2.5.17, steps (F)–(G) of the proof, PDF pp. 220–221). For `Δ[n] ⟶ N(C)` with `n ≥ 2` and Z its spine, the map `F⁺_{Z^♭}(C) ⟶ F⁺_{Δ[n]^♭}(C)`, and its unmarked version, is a weak equivalence of projective diagrams.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Factor through `N([n])` and reduce to `C = [n]` by 3.2.5.14, since left Kan extension preserves weak equivalences between projectively cofibrant diagrams. At `i ∈ [n]` the map is the opposite of the spine inclusion of `Δ[i]`, which is marked anodyne (3.1.1.5).

*Needs:* 3.2.5.14, 3.2.5.15; 3.1.1.5 (L4.2); `HTT.A.2.8.2/projective` (F3.2).

**Relative nerves present straightening** (HTT Proposition 3.2.5.18, Corollary 3.2.5.19, Proposition 3.2.5.21, PDF pp. 221–222). For a small category C: `(F_•(C), N_•(C))` is a Quillen equivalence between `SSet/N(C)` with the covariant structure and `SSet^C` with the projective structure, and `(F⁺_•(C), N⁺_•(C))` one between `(Set⁺_Δ)/N(C)` with the coCartesian structure and `(Set⁺_Δ)^C` with the projective structure (3.2.5.18). If every `f(C) ⟶ f'(C)` is a Kan fibration, `N_f(C) ⟶ N_{f'}(C)` is a covariant fibration over `N(C)`; in particular `N_f(C) ⟶ N(C)` is a left fibration when every `f(C)` is a Kan complex (3.2.5.19). If every `f(C)` is an ∞-category, `p : N_f(C) ⟶ N(C)` is a coCartesian fibration, an edge over `C ⟶ C'` is p-coCartesian exactly when its component in `f(C')` is an equivalence, and p is classified by `N(f) : N(C) ⟶ Cat∞` (3.2.5.21, in the sense of 3.3.2.2).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: 3.2.5.18 from 3.2.5.15, 3.2.5.17 and Theorem 3.2.0.1; 3.2.5.21 from 3.2.5.18 and 3.1.4.1 applied to `C ↦ f(C)^♮`, and for (3) from 3.2.5.20. Parts (1)–(2) of 3.2.5.21 alone have an elementary proof (Kerodon §5.3.3, the weighted nerve), which applications needing only them should use.

*Needs:* the items above; Theorem 3.2.0.1 (L4.5); 3.1.4.1 (L4.3); L2.6 (covariant model structure, 2.1.4.5, 2.1.4.8/after); 3.3.2.2 (L4.7) for 3.2.5.21 (3); A.2.5.1, `HTT.A.2.8.2/projective`.

### L4.7 Applications

**Invariance under change of base** (HTT Proposition 3.3.1.1, Corollary 3.3.1.2, PDF pp. 222–223). For a categorical equivalence `p : S ⟶ T`, `(p_!, p^*)` is a Quillen equivalence between the Cartesian model structures on `(Set⁺_Δ)/S` and `(Set⁺_Δ)/T` (3.3.1.1). Hence for a Cartesian fibration `X ⟶ S` there is a Cartesian fibration `Y ⟶ T` with X equivalent to `S ×_T Y` as Cartesian fibrations over S (3.3.1.2).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: straightening (3.2.0.1, 3.2.1.4) turns `p_!` into `C[p]_!`, a Quillen equivalence by A.3.3.8.

*Needs:* Theorem 3.2.0.1 (L4.5); `HTT.3.2.1.4/base-change` (L4.4); A.3.3.8 (F3.5); L1.5.

**Base change along categorical equivalences** (HTT Proposition 3.3.1.3, Corollary 3.3.1.4, PDF pp. 223–224). For a Cartesian fibration `X ⟶ S` and a categorical equivalence `T ⟶ S`, `X ×_S T ⟶ X` is a categorical equivalence (3.3.1.3). Hence a pullback square along a Cartesian fibration is a categorical pullback square (homotopy Cartesian for the Joyal structure) (3.3.1.4).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: first for inner horns `Λ[n, i] ⊆ Δ[n]` through mapping simplices (3.2.2.7), then in general with 3.3.1.2 and 2.4.4.5.

*Needs:* the previous entry; 3.2.2.7 (L4.5); L3.7 (2.4.4.5); L3.8 (Joyal model structure).

**Fibrewise criterion over any base** (HTT Proposition 3.3.1.5, PDF p. 225). For Cartesian fibrations `p : X ⟶ S`, `q : Y ⟶ S` and `f : X ⟶ Y` over S carrying p-Cartesian edges to q-Cartesian edges, the following are equivalent: f is a categorical equivalence; every `X_s ⟶ Y_s` is one; `X^♮ ⟶ Y^♮` is a Cartesian equivalence. Unlike 2.4.4.4 (L3.7), S need not be an ∞-category.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: (2) ⇔ (3) is 3.1.3.5; (2) ⇒ (1) by 3.2.2.8 and 2.4.4.4; (1) ⇒ (3) by extending S to an ∞-category and 3.3.1.1, 3.3.1.3.

*Needs:* the previous entries; 3.1.3.5 (L4.3); 3.2.2.8 (L4.5); L3.7 (2.4.4.4).

**Pullbacks of right fibrations** (HTT Corollary 3.3.1.6, PDF p. 226). A pullback square of right fibrations over a further right fibration to S, `W = X ×_Z Y` with `Y, X ⟶ Z ⟶ S`, is homotopy Cartesian for the contravariant model structure on `SSet/S`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: compare fibres with a fibrant replacement, through 2.2.3.13 and 2.1.3.1. It uses only L2 and could be formalized right after L2.8.

*Needs:* L2.4 (2.1.3.1); L2.6; L2.8 (2.2.3.13).

**Cartesian fibrations are categorical fibrations** (HTT Propositions 3.3.1.7–3.3.1.8, PDF pp. 227–228). Every Cartesian fibration is a categorical fibration (3.3.1.7). Over a Kan complex S, for `p : X ⟶ S`, being a Cartesian fibration, a coCartesian fibration and a categorical fibration are equivalent (3.3.1.8).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: 3.3.1.7 by replacing S by an ∞-category with 3.3.1.2 and lifting homotopies along Cartesian fibrations; 3.3.1.8 (3) ⇒ (1) by lifting edges of S through a contractible Kan complex.

*Needs:* 3.3.1.2; L3.6, L3.8 (`HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration`, 2.4.6.5).

**The universal Cartesian fibration** (`SSet.universalCartesianFibration`; HTT §3.3.2 (`HTT.3.3.2/intro`), PDF pp. 228–229). The simplicial functor `Cat^Δ_∞ ⥤ Set⁺_Δ`, `C ↦ C^♮`, is a projectively fibrant diagram: it is a simplicial functor because `Map^♯(C^♮, D^♮)` is the core `Fun(C, D)^≃` (HTT Remark 3.1.3.1), and each `C^♮` is fibrant (3.1.4.1). Its unstraightening along the counit `C[Cat∞^op] ⟶ (Cat^Δ_∞)^op` is a fibrant object of `(Set⁺_Δ)/Cat∞^op`, that is a Cartesian fibration `q : Z ⟶ Cat∞^op`, the universal Cartesian fibration. Its fibre over C is `U(C)` (U of 3.2.3.1), with a canonical categorical equivalence `C ⟶ U(C)`.

*Lean:* `SSet.universalCartesianFibration : SSet.universalCartesian ⟶ catInfty.op` in `SSet.{u + 1}`, defined as `(markedUnstraightening φ).obj F` for that counit φ and F as above, with values lifted along `SSet.uliftFunctor`/`MarkedSSet` lifting to universe `u + 1`; prove it is a Cartesian fibration with fibres `U(C)`.

*Needs:* Theorem 3.2.0.1 (L4.5); 3.2.3.1 (L4.5); 3.1.4.1 (L4.3); L4.1; L2.8 (the counit of `C[−] ⊣ N`).

**Classifying maps** (`SSet.ClassifiesCartesianFibration`; HTT Definition 3.3.2.2, Remark 3.3.2.3, Warning 3.3.2.4, PDF p. 229). A functor `f : S ⟶ Cat∞^op` classifies a Cartesian fibration `p : X ⟶ S` when X is equivalent, as a Cartesian fibration over S, to the pullback `Z ×_{Cat∞^op} S` of the universal Cartesian fibration, which is `Un⁺_S f` (3.3.2.2). Dually, `f : S ⟶ Cat∞` classifies a coCartesian fibration p when `f^op` classifies `p^op`. Every Cartesian fibration between small simplicial sets has a classifying map, unique up to equivalence; more precisely, for κ uncountable regular, p is classified by a map to `Cat∞(κ)^op` (κ-small ∞-categories) exactly when its fibres are essentially κ-small, uniquely up to homotopy, and the same holds for large S with essentially small fibres (3.3.2.3). A map that is both Cartesian and coCartesian is classified both by a functor to `Cat∞^op` and by one to `Cat∞` (3.3.2.4).

*Lean:* the definition is stated at the large base, which Remark 3.3.2.3 (PDF p. 229) needs, and the small case is recovered by lifting. `SSet.ClassifiesCartesianFibration {X S : SSet.{u + 1}} (p : X ⟶ S) [SSet.CartesianFibration p] (f : S ⟶ SSet.catInfty.{u}.op) : Prop`: `∃ g : natural.over p ⟶ natural.over (pullback.snd universalCartesianFibration f), MarkedSSet.IsCartesianEquivalence g` (with `natural.over` of L4.3, and the instance that pullbacks of `SSet.universalCartesianFibration` are Cartesian fibrations) (equivalently, by 3.1.3.5, a fibrewise categorical equivalence preserving Cartesian edges, in either direction since both are fibrant). For p in `SSet.{u}`, `f : uliftFunctor.obj S ⟶ catInfty.op` classifies p when it classifies `uliftFunctor.map p`. CoCartesian form: `f : S ⟶ catInfty` classifies a coCartesian p when `opFunctor.map f` classifies `opFunctor.map p`.

**Checks.**

- `q` itself (in `SSet.{u + 1}`) is classified by the identity of `Cat∞^op`.
- For an ∞-category C, `C ⟶ Δ[0]` is classified by the vertex C of `Cat∞`.

*Proof route.* 3.3.2.3 from Theorem 3.2.0.1 (essential surjectivity of the derived unstraightening) with `Cat∞ ≃ N((Set⁺_Δ)°)`; Kerodon's Universality Theorem 5.6.0.2 is the same classification and is not a separate target. The κ-small refinement needs essentially κ-small ∞-categories (L7.2, 5.4.1.2); state it in the layer of that notion if it is formalized.

*Needs:* the universal Cartesian fibration; Theorem 3.2.0.1 (L4.5); 3.1.3.5 (L4.3); L3.6; F1 A.1.1.1 (universes); HTT 1.2.11/intro (full subcategories).

**Right fibrations and the universal right fibration** (HTT Propositions 3.3.2.5–3.3.2.6, PDF p. 230). For a Cartesian fibration `p : X ⟶ S`, the following are equivalent: p is a right fibration; every classifying map `S ⟶ Cat∞^op` factors through `S^op ⊆ Cat∞^op` (the ∞-category of spaces); some classifying map lands in `S^op` (3.3.2.5). The restriction `q' : Z' ⟶ S^op` of the universal Cartesian fibration is a right fibration, the universal right fibration, and its unique vertex `∗_Z` over the point `Δ[0]` is a final object of `Z'` (3.3.2.6).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: 3.3.2.5 from 2.4.2.4; 3.3.2.6 by extending simplicial functors out of `C[∂Δ[n] ⋆ Δ[0]]`, using that the inclusion of mapping spaces is a pushout-product with `{1} ⊆ Δ[1]`, hence anodyne.

*Needs:* the items above; L3.6 (2.4.2.4); L1.5 (`HTT.1.2.12/final`); L1.4 (`C[−]`); `S` (L1).

## Layer L5: Limits, colimits and Kan extensions

HTT chapter 4, with HTT's §§3.3.2–3.3.4 (the universal left fibration, limits and colimits of ∞-categories and of spaces), whose proofs use chapter 4. The definitions follow the Conventions table: limits and colimits are final and initial vertices of slices (L1.5), cofinality is HTT's right-fibration definition (4.1.1.1, Kerodon's right cofinality 7.2.1.1), and Kan extensions are pointwise (4.3.2.2; along arbitrary maps Kerodon 7.3.1.2). The model-categorical comparison of §4.2.4 (L5.7) is used where Lurie uses it.

The items are written in the book's order. Several of them need later items of the layer:

- L5.1 needs L5.2–L5.3, L5.6–L5.7 and L5.10 (4.1.1.3, 4.1.2.15, 4.2.3.14, 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4, 4.4.4.5).
- L5.2 needs L5.5 and L5.7: the direction (3) ⇒ (1) of 4.1.1.8 uses that `S` has small limits (4.2.4.8), and through 3.3.2.8 it needs 4.4.4.5 (L5.10); 4.1.1.9 uses the fat slices of L5.5.
- L5.4 needs L5.5 (4.1.3.1 uses the fat slice, 4.2.1.5).
- L5.6 needs L5.7 (4.2.3.15 uses 6.5.3.7, which needs only Theorem A, L5.4).
- L5.8 needs L5.10 (4.3.1.12 uses 4.4.4.10).

Lurie's text is circular at one point: 4.1.1.8 (3) ⇒ (1) uses 4.2.4.8, whose proof uses 4.2.3.14, whose proof uses 4.1.1.8 (2) ⇒ (1). The cycle is broken in 4.2.4.8 (L5.7, see its proof route), which can be proved from §4.2.1 and 4.2.4.1–4.2.4.4 alone. The formalization order is therefore: §4.2.1 (L5.5), then 4.2.4.1–4.2.4.8 (L5.7), 4.1.2.1 (L5.3), 4.4.4.5 (L5.10), 3.3.2.7–3.3.2.8 (L5.1), and then §4.1.1 from 4.1.1.8 on.

### L5.1 Limits and colimits of ∞-categories and of spaces

**The universal right fibration is represented** (HTT Corollary 3.3.2.7, PDF p. 231). The universal right fibration `q' : Z' ⟶ S^op` of §3.3.2 is representable in the sense of 4.4.4.5. It is represented by the one-point space `q'(∗_Z)`, a final object of `S`, together with the component of `∗_Z`; equivalently, `∗_Z` is a final object of `Z'`.

*Proof route.* `∗_Z` is a final object of `Z'` (3.3.2.6, L4.7); apply 4.4.4.5 (2) ⇒ (1).

*Needs:* 3.3.2.6 (L4.7), 4.4.4.5 (L5.10); `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**Left fibrations are pulled back from the universal one** (HTT Corollary 3.3.2.8, PDF p. 231). For a left fibration `X ⟶ S` between small simplicial sets, there are a map `S ⟶ S` (into the ∞-category of spaces) and an equivalence of left fibrations over S between X and `S ×_S S_{∗/}`.

*Needs:* 3.3.2.3 (L4.7), 3.3.2.7.

**Limits in `Cat∞`** (HTT Proposition 3.3.3.1, PDF p. 232). Let K be a simplicial set, `p̄ : K^▷ ⟶ Cat∞^op` a diagram (Lurie's "in the ∞-category of spaces" is a slip for `Cat∞`), `X̄ ⟶ K^▷` a Cartesian fibration classified by p̄ (3.3.2.2), and `X = X̄ ×_{K^▷} K`. Then (1) p̄ is a limit of `p = p̄|K` in `Cat∞` (that is, `p̄^op` is a limit diagram of `Cat∞`) exactly when (2) restriction of Cartesian sections `Map♭_{K^▷}((K^▷)^♯, X̄^♮) ⟶ Map♭_K(K^♯, X^♮)` is an equivalence of ∞-categories. Here `Map♭_K(K^♯, X^♮)` is the ∞-category of sections of `X ⟶ K` carrying every edge to a Cartesian edge.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.3.3.3.1/reduce` (reduction to the nerve of a strongly fibrant diagram), `HTT.3.3.3.1/sections` (Cartesian sections as derived global sections) and `HTT.3.3.3.1/compare` (the comparison with homotopy limits, which proves the statement), and this entry's own target `HTT.3.3.3.1`, which collects them.

**Checks.**

- For K = ∅ the condition says that the fibre of X̄ over the cone point is equivalent to `Δ[0]`, the final object of `Cat∞`.
- For a set A viewed as a discrete simplicial set, the limit is the product of the fibres.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: replace K by the nerve of a category (4.2.3.14) and the diagram by a strict one (4.2.4.4), as in `HTT.3.3.3.1/reduce`; identify Cartesian sections with derived global sections through straightening (3.2.0.1, 3.2.1.13), as in `HTT.3.3.3.1/sections`; then compare with homotopy limits in `Set⁺_Δ` by 4.2.4.1 (`HTT.3.3.3.1/compare`).

*Needs:* `HTT.3.3.3.1/reduce`, `HTT.3.3.3.1/sections`, `HTT.3.3.3.1/compare` (below); 3.3.2.2 (L4.7).

**Cartesian sections under cofinal reindexing** (`HTT.3.3.3.1/reduce`, part 1 of 3 of limits in `Cat∞` above; first step of the proof of HTT Proposition 3.3.3.1, PDF p. 232). In the situation of 3.3.3.1, let `f : N(C) ⟶ K` be cofinal with C a small category (4.2.3.14) and `f̄ : N(C^▷) ⟶ K^▷` its cone. Condition (2) holds for p̄ exactly when it holds for `p̄ ∘ f̄`. Moreover `p̄ ∘ f̄ : N(C^▷) ⟶ Cat∞^op` is equivalent to the nerve of a strongly fibrant (injective) diagram `(C^▷)^op ⥤ Set⁺_Δ`: apply 4.2.4.4 to `(p̄ ∘ f̄)^op` with `A = Set⁺_Δ` (injective structure, HTT Remark 4.2.4.5), `U = A` (a chunk of itself, HTT Example A.3.4.4) and u the counit `C[N((C^▷)^op)] ⟶ (C^▷)^op`, and use essential surjectivity of `N((A^{(C^▷)^op})°) ⟶ Fun(N((C^▷)^op), N(A°))`. Lurie's text cites 4.2.4.7 here; that corollary rectifies only into a new simplicial category, not into `Set⁺_Δ`.

*Proof route.* f̄ is cofinal, since it carries cone point to cone point and the inclusion of the cone point of a right cone is cofinal (4.1.1.3). So f and f̄ are contravariant equivalences over `K^▷` (4.1.2.5), hence give Cartesian equivalences `N(C)^♯ ⟶ K^♯` and `N(C^▷)^♯ ⟶ (K^▷)^♯` (the Quillen equivalence `(F₂, G₂)` of 3.1.5.6, with `G₂ X = X^♯`), and restriction of Cartesian sections along them is a categorical equivalence by the `Map^♭` form of 3.1.3.3.

*Needs:* 4.2.3.14 (L5.6); 4.2.4.4 (L5.7); 4.1.1.3 (L5.2); 4.1.2.5 (L5.3); 3.1.3.3, `HTT.3.1.3.3/after`, 3.1.5.6 (L4.3).

**Cartesian sections as derived global sections** (`HTT.3.3.3.1/sections`, part 2 of 3 of limits in `Cat∞` above; proof of HTT Proposition 3.3.3.1, PDF pp. 232–233). For a small category C, a strongly fibrant `F : C^op ⥤ Set⁺_Δ` and the counit `φ : C[N(C)]^op ⟶ C^op`, the ∞-category `Map♭_{N(C)}(N(C)^♯, Un⁺_φ F)` is isomorphic in `hSet⁺_Δ` to the right derived global sections (homotopy limit) of F, naturally in restriction along full subcategories of C. `Un⁺_φ F` is fibrant over `N(C)` (`Un⁺_φ` is right Quillen, 3.2.0.1), so it is `X^♮` for the Cartesian fibration X it classifies (3.1.4.1). Lurie's text writes `St⁺_φ F` here; the target reads it as `Un⁺_φ F`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the maps `St⁺_φ(K^♯ × Z) ⟶ St⁺_φ(K^♯) ⊠ St⁺_∗(Z) ⟶ δ(Z)` are weak equivalences (3.2.1.13, and 3.2.0.1 for the final object), so the derived right adjoints of `Z ↦ K^♯ × Z` and of the diagonal agree under straightening.

*Needs:* 3.2.0.1 (L4.5); 3.2.1.13 (L4.4); 3.1.4.1 (L4.3); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3.2).

**Comparison with homotopy limits** (`HTT.3.3.3.1/compare`, part 3 of 3 of limits in `Cat∞` above; HTT Proposition 3.3.3.1 and its proof, PDF pp. 232–233). The statement of 3.3.3.1 above.

*Proof route.* Reduce by `HTT.3.3.3.1/reduce`. By `HTT.3.3.3.1/sections`, condition (2) says that the global sections of F are the homotopy limit of `F|C`, which by the dual of 4.2.4.1 for the simplicial nerve is condition (1).

*Needs:* `HTT.3.3.3.1/reduce`, `HTT.3.3.3.1/sections`; 4.2.4.1 (L5.7); 2.4.2.1 (L3.6); 1.2.16.1 (L1.4).

**Limits in `Cat∞` are ∞-categories of Cartesian sections** (HTT Corollary 3.3.3.2, PDF p. 234). For `p : K ⟶ Cat∞^op` classifying a Cartesian fibration `X ⟶ K`, the limit of p in `Cat∞` is isomorphic in `hCat∞` to `Map♭_K(K^♯, X^♮)`.

*Needs:* 3.3.3.1; 3.1.0.2, 3.1.1.6, 3.1.1.7 (L4.2).

**Limits in `S`** (HTT Corollaries 3.3.3.3–3.3.3.4, PDF p. 234). For `p̄ : K^◁ ⟶ S` classifying a left fibration `X̄ ⟶ K^◁` with restriction `X ⟶ K`, p̄ is a limit of `p̄|K` exactly when restriction of sections `Map_{K^◁}(K^◁, X̄) ⟶ Map_{K^◁}(K, X̄)` is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes (3.3.3.3). Hence the limit of `p : K ⟶ S` is the Kan complex of sections `Map_K(K, X)` of the classified left fibration, up to isomorphism in H (3.3.3.4).

*Proof route.* Lurie's. The Kan–Quillen structure is a left Bousfield localization of the Joyal structure: the cofibrations agree, and categorical equivalences are weak homotopy equivalences (through the bridge, `SSet.Joyal.weakEquivalence_inverse_map`: `WeakEquivalence f` in `SSet.Joyal` gives `WeakEquivalence (SSet.Joyal.equivalence.inverse.map f)` in `SSet`). Hence the identity from Kan–Quillen to Joyal is right Quillen, and `Kan ⊆ Cat^Δ_∞` preserves homotopy limits of diagrams indexed by categories. With 4.2.3.14, 4.2.4.4 (strictifying a diagram in `N(Kan)`; Lurie cites 4.2.4.7) and 4.2.4.1, `S ⊆ Cat∞` preserves small limits. Then apply 3.3.3.1. 3.3.3.4 is 3.3.3.2 for the classified left fibration.

*Needs:* 3.3.3.1, 3.3.3.2; 4.2.3.14; 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4; `HTT.A.2.8.7/after`; 1.2.16.1; the Joyal and Kan–Quillen model structures and their comparison (L3.8, F2.4).

**Cofinal base change and Cartesian equivalences** (HTT Lemma 3.3.4.1, PDF p. 235). In a pullback square of simplicial sets `X' = X ×_S S'` with `X ⟶ S` a Cartesian fibration and `q : S' ⟶ S` such that `q^op` is cofinal, the induced map `X'^♮ ⟶ X^♮` is a Cartesian equivalence in `Set⁺_Δ` (over a point).

*Needs:* 4.1.1.3 (L5.2); 3.1.4.2, 3.1.5.7, 3.2.2.7, 3.2.2.14 (L4.3, L4.5); `HTT.3.1.3.3/after`; `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

**Colimits in `Cat∞`** (HTT Proposition 3.3.4.2, PDF pp. 236–237; Corollary 3.3.4.3, PDF p. 237). Let `p̄ : K^◁ ⟶ Cat∞^op` classify a Cartesian fibration `X̄ ⟶ K^◁` and `X = X̄ ×_{K^◁} K`. The following are equivalent: p̄ is a limit of `p̄|K` in `Cat∞^op` (a colimit in `Cat∞`); the inclusion `X^♮ ⊆ X̄^♮` is a Cartesian equivalence in `Set⁺_Δ/K^◁`; it is a Cartesian equivalence in `Set⁺_Δ` (3.3.4.2). Consequently, for `p : K^op ⟶ Cat∞` classifying a Cartesian fibration `X ⟶ K`, the colimit of p is isomorphic in `hCat∞ ≃ h(Set⁺_Δ)` to `X^♮`, that is to a fibrant replacement of `X^♮` in `Set⁺_Δ` (X with its Cartesian edges inverted) (3.3.4.3). `X^♮` itself is usually not fibrant (HTT Warning 3.3.4.4), so X is in general not the colimit.

*Parts.* Proposition 3.3.4.2 is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.3.3.4.2/marked` (Cartesian equivalence over the cone and over a point), `HTT.3.3.4.2/cofinal` (reduction to the nerve of a category) and `HTT.3.3.4.2/strict` (the strict case), and the target `HTT.3.3.4.2`, which rectifies the diagram and combines the parts.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. The equivalence of the last two conditions is `HTT.3.3.4.2/marked`. For the first two, choose a small category C and a map `N(C) ⟶ K` with cofinal opposite (4.2.3.14), reduce to `K = N(C)` by `HTT.3.3.4.2/cofinal`, rectify p̄ to the nerve of a projectively fibrant diagram `C^◁ ⥤ Set⁺_Δ` (4.2.4.4; Lurie cites 4.2.4.7), and apply `HTT.3.3.4.2/strict`. 3.3.4.3 follows with 3.3.4.1.

*Needs:* `HTT.3.3.4.2/marked`, `HTT.3.3.4.2/cofinal`, `HTT.3.3.4.2/strict` (below); 3.3.4.1; `HTT.3.1.3.3/after`; 4.2.3.14; 4.2.4.4 (L5.7; Lurie cites 4.2.4.7 for the strict diagram `C → (Set⁺_Δ)°`).

**Cartesian equivalence over the cone and over a point** (`HTT.3.3.4.2/marked`, part 1 of 3 of Proposition 3.3.4.2 in colimits in `Cat∞` above; HTT Proposition 3.3.4.2, (2) ⇔ (3), PDF p. 236). In the setting of 3.3.4.2, the inclusion `X^♮ ⊆ X̄^♮` is a Cartesian equivalence in `(Set⁺_Δ)/K^◁` exactly when it is one in `Set⁺_Δ`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's.

1. Factor `X^♮ ⟶ (K^◁)^♯` by the small object argument as a marked anodyne map `X^♮ ⟶ Y^♮` followed by a Cartesian fibration `Y ⟶ K^◁` with `X ≅ Y ×_{K^◁} K`, and lift to `q : Y ⟶ X̄`.
2. The relative condition holds exactly when q is an equivalence of Cartesian fibrations, that is, when `q_v` is an equivalence at the cone point v (3.1.3.5).
3. Compare with the absolute condition through the Cartesian equivalences `Y_v^♮ ⊆ Y^♮` and `X̄_v^♮ ⊆ X̄^♮` (3.3.4.1).

*Needs:* 3.3.4.1; 3.1.1.6 (L4.2); 3.1.3.5, 3.1.3.7 (L4.3); A.1.2.5 (F1.1).

**Reduction of colimits in `Cat∞` to the nerve of a category** (`HTT.3.3.4.2/cofinal`, part 2 of 3 of Proposition 3.3.4.2 in colimits in `Cat∞` above; HTT Proposition 3.3.4.2, first step of the proof of (1) ⇔ (2), PDF pp. 236–237). Let C be a small category, `r : N(C) ⟶ K` a map with `r^op` cofinal, and `C^◁ = [0] ⋆ C`. Then p̄ satisfies the first condition of 3.3.4.2 exactly when its restriction along `N(C^◁) ⟶ K^◁` does, and likewise for the second.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Both conditions are invariant: the first by cofinality (4.1.1.8), the second, in the absolute form of `HTT.3.3.4.2/marked`, because the comparison maps are Cartesian equivalences (3.3.4.1).

*Needs:* `HTT.3.3.4.2/marked`; 3.3.4.1; 4.1.1.8 (L5.2).

**Colimits in `Cat∞` of strict diagrams** (`HTT.3.3.4.2/strict`, part 3 of 3 of Proposition 3.3.4.2 in colimits in `Cat∞` above; HTT Proposition 3.3.4.2, proof of (1) ⇔ (2), PDF p. 237). Let C be a small category, `F : C^◁ ⥤ Set⁺_Δ` a projectively fibrant diagram, and `X̄ = Un⁺_φ F` over `N(C^◁)`. Then `N(F)` is a limit diagram in `Cat∞^op` exactly when `X^♮ ⊆ X̄^♮` is a Cartesian equivalence over `N(C^◁)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's.

1. The square of homotopy categories formed by the right derived unstraightenings (equivalences, 3.2.0.1) and the restrictions along `C ⊆ C^◁` commutes.
2. By 4.2.4.1, the limit condition says that F lies in the essential image of the derived left adjoint of restriction.
3. That left adjoint is fully faithful, since `C ⊆ C^◁` is (4.3.2.15 through 4.2.4.4). So the limit condition says that the counit at `X̄` is an isomorphism, which is the Cartesian equivalence condition.

*Needs:* 3.2.0.1 (L4.5); 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4 (L5.7); 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); `HTT.A.2.8.2/projective` (F3.2); `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful` (L1.5).

**Colimits in `S`** (HTT Proposition 3.3.4.5, PDF pp. 237–239; Corollary 3.3.4.6, PDF p. 239). Let `p̄ : K^▷ ⟶ S` classify a left fibration `X̄ ⟶ K^▷` and `X = X̄ ×_{K^▷} K`. The following are equivalent: p̄ is a colimit of `p̄|K`; the inclusion `X ⊆ X̄` is a covariant equivalence in `SSet/K^▷`; it is a weak homotopy equivalence (3.3.4.5). Consequently, if `p : K ⟶ S` classifies the left fibration `K̃ ⟶ K` and X is a colimit of p, then `K̃ ≅ X` in H (3.3.4.6): the colimit is the weak homotopy type of the total space.

*Parts.* Proposition 3.3.4.5 is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.3.3.4.5/weak` (covariant equivalence over the cone and weak homotopy equivalence), `HTT.3.3.4.5/cofinal` (reduction to the nerve of a category) and `HTT.3.3.4.5/strict` (the strict case), and the target `HTT.3.3.4.5`, which rectifies the diagram and combines the parts.

**Checks.** For p constant at the point, `K̃ = K`, so the colimit of the constant point diagram is the weak homotopy type of K.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. The equivalence of the last two conditions is `HTT.3.3.4.5/weak`. For the first two, choose a small category C and a cofinal map `N(C) ⟶ K` (4.2.3.14), reduce to `K = N(C)` by `HTT.3.3.4.5/cofinal`, rectify p̄ to the nerve of a projectively fibrant diagram `C^▷ ⥤ Kan` (4.2.4.4; Lurie cites 4.2.4.7), and apply `HTT.3.3.4.5/strict`.

*Needs:* `HTT.3.3.4.5/weak`, `HTT.3.3.4.5/cofinal`, `HTT.3.3.4.5/strict` (below); 4.2.3.14; 4.2.4.4 (L5.7; Lurie cites 4.2.4.7 for the strict diagram `C → Kan`); `SSet.Over.IsCovariantEquivalence` (L2.6); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

**Covariant equivalence over the cone and weak homotopy equivalence** (`HTT.3.3.4.5/weak`, part 1 of 3 of Proposition 3.3.4.5 in colimits in `S` above; HTT Proposition 3.3.4.5, (2) ⇔ (3), PDF p. 238). In the setting of 3.3.4.5, the inclusion `X ⊆ X̄` is a covariant equivalence over `K^▷` exactly when it is a weak homotopy equivalence.

*Proof route.* Lurie's.

1. Factor `X ⟶ K^▷` as a left anodyne map `X ⟶ Y` followed by a left fibration with `X ≅ Y ×_{K^▷} K`, and lift to `q : Y ⟶ X̄`.
2. The covariant condition holds exactly when `q_v` is an equivalence at the cone point v (2.2.3.13).
3. The inclusions of the fibres over v are right anodyne (4.1.2.15), hence weak homotopy equivalences.

*Needs:* 2.1.4.7 (L2.6); 2.2.3.13 (L2.8); 4.1.2.15 (L5.3); A.1.2.5 (F1.1); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences` (F2.4).

**Reduction of colimits in `S` to the nerve of a category** (`HTT.3.3.4.5/cofinal`, part 2 of 3 of Proposition 3.3.4.5 in colimits in `S` above; HTT Proposition 3.3.4.5, first step of the proof of (1) ⇔ (2), PDF p. 238). Let C be a small category, `r : N(C) ⟶ K` a cofinal map, and `C^▷ = C ⋆ [0]`. Then p̄ satisfies the first condition of 3.3.4.5 exactly when its restriction along `N(C^▷) ⟶ K^▷` does, and likewise for the second.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. The first condition is invariant by 4.1.1.8; the second, in the form of `HTT.3.3.4.5/weak`, because the comparison maps are pullbacks of a cofinal map along the smooth projection, hence cofinal (4.1.2.15) and so weak homotopy equivalences (4.1.1.3).

*Needs:* `HTT.3.3.4.5/weak`; 4.1.1.3, 4.1.1.8 (L5.2); 4.1.2.15 (L5.3).

**Colimits in `S` of strict diagrams** (`HTT.3.3.4.5/strict`, part 3 of 3 of Proposition 3.3.4.5 in colimits in `S` above; HTT Proposition 3.3.4.5, proof of (1) ⇔ (2), PDF p. 239). Let C be a small category, `F : C^▷ ⥤ Kan` a projectively fibrant diagram, and `X̄^op = Un_φ F`. Then `N(F)` is a colimit diagram in `S` exactly when `X ⊆ X̄` is a covariant equivalence over `N(C^▷)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, as for `HTT.3.3.4.2/strict`, with the right derived unstraightenings of 2.2.1.2 in place of 3.2.0.1: by 4.2.4.1 the colimit condition is membership in the essential image of the derived left adjoint of restriction along `C ⊆ C^▷`, which is fully faithful (4.3.2.15 through 4.2.4.4).

*Needs:* 2.2.1.2, 2.2.3.11 (L2.8); 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4 (L5.7); 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); `HTT.A.2.8.2/projective` (F3.2); `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful` (L1.5).

### L5.2 Cofinal maps

**Cofinal maps** (`SSet.IsCofinal`; HTT Definition 4.1.1.1, PDF p. 241). A map `p : S ⟶ T` of simplicial sets is cofinal when, for every right fibration `X ⟶ T`, restriction of sections `Map_T(T, X) ⟶ Map_T(S, X)` is a homotopy equivalence. Both section spaces are Kan complexes (HTT Remark 4.1.1.2, a lemma here): `Map_T(S, X)` is the fibre of the right fibration `Fun(S, X) ⟶ Fun(S, T)` over p.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsCofinal p` for any `p : S ⟶ T` in `SSet.{u}`: `∀ (X : SSet.{u}) (q : X ⟶ T) [SSet.RightFibration q], SSet.IsHomotopyEquivalence (sectionsRestrict p q)`, where `SSet.sectionsRestrict p q : Map_T(T, X) ⟶ Map_T(S, X)` (propose) is precomposition with p, both sides the fibres of `Fun(−, X) ⟶ Fun(−, T)` over `𝟙 T` and p. Right fibrations in the same universe u; no hypothesis on T. Target `SSet.isCofinal_uliftFunctor_iff`: `IsCofinal p ↔ IsCofinal (SSet.uliftFunctor.map p)`, so testing against right fibrations in `SSet.{u}` suffices. Theorem A (L5.4) is the characterization over an ∞-category.

**Checks.**

- The inclusion of the last vertex `Δ[0] ⟶ Δ[n]` is cofinal; the inclusion of the first vertex is not, for n ≥ 1.
- An isomorphism is cofinal.
- A map to `Δ[0]` is cofinal exactly when its source is weakly contractible (4.1.2.6).

*Needs:* 2.0.0.3 (L2.1, `SSet.RightFibration`); `HTT.A.2.7/kan-fibrations`.

**First properties** (HTT Proposition 4.1.1.3, PDF p. 241). Isomorphisms are cofinal. If `f : K ⟶ K'` is cofinal, then `g : K' ⟶ K''` is cofinal exactly when `g ∘ f` is. Cofinal maps are weak homotopy equivalences. A monomorphism is cofinal exactly when it is right anodyne.

*Needs:* 4.1.1.1; right anodyne maps and their pushout-products with monomorphisms (L2.4); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

**Two models of the space of cones** (HTT Lemma 4.1.1.5, PDF p. 242; Remark 4.1.1.6, PDF p. 243). For an ∞-category C and diagrams `p : K ⟶ C`, `q : K' ⟶ C`, let M parametrize maps `(X × K) ⋆ K' ⟶ C` restricting to `p ∘ π_K` and q, and N maps `K ⋆ (X × K') ⟶ C` restricting to p and `q ∘ π_{K'}`. Then M and N are Kan complexes, naturally homotopy equivalent (4.1.1.5). The equivalence is a zigzag of weak homotopy equivalences through `|M|_Q`, the mapping space of `C[D]` and `|N|_Q`, natural in `(C, p, q)` (4.1.1.6).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: identify both with mapping spaces of `C[−]` of a join, through straightening over a point (2.2.2.7) and 2.2.4.1.

*Needs:* 1.2.2.3, 2.1.2.3, 2.1.2.7, 2.2.2.7, 2.2.4.1 (L2.2–L2.4, L2.8); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

**Cofinal maps and undercategories** (HTT Proposition 4.1.1.7, PDF p. 244). For `v : K' ⟶ K` cofinal and `p : K ⟶ C` a diagram in an ∞-category, `C_{p/} ⟶ C_{pv/}` is an equivalence of left fibrations over C: it is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes on the fibre over every object.

*Needs:* 4.1.1.1, 4.1.1.5–4.1.1.6.

**Cofinality through colimits** (HTT Proposition 4.1.1.8, PDF p. 244). For a map `v : K' ⟶ K` of small simplicial sets, the following are equivalent: v is cofinal; for every ∞-category C and `p : K ⟶ C`, `C_{p/} ⟶ C_{pv/}` is an equivalence of ∞-categories; for every ∞-category C, restriction along `v^▷` carries colimit diagrams `K^▷ ⟶ C` to colimit diagrams.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. (1) ⇒ (2) by 4.1.1.7 and 2.4.4.4; (2) ⇒ (3) since equivalences preserve initial objects. (3) ⇒ (1) classifies a right fibration over K by a map to `S^op` (3.3.2.8), takes a colimit in `S^op` (4.2.4.8: `S` has small limits) and compares section spaces with undercategories through 4.1.1.5. State the implications separately: 4.2.3.14 and 4.1.1.9 use (2) ⇒ (1), so 4.2.4.8 must be proved first, by the route given there.

*Needs:* 4.1.1.5, 4.1.1.7; 2.4.4.4 (L3.7); 3.3.2.8 (L5.1); 4.2.4.8 (L5.7); `HTT.1.2.12/final`, 1.2.16.1.

**Invariance** (HTT Corollaries 4.1.1.9–4.1.1.10, PDF p. 245). If `q : K' ⟶ K''` is a categorical equivalence, then `p : K ⟶ K'` is cofinal exactly when `q ∘ p` is; in particular categorical equivalences are cofinal (4.1.1.9). Cofinality depends only on the class of a map in the homotopy category of the Joyal model structure (4.1.1.10).

*Proof route.* 4.1.1.9 uses that `C_{r/} ⟶ C_{rq/}` is a categorical equivalence for a categorical equivalence q, which Lurie leaves unproved; it follows from the fat slices of L5.5 (4.2.1.3, 4.2.1.5) and the invariance of `Fun(−, C)` (1.2.7.3, L3.2). 4.1.1.10 uses a cylinder object for the Joyal model structure.

*Needs:* 4.1.1.3, 4.1.1.8; 4.2.1.3, 4.2.1.5 (L5.5); 1.2.7.3 (L3.2); 2.2.5.1 (L3.8).

**Cofinal right fibrations; factorization** (HTT Corollaries 4.1.1.11–4.1.1.12, PDF pp. 245–246). A right fibration is cofinal exactly when it is a trivial fibration (4.1.1.11). A map is cofinal exactly when it factors as a right anodyne map followed by a trivial fibration (4.1.1.12).

*Needs:* 4.1.1.3, 4.1.1.9; 2.1.3.4 (L2.4, dual); A.1.2.5 (F1.1, small object argument).

**Products** (HTT Corollary 4.1.1.13, PDF p. 246). If `p : S ⟶ S'` is cofinal, so is `K × S ⟶ K × S'` for every simplicial set K.

*Needs:* 4.1.1.12; products of right anodyne maps with simplicial sets (L2.4).

### L5.3 Right anodyne maps and smooth maps

**Right anodyne maps are the contravariant trivial cofibrations** (HTT Proposition 4.1.2.1, PDF p. 246). For `i : A ⟶ B` the following are equivalent: i is right anodyne; for every `B ⟶ C`, i is a trivial cofibration of the contravariant model structure on `SSet/C`; i is one over B.

*Needs:* 2.1.4.9, `HTT.2.1.4.8/after`, 2.2.3.12 (L2.6, L2.8).

**Cancellation, pushouts and filtered colimits** (HTT Corollaries 4.1.2.2–4.1.2.4, PDF pp. 247–248). For `A ⟶ B ⟶ C` with i and `j ∘ i` right anodyne and j a monomorphism, j is right anodyne (4.1.2.2). Given right anodyne maps `f' : A' ⟶ B'`, `f : A ⟶ B`, `f'' : A'' ⟶ B''` compatible with spans `A' ⟵ A ⟶ A''` and `B' ⟵ B ⟶ B''` whose left legs are monomorphisms, the induced map of pushouts `A' ⊔_A A'' ⟶ B' ⊔_B B''` is right anodyne (4.1.2.3). Right anodyne maps are stable under filtered colimits (4.1.2.4).

*Needs:* 4.1.2.1; pushouts and filtered colimits of contravariant equivalences (L2.6).

**Cofinal maps are the contravariant equivalences** (HTT Proposition 4.1.2.5, Corollaries 4.1.2.6–4.1.2.7, PDF p. 248). For `i : A ⟶ B` the following are equivalent: i is cofinal; for every `B ⟶ C`, i is a contravariant equivalence in `SSet/C`; it is one over B (4.1.2.5). A map to a Kan complex is cofinal exactly when it is a weak homotopy equivalence (4.1.2.6). Cofinal maps are stable under pushout along any map, provided that the cofinal map or the other map is a monomorphism (4.1.2.7).

*Needs:* 4.1.1.12, 4.1.2.1; 3.1.5.7 (L4.3); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

**Smooth maps** (`SSet.IsSmooth`; HTT Proposition 4.1.2.8, PDF p. 249; Definition 4.1.2.9, PDF p. 250). For `p : X ⟶ Y` the following are equivalent:

1. for every right anodyne map `A ⟶ B` over Y, `A ×_Y X ⟶ B ×_Y X` is right anodyne;
2. for every pullback `X' = X ×_Y Y'`, pullback `p'^* : SSet/Y' ⥤ SSet/X'` preserves contravariant equivalences;
3. for every such pullback, `(p'^*, p'_*)`, with the pullback `p'^*` as left adjoint, is a Quillen adjunction of the contravariant model structures.

p is smooth when these hold.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsSmooth p` for any `p : X ⟶ Y`: for every `B ⟶ Y` and every right anodyne `i : A ⟶ B`, the map `pullback.map … : A ×_Y X ⟶ B ×_Y X` is right anodyne (condition (1)). Conditions (2) and (3) are `iff` lemmas (4.1.2.8).

**Checks.**

- Identities and isomorphisms are smooth.
- Smooth maps are stable under base change (from (1)).
- Left fibrations are smooth (4.1.2.15).

*Needs:* 4.1.2.1; `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions` (F1.5).

**Smooth base change of cofinal maps; the base-change transformation** (HTT Remark 4.1.2.10, Proposition 4.1.2.11, PDF p. 250). In a pullback square along a smooth p, the pullback of a cofinal map is cofinal (4.1.2.10). For a pullback square `X' = X ×_Y Y'` with `q : Y' ⟶ Y`, the base-change transformation `ψ_{p,q} : L q'_! R p'^* ⟶ R p^* L q_!` of derived functors between the homotopy categories of the contravariant model structures is defined, and p is smooth exactly when `ψ_{p', q}` is an isomorphism for every pasted pair of pullback squares over `Y'' ⟶ Y' ⟶ Y` (4.1.2.11).

*Needs:* 4.1.2.5, 4.1.2.8–4.1.2.9; `HTT.2.1.4.8/after`; A.2.5.1 (F1.5, derived functors).

**Pushouts and filtered colimits of smooth maps** (HTT Propositions 4.1.2.13, PDF p. 251, and 4.1.2.14, PDF p. 252). If `X ⟶ X'` is a monomorphism, `X ⟶ X''` any map, all over S, and the three maps to S are smooth, then `X' ⊔_X X'' ⟶ S` is smooth (4.1.2.13). Smooth maps to S are stable under filtered colimits in `SSet/S` (4.1.2.14).

*Needs:* 4.1.2.3, 4.1.2.4, 4.1.2.8–4.1.2.9.

**CoCartesian fibrations are smooth** (HTT Proposition 4.1.2.15, PDF p. 252). Every coCartesian fibration of simplicial sets is smooth; in particular every left fibration is.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: reduce to a simplex base and use the mapping simplex of 3.2.2.7.

*Needs:* 4.1.1.3, 4.1.1.9 (L5.2); 4.1.2.3, 4.1.2.4, 4.1.2.9; 2.4.2.1 (L3.6); 3.2.2.7, `HTT.3.2.2/intro` (L4.5).

**Bifibrations** (HTT Proposition 4.1.2.16, PDF p. 252). For a bifibration `p : X ⟶ S × T` (2.4.7.2), the composite `π_S ∘ p : X ⟶ S` is smooth.

*Needs:* 2.4.7.2, 2.4.7.5 (L3.9); 4.1.2.13–4.1.2.15.

**Covariant equivalences through overcategories** (HTT Lemma 4.1.2.17, Proposition 4.1.2.18, PDF pp. 252–253). For an ∞-category C, an object c and a covariant equivalence `X ⟶ Y` in `SSet/C`, the map `X ×_C C_{/c} ⟶ Y ×_C C_{/c}` is a covariant equivalence over `C_{/c}` (4.1.2.17). For `f : X ⟶ Y` over C with both structure maps smooth, f is a covariant equivalence exactly when every map of fibres `X_c ⟶ Y_c` is a weak homotopy equivalence (4.1.2.18).

*Needs:* 4.1.2.5, 4.1.2.9, 4.1.2.15; 2.2.3.12 (L2.8); `HTT.2.1.4.8/after`; `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

### L5.4 Joyal's Theorem A

**Cartesian fibrations with weakly contractible fibres** (HTT Lemma 4.1.3.2, PDF p. 254). A Cartesian fibration `U ⟶ S` all of whose fibres are weakly contractible is cofinal.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: induction over the simplices of the base, reducing to `S = Δ[n]`, where 3.2.2.7 replaces U by a mapping simplex.

*Needs:* 4.1.1.1; 2.4.2.1; 3.2.2.7, 3.3.1.7 (L4.5, L4.7); `HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration` (L3.8); `SSet.IsWeaklyContractible` (F2.4).

**Theorem A** (`SSet.isCofinal_iff_isWeaklyContractible`; HTT Theorem 4.1.3.1, PDF p. 254; Kerodon Theorem 7.2.3.1). For a map `f : C ⟶ D` of simplicial sets with D an ∞-category, f is cofinal exactly when `C ×_D D_{d/}` is weakly contractible for every object d of D. It is an `iff` over an ∞-category target.

**Checks.**

- The inclusion of a final object `Δ[0] ⟶ D` is cofinal.
- For a functor F of ordinary categories with a left adjoint, `N(F)` is cofinal: each `d ↓ F` has an initial object.
- If `N(F)` is cofinal, F is final in Mathlib's sense (`Functor.Final`); the converse fails, since Mathlib's condition asks only for connected comma categories.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Reduce to C an ∞-category (4.1.1.10, 3.3.1.3). (1) ⇒ (2): `D_{d/} ⟶ D` is a left fibration, hence smooth (4.1.2.15), so `C ×_D D_{d/} ⟶ D_{d/}` is cofinal (4.1.2.10), hence a weak homotopy equivalence (4.1.1.3), and `D_{d/}` has an initial object. (2) ⇒ (1): factor f through `Fun(Δ[1], D) ×_D C`; the first map is right anodyne (2.1.2.11), the second a Cartesian fibration (2.4.7.12) whose fibres are the fat versions of `C ×_D D_{d/}` (4.2.1.5), and apply 4.1.3.2.

*Needs:* 4.1.1.3, 4.1.1.10; 4.1.2.10, 4.1.2.15; 4.1.3.2; 4.2.1.5 (L5.5); 2.1.2.11 (L2.4); 2.4.7.12 (L3.9); 3.3.1.3 (L4.7); `SSet.IsWeaklyContractible`, `SSet.coslice`.

**Quillen's Theorem A** (HTT Corollary 4.1.3.3, PDF p. 256). For a functor `f : C ⥤ D` of ordinary categories such that every `C ×_D D_{d/}` has weakly contractible nerve, `N(f)` is a weak homotopy equivalence.

*Needs:* 4.1.1.3, 4.1.3.1; `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

### L5.5 Fat joins and morphism spaces

**The fat join** (`SSet.fatJoin`; HTT Definition 4.2.1.1, PDF p. 257). For simplicial sets X and Y, `X ⋄ Y` is the pushout `X ⊔_{X × Y × {0}} (X × Y × Δ[1]) ⊔_{X × Y × {1}} Y`. It maps to `Δ[1]` with fibres X and Y, and there is a unique map `X ⋄ Y ⟶ X ⋆ Y` over `Δ[1]` that is the identity on X and Y. Since the pushout is a homotopy pushout for the Joyal model structure, categorical equivalences `X ⟶ X'`, `Y ⟶ Y'` induce a categorical equivalence `X ⋄ Y ⟶ X' ⋄ Y'`.

*Lean:* `SSet.fatJoin X Y : SSet` as the iterated pushout above, with `SSet.fatJoin.toΔ1`, the inclusions of X and Y, and `SSet.fatJoin.toJoin : X ⋄ Y ⟶ X ⋆ Y` over `Δ[1]`.

**Checks.**

- `Δ[0] ⋄ Δ[0] ≅ Δ[1]`, and `fatJoin.toJoin` is then an isomorphism.
- `∅ ⋄ Y ≅ Y` and `X ⋄ ∅ ≅ X`.

*Needs:* Tau Ceti `SSet.join`; `HTT.A.2.4.3/after`, A.2.4.4 (F1.5, homotopy pushouts); 2.2.5.1 (L3.8).

**Fat join and join agree** (HTT Proposition 4.2.1.2, Corollaries 4.2.1.3–4.2.1.4, PDF p. 258). `X ⋄ Y ⟶ X ⋆ Y` is a categorical equivalence for all simplicial sets X, Y (4.2.1.2). Hence joins preserve categorical equivalences (4.2.1.3), and `C[X ⋆ Y] ⟶ C[X] ⋆ C[Y]` is a Dwyer–Kan equivalence of simplicial categories (4.2.1.4).

*Proof route.* Lurie's; reduce to `X, Y ∈ {Δ[0], Δ[1]}` through spine inclusions, which are inner anodyne. In 4.2.1.4 Lurie computes the mapping spaces of `C[X ⋆ Y]` through Theorem 1.1.5.13, which is out of scope; use its simplicial form 2.2.4.1 (L2.8), comparing with `Hom^R_{X ⋆ Y}(x, y) = Δ[0]`.

*Needs:* 4.2.1.1; 2.2.5.2 (L2.7); 2.2.4.1; 2.3.1.3 (L3.1, correspondences); Tau Ceti `SSet.join`.

**The fat slice** (`SSet.fatCoslice`; HTT Proposition 4.2.1.5, PDF p. 259). For `p : X ⟶ C`, the fat slice `C^{p/}` represents maps `X ⋄ Y ⟶ C` extending p; concretely it is `Fun(X × Δ[1], C) ×_{Fun(X × ∂Δ[1], C)} ({p} × C)`, with C mapping to `Fun(X, C)` by constant diagrams. `fatJoin.toJoin` induces `C_{p/} ⟶ C^{p/}`, an equivalence of ∞-categories when C is an ∞-category (4.2.1.5). Consequently colimits may be computed in `C^{p/}`.

*Lean:* `SSet.fatCoslice p` defined by the fibre product above, with its representing property; dually `SSet.fatSlice`.

*Needs:* 4.2.1.2; 2.1.2.1 (L2.3); Tau Ceti `SSet.coslice`.

**Fat slices are left fibrations** (HTT Proposition 4.2.1.6, PDF p. 259). For `K₀ ⊆ K ⟶ X ⟶ S` with `q : X ⟶ S` a categorical fibration, `r = q ∘ p`, `p₀ = p|K₀`, `r₀ = r|K₀`, the map `X^{p/} ⟶ X^{p₀/} ×_{S^{r₀/}} S^{r/}` is a left fibration.

*Needs:* 4.2.1.5; 2.1.2.3 (L2.3); `HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration` (L3.8).

**Fibres of fat slices; the morphism spaces agree** (HTT Corollaries 4.2.1.7–4.2.1.8, PDF p. 260). For an ∞-category C, `p : K ⟶ C` and a vertex v, `C_{p/} ×_C {v} ⟶ C^{p/} ×_C {v}` is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes (4.2.1.7). Hence `Hom^R_C(x, y) ⟶ Hom_C(x, y) ⟵ Hom^L_C(x, y)` are homotopy equivalences (4.2.1.8). 4.2.1.8 is the comparison that makes L1.5's `Hom_C` agree with Tau Ceti's `SSet.rightMappingSpace`.

*Lean (4.2.1.8):* `SSet.morphismSpace_pinch_isHomotopyEquivalence C x y : IsHomotopyEquivalence (rightMappingSpace.toMorphismSpace C x y) ∧ IsHomotopyEquivalence (leftMappingSpace.toMorphismSpace C x y)` for `[Quasicategory C]`, with the pinch inclusions of L1.5.

*Proof route.* Lurie's for 4.2.1.2–4.2.1.6, and for 4.2.1.8 through 4.2.1.7, with one substitution in 4.2.1.7: Lurie concludes with the fibrewise criterion 3.3.1.5, whose proof uses straightening, but only its easy direction is needed. An equivalence between left fibrations over C restricts to equivalences of fibres, because fibres of categorical fibrations between ∞-categories are homotopy pullbacks in the Joyal model structure (2.2.5.1, 2.4.6.5, and the dual of A.2.4.4). This is Kerodon's argument (Proposition 4.6.5.10 through Corollary 4.5.3.31). With it, 4.2.1.8 needs the Joyal model structure (L3.8) and §4.2.1's fat joins, but not straightening, so it can be formalized right after L3.8.

*Needs:* 4.2.1.5–4.2.1.6; 2.2.5.1, 2.4.6.5 (L3.8); A.2.4.4 (F1.5); `HTT.1.2.2/morphism-space`.

**Fully faithful maps through `Hom_C`** (Kerodon 4.8.3.1, characterization of HTT 1.2.10.1). For ∞-categories, f is fully faithful (L1.5) exactly when the maps `Hom_C(x, y) ⟶ Hom_C(fx, fy)` are homotopy equivalences: the `Hom^R` form of L2.8 with 4.2.1.8.

*Lean:* `SSet.isFullyFaithful_iff_morphismSpace`, with `SSet.morphismSpace.map f x y` (L1.5).

*Needs:* `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`, its `Hom^R` characterization (L2.8), 4.2.1.8.

### L5.6 Colimits in families; decomposing diagrams

**The relative fat join and relative slices** (`SSet.Over.fibreJoin`; HTT Definition 4.2.2.1, PDF p. 260). For X, Y in `SSet/S`, `X ⋄_S Y` is the pushout `X ⊔_{X ×_S Y × {0}} (X ×_S Y × Δ[1]) ⊔_{X ×_S Y × {1}} Y` over S. It commutes with base change along `T ⟶ S`, and over a point it is the fat join. For K in `SSet/S`, `X ↦ K ⋄_S X` has a right adjoint: for `p_S : K ⟶ Y` over S, the relative slice `Y^{p_S/}` over S, whose maps from X over S classify extensions of `p_S` to `K ⋄_S X ⟶ Y` over S. Its fibre over a vertex s is the fat slice `Y_s^{p_s/}`.

*Lean:* `SSet.Over.fibreJoin X Y : SSet/S` as the pushout above, and `SSet.Over.fatCoslice p_S : SSet/S` with the adjunction `(K ⋄_S −) ⊣ fatCoslice` from `SSet/S` to `(SSet/S)_{K/}`, and the base-change isomorphisms.

**Checks.** For `S = Δ[0]` these are `SSet.fatJoin` and `SSet.fatCoslice`. The fibre of `Y^{p_S/}` over s is `Y_s^{p_s/}`.

*Needs:* 4.2.1.1, 4.2.1.5.

**A lifting lemma for Cartesian fibrations** (HTT Lemma 4.2.2.3, PDF p. 261). Let `n > 0` and `B = (Λ[n, n] × Δ[1]) ⊔ (Δ[n] × ∂Δ[1]) ⊆ Δ[n] × Δ[1]`. For a Cartesian fibration `q : Y ⟶ S`, every map `A × B ⟶ Y` over a given `A × Δ[n] × Δ[1] ⟶ S` that carries each `{a} × Δ^{n−1,n} × {1}` to a q-Cartesian edge extends to `A × Δ[n] × Δ[1]`.

*Needs:* 2.1.2.6 (L2.4); 2.4.1.1, 2.4.2.1 (L3.5–L3.6); 3.1.2.1 (L4.2).

**Relative slices of Cartesian fibrations** (HTT Proposition 4.2.2.4, PDF p. 262). Given `p_S : K ⟶ X` and a Cartesian fibration `q : X ⟶ Y`, all over S, with the structure map `K ⟶ S` a coCartesian fibration, the induced map `X^{p_S/} ⟶ Y^{q p_S/}` is a Cartesian fibration, and an edge of `X^{p_S/}` is Cartesian exactly when its image in X is q-Cartesian.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.4.2.2.4/inner` (the map of relative slices is an inner fibration) and `HTT.4.2.2.4/cartesian` (it is a Cartesian fibration with the stated Cartesian edges, which proves the statement), and this entry's own target `HTT.4.2.2.4`, which collects them.

*Needs:* `HTT.4.2.2.4/inner`, `HTT.4.2.2.4/cartesian` (below); `HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration`.

**Relative slices are inner fibrations** (`HTT.4.2.2.4/inner`, part 1 of 2 of relative slices of Cartesian fibrations above; first step of the proof of HTT Proposition 4.2.2.4, PDF p. 263). In the situation of 4.2.2.4 (q a Cartesian fibration over S, `K ⟶ S` coCartesian), the induced map `r : X^{p_S/} ⟶ Y^{q p_S/}` is an inner fibration.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: by adjunction, an inner horn filler for r is an extension along `K ⋄_S Λ[n, i] ⊆ K ⋄_S Δ[n]` against q, which is a categorical fibration (3.3.1.7). That inclusion is a categorical equivalence because `K ×_S Λ[n, i] ⊆ K ×_S Δ[n]` is one (dual of 3.3.1.3) and the relative fat join is built as a homotopy pushout.

*Needs:* 4.2.2.1; 3.3.1.3, 3.3.1.7 (L4.7).

**Special edges are Cartesian** (`HTT.4.2.2.4/cartesian`, part 2 of 2 of relative slices of Cartesian fibrations above; HTT Proposition 4.2.2.4 and its proof, PDF pp. 262–265). The statement of 4.2.2.4 above.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: call an edge special when its image in X is q-Cartesian. Lifting against `Λ[n, n] ⊆ Δ[n]` with special last edge (and for `n = 1`) is an extension problem for `K ⋄_S Δ[n]`. First extend over a q-Cartesian edge of X; then reduce to `S = Δ[n]`, replace K by a mapping simplex (dual of 3.2.2.7, with A.2.3.1), and conclude by 4.2.2.3.

*Needs:* `HTT.4.2.2.4/inner`; 4.2.2.3; 3.2.2.7 (L4.5); A.2.3.1 (F1.4).

**Fibrewise colimits in a Cartesian fibration** (HTT Proposition 4.2.2.7, PDF p. 265). Let `q : Y ⟶ S` be a Cartesian fibration and `p_S : K ⟶ Y` a map such that each `p_s : K_s ⟶ Y_s` has a colimit and `q ∘ p_S` is a coCartesian fibration. Then `p_S` extends to `K ⋄_S S ⟶ Y` over S restricting on each fibre to a colimit of `p_s`, and the space of such extensions is a contractible Kan complex.

*Needs:* 4.2.2.1, 4.2.2.4; 2.4.4.9 (L3.7).

**The decomposition simplicial set** (`SSet.decompositionCylinder`; HTT Notation 4.2.3.1, PDF p. 266). Fix a simplicial set K, an ordinary category I and `F : I ⥤ SSet/K`, writing `K_I = F(I)` and `π_I : K_I ⟶ K`. An n-simplex of `K_F` is: a splitting `[n] = {0, …, i} ∪ {i+1, …, n}`; a simplex `e₋ : Δ^{0,…,i} ⟶ K`; a chain `I(i+1) ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ I(n)` in I; and lifts `e_j : Δ^{0,…,i} ⟶ K_{I(j)}` of `e₋` for `j > i`, compatible with the maps `K_{I(j)} ⟶ K_{I(k)}`. `K_F` maps to `Δ[1]` with fibres K and `N(I)`, and each `π_I` extends to `K_I^▷ ⟶ K_F` sending the cone point to the vertex I.

*Lean:* `SSet.decompositionCylinder F : SSet` with its simplices as above, `SSet.decompositionCylinder.toΔ1`, the inclusions of K and `N(I)`, and the maps `K_I^▷ ⟶ K_F`.

**Checks.**

- For I the terminal category and `K_I = K`, `K_F ≅ K^▷`.
- For I empty, `K_F ≅ K`.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.nerve`; `SSet.rightCone`.

**Initial vertices and boundaries** (HTT Lemma 4.2.3.3, PDF p. 267). If `σ : Δ[n] ⟶ C` is a simplex of an ∞-category with `σ(0)` initial, then `C_{σ/} ⟶ C_{∂σ/}` is a trivial fibration.

*Needs:* `HTT.1.2.12/final`; Tau Ceti `SSet.coslice`.

**Assembling colimits over a decomposition** (HTT Proposition 4.2.3.4, PDF p. 267). Let `p : K ⟶ C` be a diagram in an ∞-category such that each `p ∘ π_I` has a colimit `q_I : K_I^▷ ⟶ C`. Then there is `q : K_F ⟶ C` restricting to p on K and to `q_I` along each `K_I^▷ ⟶ K_F`, and for every such q the map `C_{q/} ⟶ C_{p/}` is a trivial fibration.

*Needs:* 4.2.3.1, 4.2.3.3; Tau Ceti `SSet.join`, `SSet.coslice`.

**Right anodyne pushout-joins** (HTT Lemmas 4.2.3.5–4.2.3.6, PDF p. 269). For monomorphisms `A₀ ⊆ A` and `B₀ ⊆ B` with `B₀ ⊆ B` a weak homotopy equivalence, `(A₀ ⋆ B) ⊔_{A₀ ⋆ B₀} (A ⋆ B₀) ⊆ A ⋆ B` is right anodyne (4.2.3.5). For B weakly contractible, `A₀ ⋆ B ⊆ A ⋆ B` is right anodyne (4.2.3.6).

*Needs:* 2.1.2.3 (L2.3); A.1.2.2 (F1.1, saturation); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

**When `N(I) ⊆ K_F` is right anodyne** (HTT Proposition 4.2.3.8, PDF p. 270). For a simplex σ of K let `I_σ` be the category of pairs `(I, σ')` with `σ'` an n-simplex of `K_I` over σ, and `I⁰_σ ⊆ I_σ` the full subcategory where `σ'` is degenerate (HTT Notation 4.2.3.7). If `N(I_σ)` is weakly contractible for every nondegenerate σ, and `N(I⁰_σ) ⊆ N(I_σ)` is a weak homotopy equivalence for every degenerate σ, then `N(I) ⊆ K_F` is right anodyne.

*Needs:* 4.2.3.1, 4.2.3.5–4.2.3.6; `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

**Colimits through a decomposition** (HTT Corollary 4.2.3.10, PDF p. 271). Under the hypotheses of 4.2.3.8, for `p : K ⟶ C` and q as in 4.2.3.4, the maps `C_{p/} ⟵ C_{q/} ⟶ C_{q|N(I)/}` are trivial fibrations; so colimits of p are colimits of `q|N(I)`.

*Needs:* 4.2.3.4, 4.2.3.8; 4.1.1.3 (4) (right anodyne inclusions are cofinal), 4.1.1.8.

**κ-small colimits from τ-small and filtered ones** (HTT Corollaries 4.2.3.11–4.2.3.12, PDF p. 271). For regular cardinals `τ ≪ κ` (HTT's relation, defined just before 4.2.3.11: `κ₀^{τ₀} < κ` for all `τ₀ < τ`, `κ₀ < κ`), an ∞-category admits κ-small colimits exactly when it admits τ-small colimits and colimits indexed by nerves of κ-small τ-filtered partially ordered sets (4.2.3.11); a functor out of an ∞-category with κ-small colimits preserves κ-small colimits exactly when it preserves those two kinds (4.2.3.12).

*Lean:* supporting predicates `SSet.HasColimitsOfShape K C` (every `K ⟶ C` has a colimit), `SSet.HasColimitsOfSize κ C` (all κ-small K, as `HasCardinalLT`) and `SSet.PreservesColimit`; for small diagrams, `SSet.HasSmallColimits.{u} (C : SSet.{v}) : Prop := ∀ K : SSet.{u}, SSet.HasColimitsOfShape (uliftFunctor.{v}.obj K) (uliftFunctor.{u}.obj C)` (both lifted to `SSet.{max u v}`; the comparison with colimits in C itself is a lemma), dually `SSet.HasSmallLimits`, and `SSet.PreservesSmallColimits.{u} F` (entries 5.1.5.7, 5.1.6.2, 5.1.6.5, 5.5.0.1, 5.5.4.5, 5.5.5.1 and 5.5.8.23 cite these); `τ ≪ κ` is `Cardinal.PowLT τ κ` (HTT Definition A.2.6.3, F1.6).

*Needs:* 4.2.3.4, 4.2.3.8, 4.2.3.10; A.1.1.1 (F1.1, κ-filtered posets).

**The category of simplices** (HTT Lemma 4.2.3.13, PDF p. 272). For I the category of simplices of K (`Δ[n] ⟶ K`), with `K_I = Δ[n]`, there is a retraction `K_F ⟶ K` fixing K.

*Needs:* 4.2.3.1.

**Every simplicial set receives a cofinal map from a nerve** (HTT Proposition 4.2.3.14, PDF p. 272). For every simplicial set K there are a category I and a cofinal map `N(I) ⟶ K`; one may take I the category of simplices.

**Checks.** For `K = Δ[0]`, I is the simplex category Δ, and `N(Δ) ⟶ Δ[0]` is cofinal because `N(Δ)` has a final object `[0]`, hence is weakly contractible.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `N(I) ⊆ K_F` is right anodyne by 4.2.3.8, and the retraction r of 4.2.3.13 is cofinal by 4.1.1.8 (2) ⇒ (1) with 4.2.3.4.

*Needs:* 4.2.3.4, 4.2.3.8, 4.2.3.13; 4.1.1.8.

**Posets and finite simplicial sets** (HTT Variant 4.2.3.15, PDF p. 273; Variant 4.2.3.16, PDF p. 274). Every simplicial set K receives a cofinal map from the nerve of a partially ordered set, functorially in K (4.2.3.15). If K is finite, the poset may be taken finite, though not functorially (4.2.3.16).

*Parts.* Variant 4.2.3.15 is formalized as five targets: the four parts that follow this entry, `HTT.4.2.3.15/first-vertex` (first objects of chains give a cofinal map), `HTT.4.2.3.15/injective` (injective maps of simplices give a cofinal inclusion), `HTT.4.2.3.15/nondegenerate` (nondegenerate simplices form a cofinal poset) and `HTT.4.2.3.15/assemble` (the composite of the five cofinal maps, which proves 4.2.3.15), and this entry's own target `HTT.4.2.3.15`, which collects them; 4.2.3.16 is a separate target.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: 4.2.3.15 composes five cofinal maps, two from 4.2.3.14 and three from `HTT.4.2.3.15/first-vertex`, `HTT.4.2.3.15/injective` and `HTT.4.2.3.15/nondegenerate` (which use Theorem A, 4.1.2.15 and HTT Lemma 6.5.3.7). 4.2.3.16 inducts on nondegenerate simplices with 4.1.2.7.

*Needs:* `HTT.4.2.3.15/first-vertex`, `HTT.4.2.3.15/injective`, `HTT.4.2.3.15/nondegenerate`, `HTT.4.2.3.15/assemble` (below); for 4.2.3.16: 4.2.3.14; 4.1.2.7; 4.1.3.1 (L5.4).

**First objects of chains** (`HTT.4.2.3.15/first-vertex`, part 1 of 4 of posets and finite simplicial sets above; step (2) of HTT Variant 4.2.3.15, PDF p. 273). For a small category I, let `I'` be the category of simplices of `N(I)`. Sending a chain `C₀ ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ Cₙ` to `C₀` is a functor `I'^op ⥤ I` (a map of simplices `σ ⟶ τ` gives the edge from the first object of τ to that of σ), and its nerve `N(I')^op ⟶ N(I)` is cofinal. Lurie's text writes the functor as `I' ⥤ I`; the target reads it as `I'^op ⥤ I`.

*Proof route.* By Theorem A (4.1.3.1) it suffices that each comma category has weakly contractible nerve. That comma category is the opposite of the simplex category of `N(I)_{C/}`, which 4.2.3.14 makes weakly equivalent to `N(I)_{C/}`, contractible since it has an initial object.

*Needs:* 4.2.3.14; 4.1.1.3 (L5.2); 4.1.3.1 (L5.4).

**Injective maps of simplices** (`HTT.4.2.3.15/injective`, part 2 of 4 of posets and finite simplicial sets above; step (3) of HTT Variant 4.2.3.15, PDF p. 273). For a simplicial set L with simplex category `I_L`, let `I_L^s ⊆ I_L` be the subcategory of maps whose underlying map in Δ is injective. Then `N(I_L^s)^op ⊆ N(I_L)^op` is cofinal.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: both are left fibrations over `N(Δ_s)^op ⊆ N(Δ)^op`, with the square a pullback. Left fibrations are smooth (4.1.2.15), and the base inclusion is cofinal (6.5.3.7).

*Needs:* 6.5.3.7 (L5.7); 4.1.2.10, 4.1.2.15 (L5.3).

**Nondegenerate simplices form a poset** (`HTT.4.2.3.15/nondegenerate`, part 3 of 4 of posets and finite simplicial sets above; step (5) of HTT Variant 4.2.3.15, PDF p. 274). Let L be a simplicial set whose simplex category has its non-identity morphisms closed under composition. Then every face of a nondegenerate simplex of L is nondegenerate, and the full subcategory of the simplex category of L on the nondegenerate simplices is reflective (so its nerve inclusion is cofinal, by Theorem A) and equivalent to a partially ordered set.

*Needs:* 4.1.3.1 (L5.4).

**Five cofinal maps** (`HTT.4.2.3.15/assemble`, part 4 of 4 of posets and finite simplicial sets above; HTT Variant 4.2.3.15, PDF pp. 273–274). The statement of 4.2.3.15 above: every simplicial set K receives a cofinal map from the nerve of a partially ordered set, functorially in K.

*Proof route.* Compose 4.2.3.14 (twice) with `HTT.4.2.3.15/first-vertex`, `HTT.4.2.3.15/injective` and `HTT.4.2.3.15/nondegenerate`; each step is functorial in K.

*Needs:* `HTT.4.2.3.15/first-vertex`, `HTT.4.2.3.15/injective`, `HTT.4.2.3.15/nondegenerate`; 4.2.3.14.

### L5.7 Homotopy colimits and ∞-categorical colimits

**Semisimplicial indexing is cofinal** (HTT Lemma 6.5.3.7, PDF p. 694; stated in §6.5.3, placed here). Here `Δ_s ⊆ Δ` is the wide subcategory of injective order-preserving maps. The inclusion `N(Δ_s^op) ⊆ N(Δ^op)` is cofinal.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: by Theorem A (4.1.3.1) it suffices that each category `Δ_s ×_Δ Δ_{/[n]}` has weakly contractible nerve; the constant functor at `[0] ⊆ [n]` and the functor adjoining an initial `[0]` give natural transformations joining the identity to a constant functor.

*Needs:* 4.1.1.1, 4.1.3.1; `SimplexCategory.inj` (the injective maps of `SimplexCategory`, defined here).

**Colimits through morphism spaces** (HTT Lemma 4.2.4.3, PDF p. 275). For `p̄ : K^▷ ⟶ C` in an ∞-category with cone point X, `δ : C ⟶ Fun(K, C)` the diagonal and `α : p ⟶ δ(X)` the induced transformation, p̄ is a colimit of `p = p̄|K` exactly when composition with α gives homotopy equivalences `Map_C(X, Y) ⟶ Map_{Fun(K, C)}(p, δ(Y))` for all Y.

*Needs:* 4.2.1.6, 4.2.1.8 (L5.5); 2.1.3.3–2.1.3.4 (L2.4); 1.2.7.2.

**Diagrams in a combinatorial simplicial model category** (HTT Proposition 4.2.4.4, PDF p. 276). For a small simplicial set S, a small simplicial category C, a Dwyer–Kan equivalence `u : C[S] ⟶ C`, a combinatorial simplicial model category A and a C-chunk U of A (A.3.4.9), the induced map `N((U^C)°) ⟶ Fun(S, N(U°))` is a categorical equivalence.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: write U as a filtered colimit of small chunks (A.3.4.15), identify `Fun(S, N(U°))` as an exponential in the homotopy category of the Joyal model structure through 2.2.5.1, and apply A.3.4.14.

*Needs:* A.3.4.9, A.3.4.14, A.3.4.15 (F3.6); A.3.1.5 (F3.1); A.2.6.1 (F1.6); 2.2.5.1 (L3.8).

**Homotopy colimits are ∞-categorical colimits** (HTT Theorem 4.2.4.1, PDF p. 275). Let C and I be locally Kan simplicial categories, `F : I ⥤ C` a simplicial functor, and `η_I : F(I) ⟶ C` a compatible family of maps to an object c of C. Then the `η_I` exhibit c as a homotopy colimit of F (HTT Remark A.3.3.13, F3.5) exactly when the extension `N(I)^▷ ⟶ N(C)` of `N(F)` determined by the `η_I` is a colimit diagram.

*Lean:* `SSet.simplicialCategory_isHomotopyColimit_iff`, for C and I locally Kan (`HomotopicalAlgebra.EnrichedCategory.IsLocallyFibrant SSet`), `F : EnrichedDiagram SSet I C` and the compatible family as a cocone `η : F ⟶ SimplicialCategory.constDiagram I c`: `SimplicialCategory.IsHomotopyColimit F η ↔ IsColimitDiagram (SimplicialCategory.nerveCocone F η)`, where `SimplicialCategory.nerveCocone F η : rightCone (SimplicialNerve I) ⟶ SimplicialNerve C` is the extension of `N(F)` determined by η (propose).

**Checks.** For I empty, both conditions say that c is initial: homotopy initial in C, initial in `N(C)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, through 4.2.4.3 and 4.2.4.4 (A.3.4.9) and L2.8. It is the bridge between model categories and ∞-categories used throughout L5–L8 and HA §1.3.4.

*Needs:* 4.2.4.3, 4.2.4.4; A.2.8.1, `HTT.A.2.8.2/injective`, `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3.2); 1.2.13.5 (L2.5); 1.1.5.5.

**Rectification of diagrams** (HTT Corollary 4.2.4.7, PDF p. 276). For a locally Kan simplicial category I, a simplicial set S and `p : N(I) ⟶ S`, there are a locally Kan simplicial category C, a simplicial functor `P : I ⥤ C`, a categorical equivalence `j : S ⟶ N(C)`, and an equivalence between `j ∘ p` and `N(P)` in `Fun(N(I), N(C))`.

*Needs:* 4.2.4.4; A.2.8.2; `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`.

**Limits and colimits in `N(A°)`** (HTT Corollary 4.2.4.8, PDF p. 278). For a combinatorial simplicial model category A, the ∞-category `N(A°)` admits small limits and colimits. In particular `S` and `Cat∞` do.

*Proof route.* Lurie reduces to diagrams indexed by `N(I)` through 4.2.3.14, which depends on 4.1.1.8, which uses this corollary; avoid the cycle. Given `p : K ⟶ N(A°)`, choose a locally Kan replacement `C[K] ⟶ I` with adjoint categorical equivalence `j : K ⟶ N(I)` (L2.8, L3.8). By 4.2.4.4 with `S = K` and `C = I`, p is equivalent to `N(F) ∘ j` for an injectively fibrant `F : I ⥤ A°`. A homotopy colimit of F exists in A, and gives a colimit diagram `N(I)^▷ ⟶ N(A°)` by 4.2.4.1. Restriction along the categorical equivalence j preserves colimits, since `C_{q/} ⟶ C_{qj/}` is a categorical equivalence by the fat-slice description (4.2.1.5) and the invariance of `Fun(−, C)` (1.2.7.3). Limits are dual.

*Needs:* 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4; 4.2.1.5; 1.2.7.3 (L3.2); 2.2.0.1, 2.2.5.1 (L2.8, L3.8); A.2.6.1, A.3.1.5, A.2.8.2.

### L5.8 Relative colimits

**Relative colimits** (`SSet.IsRelColimit`; HTT Definition 4.3.1.1, PDF p. 279). For an inner fibration `f : C ⟶ D` of simplicial sets and `p̄ : K^▷ ⟶ C` with `p = p̄|K`, p̄ is an f-colimit of p when `C_{p̄/} ⟶ C_{p/} ×_{D_{fp/}} D_{fp̄/}` is a trivial fibration.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsRelColimit f p̄` for `f : C ⟶ D` with `[SSet.InnerFibration f]` and `p̄ : K.rightCone ⟶ C`: the canonical map `C_{p̄/} ⟶ C_{p/} ×_{D_{fp/}} D_{fp̄/}` has the right lifting property against every `∂Δ[n] ⟶ Δ[n]`. Dually `SSet.IsRelLimit`. For `D = Δ[0]` it is equivalent to `SSet.IsColimit` (L1.5), through `(C_{p/})_{p̄/} ≅ C_{p̄/}`; state this as a lemma.

**Checks.**

- If f is a trivial fibration, every p̄ is an f-colimit (4.3.1.5).
- For `K = Δ[0]`, f-colimits are the f-coCartesian edges (4.3.1.4).

*Needs:* 2.0.0.3; Mathlib `SSet.InnerFibration`; Tau Ceti `SSet.coslice`; `SSet.IsColimit` (L1.5).

**Categorical equivalence suffices** (HTT Remark 4.3.1.2, PDF p. 279). p̄ is an f-colimit exactly when the map of Definition 4.3.1.1 is a categorical equivalence; equivalently, when `C_{p̄/}` is the homotopy fibre product of `C_{p/}` and `D_{fp̄/}` over `D_{fp/}` for the Joyal model structure.

*Needs:* 4.3.1.1; 2.1.2.1 (L2.3); 3.3.1.3, 3.3.1.7 (L4.7); `HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration`; `HTT.A.2.4.3/after` (F1.5).

**Edges** (HTT Example 4.3.1.4, PDF p. 279). An edge `Δ[1] = Δ[0]^▷ ⟶ C` is an f-colimit exactly when it is f-coCartesian.

*Needs:* 4.3.1.1; `HTT.2.4.1.7/after` (L3.5).

**Stability** (HTT Proposition 4.3.1.5, PDF p. 279). For a trivial fibration f, every diagram is an f-colimit. For inner fibrations `f : C ⟶ D`, `g : D ⟶ E` with `f ∘ p̄` a g-colimit, p̄ is an f-colimit exactly when it is a `(g ∘ f)`-colimit. For an inner fibration of ∞-categories, equivalent diagrams in `Fun(K^▷, C)` are f-colimits together. f-colimits pull back along base change of f.

*Needs:* 4.3.1.1.

**Invariance under equivalence** (HTT Proposition 4.3.1.6, PDF p. 280). Given a square of ∞-categories with inner fibrations `p : C ⟶ D`, `p' : C' ⟶ D'` and categorical equivalences `C ⟶ C'`, `D ⟶ D'`, q̄ is a p-colimit exactly when its image is a p'-colimit.

*Needs:* 4.3.1.2; `HTT.1.2.9.3/2` (L3.8); 3.3.1.3.

**Cofinal reindexing** (HTT Propositions 4.3.1.7–4.3.1.8, PDF p. 281). For an inner fibration `p : C ⟶ D` of ∞-categories, a cofinal `i : A ⟶ B` and `q̄ : B^▷ ⟶ C`, q̄ is a p-colimit exactly when `q̄ ∘ i^▷` is (4.3.1.7). If p is a coCartesian fibration, `q : B ⟶ C`, `q̄' : B^▷ ⟶ D` extends `p ∘ q`, and `q ∘ i` has a p-colimit lifting `q̄' ∘ i^▷`, then q has a p-colimit lifting `q̄'` (4.3.1.8).

*Needs:* 4.1.1.1, 4.1.1.7–4.1.1.8 (L5.2); 4.3.1.2; 2.4.3.1 (L3.6); 3.3.1.3, 3.3.1.5.

**Transport by coCartesian natural transformations** (HTT Proposition 4.3.1.9, PDF p. 282). For an inner fibration `p : X ⟶ S` of ∞-categories and `h : Δ[1] × K^▷ ⟶ X` from `h₀` to `h₁` whose components are p-coCartesian edges and whose component at the cone point maps to a degenerate edge of S, `h₀` is a p-colimit exactly when `h₁` is.

*Needs:* 4.3.1.2; `HTT.2.4.1.7/after`; 3.1.1.11 (L4.2).

**Relative colimits in locally coCartesian fibrations** (HTT Proposition 4.3.1.10, PDF p. 283). For a locally coCartesian fibration `q : X ⟶ S` of ∞-categories, an object s and `p̄ : K^▷ ⟶ X_s`, p̄ is a q-colimit exactly when `e_! ∘ p̄` is a colimit in `X_{s'}` for every `e : s ⟶ s'`.

*Needs:* 4.3.1.1; 2.1.2.1; 2.4.2.1, 2.4.2.6 (L3.6, locally coCartesian fibrations); 3.1.1.11, 3.3.1.7; `HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration`.

**Existence in coCartesian fibrations** (HTT Corollary 4.3.1.11, PDF p. 284). If `p : X ⟶ S` is a coCartesian fibration of ∞-categories whose fibres admit K-indexed colimits preserved by every transport functor, then every `q : K ⟶ X` with an extension `K^▷ ⟶ S` of `p ∘ q` has a p-colimit lifting it.

*Needs:* 4.3.1.9–4.3.1.10.

**Weakly contractible diagrams of coCartesian edges** (HTT Proposition 4.3.1.12, PDF p. 285). For a coCartesian fibration `p : X ⟶ S` of ∞-categories and `q̄ : K^▷ ⟶ X` carrying the edges of K to p-coCartesian edges, with K weakly contractible, q̄ is a p-colimit exactly when it carries every edge of `K^▷` to a p-coCartesian edge.

*Needs:* 4.3.1.9–4.3.1.10; 2.4.1.7 (L3.5); 4.4.4.10 (L5.10).

**Relative initial objects** (HTT Lemma 4.3.1.13, PDF p. 286). For an inner fibration `p : C ⟶ D` of ∞-categories and an object c over `d = p(c)`, c is p-initial exactly when `(c, id_d)` is initial in `C ×_D D_{d/}`.

*Needs:* 4.3.1.1; 3.3.1.7; `HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration`.

**Relative initial objects in Cartesian families** (HTT Proposition 4.3.1.14, PDF p. 286). Let `p : C ⟶ D` and `r : D ⟶ E` be inner fibrations of ∞-categories with `q = r ∘ p` a Cartesian fibration and p carrying q-Cartesian morphisms to r-Cartesian ones. If an object c over `e = q(c)` is `p_e`-initial in the fibre `C_e` (relative to `D_e`), then c is p-initial.

*Needs:* 4.3.1.13; 2.4.1.1, 2.4.2.1; 2.4.4.7 (L3.7).

**Relative colimits and base change of Cartesian families** (HTT Corollaries 4.3.1.15–4.3.1.16, PDF pp. 288–289). In the situation of 4.3.1.14 with q and r Cartesian fibrations, for `s : E' ⟶ E` and `f' : K^▷ ⟶ C' = C ×_E E'`, `f'` is a `p'`-colimit exactly when its image in C is a p-colimit (4.3.1.15). For a Cartesian fibration `p : C ⟶ E`, an object e and `f : K^▷ ⟶ C_e`, f is a colimit in `C_e` exactly when it is a p-colimit in C (4.3.1.16).

*Needs:* 4.3.1.14; 1.2.13.5 (L2.5).

### L5.9 Kan extensions

**Kan extensions along full inclusions** (`SSet.IsRelLeftKanExtension`, `SSet.IsLeftKanExtension`; HTT Definition 4.3.2.2, PDF p. 289). Let `C⁰ ⊆ C` be a full subcategory of an ∞-category, `p : D ⟶ D'` an inner fibration of ∞-categories, `F : C ⟶ D` and `G = p ∘ F`. F is a p-left Kan extension of `F|C⁰` at an object c when the cone `(C⁰_{/c})^▷ ⟶ (C_{/c})^▷ ⟶ C ⟶ D`, with `C⁰_{/c} = C⁰ ×_C C_{/c}`, is a p-colimit (over the induced cone in D'). F is a p-left Kan extension of `F|C⁰` when this holds at every object; for `D' = Δ[0]` it is a left Kan extension. This is the Conventions' definition along full inclusions (= Kerodon 7.3.2.1).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsRelLeftKanExtensionAt p C₀ F c`, for quasicategories C, D, D', `[SSet.InnerFibration p]`, a full subcategory `C₀` of C (`SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory`) and `F : C ⟶ D`: `SSet.IsRelColimit p` of the composite `(C₀ ×_C C_{/c})^▷ ⟶ C_{/c}^▷ ⟶ C ⟶ D`, where `C_{/c}^▷ ⟶ C` is the tautological cone. `IsRelLeftKanExtension p C₀ F := ∀ c, IsRelLeftKanExtensionAt p C₀ F c`, and `IsLeftKanExtension C₀ F` is the case `D' = Δ[0]`. Duals for right Kan extensions, with the same argument shape: `SSet.IsRelRightKanExtension p C₀ F` and `SSet.IsRightKanExtension C₀ F` (used by 6.1.2.11 and `HTT.6.5.3.7/after`).

**Checks.**

- For `C⁰ = C`, every F is a left Kan extension of itself: `C_{/c}` has the final object `id_c`.
- At an object c of `C⁰` the condition always holds, for the same reason.
- For nerves of ordinary categories, a left Kan extension is a pointwise left Kan extension along the inclusion in Mathlib's sense (`Functor.LeftExtension.IsPointwiseLeftKanExtension`), through the L1.5 check on colimits in nerves.

*Needs:* 4.3.1.1; `HTT.1.2.11/intro`; Tau Ceti `SSet.slice`; `SSet.rightCone`.

**Invariance** (HTT Lemmas 4.3.2.5–4.3.2.6, PDF pp. 290–291). Being a p-left Kan extension at c depends only on the equivalence class of c (4.3.2.5). Equivalent functors in `Fun(C, D)` are p-left Kan extensions together, and the notion is invariant under categorical equivalences of the full inclusion `C⁰ ⊆ C` and of the inner fibration p (4.3.2.6).

*Needs:* 4.3.2.2; 4.3.1.5–4.3.1.7; `HTT.1.2.9.3/2`; `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`, `HTT.1.2.10/essentially-surjective`.

**Relative colimits of a Kan extension** (HTT Lemma 4.3.2.7, PDF p. 292). If p is a categorical fibration and F a p-left Kan extension of `F⁰ = F|C⁰`, then `D_{F/} ⟶ D'_{pF/} ×_{D'_{pF⁰/}} D_{F⁰/}` is a trivial fibration; so p-colimits of F are p-colimits of `F⁰`.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as five targets: the four parts that follow this entry, `HTT.4.3.2.7/filtration` (the simplex filtration of C), `HTT.4.3.2.7/degenerate` (adjoining a degenerate simplex), `HTT.4.3.2.7/nondegenerate` (adjoining a nondegenerate simplex) and `HTT.4.3.2.7/assemble` (the transfinite induction, which proves the statement), and this entry's own target `HTT.4.3.2.7`, which collects them.

*Needs:* `HTT.4.3.2.7/filtration`, `HTT.4.3.2.7/degenerate`, `HTT.4.3.2.7/nondegenerate`, `HTT.4.3.2.7/assemble` (below).

**The simplex filtration of a relative Kan extension problem** (`HTT.4.3.2.7/filtration`, part 1 of 4 of relative colimits of a Kan extension above; first step of the proof of HTT Lemma 4.3.2.7, PDF pp. 292–293). Let `C⁰ ⊆ C` be a full subcategory of an ∞-category, and A the set of simplices of C whose vertex 0 is not in C⁰, well-ordered so that dimension is non-decreasing. For a simplex σ not in C⁰, `r(σ) ∈ A` is its face from the first vertex outside C⁰ onward. For `β ≤ α` (α the order type of A), `C_β ⊆ C` consists of the simplices lying in C⁰ or with `r(σ)` among the first β elements. Then `C_0 = C⁰`, `C_α = C`, `C_λ = ⋃_{β<λ} C_β` for limit λ, and if `σ_β : Δ[n] ⟶ C` is nondegenerate, `C_{β+1}` is the pushout of `C_β ⟵ C⁰_{/σ_β} ⋆ ∂Δ[n] ⟶ C⁰_{/σ_β} ⋆ Δ[n]`.

*Needs:* 4.3.2.2 (`C⁰_{/c}`); `SSet.join`.

**Adjoining a degenerate simplex** (`HTT.4.3.2.7/degenerate`, part 2 of 4 of relative colimits of a Kan extension above; proof of HTT Lemma 4.3.2.7, PDF pp. 294–295). In the filtration of `HTT.4.3.2.7/filtration`, if `σ_β` is degenerate then `C_β ⊆ C_{β+1}` is a categorical equivalence.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `C_{β+1}` is a pushout of `C_β` along a map built from the subset `K ⊆ C⁰_{/σ}` of simplices factoring through a lower-dimensional degeneration. K is the colimit of a cofibrant diagram `τ ↦ C⁰_{/τ}` indexed by factorizations of σ through surjections. This diagram is weakly equivalent to the constant one at `C⁰_{/σ}`, and its index category has a final object (the nondegenerate factor of σ), so `K ⊆ C⁰_{/σ}` is a categorical equivalence and the pushout is a homotopy pushout.

*Needs:* `HTT.4.3.2.7/filtration`; 4.2.1.3 (L5.5, joins preserve categorical equivalences); `HTT.A.2.4.3/after` (F1.5); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3.2).

**Adjoining a nondegenerate simplex** (`HTT.4.3.2.7/nondegenerate`, part 3 of 4 of relative colimits of a Kan extension above; proof of HTT Lemma 4.3.2.7, PDF p. 293). In the situation of 4.3.2.7 (p a categorical fibration, F a p-left Kan extension of `F|C⁰`), if `σ_β` is nondegenerate, then `D_{F_{β+1}/} ⟶ D'_{pF_{β+1}/} ×_{D'_{pF_β/}} D_{F_β/}` is a trivial fibration, where `F_β = F|C_β`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: by the pushout of `HTT.4.3.2.7/filtration` the map is a pullback of a map of slices of `E = D_{g₀/}` over `E' = D'_{pg₀/}`, with `g₀ = F|C⁰_{/σ}`. Lifting against `∂Δ[m] ⊆ Δ[m]` becomes extending `∂Δ[n+m+1] ⟶ E` over `E'`, which is possible because the initial vertex goes to a q-initial vertex, for the induced map `q : E ⟶ E'` (the Kan extension hypothesis).

*Needs:* `HTT.4.3.2.7/filtration`; 4.3.2.2; `HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration` (L3.8).

**Transfinite induction over the filtration** (`HTT.4.3.2.7/assemble`, part 4 of 4 of relative colimits of a Kan extension above; HTT Lemma 4.3.2.7 and its proof, PDF pp. 292–293). The statement of 4.3.2.7 above.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. For `β ≤ β′ ≤ α` let `φ_{β′,β} : D_{F_{β′}/} ⟶ D'_{pF_{β′}/} ×_{D'_{pF_β/}} D_{F_β/}`, with `F_β = F|C_β`; the statement is `φ_{α,0}`. Show by induction on β′ that `φ_{β′,β}` is a trivial fibration for all `β ≤ β′`. For `β′ = β` it is an isomorphism. At a limit β′ it is the limit of a tower of trivial fibrations. At a successor, `φ_{β′+1,β}` is a pullback of `φ_{β′,β}` composed with `φ_{β′+1,β′}`, so it suffices that `φ_{β′+1,β′}` is a trivial fibration. If `σ_{β′}` is nondegenerate, this is `HTT.4.3.2.7/nondegenerate`. If it is degenerate, `C_{β′} ⊆ C_{β′+1}` is a categorical equivalence (`HTT.4.3.2.7/degenerate`), so restriction gives categorical equivalences `D_{F_{β′+1}/} ⟶ D_{F_{β′}/}` and `D'_{pF_{β′+1}/} ⟶ D'_{pF_{β′}/}` (4.2.1.5 with 1.2.7.3); the second is a left fibration, hence a trivial fibration (the dual of 2.4.4.6), so `φ_{β′+1,β′}` is a categorical equivalence by two-out-of-three, and it is a left fibration (2.1.2.1), hence a trivial fibration (the dual of 2.4.4.6).

*Needs:* `HTT.4.3.2.7/degenerate`, `HTT.4.3.2.7/nondegenerate`; 2.1.2.1 (L2.3); 1.2.7.3 (L3.2); 2.4.4.6 (L3.7); 4.2.1.5 (L5.5).

**Transitivity and parameters** (HTT Propositions 4.3.2.8–4.3.2.9, PDF p. 295). For full subcategories `C⁰ ⊆ C¹ ⊆ C` and a categorical fibration p with `F|C¹` a p-left Kan extension of `F|C⁰`, F is a p-left Kan extension of `F|C¹` exactly when it is one of `F|C⁰` (4.3.2.8). For `F : C × C' ⟶ D`, F is a p-left Kan extension of `F|C⁰ × C'` exactly when each `F(−, c')` is one of its restriction to `C⁰` (4.3.2.9).

*Needs:* 4.3.1.7, 4.3.2.7; `HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration`.

**Lifting lemmas** (HTT Lemmas 4.3.2.10–4.3.2.11, PDF p. 296). For an inner fibration `p : X ⟶ S`, `m ≥ 0`, `n ≥ 1`, every map `(∂Δ[m] × Δ[n]) ⊔ (Δ[m] × ∂Δ[n]) ⟶ X` over `Δ[m] × Δ[n] ⟶ S` sending `(0, 0)` to a p-initial vertex extends to `Δ[m] × Δ[n]` (4.3.2.10). For an inner fibration `p : X ⟶ Y` over S and `q_S : K × S ⟶ X` over S, the map of relative fat slices `X^{q_S/} ⟶ Y^{p q_S/}` is an inner fibration (4.3.2.11).

*Needs:* 4.3.1.1; 2.3.2.4 (L3.2); 4.2.2.1 (L5.6).

**Extension along a boundary** (HTT Lemma 4.3.2.12, PDF p. 297). For a categorical fibration `p : D ⟶ D'`, a map `C ⟶ D'`, a full subcategory `C⁰ ⊆ C` and `n > 0`, a square from `∂Δ[n] ⟶ Fun_{D'}(C, D)` to `Δ[n] ⟶ Fun_{D'}(C⁰, D)` has a filler whenever the functor at the vertex 0 is a p-left Kan extension of its restriction to `C⁰`.

*Needs:* 4.2.2.4; 4.3.1.14; `HTT.4.3.2.7/filtration`, `HTT.4.3.2.7/degenerate`, 4.3.2.10–4.3.2.11; A.2.3.1 (F1.4).

**Existence** (HTT Lemma 4.3.2.13, PDF p. 300; Corollary 4.3.2.14, PDF p. 301). For a categorical fibration `p : D ⟶ D'`, a full subcategory `C⁰ ⊆ C`, `F⁰ : C⁰ ⟶ D` and `G : C ⟶ D'` extending `p ∘ F⁰`, a p-left Kan extension F of `F⁰` over G exists exactly when every `C⁰_{/c} ⟶ D` has a p-colimit over the cone given by G (4.3.2.13). If `p : D ⟶ E` is a coCartesian fibration whose fibres admit small colimits preserved by the transport functors, then for a small ∞-category C, a full subcategory `C⁰`, `F⁰ : C⁰ ⟶ D` and any `G : C ⟶ E` extending `p ∘ F⁰`, `F⁰` has a p-left Kan extension over G (4.3.2.14).

*Needs:* 4.3.2.7, 4.3.2.12; 4.3.1.11.

**Kan extension is a trivial fibration** (HTT Proposition 4.3.2.15, Corollary 4.3.2.16, PDF p. 302). For a categorical fibration `p : D ⟶ D'`, a map `C ⟶ D'` and a full subcategory `C⁰`, let `K ⊆ Map_{D'}(C, D)` be spanned by the p-left Kan extensions of their restrictions and `K⁰ ⊆ Map_{D'}(C⁰, D)` by the functors whose diagrams `C⁰_{/c} ⟶ D` all have p-colimits. Restriction `K ⟶ K⁰` is a trivial fibration (4.3.2.15). If every functor `C⁰ ⟶ D` over D' has a p-left Kan extension, restriction has a section `i_!` whose essential image is the p-left Kan extensions (4.3.2.16).

**Checks.** For `C⁰ = C`, K and `K⁰` are all of `Map_{D'}(C, D)` and the restriction is the identity.

*Needs:* 4.3.2.12–4.3.2.13; `HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration`.

**Left extensions and the mapping cylinder** (`SSet.LeftExtension`, `SSet.mappingCylinderOp`; HTT Definition 4.3.3.1, PDF p. 303). For `δ : K ⟶ K'` and `f : K ⟶ D` with D an ∞-category, a left extension of f along δ is a map `f' : K' ⟶ D` with a morphism `f ⟶ f' ∘ δ` in `Fun(K, D)`; equivalently a map `M^op(δ) ⟶ D` restricting to f, where `M^op(δ) = (K × Δ[1]) ⊔_{K × {1}} K'`.

*Lean:* `SSet.mappingCylinderOp δ` as that pushout, over `Δ[1]`; `SSet.LeftExtension δ f` the structure `(f' : K' ⟶ D, α : Δ[1] ⟶ Fun(K, D))` with `α` from f to `δ ≫ f'`, and its equivalence with maps `mappingCylinderOp δ ⟶ D` extending f.

*Needs:* 1.2.7.2; Mathlib pushouts in `SSet`.

**Kan extensions along arbitrary maps** (`SSet.IsLeftKanExtensionAlong`, `SSet.IsLeftKanExtensionCyl`; HTT Definition 4.3.3.2, PDF p. 303). HTT: `F : M^op(δ) ⟶ D` is a left Kan extension of `F|K` along δ when it factors as `F' ∘ F''` with `F'' : M^op(δ) ⟶ 𝒦` a categorical equivalence over `Δ[1]` to an ∞-category and `F'` a left Kan extension of its restriction to the fibre `𝒦 ×_{Δ[1]} {0}` (4.3.2.2). The roadmap's definition is the Conventions' pointwise one (Kerodon 7.3.1.2); HTT's is a characterization.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsLeftKanExtensionAlong δ α` for `δ : K ⟶ K'`, a quasicategory D, `f : K ⟶ D`, `f' : K' ⟶ D` and `α : Edge (ihomVertexEquiv.symm f) (ihomVertexEquiv.symm (δ ≫ f'))`, an edge of `Fun(K, D)` (with `SSet.ihomVertexEquiv : ((ihom K).obj Z) _⦋0⦌ ≃ (K ⟶ Z)`, propose; no Mathlib counterpart; reused in 5.2.6.1, 5.3.5.1 and `HTT.6.1.4.3/after`): for every vertex c of K', put `K_{/c} := K ×_{K'} K'_{/c}` with projection `π : K_{/c} ⟶ K`, and let `τ_c : δ ∘ π ⟶ const_c` be the transformation `K_{/c} ⋄ Δ[0] ⟶ K_{/c} ⋆ Δ[0] ⟶ K'_{/c} ⋆ Δ[0] ⟶ K'` (`SSet.fatJoin.toJoin`, 4.2.1.1). The condition: `∀ c, ∃ p̄ (h : inl ≫ p̄ = π ≫ f), SSet.IsColimitDiagram p̄ ∧ ∃ e : Edge (SSet.fatCoslice.ofCone p̄ h) (composite c), e.IsEquivalence`, for cones `p̄ : rightCone K_{/c} ⟶ D`, where `SSet.fatCoslice.ofCone p̄ h` is the image of p̄ in the fat coslice `D^{(f∘π)/}` (`SSet.fatCoslice`, 4.2.1.5) and `composite c` is a composite `(α ∘ π) ≫ f'(τ_c) : f ∘ π ⟶ const_{f'(c)}`. Colimits are invariant under equivalence in the slice, so "some composite" and "every composite" agree (a lemma). `SSet.IsLeftKanExtensionCyl δ F` is HTT's 4.3.3.2 condition, stated as above; it is kept as an auxiliary predicate, used only to state HTT 4.3.3.2 as the `iff` target below, and the notion's one definition remains `SSet.IsLeftKanExtensionAlong`. Targets: `IsLeftKanExtensionAlong δ α ↔ IsLeftKanExtensionCyl δ F` for the corresponding F, and, for a full inclusion δ and `α = id`, `IsLeftKanExtensionAlong δ id ↔ IsLeftKanExtension C₀ f'` (with 4.3.3.5).
