*Lean:* `SSet.IsReflectiveLocalization.isLocalization`: for `f : C ⟶ D` with `IsReflectiveLocalization (QCat.homMk f)`, `IsLocalization f W` with `W` the edges e such that `e.map f` is an equivalence. This W, the morphisms f inverts, is Lurie's S (the morphisms `L = g ∘ f` inverts), since g is fully faithful.

*Needs:* 5.2.7.2, 5.2.7.4, 5.2.7.7; 4.3.2.2, 4.3.2.15 (L5.9, right Kan extensions); `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`, `HTT.1.2.10/essentially-surjective`.

**Orthogonality** (`SSet.LeftOrthogonal`; HTT Definition 5.2.8.1, Remark 5.2.8.3, PDF pp. 387–388). In an ∞-category C, `f : A ⟶ B` is left orthogonal to `g : X ⟶ Y`, `f ⊥ g`, when for every commutative square from f to g the morphism space `Map_{C_{A/ /Y}}(B, X)` in the double slice `C_{A/ /Y} = (C_{A/})_{/Y}` is contractible. Equivalently (5.2.8.3), for every lift `g̃ : X̃ ⟶ Ỹ` of g to `C_{A/}`, composition with g̃ is a homotopy equivalence `Map_{C_{A/}}(B̃, X̃) ⟶ Map_{C_{A/}}(B̃, Ỹ)`, where B̃ is f viewed as an object of `C_{A/}`.

*Lean:* `SSet.LeftOrthogonal f g` for edges f, g of a quasicategory C: for every `σ : Δ[1] ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ C` with sides f and g, the morphism space `SSet.morphismSpace` (L1.5, `Hom`) of `(C_{A/})_{/Ỹ}` between the objects determined by σ (the helper `orthogonalityData σ`, propose, from the join and slice universal properties) is contractible (a Kan complex weakly equivalent to `Δ[0]`). 5.2.8.3 and 5.2.8.22 are characterizations. For a class `S : ∀ ⦃x y : C _⦋0⦌⦄, C.Edge x y → Prop` of edges, `S^⊥` and `^⊥S` (HTT Notation 5.2.8.4) are classes of the same type.

**Checks.** Every equivalence is left and right orthogonal to every morphism (5.2.8.6 (1)). For an ordinary category, `N(f) ⊥ N(g)` exactly when every square has a unique diagonal filler.

*Needs:* Tau Ceti `SSet.slice`, `SSet.coslice`; `HTT.1.2.2/morphism-space` (L1.5); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

**Orthogonality in ordinary categories** (HTT Remark 5.2.8.5, PDF p. 388). In an ordinary category, `f ⊥ g` implies that f has the left lifting property with respect to g; hence `S^⊥` and `^⊥S` lie in the classes of A.1.2 defined by lifting properties.

*Needs:* 5.2.8.1, 5.2.8.3; Mathlib `HasLiftingProperty`.

**Closure properties** (HTT Proposition 5.2.8.6, PDF pp. 389–390). For a set S of morphisms of an ∞-category C: `S^⊥` and `^⊥S` contain all equivalences and are closed under retracts; in a triangle `h = g ∘ f` with `g ∈ S^⊥`, `f ∈ S^⊥` exactly when `h ∈ S^⊥`, and dually with `f ∈ ^⊥S`; `S^⊥` is stable under pullbacks and `^⊥S` under pushouts; and in `Fun(Δ[1], C)`, `^⊥S` is closed under the K-indexed colimits and `S^⊥` under the K-indexed limits that C admits.

*Needs:* 5.2.8.3; 1.2.13.4; 5.1.2.3 (L6.1, colimits in `Fun(Δ[1], C)`); `HTT.4.4.5/intro` (retracts); 4.4.2.1 (L5.10, pushouts).

**Factorization systems** (`SSet.FactorizationSystem`; HTT Definition 5.2.8.8, PDF p. 390). A factorization system (Joyal) on an ∞-category C is a pair `(S_L, S_R)` of collections of morphisms such that both are closed under retracts, every morphism of `S_L` is left orthogonal to every morphism of `S_R`, and every morphism factors as a morphism of `S_L` followed by one of `S_R` (a 2-simplex of C).

*Lean:* `SSet.FactorizationSystem C` for a quasicategory C: a structure with `left right : ∀ ⦃x y : C _⦋0⦌⦄, C.Edge x y → Prop`, each closed under retracts in `Fun(Δ[1], C)` (edges as vertices of `Fun(Δ[1], C)`; `SSet.IsRetract`, L5.10); `∀ f g, left f → right g → SSet.LeftOrthogonal f g`; and for every edge `h : C.Edge x z` a 2-simplex `σ` with `left (d₂ σ)`, `right (d₀ σ)` and `d₁ σ = h`. Mathlib's `SSet.Edge x₀ x₁` is indexed by its endpoints, so a class of morphisms always has this type, in Mathlib's `MorphismProperty` shape (also in 5.2.8.1, 5.5.4.1, 5.5.4.5, 5.5.5.1).

**Checks.** (all equivalences, all morphisms) is a factorization system (HTT Example 5.2.8.9). The opposite pair on `C^op` is one (Remark 5.2.8.10).

*Needs:* 5.2.8.1; `HTT.4.4.5/intro`.

**Each class determines the other** (HTT Proposition 5.2.8.11, Corollary 5.2.8.13, PDF pp. 390–391). For a factorization system, `S_L = ^⊥S_R` and `S_R = S_L^⊥` (5.2.8.11). Hence both classes contain all equivalences and are closed under composition (5.2.8.13).

*Needs:* 5.2.8.8, 5.2.8.6, 5.2.8.22 (the `Δ[3]`-filler form of orthogonality, below).

**The double-slice mapping space** (HTT Lemma 5.2.8.20, Lemma 5.2.8.22, PDF pp. 393–394). For simplicial sets K, A, B, the square `K × B ⟶ K × (A ⋆ B)`, `B ⟶ (K × A) ⋆ B` is a homotopy pushout for the Joyal model structure (5.2.8.20). Let Q be the simplicial subset of `Δ[3]` of simplices not containing `Δ^{1,2}` (Notation 5.2.8.21, `Q ≅ Δ[1] × Δ[1]`). For a square `σ : Q ⟶ C` in an ∞-category from `A ⟶ B` to `X ⟶ Y`, there is a canonical categorical equivalence `Fun(Δ[3], C) ×_{Fun(Q, C)} {σ} ⟶ Map_{C_{A/ /Y}}(B, X)`; in particular the left side is a Kan complex (5.2.8.22). This gives the `Δ[3]`-filler form of 5.2.8.1.

*Needs:* 4.2.1.2 (L5.5); A.2.4.1, `HTT.A.2.4.3/after` (F1.5, left properness and homotopy pushouts); 2.2.5.1 (L3.8); 1.2.7.2.

**Factorization systems are localizations of `Fun(Δ[1], C)`** (HTT Lemma 5.2.8.19, PDF p. 392). For a factorization system on C, the full subcategory of `Fun(Δ[1], C)` on `S_R` is reflective, and a morphism from h to g in `Fun(Δ[1], C)`, given by a square with top edge f and bottom edge e, exhibits g as a localization of h exactly when `g ∈ S_R`, `f ∈ S_L` and e is an equivalence.

*Needs:* 5.2.8.1, 5.2.8.8; 5.2.7.2, 5.2.7.6, 5.2.7.8; `HTT.A.2.4.3/after`.

**Factorizations are unique** (HTT Proposition 5.2.8.17, Corollary 5.2.8.18, PDF pp. 391–392). Let `S_L`, `S_R` be collections of morphisms of an ∞-category C that are closed under equivalence in `Fun(Δ[1], C)` and contain all equivalences. They form a factorization system exactly when restriction `Fun⁰(Δ[2], C) ⟶ Fun(Δ^{0,2}, C)` is a trivial fibration, where `Fun⁰(Δ[2], C)` is spanned by the 2-simplices with first edge in `S_L` and second edge in `S_R` (5.2.8.17). For any simplicial set K, the pointwise classes `(S_L^K, S_R^K)` form a factorization system on `Fun(K, C)` (5.2.8.18).

*Parts.* Proposition 5.2.8.17 is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.5.2.8.17/forward` ((1) ⇒ (2)) and `HTT.5.2.8.17/backward` ((2) ⇒ (1)), and this entry's own target `HTT.5.2.8.17`, which combines them into the equivalence; 5.2.8.18 is a separate target.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.2.8.17/forward`, `HTT.5.2.8.17/backward` (below).

**Factorization systems give unique factorizations** (`HTT.5.2.8.17/forward`, part 1 of 2 of the uniqueness of factorizations above; (1) ⇒ (2) of HTT Proposition 5.2.8.17, PDF pp. 391–392, proof pp. 394–396). If `(S_L, S_R)` is a factorization system on C, restriction `Fun⁰(Δ[2], C) ⟶ Fun(Δ^{0,2}, C)` is a trivial fibration.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: it is a categorical fibration, so it suffices that it is an equivalence. Factor it through the squares `D ⊆ Fun(Δ[1] × Δ[1], C)` with one side an equivalence. The first factor has a left inverse that is a pullback of a trivial fibration (4.3.2.15). The second is evaluation at the initial vertex on coCartesian sections of a fibration over `Δ[1]` that is coCartesian by 5.2.8.19.

*Needs:* 5.2.8.8, 5.2.8.19; 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); `HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration` (L3.8).

**Unique factorizations give factorization systems** (`HTT.5.2.8.17/backward`, part 2 of 2 of the uniqueness of factorizations above; (2) ⇒ (1) of HTT Proposition 5.2.8.17, PDF pp. 391–392, proof pp. 396–397). If restriction `Fun⁰(Δ[2], C) ⟶ Fun(Δ^{0,2}, C)` is a trivial fibration, then `(S_L, S_R)` is a factorization system; with `HTT.5.2.8.17/forward` this is the equivalence of 5.2.8.17 above.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: a section s of the trivial fibration shows that f is in `S_L` exactly when its right factor is an equivalence, so both classes are closed under retracts. Orthogonality reduces by 5.2.8.22 to contractibility of a fibre of `Fun(Δ[3], C) ⟶ Fun(Q, C)`. Two applications of 4.3.2.15 identify that fibre with a fibre of a full subcategory of `Fun(Δ[2] × Δ[1], C)`, contractible by (2).

*Needs:* `HTT.5.2.8.17/forward`; 5.2.8.22; 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); 2.4.2.1 (L3.6); 1.1.5.14 (L1.5).

### L6.6 Filtered ∞-categories and right exact functors

κ is a regular cardinal (`Cardinal.IsRegular`) throughout, and a simplicial set is κ-small when it has fewer than κ nondegenerate simplices (`HasCardinalLT`, as in L5.6's `SSet.HasColimitsOfSize`).

**κ-filtered ∞-categories** (`SSet.IsCardinalFiltered` (Tau Ceti main), `SSet.IsFiltered`; HTT Definition 5.3.1.7, PDF p. 400). An ∞-category C is κ-filtered when every map `K ⟶ C` from a κ-small simplicial set extends to `K^▷`. It is filtered when it is ω-filtered. This is the ∞-categorical notion of the Conventions; Mathlib's `IsFiltered` and `IsCardinalFiltered` are 1-categorical and agree with it only for nerves.

*Lean:* Tau Ceti main's `SSet.IsCardinalFiltered C κ` (`class SSet.IsCardinalFiltered (K : SSet.{u}) (κ : Cardinal.{w}) : Prop`, `SimplicialSet/CardinalFiltered.lean`: every `Y ⟶ K` with `HasCardinalLT Y.N κ` extends to `Y ⋆ Δ[0]`, with `of_le`, `of_iso`, `exists_edge` and `isCardinalFiltered_nerve_iff`), kept as it stands; targets about κ-filtered ∞-categories state `[Quasicategory C]` and `[Fact κ.IsRegular]` as hypotheses. `SSet.IsFiltered C := C.IsCardinalFiltered ℵ₀`.

**Checks.**

- The nerve of a category J is κ-filtered exactly when `IsCardinalFiltered J κ` (Mathlib); for `κ = ℵ₀`, exactly when J is filtered (Mathlib `isCardinalFiltered_aleph0_iff`). For a partially ordered set this is HTT Example 5.3.1.8: every κ-small subset has an upper bound.
- An ∞-category with a final object is κ-filtered for every κ (5.3.1.17).
- The empty ∞-category is not filtered (take `K = ∅`).

*Needs:* `SSet.rightCone` (L1.3); A.1.1.1 (F1.1, κ-small and κ-filtered); `HTT.1.2.15/intro`.

**First examples** (HTT Example 5.3.1.9, Remarks 5.3.1.10, 5.3.1.17, PDF pp. 401, 404). If the inclusion `C ⊆ C^▷` has a retraction, C is κ-filtered for every κ; in particular `Idem` is (4.4.5.9) (5.3.1.9). An ∞-category admitting small κ-filtered colimits is idempotent complete, by 5.3.1.9 and 4.4.5.15 (5.3.1.10). An ∞-category with a final object is κ-filtered for every κ (5.3.1.17).

*Needs:* 5.3.1.7; 4.4.5.2, 4.4.5.9, 4.4.5.15 (L5.10); `HTT.1.2.12/final`; 1.2.13.5.

**Testing on posets and on boundaries** (HTT Remark 5.3.1.12, Lemma 5.3.1.14, PDF p. 401). C is κ-filtered exactly when it has the right lifting property against `N(A) ⊆ N(A)^▷` for every κ-small partially ordered set A (5.3.1.12). C is filtered exactly when every map `∂Δ[n] ⟶ C`, `n ≥ 0`, extends along `∂Δ[n] ⊆ Λ[n+1, n+1] ≅ (∂Δ[n])^▷` (5.3.1.14).

*Proof route.* 5.3.1.12: precompose with a cofinal map from a κ-small poset, from 4.2.3.15 for κ uncountable and 4.2.3.16 for `κ = ω`, and compare undercategories (4.1.1.8 (2)). 5.3.1.14: induction on the nondegenerate simplices of K, with 2.1.2.3.

*Needs:* 5.3.1.7; 4.2.3.15, 4.2.3.16 (L5.6); 4.1.1.1, 4.1.1.8 (L5.2); 2.1.2.3 (L2.3); 1.1.5.14.

**Cofinal maps from filtered posets** (HTT Proposition 5.3.1.18, PDF p. 404). Every κ-filtered ∞-category C receives a cofinal map `N(A) ⟶ C` from the nerve of a κ-filtered partially ordered set A.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: replace C by `C × N(X)` for a contractible groupoid on a set X of size at least κ, take A the κ-small simplicial subsets with a final vertex, and build a retraction of the decomposition cylinder `K_F` (4.2.3.1) as in 4.2.3.4; cofinality by 4.2.3.4 and 4.2.3.8. This reduction to posets is used throughout L6.6–L7.

*Needs:* 5.3.1.7; 4.2.3.1, 4.2.3.4, 4.2.3.8 (L5.6); 4.1.1.1; `HTT.1.2.12/final`; A.1.1.1.

**Filtered colimits of idempotent complete ∞-categories** (HTT Corollary 4.4.5.21, PDF p. 328; stated in §4.4.5, placed here: its proof reduces to filtered posets by 5.3.1.18). A filtered colimit in `Cat∞` of idempotent complete ∞-categories is idempotent complete.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Reduce the indexing ∞-category to a filtered poset A (5.3.1.18). Strictify the diagram to a functor `A ⥤ Set⁺_Δ` with fibrant values (4.2.4.4). Compute its colimit in `Cat∞` as the ordinary filtered colimit (4.2.4.1, since categorical equivalences are stable under filtered colimits). The finite 3-skeleton of `Idem` then maps into some stage. There, 4.4.5.20 extends the resulting `(X, e)` to an idempotent, and its colimit maps to a colimit of the given idempotent (4.4.5.18).

*Needs:* 4.4.5.17–4.4.5.18 (L5.10); 4.4.5.20 (L6.1); 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4 (L5.7); 5.3.1.18; 3.1.4.1 (L4.3, the fibrant objects of `Set⁺_Δ`, for `Cat∞ ≃ N((Set⁺_Δ)°)`); `HTT.3.1.3.7/perfect` (L4.3, filtered colimits of Cartesian equivalences).

**Filtered simplicial sets** (HTT Proposition 5.3.1.19, PDF p. 405). For a simplicial set S (κ-filtered meaning categorically equivalent to a κ-filtered ∞-category, HTT Remark 5.3.1.13), the following are equivalent: S is κ-filtered; S is categorically equivalent to a colimit `Y` of a κ-filtered diagram of κ-filtered simplicial sets `Y_α`; S is categorically equivalent to an ∞-category that is a κ-filtered union of simplicial subsets `C_α`, each an ∞-category with a final object.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsEssentiallyCardinalFiltered S κ := ∃ C f, Quasicategory C ∧ IsCategoricalEquivalence (f : S ⟶ C) ∧ IsCardinalFiltered C κ`, with invariance under categorical equivalence (HTT Remark 5.3.1.11, through 1.2.9.3) as a lemma.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, with the fibrant replacement `T(X) = N(|C[X]|)` replaced by `T(X) = N(Ex^∞ C[X])`: natural, with `X ⟶ T(X)` a categorical equivalence onto an ∞-category (2.2.0.1), and preserving inclusions and filtered colimits as Lurie's T does (F2.3).

*Needs:* 5.3.1.7, 5.3.1.18; 1.2.9.3 (L3.8); 2.2.0.1 (L2.8); `Ex^∞` (F2.3); A.1.1.1; A.2.1.1 (F1.4).

**Filtered ∞-categories are weakly contractible; undercategories** (HTT Lemmas 5.3.1.20–5.3.1.21, PDF p. 406). A filtered ∞-category is weakly contractible (5.3.1.20). If C is κ-filtered and `p : K ⟶ C` has κ-small source, `C_{p/}` is κ-filtered (5.3.1.21).

*Proof route.* 5.3.1.20: Lurie argues with `|C|`, Whitehead's theorem and finite subcomplexes. Combinatorially: C is nonempty; `Ex^∞` commutes with filtered colimits, so every class in `π_i(Ex^∞ C, c)` comes from a finite `K ⊆ C` containing c, and it dies in `K^▷ ⟶ C`, which is weakly contractible; conclude with the combinatorial Whitehead theorem (F2.2). 5.3.1.21: `(C_{p/})_{p'/} ≅ C_{q/}` for the join `q : K ⋆ K' ⟶ C`.

*Needs:* 5.3.1.7; homotopy groups and Whitehead's theorem, `HTT.A.2.7/kan-weak-equivalences` (F2.2); `Ex^∞` (F2.3); `SSet.join`, Tau Ceti `SSet.coslice`; A.1.1.1.

**Filtered through diagonals** (HTT Proposition 5.3.1.22, PDF p. 406). An ∞-category C is κ-filtered exactly when, for every κ-small simplicial set K, the diagonal `C ⟶ Fun(K, C)` is cofinal.

*Needs:* 5.3.1.7, 5.3.1.20, 5.3.1.21; 4.1.1.1 (L5.2), 4.1.3.1 (L5.4); A.2.3.1; A.1.1.1.

**κ-right exact functors** (`SSet.IsCardinalRightExact`; HTT Definition 5.3.2.1, PDF p. 407; Remark 5.3.2.10, PDF p. 411). A functor `F : A ⟶ B` of ∞-categories is κ-right exact when, for every right fibration `B' ⟶ B` with B' κ-filtered, `A ×_B B'` is κ-filtered. Right exact means ω-right exact. Dually (HTT Remarks 5.3.2.2 and 5.3.2.10, the latter a target), G is κ-left exact when `G^op` is κ-right exact, and left exact when ω-left exact; when A has κ-small limits this means G preserves them (dual of 5.3.2.9).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsCardinalRightExact F κ` for `F : A ⟶ B` of quasicategories in `SSet.{u}`: `∀ (B' : SSet.{u}) (r : B' ⟶ B) [RightFibration r], IsCardinalFiltered B' κ → IsCardinalFiltered (pullback F r) κ`; `SSet.IsCardinalLeftExact G κ := IsCardinalRightExact (SSet.opFunctor.map G) κ` (`G.op` would be a morphism of `SSetᵒᵖ`), `SSet.IsLeftExact G := IsCardinalLeftExact G (ℵ₀ : Cardinal.{u})`, `SSet.IsRightExact F := IsCardinalRightExact F (ℵ₀ : Cardinal.{u})`. Target `SSet.isCardinalRightExact_uliftFunctor_iff`, the same statement as `SSet.isCofinal_uliftFunctor_iff` (4.1.1.1) for κ-right exactness, so testing in `SSet.{u}` suffices.

**Checks.** Equivalences are κ-right exact (5.3.2.4). A functor between ∞-categories with κ-small colimits is κ-right exact exactly when it preserves them (5.3.2.9).

*Needs:* 5.3.1.7; 2.0.0.3 (L2.1, `SSet.RightFibration`).

**Stability and a test on overcategories** (HTT Propositions 5.3.2.4–5.3.2.5, PDF pp. 407–408). κ-right exact functors are closed under composition, contain the equivalences, and are closed under equivalence in `Fun(A, B)` (5.3.2.4). F is κ-right exact exactly when `A ×_B B_{/b}` is κ-filtered for every object b of B (5.3.2.5).

*Parts.* Proposition 5.3.2.5 is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.5.3.2.5/replacement` (a right-fibrant replacement commuting with filtered colimits) and `HTT.5.3.2.5/good` (the good-objects argument, which proves 5.3.2.5), and this entry's own target `HTT.5.3.2.5`, which collects them; 5.3.2.4 is a separate target.

*Proof route.* 5.3.2.4 by 3.3.1.3. 5.3.2.5 is Lurie's "good objects" argument with the functor `T = Un ∘ R ∘ St` on `SSet/B` built from straightening (2.2.1.2) in `HTT.5.3.2.5/replacement`; Lurie takes `R = Sing |−|` objectwise, and the roadmap takes `R = Ex^∞`, which gives a projectively fibrant replacement commuting with filtered colimits. The argument is `HTT.5.3.2.5/good`; its key input is 5.3.1.19.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.3.2.5/replacement`, `HTT.5.3.2.5/good` (below); 5.3.2.1; 3.3.1.3 (L4.7).

**A right-fibrant replacement commuting with filtered colimits** (`HTT.5.3.2.5/replacement`, part 1 of 2 of stability and a test on overcategories above; proof of HTT Proposition 5.3.2.5, PDF p. 408). For an ∞-category B there is a functor `T : SSet/B ⥤ SSet/B` with a natural map `j_X : X ⟶ T(X)` such that `j_X` is a contravariant equivalence, `T(X) ⟶ B` is a right fibration, and T commutes with filtered colimits.

*Proof route.* `T = Un_φ ∘ (Ex^∞ objectwise) ∘ St_φ` (2.2.1.2), the roadmap's replacement for Lurie's `Sing |−|`. `St` is a left adjoint. `Ex^∞` commutes with filtered colimits and gives projectively fibrant replacements. `Un` commutes with filtered colimits because it is computed by maps out of the straightenings of simplices, which are finite simplicial categories (compact objects). Fibrancy of `T(X)` is 2.2.3.12.

*Needs:* 2.2.1.2, 2.2.3.12 (L2.8); `Ex^∞` (F2.3); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences` (F2.4).

**A test on overcategories** (`HTT.5.3.2.5/good`, part 2 of 2 of stability and a test on overcategories above; HTT Proposition 5.3.2.5 and its proof, PDF pp. 408–410). The 5.3.2.5 half of the entry above: F is κ-right exact exactly when `A ×_B B_{/b}` is κ-filtered for every object b of B.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: call X good when `T(X) ×_B A` is κ-filtered (T from `HTT.5.3.2.5/replacement`). Good objects are invariant under contravariant equivalences and closed under κ-filtered colimits. Overcategories are good by hypothesis, hence so are vertices, ∞-categories with a final object, and then κ-filtered ∞-categories (5.3.1.19). For a right fibration X, being good means that `X ×_B A` is κ-filtered.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.3.2.5/replacement`; 5.3.2.1; 5.3.1.7, 5.3.1.19; 3.3.1.3 (L4.7).

**Right exact functors preserve initial objects** (HTT Lemmas 5.3.2.6–5.3.2.8, PDF p. 410). If `B' ⟶ B` is a Cartesian fibration with B' filtered and b initial in B, the fibre over b is a contractible Kan complex (5.3.2.6). A right exact functor carries initial objects to initial objects (5.3.2.7). If `f : A ⟶ B` is κ-right exact and `p : K ⟶ A` is κ-small, `A_{p/} ⟶ B_{fp/}` is κ-right exact (5.3.2.8).

*Needs:* 5.3.1.7, 5.3.1.20, 5.3.2.1, 5.3.2.5; 4.1.2.15 (L5.3); 4.1.1.1; 2.4.2.1; `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

**κ-right exactness through colimits** (HTT Proposition 5.3.2.9, PDF p. 410). A κ-right exact functor preserves all κ-small colimits that exist in its source. Conversely, if A admits κ-small colimits and f preserves them, f is κ-right exact.

*Needs:* 5.3.2.1, 5.3.2.5, 5.3.2.7, 5.3.2.8; 5.3.1.7; 1.2.13.5; A.1.1.1.

**κ-closed ∞-categories and colimit functors** (`SSet.IsCardinalClosed`; HTT Definition 5.3.3.1, PDF p. 411). An ∞-category is κ-closed when every diagram indexed by a κ-small simplicial set has a colimit. When every K-indexed diagram in C has a colimit, the colimit diagrams span a full subcategory `D ⊆ Fun(K^▷, C)` with `D ⟶ Fun(K, C)` a trivial fibration (4.3.2.15); a section followed by evaluation at the cone point is a colimit functor `colim_K : Fun(K, C) ⟶ C`, unique up to contractible choice.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsCardinalClosed C κ := SSet.HasColimitsOfSize κ C` (L5.6), an abbreviation. `SSet.colimFunctor K C : Fun(K, C) ⟶ C` from a chosen section of the trivial fibration, with its defining property as a lemma.

*Needs:* 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); `SSet.HasColimitsOfShape` (L5.6); 1.2.13.4, 1.2.13.5; A.1.1.1.

**Colimits of corepresentables are contractible** (HTT Lemma 5.3.3.2, PDF p. 412). For a corepresentable `F : K ⟶ S` (in the essential image of the Yoneda embedding of `K^op`), every colimit of F is a contractible Kan complex.

*Needs:* 3.3.4.6 (L5.1); `HTT.5.1.3/intro`; 1.2.12.4.

**Filtered colimits commute with finite limits in `S`** (HTT Proposition 5.3.3.3, PDF pp. 412–413). An ∞-category I is κ-filtered exactly when `colim_I : Fun(I, S) ⟶ S` preserves κ-small limits.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.5.3.3.3/kan-complexes` (filtered colimits of Kan complexes) and `HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if` (κ-filtered colimits are κ-continuous), and this entry's own target `HTT.5.3.3.3`, which proves the converse and combines them.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. "Only if" is `HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if`. "If": a missing cone gives a limit of corepresentables that is initial in `Fun(I, S)` (5.1.5.2). Its colimit is then initial in S, since `colim_I` is a left adjoint, but it is also a limit of contractible spaces (5.3.3.2), hence final: a contradiction.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if` (below); 5.3.1.7, 5.3.3.2; 5.1.5.2; 4.1.1.1.

**Filtered colimits of Kan complexes** (`HTT.5.3.3.3/kan-complexes`, part 1 of 2 of filtered colimits commute with finite limits in `S` above; in the proof of HTT Proposition 5.3.3.3, PDF p. 413). Let A be a κ-filtered poset.

1. The colimit in `SSet` of an A-indexed diagram of homotopy pullback squares of Kan complexes is a homotopy pullback square.
2. For a κ-small family `{X_i}` of A-indexed diagrams of Kan complexes, `colim_A ∏_i X_i ⟶ ∏_i colim_A X_i` is a weak homotopy equivalence.

*Proof route.* Classical; Lurie states it without proof. For (1), replace the cospans functorially by Kan fibrations through the path object; filtered colimits preserve Kan fibrations and weak equivalences and commute with homotopy groups, and the fibres compare through the long exact sequence. For (2), the homotopy groups of a product of Kan complexes are the products, and κ-filtered colimits of sets commute with κ-small products.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.2.7/model-properties/combinatorial` (F3.1); `HTT.A.2.7/fibration-sequence/exact`, `HTT.A.2.7/kan-weak-equivalences/whitehead`, `HTT.A.2.7/homotopy-groups` (F2.2); A.2.4.1, `HTT.A.2.4.3/after` (F1.5).

**κ-filtered colimits are κ-continuous** (`HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if`, part 2 of 2 of filtered colimits commute with finite limits in `S` above; HTT Proposition 5.3.3.3, (1) ⇒ (2), PDF pp. 412–413). For κ regular and I a κ-filtered ∞-category, `colim_I : Fun(I, S) ⟶ S` preserves κ-small limits.

*Proof route.* Lurie's.

1. Reduce to `I = N(A)` for a κ-filtered poset A, by 5.3.1.18 and by 5.1.2.2 for restriction along the cofinal map.
2. By 4.2.4.4, the diagonal `S ⟶ Fun(N(A), S)` is the right derived functor of the constant-diagram functor on projective diagrams `A ⥤ SSet`, so `colim_I` is the left derived functor of the strict colimit.
3. By the dual of 4.4.2.6 and by 4.2.4.1, it suffices that the strict colimit preserves homotopy pullbacks and κ-small homotopy products, which is `HTT.5.3.3.3/kan-complexes`.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.3.3.3/kan-complexes`; 5.3.1.18; 5.1.2.2 (L6.1); 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4 (L5.7); 4.4.2.6 (L5.10); `HTT.A.2.8.2/projective` (F3.2), `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions` (F1.5); `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction` (L1.2).

**κ-continuous functors, κ-compact objects and κ-compact left fibrations** (`SSet.IsCardinalContinuous`, `SSet.IsCardinalPresentable`, `SSet.LeftFibration.IsCardinalPresentable`; HTT Definition 5.3.4.5, PDF p. 414). For an ∞-category C with small κ-filtered colimits: a functor out of C is κ-continuous when it preserves κ-filtered colimits; an object X is κ-compact when its corepresented functor `j_X : C ⟶ Ŝ` is κ-continuous, and compact when ω-compact; a left fibration `C̃ ⟶ C` is κ-compact when it is classified by a κ-continuous functor `C ⟶ Ŝ`. `C^κ` is the full subcategory of κ-compact objects (HTT Notation 5.3.4.6).

*Lean:* all for `[Fact κ.IsRegular]`. `SSet.HasCardinalFilteredColimits.{u} C κ := ∀ (K : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory K] [K.IsCardinalFiltered κ], SSet.HasColimitsOfShape (uliftFunctor.{v}.obj K) (uliftFunctor.{u}.obj C)` (propose; L5.6) for `C : SSet.{v}`. `SSet.IsCardinalContinuous F κ (hC : SSet.HasCardinalFilteredColimits.{u} C κ)` for `F : C ⟶ D` of quasicategories: `∀ K … (p̄ : rightCone (uliftFunctor.{v}.obj K) ⟶ uliftFunctor.{u}.obj C), SSet.IsColimitDiagram p̄ → SSet.IsColimitDiagram (p̄ ≫ uliftFunctor.map F)`. `SSet.IsCardinalPresentable X κ hC := IsCardinalContinuous (SSet.corepresented C X) κ hC.uliftFunctor`, since `SSet.corepresented C X` has source `uliftFunctor.obj C`, with the lemma `SSet.HasCardinalFilteredColimits.uliftFunctor`; `SSet.LeftFibration.IsCardinalPresentable φ κ hC` as in 5.1.6.5, with κ-continuity in place of preserving small colimits. The existence of small κ-filtered colimits is the explicit argument hC, as in 5.4.2.5. Mathlib's `IsCardinalPresentable` is the 1-categorical counterpart and applies to `hC` only.

**Checks.** In `P(S)`, every `j(s)` is κ-compact for every κ (5.1.6.8). Completely compact objects are κ-compact. `X` is κ-compact exactly when `C_{X/} ⟶ C` is a κ-compact left fibration (5.3.4.8 (1)).

*Needs:* 5.3.1.7; `HTT.5.1.6/intro`; 3.3.2.2, 3.3.2.8; `HTT.1.2.15/intro`.

**κ-continuous functors are closed under κ-small limits** (HTT Lemma 5.3.4.7, PDF p. 414). For C with small κ-filtered colimits, the full subcategory of `Fun(C, Ŝ)` on the κ-continuous functors is closed under κ-small limits.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if`; 5.1.2.2; 5.3.1.7, 5.3.4.5.

**κ-compact left fibrations** (HTT Lemma 5.3.4.8, PDF p. 414). For C with small κ-filtered colimits:

1. an object X is κ-compact exactly when `C_{X/} ⟶ C` is a κ-compact left fibration;
2. the pullback of a κ-compact left fibration along a κ-continuous functor is κ-compact;
3. the κ-compact left fibrations over C are closed under κ-small homotopy limits for the covariant model structure: homotopy pullbacks, κ-small products, and, for κ uncountable, homotopy limits of towers.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: (3) reduces to colimits indexed by κ-filtered posets (5.3.1.18) and, through straightening (2.2.1.2), to the fact that κ-filtered homotopy colimit diagrams of Kan complexes are closed under κ-small homotopy limits, the input of 5.3.3.3.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.3.3.3/kan-complexes`; 5.3.4.5; 5.3.1.7, 5.3.1.18; 2.2.1.2; `HTT.2.1.4.8/after` (L2.6); `HTT.A.2.4.3/after`; `HTT.A.2.8.7/after`.

**Compactness in arrow categories, products and towers** (HTT Lemmas 5.3.4.9–5.3.4.12, PDF pp. 415–416).

- A morphism between κ-compact objects is a κ-compact object of `Fun(Δ[1], C)` (5.3.4.9).
- For a κ-small family of ∞-categories `C_α` with small κ-filtered colimits, the product has them, and an object whose components are κ-compact is κ-compact (5.3.4.10).
- For a tower `⋯ ⟶ X(1) ⟶ X(0) ⟶ S` of left fibrations, the inverse limit is a homotopy limit in the covariant model structure on `SSet/S` (5.3.4.11).
- For κ uncountable and a tower `⋯ ⟶ C₁ ⟶ C₀` of ∞-categories with small κ-filtered colimits along κ-continuous categorical fibrations, the limit C has small κ-filtered colimits, the projections are κ-continuous, and an object with κ-compact images in every `C_i` is κ-compact (5.3.4.12).

*Needs:* 5.3.4.8; 2.1.2.1, 2.1.3.3 (L2.3–L2.4); 2.1.4.5, `HTT.2.1.4.8/after` (L2.6); `HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration`; A.2.1.1; A.1.1.1.

**Retracts of κ-compact objects** (HTT Remark 5.3.4.16, PDF p. 419). `C^κ` is closed under retracts.

*Needs:* 5.1.6.3; 5.3.1.7, 5.3.4.5; 5.1.0.1, `HTT.5.1.3/intro`; `HTT.4.4.5/intro`.

The rest of §5.3.4 (5.3.4.13–5.3.4.15, 5.3.4.17–5.3.4.18) is in L7: Lurie's proof of 5.3.4.13 uses Lemma 5.4.5.7.

### L6.7 Ind-completion

**`Ind_κ`** (`SSet.ind`; HTT Definition 5.3.5.1, Remark 5.3.5.2, PDF p. 421). For a small ∞-category C, `Ind_κ(C) ⊆ P(C)` is the full subcategory on the presheaves whose classified right fibration `C̃ ⟶ C` has κ-filtered total space; `Ind(C) = Ind_ω(C)`. This is the Conventions' definition (Kerodon's κ-flat presheaves are a characterization). The Yoneda embedding factors through `Ind_κ(C)`, since `j(c)` classifies `C_{/c} ⟶ C`, which has a final object (5.3.5.2).

*Lean:* `SSet.ind κ C := fullEnhancedSubcategory (SSet.presheaf C) fun F ↦ IsCardinalFiltered (pullback (SSet.opFunctor.map (ihomVertexEquiv F)) SSet.universalRightFibration) κ` for a small quasicategory C and `[Fact κ.IsRegular]`, as in Lurie, with the helper `SSet.ihomVertexEquiv` (proposed in L5.9, 4.3.3.2) turning the vertex F of `SSet.presheaf C` into a map, with `SSet.universalRightFibration : Z' ⟶ S^op` the universal right fibration of §3.3.2 (3.3.2.6, L4.7; proposed name). `SSet.ind.yoneda κ C : uliftFunctor.obj C ⟶ SSet.ind κ C` (propose) from 5.3.5.2, and the instance `SSet.quasicategory_ind : Quasicategory (ind κ C)` (a full subcategory of the ∞-category `P(C)`; needed because `ind` is not reducible).

**Characterization: κ-flat presheaves** (separate target; Kerodon 9.3.4.7, Theorem 9.3.4.14). Kerodon's form views F as a functor `C^op ⟶ S` and goes through the left fibration it classifies, the pullback of `SSet.universalLeftFibration` along F, while `SSet.ind` goes through the right fibration over C (pullback of `SSet.universalRightFibration`). *Lean:* `SSet.IsCardinalFlat F κ` (propose), the condition that the total space of the left fibration over `C^op` is κ-cofiltered (its opposite, up to equivalence the total space used by `SSet.ind`, is κ-filtered); the comparison lemma `SSet.universalLeftFibration_pullback_equiv_op` (propose), identifying that total space with the opposite of the total space used by `SSet.ind`, up to equivalence; and the target `SSet.mem_ind_iff_isCardinalFlat`.

**Checks.** `Ind_κ(Δ[0])` is the full subcategory of `S` on the contractible Kan complexes, equivalent to `Δ[0]`. For a small ordinary category A, `Ind(N A)` is equivalent to the nerve of Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Ind A` (HTT Remark 5.3.5.6).

*Needs:* 5.3.1.7, 5.3.1.17; 5.1.0.1, 5.1.5.2; 3.3.2.2, 3.3.2.7 (L4.7, L5.1); 2.0.0.3; `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**Stability under filtered colimits; objects of `Ind_κ`** (HTT Proposition 5.3.5.3, Corollary 5.3.5.4, PDF pp. 421–422). `Ind_κ(C) ⊆ P(C)` is stable under κ-filtered colimits (5.3.5.3). For a presheaf F on a small C, the following are equivalent: F is a colimit of `j ∘ p` for some `p : I ⟶ C` with I small and κ-filtered; F lies in `Ind_κ(C)`. If C has κ-small colimits, these are also equivalent to F preserving κ-small limits (5.3.5.4).

*Proof route.* 5.3.5.3 is Lurie's: through the right-fibration model of 5.1.1.1, reduce to κ-filtered posets (5.3.1.18) and strict diagrams (4.2.4.4), where homotopy colimits are computed by 4.2.4.1 and κ-filtered colimits of contravariant equivalences are contravariant equivalences. In 5.3.5.4, (3) ⇒ (2) is 5.3.2.9 (Lurie cites 5.3.3.3 at that step) with the representability of the universal right fibration (3.3.2.7); (1) ⇒ (3) is 5.3.3.3.

*Needs:* 5.3.5.1, 5.3.5.2; 5.1.1.1; 5.3.1.7, 5.3.1.18; 1.1.5.5; 3.3.2.5 (L4.7); 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4; `HTT.2.1.4.8/after`; `HTT.A.2.8.7/after`; 5.1.2.2, 5.1.3.2, 5.1.5.2, 5.1.5.3; 5.3.2.9, `HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if`; 3.3.2.7.

**Representables are κ-compact in `Ind_κ`** (HTT Proposition 5.3.5.5, PDF p. 422). For a small C, every `j(c)` is a κ-compact object of `Ind_κ(C)`.

*Needs:* 5.3.5.3; 5.1.2.2, 5.1.5.2; `HTT.5.1.6/intro`; 5.3.1.7, 5.3.4.5.

**Embedding into a cocomplete ∞-category; Kan extensions into `Ind_κ`** (HTT Lemmas 5.3.5.7–5.3.5.8, Remark 5.3.5.9, PDF pp. 423–424). Every ∞-category D (not necessarily small) has a fully faithful functor `i : D ⟶ D'` into an ∞-category with small colimits such that a small diagram `K^▷ ⟶ D` is a colimit exactly when its image is; take `D' = Fun(D, Ŝ)^op` (5.3.5.7). For a small C, `C⁰ ⊆ Ind_κ(C)` the essential image of j, and D with small κ-filtered colimits: every `f₀ : C⁰ ⟶ D` has a left Kan extension to `Ind_κ(C)`, and a functor `Ind_κ(C) ⟶ D` is a left Kan extension of its restriction to `C⁰` exactly when it is κ-continuous (5.3.5.8). The same argument applies to any class of colimits in place of κ-filtered ones (5.3.5.9); 5.1.5.5 and 5.3.5.8 are two instances, and 5.3.6.2 a third.

*Needs:* 5.1.2.2, 5.1.3.2 (Yoneda of `D^op`); 5.1.5.5; 5.3.5.4; 5.3.1.7, 5.3.4.5; 4.3.2.2 (L5.9); 5.1.5.7.

**The universal property of `Ind_κ`** (HTT Proposition 5.3.5.10, PDF p. 424). For a small ∞-category C and an ∞-category D with small κ-filtered colimits, restriction along j is an equivalence from the ∞-category of κ-continuous functors `Ind_κ(C) ⟶ D` to `Fun(C, D)`. Kerodon's universal property (9.3.1.1) is a characterization target.

*Lean:* `SSet.funCardinalContinuous P D κ hP` (propose), for `hP : HasCardinalFilteredColimits P κ`, the full subcategory of `Fun(P, D)` on κ-continuous functors (`IsCardinalContinuous`); the target is `IsCategoricalEquivalence` of the restriction `funCardinalContinuous (ind κ C) D κ hI ⟶ Fun(C, D)` along `SSet.ind.yoneda κ C`.

Kerodon's universal property (9.3.1.1) is stated in this κ-form as `SSet.ind_universal κ C`: there is `hI : HasCardinalFilteredColimits (ind κ C) κ` such that for every quasicategory `D : SSet.{u + 1}` with κ-filtered colimits, `(funCardinalContinuous (ind κ C) D κ hI).ι ≫ (MonoidalClosed.pre (ind.yoneda κ C)).app D` is a categorical equivalence. It thus also records that `Ind_κ(C)` has small κ-filtered colimits.

*Needs:* 5.3.5.8; 5.3.1.7, 5.3.4.5; 4.3.2.16 (L5.9).

**Recognizing `Ind_κ`** (HTT Proposition 5.3.5.11, PDF p. 425). For a small C, D with κ-filtered colimits, a κ-continuous `F : Ind_κ(C) ⟶ D` and `f = F ∘ j`: if f is fully faithful with κ-compact values, F is fully faithful; and F is an equivalence exactly when f is fully faithful, f lands in `D^κ`, and the `f(c)` generate D under κ-filtered colimits.

*Needs:* 5.3.5.4, 5.3.5.5; 5.1.3.1, 5.1.3.2; 5.1.6.10 (same argument), `HTT.5.1.6/intro`; 5.3.1.7; 5.3.4.5; `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`, `HTT.1.2.10/essentially-surjective`.

**Functoriality and right exactness** (HTT Proposition 5.3.5.13, PDF p. 427). For a functor `f : C ⟶ C'` of small ∞-categories, the following are equivalent: f is κ-right exact; restriction `P(C') ⟶ P(C)` carries `Ind_κ(C')` into `Ind_κ(C)`; `Ind_κ f` (the κ-continuous extension of `j ∘ f`) has a right adjoint. Then the restricted functor is that right adjoint.

*Needs:* 5.3.2.1; 5.3.5.10; 5.2.6.3 (L6.4); `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`.

**The Yoneda embedding into `Ind_κ` preserves κ-small colimits** (HTT Proposition 5.3.5.14, PDF p. 427). For a small C, `j : C ⟶ Ind_κ(C)` preserves every κ-small colimit that exists in C.

*Needs:* 5.3.2.1, 5.3.2.9; 5.3.5.4; 5.1.3.2; 1.2.13.5; A.1.1.1.

5.3.5.12 and 5.3.5.15 are in L7.

**Freely adjoining colimits: notation** (`SSet.funPreserving`, `SSet.funRespecting`; HTT Notation 5.3.6.1, PDF p. 430). For ∞-categories C, D and a collection R of diagrams `p_α : K_α^▷ ⟶ C`, `Fun_R(C, D) ⊆ Fun(C, D)` is spanned by the functors carrying every member of R to a colimit diagram. For a collection 𝒦 of simplicial sets, C admits 𝒦-indexed colimits when it admits K-indexed colimits for each K in 𝒦, and `Fun_𝒦(C, D)` is spanned by the functors preserving them.

*Lean:* `SSet.funRespecting R C D` and `SSet.funPreserving 𝒦 C D` as full subcategories (`fullEnhancedSubcategory`), with `R : Set (Σ K, K.rightCone ⟶ C)` and `𝒦 : Set SSet.{u}`.

*Needs:* `SSet.IsColimit`, `SSet.PreservesColimit`; `HTT.1.2.11/intro`.

### L6.8 Simplicial objects and groupoid objects

**Simplicial objects** (`SSet.simplicialObjects`, `SSet.augmentedSimplicialObjects`; HTT Definition 6.1.2.2, PDF p. 554). A simplicial object of an ∞-category C is a map `U : N(Δ)^op ⟶ C`, and an augmented simplicial object a map `N(Δ₊)^op ⟶ C`, with `Δ₊` the finite, possibly empty, linearly ordered sets. `C_Δ = Fun(N(Δ)^op, C)` and `C_{Δ₊}` are their ∞-categories, and `U_n = U([n])`.

*Lean:* `SSet.simplicialObjects C := (ihom (uliftFunctor.obj (nerve SimplexCategory).op)).obj C` (lifted, as below and as in `SSet.IsGroupoidObject`) and `SSet.augmentedSimplicialObjects C := uliftFunctor.obj (nerve AugmentedSimplexCategory).op ⟶ C`, with Mathlib's `SimplexCategory` and `AugmentedSimplexCategory = WithInitial SimplexCategory`, lifted to the universe of C.

**Checks.** For C the nerve of a category D, `C_Δ` is isomorphic to the nerve of Mathlib's `SimplicialObject D` (HTT Remark 6.1.2.3).

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.nerve`, `SimplexCategory`, `AugmentedSimplexCategory`; 1.2.7.2.

**A recognition lemma for trivial fibrations** (HTT Lemma 6.1.2.4, PDF p. 555). Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a map of simplicial sets that is bijective on vertices, has Y a Kan complex, has the right lifting property against every horn `Λ[n, i] ⊆ Δ[n]` with `n ≥ 2`, and is a weak homotopy equivalence. Then f is a trivial fibration.

*Proof route.* Lurie's reduction to lifting against `Λ[1, 0] ⊆ Δ[1]`, with the topological path argument replaced by a combinatorial one. X is a Kan complex (horns of dimension at least 2 lift through f; horns of dimension 1 fill by degenerate edges). Given an edge `e : f x ⟶ f x'` of Y, the bijections on `π₀` and `π₁` (F2.2) give an edge `x ⟶ x'` whose image is homotopic to e relative to the endpoints, and lifting against `Λ[2, i]` corrects it to a lift of e. Then f is a Kan fibration and a weak equivalence, hence trivial (F2.4).

*Needs:* homotopy groups of Kan complexes (F2.2); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences` (F2.4); 2.0.0.1.

**Geometric realization** (`SSet.IsGeometricRealization`; HTT Notation 6.1.2.12, PDF p. 561). For a simplicial object U of C, a geometric realization `|U•| : N(Δ₊)^op ⟶ C` is a colimit diagram extending U, through the identification of `N(Δ₊)^op` with the right cone `(N(Δ)^op)^▷` (`Δ₊` adjoins an initial object to Δ). It is a diagram, not an object. It is determined up to contractible choice (HTT Remark 6.1.2.13).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsGeometricRealization (U₊ : SSet.augmentedSimplicialObjects C) := SSet.IsColimitDiagram (e.hom ≫ U₊)`, where `e : rightCone (uliftFunctor.obj (nerve SimplexCategory).op) ≅ uliftFunctor.obj (nerve AugmentedSimplexCategory).op` is the canonical isomorphism (the empty set is final in `Δ₊^op`); provide `e`.

**Checks.** A constant simplicial object at X has geometric realization X (`N(Δ)^op` is weakly contractible, 4.4.4.10).

*Needs:* 6.1.2.2; `SSet.IsColimit` (L1.5), `SSet.rightCone`.

Notation: for a simplicial object `U : N(Δ)^op ⟶ C` and a simplicial set K, `C_{/U[K]}` is the over-category of the diagram `N(Δ_{/K})^op ⟶ N(Δ)^op ⟶ C`.

**Groupoid objects** (`SSet.IsGroupoidObject`; HTT Proposition 6.1.2.6, Definition 6.1.2.7, PDF pp. 556, 559). For an ∞-category C and a simplicial object U, the following are equivalent (6.1.2.6): for every weak homotopy equivalence `K ⟶ K'` bijective on vertices, `C_{/U[K']} ⟶ C_{/U[K]}` is a categorical equivalence; the same for such monomorphisms, as a categorical equivalence or as a trivial fibration; the same for `Λ[n, i] ⊆ Δ[n]`, `n ≥ 2`; the same for `Δ^S ⊔_{\{s\}} Δ^{S'} ⊆ Δ[n]` with `[n] = S ∪ S'`, `S ∩ S' = {s}`; and (Lurie's (4″)) every square `U([n]) ⟶ U(S), U(S') ⟶ U({s})` is a pullback in C. U is a groupoid object when these hold; `Gpd(C) ⊆ C_Δ` is their full subcategory (6.1.2.7).

*Parts.* Proposition 6.1.2.6 is formalized as five targets: the four parts that follow this entry, `HTT.6.1.2.6/eval` (`U[K]`, its slice maps, and the primed conditions), `HTT.6.1.2.6/pullback` ((4) ⇔ (4″)), `HTT.6.1.2.6/spine` ((1) ⇒ (4) and (4′) ⇒ (3)) and `HTT.6.1.2.6/horns` ((3) ⇒ (1), and (1) ⇒ (2) ⇒ (3)), and this entry's own target `HTT.6.1.2.6`, which combines them into the equivalences with `SSet.IsGroupoidObject`; Definition 6.1.2.7 is a separate target.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsGroupoidObject U` (propose) for a simplicial object `U : uliftFunctor.{u}.obj (nerve SimplexCategory).op ⟶ C` of a quasicategory `C : SSet.{u}`, defined by Lurie's (4″): for every n and every `S, S' ⊆ [n]` with `S ∪ S' = [n]` and `S ∩ S' = {s}`, the square `U([n]) ⟶ U(S), U(S') ⟶ U({s})` is `SSet.IsPullback`, the square being U composed with the nerve of the square of inclusions in Δ (a map `Δ[1] ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ C`), through the order isomorphisms `S ≅ [|S| − 1]`. This is the form users need; Lurie defines groupoid objects by the conditions of 6.1.2.6 together, so the other conditions are characterization targets.

*Lean (the other conditions):* every condition except (4″) uses `U[K]` for a simplicial set K, the diagram `N(Δ_{/K})^op ⟶ N(Δ)^op ⟶ C` of Notation 6.1.2.5, and the maps `C_{/U[K']} ⟶ C_{/U[K]}` induced by `K ⟶ K'`; both are defined in the part `HTT.6.1.2.6/eval`: the L6.8 helper `SSet.simplicialObjectEval U K`, that diagram itself rather than its limit, which C need not have (where the limit exists it is the value at K of the right Kan extension of U, and for `K = Δ[n]` it is `U([n])`, since `N(Δ_{/Δ[n]})^op` has the initial vertex `id_{[n]}`), and the slice maps `SSet.simplicialObjectEval.sliceMap U i : C_{/U[K']} ⟶ C_{/U[K]}` over these diagrams (Tau Ceti `SSet.slice`), induced by restriction along `N(Δ_{/K})^op ⟶ N(Δ_{/K'})^op` for `i : K ⟶ K'`. Then each remaining condition of 6.1.2.6 is a separate `iff` with `SSet.IsGroupoidObject U`: categorical equivalence (or trivial fibration) of `sliceMap U i` for every i in the stated class (weak homotopy equivalences bijective on vertices; such monomorphisms; `Λ[n, i] ⊆ Δ[n]` with `n ≥ 2`; `Δ^S ⊔_{\{s\}} Δ^{S'} ⊆ Δ[n]`).

**Checks.** The Čech nerve of any morphism in an ∞-category with pullbacks is a groupoid object (6.1.2.11); the nerve of a groupoid, as a simplicial object of `N(Set)`, is one.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the primed conditions by `HTT.6.1.2.6/eval`, (4) ⇔ (4″) by `HTT.6.1.2.6/pullback`, (1) ⇒ (4) and (4′) ⇒ (3) by `HTT.6.1.2.6/spine`, and the rest by `HTT.6.1.2.6/horns`. The weakly saturated class in the proof is A.1.2.2's (F1), not the strongly saturated classes of 5.5.4.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.2.6/eval`, `HTT.6.1.2.6/pullback`, `HTT.6.1.2.6/spine`, `HTT.6.1.2.6/horns` (below); `SSet.IsLimit`.

**Evaluating a simplicial object on a simplicial set** (`HTT.6.1.2.6/eval`, part 1 of 4 of groupoid objects above; HTT Notation 6.1.2.5 and the first step of the proof of Proposition 6.1.2.6, PDF pp. 556–557). For a simplicial object U of C and a simplicial set K, `U[K]` is the composite `N(Δ_{/K})^op ⟶ N(Δ)^op ⟶ C`. Its limit, where it exists, is the value at K of the right Kan extension of U, and the slice ∞-categories `C_{/U[K]}` are functorial in K. A monomorphism `K ⟶ K'` induces a right fibration `C_{/U[K']} ⟶ C_{/U[K]}`, so for monomorphisms "categorical equivalence" and "trivial fibration" agree: (2) ⇔ (2′), (3) ⇔ (3′) and (4) ⇔ (4′).

*Lean:* `SSet.simplicialObjectEval U K` and `SSet.simplicialObjectEval.sliceMap U i`, as in the entry above.

*Needs:* 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); 2.1.2.1 (L2.3); 2.4.4.6 (L3.7).

**Pullback form of the groupoid condition** (`HTT.6.1.2.6/pullback`, part 2 of 4 of groupoid objects above; HTT Proposition 6.1.2.6, (4) ⇔ (4″), PDF pp. 558–559). For `[n] = S ∪ S'` with `S ∩ S' = {s}` and `K = Δ^S ⊔_{\{s\}} Δ^{S'}`, the map `C_{/U[Δ[n]]} ⟶ C_{/U[K]}` is a categorical equivalence exactly when the square `U([n]) ⟶ U(S), U(S') ⟶ U({s})` is a pullback.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: compare both with slices over the restriction of U to the four-object category `{[n], S, S', {s}}`. On the `[n]` side use final objects. On the K side the inclusion of the three-object category into `Δ_{/K}` has a left adjoint, so its nerve is right anodyne (2.1.2.11).

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.2.6/eval`; 2.1.2.11 (L2.4); `SSet.IsLimit`, `SSet.IsPullback`.

**Spine decompositions suffice for horns** (`HTT.6.1.2.6/spine`, part 3 of 4 of groupoid objects above; HTT Proposition 6.1.2.6, (1) ⇒ (4) and (4′) ⇒ (3), PDF p. 558). Condition (1) implies (4), and condition (4′) implies (3).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: induction on n. For `0 ≤ i < n` with `(n, i) ≠ (2, 0)`, factor `Δ^{n−1} ⊔ Δ^{n−1,n} ⊆ Λ[n, i] ⊆ Δ[n]`; two-out-of-three in the class of maps inducing slice equivalences (with (4′) for the composite) gives the horn. `Λ[2, 0]` is itself of the form `Δ^S ⊔ Δ^{S'}` after relabelling, and `i = n` is dual.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.2.6/eval`.

**Horns suffice** (`HTT.6.1.2.6/horns`, part 4 of 4 of groupoid objects above; HTT Proposition 6.1.2.6, (3) ⇒ (1), PDF pp. 557–558). Condition (3) implies (1); and (1) ⇒ (2) ⇒ (3) are immediate.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, with the weakly saturated class of A.1.2.2. The cofibrations inducing trivial fibrations of slices form a weakly saturated class containing the horns `Λ[n, i] ⊆ Δ[n]`, `n ≥ 2`. For a weak equivalence `f : K ⟶ K'` bijective on vertices, factor through A.1.2.5 to a map g that is bijective on vertices, lifts against those horns, has Kan target and is a weak equivalence. Then g is a trivial fibration by 6.1.2.4, and a retract argument puts f in the class.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.2.6/eval`; 6.1.2.4; A.1.2.5 (F1.1).

**Čech nerves** (`SSet.IsCechNerve`; HTT Proposition 6.1.2.11 and the definition after it (`HTT.6.1.2.11/after`), PDF pp. 559–561). For an augmented simplicial object `U⁺ : N(Δ₊)^op ⟶ C`, the following are equivalent: `U⁺` is a right Kan extension of its restriction to `N(Δ₊^{≤0})^op`; the underlying simplicial object is a groupoid object and `U₁ ⟶ U₀ ⇉ U₋₁` is a pullback square (6.1.2.11). `U⁺` is then a Čech nerve, of `u : U₀ ⟶ U₋₁`, determined by u up to equivalence (`/after`).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsCechNerve U⁺ := SSet.IsRightKanExtension` (L5.9, dual of `SSet.IsLeftKanExtension`) of `U⁺ : uliftFunctor.{u}.obj (nerve AugmentedSimplexCategory).op ⟶ C`, for a quasicategory `C : SSet.{u}`, along the full inclusion of `N(Δ₊^{≤0})^op`. Propose.

The characterization (6.1.2.11 (2)) is `SSet.isCechNerve_iff : IsCechNerve U ↔ IsGroupoidObject (augmentationInclusion ≫ U) ∧ IsPullback (cechSquare ≫ U)`, with the square `U₁ ⟶ U₀ ⇉ U₋₁` as `SSet.cechSquare : Δ[1] ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ N(Δ₊)^op` (propose), formed by the two faces `[0] ⇉ [1]` and the augmentation.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.2.6/pullback`, 6.1.2.7; 4.2.3.10 (L5.6); 4.4.2.2 (L5.10); `SSet.IsLeftKanExtension` (L5.9).

**Pointed objects and group objects** (`HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed`; HTT Definition 7.2.2.1, PDF p. 742). For an ∞-category X with a final object 1, a pointed object is a morphism `1 ⟶ X`; `X_*` is their full subcategory of `Fun(Δ[1], X)`. A group object is a groupoid object `U_•` with `U₀` final; `Grp(X) ⊆ X_Δ` is their full subcategory. (The Eilenberg–MacLane objects of 7.2.2.1 belong to L11.)

*Lean:* `SSet.pointedObjects X` (full subcategory of `Fun(Δ[1], X)` on edges with final source) and `SSet.IsGroupObject U := IsGroupoidObject U ∧ IsTerminalVertex (U [0])`, with `SSet.grp X`. Propose.

*Needs:* 6.1.2.7; `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**Effective groupoids** (`SSet.IsEffectiveGroupoid`; HTT Definition 6.1.2.14, PDF p. 561). A simplicial object U is an effective groupoid when it extends to a colimit diagram `U₊ : N(Δ₊)^op ⟶ C` (a geometric realization, 6.1.2.12) that is a Čech nerve (above).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsEffectiveGroupoid U := ∃ U₊, U₊ extends U ∧ IsGeometricRealization U₊ ∧ IsCechNerve U₊`.

**Checks.** In an ∞-category with pullbacks, the Čech nerve of `u : U₀ ⟶ U₋₁` has `U₁ ≃ U₀ ×_{U₋₁} U₀`. In `S`, the Čech nerve of the map from a point to a connected X has `U₁ ≃ ΩX`.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.2.11/after`; 6.1.2.2, 6.1.2.12; 1.2.13.5.

**Semisimplicial objects** (`SSet.semisimplicialObjects`; HTT Notation 6.5.3.6, PDF p. 694). Let `Δ_s ⊆ Δ` be the subcategory with the same objects and the injective order-preserving maps. A semisimplicial object of an ∞-category X is a map `N(Δ_s)^op ⟶ X`.

*Lean:* `SimplexCategory.inj` (defined at 6.5.3.7, L5.7: the wide subcategory of `SimplexCategory` on the monomorphisms, Mathlib `WideSubcategory` of `MorphismProperty.monomorphisms`), and `SSet.semisimplicialObjects X := (ihom (uliftFunctor.obj (nerve SimplexCategory.inj).op)).obj X`. The cofinality of `N(Δ_s)^op ⊆ N(Δ)^op` (HTT Lemma 6.5.3.7) is proved in L5.7, where it is placed for its use in 4.2.3.15 (L5.6).

*Needs:* Mathlib `SimplexCategory`, `WideSubcategory`; 1.2.7.2.

### L6.9 Kan extensions as adjoints

These two statements of HTT §§4.3.2–4.3.3 sit here because their proofs use 5.2.2.6, 5.2.2.8 and 5.2.4.3.

**Relative left Kan extension is left adjoint to restriction** (HTT Proposition 4.3.2.17, PDF p. 302). Let `C ⟶ D' ⟵ D` be functors of ∞-categories with `p : D ⟶ D'` a categorical fibration, and `i : C⁰ ⊆ C` a full subcategory such that every functor in `Map_{D'}(C⁰, D)` has a p-left Kan extension. Then the left Kan extension functor `i_! : Map_{D'}(C⁰, D) ⟶ Map_{D'}(C, D)` (4.3.2.16) is left adjoint to restriction `i^*`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the identity is a unit transformation (5.2.2.8), because restriction of right-pinched morphism spaces is a trivial fibration (4.3.2.12).

*Needs:* 4.3.2.2, 4.3.2.12, 4.3.2.16 (L5.9); 5.2.2.7, 5.2.2.8 (L6.4); `HTT.2.2.5/categorical-fibration`; `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`.

**Left Kan extension along any map is left adjoint to restriction** (HTT Proposition 4.3.3.7, PDF p. 306). For a map `δ : K⁰ ⟶ K¹` of simplicial sets and an ∞-category D, a left Kan extension functor `δ_! : Fun(K⁰, D) ⟶ Fun(K¹, D)` (one that sends each F, with its unit, to a left Kan extension of F along δ, `SSet.IsLeftKanExtensionAlong`) is left adjoint to `δ^*`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: factor δ through the mapping cylinder `K⁰ ⟶ M^op(δ) ⟶ K¹` (4.3.3.1, with HTT's form 4.3.3.2 of L5.9); the first restriction has left adjoint `i_!` by 4.3.2.17, the retraction `r^*` is right adjoint to restriction to `K¹` by the dual of 5.2.4.3 (that restriction is a coCartesian fibration by 2.4.7.12, and `r^*F` is final in the fibre over F), and compose (5.2.2.6).

*Needs:* 4.3.2.17; 4.3.2.2, 4.3.3.1, 4.3.3.2 (L5.9); 5.2.2.6, 5.2.4.3 (L6.4); 2.4.7.12 (L3.9); 2.4.2.1; `HTT.1.2.12/final`; `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`.

## Layer L7: Accessible and presentable ∞-categories

HTT §§5.4–5.5, with the parts of §§5.3.4–5.3.5 whose proofs use §5.4.5, groupoid objects (§6.1.2) in presentable ∞-categories, and three Reedy statements about ∞-categories (A.2.9.14, A.2.9.16, A.2.9.18). Definitions follow the Conventions: essentially κ-small and locally small are the Conventions' size notions (5.4.1.3, 5.4.1.7), accessible means `Ind_κ(C₀) ≃ C` with C₀ small (5.4.2.1), with the generator form 5.4.2.2 as a characterization, and presentable means accessible with small colimits (5.5.0.1). Cardinal hypotheses are stated in the Universes convention's vocabulary; `κ ≪ τ` is A.2.6.3 (F1.6): `τ₀^{κ₀} < τ` for all `τ₀ < τ`, `κ₀ < κ`. `Cat∞^` is the ∞-category of not necessarily small ∞-categories, `SSet.catInfty` one universe up (L4.1); subcategories of `Cat∞^` and of `Cat∞` are HTT 1.2.11 subcategories (L1.3). The L6 names used below (`SSet.presheaf`, `SSet.ind`, `SSet.IsCardinalPresentable`, `SSet.IsCardinalContinuous`, `SSet.IsReflectiveLocalization`, `SSet.funL`) are those of Layer L6.

The items are written in the book's order. Two of them need later items of the layer:

- L7.1 needs L7.4: the gluing step (1) of the proof of 5.3.4.13 applies Lemma 5.4.5.7.
- L7.1 needs L7.2: the proof of 5.3.5.12 starts from the local smallness of `P(C)` (5.4.1.7–5.4.1.8).
- L7.5 needs L7.6: the proof of 5.5.3.17 applies Lemmas 5.5.4.17 and 5.5.4.18.

Inside L7.6, Proposition 5.5.4.15 uses Definition 5.5.5.1 and Lemma 5.5.5.14, stated later in the same item; inside L7.4, Lemma A.2.9.18 uses Lemma 5.4.5.10. The other in-item uses of later statements follow Lurie's order (a result, then its lemmas): 5.4.2.2 uses 5.4.2.4 (L7.3); 5.4.5.4 uses 5.4.5.3 (L7.4); 5.5.1.1 uses 5.5.1.2–5.5.1.4 and 5.5.1.2 uses 5.5.1.3–5.5.1.4 (L7.5); `HTT.5.5.4.2/iii⇒i` uses 5.5.4.4, and 5.5.5.7 uses 5.5.5.10 and 5.5.5.14 (L7.6); 5.5.8.10 uses 5.5.8.11–5.5.8.12, 5.5.9.2 uses 5.5.9.9, and 5.5.9.7 uses 5.5.9.13 (L7.8). Nothing in these lemmas uses the statements that need them, so the formalization order is: §5.4.5 through 5.4.5.7, then L7.1 through 5.3.4.18, then L7.2, then the rest of L7.1 and of L7.4; and in L7.5–L7.6, §5.5.4 up to 5.5.4.14 and §5.5.5, then 5.5.4.15–5.5.4.20, then 5.5.3.17–5.5.3.18.

### L7.1 Compact objects of functor and presheaf ∞-categories

**κ-compact diagrams** (HTT Proposition 5.3.4.13, PDF p. 417). Let κ be regular and C an ∞-category with small κ-filtered colimits. If K is a κ-small simplicial set and `f : K ⟶ C` takes every vertex to a κ-compact object, then f is a κ-compact object of `Fun(K, C)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's induction on K: good simplicial sets are closed under pushouts along monomorphisms (by 5.4.5.7 applied to the categorical pullback square of functor ∞-categories, whose maps preserve κ-filtered colimits by 5.1.2.2), under categorical equivalences, and under κ-small coproducts (5.3.4.10); simplices reduce to `Δ[1]` (5.3.4.9) through the spine; then skeleta, and for κ uncountable the tower of skeleta (5.3.4.11–5.3.4.12).

*Needs:* 5.1.2.2 (L6.1); 5.3.4.9–5.3.4.12 (L6.6); 5.4.5.7 (L7.4); `SSet.IsCardinalPresentable` (L6.6).

**Compact left fibrations of diagrams; closure under κ-small colimits** (HTT Corollaries 5.3.4.14–5.3.4.15, PDF p. 419). For C with small κ-filtered colimits and a κ-small `p : K ⟶ C` with κ-compact values, the left fibration `C_{p/} ⟶ C` is κ-compact (5.3.4.14). Hence the full subcategory `C^κ` of κ-compact objects is stable under every κ-small colimit that exists in C (5.3.4.15).

*Needs:* 5.3.4.13; 5.3.4.8 (L6.6); 5.1.2.2.

**κ-compact presheaves** (HTT Proposition 5.3.4.17, PDF p. 420). For a small ∞-category C, κ regular, and `X ∈ P(C)`, the following are equivalent: X is a retract of a colimit of `j ∘ p` for some κ-small `p : K ⟶ C`; X is κ-compact.

*Needs:* 5.3.4.15, 5.3.4.16 (L6.6); 5.1.5.3, 5.1.6.8 (L6.3); 4.2.3.11 (L5).

**κ-small colimits and the Yoneda embedding into `P^κ(C)`** (HTT Proposition 5.3.4.18, PDF p. 420). For a small idempotent complete ∞-category C and κ regular, let `P^κ(C) ⊆ P(C)` be the κ-compact presheaves. C has κ-small colimits exactly when `j : C ⟶ P^κ(C)` has a left adjoint.

*Needs:* 5.3.4.15, 5.3.4.17; 5.1.2.2, 5.1.3.2 (L6.1); 5.2.4.2 (L6.4).

**`P^κ(C)` is essentially small and generates `P(C)`** (HTT Proposition 5.3.5.12, PDF p. 426). For a small ∞-category C and κ regular, `P^κ(C)` is essentially small; for a small D with an equivalence `i : D ⟶ P^κ(C)`, the κ-continuous extension `F : Ind_κ(D) ⟶ P(C)` of i (5.3.5.10) is an equivalence.

*Needs:* 5.3.4.15, 5.3.4.17; 5.3.5.10–5.3.5.11 (L6.7); 5.1.5.3; 4.2.3.11; 5.4.1.7, 5.4.1.8 (L7.2: `P(C)` is locally small, so the full subcategory on a small set of objects is essentially small).

**`Ind_κ` commutes with finite poset diagrams** (HTT Proposition 5.3.5.15, PDF p. 428). For a small ∞-category C, κ regular, and a finite partially ordered set A, the functor `Fun(N(A), C) ⟶ Fun(N(A), Ind_κ(C))` induced by j induces an equivalence `Ind_κ(Fun(N(A), C)) ⟶ Fun(N(A), Ind_κ(C))`. Lurie's Warning 5.3.5.16 records that finite simplicial sets in place of `N(A)` do not work.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.5.3.5.15/ff-compact` (the induced functor is fully faithful with κ-compact image), `HTT.5.3.5.15/filtered` (diagrams in C over a diagram in `Ind_κ(C)` form a κ-filtered ∞-category) and `HTT.5.3.5.15/colimit` (each diagram is their colimit, which proves the statement), and this entry's own target `HTT.5.3.5.15`, which collects them.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.3.5.15/ff-compact`, `HTT.5.3.5.15/filtered`, `HTT.5.3.5.15/colimit` (below).

**Diagrams in C are compact in `Fun(N(A), Ind_κ(C))`** (`HTT.5.3.5.15/ff-compact`, part 1 of 3 of `Ind_κ` commuting with finite poset diagrams above; steps (i) and (ii) of the proof of HTT Proposition 5.3.5.15, PDF p. 428). For a small ∞-category C, κ regular and a finite poset A, the functor `j' : Fun(N(A), C) ⟶ Fun(N(A), Ind_κ(C))` induced by the Yoneda embedding is fully faithful, with essential image consisting of κ-compact objects.

*Needs:* 5.3.4.13.

**Diagrams in C over a diagram in `Ind_κ(C)`** (`HTT.5.3.5.15/filtered`, part 2 of 3 of `Ind_κ` commuting with finite poset diagrams above; proof of HTT Proposition 5.3.5.15 (a), PDF pp. 428–429). For a finite poset A and `F : N(A) ⟶ Ind_κ(C)`, the ∞-category `D = Fun(N(A), C) ×_{Fun(N(A), Ind_κ(C))} Fun(N(A), Ind_κ(C))_{/F}` is κ-filtered.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: by 5.3.1.12 it suffices to test κ-small posets B. Enumerate A along a linear extension and extend one element `a_k` at a time. Each extension is an object of a slice of `C_{/F(a_k)}`, κ-filtered because `F(a_k) ∈ Ind_κ(C)`, after replacing `A_{≥a_k}` by `{a_k}` (a left anodyne inclusion).

*Needs:* `HTT.5.3.5.15/ff-compact`; 5.3.1.12 (L6.6).

**Diagrams in `Ind_κ(C)` as filtered colimits** (`HTT.5.3.5.15/colimit`, part 3 of 3 of `Ind_κ` commuting with finite poset diagrams above; HTT Proposition 5.3.5.15, PDF p. 428, proof pp. 428–429). The statement of 5.3.5.15 above.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: by 5.3.5.11 and `HTT.5.3.5.15/ff-compact`, it suffices that F is a colimit of `D ⟶ Fun(N(A), C)` with D from `HTT.5.3.5.15/filtered`. Check this pointwise at `a ∈ A`, where `D ⟶ D(a)` is cofinal by Theorem A: its comma categories are filtered by the argument of `HTT.5.3.5.15/filtered`, hence weakly contractible (5.3.1.20).

*Needs:* `HTT.5.3.5.15/filtered`; 4.1.3.1 (L5.4); 5.3.1.20 (L6.6); 5.3.5.11 (L6.7).

### L7.2 Size

Smallness of a simplicial set is HTT §1.2.15: K is κ-small when it has fewer than κ nondegenerate simplices (for κ uncountable, equivalently fewer than κ simplices). The size notions below constrain homotopy types, not sets of simplices (Universes convention), and are stated for κ uncountable regular.

**Homotopies relative to the boundary in a simplicial nerve** (HTT Lemma 5.4.1.1, PDF p. 437). For a simplicial category C, `n ≥ 1` and `f₀ : ∂Δ[n] ⟶ N(C)` with `X = f₀(0)`, `Y = f₀(n)`, extensions f, f' of `f₀` to `Δ[n]` correspond to extensions g, g' of the induced `∂(Δ[1])^{n−1} ⟶ Map_C(X, Y)`, and f, f' are homotopic relative to `∂Δ[n]` exactly when g, g' are homotopic relative to `∂(Δ[1])^{n−1}`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: both are left homotopy in under-categories of the Joyal and Bergner model structures; compare through the Quillen equivalence 2.2.5.1.

*Needs:* 2.2.5.1 (L3.8); 1.1.5.10 (L1.4).

**Essentially κ-small ∞-categories** (`SSet.IsEssentiallyCardinalSmall`, `SSet.IsEssentiallySmall`; HTT Proposition 5.4.1.2, Definition 5.4.1.3, PDF pp. 437–439). For an ∞-category C and κ uncountable regular, the following are equivalent:

1. C has fewer than κ equivalence classes of objects, and every `π_i(Hom^R_C(X, Y), f)` is κ-small;
2. a minimal model of C (L3.3) is κ-small;
3. some κ-small ∞-category is equivalent to C;
4. some κ-small simplicial set admits a categorical equivalence to C;
5. C is κ-compact as an object of `Cat∞`.

C is *essentially κ-small* when these hold, and *essentially small* when it is essentially κ-small for some small regular κ (5.4.1.3).

*Parts.* Proposition 5.4.1.2 is formalized as six targets: the five parts that follow this entry, `HTT.5.4.1.2/1⇒2` ((1) ⇒ (2)), `HTT.5.4.1.2/4⇒3` ((4) ⇒ (3), with (2) ⇒ (3) ⇒ (4)), `HTT.5.4.1.2/3⇒5` ((3) ⇒ (5)), `HTT.5.4.1.2/small⇒1` (κ-small ∞-categories satisfy (1), which passes to equivalences and retracts) and `HTT.5.4.1.2/5⇒1` ((5) ⇒ (1)), and this entry's own target `HTT.5.4.1.2`, which combines them into the equivalence; Definition 5.4.1.3 and the characterizations below are separate targets.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsEssentiallyCardinalSmall (C : SSet.{v}) [Quasicategory C] (κ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop`, with hypotheses `[Fact κ.IsRegular]` and `ℵ₀ < κ` in the statement: there are a quasicategory `D : SSet.{u}` with fewer than κ nondegenerate simplices and a categorical equivalence from `uliftFunctor.obj D` to `uliftFunctor.obj C` (condition (3), the Conventions' definition). `SSet.IsEssentiallySmall.{u} C`: `∃ (κ : Cardinal.{u}) (_ : Fact κ.IsRegular), ℵ₀ < κ ∧ IsEssentiallyCardinalSmall C κ`. Propose both names.

**Characterizations** (separate targets): conditions (1), (2), (4) and (5) of 5.4.1.2, each as an `iff`. Condition (1) is Kerodon's form (4.9.7.7, locally κ-small with κ-small `π₀(C^≃)`). *Lean:* all at `C : SSet.{u}`, `κ : Cardinal.{u}` regular with `ℵ₀ < κ`. (1) `SSet.isEssentiallyCardinalSmall_iff_homotopy`: "fewer than κ equivalence classes of objects" is `HasCardinalLT (π₀ (core C)) κ`, together with `HasCardinalLT (KanComplex.π i (rightMappingSpace C X Y) f) κ` for all X, Y, f and i. (2) `SSet.isEssentiallyCardinalSmall_iff_minimal`: *some* minimal model, `∃ D (i : D ⟶ C), Mono i ∧ IsCategoricalEquivalence i ∧ Quasicategory.IsMinimal D ∧ HasCardinalLT D.N κ` (minimal models are unique up to isomorphism, so "a" and "some" agree). (4) `SSet.isEssentiallyCardinalSmall_iff_sSet`: `∃ K (f : K ⟶ C), HasCardinalLT K.N κ ∧ IsCategoricalEquivalence f`. (5) `SSet.isEssentiallyCardinalSmall_iff_compact`: `IsCardinalPresentable` takes the κ-filtered colimits of `Cat∞` as an argument, so the statement is `∃ hC : HasCardinalFilteredColimits catInfty κ, IsCardinalPresentable (catInfty.vertexOf C) κ hC`; the universe is forced, since (5) puts C in `Cat∞.{u}`. *Needs:* 2.2.4.1, 2.2.5.1 (L2.8, L3.8), to compare Lurie's `Hom^R_C(X, Y)` with `Map_D(X, Y)` for a locally Kan D equivalent to `C[C]`.

**Checks.**

- A κ-small ∞-category is essentially κ-small; so is the nerve of a category with fewer than κ morphisms.
- `Δ[0]` and every finite ∞-category are essentially ℵ₁-small.
- The nerve of the category of countable sets is not essentially ℵ₁-small: `Hom(ℕ, ℕ)` has `2^ℵ₀` elements.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. (1) ⇒ (2) (`HTT.5.4.1.2/1⇒2`) counts simplices of a minimal model by induction on dimension with 5.4.1.1; Lurie first writes C as the nerve of a topological category, and the formalization takes instead the simplicial nerve of a locally Kan simplicial category equivalent to C (2.2.5.1, 2.2.0.1), which is what 5.4.1.1 needs. (4) ⇒ (3) (`HTT.5.4.1.2/4⇒3`) by a countable sequence of inner horn pushouts. (3) ⇒ (5) (`HTT.5.4.1.2/3⇒5`) computes κ-filtered colimits in `Cat∞` by marked simplicial sets (5.3.1.18, 4.2.4.4, 4.2.4.1) and the corepresented functor by 5.1.5.2. (5) ⇒ (1) (`HTT.5.4.1.2/5⇒1`, with `HTT.5.4.1.2/small⇒1`) writes C as the κ-filtered union of its κ-small sub-∞-categories and retracts C onto one.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.4.1.2/1⇒2`, `HTT.5.4.1.2/4⇒3`, `HTT.5.4.1.2/3⇒5`, `HTT.5.4.1.2/small⇒1`, `HTT.5.4.1.2/5⇒1` (below); `SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence` (L1.5); `SSet.uliftFunctor`.

**Small homotopy data give a small minimal model** (`HTT.5.4.1.2/1⇒2`, part 1 of 5 of essentially κ-small ∞-categories above; HTT Proposition 5.4.1.2, (1) ⇒ (2), PDF pp. 437–438). If C has fewer than κ equivalence classes of objects and κ-small homotopy sets of mapping spaces (κ uncountable regular), every minimal model of C is κ-small.

*Proof route.* As in the entry above: present C as the simplicial nerve of a locally Kan simplicial category (2.2.5.1, 2.2.0.1). By induction on n, each boundary `∂Δ[n] ⟶ C₀` has fewer than κ fillers up to homotopy relative to the boundary (5.4.1.1), and minimality makes homotopic fillers equal.

*Needs:* 5.4.1.1; minimal models (2.3.3.1–2.3.3.8, L3.3); 2.2.5.1 (L3.8); 2.2.0.1 (L2.8).

**Small presentations give small ∞-categories** (`HTT.5.4.1.2/4⇒3`, part 2 of 5 of essentially κ-small ∞-categories above; HTT Proposition 5.4.1.2, (4) ⇒ (3), PDF p. 438). If a κ-small simplicial set K admits a categorical equivalence to C, then some κ-small ∞-category is equivalent to C. Also (2) ⇒ (3) ⇒ (4).

*Proof route.* Attach all inner horns, countably often. Each stage is κ-small because κ is regular, and so is the union because κ is uncountable. The union is an ∞-category and K ⊆ union is inner anodyne, so the map to C extends.

*Needs:* 2.2.5.2 (L2.7: the inclusion of K into the union is inner anodyne, hence a categorical equivalence); minimal models (2.3.3.8, L3.3) for (2) ⇒ (3); `SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence` (L1.5).

**κ-small ∞-categories are κ-compact** (`HTT.5.4.1.2/3⇒5`, part 3 of 5 of essentially κ-small ∞-categories above; HTT Proposition 5.4.1.2, (3) ⇒ (5), PDF p. 438). A κ-small ∞-category is κ-compact as an object of `Cat∞`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: by 5.3.1.18 and 4.2.4.4 a κ-filtered diagram in `Cat∞` comes from a diagram of fibrant marked simplicial sets on a κ-filtered poset. Its ordinary colimit is a homotopy colimit, hence the ∞-categorical colimit (4.2.4.1). The functor corepresented by C (5.1.5.2) is `D ↦ (D^C)^≃`, which commutes with κ-filtered colimits since C is κ-small.

*Needs:* 5.1.5.2 (L6.3); 5.3.1.18 (L6.6); 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4 (L5.7).

**Small ∞-categories have small homotopy data** (`HTT.5.4.1.2/small⇒1`, part 4 of 5 of essentially κ-small ∞-categories above; used in HTT Proposition 5.4.1.2, (5) ⇒ (1), PDF p. 439). A κ-small ∞-category satisfies condition (1), and condition (1) is invariant under categorical equivalence and passes to retracts in `hCat∞`.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.2.7/homotopy-groups` (F2.2); `SSet.morphismSpace` (L1.5); Tau Ceti `SSet.rightMappingSpace` and 2.2.4.1 (L2.8, `SSet.isFullyFaithful_iff_rightMappingSpace`: a categorical equivalence induces homotopy equivalences of `Hom^R`, so condition (1) is invariant).

**Compact ∞-categories are retracts of small ones** (`HTT.5.4.1.2/5⇒1`, part 5 of 5 of essentially κ-small ∞-categories above; HTT Proposition 5.4.1.2, (5) ⇒ (1), PDF pp. 438–439). A κ-compact object of `Cat∞` satisfies condition (1); with the other parts this closes the cycle of 5.4.1.2 above.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: C is the union of its κ-small sub-∞-categories, a κ-filtered poset (cofinal among κ-small simplicial subsets since κ is uncountable). By the computation of `HTT.5.4.1.2/3⇒5`, `id_C` factors up to homotopy through one of them, so C is a retract of it in `hCat∞`; apply `HTT.5.4.1.2/small⇒1`. Comparing Lurie's `Hom^R_C` with mapping spaces uses 2.2.4.1.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.4.1.2/3⇒5`, `HTT.5.4.1.2/small⇒1`; 2.2.4.1 (L2.8).

**Cartesian fibrations with small base and fibres** (HTT Proposition 5.4.1.4, PDF p. 439). If `p : C ⟶ D` is a Cartesian fibration of ∞-categories, κ uncountable regular, D essentially κ-small and every fibre `C_D` essentially κ-small, then C is essentially κ-small.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.4.1.2/small⇒1` (condition (1) for D and for each fibre), `HTT.5.4.1.2/1⇒2` and `HTT.5.4.1.2/4⇒3` (back from (1) to (3) for C, through (2) ⇒ (3)); 2.4.4.2 (L3.7); `HTT.A.2.7/fibration-sequence` (F2.2, the long exact sequence of homotopy groups).

**Essentially small spaces** (HTT Corollary 5.4.1.5, PDF p. 439). For a Kan complex X and κ uncountable regular, the following are equivalent: every `π_n(X, x)` is κ-small; a minimal model of X is κ-small; X is homotopy equivalent to a κ-small Kan complex; some κ-small simplicial set is weakly homotopy equivalent to X; X is κ-compact in `S`; X is essentially κ-small as an ∞-category (Lurie writes "essentially small"; the proof, through 5.4.1.2, gives the κ-form). Tau Ceti `TauCeti.HasSmallSpaceModel` (a Kan model in universe u with comparison maps inverse up to simplicial homotopy) is the u-small form of the third condition; Tau Ceti main proves that a simplicial set with a small model has small `π₀` (`TauCeti.HasSmallSpaceModel.small_π₀`).

*Needs:* 5.4.1.2, `HTT.5.4.1.2/3⇒5`; 5.3.4.15 (L7.1); 5.1.5.2, 5.1.6.8 (L6.3); 3.3.4.5 (L5.1); 4.1.2.15 (L5.3); Tau Ceti `TauCeti.SmallSpaceModel`.

**Locally small ∞-categories** (Tau Ceti `SSet.IsLocallySmall`; HTT Proposition 5.4.1.7 and the definition after it (`HTT.5.4.1.7/after`), PDF p. 441). For an ∞-category C, the following are equivalent: every `Map_C(X, Y)` is essentially small; every full subcategory spanned by a small set of objects is essentially small (5.4.1.7). C is *locally small* when they hold (`/after`).

*Lean:* Tau Ceti main's `SSet.IsLocallySmall.{u} X`: every `Hom^R_X(x, y)` has a Kan model in `SSet.{u}` (`TauCeti.HasSmallSpaceModel`), kept as it stands and the Conventions' definition of local smallness; it is condition (1) through 5.4.1.5 (3). The second condition of 5.4.1.7 and the `Hom_C` form (through 4.2.1.8) are characterization targets.

**Checks.** Tau Ceti main proves that the nerve of a category is locally u-small exactly when the category is (`CategoryTheory.nerve.isLocallySmall_iff`); every small ∞-category is locally small.

*Needs:* 5.4.1.2, 5.4.1.5; 4.2.1.8 (L5.5) for the `Hom_C` form; Tau Ceti `SSet.IsLocallySmall`, `SSet.rightMappingSpace`.

**Functor ∞-categories into locally small ones** (HTT Example 5.4.1.8, PDF p. 441). If C is locally small and D essentially small, `Fun(D, C)` is locally small; in particular `P(D)` is locally small for small D. (Lurie's first sentence says "essentially small", but the argument proves, and later uses, local smallness.)

*Needs:* `HTT.5.4.1.2/small⇒1`, `HTT.5.4.1.2/1⇒2` (the minimal models of D and of each small full subcategory of a minimal C are small), 5.4.1.7; minimal models (L3.3).

### L7.3 Accessible ∞-categories

**κ-accessible ∞-categories** (`SSet.IsCardinalAccessible`, `SSet.IsAccessible`; HTT Definition 5.4.2.1, PDF p. 441). For κ regular, an ∞-category C is κ-accessible when there are a small ∞-category C₀ and an equivalence `Ind_κ(C₀) ⟶ C`; accessible when κ-accessible for some regular κ.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsCardinalAccessible (C : SSet.{v}) [Quasicategory C] (κ : Cardinal.{u}) [Fact κ.IsRegular] : Prop`: `∃ (C₀ : SSet.{u}) (_ : Quasicategory C₀)`, and a categorical equivalence `uliftFunctor.obj (SSet.ind κ C₀) ⟶ uliftFunctor.obj C`. `SSet.IsAccessible.{u} C := ∃ κ (_ : Fact κ.IsRegular), IsCardinalAccessible C κ`. Propose both. Mathlib's `IsCardinalAccessibleCategory` is the 1-categorical counterpart.

**Characterizations** (separate target): 5.4.2.2 below.

**Checks.**

- `Ind_κ(C₀)` is κ-accessible for small C₀; `S` and `P(C)` are accessible (5.4.2.7).
- For a small category C₀, `Ind_κ(N(C₀))` is equivalent to the nerve of the 1-categorical κ-Ind-completion (κ-filtered colimits of discrete spaces are discrete, so these presheaves are set-valued); hence the nerve of a category that is κ-accessible in Mathlib's sense (`IsCardinalAccessibleCategory`) is κ-accessible.
- A small ∞-category that is not idempotent complete (for instance the nerve of a non-idempotent-complete category) is not accessible (5.4.3.6).

*Needs:* `SSet.ind` (5.3.5.1, L6.7); `SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence`; `HTT.1.2.15/intro`.

**The generator characterization** (HTT Proposition 5.4.2.2, PDF p. 441). For an ∞-category C and κ regular, the following are equivalent: C is κ-accessible; C is locally small, has small κ-filtered colimits, `C^κ` is essentially small and generates C under small κ-filtered colimits; C has small κ-filtered colimits and an essentially small full subcategory of κ-compact objects generating C under small κ-filtered colimits. The last is the shape of Mathlib's `IsCardinalAccessibleCategory`.

*Lean:* `SSet.GeneratesUnderCardinalFilteredColimits (A : Set (C _⦋0⦌)) κ` (propose), the κ-filtered form of `SSet.GeneratesUnderColimits` (L6): the only full subcategory containing A and stable under colimits of small κ-filtered diagrams (K a quasicategory with `IsCardinalFiltered K κ`, the `IsStableUnderColimits` condition restricted to such K) is C itself. This is Lurie's meaning: HTT defines generation under colimits by this closure condition (§5.1.5, before Corollary 5.1.5.8, PDF p. 346), and "generates under small κ-filtered colimits" in 5.4.2.2 is read the same way. The target `SSet.isCardinalAccessible_tfae C κ` is the `List.TFAE` of: `IsCardinalAccessible C κ`; `IsLocallySmall C ∧ ∃ hC : HasCardinalFilteredColimits C κ, IsEssentiallySmall (compactObjects C κ hC) ∧ GeneratesUnderCardinalFilteredColimits {X | IsCardinalPresentable X κ hC} κ`; and `∃ hC, ∃ A`, all κ-compact, `fullEnhancedSubcategory C (· ∈ A)` essentially small, generating under small κ-filtered colimits. `SSet.compactObjects C κ hC` is the full subcategory `C^κ`, as in 5.5.1.1.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. The substantial step is that `Ind_κ(C₀)` has an essentially small set of κ-compact objects, which is Lemma 5.4.2.4 (Example 5.4.2.3: they need not come from C₀).

*Needs:* 5.4.2.4; 5.4.1.7, 5.4.1.8; 5.3.5.3–5.3.5.5, 5.3.5.10–5.3.5.11 (L6.7).

**Compact objects of `Ind_κ` form the idempotent completion** (HTT Lemma 5.4.2.4, PDF p. 442). For a small ∞-category C and κ regular, `j : C ⟶ Ind_κ(C)^κ` exhibits the κ-compact objects as an idempotent completion of C; in particular they form an essentially small ∞-category.

*Needs:* 5.1.3.1 (L6.1); 5.1.5.3 (L6.3); 5.3.1.10 (L6.6); 3.3.4.5; `SSet.IsIdempotentCompletion` (L6.2).

**Accessible functors** (`SSet.IsAccessibleFunctor`; HTT Definition 5.4.2.5, PDF p. 443). For C accessible, `F : C ⟶ C'` is accessible when it is κ-continuous for some regular κ; it is then τ-continuous for every regular `τ ≥ κ`.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsAccessibleFunctor F := ∃ (κ : Cardinal.{u}) (_ : Fact κ.IsRegular) (hC : SSet.HasCardinalFilteredColimits.{u} C κ), SSet.IsCardinalContinuous F κ hC`, for F between quasicategories; the κ-filtered-colimit hypothesis is the same explicit argument as in 5.3.4.5, supplied inside the `∃` because an accessible C has small κ-filtered colimits only for κ large enough (5.4.2.2). With `IsAccessible C` a hypothesis of the results, not of the definition (HTT Remark 5.4.2.6 allows C' arbitrary). Propose.

*Needs:* `SSet.IsCardinalContinuous` (5.3.4.5, L6.6).

**`S` and `P(C)` are accessible** (HTT Example 5.4.2.7, PDF p. 443). For a small ∞-category C, `P(C)` is accessible; in particular `S = P(Δ[0])` is.

*Needs:* 5.3.5.12 (L7.1).

**Raising the accessibility cardinal** (HTT Lemma 5.4.2.8, Proposition 5.4.2.9, PDF pp. 443–444). If `κ ≪ κ'`, every κ'-filtered partially ordered set is the union of its κ-filtered κ'-small subsets, and these form a κ'-filtered family (5.4.2.8). A κ-accessible ∞-category is κ'-accessible for every `κ' ≫ κ` (5.4.2.9). Lurie's Remark 5.4.2.10 notes that `κ' > κ` alone does not suffice.

*Needs:* A.2.6.3; 5.4.2.2; 5.3.4.15; 5.3.1.18; 4.2.3.4, 4.2.3.8 (L5).

**`Acc_κ`** (`SSet.accCardinal`; HTT Definition 5.4.2.14, PDF p. 445). For κ regular, `Acc_κ ⊆ Cat∞^` is the subcategory whose objects are the κ-accessible ∞-categories and whose morphisms are the κ-continuous functors preserving κ-compact objects; `Acc = ⋃_κ Acc_κ` is the ∞-category of accessible ∞-categories.

*Lean:* `SSet.accCardinal κ` and `SSet.acc`: HTT 1.2.11 subcategories of `SSet.catInfty.{u+1}`, given by the stated classes of objects and of morphisms (closed under equivalence and composition), as `catInfty.subcategory P W := SSet.subcategory catInfty (catInfty.objectClass P) (catInfty.functorClass W)` with `[(catInfty.functorClass W).IsMultiplicative]` an instance argument (a theorem for each class). P and W are phrased on quasicategories and functors through `catInftyObj v`, the quasicategory of a vertex, and `catInfty.homMk f`, the edge of a functor (L4.1). Propose.

*Needs:* 5.4.2.1, 5.4.2.5; 5.3.4.5; `HTT.1.2.11/intro`; `SSet.catInfty` (L4.1).

**Compact objects embed `Acc_κ` into `Cat∞^`** (HTT Proposition 5.4.2.15, PDF p. 445). For κ regular, let `θ : Acc_κ ⟶ Cat∞^` send C to `C^κ`. θ is fully faithful, and its essential image is the essentially small idempotent complete ∞-categories.

*Needs:* 5.4.2.14; 5.3.5.10; 5.4.2.4.

**Idempotent completion functor; `Ind_κ` as a localization** (HTT Proposition 5.4.2.16, the definition after it (`HTT.5.4.2.16/after`), Proposition 5.4.2.17, PDF p. 445). `Cat∞^∨ ⊆ Cat∞` is the full subcategory of idempotent complete ∞-categories; the inclusion has a left adjoint (5.4.2.16), the *idempotent completion functor* (`/after`). Composing it with the equivalence `Cat∞^∨ ≃ Acc_κ` of 5.4.2.15 gives `Ind_κ : Cat∞ ⟶ Acc_κ` (`/after`), which exhibits `Acc_κ` as a localization of `Cat∞` (5.4.2.17; HTT's "localization" here is the reflective localization of 5.2.7.2).

*Lean:* `SSet.catInftyIdem` (propose), the full subcategory (`fullEnhancedSubcategory`) of `SSet.catInfty.{u}` on the C with `SSet.IsIdempotentComplete C`, with inclusion `ι`, and the instance `Quasicategory catInfty` (L4.1). `SSet.IsIdempotentCompletionFunctor (L : ⟨SSet.catInfty.{u}, _⟩ ⟶ ⟨SSet.catInftyIdem, _⟩) : Prop := Nonempty (Bicategory.Adjunction L (QCat.homMk (Subcomplex.ι _)))` in `SSet.QCat.bicategory` (propose). 5.4.2.16 is `∃ L, IsIdempotentCompletionFunctor L`, equivalently `∃ L, SSet.IsReflectiveLocalization L` with right adjoint ι (`IsReflectiveLocalization` is a `Prop` about the left adjoint). `Ind_κ` is defined only up to equivalence (HTT Remark 5.4.2.18): state 5.4.2.17 as the existence of `F : uliftFunctor.obj SSet.catInfty.{u} ⟶ SSet.accCardinal κ` (`accCardinal κ` is a subcomplex of `SSet.catInfty.{u+1}`, one universe above `SSet.catInfty.{u}`, so the source is lifted as the Universes convention requires) with `SSet.IsReflectiveLocalization F` and `F(C)` equivalent to `SSet.ind κ C` for every C. Propose.

*Needs:* 5.4.2.15; 5.1.4.2, 5.1.4.9 (L6.2); 5.2.7.8 (L6.5).

**Filtered colimits of essentially small Kan complexes** (HTT Lemmas 5.4.3.1–5.4.3.2, PDF pp. 446–447). For uncountable regular `κ < τ`, a τ-filtered poset A and `F : A ⟶ Kan` with essentially κ-small values, every τ-small `A₀ ⊆ A` lies in a filtered τ-small `A₀' ⊆ A` with `colim_{A₀'} F ⟶ colim_A F` a homotopy equivalence (5.4.3.1); the same holds simultaneously for a τ-small family of such diagrams (5.4.3.2).

*Needs:* 5.4.1.5; `HTT.A.2.7/kan-weak-equivalences` (F2.2, with filtered colimits of Kan complexes).

**Redundant filtered colimits** (HTT Lemma 5.4.3.3, Proposition 5.4.3.4, PDF pp. 447–448). Let `κ < τ` be uncountable regular, C a τ-small ∞-category with essentially κ-small morphism spaces, K τ-filtered and `p : K ⟶ C`. A colimit of `j ∘ p` in `P(C)` is already a colimit over some τ-small sub-diagram `K₀ ⟶ K` (5.4.3.3), and it is a retract of `j(C)` for some object C (5.4.3.4).

*Needs:* 5.4.3.1–5.4.3.2; 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4; 5.1.2.2; 5.3.1.18.

**Small accessible ∞-categories** (HTT Corollaries 5.4.3.5–5.4.3.6, PDF pp. 448–449). Under the hypotheses of 5.4.3.4, `j : C ⟶ Ind_τ(C)` exhibits `Ind_τ(C)` as an idempotent completion of C (5.4.3.5). A small ∞-category is accessible exactly when it is idempotent complete, and then every functor from it to an accessible ∞-category is accessible (5.4.3.6).

*Needs:* 5.4.3.4; 5.3.1.10; 5.3.5.10.

**Sections of coCartesian fibrations with filtered fibres** (HTT Lemmas 5.4.4.1–5.4.4.2, PDF pp. 449–450). For τ regular and a coCartesian fibration `q : Y ⟶ X` with τ-filtered fibres, q has the right lifting property against `K ⊆ K^▷` for every τ-small K (5.4.4.1). If moreover `κ < τ`, `κ ≪ τ`, X is τ-small, the fibres have τ-small κ-filtered colimits and the transport functors preserve them, then the ∞-category of sections `Map_X(X, Y)` is τ-filtered and each evaluation `Map_X(X, Y) ⟶ Y_x` is cofinal (5.4.4.2).
