For C with finite products, `φ⁺ : EnvPlus C ⥤ C` sends `(J, (C_j)) ↦ ∏ᶜ C_j`, and `φ` is its restriction. `L := E ⋙ φ.lan` and `L⁺ := E⁺ ⋙ φ⁺.lan` (Mathlib `Functor.lan`); `α : 𝟭 ⟶ L` comes from `θ^* ∘ E ≅ 𝟭`, and `β : L ⟶ L⁺` from `Env C ⊆ EnvPlus C`. Propose.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.lan`.

**Construction of the left adjoint** (HTT Lemmas 5.5.9.6–5.5.9.9, PDF pp. 536–537). For C with finite products and `F ∈ SSet^C`: `L⁺(F)` preserves finite products, and composition with `β ∘ α` identifies `Map(L⁺(F), F')` with `Map(F, F')` for product-preserving F' (5.5.9.6). If F sends the final object to a contractible Kan complex, `β : L(F) ⟶ L⁺(F)` is a weak equivalence (5.5.9.7). E preserves projectively cofibrant objects (5.5.9.8). `F ⊣ G` is a Quillen adjunction, and for projectively cofibrant, weakly product-preserving F the unit `F ⟶ G(F(F))` is a weak equivalence (5.5.9.9). Lurie states 5.5.9.6, 5.5.9.8 and 5.5.9.9 for simplicial categories; the formalization needs the case of ordinary categories (Remark 5.5.9.10).

*Parts.* Lemma 5.5.9.8 is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.5.5.9.8/reduce` (reduction to one pushout of a generating projective cofibration), `HTT.5.5.9.8/index` (the index filtration) and `HTT.5.5.9.8/step` (each step of the filtration is a projective cofibration, which proves 5.5.9.8), and this entry's own target `HTT.5.5.9.8`, which collects them; 5.5.9.6, 5.5.9.7 and 5.5.9.9 are separate targets.

*Needs:* 5.5.9.4–5.5.9.5; 5.5.9.13, `HTT.A.2.7/simplexwise-contractible` (F2.4) for 5.5.9.7; `HTT.5.5.9.8/reduce`, `HTT.5.5.9.8/index`, `HTT.5.5.9.8/step` (below) for 5.5.9.8; F3.2 (projective cofibrations); for 5.5.9.9: 5.5.9.6–5.5.9.8.

**Reducing to a generating cofibration** (`HTT.5.5.9.8/reduce`, part 1 of 3 of the construction of the left adjoint above; proof of HTT Lemma 5.5.9.8, PDF pp. 538–539). The functor `E : SSet^C ⥤ SSet^{Env(C)}` preserves the initial object, filtered colimits and retracts. Hence, by the small object argument, E preserves projectively cofibrant objects if: whenever `E(G)` is projectively cofibrant and `G'` is a pushout of G along a generating projective cofibration `Map_C(C, −) × K ⟶ Map_C(C, −) × K'`, `E(G')` is projectively cofibrant.

*Needs:* 5.5.9.4; A.2.8.2 (F3.2); Mathlib's small object argument.

**The index filtration** (`HTT.5.5.9.8/index`, part 2 of 3 of the construction of the left adjoint above; proof of HTT Lemma 5.5.9.8, PDF pp. 539–540). With G, G' as in `HTT.5.5.9.8/reduce`, a simplex of `E(G')(J, (C'_j))` has index at most k when at most k distinct simplices of K' outside K occur among its coordinates outside G. The simplices of index at most k form a subfunctor `E(G')⁽ᵏ⁾` of `E(G')` on `Env(C)`, with `E(G')⁽⁰⁾ = E(G)` and union `E(G')`.

*Needs:* 5.5.9.4.

**Each index step is a projective cofibration** (`HTT.5.5.9.8/step`, part 3 of 3 of the construction of the left adjoint above; HTT Lemma 5.5.9.8, PDF p. 537, proof pp. 538–540). The 5.5.9.8 item of the entry above.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: after `HTT.5.5.9.8/reduce`, let `K'_old ⊆ K'^k` be the simplices that are not k distinct new simplices, and `ψ : Env(C) ⥤ Env(C)` adjoin k copies of C. `ψ_!` preserves projective cofibrations, and `E(G) ⊗ −` preserves cofibrations since `E(G)` is cofibrant. The square from `ψ_!(E(G) ⊗ K'_old) ⟶ ψ_!(E(G) ⊗ K'^k)` to the step `E(G')⁽ᵏ⁻¹⁾ ⟶ E(G')⁽ᵏ⁾` of `HTT.5.5.9.8/index` is a pushout. Lurie treats this as routine; it is the bulk of the Lean proof, checked objectwise on `Env(C)`.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.5.9.8/reduce`, `HTT.5.5.9.8/index`.

**Nonempty finite subsets** (HTT Notation 5.5.9.11, Lemmas 5.5.9.12–5.5.9.13, PDF pp. 540–542). `M(K)` is K composed with the functor sending a set to its nonempty finite subsets (5.5.9.11). For a finite simplicial set K, a simplicial subset `X ⊆ M(K^▷) × Δ[n]` surjecting onto `Δ[n]` and closed under enlarging the first coordinate is weakly contractible (5.5.9.12); the same holds with `M(K)` for a contractible Kan complex K (5.5.9.13).

*Parts.* Lemma 5.5.9.12 is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.5.5.9.12/cone-retract` (a deformation retraction onto the simplices containing the cone point) and `HTT.5.5.9.12/semisimplicial` (a semisimplicial deformation retraction onto a copy of `Δ[n]`, which proves 5.5.9.12), and this entry's own target `HTT.5.5.9.12`, which collects them; Notation 5.5.9.11 and Lemma 5.5.9.13 are separate targets.

*Lean:* `SSet.nonemptyFinsets K := K ⋙ SSet.nonemptyFinsetFunctor` (both propose; Mathlib has no such functor), where `nonemptyFinsetFunctor : Type u ⥤ Type u` sends S to `{s : Finset S // s.Nonempty}` and f to `s ↦ ⟨s.1.image f, s.2.image f⟩`, with classical decidable equality.

*Needs:* `SSet.IsWeaklyContractible`; for 5.5.9.12: `HTT.5.5.9.12/cone-retract`, `HTT.5.5.9.12/semisimplicial` (below), 5.5.8.11–5.5.8.12 (siftedness of `N(Δ)^op`: products with `Δ[1]` commute with realization), 4.2.4.1 (L5.7); for 5.5.9.13: 5.5.9.12, homotopy groups of filtered colimits of Kan complexes (F2.2).

**Retracting onto the cone point** (`HTT.5.5.9.12/cone-retract`, part 1 of 2 of nonempty finite subsets above; proof of HTT Lemma 5.5.9.12, PDF p. 541). For K finite and `X ⊆ M(K^▷) × Δ[n]` as in 5.5.9.12, let `X' ⊆ X` consist of the simplices whose first coordinate contains the constant simplex at the cone point. An explicit `h' : M(K^▷) × Δ[1] ⟶ M(K^▷)`, adjoining the simplices that agree with a member up to some vertex and are constant at the cone point from there on, makes `h' × id` a deformation retraction of X onto X' preserving X'.

*Lean:* h' is defined on m-simplices by an explicit `Finset` formula; its simpliciality and the preservation of X (hypothesis (ii)) are the content.

*Needs:* 5.5.9.11.

**A semisimplicial retraction onto a simplex** (`HTT.5.5.9.12/semisimplicial`, part 2 of 2 of nonempty finite subsets above; HTT Lemma 5.5.9.12, PDF pp. 540–541, proof pp. 541–542). The 5.5.9.12 item of the entry above.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: after `HTT.5.5.9.12/cone-retract`, forget degeneracies. Let `X''` be the semisimplicial subset whose first coordinate is the set of all simplices. Then `X'' ⊆ X'` by (i)–(ii), `X'' ≅ Δ[n]` as semisimplicial sets, and a second explicit homotopy g' retracts `X'` onto `X''` semisimplicially. Weak homotopy types are read off semisimplicial sets by 6.5.3.7.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.5.9.12/cone-retract`; 6.5.3.7 (L5.7, the weak homotopy type of a simplicial set through its underlying semisimplicial object); 5.5.8.4.

**Homotopy colimits of simplicial objects in A** (HTT Proposition 5.5.9.14, Lemma 5.5.9.15, PDF p. 543). For C with finite products and A as in 5.5.9.1, evaluation at each object preserves homotopy colimits of simplicial objects (5.5.9.15); for a simplicial object of A, viewed as a bisimplicial object, its homotopy colimit is isomorphic in hA to its diagonal (5.5.9.14).

*Needs:* 5.5.9.3; 4.2.4.1; 5.5.8.4; 5.5.8.10; A.2.9.30–A.2.9.31 (F3) for 5.5.9.14.

### L7.9 Groupoid objects

Groupoid objects, Čech nerves and group objects are L6.8; this item needs presentability.

**`Gpd(C)` is strongly reflective** (HTT Proposition 6.1.2.9, PDF p. 559). For presentable C, `Gpd(C) ⊆ C_Δ` is strongly reflective.

*Needs:* 6.1.2.6; 5.5.4.17–5.5.4.19 (L7.6); 5.5.3.6.

## Layer L8: Model-categorical presentations of presentable ∞-categories

HTT A.3.7.6–A.3.7.10: presentable ∞-categories are exactly the underlying ∞-categories `N(A°)` of combinatorial simplicial model categories, and accessible reflective localizations of `N(A°)` are exactly the left Bousfield localizations of A. Every target here combines F3 (Bousfield localization A.3.7.1–A.3.7.5 and Dugger's theorem, F3.9) with L7 (presentability, §5.5.4). Throughout, a model category A is locally small with a large class of objects, `A°` is its full simplicial subcategory of bifibrant objects, and `N(A°)` is a large ∞-category (`CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve.quasicategory`, an `SSet.{u + 1}` under the Universes convention); `hA ≃ h N(A°)`, with mapping objects `Map_hA(X, Y) = [Map_A(X, Y)]` for X cofibrant and Y fibrant (`HTT.A.3.7/intro`). "Localization of a model category" is HTT's Bousfield localization of `HTT.A.3.7/intro` (same underlying category and cofibrations, more weak equivalences); "accessible localization" of an ∞-category is an accessible reflective localization (Conventions, L6.5).

The only user of this layer outside it is HA Proposition 1.3.4.22 (L9.5: the underlying ∞-category of a combinatorial model category is presentable), whose proof cites A.3.7.6. There are no in-layer forward needs: the items are in book order and each uses only earlier ones (A.3.7.8 and A.3.7.10 use A.3.7.6; A.3.7.10 uses A.3.7.9).

**Presentable ∞-categories are underlying ∞-categories of combinatorial simplicial model categories** (HTT Proposition A.3.7.6, PDF p. 929). For an ∞-category C (large), the following are equivalent: (1) C is presentable (5.5.0.1); (2) there are a combinatorial simplicial model category A (A.2.6.1, A.3.1.5) and a categorical equivalence `C ≃ N(A°)`. Neither direction asks A to be left proper.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as five targets: the four parts that follow this entry, `HTT.A.3.7.6/local-nerve` (local objects of a left Bousfield localization, on nerves), `HTT.A.3.7.6/quillen-nerve` (simplicial Quillen equivalences give equivalent underlying ∞-categories), `HTT.A.3.7.6/1⇒2` ((1) ⇒ (2)) and `HTT.A.3.7.6/2⇒1` ((2) ⇒ (1)), and this entry's own target `HTT.A.3.7.6`, which combines `/1⇒2` and `/2⇒1` into the equivalence.

**Checks.** `S = N(Kan)` is presentable (5.5.1.8), with A = `SSet` in the Kan–Quillen structure (F3.1). For a small simplicial set K, `P(K) ≃ N(B°)` with B the simplicial functors `C[K]^op ⥤ SSet` in the injective structure (4.2.4.4). `Δ[0]` is `N(A°)` for the terminal category with its unique model structure.

*Proof route.* (1) ⇒ (2), Lurie's (`HTT.A.3.7.6/1⇒2`). By 5.5.1.1 and 5.5.4.15 (with 5.5.4.2 (3)), `C ≃ S⁻¹P(K)` for a small simplicial set K and a small set S of morphisms of `P(K)`. Let B be the category of simplicial functors `C[K]^op ⥤ SSet` with the injective model structure (A.3.3.2, F3.5): combinatorial, simplicial, every object cofibrant, hence left proper (A.2.4.2). Proposition 4.2.4.4 (with `U = SSet`, so `N(U°) = S`, and the isomorphism `C[K^op] ≅ C[K]^op` of `HTT.5.1.3/intro/op`) gives `P(K) ≃ N(B°)`. Represent the elements of S by a set `S̃` of cofibrations of B and form `S̃⁻¹B` (A.3.7.3): it is combinatorial and simplicial with the same cofibrations, and its bifibrant objects are the bifibrant `S̃`-local objects of B (A.3.7.3 (3)). So `N((S̃⁻¹B)°)` is the full subcategory of `N(B°)` spanned by the S-local objects (`HTT.A.3.7.6/local-nerve`). This uses two facts: the S-local objects of 5.5.4.1 are the `S̃`-local objects of `HTT.A.3.7/intro`, because the mapping spaces of `N(B°)` are those of `B°` (2.2.0.1); and the simplicial nerve of a full simplicial subcategory is the corresponding full subcategory of the nerve. That full subcategory is `S⁻¹P(K) ≃ C`. Lurie also cites A.3.7.4 here, for the converse correspondence (every combinatorial localization of B comes from a set S); the implication needs only A.3.7.3.

(2) ⇒ (1) (`HTT.A.3.7.6/2⇒1`). By the simplicial refinement in `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/simplicial`, A is joined by a simplicial Quillen equivalence to `L = T⁻¹Fun(D^op, SSet)_proj`, for a small category D and a small set T of morphisms. The same argument as in (1) ⇒ (2), with the projective structure (4.2.4.4 applies to it too; Remark 4.2.4.5), identifies `N(L°)` with the T-local objects of `P(N(D))`. By 5.5.4.15 this is an accessible localization of a presentable ∞-category, so it is presentable. It remains to compare `N(A°)` with `N(L°)`. Lurie leaves this step implicit, and A.3.1.12 (L2.8) does not apply: it needs every object of the left adjoint's source to be cofibrant, and Dugger's left adjoint starts at the projective structure, where this fails. Repair (`HTT.A.3.7.6/quillen-nerve`): the simplicial Quillen adjunction induces an adjunction `f ⊣ g` between `N(L°)` and `N(A°)` (5.2.4.6, L6.4). On homotopy categories, f and g are the derived functors (HTT Remark 5.2.4.7, which is proved with 5.2.4.6). Since `LF` and `RG` are inverse equivalences (A.2.5.1), the unit and counit of `f ⊣ g` are equivalences, so f is an equivalence of ∞-categories (in `SSet.QCat.bicategory`, hence a categorical equivalence, L1.5).

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7.6/local-nerve`, `HTT.A.3.7.6/quillen-nerve`, `HTT.A.3.7.6/1⇒2`, `HTT.A.3.7.6/2⇒1` (below); 5.5.0.1 (L7.5); 1.1.5.10 (`CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve.quasicategory`); A.3.7.4 (F3.9); A.2.6.1 (F1.6).

**Local objects of a left Bousfield localization, on nerves** (`HTT.A.3.7.6/local-nerve`, part 1 of 4 of presentable ∞-categories as underlying ∞-categories of combinatorial simplicial model categories above; proof of HTT Proposition A.3.7.6, PDF p. 929). Let B be a left proper combinatorial simplicial model category and `S̃` a small set of cofibrations, with image S in `N(B°)`. The bifibrant objects of `S̃⁻¹B` are the bifibrant `S̃`-local objects of B (A.3.7.3 (3)), and `N((S̃⁻¹B)°)` is the full subcategory of `N(B°)` spanned by the S-local objects (5.5.4.1).

*Proof route.* As in the entry above: the mapping spaces of `N(B°)` are those of `B°` (2.2.0.1), so `S̃`-locality in hB is S-locality in `N(B°)`; and the simplicial nerve of a full simplicial subcategory is the corresponding full subcategory.

*Needs:* A.3.7.3, `HTT.A.3.7/intro` (F3.9); 2.2.0.1 (L2.8); 5.5.4.1 (L7.6).

**Simplicial Quillen equivalences give equivalent underlying ∞-categories** (`HTT.A.3.7.6/quillen-nerve`, part 2 of 4 of presentable ∞-categories as underlying ∞-categories of combinatorial simplicial model categories above; the step of HTT Proposition A.3.7.6 (2) ⇒ (1) that Lurie leaves implicit, PDF p. 930). Let `F : A ⇄ B : G` be a simplicial Quillen equivalence between combinatorial simplicial model categories. The induced adjunction `f ⊣ g` between `N(A°)` and `N(B°)` (5.2.4.6) is an adjoint equivalence.

*Proof route.* The repair in the entry above: on homotopy categories f and g are the derived functors (HTT Remark 5.2.4.7). These are inverse equivalences (A.2.5.1), so the unit and counit are equivalences and f is an equivalence in `SSet.QCat.bicategory`. A.3.1.12 does not apply, since not every object of the source is cofibrant.

*Needs:* 5.2.4.6 (L6.4); A.2.5.1, `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions` (F1.5); A.3.1.5 (F3.3).

**Presentable ∞-categories have combinatorial models** (`HTT.A.3.7.6/1⇒2`, part 3 of 4 of presentable ∞-categories as underlying ∞-categories of combinatorial simplicial model categories above; HTT Proposition A.3.7.6, (1) ⇒ (2), PDF pp. 929–930). A presentable ∞-category is equivalent to `N(A°)` for a combinatorial simplicial model category A.

*Proof route.* The (1) ⇒ (2) paragraph of the entry above, with the comparison step given by `HTT.A.3.7.6/local-nerve`.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7.6/local-nerve`; 5.5.1.1 (L7.5); 5.5.4.2, 5.5.4.15 (L7.6); 4.2.4.4 (L5.7); A.3.3.2 (F3.5); A.2.4.2 (F1.5); `HTT.5.1.3/intro/op` (L6.1).

**Combinatorial models are presentable** (`HTT.A.3.7.6/2⇒1`, part 4 of 4 of presentable ∞-categories as underlying ∞-categories of combinatorial simplicial model categories above; HTT Proposition A.3.7.6, (2) ⇒ (1), PDF pp. 929–930). For a combinatorial simplicial model category A, `N(A°)` is presentable; with `HTT.A.3.7.6/1⇒2` this is the equivalence of A.3.7.6 above.

*Proof route.* The (2) ⇒ (1) paragraph of the entry above. `HTT.A.3.7.6/local-nerve` (in the projective variant, Remark 4.2.4.5) identifies `N(L°)` with a localization of `P(N(D))`, presentable by 5.5.4.15, and `HTT.A.3.7.6/quillen-nerve` compares it with `N(A°)`.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.7.6/local-nerve`, `HTT.A.3.7.6/quillen-nerve`; `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-presentation/simplicial` (F3.9); 5.5.4.15 (L7.6); 4.2.4.4 (L5.7); 5.2.4.7 (L6.4).

**Accessible localizations are Bousfield localizations** (HTT Proposition A.3.7.8, PDF p. 930). Let A be a left proper combinatorial simplicial model category, `C = N(A°)`, `C⁰ ⊆ C` an accessible reflective localization, and `L : C ⟶ C⁰` a left adjoint of the inclusion. Then A has a Bousfield localization A′ (`HTT.A.3.7/intro`) in which (1) an object is fibrant exactly when it is fibrant in A and its image in `hA ≃ hC` lies in `hC⁰`, and (2) a morphism f is a weak equivalence exactly when `hL : hC ⟶ hC⁰` sends f to an isomorphism. A′ is of the form `S̃⁻¹A` for a small set `S̃` of cofibrations between cofibrant objects, so it is again left proper, combinatorial and simplicial (A.3.7.3).

*Proof route.* Lurie's. C is presentable (A.3.7.6). By 5.5.4.2 (3), there is a small set S of morphisms with `C⁰` the S-local objects; 5.5.4.15 identifies the S-equivalences with the morphisms that L inverts. Represent S by a set `S̃` of cofibrations between cofibrant objects of A (factor a representative between bifibrant objects as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration) and set `A′ = S̃⁻¹A`. Then (1) is A.3.7.3 (3), and (2) is the definition of the weak equivalences of `S̃⁻¹A` (`S̃`-equivalences). Both use the identification of `S̃`-local objects and `S̃`-equivalences in `hA` (`HTT.A.3.7/intro`) with S-local objects and S-equivalences in C (5.5.4.1), through the mapping spaces of `N(A°)` (2.2.0.1). Lurie writes only "the results of §5.5.4"; 5.5.4.2 and 5.5.4.15 are the ones used.

*Needs:* A.3.7.6, `HTT.A.3.7.6/local-nerve`; 5.5.4.1, `HTT.5.5.4.2/i⇒ii`, `HTT.5.5.4.2/ii⇒iii`, 5.5.4.15 (L7.6); 5.2.7.2 (L6.5, reflective localizations); 2.2.0.1 (L2.8); A.3.7.3, `HTT.A.3.7/intro` (F3.9); A.2.4.1 (F1.5); `HTT.A.2.2/homotopy-category` (F1.4).

**Descent of Quillen adjunctions to a localization** (HTT Proposition A.3.7.9, PDF p. 930). Let `F : A ⇄ B : G` be a simplicial Quillen adjunction between left proper combinatorial simplicial model categories, and let A′ be a Bousfield localization of A that is combinatorial. The following are equivalent: (1) F and G form a Quillen adjunction `A′ ⇄ B`; (2) `LF : hA ⟶ hB` sends every weak equivalence of A′ to an isomorphism; (3) G sends fibrant objects of B to fibrant objects of A′. Lurie's statement says only "a Bousfield localization". His proof applies A.3.7.4, which assumes A′ combinatorial, so the target states that hypothesis. Then `A′ = S⁻¹A` (A.3.7.4), so A′ is again simplicial (A.3.7.3), as A.3.7.2 needs.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. (1) ⇒ (2) is immediate. (3) ⇒ (1) is A.3.7.2, applied to `A′ ⇄ B`. For (2) ⇒ (3), write `A′ = S⁻¹A` with S a small set of cofibrations between cofibrant objects (A.3.7.4, A.3.7.5). For fibrant X in B, GX is fibrant in A, so it is fibrant in A′ once it is S-local (A.3.7.3 (3)). For `α ∈ S`, the map `Map_A(α, GX)` is `Map_B(Fα, X)`, and Fα is a weak equivalence between cofibrant objects because it represents `LF(α)`.

*Needs:* A.3.7.2, A.3.7.3, A.3.7.4, A.3.7.5, `HTT.A.3.7/intro` (F3.9); A.3.1.5 (F3.3); `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions` (F1.5); A.2.4.1 (F1.5); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences` (F2.4).

**Localizing at the morphisms a left Quillen functor inverts** (HTT Corollary A.3.7.10, PDF pp. 931–932). Let `F : A ⇄ B : G` be a simplicial Quillen adjunction between left proper combinatorial simplicial model categories. (1) The category of A carries a left proper combinatorial simplicial model structure A′ whose cofibrations are those of A, whose weak equivalences are the morphisms α with `LF(α)` an isomorphism in `hB`, and whose fibrations are the maps with the right lifting property against the morphisms that are both. (2) F and G form a simplicial Quillen adjunction `A′ ⇄ B`. (3) If `RG : hB ⟶ hA` is fully faithful, `A′ ⇄ B` is a Quillen equivalence.

**Checks.** If B is the terminal category (its unique model structure, tensored trivially), `G` picks out a terminal object of A, every morphism of A′ is a weak equivalence, and (3) applies: `hA′` is equivalent to the terminal category. If `F ⊣ G` is the identity of A, then `A′ = A`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. By 5.2.4.6, F and G induce an adjunction `f ⊣ g` between `N(A°)` and `N(B°)`, both presentable (A.3.7.6). Let `𝒮` be the morphisms of `N(A°)` that f inverts. Since f preserves small colimits (a left adjoint, 5.2.3.5), `𝒮` is a strongly saturated class of small generation (5.5.4.16, applied to the equivalences of `N(B°)`), generated by a small subset S. Represent S by a set T of cofibrations between cofibrant objects of A and set `A′ = T⁻¹A` (A.3.7.3). (1): after replacing α by a morphism between bifibrant objects, α is a T-equivalence exactly when it lies in `𝒮` (5.5.4.15 (4), with the mapping spaces of 2.2.0.1), exactly when `LF(α)` is an isomorphism (f is `LF` on homotopy categories, HTT Remark 5.2.4.7). (2) is A.3.7.9, (2) ⇒ (1). (3): `hA′` is the full subcategory of `hA` on the T-local objects, and `LF′` is the restriction of `LF`. So the derived counit `LF′ ∘ RG′ ⟶ id` is that of `LF ⊣ RG`, an isomorphism because RG is fully faithful; and `LF′` is conservative by (1). Hence `LF′` is an equivalence (A.2.5.1).

*Needs:* A.3.7.6, A.3.7.9; 5.2.4.6, 5.2.3.5 (L6.4); 5.5.4.15, 5.5.4.16, `HTT.5.5.4.16/after` (L7.6); 2.2.0.1 (L2.8); A.3.7.3, `HTT.A.3.7/intro` (F3.9); A.3.1.5 (F3.3); A.2.5.1, `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions`, A.2.4.1 (F1.5); A.1.2.4 (F1.1).

## Layer L9: Stable ∞-categories

HA chapter 1: stable ∞-categories and their triangulated homotopy categories (L9.1), t-structures and spectral sequences (L9.2), the classical and ∞-categorical Dold–Kan correspondences (L9.3), dg categories, the dg nerve and derived ∞-categories (L9.4), localizations and underlying ∞-categories of model categories (L9.5), and spectra, stabilization and presentable stable ∞-categories (L9.6). HA's appendices are outside this roadmap; where HA cites them, the entry names the HTT or F3 target that replaces them.

The layer fixes three rows of the Conventions table: *t-structure* (*t-structures on triangulated categories* and *t-structures on stable ∞-categories*, L9.2: Mathlib's `Triangulated.TStructure` on `hC`, as `SSet.TStructure`), *dg category* (*Differential graded categories*, L9.4: Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.DGCategory`) and *localization* (`SSet.IsLocalization`, L9.5). "Localization" in §1.3.4 is the Conventions' universal notion (HA 1.3.4.1, Kerodon 6.3.1.9); HTT's localizations (HTT 5.2.7.2, used throughout §1.2.1) are called reflective localizations.

**Conventions of this layer.**

- HA uses homological indexing for t-structures (`C_{≥0}`, `C_{≤0}`, `C_{≥n} = C_{≥0}[n]`). Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure` is cohomological, with fields `le n`, `ge n`. The dictionary is `C_{≥n} = le (−n)` and `C_{≤n} = ge (−n)`; with it, HA's axiom 1.2.1.1 (1) is Mathlib's `zero'`, and the heart `C_{≥0} ∩ C_{≤0}` is Mathlib's `TStructure.heart`.
- HA's "left cofinal" is the roadmap's *cofinal* (HTT 4.1.1.1, `SSet.IsCofinal`; Terms).
- A *stable ∞-category* is a quasicategory with the property `SSet.IsStable` (L9.1). Its homotopy category is Mathlib's `SSet.hoFunctor.obj C`, and the triangulated structure of HA 1.1.2.14 is a Mathlib `Pretriangulated` and `IsTriangulated` instance on it, built from a choice of suspension functor.
- "Exact functor" between stable ∞-categories is HA's notion (`HA.1.1.4/intro`, L9.1).

Its inputs are L5–L7 (limits, Kan extensions, `SSet.IsPushout` and `SSet.IsPullback` of L5.10, presheaves, adjunctions, L6.8's `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed`, presentability); L1.5's `SSet.IsFullyFaithful`, `HTT.1.2.12/final` and L1.2's `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`; the model-categorical targets `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions` (F1.5), `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3.2) and `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-simplicial` (F3.9); F2's `HTT.A.2.7/postnikov`, `HTT.A.2.7/eilenberg-maclane` and `HTT.A.2.7/realization-connectivity`; Mathlib's homological algebra (additive and abelian categories, pretriangulated and triangulated categories and t-structures, chain complexes, the Dold–Kan correspondence, Grothendieck abelian categories and their injectives), where the heart of a t-structure is not yet abelian, so L9.2 adds three Mathlib-level sub-targets of 1.2.1.12 (`HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart`, the heart is abelian; `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-ker-coker`, its kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences; `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-homology`, the homological functor `H⁰`); and Tau Ceti's differential graded nerve (`TauCeti.dgNerve`, with its quasicategory instance, homotopy category and right mapping spaces).

The main results are HA 1.1.2.14, 1.1.3.4, 1.1.4.1, 1.2.1.17, 1.2.2.14, 1.2.3.7, 1.2.4.1, 1.3.1.17, 1.3.2.19, 1.3.3.2, 1.3.3.8, 1.3.4.20, 1.3.4.22, 1.3.5.18, 1.4.1.2, 1.4.2.23, 1.4.3.6, 1.4.4.4 and 1.4.4.9.

Routes that depart from Lurie's:

- 1.3.4.7 and 1.3.4.20 use `Ex^∞` on every mapping space in place of the topological category `|C|` (L9.5).
- 1.3.4.10 uses F3's `HTT.A.3.2/fixed-objects` and `HTT.A.3.2/sifted-hocolim` in place of HA 4.1.8.3 and 4.1.8.13 (L9.5).
- The converse of 1.3.3.10 uses `HTT.A.2.7/realization-connectivity` in place of HTT 6.5.3.10 (L9.4).
- 1.3.3.16 uses `HTT.A.2.7/postnikov` in place of HTT 6.5.1.2 and 7.2.1.10 (L9.4).
- The heart in 1.4.3.6 uses `HTT.A.2.7/eilenberg-maclane` in place of HTT 7.2.2.12 (L9.6).
- 1.2.4.17 is proved by a combinatorial poset argument in place of Lurie's topological one (L9.3).
- 1.3.5.7 is Mathlib's instance (L9.5).

**Forward needs inside the layer.** The items are written in the book's order. These entries need a later item of L9:

- L9.2 → L9.6: Proposition 1.2.1.17 (1), stability of the left completion, is proved through 1.4.2.24 and Corollary 1.4.2.17.
- L9.4 → L9.6: Proposition 1.3.2.10, stability of `N_dg(Ch(A))`, concludes with Corollary 1.4.2.27.
- L9.5 → L9.6: Proposition 1.3.5.21 uses Definition 1.4.4.12 (accessible t-structures).
- Inside L9.6: Propositions 1.4.3.4 and 1.4.3.7 use Proposition 1.4.4.4, and 1.4.3.4 also uses Proposition 1.4.4.11 and Definition 1.4.4.12. Inside §1.4.2, Proposition 1.4.2.11 uses Proposition 1.4.2.13, which uses Lemma 1.4.2.15, and Proposition 1.4.2.24 uses Lemma 1.4.2.26.
- Inside L9.3–L9.5, results use lemmas that HA states after them in the same item: 1.2.4.1 (`/filtered`) uses 1.2.4.19, 1.2.4.3 uses 1.2.4.18, 1.2.4.5 uses 1.2.4.7, 1.2.4.13 uses 1.2.4.15; 1.3.2.10 uses 1.3.2.16, 1.3.2.19 uses 1.3.2.21, 1.3.2.22 uses 1.3.2.23, 1.3.3.2 uses 1.3.3.9 and 1.3.3.12, 1.3.3.7 and 1.3.3.12 use 1.3.3.16, 1.3.3.8 uses 1.3.3.14 and 1.3.3.17; 1.3.4.4 uses 1.3.4.5–1.3.4.6, 1.3.4.5 uses 1.3.4.7, 1.3.4.11 and 1.3.4.14, and 1.3.4.7 uses 1.3.4.14.
- Inside L9.1: Proposition 1.1.3.4 uses the direction (2) ⇒ (3) of 1.1.4.1, which is immediate from the definitions.

None of these is circular: §1.4.2 through 1.4.2.27 uses only L9.1 and HTT, and 1.4.4.11–1.4.4.12 use L9.1–L9.2 and HTT. The formalization order is L9.1, then §1.4.2 (L9.6, from 1.4.2.1 to 1.4.2.27), then L9.2–L9.5, then the rest of L9.6.

### L9.1 Stable ∞-categories and their homotopy categories

**Terminology remark** (HA Remark 1.1.0.1, PDF p. 17). The Remark itself is a literature note with no mathematical content. As a target it fixes HA's terminology for spaces and cofinality used across chapter 1: HA's *left cofinal* is the roadmap's *cofinal*; a space is *n-connective* when it is nonempty and its homotopy groups vanish below degree n (F2's `(n−1)`-connected Kan complexes; HTT's own notion, 6.5.1.12, sits in L11 and is not used here); *n-truncated* is HTT 5.5.6.1's. Formalizing it means fixing these names; no statement is proved.

*Needs:* —

**Zero objects and pointed ∞-categories** (`SSet.IsZeroObject`, `SSet.IsPointed`; HA Definition 1.1.1.1, PDF p. 17). An object of an ∞-category C is a zero object when it is both initial and final; C is pointed when it has a zero object. Zero objects are unique up to equivalence: the full subcategory they span is empty or a contractible Kan complex (HTT 1.2.12.9).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsZeroObject X` for a vertex X of a quasicategory C: `SSet.IsTerminalVertex X ∧ SSet.IsInitialVertex X` (the initial notion is the final notion in `Cᵒᵖ`, L1.5). `SSet.IsPointed C := ∃ X, SSet.IsZeroObject X`.

**Checks.**

- In the nerve of a category, a vertex is a zero object exactly when it is a zero object of the category (Mathlib `Limits.IsZero`).
- `Δ[0]` is pointed; `Δ[1]` is not.

*Needs:* `HTT.1.2.12/final`, `SSet.IsInitialVertex` (L1.5); 1.2.12.9 (L2).

**Zero morphisms** (HA Remark 1.1.1.3, PDF p. 18). In a pointed ∞-category, `Map(X, 0) × Map(0, Y) ⟶ Map(X, Y)` has contractible source, so composition through a zero object gives a well-defined morphism `0 : X ⟶ Y` of `hC`, independent of the zero object chosen. Provide it as a morphism of `hoFunctor.obj C`, and the fact that `hoFunctor.obj C` has a zero object (Mathlib `HasZeroObject`) and zero morphisms agreeing with these.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.1.

**Triangles, fibre and cofibre sequences** (`SSet.Triangle`; HA Definition 1.1.1.4, PDF p. 18). In a pointed ∞-category C, a triangle is a square `σ : Δ[1] × Δ[1] ⟶ C` whose vertex `(1, 0)` is a zero object; it is drawn `X ⟶ Y`, `X ⟶ 0`, `Y ⟶ Z`, `0 ⟶ Z`. It is a fibre sequence when σ is a pullback square and a cofibre sequence when it is a pushout square.

*Lean:* `SSet.squareVertex σ i j := yonedaEquiv (lift (vertexMap i) (vertexMap j) ≫ σ)` for `σ : Δ[1] ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ C`, with edges `Edge.mk' (yonedaEquiv (squareH j ≫ σ))` and `Edge.mk' (yonedaEquiv (squareV i ≫ σ))` (σ is a map, so it cannot be applied to a pair); `SSet.Triangle C` the subtype of `Δ[1] ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ C` with `SSet.IsZeroObject (squareVertex σ 1 0)`; `Triangle.IsFiberSequence σ := SSet.IsPullback σ`, `Triangle.IsCofiberSequence σ := SSet.IsPushout σ` (L5.10, HTT 4.4.2.1).

*Needs:* 1.1.1.1; `SSet.IsPushout`, `SSet.IsPullback` (L5.10).

**Fibres and cofibres** (HA Definition 1.1.1.6, PDF p. 19). For `g : X ⟶ Y` in a pointed ∞-category, a fibre of g is a fibre sequence `W ⟶ X ⟶ Y` with g as its second map, and a cofibre of g a cofibre sequence `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z` with g as its first map; W and Z are written `fib(g)`, `cofib(g)`.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsFiber g σ` for a triangle σ that is a fibre sequence and whose edge `(0, 1) ⟶ (1, 1)` is g; `SSet.IsCofiber g σ` for a cofibre sequence whose edge `(0, 0) ⟶ (0, 1)` is g. `SSet.HasFibers C`, `SSet.HasCofibers C`: every edge has one.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.4.

**The cofibre functor is a left adjoint** (HA Remark 1.1.1.8, PDF p. 19). If every morphism of the pointed ∞-category C has a cofibre, the cofibre construction is a functor `cofib : Fun(Δ[1], C) ⟶ C` (a section of the trivial fibration of Remark 1.1.1.7 followed by evaluation at `(1, 1)`), and it is left adjoint to the functor `C ⟶ Fun(Δ[1], C)` sending X to a zero morphism `0 ⟶ X` (the left Kan extension along `{1} ⊆ Δ[1]`). Hence cofib preserves all colimits that exist in `Fun(Δ[1], C)`.

*Proof route.* The trivial fibration of Remark 1.1.1.7 is two applications of HTT 4.3.2.15; the adjunction is checked on morphism spaces; then HTT 5.2.3.5.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.6; 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`; 5.2.3.5 (L6).

**Stable ∞-categories** (`SSet.IsStable`; HA Definition 1.1.1.9, PDF pp. 19–20). An ∞-category C is stable when it has a zero object, every morphism has a fibre and a cofibre, and a triangle is a fibre sequence exactly when it is a cofibre sequence.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsStable C` for `C : SSet` with `[C.Quasicategory]`: `IsPointed C ∧ HasFibers C ∧ HasCofibers C ∧ ∀ σ : Triangle C, σ.IsFiberSequence ↔ σ.IsCofiberSequence`. A class, so that instances on `Fun(K, C)` and on the dg nerve can be found.

**Checks.**

- `Cᵒᵖ` is stable when C is (HA Remark 1.1.1.13).
- `Δ[0]` is stable. The nerve of an additive category with a nonzero object is not: in a nerve the pushout of `0 ⟵ X ⟶ 0` is 0, so `ΣX ≅ 0`, while Σ is an equivalence in a stable ∞-category.
- `Fun(K, C)` is stable for stable C (1.1.3.1).

*Needs:* 1.1.1.1, 1.1.1.4, 1.1.1.6.

**Additive categories** (HA Definition 1.1.2.1, PDF p. 21; Remark 1.1.2.4, PDF p. 22). HA's additive category is a category with a zero object, finite products and coproducts, the canonical map `X ⊔ Y ⟶ X × Y` an isomorphism, and the induced commutative monoid structure on each `Hom(X, Y)` a group; the product and coproduct are then written `X ⊕ Y` (1.1.2.4). This is a property of the category. Mathlib states additivity as structure (`Preadditive` with `HasFiniteBiproducts`); the target is the comparison: a category satisfying HA's conditions has a unique `Preadditive` structure whose biproducts are the given products and coproducts, and conversely.

*Lean:* `class CategoryTheory.IsHAAdditive C : Prop` (propose) with fields `hasZeroObject`, `hasFiniteProducts`, `hasFiniteCoproducts`, `isIso_coprodToProd` (for all X, Y the canonical `X ⨿ Y ⟶ X ⨯ Y`, components `𝟙` and `0`, is an isomorphism) and `exists_neg f : ∃ g, prod.lift f g ≫ inv (coprod.desc (prod.lift 𝟙 0) (prod.lift 0 𝟙)) ≫ coprod.desc 𝟙 𝟙 = 0` (HA's addition written directly); each field uses the earlier ones through `letI`, and the zero maps come from `HasZeroObject.zeroMorphismsOfZeroObject`. The target: `IsHAAdditive C` holds exactly when C admits a `Preadditive` structure with `HasFiniteBiproducts C`, and that structure is unique.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Preadditive`, `Limits.HasFiniteBiproducts`, `Limits.HasZeroObject`.

**Triangulated categories** (HA Definition 1.1.2.5, PDF pp. 22–23). Verdier's definition: an additive category with an automorphism `X ↦ X[1]` and a class of distinguished triangles satisfying TR1–TR4. This is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated` (TR1–TR3) with `CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated` (TR4, the octahedral axiom). Mathlib's statements of TR3 and TR4 differ in form from HA's; the target is that HA's axioms, as stated, are equivalent to the Mathlib classes, and no new definition is made.

*Lean:* no new definition: Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated C` (TR1–TR3) and `CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated C` (TR4), on a preadditive C with `HasZeroObject C`, `HasShift C ℤ` and additive shift functors. The target states HA's TR1–TR4 as written and proves them equivalent to these classes.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated`, `CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated`.

**Suspension and loops** (`SSet.suspension`, `SSet.loops`; HA construction before Remark 1.1.2.6, Remark 1.1.2.6, Notation 1.1.2.7, PDF pp. 23–24). Let C be pointed with cofibres. The full subcategory `M_Σ ⊆ Fun(Δ[1] × Δ[1], C)` of pushout squares `X ⟶ 0, X ⟶ 0', 0 ⟶ Y, 0' ⟶ Y` with `0, 0'` zero objects maps to C by evaluation at the initial vertex, and this map is a trivial fibration (HTT 4.3.2.15 twice). A section followed by evaluation at the final vertex is the suspension `Σ_C : C ⟶ C`; dually `Ω_C` from pullback squares when C has fibres. When C is stable the two subcategories coincide and Σ, Ω are inverse equivalences. Notation 1.1.2.7: `X[n]` is `Σⁿ X` for `n ≥ 0` and `Ω^{−n} X` for `n ≤ 0`, on C and on `hC`.

*Lean:* `SSet.suspension C : C ⟶ C` as a chosen section composed with evaluation, together with the trivial fibration `M_Σ ⟶ C`; any two choices are naturally equivalent. On `hoFunctor.obj C`, a Mathlib shift `HasShift (hoFunctor.obj C) ℤ` with `shiftFunctor 1` induced by Σ, for C pointed with cofibres and Σ an equivalence, together with `SSet.hoFunctor.shiftOneIso C X : X⟦1⟧ ≅ Σ X` (Σ the functor of `hoFunctor.obj C` induced by `SSet.suspension C`), which ties Mathlib's shift to the suspension so that triangles ending in `Σ X` (1.1.2.11) can be read as Mathlib triangles ending in `X⟦1⟧`. Theorem 1.1.2.14 in Lurie's hypotheses needs the shift (and the preadditive structure of 1.1.2.9) whenever C is pointed with cofibres and Σ an equivalence; provide them in that generality, with the stable case as a specialization.

**Checks.**

- For C stable, `Ω ∘ Σ` and `Σ ∘ Ω` are naturally equivalent to the identity.
- In `Fun(K, C)` suspension is computed pointwise.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.9; 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); `SSet.IsPushout` (L5.10); Mathlib `CategoryTheory.HasShift`.

**The homotopy category is additive** (HA Lemma 1.1.2.9, PDF pp. 24–25). If C is pointed, has cofibres, and Σ is an equivalence, then `hC` is additive. Moreover C itself has finite coproducts: `X ⊔ Y` is the cofibre of the zero map `X[−1] ⟶ Y`.

*Lean:* `Preadditive (hoFunctor.obj C)`, `HasZeroObject (hoFunctor.obj C)` and `HasFiniteBiproducts (hoFunctor.obj C)` (additivity in Mathlib's form, 1.1.2.1) under the hypotheses of the lemma (pointed, cofibres, Σ an equivalence), not only for `[SSet.IsStable C]`, so that 1.1.2.14 can be stated in Lurie's generality.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `Map(ΣX, Y) ≃ Ω Map(X, Y)` (Remark 1.1.2.8) makes `π₀ Map(Σ²X, Y) ≅ π₂ Map(X, Y)` an abelian group functorially; coproducts through cofib preserving coproducts in `Fun(Δ[1], C)` (Remark 1.1.1.8, HTT 5.1.2.2).

*Needs:* 1.1.1.8, suspension (above); 5.1.2.2 (L6); `SSet.KanComplex.π` with its group structure (Tau Ceti); 1.1.2.1.

**Transposing a suspension square negates the class** (HA Lemma 1.1.2.10, PDF pp. 25–26). For C pointed with cofibres, a pushout square `X ⟶ 0, X ⟶ 0', 0 ⟶ Y, 0' ⟶ Y` classifies θ in `Hom_{hC}(X[1], Y) ≅ π₁ Map_C(X, Y)`; its transpose (swapping the roles of 0 and 0') classifies −θ.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: compare the involution on `C_{σ/} ×_C {Y}` with loop reversal on the based loop space of `Hom^L_C(X, Y)`.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.6; `HTT.A.2.7/kan-fibrations`; `SSet.KanComplex.π` (Tau Ceti).

**Distinguished triangles** (HA Definition 1.1.2.11 and Remark 1.1.2.12, PDF p. 26). For C pointed with cofibres, a diagram `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z ⟶ X[1]` in `hC` is distinguished when there is a diagram `Δ[1] × Δ[2] ⟶ C` with rows `X ⟶ Y ⟶ 0` and `0' ⟶ Z ⟶ W`, both squares pushouts and `0, 0'` zero objects, whose edges represent f and g, and whose last map is the edge `Z ⟶ W` composed with the equivalence `W ≃ X[1]` given by the outer rectangle. The definition is used mostly for stable C, but needs only cofibres (1.1.2.12).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsDistinguishedTriangle (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (h : Z ⟶ Σ X)`, for morphisms of `hoFunctor.obj C` with C a pointed quasicategory with cofibres (HA's generality; not restricted to stable C) and `Σ` induced by `SSet.suspension`: some `Δ[1] ⊗ Δ[2] ⟶ C` satisfies HA's conditions (i)–(iv) above. For stable C, the `Pretriangulated` instance of 1.1.2.14 takes as `distinguishedTriangles` the Mathlib triangles `Triangle.mk f g h` satisfying it.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.6, suspension (above).

**Distinguished triangles from a column of pushouts** (HA Lemma 1.1.2.13, PDF p. 27). For C stable and a diagram `Δ[2] × Δ[1] ⟶ C` with columns `X ⟶ Y ⟶ 0'` and `0 ⟶ Z ⟶ W`, both squares pushouts and `0, 0'` zero, the triangle `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z ⟶ X[1]` with last map `−h'` is distinguished, where `h'` is `Z ⟶ W` composed with the outer-square equivalence `W ≃ X[1]`.

*Needs:* 1.1.2.10, 1.1.2.11.

**The homotopy category is triangulated** (HA Theorem 1.1.2.14, PDF pp. 27–30). If C is pointed, has cofibres, and Σ is an equivalence, then `hC`, with the translation of Notation 1.1.2.7 and the distinguished triangles of 1.1.2.11, is a triangulated category. The hypotheses hold when C is stable.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HA.1.1.2.14/cofiber-diagrams` (cofibre diagrams, axioms TR1 and TR3), `HA.1.1.2.14/rotation` (axiom TR2) and `HA.1.1.2.14/octahedral` (axiom TR4), and this entry's own target `HA.1.1.2.14`, which assembles them into the `Pretriangulated` and `IsTriangulated` structures on `hoFunctor.obj C`.

*Lean:* `SSet.hoFunctor_isTriangulated` for C a pointed quasicategory with cofibres whose suspension is an equivalence (the hypotheses under which the suspension and additivity entries give the shift and the preadditive structure): there are a zero object, additive shift functors and a `Pretriangulated` structure on `hoFunctor.obj C` that is `IsTriangulated`, whose distinguished triangles are exactly those isomorphic to `Triangle.mk f g (h ≫ (hoFunctor.shiftOneIso C X).inv)` with `SSet.IsDistinguishedTriangle f g h` (f, g, h between images of vertices of C). The `Pretriangulated` and `IsTriangulated` instances are derived from it. For `[SSet.IsStable C]` the hypotheses hold; this specialization gives the triangulated structure on `hoFunctor.obj C` that the t-structure targets (1.2.1.1 on) use.

**Checks.**

- For `f = id_X` the cofibre is a zero object, so `X ⟶ X ⟶ 0 ⟶ X[1]` is distinguished (TR1 (c)).
- An exact functor of stable ∞-categories (`HA.1.1.4/intro`) induces a Mathlib triangulated functor (`Functor.IsTriangulated`) of homotopy categories.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. TR1 and TR3 from the trivial fibration `E ⟶ Fun(Δ[1], C)` restricting diagrams of 1.1.2.11 to their first edge (`HA.1.1.2.14/cofiber-diagrams`); TR2 from 1.1.2.13 (`HA.1.1.2.14/rotation`); TR4 from one diagram on a poset of pushout squares (`HA.1.1.2.14/octahedral`).

*Needs:* `HA.1.1.2.14/cofiber-diagrams`, `HA.1.1.2.14/rotation`, `HA.1.1.2.14/octahedral` (below); 1.1.2.5, 1.1.2.11; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Triangulated`.

**Cofibre diagrams and TR1, TR3** (`HA.1.1.2.14/cofiber-diagrams`, part 1 of 3 of the triangulation of the homotopy category above; HA Theorem 1.1.2.14, axioms TR1 and TR3, PDF pp. 27–29). Let C be pointed with cofibres and Σ an equivalence, and let E ⊆ `Fun(Δ[1] × Δ[2], C)` be the full subcategory of diagrams of the shape of 1.1.2.11. Restriction to the first edge `E ⟶ Fun(Δ[1], C)` is a trivial fibration. Hence every morphism of hC extends to a distinguished triangle, the distinguished triangles are closed under isomorphism and include `X ⟶ X ⟶ 0 ⟶ X[1]`, and a commutative square between the first edges of two distinguished triangles extends to a morphism of triangles.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: 4.3.2.15 once per Kan-extension step of the diagram; TR3 by lifting a square `Δ[1] × Δ[1] ⟶ C` through the same trivial fibration, with `Δ[1]` as a parameter.

*Needs:* 1.1.2.7, 1.1.2.9, 1.1.2.11; 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated` (field shapes).

**Rotation of distinguished triangles** (`HA.1.1.2.14/rotation`, part 2 of 3 of the triangulation of the homotopy category above; HA Theorem 1.1.2.14, axiom TR2, PDF pp. 28–29). A triangle `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z ⟶ X[1]` in hC is distinguished exactly when its rotation `Y ⟶ Z ⟶ X[1] ⟶ Y[1]`, with last map `−f[1]`, is.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: extend a distinguished diagram by one more pushout and apply 1.1.2.13 to the right-hand rectangle, with its sign; for the converse, desuspend and rotate repeatedly, using that Σ is an equivalence.

*Needs:* `HA.1.1.2.14/cofiber-diagrams`; 1.1.2.13.

**The octahedral axiom** (`HA.1.1.2.14/octahedral`, part 3 of 3 of the triangulation of the homotopy category above; HA Theorem 1.1.2.14, axiom TR4, PDF pp. 29–30). For composable `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` in hC, the distinguished triangles on f, g and `g ∘ f`, together with a distinguished triangle `Y/X ⟶ Z/X ⟶ Z/Y ⟶ (Y/X)[1]`, form the octahedral diagram of Mathlib's `Triangulated.Octahedron`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: one functor from the nerve of the poset indexing a staircase of pushout squares with zero corners, built by 4.3.2.15; its rectangles give the four triangles, and the required commutativity already holds in C.

*Needs:* `HA.1.1.2.14/cofiber-diagrams`; 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated`, `Triangulated.Octahedron`.

**Ext groups** (HA Notation 1.1.2.17, PDF p. 30). For X, Y in a stable ∞-category, `Extⁿ_C(X, Y) = Hom_{hC}(X[−n], Y)`, an abelian group; for `n < 0` it is `π_{−n} Map_C(X, Y)`.

*Lean:* no new definition beyond the notation: `Hom` in `hoFunctor.obj C` from `X⟦−n⟧`; the identification with homotopy groups of `Hom_C(X, Y)` at the zero map is a lemma.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.9, 1.1.2.14.

**Functor ∞-categories are stable** (HA Proposition 1.1.3.1, PDF p. 30). For C stable and K any simplicial set, `Fun(K, C)` is stable.

*Proof route.* Zero objects, fibres and cofibres in `Fun(K, C)` are computed pointwise (HTT 5.1.2.2), and pushout and pullback squares are detected pointwise.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.9; 5.1.2.2 (L6).

**Stable subcategories** (HA Definition 1.1.3.2, PDF p. 30). A full subcategory `C' ⊆ C` of a stable ∞-category that contains a zero object and is closed under fibres and cofibres is stable; it is then a stable subcategory.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsStableSubcategory C'` for a full subcategory (`SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory` on a set of objects closed under equivalence) of a stable C, as the three closure conditions; the stability of `C'` is a lemma.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.9.

**Closure under cofibres and shifts suffices** (HA Lemma 1.1.3.3, PDF pp. 30–31). A nonempty full subcategory of a stable ∞-category closed under cofibres and under the translations `X ↦ X[n]`, `n ∈ ℤ`, is a stable subcategory. (Lurie's statement omits nonemptiness; the empty subcategory satisfies both closure conditions but has no zero object, which 1.1.3.2 requires.)

*Proof route.* `fib(f) ≃ cofib(f)[−1]` (from 1.1.2.14); for any X in the subcategory, `cofib(id_X)` is a zero object in it.

*Needs:* 1.1.3.2, 1.1.2.14.

**Stability through finite limits and colimits** (HA Proposition 1.1.3.4, PDF pp. 31–32). A pointed ∞-category C is stable exactly when it has finite limits and finite colimits and a square in C is a pushout exactly when it is a pullback.

**Checks.**

- In a stable C, `X ⊔ Y ⟶ X × Y` is an equivalence (Remark 1.1.3.5), so finite coproducts are biproducts.
- A coequalizer of `f, f' : X ⇉ Y` is `cofib(f − f')`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Finite colimits from coequalizers and finite coproducts (HTT 4.4.3.2, 1.1.2.9). Pushouts are pullbacks: pullback squares form a stable subcategory D of `Fun(Δ[1] × Δ[1], C)` (1.1.3.3); left Kan extension `i_! : Fun(Λ[2, 0], C) ⟶ Fun(Δ[1] × Δ[1], C)` preserves finite colimits, hence is exact (1.1.4.1, the easy direction (2) ⇒ (3)), and every span is a finite colimit of five spans whose pushouts are visibly pullbacks.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.9, 1.1.2.9, 1.1.3.1, 1.1.3.3; 1.1.4.1 ((2) ⇒ (3) only, which is immediate from the definition); 4.4.3.2 (L5.10); 4.3.2.15 (L5.9).

**`Ind_κ` of a stable ∞-category is stable** (HA Proposition 1.1.3.6, PDF pp. 32–33). For a small stable ∞-category C and κ regular, `Ind_κ(C)` is stable.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the Yoneda embedding j preserves finite limits and colimits (HTT 5.1.3.2, 5.3.5.14); morphisms of `Ind_κ(C)` are κ-filtered colimits of morphisms in the image of j (5.3.5.15); fibres are computed in `P(C)`, where filtered colimits are left exact. Lurie cites HTT Example 7.3.4.7 (L11) for left exactness of filtered colimits in the ∞-topos `P(C)`; use instead HTT 5.3.3.3 (κ-filtered colimits commute with κ-small limits in `S`, L6) with pointwise computation in `P(C)` (5.1.2.2), which avoids chapter 7.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.9; 5.3.5.1, 5.3.5.14 (L6), 5.3.5.15 (L7); 5.1.3.2, 5.1.2.2, `HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if` (L6).

**Idempotent completions are stable** (HA Corollary 1.1.3.7, PDF p. 33). The idempotent completion of a stable ∞-category is stable.

*Proof route.* By HTT 5.4.2.4 it is a full subcategory of `Ind(C)` closed under shifts and finite colimits; apply 1.1.3.3 and 1.1.3.6.

*Needs:* 1.1.3.3, 1.1.3.6; 5.4.2.4 (L7); 5.1.4.1 (L6).

**Exact functors and `Cat∞^Ex`** (`SSet.IsExact`, `SSet.catInftyEx`; `HA.1.1.4/intro`, PDF p. 33). A functor `F : C ⟶ C'` between stable ∞-categories is exact when it carries zero objects to zero objects and fibre sequences to fibre sequences. Identities and composites of exact functors are exact, so the stable (small) ∞-categories and exact functors form a subcategory `Cat∞^Ex ⊆ Cat∞`.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsExact F` for `F : C ⟶ C'` with `[SSet.IsStable C] [SSet.IsStable C']`: `(∀ X, IsZeroObject X → IsZeroObject (F X)) ∧ ∀ σ : Triangle C, σ.IsFiberSequence → IsPullback (σ.1 ≫ F)`. `SSet.catInftyEx := subcomplexOf catInfty (fun v ↦ IsStable (catInfty.obj v)) (fun e ↦ ∀ (_ : IsStable (obj (δ 1 e))) (_ : IsStable (obj (δ 0 e))), IsExact (catInfty.edgeMap (Edge.mk' e)))`, the subcategory on stable objects and exact edges, with the decodings `catInfty.obj` and `catInfty.edgeMap` of vertices and edges of `SSet.catInfty` (propose).

*Needs:* 1.1.1.4, 1.1.1.9; Tau Ceti `SSet.catInfty`.

**Exactness is left or right exactness** (HA Proposition 1.1.4.1, PDF pp. 33–34). For a functor between stable ∞-categories, the following are equivalent: it preserves finite limits; it preserves finite colimits; it is exact.

*Proof route.* Exact functors preserve coequalizers and finite coproducts (the proofs of 1.1.3.4 and 1.1.2.9), hence finite colimits (HTT 4.4.3.2); dually.

*Needs:* `HA.1.1.4/intro`, 1.1.2.9, 1.1.3.4; 4.4.3.2 (L5.10).

**Fibre products of stable ∞-categories** (HA Proposition 1.1.4.2, PDF p. 34). In a categorical pullback square of ∞-categories `C' = C ×_D D'` with C, D, D' stable and `F : C ⟶ D`, `G : D' ⟶ D` exact, C' is stable, the projections are exact, and a functor from a stable E to C' is exact exactly when both composites are.

*Proof route.* 1.1.3.4 with HTT 5.4.5.5 (limits in a homotopy fibre product are computed componentwise).

*Needs:* 1.1.3.4, 1.1.4.1; 5.4.5.5 (L7).

**Products of stable ∞-categories** (HA Proposition 1.1.4.3, PDF p. 34). A product `∏_α C_α` of stable ∞-categories is stable, and a functor into it is exact exactly when each component is.

*Needs:* `HA.1.1.4/intro`, 1.1.4.1; limits in products computed componentwise (5.1.2.2, L6).

**`Cat∞^Ex` has small limits** (HA Theorem 1.1.4.4, PDF p. 35). `Cat∞^Ex` has small limits, and the inclusion into `Cat∞` preserves them.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: 1.1.4.2 and 1.1.4.3 in the argument of HTT 5.4.7.3 (limits as products and fibre products).

*Needs:* 1.1.4.2, 1.1.4.3; 5.4.7.3 (L7).

**Sections of a family of stable ∞-categories** (HA Proposition 1.1.4.5, PDF p. 35). Let `p : X ⟶ S` be an inner fibration whose fibres are stable ∞-categories and such that over every edge `Δ[1] ⟶ S` the pullback is a coCartesian fibration associated to an exact functor. Then the ∞-category `Map_S(S, X)` of sections is stable; a functor from a stable ∞-category into it is exact when every evaluation at a vertex is; and for any set E of edges of S, the full subcategory of sections carrying each edge of E to a coCartesian edge is a stable subcategory.

*Proof route.* HTT 5.4.7.11 with 1.1.4.4 and 1.1.3.1.

*Needs:* 1.1.3.1, 1.1.3.2, 1.1.4.4; 5.4.7.11 (L7); 2.4.2.1 (L3).

**`Cat∞^Ex` has filtered colimits** (HA Proposition 1.1.4.6, PDF pp. 35–36). `Cat∞^Ex` has small filtered colimits, preserved by the inclusion into `Cat∞`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's (PDF pp. 35–36): show that the colimit C in `Cat∞` of a filtered diagram of stable ∞-categories and exact functors is stable, that the maps `C_I ⟶ C` are exact, and that exactness of `C ⟶ D` is tested on the `C_I`; finite diagrams in C come from a stage, through the description of filtered colimits in `Cat∞` (HTT 5.4.1.2, 5.5.7.11).

*Needs:* 1.1.4.1; 5.3.1.7, 5.3.1.18 (L6); 5.4.1.2, 5.5.7.11 (L7).

### L9.2 t-structures and spectral sequences

**t-structures on triangulated categories** (HA Definition 1.2.1.1 and Notation 1.2.1.2, PDF p. 37). A t-structure on a triangulated category D is a pair of full subcategories `D_{≥0}`, `D_{≤0}`, closed under isomorphism, with `Hom(X, Y[−1]) = 0` for `X ∈ D_{≥0}`, `Y ∈ D_{≤0}`; `D_{≥0}[1] ⊆ D_{≥0}` and `D_{≤0}[−1] ⊆ D_{≤0}`; and for every X a fibre sequence `X' ⟶ X ⟶ X''` with `X' ∈ D_{≥0}`, `X'' ∈ D_{≤0}[−1]`. Notation 1.2.1.2: `D_{≥n} = D_{≥0}[n]`, `D_{≤n} = D_{≤0}[n]` (homological indexing).

*Lean:* Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure D`, through the layer's dictionary `D_{≥n} = t.le (−n)`, `D_{≤n} = t.ge (−n)`. Provide `TStructure.mkHomological` building a Mathlib t-structure from HA's three axioms on a pair of `ObjectProperty`s, and the two simp lemmas expressing `D_{≥n}`, `D_{≤n}` through `le`, `ge`: `TStructure.mkHomological_le_iff` (`(mkHomological …).le n X ↔ Dge (X⟦n⟧)`) and `TStructure.mkHomological_ge_iff` (`(mkHomological …).ge n X ↔ Dle (X⟦n⟧)`); no new structure.

**Checks.**

- HA's axiom (1) at `n = 0` is Mathlib's `zero'` (`le 0` to `ge 1`).
- `D_{≥n}[1] = D_{≥n+1}` under the dictionary (Mathlib `TStructure.shift_le`).

*Needs:* 1.1.2.5; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.Basic`.

**t-structures on stable ∞-categories** (HA Definition 1.2.1.4, PDF p. 38). A t-structure on a stable ∞-category C is a t-structure on `hC` (1.1.2.14); `C_{≥n}`, `C_{≤n}` are the full subcategories of C on the objects of `(hC)_{≥n}`, `(hC)_{≤n}`.

*Lean:* `SSet.TStructure C := TStructure (hoFunctor.obj C)`, taking as instance arguments Mathlib's `[Preadditive (hoFunctor.obj C)]`, `[HasZeroObject (hoFunctor.obj C)]`, `[HasShift (hoFunctor.obj C) ℤ]`, `[∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor (hoFunctor.obj C) n).Additive]` and `[Pretriangulated (hoFunctor.obj C)]`, which are constructed from `[SSet.IsStable C]` (HA 1.1.2.14) as instances, with `SSet.TStructure.geq t n`, `SSet.TStructure.leq t n` the full subcategories of C (`SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory`) in HA's indexing.

*Needs:* 1.2.1.1, 1.1.2.14.

**Truncations are reflective localizations** (HA Proposition 1.2.1.5, PDF p. 38). For a t-structure on a stable ∞-category C and every n, `C_{≤n} ⊆ C` is a reflective localization (the inclusion has a left adjoint `τ_{≤n}`); dually `C_{≥n} ⊆ C` has a right adjoint `τ_{≥n}` (Notation 1.2.1.7, not a target).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: by HTT 5.2.7.8 it suffices that the map `X ⟶ X''` of axiom (3) induces equivalences `Map(X'', Y) ⟶ Map(X, Y)` for `Y ∈ C_{≤−1}`; by Whitehead's theorem this is a statement about `Ext^k` for `k ≤ 0`, which follows from the long exact sequence and axioms (1)–(2).

*Needs:* 1.2.1.4, 1.1.2.17; 5.2.7.8 (L6); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`, `HTT.A.2.7/kan-weak-equivalences` (F2, Whitehead).

**Closure under limits and colimits** (HA Corollary 1.2.1.6, PDF p. 38). `C_{≤n}` is closed under all limits that exist in C, and `C_{≥n}` under all colimits that exist in C.

*Proof route.* A reflective subcategory is closed under limits (the inclusion is a right adjoint, HTT 5.2.3.5); dually.

*Needs:* 1.2.1.5; 5.2.3.5 (L6).

**Truncations commute** (HA Proposition 1.2.1.10, PDF pp. 39–40). For all m, n, the natural transformation `τ_{≤m} ∘ τ_{≥n} ⟶ τ_{≥n} ∘ τ_{≤m}` of functors `C ⟶ C_{≤m} ∩ C_{≥n}` is an equivalence. The transformation comes from the commuting square of Remark 1.2.1.8 (truncations preserve each `C_{≤m}`), as in HTT §7.3.1; in Lean it is the mate of the identity of inclusions under the two adjunctions, which needs nothing from HTT chapter 7.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: a five-lemma argument on `Ext⁰` and `Ext¹`. Since both sides are objects of `hC`, the statement is the classical one in the triangulated category `hC`; Mathlib's `TStructure.truncGELEIsoLEGE (−m) (−n)` gives it in hC (by the dictionary HA's `τ_{≤m} τ_{≥n}` is `truncGELE (−m) (−n) = truncLE (−n) ⋙ truncGE (−m)` and `τ_{≥n} τ_{≤m}` is `truncLEGE (−m) (−n)`; the target checks that this isomorphism is θ) (with `TStructure.truncLE`, `TStructure.truncGE`, `TStructure.truncLTGE`); the target is the transfer.

*Needs:* 1.2.1.5, 1.1.2.17; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.truncGELEIsoLEGE` (in `Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Triangulated.TStructure.TruncLEGT`).

**The heart and homotopy objects** (`SSet.TStructure.heart`, `SSet.TStructure.homotopyObject`; HA Definition 1.2.1.11, PDF p. 40). The heart `C^♥ = C_{≥0} ∩ C_{≤0}`. `π₀ : C ⟶ C^♥` is `τ_{≤0} ∘ τ_{≥0} ≃ τ_{≥0} ∘ τ_{≤0}`, and `π_n X = π₀(X[−n])`. Lurie identifies `C^♥` with the abelian category `h(C^♥)` (Remark 1.2.1.12, below).

*Lean:* `SSet.TStructure.heart t := fullEnhancedSubcategory C fun x ↦ Triangulated.TStructure.heart t (mk x)` (Mathlib's heart named in full, since dot notation on the `abbrev` `SSet.TStructure` resolves `t.heart` to this definition); `homotopyObject t n : C ⟶ heart` as the composite of the shift `X ↦ X[−n]` (Notation 1.1.2.7: `Ω^n` for `n ≥ 0`, `Σ^{−n}` for `n < 0`) with `π₀ = τ_{≤0} ∘ τ_{≥0}`. That `h(C^♥)` is abelian is HA Remark 1.2.1.12, below, transported from the Mathlib-level `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart`; every target that speaks of homotopy objects in an abelian category (1.2.2.6 onward, 1.2.4.5, 1.3.2.19) uses it.

**Checks.**

- `X ∈ C_{≥n}` exactly when `τ_{≤n−1} X ≃ 0`.
- On the heart, `π₀` is equivalent to the identity.

*Needs:* 1.2.1.5, 1.2.1.10; Mathlib `TStructure.heart`.

**The heart of a t-structure is abelian** (`Triangulated.TStructure.heartAbelian`; `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart`; Beilinson–Bernstein–Deligne, *Faisceaux pervers*, Théorème 1.3.6; Kashiwara–Schapira, *Categories and Sheaves*, Theorem 10.1.11). Let C be a triangulated category and t a t-structure on C. Its heart, the full subcategory of objects that are both `≤ 0` and `≥ 0`, is an abelian category; it is closed under extensions in C.

*Lean:* in Mathlib's setting (`[Category C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [∀ n, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] [IsTriangulated C]`, `t : TStructure C`, `H` preadditive with `[t.Heart H]`): propose `noncomputable def TStructure.heartAbelian : Abelian H` (`@[instance_reducible]`, as `AbelianSubcategory.abelian`), and the instance `Abelian t.heart.FullSubcategory` obtained from it through `t.hasHeartFullSubcategory`. Supporting declarations (propose): `TStructure.heart_hom_shift_eq_zero` (`f : t.ιHeart.obj X ⟶ (t.ιHeart.obj Y)⟦n⟧`, `n < 0` ⊢ `f = 0`), `TStructure.admissibleMorphism_ιHeart` (`AbelianSubcategory.admissibleMorphism t.ιHeart = ⊤`), instances `(t.le n).IsTriangulatedClosed₂`, `(t.ge n).IsTriangulatedClosed₂`, `t.heart.ContainsZero`, `t.heart.IsClosedUnderFiniteProducts`, and `HasFiniteProducts H`. This closes the TODO of `TStructure/Heart.lean` and of `TStructure/Basic.lean`.

**Checks.**

- For `H = t.heart.FullSubcategory`, the zero object of C lies in the heart and is a zero object of H; `X ⊞ Y` of C lies in the heart when X and Y do (`binaryProductTriangle_distinguished`, `isLE₂`, `isGE₂`).
- For X, Y in the heart and `n = 1`, `ι X ⟶ (ι Y)⟦1⟧` need not vanish (it is `Ext¹` in the heart), so `heart_hom_shift_eq_zero` is sharp.

*Proof route.* Apply `AbelianSubcategory.abelian t.ιHeart`; four inputs.

1. Negative Ext vanishing (`hι`). `t.ιHeart.obj X` is `≤ 0`; for `n < 0`, `(t.ιHeart.obj Y)⟦n⟧` is `≥ −n` by `isGE_shift` (from `≥ 0`, since `n + (−n) = 0`), and `−n ≥ 1`; conclude by `TStructure.zero f 0 (−n)`.
2. Extension closure and finite products. `(t.le n).IsTriangulatedClosed₂` and `(t.ge n).IsTriangulatedClosed₂` by `IsTriangulatedClosed₂.mk'` from `isLE₂`, `isGE₂`; the `⊓` instance gives it for `t.heart`. Binary products: the proof of Mathlib's `IsClosedUnderBinaryProducts` instance for triangulated subcategories, with `binaryProductTriangle_distinguished`, under `IsTriangulatedClosed₂` instead of `IsTriangulated` (or generalize that Mathlib instance). Empty products from `ContainsZero` (0 is `≤ n` and `≥ n` for all n). Then `IsClosedUnderFiniteProducts.mk'` and `HasFiniteProducts t.heart.FullSubcategory`; for general H, transport along the equivalence `t.ιHeart.toEssImage` (and `essImage_ιHeart`) by `Adjunction.hasLimitsOfShape_of_equivalence`.
3. Admissibility (`hA`). Let `f₁ : X₁ ⟶ X₂` in H and `ι X₁ ⟶ ι X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ (ι X₁)⟦1⟧` distinguished (any completion, as `admissibleMorphism` quantifies over all of them). On the rotated triangle `ι X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ (ι X₁)⟦1⟧ ⟶ …`, `isLE₂` gives `X₃` `≤ 0` (`(ι X₁)⟦1⟧` is `≤ −1`) and `isGE₂` gives `X₃` `≥ −1`. Take `t.triangleLTGE_distinguished 0 X₃`: `(t.truncLT 0).obj X₃ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ (t.truncGE 0).obj X₃ ⟶ …` (HA's `τ_{≥1} Z ⟶ Z ⟶ τ_{≤0} Z`; `truncLT 0 = truncLE (−1)`). The first vertex is `≤ −1` (instance) and `≥ −1` (the `[IsGE X a]` instance on `truncLT`, needs `IsTriangulated`); the third is `≥ 0` (instance) and `≤ 0` (the `[IsLE X b]` instance on `truncGE`). So `K₀ := ((t.truncLT 0).obj X₃)⟦−1⟧` and `Q₀ := (t.truncGE 0).obj X₃` lie in the heart (`isLE_shift`, `isGE_shift`); choose `K Q : H` with `ι K ≅ K₀`, `ι Q ≅ Q₀` (`essImage_ιHeart`, `Functor.objObjPreimageIso`), compose with `shiftFunctorCompIsoId C (−1) 1`, and transport the truncation triangle by `isomorphic_distinguished` and `Triangle.isoMk` to the shape `(ι K)⟦1⟧ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ ι Q ⟶ (ι K)⟦1⟧⟦1⟧`.
4. `[IsTriangulated C]` is used for the image–coimage step inside `AbelianSubcategory.abelian` (octahedron) and for the truncation instances of step 3.

*Needs:* Mathlib `Triangulated.TStructure` (`Basic`, `Heart`, `TruncLTGE`, `TruncLEGT`), `Triangulated.AbelianSubcategory.abelian`, `ObjectProperty.IsTriangulatedClosed₂`, `ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderFiniteProducts`, `IsTriangulated`.

**Kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences in the heart** (`HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-ker-coker`; part of BBD Théorème 1.3.6, the heart being an admissible abelian subcategory in the sense of BBD 1.2.5). In the setting of `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart`, let `f : X₁ ⟶ X₂` in the heart and `ι X₁ ⟶ ι X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ (ι X₁)⟦1⟧` distinguished. Then `ι (kernel f) ≅ ((t.truncLT 0).obj X₃)⟦−1⟧` (HA: `ker f ≅ π₁ Z`, Z the cofibre), with `(ι (kernel.ι f))⟦1⟧` matching `(t.truncLTι 0).app X₃ ≫ f₃`, and `ι (cokernel f) ≅ (t.truncGE 0).obj X₃` (HA: `coker f ≅ π₀ Z`), with `ι (cokernel.π f)` matching `f₂ ≫ (t.truncGEπ 0).app X₃`. A sequence `0 ⟶ A ⟶ B ⟶ D ⟶ 0` in the heart is short exact exactly when there is `δ : ι D ⟶ (ι A)⟦1⟧` making `ι A ⟶ ι B ⟶ ι D ⟶ (ι A)⟦1⟧` distinguished.

*Lean:* propose `TStructure.ιHeartKernelIso` and `TStructure.ιHeartCokernelIso` (isomorphisms in C with the two compatibilities as `@[reassoc]` lemmas); `TStructure.shortExact_of_distTriang` (`Triangle.mk (ι.map S.f) (ι.map S.g) δ ∈ distTriang C → S.ShortExact` for `S : ShortComplex H`); `TStructure.exists_distTriang_of_shortExact` (`S.ShortExact → ∃ δ, Triangle.mk (ι.map S.f) (ι.map S.g) δ ∈ distTriang C`).

**Checks.**

- f is a monomorphism exactly when `X₃` is `≥ 0`, i.e. `X₃` lies in the heart and is the cokernel; f is an epimorphism exactly when `X₃` is `≤ −1`, i.e. `X₃ ≅ (ι (kernel f))⟦1⟧`.

*Proof route.* 1. Kernel and cokernel: the admissibility triangle of step 3 of `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart` fed to `AbelianSubcategory.isLimitKernelFork` and `isColimitCokernelCofork`; compare with `kernel f`, `cokernel f` by `IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso` and its colimit dual; the compatibilities are `shift_ι_map_ιK` and `ι_map_πQ`. 2. Triangle to short exact: `isLimitKernelForkOfDistTriang` (f is a kernel of g, hence mono, and exact) and `isColimitCokernelCoforkOfDistTriang` (g is a cokernel of f, hence epi). 3. Short exact to triangle: `exists_distinguished_triangle_of_epi` for `S.g` gives a triangle `ι X ⟶ ι B ⟶ ι D`; X is a kernel of `S.g` by `isLimitKernelForkOfDistTriang`, as is `S.X₁` by `ShortExact.fIsKernel`; transport the triangle along the unique isomorphism of kernels.

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart`; Mathlib `Triangulated.AbelianSubcategory`, `ShortComplex.ShortExact`.

**`H⁰` is a homological functor to the heart** (`Triangulated.TStructure.homology₀`, `Triangulated.TStructure.homology`; `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-homology`; BBD Théorème 1.3.6). In the setting of `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart`, the functor `H⁰ = τ^{≥0} τ^{≤0} : C ⟶ heart` (HA's `π₀`, Definition 1.2.1.11) sends distinguished triangles to exact sequences; hence each triangle gives a long exact sequence `⋯ ⟶ Hⁿ X ⟶ Hⁿ Y ⟶ Hⁿ Z ⟶ Hⁿ⁺¹ X ⟶ ⋯` with `Hⁿ X = H⁰(X⟦n⟧)` (HA's `π_{−n} X`). On the heart, `H⁰` is isomorphic to the identity.

*Lean:* propose `TStructure.homology₀ : C ⥤ H` with `TStructure.homology₀ιHeartIso : t.homology₀ ⋙ t.ιHeart ≅ t.truncGELE 0 0` (lift of `t.truncGELE 0 0` through ι, whose objects lie in the heart, using `essImage_ιHeart` and an inverse of `t.ιHeart.toEssImage`; for `H = t.heart.FullSubcategory`, `ObjectProperty.lift`); instance `t.homology₀.IsHomological`; `t.homology₀.ShiftSequence ℤ` by `ShiftSequence.tautological`, so that `homology n := t.homology₀.shift n` and Mathlib's `homologySequence_exact₁/₂/₃`, `homologySequenceδ` give the long exact sequence; `TStructure.ιHeartCompHomology₀Iso : t.ιHeart ⋙ t.homology₀ ≅ 𝟭 H`.

**Checks.**

- For X in the heart, `Hⁿ X = 0` for `n ≠ 0` (`truncLT`/`truncGE` of a shifted heart object vanish).
- For `f` in the heart with cone `X₃`, the long exact sequence of `ι X₁ ⟶ ι X₂ ⟶ X₃` reads `0 ⟶ H⁻¹ X₃ ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ H⁰ X₃ ⟶ 0`, recovering `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-ker-coker`.

*Proof route.* Prove exactness of `H⁰ X ⟶ H⁰ Y ⟶ H⁰ Z` for every distinguished `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z ⟶ X⟦1⟧` (`IsHomological.mk'`; additivity from `truncLE`, `truncGE` being additive):

1. If X, Y, Z are `≤ 0`: `H⁰ ≅ truncGE 0` there, and for W in the heart `Hom(truncGE 0 A, W) ≅ Hom(A, W)` (`descTruncGE`, `from_truncGE_obj_ext`); since `X⟦1⟧` is `≤ −1`, `Hom(X⟦1⟧, W) = 0`, so `Hom(−, W)` turns the triangle into a left exact sequence for every W, and `H⁰ X ⟶ H⁰ Y ⟶ H⁰ Z ⟶ 0` is exact. Dually if X, Y, Z are `≥ 0` (`H⁰ ≅ truncLE 0`, `liftTruncLE`, `to_truncLE_obj_ext`, `Hom(W, Z⟦−1⟧) = 0`): `0 ⟶ H⁰ X ⟶ H⁰ Y ⟶ H⁰ Z` is exact.
2. If X is `≤ 0` alone: `truncGE 1` of `Y ⟶ Z` is an isomorphism (`isIso₂_truncGE_map_of_isLE` with `n₀ = 0`), and the octahedron on `X ⟶ truncLE 0 Y ⟶ Y` produces a distinguished `X ⟶ truncLE 0 Y ⟶ truncLE 0 Z ⟶ X⟦1⟧` (its third vertex is `≤ 0` and maps to Z with cone `truncGE 1 Z`; identify by uniqueness of truncation triangles, `isLE_iff_isIso_truncLEι_app`); apply step 1 and `H⁰ ∘ truncLE 0 ≅ H⁰`. Dually if Z is `≥ 0` alone, with `isIso₁_truncLE_map_of_isGE`.
3. General case: with `X' = truncLE 0 X`, `X'' = truncGT 0 X`, the octahedron on `X' ⟶ X ⟶ Y` gives triangles `X' ⟶ Y ⟶ C'` and `X'' ⟶ C' ⟶ Z`. Step 2 for the first (X' is `≤ 0`) gives `H⁰ X' ⟶ H⁰ Y ⟶ H⁰ C' ⟶ 0` exact; step 2 for the rotation `C' ⟶ Z ⟶ X''⟦1⟧` (`X''⟦1⟧` is `≥ 0`) makes `H⁰ C' ⟶ H⁰ Z` a monomorphism; and `H⁰ X' ⟶ H⁰ X` is an isomorphism. Since `Y ⟶ C' ⟶ Z` is `Y ⟶ Z` (octahedron), the kernel of `H⁰ Y ⟶ H⁰ Z` is the image of `H⁰ X`.
4. `H⁰ ∘ ι ≅ 𝟭`: on heart objects `truncLEι 0` and `truncGEπ 0` are isomorphisms.

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart`, `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-ker-coker` (the second Check); Mathlib `TStructure.truncGELE`, `truncGELEIsoLEGE`, `isIso₂_truncGE_map_of_isLE`, `isIso₁_truncLE_map_of_isGE`, `Functor.IsHomological`, `Functor.ShiftSequence`, `IsTriangulated`.

**The heart is abelian** (`SSet.TStructure.heart_discrete`, `SSet.TStructure.heartHoEquiv`; HA Remark 1.2.1.12, PDF p. 40). Let C be a stable ∞-category with a t-structure. For X, Y in `C^♥` the mapping space `Map_C(X, Y)` is discrete, so `C^♥` is equivalent to the nerve of its homotopy category `h(C^♥)`; and `h(C^♥)` is an abelian category.

*Lean:* the abelian structure is the instance `Abelian (Triangulated.TStructure.heart t).FullSubcategory` of `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart` for `t : SSet.TStructure C` on `hoFunctor.obj C`, which is `IsTriangulated` by 1.1.2.14; no separate theorem. Propose `SSet.TStructure.heartHoEquiv t : hoFunctor.obj (SSet.TStructure.heart t) ≌ (Triangulated.TStructure.heart t).FullSubcategory` (the homotopy category of a full enhanced subcategory of a quasicategory is the full subcategory of the homotopy category, `HTT.1.2.11/intro`), `SSet.TStructure.heart_discrete` (for vertices x, y of `SSet.TStructure.heart t`, every homotopy group `π_n` of `Hom^R(x, y)`, `n ≥ 1`, at every base point is trivial), and `SSet.TStructure.isCategoricalEquivalence_heart` (the unit `SSet.TStructure.heart t ⟶ nerve (hoFunctor.obj (SSet.TStructure.heart t))` is an `SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence`).

*Proof route.* 1. Discreteness: mapping spaces in a stable ∞-category are grouplike, so all components of `Map(X, Y)` are equivalent and `π_n Map(X, Y) ≅ Ext^{−n}(X, Y) = Hom_{hC}(X[n], Y)` (1.1.2.17); for `n ≥ 1`, `X[n] ∈ C_{≥n}` and `Y ∈ C_{≤0}` (Mathlib: `X⟦n⟧` is `≤ −n`, Y is `≥ 0`), so it vanishes by `TStructure.zero`. 2. A quasicategory with discrete mapping spaces is equivalent to the nerve of its homotopy category (HTT 2.3.4.18 with n = 1, via 2.3.4.12). 3. Abelianness: transport `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart` along `heartHoEquiv`.

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart`; 1.2.1.4, 1.2.1.11, 1.1.2.14, 1.1.2.17; 2.3.4.18 (L3); `HTT.1.2.11/intro` (`SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory`).

**Quasisaturated classes** (HA Definition 1.2.1.14, PDF p. 41). In an ∞-category with pushouts, a class S of morphisms is quasisaturated when it contains the equivalences, has two-out-of-three for 2-simplices, and is closed under pushout. Intersections of quasisaturated classes are quasisaturated, so every class generates one.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsQuasisaturated S` for `S` a predicate on edges of a quasicategory C, as the three conditions; `SSet.quasisaturatedClosure S` as the intersection.

*Needs:* `SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence`; `SSet.IsPushout` (L5.10).

**Closed under extensions** (HA Definition 1.2.1.15, PDF p. 42). A full subcategory `C' ⊆ C` of a stable ∞-category is closed under extensions when, for every fibre sequence `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z` with X and Z in C', Y is in C'.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsClosedUnderExtensions C'`, a predicate on full subcategories (sets of objects closed under equivalence) of a stable C: for every triangle σ of C that is a fibre sequence, if `squareVertex σ 0 0` and `squareVertex σ 1 1` are in C', then `squareVertex σ 0 1` is in C' (L9.1).

*Needs:* 1.1.1.4, 1.1.1.9.

**t-localizations** (HA Proposition 1.2.1.16, PDF pp. 42–43). For a stable ∞-category C, a localization functor `L : C ⟶ C` (a reflective localization onto its essential image) and S the morphisms inverted by L, the following are equivalent: S is generated, as a quasisaturated class, by some morphisms of the form `0 ⟶ X`; it is generated by `{0 ⟶ X : LX ≃ 0}`; the essential image of L is closed under extensions; `Ext¹(LA, B) ⟶ Ext¹(A, B)` is injective for every A and every local B; `C_{≥0} = {A : LA ≃ 0}` and `C_{≤−1} = {A : LA ≃ A}` form a t-structure.

*Needs:* 1.2.1.1, 1.2.1.4, 1.2.1.14, 1.2.1.15, 1.1.2.17; 5.2.7.4, 5.2.7.8 (L6); 5.5.4.1 (L7, S-local objects).

**Bounded t-structures and the left completion** (`HA.1.2.1.16/after`, PDF p. 44). For a stable ∞-category C with a t-structure: `C⁺ = ⋃ₙ C_{≤n}`, `C⁻ = ⋃ₙ C_{≥−n}`, `C^b = C⁺ ∩ C⁻` are stable subcategories; C is left bounded, right bounded, bounded when `C = C⁺`, `C⁻`, `C^b`. The left completion `Ĉ` is the limit in `Cat∞` of the tower `⋯ ⟶ C_{≤1} ⟶ C_{≤0} ⟶ C_{≤−1} ⟶ ⋯` of truncation functors; concretely, the full subcategory of `Fun(N(ℤ), C)` of functors F with `F(n) ∈ C_{≤−n}` for each n and `τ_{≤−n} F(m) ⟶ F(n)` an equivalence for `m ≤ n`.

*Lean:* `SSet.TStructure.leftCompletion t` defined as the concrete full subcategory of `Fun(uliftFunctor.{u}.obj (nerve ℤ), C)` (with ℤ ordered as a poset; `nerve ℤ : SSet.{0}` is lifted to C's universe); the identification with the limit of the tower (HTT 3.3.3.1–3.3.3.2) is a lemma. `IsLeftBounded`, `IsRightBounded`, `IsBounded` as predicates on t.

*Needs:* 1.2.1.5, 1.1.3.2; 3.3.3.1 (L5.1); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3).

**The left completion** (HA Proposition 1.2.1.17, PDF pp. 44–45). For C stable with a t-structure: `Ĉ` is stable; the full subcategories of functors landing in `C_{≤0}`, resp. `C_{≥0}`, form a t-structure on `Ĉ`; and there is an exact functor `C ⟶ Ĉ` restricting to an equivalence `C_{≤0} ⟶ Ĉ_{≤0}`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. (1): `Ĉ` is also the limit of the tower `⋯ ⟶ C_{≤0} ⟶ C_{≤0}` whose maps are `τ_{≤0} ∘ Σ`, the suspension of `C_{≤0}`; so `Ĉ^op ≃ Sp((C_{≤0})^op)` by 1.4.2.24, stable by 1.4.2.17 (L9.6). (Lurie writes `Ĉ^op ≃ Sp(C_{≤0})`, PDF p. 44; the opposite belongs on `C_{≤0}`, whose suspension `τ_{≤0} ∘ Σ` is the loop functor of `(C_{≤0})^op`.) (3): the functor comes from a left adjoint to `D ⊆ N(ℤ) × C` (HTT 5.2.7.8), and exactness is right exactness (1.1.4.1).

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.1.16/after`; 1.1.4.1; 1.4.2.17, 1.4.2.24 (L9.6, forward); 5.2.7.8 (L6); `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`.

**Left complete** (`SSet.TStructure.IsLeftComplete`; `HA.1.2.1.17/after`, PDF p. 45). C with a t-structure is left complete when the functor `C ⟶ Ĉ` of 1.2.1.17 is an equivalence.

*Lean:* `IsLeftComplete t := SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence (toLeftCompletion t)`; right completeness dually (Remark 1.2.1.20, not a target).

*Needs:* 1.2.1.17.

**A criterion for left completeness** (HA Proposition 1.2.1.19, PDF pp. 45–46). If C has countable products and `C_{≥0}` is closed under them, then C is left complete exactly when `C_{≥∞} = ⋂ₙ C_{≥n}` consists of zero objects.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: towers have limits (fibre of a map of products), the functor `C ⟶ Ĉ` has a right adjoint `lim`, and the unit and counit are checked on truncations using TR4.

*Needs:* 1.2.1.17, `HA.1.2.1.17/after`, 1.1.2.5; `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`.

**I-complexes** (`SSet.gap`; HA Definition 1.2.2.2, PDF p. 47). For a pointed ∞-category C and a linearly ordered set I, let `I^{[1]}` be the poset of pairs `i ≤ j` ordered componentwise. An I-complex is a functor `F : N(I^{[1]}) ⟶ C` with every `F(i, i)` a zero object and, for `i ≤ j ≤ k`, the square `F(i, j) ⟶ F(i, k)`, `F(j, j) ⟶ F(j, k)` a pushout. `Gap(I, C) ⊆ Fun(N(I^{[1]}), C)` is the full subcategory of I-complexes.

*Lean:* `SSet.gap I C` for `[LinearOrder I]` and a pointed quasicategory C, as a full subcategory of `Fun(nerve (I × I restricted to i ≤ j), C)`; the poset `I^{[1]}` as `{p : I × I // p.1 ≤ p.2}` with the product order.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.1; `SSet.IsPushout` (L5.10); Mathlib `nerve`.

**The chain complex of a ℤ-complex** (HA Remark 1.2.2.3, PDF pp. 47–48). For `F ∈ Gap(ℤ, C)` with C stable, the pushout squares give boundary maps `δ : F(n, n+1) ⟶ F(n−1, n)[1]`, and `C_n = F(n−1, n)[−n]` with the induced maps is a chain complex in `hC` (`d ∘ d = 0`, because `F(n−2, n−2) ≃ 0`).

*Lean:* a functor from `SSet.gap ℤ C` to `CochainComplex (hoFunctor.obj C) ℤ` (Mathlib `HomologicalComplex`), with HA's `C_n` in cochain degree −n (the Conventions' dictionary).

*Needs:* 1.2.2.2, 1.1.2.14.

**Complexes are determined by their first row** (HA Lemma 1.2.2.4, PDF p. 48). For a pointed C with pushouts and `I = I₀ ∪ {−∞}` with least element −∞, restriction along `i ↦ (−∞, i)` is a trivial fibration, in particular an equivalence, `Gap(I, C) ⟶ Fun(N(I₀), C)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: a complex is a left Kan extension of its restriction to `J = {(−∞, j)} ∪ {(i, i)}`, which is a right Kan extension of its restriction to `I₀`; existence by HTT 4.3.2.13 and conclusion by 4.3.2.15.

*Needs:* 1.2.2.2; 4.3.2.13, 4.3.2.15 (L5.9).

**The spectral sequence of a ℤ-complex** (HA Construction 1.2.2.6 and Proposition 1.2.2.7, PDF pp. 49–51). Let C be stable with a t-structure whose heart is (the nerve of) an abelian category A, and `X ∈ Gap(ℤ, C)`. Set `E_r^{p,q} = im(π_{p+q} X(p−r, p) ⟶ π_{p+q} X(p−1, p+r−1))` for `r ≥ 1`, with the differential `d_r : E_r^{p,q} ⟶ E_r^{p−r, q+r−1}` induced by the boundary maps of the long exact sequences (1.2.2.6). Then `d_r ∘ d_r = 0` and `E_{r+1} ≅ ker d_r / im d_r` canonically (1.2.2.7): `{E_r, d_r}` is a spectral sequence in A.

*Parts.* Proposition 1.2.2.7 is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HA.1.2.2.7/d-squared` (the differentials square to zero) and `HA.1.2.2.7/pages` (each page is the homology of the one before), and the target `HA.1.2.2.7`, which combines them into the spectral sequence of the *Lean* line.

*Lean:* a homological spectral sequence in `h(C^♥)`, in Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence`-shaped API if one exists at the baseline; otherwise propose `SSet.TStructure.spectralSequence X : ℕ → (ℤ × ℤ → heart)` with `d`, `d_comp_d` and the page isomorphism as fields. Mathlib's spectral objects (`CategoryTheory.Abelian.SpectralObject`, `Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.SpectralObject`) give an alternative construction: the homotopy objects of `X(i, j)` form a spectral object over the poset ℤ; if that is used, the target is the identification of the pages with HA's formula, and `HA.1.2.2.7/d-squared` and `HA.1.2.2.7/pages` reduce to that identification.

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.2.7/d-squared`, `HA.1.2.2.7/pages` (below); 1.2.2.2, 1.2.1.11, 1.2.1.12 (the heart abelian, `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart`), 1.2.1.2; long exact sequences of homotopy objects (`HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-homology`, through Mathlib's `Functor.IsHomological` and `homologySequence`).

**Differentials square to zero** (`HA.1.2.2.7/d-squared`, part 1 of 2 of Proposition 1.2.2.7 in the spectral sequence of a ℤ-complex above; HA Proposition 1.2.2.7 (1), PDF pp. 49–50). For `X ∈ Gap(ℤ, C)` and `r ≥ 1`, the composite `d_r ∘ d_r : E_r^{p+r, q−r+1} ⟶ E_r^{p−r, q+r−1}` is zero.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `E_r^{p,q}` is a quotient of `π_{p+q} X(p − r, p)`, and the composite of the two boundary maps factors through `π_* X(p − r, p − r) = 0`.

*Needs:* 1.2.2.6; `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-homology`.

**The next page is the homology** (`HA.1.2.2.7/pages`, part 2 of 2 of Proposition 1.2.2.7 in the spectral sequence of a ℤ-complex above; HA Proposition 1.2.2.7 (2), PDF pp. 49–51). With `Z = ker d_r` and `B = im d_r` on `E_r^{p,q}`, there is a canonical isomorphism `E_{r+1}^{p,q} ≅ Z / B` in the heart, natural in X.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `E_{r+1}^{p,q}` is the image in the factorization `π_{p+q} X(p−r−1, p) ⟶ Z ⟶ Z/B ⟶ E_r/B ⟶ π_{p+q} X(p−1, p+r)`. The first composite is an epimorphism (two pullbacks of epimorphisms along exact rows), and dually the last composite is a monomorphism.

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.2.7/d-squared`; 1.2.2.6; `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-heart`, `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-homology`.

**The first page** (HA Remark 1.2.2.8, PDF p. 49). For fixed q, the complex `(E_1^{∗,q}, d_1)` is the chain complex of Remark 1.2.2.3 with the homological functor `π_q` applied.

*Needs:* 1.2.2.3, 1.2.2.6; `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-homology` (`π_q` is homological); Mathlib `Functor.IsHomological`.

**Filtered objects and their spectral sequence** (HA Definition 1.2.2.9, PDF p. 52). A filtered object of a stable C is a functor `X : N(ℤ) ⟶ C`. With a t-structure, extend X to a complex in `Gap(ℤ ∪ {−∞}, C)` (1.2.2.4), restrict to `Gap(ℤ, C)`, and take its spectral sequence (1.2.2.6–1.2.2.7). It is independent of the extension up to canonical isomorphism (Remark 1.2.2.10).

*Lean:* filtered objects are `Fun(uliftFunctor.{u}.obj (nerve ℤ), C)`, no new definition; `SSet.TStructure.filteredSpectralSequence X` through a chosen inverse of the trivial fibration of 1.2.2.4.

*Needs:* 1.2.2.4, 1.2.2.6, `HA.1.2.2.7/pages`.

**Sequential colimits and compatible t-structures** (HA Definition 1.2.2.12, PDF p. 52). An ∞-category admits sequential colimits when every `N(ℤ_{≥0}) ⟶ C` has a colimit. For C stable with sequential colimits, a t-structure is compatible with sequential colimits when `C_{≤0}` is closed under them.

*Lean:* `SSet.HasColimitsOfShape (uliftFunctor.{u}.obj (nerve ℕ)) C` (L5.6 supporting predicate); `SSet.TStructure.IsCompatibleWithSequentialColimits t`, the same as `IsCompatibleWithFilteredColimits` (1.3.5.20) with `I = uliftFunctor.{u}.obj (nerve ℕ)`.

*Needs:* 1.2.1.4; `SSet.IsColimit` (L1.5).

**Sequential colimits in the heart are exact** (HA Remark 1.2.2.13, PDF p. 52). For C stable with sequential colimits and a t-structure compatible with them, the inclusion of the heart and every `π_n` preserve sequential colimits, so sequential colimits of monomorphisms in the heart are monomorphisms.

*Needs:* 1.2.2.12, 1.2.1.11; 1.2.1.5, 1.2.1.6.

**Convergence** (HA Proposition 1.2.2.14, PDF pp. 52–53). If C is stable with sequential colimits and a t-structure compatible with them, and the filtered object X has `X(n) ≃ 0` for `n ≪ 0`, its spectral sequence converges to `π_{p+q} colim X`.

*Lean:* state convergence in the explicit form: for each n, the filtration of `π_n(colim X)` by the images of `π_n X(p)` has associated graded `E_∞^{p, n−p} = colim_r E_r^{p, n−p}` (the `E_r` stabilize to a colimit of quotients for `r > p − p₀`, where `X(p) = 0` for `p < p₀`), vanishes for `p < p₀`, and is exhaustive.

*Needs:* 1.2.2.9, 1.2.2.12, 1.2.2.13.

### L9.3 The Dold–Kan correspondence
