The classical part (§1.2.3) is Mathlib's, for additive categories: `AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan` (`Γ₀`, `N₁`, `N₂`, `Γ₂`) and `CategoryTheory.Idempotents.DoldKan.equivalence` for idempotent complete preadditive categories with finite coproducts, with `AlgebraicTopology.normalizedMooreComplex` and `AlgebraicTopology.alternatingFaceMapComplex`. Tau Ceti main adds `TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/DoldKan/` (homotopy groups of simplicial modules as homology, `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.piAddEquivNormalizedMooreComplexHomology`, and of `DK K` as the homology of K, `ChainComplex.doldKanPiAddEquivHomology`) and the Alexander–Whitney and Eilenberg–Zilber maps of simplicial sets (`SSet.alexanderWhitney`, `SSet.eilenbergZilberHomotopyEquiv`). The targets below are HA's statements, mostly comparisons with these.

**Chain complexes** (HA Definition 1.2.3.1, PDF p. 54). For an additive category A, `Ch(A)` is the additive category of ℤ-graded chain complexes with differential of degree −1 (homological indexing), and `Ch(A)_{≥n}`, `Ch(A)_{≤n}` the full subcategories of complexes vanishing below, resp. above, degree n.

*Lean:* `Ch(A)` is Mathlib `CochainComplex A ℤ` throughout L9, by the Conventions' dictionary: HA's chain degree m is cochain degree −m. Vanishing conditions are stated in cochain degrees: `Ch(A)_{≥n}` is `CochainComplex.IsStrictlyLE (−n)` (`∀ k > −n, Limits.IsZero (K.X k)`) and `Ch(A)_{≤n}` is `CochainComplex.IsStrictlyGE (−n)` (`∀ k < −n, Limits.IsZero (K.X k)`), as `ObjectProperty (CochainComplex A ℤ)`. `Ch(A)_{≥0}` is compared with `ChainComplex A ℕ` through Mathlib's `ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat : Embedding (down ℕ) (up ℤ)`, which sends chain degree k to cochain degree −k, with its extension functor.

*Needs:* Mathlib `HomologicalComplex`.

**The Dold–Kan construction** (HA Construction 1.2.3.5, PDF p. 55). For a nonnegatively graded complex A in an additive category, `DK_n(A) = ⊕_{α : [n] ↠ [k]} A_k`, with face and degeneracy maps given by identities, differentials or zero according to the factorization of `α ∘ β`. This is Mathlib's `AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀`, which is defined by the same sum over epimorphisms (`Splitting.IndexSet`); the target is the identification of the structure maps with HA's matrix.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.1; Mathlib `AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀`.

**`DK` of a shifted ℤ** (HA Example 1.2.3.6, PDF p. 55). `DK(ℤ[n]) ≅ ℤΔ[n] / ℤ∂Δ[n]`, the free simplicial abelian group on `Δ[n]` modulo the one on its boundary.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.5; Mathlib `SSet.stdSimplex`, `SSet.boundary`, free simplicial abelian groups (`CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject (ModuleCat ℤ)`).

**The Dold–Kan correspondence** (HA Theorem 1.2.3.7, PDF pp. 56, 58–59). For an additive category A, `DK : Ch(A)_{≥0} ⟶ Fun(Δ^op, A)` is fully faithful, and an equivalence when A is idempotent complete.

*Lean:* for idempotent complete A with finite coproducts this is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Idempotents.DoldKan.equivalence` with `Γ` its inverse direction; the target adds full faithfulness of `Γ₀` for any additive A (Mathlib's `Γ₀` factors through the Karoubi envelope, where `Γ₂` is an equivalence, which gives it).

*Proof route.* Mathlib's. HA's route (reduce to abelian groups through `A ⟶ Fun(A^op, Ab)` and Lemma 1.2.3.13) is not needed.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.5; Mathlib `AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan`, `CategoryTheory.Idempotents.DoldKan`.

**Unnormalized chain complexes** (HA Definition 1.2.3.8, PDF p. 56). For a semisimplicial (or simplicial) object of an additive category, `C_*(A)` has `C_n = A_n` and differential `Σᵢ (−1)ⁱ dᵢ`. Mathlib's `AlgebraicTopology.alternatingFaceMapComplex` (for simplicial objects); for semisimplicial objects propose `AlgebraicTopology.alternatingFaceMapComplexSemi` on functors from `Δ_s^op` (needed by 1.2.4.3; an additive construction, so not under `SSet`).

*Lean:* Mathlib `AlgebraicTopology.alternatingFaceMapComplex A : SimplicialObject A ⥤ ChainComplex A ℕ` for simplicial objects, viewed in `Ch(A) = CochainComplex A ℤ` through the embedding of 1.2.3.1. For semisimplicial objects (`Δ_sᵒᵖ ⥤ A`, 6.5.3.6), propose `AlgebraicTopology.alternatingFaceMapComplexSemi`, with `C_n = A_n` and differential `∑ i, (−1)^i d_i`; its restriction along `Δ_s ⊆ Δ` agrees with the former.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.1; Mathlib `AlgebraicTopology.alternatingFaceMapComplex`; 6.5.3.6 (L6, semisimplicial objects).

**Normalized chain complexes** (HA Definition 1.2.3.9, PDF p. 56). For a simplicial object of an abelian category, `N_n(A) = ⋂_{1 ≤ i ≤ n} ker dᵢ ⊆ A_n` with differential `d₀`. Mathlib's `AlgebraicTopology.normalizedMooreComplex`, which uses the same faces (`δ k.succ`).

*Lean:* no new definition: Mathlib `AlgebraicTopology.normalizedMooreComplex A : SimplicialObject A ⥤ ChainComplex A ℕ` for abelian A, with `N_n = ⨅_{1 ≤ i ≤ n} ker d_i` and differential `d₀` (in `Ch(A)` through the embedding of 1.2.3.1).

*Needs:* 1.2.3.1; Mathlib `AlgebraicTopology.normalizedMooreComplex`.

**`N ∘ DK ≅ id`** (HA Remark 1.2.3.11, PDF p. 57). For A abelian and a nonnegative complex A, `N_*(DK(A)) ≅ A` naturally, through the summand of the identity `[n] ⟶ [n]`.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.5, 1.2.3.9; Mathlib `AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.N₁Γ₀`.

**`N` is right adjoint to `DK`** (HA Lemma 1.2.3.12, PDF p. 57). For A abelian, the isomorphism of 1.2.3.11 is the unit of an adjunction `DK ⊣ N_*`.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.11; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Adjunction`, `AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan`.

**Dold–Kan for abelian groups** (HA Lemma 1.2.3.13, PDF pp. 57–58). `DK : Ch(Ab)_{≥0} ⟶ Fun(Δ^op, Ab)` is an equivalence. A special case of Mathlib's equivalence; the target is that the counit `DK(N_*(A)) ⟶ A` of 1.2.3.12 is an isomorphism.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.12; Mathlib `AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan` (or the pseudoabelian `CategoryTheory.Idempotents.DoldKan.equivalence`).

**Homotopy groups of simplicial abelian groups** (HA Remark 1.2.3.14, PDF p. 58). The underlying simplicial set of a simplicial abelian group is a Kan complex based at 0; its homotopy groups carry the induced abelian group structure, agreeing with the usual one for `n > 0`, and `π_n A ≅ H_n(N_*(A))`. Tau Ceti main: `kanComplex_comp_forget_addCommGrpCat` (Kan) and `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.piAddEquivNormalizedMooreComplexHomology`, `piZeroEquivNormalizedMooreComplexHomology` (the identification, for a simplicial module A); its Dold–Kan form is `ChainComplex.doldKanPiAddEquivHomology`, identifying `π_n(DK K)` with `H_n(K)` for a chain complex K.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.9; `SSet.KanComplex.π` (Tau Ceti); Tau Ceti `DoldKan/HomotopyGroups.lean`, `TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/KanComplex/MooreComplex.lean`.

**Normalization in idempotent complete additive categories** (HA Remark 1.2.3.15, PDF pp. 59–60). For A idempotent complete additive, `N_*` is the inverse of DK; `N_n(A)` is a kernel of `(d₁, …, d_n) : A_n ⟶ ⊕ A_{n−1}` (which exists although A need not be abelian), giving a monomorphism `u : N_*(A) ⟶ C_*(A)`. Mathlib: `N₁`, `PInftyToNormalizedMooreComplex`, `inclusionOfMooreComplexMap` (in the abelian case), with the Karoubi-envelope form of `N` for idempotent complete A.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.7, 1.2.3.9, 1.2.3.12.

**The dual description by degeneracies** (HA Remark 1.2.3.16, PDF p. 60). In the same setting, `N_n(A)` is also a cokernel of `(s₀, …, s_{n−1}) : ⊕ A_{n−1} ⟶ A_n`, giving an epimorphism `v : C_*(A) ⟶ N_*(A)` with `v ∘ u = id`. Mathlib's `PInfty` is the corresponding idempotent.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.15; Mathlib `AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.PInfty`.

**Normalization is a quasi-isomorphism** (HA Proposition 1.2.3.17, PDF pp. 60–61). For A abelian and a simplicial object of A, u and v are quasi-isomorphisms. Mathlib proves the stronger statement that they are chain homotopy equivalences (`AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.homotopyEquivNormalizedMooreComplexAlternatingFaceMapComplex`); the target is the corollary.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.15, 1.2.3.16; Mathlib `AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.HomotopyEquivalence`.

**Multi-additive functors** (HA Definition 1.2.3.19, PDF p. 61). A functor `F : A₁ × ⋯ × A_n ⟶ B` between additive categories is multi-additive when it preserves direct sums separately in each variable.

*Lean:* for `n = 2`, a functor `A₁ ⥤ A₂ ⥤ B` additive in each variable (Mathlib `Functor.Additive` on each partial functor); for general n, propose `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMultiAdditive` on functors out of `(i : Fin n) → A i` (Mathlib `Functor.pi`-style), each partial functor additive.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.1; Mathlib `Functor.Additive`.

**Chain complexes of a multi-additive functor** (HA Remark 1.2.3.21, PDF p. 62). A multi-additive F induces `Ch(F)_{≥0} : ∏ Ch(Aᵢ)_{≥0} ⟶ Ch(B)_{≥0}` with `Ch(F)_p = ⊕_{p = p₁ + ⋯ + p_n} F(A¹_{p₁}, …, Aⁿ_{p_n})` and the Koszul-signed differential; and `Ch(F)` on unbounded complexes when B has countable coproducts. For `n = 2` this is Mathlib's total complex of the bicomplex `HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor` (`HomologicalComplex₂.total`).

*Needs:* 1.2.3.19; Mathlib `HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor`, `HomologicalComplex₂.total`.

**Alexander–Whitney maps** (HA Construction 1.2.3.22, PDF pp. 62–63). For a multi-additive F between idempotent complete additive categories and simplicial objects `Aⁱ`, the front-face/back-face maps `F(A¹_p, …, Aⁿ_p) ⟶ F(A¹_{p₁}, …, Aⁿ_{p_n})` along the consecutive inclusions `[pᵢ] ⊆ [p]` assemble to chain maps `AW : C_*(F(A¹, …, Aⁿ)) ⟶ Ch(F)_{≥0}(C_*(A¹), …, C_*(Aⁿ))`, and descend to normalized complexes. Tau Ceti main has `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.alexanderWhitney` (for a monoidal preadditive category, `n = 2`) and `SSet.alexanderWhitney` (chains of simplicial sets).

*Needs:* 1.2.3.16, 1.2.3.21; Tau Ceti `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.alexanderWhitney`.

**Order dependence** (HA Remark 1.2.3.23, PDF p. 63). The Alexander–Whitney maps depend on the ordering of the factors: they are not symmetric. A Remark with nothing to prove beyond fixing the ordering convention in 1.2.3.22; record a counterexample to symmetry as a check (for `F = ⊗` on abelian groups, swapping the factors of `AW` on `Δ[1] × Δ[1]` gives a different map).

*Needs:* 1.2.3.22.

**Compatibility with composition** (HA Remark 1.2.3.25, PDF pp. 63–64). For an order-preserving `α : {1, …, n} ⟶ {1, …, m}`, multi-additive `F : ∏ Bᵢ ⟶ C` and `Gᵢ : ∏_{α(j) = i} A_j ⟶ Bᵢ`, with composite H: `Ch(H)_{≥0} ≅ Ch(F)_{≥0} ∘ ∏ Ch(Gᵢ)_{≥0}`, and `AW_H` is the composite of `AW_F` with the `AW_{Gᵢ}`, on normalized and on unnormalized complexes.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.21, 1.2.3.22.

**Normalized chains are lax monoidal** (HA Example 1.2.3.26, PDF p. 64). For a monoidal, additive, idempotent complete A with ⊗ additive in each variable, `Ch(A)_{≥0}` is monoidal and `N_*`, `C_*` are lax monoidal through AW (oplax in Mathlib's direction: maps `N(A ⊗ B) ⟶ N(A) ⊗ N(B)`), so DK is lax monoidal (HTT A.1.3.5). Tau Ceti main proves this for `MonoidalPreadditive` categories with finite coproducts (`TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/DoldKan/Monoidal.lean`: N oplax monoidal through `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.alexanderWhitney`, Γ lax monoidal); the target is that statement, plus the unnormalized `C_*`.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.22, 1.2.3.25, 1.2.3.7; HTT A.1.3.5 (F1.2); Mathlib `MonoidalCategory`, `Functor.OplaxMonoidal`, `Functor.LaxMonoidal`.

**Lattices act on additive categories** (HA Example 1.2.3.27, PDF pp. 64–65). `Lat`, the full subcategory of free abelian groups of finite rank, acts on any additive A by `ℤⁿ ⊗ A = Aⁿ`, a multi-additive functor `Lat × A ⟶ A` unique up to isomorphism; for idempotent complete A, AW gives `N_*(L ⊗ A) ⟶ N_*(L) ⊗ N_*(A)`, compatible with the action of a second `L'`.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.22, 1.2.3.25.

**Alexander–Whitney maps are quasi-isomorphisms** (HA Proposition 1.2.3.28, PDF p. 65). For a multi-additive F between idempotent complete additive categories with B abelian, and simplicial objects `Aⁱ`, `AW : N_*(F(A¹, …, Aⁿ)) ⟶ Ch(F)_{≥0}(N_*(A¹), …, N_*(Aⁿ))` is a quasi-isomorphism.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: by Dold–Kan and filtration by degree, reduce to `Aⁱ = DK(Mⁱ[pᵢ])`, where the map is `F(M¹, …, Mⁿ)` tensored (through 1.2.3.27) with the map `N_*(K)/N_*(∂K) ⟶ ℤ[p]` for `K = ∏ Δ[pᵢ]` and ∂K its simplices non-surjective in some factor; that map is a quasi-isomorphism by a direct computation of `H_*(K, ∂K)` (Lurie); the Eilenberg–Zilber equivalence `N_*(∏ Δ[pᵢ]) ≃ ⊗ N_*(Δ[pᵢ])` (Tau Ceti `SSet.eilenbergZilberHomotopyEquiv`) gives it as well.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.6, 1.2.3.7, 1.2.3.22, 1.2.3.27; Tau Ceti `SSet.eilenbergZilberHomotopyEquiv`.

**The ∞-categorical Dold–Kan correspondence** (HA Theorem 1.2.4.1, PDF pp. 66, 76–77). For a stable ∞-category C, `Fun(N(ℤ_{≥0}), C)` and `Fun(N(Δ)^op, C)` are equivalent. The equivalence sends a simplicial object X to the filtered object of colimits of its skeleta (Remark 1.2.4.2). That `D(k)` is a colimit of `X|N(Δ_{≤k})^op`, so that `colim_k D(k)` is a geometric realization of X when either exists, is a lemma of this target, used by `HA.1.2.4.5/realization`.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HA.1.2.4.1/simplicial` (simplicial objects as functors on I), `HA.1.2.4.1/extension` (extending to the augmentation) and `HA.1.2.4.1/filtered` (restricting to the filtration), and this entry's own target `HA.1.2.4.1`, which composes the three equivalences.

*Lean:* an equivalence (`SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence`, or a zigzag of them) built as Lurie's zigzag `Fun(N(Δ)^op, C) ⟶ Fun⁰(I, C) ⟵ Fun⁰(I⁺, C) ⟶ Fun(N(ℤ_{≥0}), C)`. The posets `I ⊆ I⁺` and `Fun⁰(I, C)` are defined in the part `HA.1.2.4.1/simplicial`, and `Fun⁰(I⁺, C)` in the part `HA.1.2.4.1/extension`. This target states the theorem as the existence of the zigzag with each map a categorical equivalence, and names the composite with chosen inverses.

**Checks.**

- The filtered object of a simplicial object X starts with `D(0) ≃ X₀`.
- A constant simplicial object at X goes to a filtered object with all `D(k) ≃ X` and equivalences as maps (`Δ_{≤k}` has the final object `[0]`, so `N(Δ_{≤k})` is weakly contractible).

*Proof route.* Lurie's (PDF pp. 76–77): each of the three maps is an equivalence. The first (composition with `I ⟶ N(Δ)^op`) is `HA.1.2.4.1/simplicial`, the middle one (restriction from `I⁺` to I) is `HA.1.2.4.1/extension`, and the third (restriction to `N(ℤ_{≥0})`) is `HA.1.2.4.1/filtered`.

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.4.1/simplicial`, `HA.1.2.4.1/extension`, `HA.1.2.4.1/filtered` (below); for the skeletal description of `D(k)`, 4.1.3.1 (L5.4) and 4.2.3.4, 4.2.3.10 (L5.6).

**Simplicial objects as functors on I** (`HA.1.2.4.1/simplicial`, part 1 of 3 of the ∞-categorical Dold–Kan correspondence above; HA Theorem 1.2.4.1, first step of the proof, PDF pp. 76–77). Let `I⁺ ⊆ N(ℤ_{≥0}) × N(Δ₊)^op` be spanned by the pairs `(n, [m])` with `m ≤ n`, `I ⊆ I⁺` by those with `0 ≤ m`, `p : I ⟶ N(Δ)^op` the projection, and `Fun⁰(I, C)` the functors carrying each `(m, [s]) ⟶ (n, [s])` to an equivalence. For every ∞-category C, composition with p is an equivalence `Fun(N(Δ)^op, C) ⟶ Fun⁰(I, C)`.

*Lean:* the posets `I ⊆ I⁺`, the projection p and the full subcategory `Fun⁰(I, C)` are defined here.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: on the truncations `I^{≤k}`, `Fun⁰` consists of right Kan extensions from `I^k ≃ N(Δ_{≤k})^op` (4.3.2.15), and p restricts to a section; take the limit over k.

*Needs:* 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); 6.1.2.2 (L6); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3, towers: G is the limit of the equivalences `G_k`).

**Extending to the augmentation** (`HA.1.2.4.1/extension`, part 2 of 3 of the ∞-categorical Dold–Kan correspondence above; HA Theorem 1.2.4.1, second step of the proof, PDF pp. 76–77). For C stable, let `Fun⁰(I⁺, C)` be the functors whose restriction to I lies in `Fun⁰(I, C)` and that are left Kan extended from I. Restriction `Fun⁰(I⁺, C) ⟶ Fun⁰(I, C)` is a trivial fibration.

*Lean:* the full subcategory `Fun⁰(I⁺, C)` is defined here.

*Proof route.* 4.3.2.15: each `I_{/(n,[−1])}` is finite and C has finite colimits.

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.4.1/simplicial`; 1.1.1.9; 4.3.2.15 (L5.9).

**Restricting to the filtration** (`HA.1.2.4.1/filtered`, part 3 of 3 of the ∞-categorical Dold–Kan correspondence above; HA Theorem 1.2.4.1, third step of the proof, PDF pp. 76–77). For C stable, restriction along `N(ℤ_{≥0}) ⟶ I⁺`, `n ↦ (n, [−1])`, is an equivalence `Fun⁰(I⁺, C) ⟶ Fun(N(ℤ_{≥0}), C)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `Fun⁰(I⁺, C)` is the limit of a tower `D(k) ⟶ D(k − 1)`. Each step factors as two restrictions that are trivial fibrations by 4.3.2.15; one of them uses 1.2.4.19 and the left cofinality of `I^k ⊆ I^{≤k}`.

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.4.1/simplicial`; 1.2.4.19, 1.1.1.9, 1.2.2.4; 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); 4.1.3.1 (L5.4: `I^k ⊆ I^{≤k}` has the left adjoint `(n, [m]) ↦ (k, [m])`, so it is cofinal).

**Its chain complex** (HA Remark 1.2.4.3, PDF p. 67). For a simplicial object X of a stable C with associated filtered object D, two chain complexes in `hC` agree: the Dold–Kan complex of the simplicial object of `hC` (with `C_n = cofib(L_n X ⟶ X_n)`, `L_n` the latching object, HTT §A.2.9), and the complex `C'_n = cofib(D(n−1) ⟶ D(n))[−n]` of 1.2.2.3–1.2.2.4. The identification uses 1.2.4.18.

*Needs:* 1.2.4.1, 1.2.4.18, 1.2.2.3, 1.2.2.4, 1.2.3.7; A.2.9.7 (F1.8, latching objects); `hC` satisfies the splitting condition (∗) (summands split, from 1.1.2.14) needed for Dold–Kan in `hC`.

**The spectral sequence of a simplicial object** (HA Remark 1.2.4.4, PDF pp. 67–68). For C stable with a t-structure whose heart is an abelian A, and X a simplicial object of C, the spectral sequence of its filtered object (1.2.2.9) has `(E₁^{∗,q}, d₁)` equal to the normalized chain complex of the simplicial object `π_q X` of A.

*Needs:* 1.2.4.3, 1.2.2.8, 1.2.2.9, 1.2.3.9.

**Convergence for connective simplicial objects** (HA Proposition 1.2.4.5, PDF pp. 68–71). Let C be stable with a t-structure whose heart is an abelian A, X a simplicial object of `C_{≥0}`, D its filtered object and `E_r^{p,q}` its spectral sequence. Then: `E_r^{p,q} = 0` unless `p, q ≥ 0`, for all `r ≥ 1`; for `r > p, q + 1` the pages are constant, with value `E_∞^{p,q}`; `cofib(D(m) ⟶ D(n)) ∈ C_{≥m+1}` for `0 ≤ m ≤ n`; `π_n D(k) ⟶ π_n D(k+1)` is an epimorphism for `k = n` and an isomorphism for `k > n`, with colimit `A_n`; `A_n` has a finite filtration `F^p A_n = im(π_n D(p) ⟶ A_n)`, `0 ≤ p ≤ n`, with `F^p A_{p+q} / F^{p−1} A_{p+q} ≅ E_∞^{p,q}`; and if C has countable colimits or is left complete, X has a geometric realization `|X| ∈ C_{≥0}` with `π_n |X| ≅ A_n`.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HA.1.2.4.5/pages` (vanishing and stabilization of the pages), `HA.1.2.4.5/filtration` (the filtration of the abutment) and `HA.1.2.4.5/realization` (the geometric realization and its homotopy), and this entry's own target `HA.1.2.4.5`, which is their conjunction.

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.4.5/pages`, `HA.1.2.4.5/filtration`, `HA.1.2.4.5/realization` (below).

**Vanishing and stabilization of pages** (`HA.1.2.4.5/pages`, part 1 of 3 of convergence for connective simplicial objects above; HA Proposition 1.2.4.5 (1)–(3), PDF pp. 68, 70–71). For X a simplicial object of `C_{≥0}` with spectral sequence `E_r^{p,q}`: `E_1^{p,q}` is the p-th term of the normalized complex of `π_q X_•`, so `E_r^{p,q} = 0` unless `p, q ≥ 0`, for every `r ≥ 1`; and for `r > p` and `r > q + 1` the maps `E_r^{p,q} ≅ E_{r+1}^{p,q} ≅ ⋯` are isomorphisms, defining `E_∞^{p,q}`.

*Needs:* 1.2.4.4, 1.2.2.9.

**The filtration of the abutment** (`HA.1.2.4.5/filtration`, part 2 of 3 of convergence for connective simplicial objects above; HA Proposition 1.2.4.5 (4)–(6), PDF pp. 68, 71). With `D(0) ⟶ D(1) ⟶ ⋯` the filtered object of X: `cofib(D(m) ⟶ D(n)) ∈ C_{≥m+1}` for `m ≤ n`; `π_n D(k) ⟶ π_n D(k+1)` is an epimorphism for `k = n` and an isomorphism for `k > n`, with stable value `A_n`; the images `F^p A_n` of `π_n D(p)` form a finite filtration with `F^p A_{p+q} / F^{p−1} A_{p+q} ≅ E_∞^{p,q}`.

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.4.5/pages`; 1.2.4.7.

**Realization and its homotopy** (`HA.1.2.4.5/realization`, part 3 of 3 of convergence for connective simplicial objects above; HA Proposition 1.2.4.5 (7), PDF pp. 69, 71). If C has countable colimits, or the t-structure is left complete, then `X_•` has a geometric realization `|X_•| ∈ C_{≥0}` and `π_n |X_•| ≅ A_n`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. With countable colimits, `|X_•| = colim D(n)`, and (4) passes to the colimit. In the left complete case, build the colimit of the tower through the truncations, using C as the limit of the `C_{≤n}`.

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.4.5/filtration`; 1.2.4.1 (its skeletal description of `D(k)`); `HA.1.2.1.17/after`, `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-homology`; 6.1.2.12 (L6); 5.5.6.23 (L7); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3).

**Idempotent completeness of a stable ∞-category** (HA Lemma 1.2.4.6, PDF pp. 69–70). A stable ∞-category is idempotent complete exactly when its homotopy category is (Mathlib `IsIdempotentComplete`). In particular idempotents of `hC` lift to C (Warning 1.2.4.8, not a target).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: (2) ⇒ (1) through a cofinal `N(ℤ_{≥0}) ⟶ Idem` (HTT 4.4.5.17) and a direct sum splitting of the sequence; (1) ⇒ (2) by embedding C in `Ind(C)` (1.1.3.6) and splitting `Ext*` along the idempotent.

*Needs:* 1.1.3.6, 1.1.3.2; `SSet.IsIdempotentComplete`, `SSet.idem`, 4.4.5.17 (L5.10); Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsIdempotentComplete`.

**Terms of a simplicial object** (HA Remark 1.2.4.7, PDF p. 70). For a simplicial object X of a stable C with filtered object D, each `X_n` is, in the idempotent completion of C, a finite coproduct of the objects `Σ^{−m} cofib(D(m−1) ⟶ D(m))`, `0 ≤ m ≤ n` (`D(−1) = 0`).

*Needs:* 1.2.4.1, 1.2.4.6, 1.1.3.7; 1.2.3.7 (in `hC^∨`).

**Semisimplicial objects** (HA Variant 1.2.4.9, PDF p. 72). For a semisimplicial object X of C (a functor `N(Δ_s)^op ⟶ C`) and Y its left Kan extension to `N(Δ)^op`, the spectral sequence of Y (1.2.4.4) has `E₁^{p,q} ≅ π_q X_p` with `d₁` the alternating sum of the faces: the unnormalized complex of `π_q X`.

*Needs:* 1.2.4.4, 1.2.3.8; 6.5.3.6 (L6, semisimplicial objects); 4.3.2.2 (L5.9).

**Realizing semisimplicial resolutions** (HA Corollary 1.2.4.11, PDF p. 72). For C stable with a left complete t-structure with heart A and X a semisimplicial object of `C_{≥0}` such that each unnormalized complex `⋯ ⟶ π_q X₁ ⟶ π_q X₀` is an acyclic resolution of `A_q = coker`, X has a geometric realization `|X| ∈ C_{≥0}` and `π_q X₀ ⟶ π_q |X|` induces `A_q ≅ π_q |X|`.

*Needs:* `HA.1.2.4.5/realization`, 1.2.4.9, `HA.1.2.1.17/after`.

**The two-sided version** (HA Corollary 1.2.4.12, PDF pp. 72–73). If the t-structure is both left and right complete, the same conclusion holds for any semisimplicial object X of C whose complexes `⋯ ⟶ π_q X₁ ⟶ π_q X₀` are acyclic resolutions of `A_q = coker` for every integer q: X has a geometric realization and `π_q X₀ ⟶ π_q |X|` induces `A_q ≅ π_q |X|` for every q. (Lurie's statement says "for every integer q ≥ 0" in the hypothesis; his proof uses every q.)

*Proof route.* Write X as the colimit of `τ_{≥−n} X` (right completeness), apply 1.2.4.11 to each, and identify the colimit with `|X|` by HTT 5.5.2.3.

*Needs:* 1.2.4.11; right completeness (dual of `HA.1.2.1.17/after`); 5.5.2.3 (L7).

**Cubes are colimits exactly when limits** (HA Proposition 1.2.4.13, PDF pp. 73–74). In a stable ∞-category, a cube `(Δ[1])ⁿ ⟶ C` is a colimit diagram exactly when it is a limit diagram (with `(Δ[1])ⁿ` the right cone of the cube minus its final vertex, and the left cone of the cube minus its initial vertex).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: induction on n through 1.2.4.15 and `cofib ≃ fib[1]`.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.9, 1.2.4.15; `SSet.IsColimit` (L1.5); 1.2.13.5 (L2).

**Pullbacks through cofibres** (HA Lemma 1.2.4.14, PDF p. 73). In a stable ∞-category, a square with vertical maps `f' : X' ⟶ Y'` and `f : X ⟶ Y` is a pullback exactly when the induced `cofib(f') ⟶ cofib(f)` is an equivalence.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.9, 1.1.3.4; 4.4.2.1 (L5.10).

**Colimit transformations through cofibres** (HA Lemma 1.2.4.15, PDF p. 74). For C stable with K-indexed colimits and a natural transformation `α : K^▷ × Δ[1] ⟶ C` between `p, q : K^▷ ⟶ C`, α is a colimit diagram exactly when `cofib(α) : K^▷ ⟶ C` is.

*Needs:* 1.2.4.14; 4.2.3.10 (L5.6); 1.2.8.4 (L1).

**A contractible space of sequences** (HA Lemma 1.2.4.16, PDF pp. 74–75). For a subset S of the open interval `(0, 1)` with at most n elements, the space of sequences `0 ≤ y₁ ≤ ⋯ ≤ y_n ≤ 1` (a subspace of `ℝⁿ`) whose value set contains S is contractible: it is homeomorphic to a simplex of dimension `n − |S|`. The proof of 1.2.4.17 below is combinatorial and does not use this lemma.

*Lean:* Mathlib `ContractibleSpace` for the subtype of `Fin n → ℝ`.

*Needs:* Mathlib topology (`ContractibleSpace`, `stdSimplex`).

**A cofinality lemma for `Δ_{≤n}`** (HA Lemma 1.2.4.17, PDF p. 75). Let I be the full subcategory of `(Δ_{≤n})_{/[n]}` on the injective maps `[m] ⟶ [n]`. Then `N(I) ⟶ N(Δ_{≤n})` is HA-right cofinal, that is, `N(I)^op ⟶ N(Δ_{≤n})^op` is cofinal (HTT 4.1.1.1).

*Proof route.* Theorem A (HTT 4.1.3.1, for the opposites) reduces the claim to weak contractibility, for each `m ≤ n`, of the nerve of the category J of diagrams `[m] ⟵ [k] ↪ [n]`. J is a poset, isomorphic to the poset of nonempty chains of the poset `V_{m,n}` on `[m] × [n]` with `(a, j) ⪯ (a', j')` when they are equal or `a ≤ a'` and `j < j'`. So `N(J) = sd N(V_{m,n})` (F2.3), and `N(V_{m,n}) ⊆ Δ[m] × Δ[n]` is Lurie's X, the simplices whose second projection is injective. Removing an element v from a finite poset Q gives a weak homotopy equivalence `N(Q − v) ⟶ N(Q)` when `N(Q_{>v})` (or, dually, `N(Q_{<v})`) is weakly contractible: the inclusion is cofinal by 4.1.3.1, its fibres being `N((Q − v)_{≥q})`, and cofinal maps are weak homotopy equivalences (4.1.1.3). Prove `N(V_{m,n})` weakly contractible for `m ≤ n` by induction on m. For m = 0, `V_{0,n}` is a chain. For m ≥ 1, remove `(m, 0), …, (m, n − 1)` in turn; each has as strict up-set the chain `(m, j + 1) < ⋯ < (m, n)`, which has a least element. Then remove `(m, n)`, whose strict down-set is `V_{m−1,n−1}`, weakly contractible by induction because `m − 1 ≤ n − 1`. What remains is `V_{m−1,n}`, weakly contractible by induction. The bound m ≤ n is needed: `N(V_{2,1})` is a circle. Lurie's topological argument (1.2.4.16 and the fibres of `|X| ⟶ |Δ^m|`, PDF p. 75) is not used.

*Needs:* 4.1.3.1, 4.1.1.3 (L5); `sd` and its last-vertex map (F2.3); `SSet.IsWeaklyContractible`.

**Colimits of truncated simplicial objects concentrated in one degree** (HA Corollary 1.2.4.18, PDF pp. 75–76). For C stable and `F : N(Δ_{≤n})^op ⟶ C` with `F([m]) ≃ 0` for `m < n`, the colimit of F is isomorphic in `hC` to `F([n])[n]`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: by 1.2.4.17 compute over `N(I)^op = sd(Δ[n])`, compare with the constant diagram, and identify the cofibre of `X ⊗ ∂Δ[n] ⟶ X ⊗ Δ[n]` (tensoring with simplicial sets, HTT §4.4.4) with `X[n]`; uses HTT 4.3.2.7.

*Needs:* 1.2.4.17; 4.3.2.7 (L5.9); colimits of constant diagrams `X ⊗ K` (HTT §4.4.4, L5.10).

**Kan extensions along augmented truncated simplex categories** (HA Lemma 1.2.4.19, PDF p. 76). For C stable, `n ≥ 0` and `F : N(Δ_{+,≤n})^op ⟶ C`, F is a left Kan extension of its restriction to `N(Δ_{≤n})^op` exactly when it is a right Kan extension of its restriction to `N(Δ_{+,≤n−1})^op`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: both conditions at `[n]` and `[−1]` reduce, through an inclusion with a right adjoint (cofinal after passing to opposites, so it preserves limits) and 1.2.4.17, to one cube `(Δ[1])^{n+1} ⟶ C` being a limit, resp. colimit, diagram; apply 1.2.4.13.

*Needs:* 1.2.4.13, 1.2.4.17; `SSet.IsLeftKanExtension` and its dual (L5.9); 1.2.13.5 (L2); `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction` (L1.2) with 4.1.3.1 (L5.4): the inclusion of the injective maps has a right adjoint, so its opposite has a left adjoint and is cofinal; that is, it is HA-right cofinal, which the right Kan extension condition at `[n]` uses.

### L9.4 Derived ∞-categories

Tau Ceti's differential graded categories are cochain-enriched (`TauCeti.DGCategory R C := EnrichedCategory (CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) C`), while HA's are chain-enriched. HA's degree-m element of `Map_C(X, Y)_*` is a Tau Ceti `DGHom R (−m) X Y`. Every target below is stated for Tau Ceti's `DGCategory` with this regrading; no chain-enriched copy is defined.

**Differential graded categories** (HA Definition 1.3.1.1, PDF p. 80; Remark 1.3.1.4, PDF p. 81). A dg category over a commutative ring k is a category enriched in chain complexes of k-modules, with Leibniz differentials, strictly associative and unital composition; equivalently (1.3.1.4) a `Ch(k)`-enriched category. Its underlying ordinary category has as morphisms the degree-0 cycles.

*Lean:* Tau Ceti `TauCeti.DGCategory R C` with `TauCeti.DGHom`, `TauCeti.dgDifferential`, `TauCeti.dgComp` (cochain grading as above). The underlying category of 1.3.1.4 is Mathlib's `ForgetEnrichment` of the enrichment, or Tau Ceti's degree-0 cycles `dgCycles`; the target is the identification of HA's description with it.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.1; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.EnrichedCategory`; Tau Ceti `TauCeti/CategoryTheory/DG/Basic.lean`.

**The homotopy category of a dg category** (HA Remark 1.3.1.5, PDF p. 81). `hC` has the objects of C and `Hom_{hC}(X, Y) = H₀(Map_C(X, Y))`, degree-0 cycles modulo boundaries. Tau Ceti `TauCeti.DGHomotopyCategory R C`.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.1; Tau Ceti `TauCeti/CategoryTheory/DG/HomotopyCategory.lean`.

**The differential graded nerve** (`TauCeti.dgNerve`; HA Construction 1.3.1.6, PDF p. 81). An n-simplex of `N_dg(C)` is a family of objects `X₀, …, X_n` with, for every subset `I = {i₋ < i_m < ⋯ < i₁ < i₊} ⊆ [n]` (m ≥ 0), an element `f_I ∈ Map_C(X_{i₋}, X_{i₊})_m` satisfying `d f_I = Σ_{1≤j≤m} (−1)^j (f_{I∖{i_j}} − f_{{i_j < ⋯ < i₊}} ∘ f_{{i₋ < ⋯ < i_j}})`; a monotone `α : [m] ⟶ [n]` acts by `f_{α(J)}` when α is injective on J, by identities on two-element J collapsed by α, and by 0 otherwise. On Tau Ceti main as `TauCeti.dgNerve R C : SSet`, with `CategoryTheory.EnrichedFunctor.mapDGNerve` for dg functors; the target is that its simplices (`Coherences`, `Simplex`) are HA's under the regrading.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.1; Tau Ceti `TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/DGNerve/Basic.lean`.

**Low-dimensional simplices** (HA Example 1.3.1.8, PDF p. 82). Vertices of `N_dg(C)` are objects; edges are degree-0 cycles; a 2-simplex is a triangle of degree-0 cycles f, g, h with `z ∈ Map_C(X, Z)₁` and `dz = g ∘ f − h`. Tau Ceti main: `dgNerveEquiv` (vertices) and the edge and 2-simplex descriptions in `DGNerve/HomotopyCategory.lean`.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.6.

**The nerve of the underlying category** (HA Remark 1.3.1.9, PDF p. 82). `N(C₀) ⊆ N_dg(C)` is the simplicial subset of simplices with `f_I = 0` for `|I| > 2`; it is bijective on simplices of dimension ≤ 1. Tau Ceti main: `TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/DGNerve/Nerve.lean` (`composableArrowsEquiv`, under a vanishing hypothesis in degree −1); the target is the inclusion in general.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.4, 1.3.1.6.

**The dg nerve is an ∞-category** (HA Proposition 1.3.1.10, PDF p. 82). Inner horns in `N_dg(C)` have fillers (with `f_{[n]} = 0` and `f_{[n]∖{j}}` given by an explicit formula). Tau Ceti main: `TauCeti.dgNerve.quasicategory`, from `TauCeti.DGNerve.Coherences.exists_simplex_of_horn`.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.6.

**Its homotopy category** (HA Remark 1.3.1.11, PDF p. 83). `h N_dg(C) ≅ hC`. Tau Ceti main: `TauCeti.dgNerve.homotopyCategoryEquiv : DGHomotopyCategory R C ≌ (dgNerve R C).HomotopyCategory`, onto Mathlib's `SSet.HomotopyCategory`, the category underlying `SSet.hoFunctor.obj (dgNerve R C)`; the target is supplied.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.5, 1.3.1.8, 1.3.1.9; L1.2 (comparison of the two homotopy categories).

**Mapping spaces of the dg nerve** (HA Remark 1.3.1.12, PDF p. 83). For objects X, Y, n-simplices of `Hom^R_{N_dg(C)}(X, Y)` are chain maps `N_*(ℤΔ[n]) ⟶ Map_C(X, Y)`, naturally, so `Hom^R_{N_dg(C)}(X, Y) ≅ DK(τ_{≥0} Map_C(X, Y))`. Tau Ceti main: `TauCeti.dgNerve.rightMappingSpaceIso` and `TauCeti.dgNerve.rightMappingSpaceIsoCochainToSSet`.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.6, 1.2.3.5, 1.2.3.12; `SSet.rightMappingSpace` (Tau Ceti).

**The underlying simplicial category** (HA Construction 1.3.1.13 and Remark 1.3.1.14, PDF pp. 83–84). The composite `Ch(Ab) ⟶ Ch(Ab)_{≥0} ⟶ Fun(Δ^op, Ab) ⟶ SSet` of `τ_{≥0}`, DK and the forgetful functor is lax monoidal (1.2.3.26), so a dg category C gives a simplicial category `C_Δ` with `Map_{C_Δ}(X, Y)` the simplicial set underlying `DK(τ_{≥0} Map_C(X, Y))`; its mapping spaces are Kan complexes, so `C_Δ` is locally Kan (1.3.1.14). Tau Ceti main: `TauCeti.DGSimplicialCategory R C` with its `EnrichedCategory SSet` instance and the Kan instance on mapping objects; Lurie's composition order is implemented there through opposites.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.1, 1.2.3.23, 1.2.3.26, 1.2.3.14; Tau Ceti `TauCeti/CategoryTheory/DG/Simplicial.lean`.

**Simplices of `C[Δ[n]]` from permutations** (HA Notation 1.3.1.15, PDF p. 84). For `I = {i₋ < i_m < ⋯ < i₁ < i₊} ⊆ [n]` and a permutation σ of `{1, …, m}`, `τ_{I,σ}` is the m-simplex of `Map_{C[Δ[n]]}(i₋, i₊) = N(P_{i₋,i₊})` given by the chain of subsets adding `i_{σ(1)}, i_{σ(2)}, …` in turn.

*Lean:* `SimplicialThickening` simplices (Mathlib, `C[Δ^J]`); propose `SimplicialThickening.permChain I σ`.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.SimplicialThickening`; 1.1.5.1 (L1.4).

**The comparison map** (HA Construction 1.3.1.16, PDF p. 84). A simplicial functor `α : C[Δ[n]] ⟶ C_Δ` gives the n-simplex `({α(i)}, {f_I})` of `N_dg(C)` with `f_I = Σ_σ (−1)^σ [α(τ_{I,σ})]`; this is natural in `[n]` and defines `θ : N(C_Δ) ⟶ N_dg(C)`, bijective on simplices of dimension ≤ 2.

*Lean:* `TauCeti.dgNerve.fromSimplicialNerve : SimplicialNerve (ForgetEnrichment SSet (DGSimplicialCategory R C)) ⟶ dgNerve R C` (propose; Tau Ceti's `DGSimplicialCategory` carries only `EnrichedCategory SSet`, and `ForgetEnrichment` gives it the `SimplicialCategory` structure Mathlib's `SimplicialNerve` asks for), with the sign conventions fixed by Tau Ceti's composition order.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.13, 1.3.1.15; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve`.

**The comparison is an equivalence** (HA Proposition 1.3.1.17, PDF p. 85). `θ : N(C_Δ) ⟶ N_dg(C)` is a categorical equivalence.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: θ is bijective on vertices, so it suffices that it is fully faithful; on right mapping spaces it is `Sing_{Q•} DK(τ_{≥0} Map_C(X, Y)) ⟵ DK(τ_{≥0} Map_C(X, Y))` up to isomorphism (HTT 2.2.2.13 and 1.3.1.12), a homotopy equivalence because the target is Kan (HTT 2.2.2.7, 2.2.2.9).

*Needs:* 1.3.1.12, 1.3.1.16; 2.2.2.7, 2.2.2.9, 2.2.2.13 (L2.8); `SSet.IsFullyFaithful` characterization through `Hom^R` (L2).

**Differential graded functors** (HA Definition 1.3.1.18, PDF p. 85). A dg functor is a map on objects with chain maps `Map_C(X, Y) ⟶ Map_D(FX, FY)` preserving identities and composition; dg categories over k and dg functors form `Cat_dg^k`. Lurie says "over a field k" here; the model structure of 1.3.1.19 is stated over any commutative ring, and the definition does not use that k is a field.

*Lean:* `CategoryTheory.EnrichedFunctor (CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) C D` for dg categories C, D over a commutative ring R; Tau Ceti's `CategoryTheory.EnrichedFunctor.ofDGMap` builds one from HA's data. `Cat_dg^R` is the category of these (propose). HA's "over a field" is not used.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.1.

**The model structure on dg categories** (HA Proposition 1.3.1.19, PDF p. 86). For k commutative, `Cat_dg^k` has a combinatorial model structure whose weak equivalences are the dg functors inducing an equivalence of homotopy categories and quasi-isomorphisms of mapping complexes, and whose fibrations are the dg functors that are isofibrations on homotopy categories and degreewise surjective on mapping complexes. Lurie cites Tabuada; supplied by DGAInfinity (Scope). Over a field Lurie also derives it from HTT A.3.2.4 and A.3.2.24 (F3.4). The weak equivalences are Tau Ceti's `CategoryTheory.EnrichedFunctor.IsQuasiEquivalence`.

*Needs:* DGAInfinity (Tabuada's model structure); 1.3.1.18; A.3.2.4, A.3.2.24 (F3.4) for the field case; A.2.6.1 (F1.6).

**The dg nerve is right Quillen** (HA Proposition 1.3.1.20, PDF pp. 86–87). `C ↦ N_dg(C)` is a right Quillen functor from `Cat_dg^k` with Tabuada's model structure to `SSet` with the Joyal model structure.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `N_dg` preserves small limits and filtered colimits, hence has a left adjoint (HTT 5.5.2.9 applied to the presentable categories involved); it preserves weak equivalences (1.3.1.11, 1.3.1.12) and fibrations (`N_dg(F)` is an inner fibration by explicit horn filling, using that F is degreewise surjective on mapping complexes; then 2.4.6.5 with the lifting of equivalences in `hC ⟶ hD`).

*Needs:* 1.3.1.19, 1.3.1.11, 1.3.1.12; 5.5.2.9 (L7); 2.4.6.5, 2.2.5.1 (L3); `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions` (F1.5); Tau Ceti `CategoryTheory.EnrichedFunctor.mapDGNerve`.

**The dg category of chain complexes** (HA Definition 1.3.2.1, PDF p. 88). For an additive category A and chain complexes M, N, `Map_{Ch(A)}(M, N)_p = ∏_n Hom_A(M_n, N_{n+p})` with `(df)(x) = d(f(x)) − (−1)^p f(dx)`; with composition, `Ch(A)` is a dg category. Tau Ceti main has the cochain form for cochain complexes, the instance `TauCeti.linearHomComplexEnrichedCategory` (`TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/LinearHomComplex/Enrichment.lean`, built on Mathlib's `CochainComplex.linearHomComplex`); the target is that dg category on `Ch(A) = CochainComplex A ℤ` (1.2.3.1), with HA's sign read through the Conventions' reindexing.

*Lean:* the dg structure on `Ch(A) = CochainComplex A ℤ` is Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.linearHomComplexEnrichedCategory` (over ℤ, built on Mathlib's `CochainComplex.HomComplex`). The target identifies its degree-p group and differential with HA's, under chain degree m ↦ cochain degree −m, including the sign `d f = d ∘ f − (−1)^p f ∘ d`.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.1, 1.3.1.1; Mathlib `CochainComplex.HomComplex`.

**Projective objects** (HA Definition 1.3.2.4, PDF p. 88). P is projective when `Hom(P, −)` carries epimorphisms to surjections; A has enough projectives when every object receives an epimorphism from a projective. Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Projective` and `CategoryTheory.EnoughProjectives`; no new definition.

*Lean:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Projective P` and `CategoryTheory.EnoughProjectives A`; no new definition.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Projective`.

**`D⁻(A)`** (propose `TauCeti.derivedCategoryInftyMinus A`; HA Definition 1.3.2.7, PDF p. 89). For A abelian with enough projectives, `D⁻(A) = N_dg(Ch⁻(A_proj))`: the dg nerve of the full dg subcategory of `Ch(A)` on the complexes of projective objects with `M_n = 0` for `n ≪ 0` (Notation 1.3.2.6). Its homotopy category is the classical bounded-above derived category (Remark 1.3.2.9, not a target).

*Lean:* `TauCeti.dgNerve R (TauCeti.DGFullSubcategory P)` for the predicate P "degreewise projective and bounded below in homological degree", in cochain degrees `∃ N, ∀ k > N, Limits.IsZero (M.X k)`, on `Ch(A)` (`CochainComplex A ℤ`, 1.2.3.1) (Tau Ceti `TauCeti/CategoryTheory/DG/FullSubcategory.lean`), with `R = ℤ`, for `A : Type u` with `[Category.{0} A]` (`TauCeti.linearHomComplexEnrichedCategory` needs `R : Type v` for `[Category.{v} A]`; larger Hom universes need `ULift ℤ` or a universe-polymorphic enrichment).

**Checks.**

- For `A = ModuleCat ℤ`, with ℤ in degree 0 and `ℤ[n]` the complex ℤ in degree n, `Hom_{h D⁻(A)}(ℤ, ℤ[n])` is ℤ for `n = 0` and 0 otherwise.
- `h D⁻(A)` is equivalent to Mathlib's `DerivedCategory.Minus A` (the full subcategory of `DerivedCategory A` on cohomologically bounded-above objects, which is homologically `H_n = 0` for `n ≪ 0`, HA's bound). This comparison is a proposed target for downstream users.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.6, 1.3.2.1, 1.3.2.4.

**`D⁺(A)`** (HA Variant 1.3.2.8, PDF p. 89). For A with enough injectives, `D⁺(A) = N_dg(Ch⁺(A_inj))`, and `D⁺(A)^op ≃ D⁻(A^op)`.

*Needs:* 1.3.2.7; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Injective`, `EnoughInjectives`.

**`N_dg(Ch(A))` is stable** (HA Proposition 1.3.2.10, PDF pp. 89, 91). For any additive category A, `N_dg(Ch(A))` is stable.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: pushouts exist because `Ch(A)_Δ` has homotopy pushouts (1.3.2.16, after replacing a map by a degreewise split one through the mapping cylinder), transported along 1.3.1.17 and HTT 4.2.4.1; the zero complex is a zero object; the suspension is the shift `M ↦ M_{∗−1}` (HA's `M[1]`, Mathlib's `⟦1⟧` on `CochainComplex A ℤ`; through the pushout `M ⟶ E(1) ⊗ M`, `0 ⟶ M_{∗−1}`), an equivalence; conclude by 1.4.2.27 (L9.6: a pointed ∞-category with finite colimits and invertible suspension is stable). Lurie's text calls 1.4.2.27 a Proposition; it is a Corollary.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.17, 1.3.2.16; 4.2.4.1 (L5.7); `HTT.A.2.4.3/after` (F1.5, homotopy pushouts); 1.4.2.27 (L9.6, forward).

**Kan fibrations of simplicial abelian groups** (HA Proposition 1.3.2.11, PDF pp. 89–90). A map of simplicial abelian groups is a Kan fibration exactly when `N_n(A) ⟶ N_n(B)` is surjective for `n > 0`.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.9; `HTT.A.2.7/kan-fibrations`; Mathlib `SSet.KanComplex` (fibrations of `SSet.modelCategoryQuillen`).

**Simplicial abelian groups are Kan** (HA Corollary 1.3.2.12, PDF p. 90). Tau Ceti main: `SSet.kanComplex_of_addGroup`, `kanComplex_comp_forget_addCommGrpCat`.

*Needs:* 1.3.2.11 (or Tau Ceti's direct proof).

**The simplicial category of chain complexes** (HA Notation 1.3.2.13, PDF p. 90). `Ch(A)_Δ` is the underlying simplicial category (1.3.1.13) of the dg category `Ch(A)`: `TauCeti.DGSimplicialCategory ℤ (Ch(A))`.

*Lean:* `TauCeti.DGSimplicialCategory ℤ (Ch(A))` for the dg category of 1.3.2.1; no new definition.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.13, 1.3.2.1.

**Kan fibrations of mapping spaces** (HA Corollary 1.3.2.14, PDF p. 90). For `f : M ⟶ M'` and Q in `Ch(A)` such that every `Hom(M'_p, Q_q) ⟶ Hom(M_p, Q_q)`, `p < q`, is surjective, `Map_{Ch(A)_Δ}(M', Q) ⟶ Map_{Ch(A)_Δ}(M, Q)` is a Kan fibration.

*Needs:* 1.3.2.11, 1.3.2.13.

**When the hypotheses hold** (HA Remark 1.3.2.15, PDF p. 90). The hypotheses of 1.3.2.14 hold when f is degreewise split, or when A is abelian, f is degreewise a monomorphism and every `Q_q` is injective.

*Needs:* 1.3.2.14.

**Degreewise split pushouts are homotopy pushouts** (HA Corollary 1.3.2.16, PDF pp. 90–91). A pushout square in `Ch(A)` along a degreewise split f is a homotopy pushout in `Ch(A)_Δ`.

*Proof route.* For each Q the square of mapping spaces is a pullback along a Kan fibration (1.3.2.14), hence a homotopy pullback (right properness of Kan–Quillen).

*Needs:* 1.3.2.14, 1.3.2.15; `HTT.A.2.7/model-structure`, `HTT.A.2.7/kan-fibrations` (F2); A.2.4.1, `HTT.A.2.4.3/after` (F1.5, proper model categories and homotopy pushouts).

**Mapping cones are cofibres** (HA Remark 1.3.2.17, PDF p. 91). For A additive and `f : M ⟶ M'` in `Ch(A)`, the mapping cone `C(f)`, with `C(f)_n = M'_n ⊕ M_{n−1}`, is the pushout of f along `M ⟶ E(1) ⊗ M`, where `E(1)` is ℤ in degrees 1 and 0 with the identity as differential (HA, proof of 1.3.2.11); this square exhibits `C(f)` as a cofibre of f in `N_dg(Ch(A))`.

*Proof route.* `M ⟶ E(1) ⊗ M` is degreewise split, so the square is a homotopy pushout in `Ch(A)_Δ` (1.3.2.16), hence a pushout in `N(Ch(A)_Δ)` (HTT 4.2.4.1) and, through θ, in `N_dg(Ch(A))` (1.3.1.17); `E(1) ⊗ M` is chain-contractible, so a zero object.

*Needs:* 1.3.2.16, 1.3.1.17; 1.1.1.6; 4.2.4.1 (L5.7).

**`D⁻(A)` is stable** (HA Corollary 1.3.2.18, PDF p. 92). For A abelian with enough projectives, `D⁻(A)` is stable: `Ch⁻(A_proj)` is closed under shifts and mapping cones, so its dg nerve is a stable subcategory of `N_dg(Ch(A))`.

*Needs:* 1.3.2.7, 1.3.2.10; 1.1.3.2, 1.1.3.3; 1.3.2.17 (mapping cones are cofibres).

**The t-structure on `D⁻(A)`** (HA Proposition 1.3.2.19, PDF pp. 92–94). For A abelian with enough projectives, the full subcategories of `D⁻(A)` on complexes with `H_n = 0` for `n < 0`, resp. `n > 0`, form a t-structure, whose heart is equivalent to `N(A)` through `H₀`.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HA.1.3.2.19/resolution` (projective approximation of a complex) and `HA.1.3.2.19/heart` (the heart is A), and this entry's own target `HA.1.3.2.19`, which proves the t-structure axioms and combines them.

**Checks.**

- A projective P in degree 0 lies in the heart and goes to P.
- `π_n M ≅ H_n(M)` in A for every `M ∈ D⁻(A)`, under the heart identification.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. The shift conditions are immediate. Orthogonality: reduce to nonnegatively graded projective sources with `HA.1.3.2.19/resolution`, then use 1.3.2.21. Truncation triangles: the cofibre of the map of `HA.1.3.2.19/resolution` is computed by the mapping cone of 1.3.2.10. The heart is `HA.1.3.2.19/heart`.

*Needs:* `HA.1.3.2.19/resolution`, `HA.1.3.2.19/heart` (below); 1.3.2.10, 1.3.2.18, 1.3.2.21; 1.2.1.1, 1.2.1.4, 1.2.1.11.

**Projective approximation of a complex** (`HA.1.3.2.19/resolution`, part 1 of 2 of the t-structure on `D⁻(A)` above; HA Proposition 1.3.2.19, construction (∗) in the proof, PDF p. 93). Let A be abelian with enough projectives. Every complex `A_*` receives a chain map `f : P_* ⟶ A_*` from a complex of projectives with `P_n = 0` for `n < 0` that induces isomorphisms on `H_k` for `k ≥ 0`. If `A_*` lies in `D⁻(A)` and `H_n(A_*) = 0` for `n < 0`, then f is a chain homotopy equivalence.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: induction on n. At each step, choose a projective object mapping onto the fibre product of `A_n` with the cycles of `P_{n−1}` over the cycles of `A_{n−1}`. The final claim holds because a quasi-isomorphism between bounded-below complexes of projectives is a chain homotopy equivalence (1.3.2.20).

*Needs:* 1.3.2.20; Mathlib `EnoughProjectives`, `HomologicalComplex.homology`.

**The heart of `D⁻(A)` is A** (`HA.1.3.2.19/heart`, part 2 of 2 of the t-structure on `D⁻(A)` above; HA Proposition 1.3.2.19, last paragraph of the proof, PDF pp. 93–94). Let A be abelian with enough projectives. `H₀` induces a functor `θ : N_dg(Ch(A)) ⟶ N(A)`, which restricts to an equivalence `D⁻(A)^♥ ⟶ N(A)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. By `HA.1.3.2.19/resolution`, the heart is equivalent to the full subcategory of nonnegatively graded complexes of projectives with homology concentrated in degree 0. θ is fully faithful there by 1.3.2.21, and essentially surjective by `HA.1.3.2.19/resolution` applied to complexes concentrated in degree 0.

*Needs:* `HA.1.3.2.19/resolution`; 1.3.2.21; 1.2.1.11 (L9.2); `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`, `HTT.1.2.10/essentially-surjective` (L1.5).

**Bounded projective complexes preserve quasi-isomorphisms** (HA Lemma 1.3.2.20, PDF p. 92). For A abelian, P a complex of projectives with `P_n = 0` for `n ≪ 0`, and `Q ⟶ Q'` a quasi-isomorphism, `Map_{Ch(A)}(P, Q) ⟶ Map_{Ch(A)}(P, Q')` is a quasi-isomorphism.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: P is the homotopy colimit of its naive truncations; reduce to P concentrated in one degree, where `H_i Map(P, Q) = Hom(P, H_i Q)`. The homotopy colimit step is a limit of a tower of chain complexes of mapping complexes (Milnor sequence with surjective transition maps); state it in that form.

*Needs:* 1.3.2.1, 1.3.2.4; `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3, homotopy limits of towers).

**Discrete mapping spaces into the heart** (HA Lemma 1.3.2.21, PDF pp. 92–93). For A abelian, P a complex of projectives vanishing in negative degrees and Q with `H_n(Q) = 0` for `n > 0`, `Map_{N_dg(Ch(A))}(P, Q)` is discrete and `Ext⁰(P, Q) ≅ Hom_A(H₀P, H₀Q)`.

*Needs:* 1.3.2.20, 1.3.1.12.

**`D⁻_{≥0}(A)` through simplicial objects** (HA Proposition 1.3.2.22, PDF pp. 94, 97). For A abelian with enough projectives, `D⁻_{≥0}(A)` is equivalent to the underlying ∞-category (the simplicial nerve) of the simplicial category `Fun(Δ^op, A_proj)`, whose mapping spaces are defined by `Hom_{SSet}(K, Map(P, P')) = Hom(ℤK ⊗ P, P')` for finite K.

*Proof route.* The zigzag `D⁻_{≥0}(A) ⟵ N_dg(Ch(A_proj)_{≥0}) ⟵ N(Ch(A_proj)_{≥0, Δ}) ⟶ N(Fun(Δ^op, A_proj))` of equivalences, by `HA.1.3.2.19/resolution`, 1.3.1.17 and 1.3.2.23.

*Needs:* `HA.1.3.2.19/resolution`, 1.3.2.23, 1.3.1.17; 1.2.3.7; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve`.

**Dold–Kan as a simplicial functor** (HA Proposition 1.3.2.23, PDF pp. 94–96). For A idempotent complete additive, `DK : Ch(A)_{≥0} ⟶ Fun(Δ^op, A)`, made a simplicial functor through Alexander–Whitney maps (1.2.3.22, 1.2.3.25), is a weak equivalence (Dwyer–Kan equivalence) of simplicial categories.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HA.1.3.2.23/cells` (good cells for Dold–Kan) and `HA.1.3.2.23/goodness` (every nonnegative complex is good), and this entry's own target `HA.1.3.2.23`, which adds essential surjectivity (1.2.3.7) to conclude.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: essential surjectivity by 1.2.3.7; on mapping spaces, show the class of good complexes contains `A[0]`, `E(n) ⊗ A[0]` (`HA.1.3.2.23/cells`), is closed under the cell attachments `A[n−1] ⟶ E(n) ⊗ A`, hence contains every bounded complex and, through the tower of truncations, every nonnegative complex (`HA.1.3.2.23/goodness`).

*Needs:* `HA.1.3.2.23/cells`, `HA.1.3.2.23/goodness` (below); 1.2.3.7, 1.2.3.22, 1.2.3.25; `CategoryTheory.EnrichedFunctor.IsDwyerKanEquivalence` (Tau Ceti main) (L1.5).

**Good cells for Dold–Kan** (`HA.1.3.2.23/cells`, part 1 of 2 of Dold–Kan as a simplicial functor above; HA Proposition 1.3.2.23, steps (1)–(3) of the proof, PDF p. 95). Fix Q ∈ `Ch(A)_{≥0}`, with A idempotent complete additive, and call P good when `θ_P : Map(P, Q) ⟶ Map(DK P, DK Q)` is a weak homotopy equivalence. For an object A of A: `A[0]` is good, `θ_{A[0]}` being an isomorphism (Alexander–Whitney); `E(n) ⊗ A[0]` is good, both mapping spaces being contractible; and for `n ≥ 1`, restriction along `A[n − 1] ⟶ E(n) ⊗ A` is a Kan fibration on the Dold–Kan side, a pullback of `Fun(Δ[n], X) ⟶ Fun(∂Δ[n], X)`.

*Needs:* 1.2.3.22, 1.2.3.25, 1.3.2.11, 1.3.1.13.

**Every nonnegative complex is good** (`HA.1.3.2.23/goodness`, part 2 of 2 of Dold–Kan as a simplicial functor above; HA Proposition 1.3.2.23, steps (4)–(6) of the proof, PDF p. 96). Good complexes are closed under pushouts along `A[n − 1] ⟶ E(n) ⊗ A[0]`. Hence every `A[n]`, every bounded complex (through its brutal truncations) and every complex in `Ch(A)_{≥0}` (as the limit of the tower) is good.

*Needs:* `HA.1.3.2.23/cells`; 1.3.2.16; `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences` (F2); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3, towers).

**t-exact functors** (`SSet.TStructure.IsRightTExact`, `IsLeftTExact`; HA Definition 1.3.3.1, PDF p. 97). For stable C, C' with t-structures, an exact functor `f : C ⟶ C'` is right t-exact when it carries `C_{≥0}` into `C'_{≥0}`, left t-exact when it carries `C_{≤0}` into `C'_{≤0}`, and t-exact when both.

*Lean:* predicates on `F : C ⟶ C'` with `SSet.IsExact F` as a conjunct. Under the layer's indexing dictionary they are Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Functor.RightTExact F t₁ t₂` and `Functor.LeftTExact F t₁ t₂` (`TStructure/TExact.lean`; they need `[F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]`) of the induced triangulated functor on homotopy categories (Mathlib's right t-exactness preserves `le`, which is HA's `≥`); state that comparison as a lemma.

*Needs:* `HA.1.1.4/intro`, 1.2.1.4.

**The universal property of `D⁻(A)`** (HA Theorem 1.3.3.2, PDF p. 97). For A abelian with enough projectives and C stable with a left complete t-structure, let `E ⊆ Fun(D⁻(A), C)` be spanned by the right t-exact functors carrying projectives of A into the heart. Then `F ↦ τ_{≤0} ∘ F|_{D⁻(A)^♥}` is an equivalence from E to the nerve of the category of right exact functors `A ⟶ C^♥`.

**Checks.**

- For `C = D⁻(B)` with B abelian with enough projectives, a right exact `f : A ⟶ B` extends to its left derived functor `D⁻(A) ⟶ D⁻(B)` (Example 1.3.3.4).
- The identity of A corresponds to the identity functor of `D⁻(A)` (which is in E, as `D⁻(A)` is left complete by 1.3.3.16).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: 1.3.3.12 (restriction to `N(A_proj)`) and 1.3.3.9 (right exact functors are determined on projectives).

*Needs:* 1.3.3.1, 1.3.3.9, 1.3.3.12; 1.3.2.19; `HA.1.2.1.17/after`; Mathlib `Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits`.

**Exactness of the restriction** (HA Remark 1.3.3.6, PDF pp. 98–99). In the setting of 1.3.3.2, for F in E with underlying right exact `f : A ⟶ C^♥`, the following are equivalent: F is left t-exact; F carries `N(A)` into the heart; f is exact.

*Needs:* 1.3.3.2, 1.3.2.19, 1.2.1.11; `HA.1.2.1.17/after`.

**A recognition criterion for `D⁻`** (HA Proposition 1.3.3.7, PDF pp. 99–101). Let C be stable with a left complete t-structure whose heart `A = h(C^♥)` has enough projectives. There is an essentially unique t-exact `F : D⁻(A) ⟶ C` extending the inclusion of the heart, and the following are equivalent: F is fully faithful; `Extⁱ_C(X, Y) = 0` for `i > 0`, X projective, Y in A; for X projective and Y in A, some monomorphism `Y ⟶ Z` in A has `Extⁱ_C(X, Z) = 0` for `i > 0`. Then the essential image of F is the right-bounded part `⋃ₙ C_{≥−n}`.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HA.1.3.3.7/extension` (the comparison functor and the Ext criterion), `HA.1.3.3.7/fully-faithful` (full faithfulness of the comparison) and `HA.1.3.3.7/essential-image` (the essential image is the right-bounded part), and this entry's own target `HA.1.3.3.7`, which combines them into the equivalence of the three conditions and the description of the essential image.

*Needs:* `HA.1.3.3.7/extension`, `HA.1.3.3.7/fully-faithful`, `HA.1.3.3.7/essential-image` (below); `SSet.IsFullyFaithful`, `SSet.IsEssentiallySurjective` (L1.5).

**The comparison functor and the Ext criterion** (`HA.1.3.3.7/extension`, part 1 of 3 of the recognition criterion for `D⁻` above; HA Proposition 1.3.3.7, existence of F and (i) ⇒ (ii) ⇔ (iii), PDF pp. 99–100). Let C be stable with a left complete t-structure whose heart A has enough projectives. There is an essentially unique t-exact `F : D⁻(A) ⟶ C` extending `N(A) ≃ C^♥`. If F is fully faithful, then `Extⁱ_C(P, Y) = 0` for `i > 0`, P projective and Y ∈ A. This vanishing is equivalent to: every Y ∈ A embeds in some Z ∈ A with `Extⁱ_C(P, Z) = 0` for `i > 0`.

*Proof route.* Existence and uniqueness from 1.3.3.2 and 1.3.3.6. (iii) ⇒ (ii) by induction on i through the Ext sequence of `0 ⟶ Y ⟶ Z ⟶ Z/Y ⟶ 0`, using projectivity of P at `i = 1`.

*Needs:* 1.3.3.2, 1.3.3.6.

**Full faithfulness of the comparison** (`HA.1.3.3.7/fully-faithful`, part 2 of 3 of the recognition criterion for `D⁻` above; HA Proposition 1.3.3.7, (ii) ⇒ (i), PDF pp. 100–101). If `Extⁱ_C(P, Y) = 0` for `i > 0`, P projective and Y in the heart, then F is fully faithful.

*Proof route.* Lurie's dévissage. Both sides are left complete (1.3.3.16), so the mapping spaces are limits over truncations of Y; this reduces to bounded Y and then, by translations and extensions, to Y in the heart. Truncating a projective resolution of X changes nothing in the relevant degrees, which reduces to finite complexes of projectives and then to a single projective, where the hypothesis applies.

*Needs:* `HA.1.3.3.7/extension`; 1.3.3.16, 1.2.1.17; 5.5.6.23 (L7); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3, towers).

**The essential image is the right-bounded part** (`HA.1.3.3.7/essential-image`, part 3 of 3 of the recognition criterion for `D⁻` above; HA Proposition 1.3.3.7, last assertion, PDF pp. 99, 101). If F is fully faithful, its essential image is `⋃_n C_{≥−n}`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Restrict to right-bounded C and write F as the limit of the `F_n : D⁻(A)_{≤n} ⟶ C_{≤n}`. Each `F_n` is essentially surjective, by descending induction on the connectivity: an object is realized as the fibre of a map `A[m] ⟶ X[1]` lifted by full faithfulness.

*Needs:* `HA.1.3.3.7/fully-faithful`; 1.2.1.17, `HA.1.2.1.12/mathlib-ker-coker`; 5.5.6.23 (L7); `SSet.IsEssentiallySurjective` (L1.5).

**Functors out of `D⁻_{≥0}(A)`** (HA Theorem 1.3.3.8, PDF pp. 101, 107). For A abelian with enough projectives and C an ∞-category with geometric realizations of simplicial objects, restriction from the functors `D⁻_{≥0}(A) ⟶ C` preserving geometric realizations to `Fun(N(A_proj), C)` is an equivalence; such a functor preserves finite coproducts exactly when its restriction does.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: identify `D⁻_{≥0}(A)` inside `P_Σ(N(A_proj))` as the closure of the representables under geometric realizations (1.3.3.17), then HTT 5.3.5.9 and 4.3.2.15 for (1); for (2) extend to `P_Σ` (1.3.3.14, HTT 5.3.5.7, 5.5.8.15).

*Needs:* 1.3.3.14, 1.3.3.17; 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); 5.3.5.7, 5.3.5.9 (L6); 5.5.8.15 (L7); 6.1.2.12 (L6, geometric realizations).

**Right exact functors are determined on projectives** (HA Lemma 1.3.3.9, PDF p. 102). For A abelian with enough projectives and B a category with finite colimits, restriction from right exact functors `A ⟶ B` to finite-coproduct-preserving functors `A_proj ⟶ B` is an equivalence of categories.

*Lean:* in Mathlib's language (`Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits`, `Limits.PreservesFiniteCoproducts`, the full subcategory of projective objects). The inverse sends A, with a projective presentation `P₁ ⟶ P₀ ⟶ A`, to the coequalizer of `f(u)` and the zero map `f(0)` from `f(P₁)` to `f(P₀)`; B has a zero map there because f preserves the empty coproduct, so `f(0)` factors through an initial object.

*Needs:* 1.3.2.4.

**Finite colimits from coproducts and geometric realizations** (HA Lemma 1.3.3.10, PDF pp. 102–103). An ∞-category with finite coproducts and geometric realizations has finite colimits; conversely an n-category with finite colimits has geometric realizations. A functor between ∞-categories with these colimits that preserves finite coproducts and geometric realizations is right exact, with the converse for n-categories.

*Proof route.* Lurie's for the first part (coequalizers as geometric realizations of a left Kan extension along `N(Δ_{s,≤1})^op ⊆ N(Δ)^op`, HTT 4.4.3.2). For the converse Lurie works in `Ind(C) ⊆ P(C)` and uses n-connective morphisms of `P(C)` and HTT 6.5.3.10, which sit in L11. Replace them by the F2 target `HTT.A.2.7/realization-connectivity` applied objectwise in `P(C) = Fun(C^op, S)`: the map from the realization of the left Kan extension of `U|N(Δ_{≤n})^op` to `|U|` is an equivalence in degrees `≤ n`, hence n-connective objectwise, hence inverted by `τ_{≤n−1}` (HTT 5.5.6, L7).

*Needs:* 4.4.3.2 (L5.10); 5.5.1.1 (L7); 5.1.3.1, 5.3.5.14 (L6); 5.5.6.18 (L7); `HTT.A.2.7/realization-connectivity/connective` (F2.5); 4.3.2.2 (L5.9); 6.1.2.12 (L6).

**Right t-exact functors through connective parts** (HA Lemma 1.3.3.11, PDF pp. 103–104). For stable C, C' with t-structures: if C is right bounded, restriction is an equivalence from right t-exact functors `C ⟶ C'` to right exact functors `C_{≥0} ⟶ C'_{≥0}`; if C and C' are left complete, `C_{≥0}` and `C'_{≥0}` have geometric realizations, and a functor `C_{≥0} ⟶ C'_{≥0}` is right exact exactly when it preserves finite coproducts and geometric realizations.

*Needs:* 1.3.3.1, 1.3.3.10; `HA.1.2.1.16/after`, `HA.1.2.1.17/after`; 3.3.3.1 (L5.1, limits of ∞-categories); 6.1.2.12 (L6).

**Right t-exact functors out of `D⁻(A)`** (HA Proposition 1.3.3.12, PDF p. 105). For A abelian with enough projectives and C stable with a left complete t-structure, restriction induces an equivalence from right t-exact functors `D⁻(A) ⟶ C` to finite-coproduct-preserving functors `N(A_proj) ⟶ C_{≥0}`.

*Needs:* 1.3.3.8, 1.3.3.11, 1.3.3.16.

**Ind-objects of an abelian category with enough projectives** (HA Proposition 1.3.3.13, PDF pp. 105–106). For A small abelian with enough projectives, the category `A^∧` of product-preserving functors `A_proj^op ⟶ Set` is the category of Ind-objects of A; it is abelian with enough projectives.

*Lean:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Ind`; the equivalence with `A^∧` through 1.3.3.9 (with `B = Setᵒᵖ`); abelianness of `Ind A` is Mathlib's instance `Abelian (Ind C)` (`CategoryTheory/Abelian/Indization.lean`); enough projectives is the target.

*Needs:* 1.3.3.9; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.Indization`.

**`D⁻_{≥0}(A^∧)` is `P_Σ` of the projectives** (HA Proposition 1.3.3.14, PDF p. 106). For A abelian with enough projectives there is an equivalence `ψ : D⁻_{≥0}(A^∧) ⟶ P_Σ(N(A_proj))` whose composite with `N(A_proj) ⊆ D⁻(A^∧)^♥` is the Yoneda embedding.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `A^∧`'s simplicial objects carry Quillen's simplicial model structure (HTT 5.5.9.1), all objects fibrant (1.3.2.12), cofibrant objects the degreewise projective ones; 1.3.2.22 gives `D⁻_{≥0}(A^∧) ≃ N(A°)` and HTT 5.5.9.3 identifies this with `P_Σ`.

*Needs:* 1.3.2.12, 1.3.2.22, 1.3.3.13; 5.5.9.1, 5.5.9.3, 5.5.8.8 (L7).

**`D⁻(A)` inside `D⁻(A^∧)`** (HA Remark 1.3.3.15, PDF p. 106). `D⁻(A)` is a full subcategory of `D⁻(A^∧)`, consisting of the objects whose homology objects all lie in A.

*Needs:* 1.3.2.7, 1.3.3.13; 1.3.2.19.

**`D⁻(A)` is left complete** (HA Proposition 1.3.3.16, PDF pp. 106–107). For A abelian with enough projectives, the t-structure on `D⁻(A)` is right bounded and left complete.

*Proof route.* Lurie's reduction to `P_Σ(N(A_proj))` being the limit of its k-truncated parts. Lurie cites HTT 6.5.1.2 (truncation commutes with finite products, L11) and HTT 7.2.1.10 (`S` is the limit of `τ_{≤k} S`, L12); both are statements about Kan complexes supplied by `HTT.A.2.7/postnikov` (F2.5: `τ_{≤n}` preserves finite products, and `X ⟶ lim τ_{≤n} X` is a weak equivalence), with the passage to `S` through HTT 5.5.6.23–5.5.6.26 (L7).

*Needs:* 1.3.3.14, 1.3.3.15; `HA.1.2.1.16/after`, `HA.1.2.1.17/after`; 5.5.6.23–5.5.6.26 (L7); `HTT.A.2.7/postnikov/limit` (F2.5, both the convergence of `X ⟶ lim τ_{≤n} X` and the truncations of a limit of a Postnikov tower).

**`D⁻_{≥0}(A)` as a closure of representables** (HA Lemma 1.3.3.17, PDF p. 107). For A small abelian with enough projectives, the image of `D⁻_{≥0}(A)` under ψ (1.3.3.14) is the smallest full subcategory of `P(N(A_proj))` closed under geometric realizations and containing the representables.

*Proof route.* Closure from 1.3.3.11; every object is the realization of the simplicial object of `A_proj` given by Dold–Kan, through HTT 4.2.4.1 and 5.5.9.14.

*Needs:* 1.3.3.11, 1.3.3.14, 1.3.3.15, 1.2.3.7; 4.2.4.1 (L5.7); 5.5.9.14 (L7); 5.1.3.1 (L6).

### L9.5 Localizations and underlying ∞-categories of model categories

Lurie's proofs of 1.3.4.7 and 1.3.4.20 pass through the topological category `|C|` obtained by realizing mapping spaces, to have a fibrant replacement of a simplicial category. Topological categories are out of scope (Scope). The replacement used here is `Ex^∞` applied to every mapping space (F2.3): `Ex^∞` preserves finite products, so it gives a simplicial category `Ex^∞ C` with Kan mapping spaces and a Dwyer–Kan equivalence `C ⟶ Ex^∞ C`, which is all that either proof uses. The vertices of `Ex^∞ K` are those of K, so the underlying ordinary category of `Ex^∞ C` is `C₀` itself; this is the identification Lurie's proof of 1.3.4.7 assumes "without loss of generality" for `|C|`, where it fails (points of `|K|` are not vertices of K).

**Localization** (`SSet.IsLocalization`; HA Definition 1.3.4.1, PDF p. 108). For a simplicial set C (HA: an ∞-category, or the nerve of a category) and a set W of edges, `f : C ⟶ D` with D an ∞-category exhibits D as `C[W⁻¹]` when, for every ∞-category E, precomposition with f is a categorical equivalence from `Fun(D, E)` onto the full subcategory of `Fun(C, E)` of functors carrying every edge of W to an equivalence. This is the Conventions' definition (Kerodon 6.3.1.9); its 1-categorical shadow is Mathlib's `Functor.IsLocalization`.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsLocalization f W` for `f : C ⟶ D`, `[D.Quasicategory]` and `W : ∀ ⦃x y : C _⦋0⦌⦄, C.Edge x y → Prop` (Mathlib's `SSet.Edge` is indexed by its endpoints), the conjunction of: (1) f carries every W-edge to an `SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence`; (2) `∀ (E : SSet.{max u w}) [E.Quasicategory], SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence (precomp : (ihom (uliftFunctor.{w}.obj D)).obj E ⟶ Fun_W(uliftFunctor.{w}.obj C, E))`, with the W-edges transported through `ULift.up` (`ihom` needs a single universe). Here `Fun_W(C, E)` is the `SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory` of `Fun(C, E)` on the functors carrying every W-edge to an equivalence, and precomposition with f factors through it by (1). The universe w is stated, and a separate target shows that `w = u` (the universe of C and D) suffices.

**Checks.**

- `id : C ⟶ C` is a localization at the equivalences of an ∞-category C.
- For an ordinary category A and W, `hoFunctor` of a localization `N(A) ⟶ D` is a Mathlib localization `A ⥤ hD` at W (`Functor.IsLocalization`).
- Localizations exist (HA Remark 1.3.4.2, not a target: fibrant replacement of `(C, W)` in `Set⁺_Δ`, L4.3).

*Needs:* `SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence` (L1.5); `SSet.IsFullyFaithful` (L1.5); 3.1.0.1, 3.1.3.7 (L4.2–L4.3, for existence).

**Reflective localizations are localizations** (HA Example 1.3.4.3, PDF p. 108). If `C' ⊆ C` is a reflective localization with left adjoint L and W the morphisms inverted by L, then `C' ⊆ C ⟶ C[W⁻¹]` is an equivalence. This is HTT 5.2.7.12 (L6) in the Conventions' language.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.1; 5.2.7.12 (L6); `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`.

**`D⁻(A)` as a localization** (HA Theorem 1.3.4.4, PDF p. 109). For A abelian with enough projectives and W the quasi-isomorphisms of `Ch⁻(A)` (an ordinary category), `N(Ch⁻(A))[W⁻¹] ≃ D⁻(A)`.

**Checks.** On homotopy categories this recovers the classical description of the bounded-above derived category by inverting quasi-isomorphisms (Mathlib `DerivedCategory` is a localization `HomotopyCategory ⥤ DerivedCategory`).

*Proof route.* Compose 1.3.4.5 (chain homotopy equivalences) with 1.3.4.6 (quasi-isomorphisms).

*Needs:* 1.3.4.5, 1.3.4.6, 1.3.2.7.

**Inverting chain homotopy equivalences** (HA Proposition 1.3.4.5, PDF pp. 109, 114–115). For an additive A and a full subcategory `Ch'(A) ⊆ Ch(A)` closed under `M ↦ N_*(Δ[1]) ⊗ M`, with W the chain homotopy equivalences, the inclusion `N(Ch'(A)) ⊆ N_dg(Ch'(A))` (1.3.1.9) induces `N(Ch'(A))[W⁻¹] ≃ N_dg(Ch'(A))`.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as two targets: the part that follows this entry, `HA.1.3.4.5/constant` (the cylinder homotopy for chain complexes), and this entry's own target `HA.1.3.4.5`, which identifies `N(C)` with `N_dg(Ch'(A))` by 1.3.1.17, writes it as a homotopy colimit of `T_• Ch'(A)` by 1.3.4.14, and reduces θ′ to `HA.1.3.4.5/constant`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's modification of the proof of 1.3.4.7 (Warning 1.3.4.9): the simplicial category with `Hom_{C_n}(M, M') = Hom(N_*(Δ[n]) ⊗ M, M')`, 1.3.4.14, and the explicit chain map χ giving a homotopy `F ∘ G ≃ id` of marked simplicial sets (`HA.1.3.4.5/constant`); with 1.3.1.17.

*Needs:* `HA.1.3.4.5/constant` (below); 1.3.1.9, 1.3.1.17, 1.3.4.7, 1.3.4.11, 1.3.4.14; weak equivalences of marked simplicial sets (3.1.0.1, 3.1.3.7, L4).

**The cylinder homotopy for chain complexes** (`HA.1.3.4.5/constant`, the only part of inverting chain homotopy equivalences above; HA Proposition 1.3.4.5, central step of the proof, PDF pp. 114–115). Let A be additive and `Ch'(A) ⊆ Ch(A)` closed under `M ↦ N_*(Δ[1]) ⊗ M`. Let `C_n` have the objects of `Ch'(A)` and as morphisms the chain maps `N_*(Δ[n]) ⊗ M ⟶ M'`, and let `W_n` be the morphisms whose vertices are chain homotopy equivalences. For each n, the map `(N(C_0), W_0) ⟶ (N(C_n), W_n)` induced by `[n] ⟶ [0]` is a weak equivalence of marked simplicial sets.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Restriction G along `[0] ⊆ [n]` is a left inverse. For a homotopy between `F ∘ G` and the identity, use the chain map `χ : N_*(Δ[n]) ⊗ N_*(Δ[1]) ⟶ N_*(Δ[1]) ⊗ N_*(Δ[n])` given on generators by Lurie's formula. It defines a functor `U(M) = N_*(Δ[1]) ⊗ M` with natural transformations `F ∘ G ⟶ U ⟵ id` through chain homotopy equivalences. Check that χ is a chain map with Tau Ceti's sign and composition conventions.

*Needs:* 1.3.1.9, 1.3.4.11; 3.1.0.1, 3.1.3.7 (L4, marked simplicial sets).

**Quasi-isomorphisms and `D⁻(A)`** (HA Proposition 1.3.4.6, PDF pp. 109–110). For A abelian with enough projectives: `D⁻(A) ⊆ N_dg(Ch⁻(A))` has a right adjoint G; `G(α)` is an equivalence exactly when α is a quasi-isomorphism; hence `N_dg(Ch⁻(A))[W⁻¹] ≃ D⁻(A)` for W the quasi-isomorphisms.

*Needs:* `HA.1.3.2.19/resolution`, 1.3.2.20, 1.3.4.3; 5.2.7.8 (L6).

**Recovering a simplicial category from its underlying category** (HA Proposition 1.3.4.7, PDF pp. 110, 113–114). Let C be a simplicial category and W a class of morphisms containing the isomorphisms, with two-out-of-three, such that every X has an interval object `Δ[1] ⊗ X` (corepresenting `Map(Δ[1], Map_C(X, −))`) whose projection `Δ[1] ⊗ X ⟶ X` is in W. For `C'` a fibrant replacement of C in `Cat_Δ` and `C₀` the underlying category of C, `(N(C₀), W) ⟶ (N(C'), W)` is a weak equivalence of marked simplicial sets. Example 1.3.4.8 (not a target): for C locally Kan with interval objects and W the homotopy equivalences, `C₀[W⁻¹] ≃ N(C)`.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as two targets: the part that follows this entry, `HA.1.3.4.7/constant` (interval objects make the levelwise diagram constant), and this entry's own target `HA.1.3.4.7`, which factors θ through `hocolim(N(T_• C), W'_•)` with `Ex^∞` in place of `|C|`, gets θ″ from 1.3.4.14 and θ′ from `HA.1.3.4.7/constant`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, with `|C|` replaced by `Ex^∞ C` (layer intro): factor through the homotopy colimit of `T_• C` (1.3.4.14) and show the simplicial object `[n] ↦ (N(C_n), W_n)` is essentially constant, using the interval objects to build a homotopy `F ∘ G ≃ id` (`HA.1.3.4.7/constant`).

*Needs:* `HA.1.3.4.7/constant` (below); 1.3.4.14; 3.1.0.1, 3.1.3.7 (L4, the Cartesian model structure over a point); A.3.2.4, A.3.2.24 (F3.4, the Bergner model structure) for the fibrant replacement; `Ex^∞` (F2.3).

**Interval objects make the levelwise diagram constant** (`HA.1.3.4.7/constant`, the only part of recovering a simplicial category from its underlying category above; HA Proposition 1.3.4.7, central step of the proof, PDF pp. 113–114). Under hypotheses (1)–(4) of 1.3.4.7, two morphisms in the same component of `Map_C(X, Y)` are both in W or both not. With `W_n` the n-simplices of mapping spaces whose vertices lie in W, the maps `(N(C_0), W) ⟶ (N(C_n), W_n)` induced by `[n] ⟶ [0]` are weak equivalences of marked simplicial sets.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the two endpoint inclusions `X ⟶ Δ¹ ⊗ X` are in W by two-out-of-three, so an edge of `Map(X, Y)` gives a map in W out of `Δ¹ ⊗ X`. G is a left inverse, and `U(X) = Δ¹ ⊗ X`, with the explicit reindexing `r : Δ[n] × Δ[1] ⟶ Δ[n] × Δ[1]`, gives natural transformations `F ∘ G ⟶ U ⟵ id` in `W_n`.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.14; 3.1.0.1, 3.1.3.7 (L4).

**Sifted homotopy colimits of simplicial categories with a fixed object set** (HA Lemma 1.3.4.10, PDF pp. 111–112). For a diagram `J ⟶ Cat_Δ`, `α ↦ C_α`, and `θ : colim C_α ⟶ C` such that each `C_α ⟶ C` is bijective on objects, each mapping space of C is the homotopy colimit of those of the `C_α`, and `N(J)` is sifted, θ exhibits C as a homotopy colimit of the `C_α` in `Cat_Δ`.

*Proof route.* Lurie works in `Alg(A)` for the monoidal model category of `S × S`-indexed simplicial sets, citing HA 4.1.8.3 and 4.1.8.13 (outside HA ch. 1). Instead: F3's `HTT.A.3.2/fixed-objects` (the model structure on simplicial categories with object set S, and its comparison with `Cat_Δ`) and `HTT.A.3.2/sifted-hocolim` (sifted homotopy colimits there are computed on mapping spaces).

*Needs:* `HTT.A.3.2/fixed-objects`, `HTT.A.3.2/sifted-hocolim` (F3); 5.5.8.1 (L7, sifted); A.3.1.2, A.3.6.5 (F3); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3).

**Translation functors and `T_• C`** (HA Notation 1.3.4.11, PDF p. 112). For a simplicial category C, `C_n` is the category with the objects of C and `Hom_{C_n}(x, y) = Hom(Δ[n], Map_C(x, y))`, a simplicial object of `Cat`. `t_{[n]} : SSet ⟶ SSet` satisfies `Hom(X, t_{[n]} Y) ≃ Hom(Δ[n] ⋆ X, Y)` for connected nonempty X (it is not a right adjoint into `SSet`: `Δ[n] ⋆ −` sends ∅ to `Δ[n]`; HA's proof of Lemma 1.3.4.12 describes it as a coproduct of coslices); it preserves products, so induces `T_{[n]} : Cat_Δ ⟶ Cat_Δ`, with maps `C_n ⟵ T_{[n]} C ⟶ C` natural in `[n]`.

*Lean:* `SSet.translation n : SSet ⥤ SSet` with `(SSet.translation n).obj Y := ∐ (σ : Δ[n] ⟶ Y), SSet.coslice σ` (Tau Ceti `SSet.coslice`). Lemmas: the bijection `(X ⟶ t_{[n]} Y) ≃ (Δ[n] ⋆ X ⟶ Y)`, natural in connected nonempty X, which is how Notation 1.3.4.11's formula is read; and `t_{[n]}(Y × Z) ≅ t_{[n]} Y × t_{[n]} Z`. `instance : (SSet.translation n).LaxMonoidal`, packaging the product lemma; `SimplicialCategory.translation n C := TransportEnrichment (SSet.translation n) C`. Propose.

*Needs:* Tau Ceti `SSet.join`; Mathlib `SimplicialCategory`; HTT A.1.4.3 (F1, change of enrichment).

**`t_{[m]} X` is a model of `Hom(Δ[m], X)`** (HA Lemma 1.3.4.12, PDF p. 112). For a simplicial set X, `t_{[m]} X ⟶ Hom(Δ[m], X)` (the set of m-simplices as a discrete simplicial set) is a homotopy equivalence: `t_{[m]} X ≅ ⊔_{σ : Δ[m] → X} X_{σ/}`, each summand weakly contractible.

*Needs:* Tau Ceti `SSet.coslice`; weak contractibility of `X_{σ/}` (σ is initial in it, L2.5); `SSet.IsWeaklyContractible`.

**`X` is the homotopy colimit of `t_• X`** (HA Lemma 1.3.4.13, PDF pp. 112–113). For a simplicial set X, `colim_n t_{[n]} X ⟶ X` exhibits X as a homotopy colimit of `[n] ↦ t_{[n]} X`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: filtered colimits, induction on cells, reduction to `[m] ↦ Hom(Δ[m], Δ[n])` having contractible homotopy colimit (HTT A.2.9.30).

*Needs:* 1.3.4.12; A.2.9.30 (F3); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after`, `HTT.A.2.4.3/after` (F3, F1).

**A simplicial category is the realization of `C_•`** (HA Proposition 1.3.4.14, PDF p. 113). For a simplicial category C, `T_• C ⟶ C_•` is a levelwise Dwyer–Kan equivalence of simplicial objects of `Cat_Δ`, and `colim T_• C ⟶ C` exhibits C as a homotopy colimit of `T_• C`.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.10, 1.3.4.12, 1.3.4.13; `CategoryTheory.EnrichedFunctor.IsDwyerKanEquivalence` (Tau Ceti main) (L1.5); 5.5.8.4 (L7, `N(Δ)^op` is sifted).

**The underlying ∞-category of a model category** (`SSet.IsLocalization`, `HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory.underlyingInfty`, propose; HA Definition 1.3.4.15, PDF p. 116). For a model category A with cofibrant objects `A^c` and W the weak equivalences between them, `f : N(A^c) ⟶ C` exhibits C as the underlying ∞-category of A when it is a localization at W (1.3.4.1).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsLocalization f W` for `f : nerve A^c ⟶ C`, `A^c` as the full subcategory of cofibrant objects of a Mathlib `HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory`; no separate structure. Name the chosen localization `HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory.underlyingInfty A`.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.1; Mathlib `HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory`; A.2.1.1 (F1.4).

**Other models of the underlying ∞-category** (HA Remark 1.3.4.16, PDF p. 116). With functorial factorizations (automatic for combinatorial A), localizing A, its fibrant objects, its cofibrant objects or its bifibrant objects at the weak equivalences gives equivalent ∞-categories.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.15; A.2.6.1 (F1.6, combinatorial model categories have functorial factorizations); 3.1.3.7 (L4, marked weak equivalences).

**The correspondence from cofibrant to bifibrant objects** (HA Construction 1.3.4.18, PDF pp. 116–117). For a simplicial model category A, M is the simplicial category with objects `(i, A)`, `i ∈ {0, 1}`, A cofibrant and fibrant when `i = 1`, with `Map((i, A), (j, B))` the simplicial mapping space when `j = 1`, the discrete `Hom(A, B)` when `i = j = 0`, and empty when `j = 0 < 1 = i`. `N(M) ⟶ Δ[1]` is a correspondence from `N(A^c)` to `N(A°)`.

*Needs:* A.3.1.5 (F3, simplicial model categories); `CategoryTheory.SimplicialNerve`; 2.3.1.3 (L3.1, `SSet.Correspondence`).

**It is a coCartesian fibration** (HA Lemma 1.3.4.19, PDF p. 117). `N(M) ⟶ Δ[1]` is a coCartesian fibration, and an edge `(0, A) ⟶ (1, B)` is coCartesian exactly when `A ⟶ B` is a weak equivalence. It therefore determines `θ : N(A^c) ⟶ N(A°)` up to equivalence.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.18; 2.4.4.3 (L3.7); 2.4.2.1 (L3.6).

**The Dwyer–Kan theorem** (HA Theorem 1.3.4.20, PDF pp. 117, 120). For a simplicial model category A, θ exhibits `N(A°)` as the underlying ∞-category of A: `N(A^c)[W⁻¹] ≃ N(A°)`.

**Checks.** For `A = SSet` with the Kan–Quillen model structure, the underlying ∞-category is `S` (`N(Kan)`).

*Proof route.* Lurie's, with `|C|` replaced by `Ex^∞ C` for `C = A^c` (layer intro): compare with `(N(Ex^∞ A^c), W)` through 1.3.4.7, and build a left homotopy inverse from a left adjoint to `N(Ex^∞ A°) ⊆ N(Ex^∞ A^c)` (fibrant replacement).

*Needs:* 1.3.4.7, 1.3.4.15, 1.3.4.19; 5.2.2.7 (L6, adjunctions); 3.1.0.1 (L4); A.3.1.5 (F3).

**Quillen equivalences induce equivalences** (HA Lemma 1.3.4.21, PDF pp. 117–118). A left Quillen equivalence `F : A ⟶ B` of combinatorial model categories induces a weak equivalence of marked simplicial sets `(N(A^c), W_A) ⟶ (N(B^c), W_B)`, hence an equivalence of underlying ∞-categories.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.15; `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions` (F1.5); A.2.6.1 (F1.6); 3.1.0.1 (L4).

**Underlying ∞-categories of combinatorial model categories are presentable** (HA Proposition 1.3.4.22, PDF p. 118). Lurie: Dugger's theorem (every combinatorial model category is Quillen equivalent to a combinatorial simplicial one), 1.3.4.21, 1.3.4.20 and HTT A.3.7.6.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.20, 1.3.4.21; `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-simplicial` (F3.9); A.3.7.6 (L8); 5.5.0.1 (L7).

**Homotopy limits are limits** (HA Proposition 1.3.4.23, PDF pp. 118–119). For A combinatorial, I small, `F : I ⟶ A^c` and `α : X ⟶ lim F` in `A^c`, α exhibits X as a homotopy limit of F exactly when the induced `N(I)^◁ ⟶ N(A^c)[W⁻¹]` is a limit diagram.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.22 (its reduction to the simplicial case); 4.2.4.1 (L5.7); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3); `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-simplicial` (F3.9).

**Homotopy colimits are colimits** (HA Proposition 1.3.4.24, PDF p. 119). Dually, `α : colim F ⟶ X` exhibits X as a homotopy colimit exactly when `N(I)^▷ ⟶ N(A^c)[W⁻¹]` is a colimit diagram.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.23; 4.2.4.4 (L5.7); 1.2.13.5 (L2).

**Diagram categories** (HA Proposition 1.3.4.25, PDF p. 119). For A combinatorial and I small, with `A^I` in the injective or projective model structure, `N(I) × N((A^I)^c) ⟶ N(A^c)` induces `N((A^I)^c)[W'⁻¹] ≃ Fun(N(I), N(A^c)[W⁻¹])`.

*Proof route.* Reduce to the simplicial case (Dugger) and apply HTT 4.2.4.4.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.24; 4.2.4.4 (L5.7); A.2.8.2 (F3.2, injective and projective model structures); `HTT.A.3.7/dugger-simplicial` (F3.9).

**Left Quillen functors preserve colimits** (HA Corollary 1.3.4.26, PDF p. 119). A left Quillen functor between combinatorial model categories induces a functor of underlying ∞-categories preserving small colimits (and so has a right adjoint, Remark 1.3.4.27, not a target).

*Needs:* 1.3.4.24, 1.3.4.25; 4.4.2.7 (L5.10); `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions` (F1.5).

**Grothendieck abelian categories** (HA Definition 1.3.5.1, PDF p. 121). An abelian category is Grothendieck when it is presentable and monomorphisms are closed under small filtered colimits. Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian` (locally small, filtered colimits, AB5, a separator) is the definition used; the target is the equivalence with HA's form, with "presentable" read for the nerve (HTT 5.5.0.1; for the nerve of an ordinary category this is local presentability of the category).

*Lean:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u} A`; no new definition. The target: for abelian A, it holds exactly when `SSet.IsPresentable (nerve A)` and monomorphisms are closed under small filtered colimits.

*Needs:* 5.5.0.1 (L7); Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian`, `CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckAxioms`.
