**The injective model structure** (HA Proposition 1.3.5.3, PDF pp. 121–123). For A Grothendieck abelian, `Ch(A)` has a left proper combinatorial model structure with cofibrations the degreewise monomorphisms, weak equivalences the quasi-isomorphisms, and fibrations determined by lifting.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HA.1.3.5.3/generating-cofibrations` (a generating set for the degreewise monomorphisms), `HA.1.3.5.3/perfect-pushout` (quasi-isomorphisms are perfect and pushout-stable) and `HA.1.3.5.3/lifting-acyclic` (maps lifting against all monomorphisms are quasi-isomorphisms), and this entry's own target `HA.1.3.5.3`, which applies A.2.6.15 to them and gets left properness from `HA.1.3.5.3/perfect-pushout` and A.2.4.1.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the cofibrations are generated by a set of monomorphisms `E(u, n) ⟶ E(id_X, n)` for a generator X (`HA.1.3.5.3/generating-cofibrations`); then Smith's recognition theorem in HTT's form A.2.6.15, with hypotheses (1)–(2) from `HA.1.3.5.3/perfect-pushout` and (3) from `HA.1.3.5.3/lifting-acyclic`.

*Needs:* `HA.1.3.5.3/generating-cofibrations`, `HA.1.3.5.3/perfect-pushout`, `HA.1.3.5.3/lifting-acyclic` (below); 1.3.5.1; A.2.6.15 (F1.6); A.2.4.1 (F1.5, left proper).

**Generating cofibrations of `Ch(A)`** (`HA.1.3.5.3/generating-cofibrations`, part 1 of 3 of the injective model structure above; HA Proposition 1.3.5.3, first step of the proof, PDF pp. 121–122). Let A be Grothendieck abelian with a generator X, and for a monomorphism `u : X' ⟶ X` let `E(u, n)` be the complex with u from degree n to degree `n − 1`. The degreewise monomorphisms of `Ch(A)` are the weakly saturated class generated by the small set of maps `E(u, n) ⟶ E(id_X, n)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: subobject lattices in A are essentially small, since X generates. Given a degreewise monomorphism `M ⟶ N`, enlarge M transfinitely by pushouts of generators, each step strictly enlarging the subobject of N; limit stages stay monomorphisms because filtered colimits of monomorphisms are monomorphisms.

*Needs:* 1.3.5.1, 1.2.3.1; A.1.2.2 (F1); 5.5.0.1 (L7).

**Quasi-isomorphisms are perfect and pushout-stable** (`HA.1.3.5.3/perfect-pushout`, part 2 of 3 of the injective model structure above; HA Proposition 1.3.5.3, hypotheses (1)–(2) of Smith's theorem, PDF pp. 122–123). The quasi-isomorphisms of `Ch(A)` form a perfect class (A.2.6.12), and a pushout of a quasi-isomorphism along a degreewise monomorphism is a quasi-isomorphism.

*Proof route.* Perfection from A.2.6.14, since total homology commutes with filtered colimits; pushout stability by the five lemma on the long exact sequences of the two cofibre sequences, whose quotients agree.

*Needs:* 1.3.5.1; A.2.6.12, A.2.6.14 (F1.6); Mathlib `HomologicalComplex.HomologySequence`.

**Maps lifting against all monomorphisms are quasi-isomorphisms** (`HA.1.3.5.3/lifting-acyclic`, part 3 of 3 of the injective model structure above; HA Proposition 1.3.5.3, hypothesis (3) of Smith's theorem, PDF p. 123). If `f : M ⟶ N` in `Ch(A)` has the right lifting property against every degreewise monomorphism, then f is a quasi-isomorphism.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: lifting against `0 ⟶ Z[n]`, with Z the n-cycles of N, gives surjectivity on `H_n`; lifting against `E(0 ⟶ Z'', n+1) ⟶ E(id, n+1)` for a suitable fibre product `Z''` gives injectivity.

*Needs:* 1.3.5.1.

**Fibrant complexes** (HA Proposition 1.3.5.6, PDF pp. 124–125). For A Grothendieck abelian, a fibrant complex is degreewise injective; conversely a degreewise injective complex with `M_n = 0` for `n ≫ 0` (homological indexing; in cochain degrees, `M.X k = 0` for `k ≪ 0`) is fibrant. (All objects are cofibrant.)

*Needs:* 1.3.5.3; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Injective`.

**Enough injectives** (HA Corollary 1.3.5.7, PDF p. 124). A Grothendieck abelian category has enough injectives. Mathlib proves this (`CategoryTheory/Abelian/GrothendieckCategory/EnoughInjectives.lean`); the target is that instance, Lurie's proof through 1.3.5.6 being an alternative.

*Needs:* 1.3.5.1; Mathlib `EnoughInjectives` for `IsGrothendieckAbelian`.

**The unbounded derived ∞-category** (propose `TauCeti.derivedCategoryInfty A`; HA Definition 1.3.5.8, PDF p. 125). For A Grothendieck abelian, `D(A) = N_dg(Ch(A)°)`, the dg nerve of the full dg subcategory of fibrant (automatically cofibrant) complexes.

*Lean:* `TauCeti.dgNerve ℤ (TauCeti.DGFullSubcategory IsFibrant)` on the dg category `Ch(A)` (1.3.2.1), with `IsFibrant` for the model structure of 1.3.5.3, for `A : Type u` with `[Category.{0} A]` (as in 1.3.2.7).

**Checks.**

- For `A = ModuleCat R`, `h D(A)` is equivalent to Mathlib's `DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)`; Tau Ceti main has a dg nerve comparison for K-injective resolutions (`dgNerveHomotopyCategoryEquiv`, `TauCeti/CategoryTheory/DG/CochainComplex/KInjective.lean`), which is the model for this check.
- `D⁺(A) ⊆ D(A)` as a full subcategory (Remark 1.3.5.10, from 1.3.5.6).

*Needs:* 1.3.1.6, 1.3.5.3; A.2.1.1 (F1.4).

**`D(A)` is stable** (HA Proposition 1.3.5.9, PDF pp. 125–126). It is a stable subcategory of `N_dg(Ch(A))`: closed under shifts and under mapping cones of maps between fibrant complexes.

*Needs:* 1.3.5.8, 1.3.2.10, 1.3.2.17, 1.1.3.2, 1.1.3.3.

**Acyclic complexes into fibrant ones** (HA Lemma 1.3.5.11, PDF p. 126). For A Grothendieck abelian, M acyclic and Q fibrant, `Map_{Ch(A)}(M, Q)` is acyclic.

*Needs:* 1.3.5.3, 1.3.2.1.

**Trivial cofibrations into fibrant targets** (HA Lemma 1.3.5.12, PDF p. 126). For a trivial cofibration `M' ⟶ M` and Q fibrant, `Map(M, Q) ⟶ Map(M', Q)` is a quasi-isomorphism.

*Needs:* 1.3.5.6, 1.3.5.11.

**`D(A)` is a reflective localization of `N_dg(Ch(A))`** (HA Proposition 1.3.5.13, PDF p. 127). The inclusion `D(A) ⊆ N_dg(Ch(A))` has a left adjoint, given by fibrant replacement. (HA says "localization" in HTT's sense.)

*Needs:* 1.3.5.12; 5.2.7.8 (L6).

**Quasi-isomorphisms into fibrant complexes** (HA Proposition 1.3.5.14, PDF p. 127). A quasi-isomorphism `M ⟶ M'` induces quasi-isomorphisms `Map(M', Q) ⟶ Map(M, Q)` for Q fibrant; a quasi-isomorphism between fibrant complexes is a chain homotopy equivalence.

*Needs:* 1.3.5.12.

**`D(A)` is the underlying ∞-category of `Ch(A)`** (HA Proposition 1.3.5.15, PDF p. 127). `N(Ch(A)) ⟶ N_dg(Ch(A)) ⟶ D(A)`, the second map the left adjoint L of 1.3.5.13, exhibits `D(A)` as the underlying ∞-category of the model category `Ch(A)` (1.3.4.15).

*Proof route.* The fibrant complexes are closed under `N_*(Δ[1]) ⊗ −`; apply 1.3.4.5 and 1.3.5.14, then 1.3.4.16.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.5, 1.3.4.16, 1.3.5.13, 1.3.5.14; `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions` (F1.5).

**Connective and coconnective complexes** (HA Definition 1.3.5.16, PDF p. 128). `N_dg(Ch(A))_{≥n}` and `_{≤n}` are the full subcategories of complexes with `H_k = 0` for `k < n`, resp. `k > n` (HA's chain indexing); `D(A)_{≥n}`, `D(A)_{≤n}` are their intersections with `D(A)`.

*Lean:* `TauCeti.dgNerveConnective A n` and `TauCeti.dgNerveCoconnective A n` (propose), the `SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory` of `TauCeti.dgNerve ℤ (Ch(A))` (for `[Category.{0} A]`, as in 1.3.2.7) on the vertices v with, in cochain degrees, `∀ k > −n, IsZero ((dgNerveEquiv ℤ _ v).homology k)`, resp. `∀ k < −n, IsZero ((dgNerveEquiv ℤ _ v).homology k)` (HA's `H_k = 0` for `k < n`, resp. `k > n`). `D(A)_{≥n}` and `D(A)_{≤n}` are the same predicates on `TauCeti.derivedCategoryInfty A`.

*Needs:* 1.3.5.8; Mathlib `HomologicalComplex.homology`.

**Coconnective fibrant models** (HA Remark 1.3.5.17, PDF p. 128). Every object of `D(A)_{≤n}` is equivalent in `D(A)_{≤n}` to a fibrant complex vanishing above degree n.

*Needs:* 1.3.5.16, 1.3.5.6, 1.3.5.7; the construction of `HA.1.3.2.19/resolution`, dualized.

**The t-structure on `N_dg(Ch(A))`** (HA Proposition 1.3.5.18, PDF pp. 128–129). For A Grothendieck abelian, `N_dg(Ch(A))_{≥0}` and `N_dg(Ch(A))_{≤0}` form a t-structure on `N_dg(Ch(A))`. (Lurie's statement writes `N_dg(A)_{≤0}`; it means `N_dg(Ch(A))_{≤0}`.)

*Needs:* 1.3.5.12, 1.3.5.17; 1.2.1.4.

**Compatibility with filtered colimits** (HA Definition 1.3.5.20, PDF p. 129). For a stable C with small filtered colimits, a t-structure is compatible with filtered colimits when `C_{≤0}` is closed under them.

*Lean:* `t.IsCompatibleWithFilteredColimits : Prop := ∀ (I : SSet.{u}) [SSet.IsFiltered I] (p : I.rightCone ⟶ C), SSet.IsColimitDiagram p → (∀ i, t.ge 0 (HomotopyCategory.mk (p.app _ (rightCone.incl i)))) → t.ge 0 (HomotopyCategory.mk (p.app _ (rightCone.pt I)))` (`t.leq 0` is a `Subcomplex`, so membership is read in the homotopy category); the sequential version 1.2.2.12 is implied.

*Needs:* 1.2.1.4; 5.3.1.7 (L6, filtered ∞-categories).

**`D(A)` is presentable with an accessible t-structure** (HA Proposition 1.3.5.21, PDF p. 129). For A Grothendieck abelian: `D(A)` is presentable; `(D(A)_{≥0}, D(A)_{≤0})` is a t-structure; it is accessible (1.4.4.12), right complete and compatible with filtered colimits. Its heart is A (Remark 1.3.5.19, not a target, from 1.3.5.12 and 1.3.5.17); it is generally not left complete.

*Needs:* 1.3.4.22, 1.3.4.24, 1.3.4.25, 1.3.5.15, 1.3.5.18, 1.3.5.20; the dual of 1.2.1.19; 5.4.6.6 (L7); 1.4.4.12 (L9.6, the definition of an accessible t-structure: a forward need of L9.5 on a definition only).

**`D⁻(A)` inside `D(A)`** (HA Proposition 1.3.5.24, PDF p. 130). For A Grothendieck abelian with enough projectives and L the left adjoint of 1.3.5.13, `D⁻(A) ⊆ N_dg(Ch(A)) ⟶ D(A)` is fully faithful with essential image `⋃_{n ≥ 0} D(A)_{≥−n}`.

*Needs:* 1.3.2.20, 1.3.5.13, 1.3.2.7; `SSet.IsFullyFaithful` (L1.5).

### L9.6 Spectra and stabilization

`S_*` is the ∞-category of pointed spaces, the pointed objects of `S` (`HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed`, L6.8), and `S^fin ⊆ S` the smallest full subcategory containing the final object and closed under finite colimits, with `S^fin_*` its pointed objects (HA Notation 1.4.2.5, not a target; Lean: propose `SSet.finiteSpaces` as that closure and `SSet.pointedObjects` from L6.8).

**Suspensions are cogroups** (HA Example 1.4.1.1, PDF p. 134). In an ∞-category with finite colimits, for `X ⟶ ∅` (∅ initial), `ΣX = ∅ ⊔_X ∅` is a cogroup object of `hC`: the fold map `ΣX ⟶ ΣX ⊔ ΣX` induces on `Hom_{hC}(ΣX, Y) ≅ π₁(Map_C(X, Y), X ⟶ ∅ ⟶ Y)` its group structure.

*Lean:* cogroup objects of `hC` as Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.GrpObj` (the class; bundled, `CategoryTheory.Grp`) in `(hoFunctor.obj C)ᵒᵖ` with the Cartesian monoidal structure from coproducts, or propose `SSet.IsCogroupObject X` with the comultiplication and the group-valued `Hom(X, −)`; the target is the cogroup structure on ΣX and the identification with `π₁`.

*Needs:* `SSet.IsPushout` (L5.10); `SSet.KanComplex.π` (Tau Ceti); 4.4.2.2 (L5.10).

**Brown representability** (HA Theorem 1.4.1.2, PDF pp. 134–135, 137–140). Let C be a presentable ∞-category with a set of objects `S_α` that are cogroup objects of `hC`, compact, and generate C under small colimits. A functor `F : hC^op ⟶ Set` is representable exactly when it carries coproducts to products and carries pushout squares of C to maps `F(D') ⟶ F(C') ×_{F(C)} F(D)` that are surjective.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HA.1.4.1.2/detection` (detecting equivalences by the generators) and `HA.1.4.1.2/cell-attachment` (attaching cells to realize F on the generators), and this entry's own target `HA.1.4.1.2`, which proves necessity and shows that the element obtained from `X = ∅` represents F.

**Checks.**

- A compactly generated presentable stable ∞-category satisfies the hypotheses, every object being a cogroup in the additive `hC` (Example 1.4.1.3).
- `S_*^{≥1}` (pointed connected spaces) satisfies them with the single generator `S¹` (Example 1.4.1.4), recovering classical Brown representability.

*Proof route.* Lurie's (PDF pp. 137–140). Enlarge `{S_α}` to be closed under suspension. (∗) A map inducing bijections on all `[S_α, −]` is an equivalence: `HA.1.4.1.2/detection`. (∗′) For `η ∈ F(X)`, attaching cells gives `X ⟶ X'` and `η' ∈ F(X')` inducing bijections `[S_α, X'] ⟶ F(S_α)`: `HA.1.4.1.2/cell-attachment`. The element obtained from `X = ∅` represents F: surjectivity and injectivity of `[Y, X'] ⟶ F(Y)` follow from (∗′) and (∗).

*Needs:* `HA.1.4.1.2/detection`, `HA.1.4.1.2/cell-attachment` (below); 1.4.1.1; 5.5.0.1 (L7).

**Detecting equivalences by the generators** (`HA.1.4.1.2/detection`, part 1 of 2 of Brown representability above; HA Theorem 1.4.1.2, step (∗) of the proof, PDF pp. 137–138). Under the hypotheses of 1.4.1.2, the family `{S_α}` may be enlarged to be closed under suspension `Σ(S) = ∅ ⨿_S ∅`. A morphism `f : C ⟶ C'` inducing bijections `[S_α, C] ⟶ [S_α, C']` for all α is then an equivalence.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the X for which `Map(X, C) ⟶ Map(X, C')` is an equivalence are closed under colimits; for `X = S_α` the cogroup structure makes these mapping spaces group-like, and `π_n` at the unit is `[Σ^n S_α, −]`.

*Needs:* 1.4.1.1; `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed` (L6.8); 5.1.5.7 (L6); the mapping-space characterization of colimits (Kerodon 7.1.1.1, L1.5), for the closure of the good objects under colimits; `HTT.A.2.7/kan-weak-equivalences` (F2.2, Whitehead's theorem for the maps of group-like mapping spaces).

**Attaching cells to realize F on the generators** (`HA.1.4.1.2/cell-attachment`, part 2 of 2 of Brown representability above; HA Theorem 1.4.1.2, step (∗′) of the proof, PDF pp. 138–139). If `F : hC^op ⟶ Set` carries coproducts to products and pushout squares to surjections onto fibre products, then for X ∈ C and η ∈ F(X) there are `X ⟶ X'` and η′ ∈ F(X′) restricting to η such that every `[S_α, X'] ⟶ F(S_α)` is bijective.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `X_0 = X ⨿ ⨿_{α, γ ∈ F(S_α)} S_α` gives surjectivity, and `X_{n+1}` cones off the kernels of `[S_α, X_n] ⟶ F(S_α)`. Lift along the sequential colimit, written as a pushout of coproducts. Injectivity uses compactness of the `S_α`.

*Needs:* 1.4.1.1 (the group structures on `[S_α, −]`, for the kernels and the injectivity step); 5.3.4.5 (L6, compactness of the `S_α`).

**Cohomology theories** (`SSet.CohomologyTheory`, propose; HA Definition 1.4.1.6, PDF pp. 135–136). For a pointed ∞-category C with small colimits, a cohomology theory is a sequence of functors `Hⁿ : hC^op ⟶ Set`, `n ∈ ℤ`, with isomorphisms `δⁿ : Hⁿ ≅ H^{n+1} ∘ Σ`, such that each `Hⁿ` carries coproducts to products and, for every cofibre sequence `C' ⟶ C ⟶ C''`, an element of `Hⁿ(C)` restricting to 0 on C' comes from `Hⁿ(C'')`. (Each `Hⁿ` is then abelian-group valued, Remark 1.4.1.7, not a target.)

*Lean:* a structure on `ℤ → (hoFunctor.obj C)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type` with the δ isomorphisms and the two axioms.

*Needs:* 1.1.1.1, 1.1.1.4; suspension (L9.1).

**The long exact sequence** (HA Remark 1.4.1.8, PDF p. 136). For a cohomology theory and a cofibre sequence `C' ⟶ C ⟶ C''`, the boundary maps `Hⁿ(C') ⟶ H^{n+1}(ΣC') ⟶ H^{n+1}(C'')` splice into a long exact sequence of abelian groups.

*Needs:* 1.4.1.6, 1.1.2.13.

**Cohomology theories satisfy Brown's conditions** (HA Remark 1.4.1.9, PDF pp. 136–137). Each `Hⁿ` of a cohomology theory satisfies conditions (a) and (b) of 1.4.1.2.

*Needs:* 1.4.1.6, 1.4.1.8.

**Representing cohomology theories** (HA Corollary 1.4.1.10, PDF p. 137). For C presentable and pointed, generated under colimits by compact cogroup objects of `hC`, each `Hⁿ` of a cohomology theory is representable by some `E(n) ∈ C`.

*Needs:* 1.4.1.2, 1.4.1.9; 5.5.0.1 (L7); 5.3.4.5 (L6).

**Excisive and reduced functors** (`SSet.IsExcisive`, `SSet.IsReduced`; HA Definition 1.4.2.1, PDF p. 141). For `F : C ⟶ D` of ∞-categories: when C has pushouts, F is excisive when it carries pushout squares to pullback squares; when C has a final object ∗, F is reduced when `F(∗)` is final. `Exc(C, D)`, `Fun_∗(C, D)` and `Exc_∗(C, D) = Exc ∩ Fun_∗` are the full subcategories of `Fun(C, D)`.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsExcisive F := ∀ σ, SSet.IsPushout σ → SSet.IsPullback (σ ≫ F)`; `SSet.IsReduced F := ∀ X, IsTerminalVertex X → IsTerminalVertex (F X)`; the three full subcategories of the internal Hom.

**Checks.** Between stable ∞-categories, reduced and excisive is exact (Remark 1.4.2.2, from 1.1.3.4 and 1.1.4.1).

*Needs:* `SSet.IsPushout`, `SSet.IsPullback` (L5.10); `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**Limits of excisive functors** (HA Remark 1.4.2.3, PDF p. 141). If C has pushouts and D has K-indexed limits, `Fun(C, D)` has them (pointwise) and `Exc(C, D)` is closed under them; so is `Fun_∗(C, D)` when C has a final object.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.1; 5.1.2.2 (L6); `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**Presentability of excisive functors** (HA Remark 1.4.2.4, PDF p. 141). For C small, pointed, with finite colimits and D presentable, `Fun_∗(C, D)`, `Exc(C, D)` and `Exc_∗(C, D)` are accessible reflective localizations of `Fun(C, D)`, hence presentable.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.1; 5.5.4.18, 5.5.4.19, 5.5.4.15 (L7); 5.5.3.6 (L7).

**The universal property of finite spaces** (HA Remark 1.4.2.6, PDF p. 141). For D with finite colimits, evaluation at ∗ is an equivalence `Fun^{Rex}(S^fin, D) ⟶ D` from right exact functors.

*Needs:* 5.3.5.9 (L6), 4.3.2.15 (L5.9).

**Spectrum objects** (`SSet.spectrumObjects`; HA Definition 1.4.2.8, PDF p. 142). For C with finite limits, a spectrum object is a reduced excisive functor `S^fin_* ⟶ C`, and `Sp(C) = Exc_∗(S^fin_*, C)`.

*Lean:* `SSet.spectrumObjects C` the full subcategory of `Fun(S^fin_*, C)` on reduced excisive functors, for a quasicategory C with finite limits; `SSet.spectrumObjects.ΩInfty : spectrumObjects C ⟶ C` evaluation at `S⁰` (Notation 1.4.2.20, not a target), with `Ω^{∞−n}` through the shift.

**Checks.**

- For C with finite limits, `Ω^∞ : Sp(C) ⟶ C` is an equivalence exactly when C is stable (1.4.2.21). For C pointed with finite limits, stability is equivalent to Ω_C being an equivalence (1.4.2.27).
- `Sp(Δ[0]) ≃ Δ[0]`.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.1; `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed` (L6.8).

**Spectrum objects of functor categories** (HA Remark 1.4.2.9, PDF p. 142). For C with finite limits and K any simplicial set, `Sp(Fun(K, C)) ≅ Fun(K, Sp(C))`.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.8, 1.4.2.3.

**`Exc_∗` is pointed with finite limits** (HA Lemma 1.4.2.10, PDF p. 142). For C pointed with finite colimits and D with finite limits, `Exc_∗(C, D)` is pointed (the constant functor at a final object is a zero object) and has finite limits.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.3; 4.3.2.2 (L5.9, the constant functor is a left Kan extension from the zero object); `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**Stability from invertible loops** (HA Proposition 1.4.2.11, PDF pp. 142–143). For C pointed with finite limits and colimits: if Σ is fully faithful, pushout squares are pullback squares; if Ω is fully faithful, pullback squares are pushout squares; if Ω is an equivalence, C is stable.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.13; 1.1.1.9; `SSet.IsFullyFaithful` (L1.5); `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction` (Σ ⊣ Ω).

**The comparison maps `η`** (HA Notation 1.4.2.12, PDF p. 143). For `F : C ⟶ D` with D having finite limits and a square τ in C, `η_τ : F(W) ⟶ F(X) ×_{F(Z)} F(Y)`; when X, Y and their images are zero and τ is a pushout, this is `η_W : F(W) ⟶ Ω_D F(Σ_C W)`.

*Lean:* `SSet.excisiveComparison F τ` (propose), for `F : C ⟶ D` with D having finite limits and `τ : Δ[1] ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ C`: the edge from `F(squareVertex τ 0 0)` to a chosen pullback (`SSet.IsPullback`) of `F(squareVertex τ 1 0) ⟶ F(squareVertex τ 1 1) ⟵ F(squareVertex τ 0 1)` induced by `τ ≫ F` (`squareVertex`, L9.1), well defined up to equivalence. When τ is a pushout whose corners `(1,0)`, `(0,1)` and their images are zero objects, it is `η_W : F W ⟶ SSet.loops (F (SSet.suspension W))`.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.1; `SSet.IsPullback` (L5.10).

**Excisiveness through `η`** (HA Proposition 1.4.2.13, PDF pp. 143, 145). For C pointed with finite colimits, D pointed with finite limits and F reduced, F is excisive exactly when every `η_X : F(X) ⟶ Ω F(ΣX)` is an equivalence.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.12, 1.4.2.15.

**Exactness through suspensions** (HA Corollary 1.4.2.14, PDF pp. 143–144). A functor between stable ∞-categories is exact exactly when it preserves zero objects and every `Σ F(X) ⟶ F(ΣX)` is an equivalence.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.13, 1.4.2.11; 1.1.4.1; Remark 1.4.2.2 (reduced excisive = exact between stable ∞-categories).

**The map `θ_τ`** (HA Lemma 1.4.2.15, PDF pp. 144–145). For C, D, F as in 1.4.2.13 and a pushout square τ, there is `θ_τ : F(X) ×_{F(Z)} F(Y) ⟶ Ω F(ΣW)` with `θ_τ ∘ η_τ ≃ η_W`, fitting into a pullback square in `Fun(Δ[1], D)` with `η_{Σ(τ)} ∘ θ_τ`, `η_X`, `η_Y`, `η_Z`.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.12; 4.4.2.1 (L5.10).

**`Exc_∗(C, D)` is stable** (HA Proposition 1.4.2.16, PDF pp. 145–146). For C pointed with finite colimits and D with finite limits, `Exc_∗(C, D)` is stable.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: for presentable D, `F ↦ F ∘ Σ_C` inverts Ω, and 1.4.2.11 applies (finite colimits from 1.4.2.4); in general embed D into `P(D)` by Yoneda and use 1.1.3.3.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.4, 1.4.2.10, 1.4.2.11, 1.1.3.3; 5.1.3.1, 5.1.3.2 (L6); 5.5.0.1 (L7).

**`Sp(C)` is stable** (HA Corollary 1.4.2.17, PDF p. 146). For C with finite limits, `Sp(C)` is stable.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.8, 1.4.2.16.

**Pointed objects do not change spectra** (HA Remark 1.4.2.18, PDF p. 146). For C with finite limits, the forgetful functor `C_∗ ⟶ C` induces an equivalence `Sp(C_∗) ⟶ Sp(C)`.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.17, 1.4.2.8; `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed` (L6.8).

**Reduced excisive functors out of pointed objects** (HA Lemma 1.4.2.19, PDF p. 146). For C with finite colimits and a final object, `f : C ⟶ C_∗` left adjoint to the forgetful functor, and D stable, composition with f is an equivalence `Exc_∗(C_∗, D) ⟶ Exc₀(C, D)`, the latter the excisive functors carrying the initial object to a final object.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.1, 1.1.3.2, 1.1.1.9; `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`; `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed` (L6.8).

**Stability through `Ω^∞`** (HA Proposition 1.4.2.21, PDF pp. 146–147). For D with finite limits, D is stable exactly when `Ω^∞ : Sp(D) ⟶ D` is an equivalence.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.17, 1.4.2.19, 1.4.2.6.

**`Sp` of the target** (HA Proposition 1.4.2.22, PDF p. 147). For C pointed with finite colimits and D with finite limits, composition with `Ω^∞` is an equivalence `Exc_∗(C, Sp(D)) ⟶ Exc_∗(C, D)`.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.16, 1.4.2.21, 1.4.2.9.

**The universal property of stabilization** (HA Corollary 1.4.2.23, PDF p. 147). For C stable and D with finite limits, composition with `Ω^∞` is an equivalence from left exact functors `C ⟶ Sp(D)` to left exact functors `C ⟶ D`.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.22; 1.1.4.1, 1.1.3.4.

**`Sp(C)` as a limit of loops** (HA Proposition 1.4.2.24, PDF pp. 147, 149). For C pointed with finite limits, `Ω^∞` lifts to an equivalence of `Sp(C)` with the limit in `Cat∞` of the tower `⋯ ⟶ C ⟶ C` of loop functors.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the limit is stable (for presentable C by HTT 5.5.3.18 and 1.4.2.11; in general through the embedding into `P_∗(C)`, 1.4.2.26, and 1.1.3.3); then compare universal properties through 1.4.2.23.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.11, 1.4.2.23, 1.4.2.26, 1.1.3.3; 5.5.3.18 (L7); 3.3.3.1 (L5.1); `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3); 1.4.2.16.

**Spectra as sequences of pointed objects** (HA Remark 1.4.2.25, PDF p. 147). For C with finite limits, `Sp(C)` is the limit of the tower `⋯ ⟶ C_∗ ⟶ C_∗` of loop functors.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.18, 1.4.2.24.

**Pointed presheaves** (HA Lemma 1.4.2.26, PDF pp. 147–148). For C small and pointed, `P_∗(C) ⊆ P(C)`, the presheaves carrying zero objects to final objects, is the localization at a single map from an initial to a final object; it is an accessible reflective localization, hence presentable; the Yoneda embedding lands in it and preserves zero objects; colimit-preserving functors out of it are the functors out of C carrying zero objects to initial objects; it is pointed, closed in `P(C)` under small limits and under colimits indexed by weakly contractible simplicial sets; j preserves the limits that exist in C; and `P_∗(C)` is compactly generated.

*Needs:* 5.5.4.15, 5.5.4.20, 5.5.7.1, 5.5.7.3 (L7); 5.1.5.6, 5.1.3.2 (L6); 4.3.2.2 (L5.9); `SSet.IsWeaklyContractible`.

**Pointed stability criteria** (HA Corollary 1.4.2.27, PDF pp. 149–150). For a pointed ∞-category C the following are equivalent: C is stable; C has finite colimits and Σ is an equivalence; C has finite limits and Ω is an equivalence. In particular the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1.2.14 (with finite colimits) characterize stability.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.17, 1.4.2.24.

**Spectra** (`SSet.spectra`, propose; HA Definition 1.4.3.1, PDF p. 150). A spectrum is a spectrum object of `S`; `Sp = Sp(S_*)` (equivalently `Sp(S)`, 1.4.2.18). Its homotopy category is the classical stable homotopy category (Remark 1.4.3.2, not a target).

*Lean:* `SSet.spectra := SSet.spectrumObjects (SSet.pointedObjects S)` for `S` the large ∞-category of spaces (Universes convention: `Sp` is large, locally small).

*Needs:* 1.4.2.8; `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed` (L6.8); L5.1 (`S` has finite limits).

**The t-structure on `Sp(C)`** (HA Proposition 1.4.3.4, PDF pp. 150–151). For C presentable, the full subcategory of `X ∈ Sp(C)` with `Ω^∞ X` final determines an accessible t-structure on `Sp(C)`, with `Sp(C)_{≤−1}` that subcategory.

*Proof route.* `Ω^∞` has a left adjoint `Σ^∞_+` (HTT 5.5.2.9); `Sp(C)_{≥0}` is generated under colimits and extensions by the `Σ^∞_+ C_α` for generators `C_α` of C (Remark 1.4.3.5), and 1.4.4.11 gives the t-structure.

*Needs:* 1.4.4.11, 1.4.4.12 (forward within L9.6); 1.4.4.4 (2); 5.5.2.9 (L7); 5.4.2.1 (L7).

**The ∞-category of spectra** (HA Proposition 1.4.3.6, PDF pp. 151–152). `Sp` is stable; `Sp_{≤−1} = {X : Ω^∞ X contractible}` is an accessible t-structure; it is left and right complete; and its heart is the nerve of the category of abelian groups.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: stability by 1.4.2.17, the t-structure by 1.4.3.4; the heart through Eilenberg–MacLane objects, where Lurie cites HTT 7.2.2.12 (L12); use instead `HTT.A.2.7/eilenberg-maclane` (F2.5: pointed Eilenberg–MacLane spaces of degree `n ≥ 2` form a category equivalent to abelian groups, through `π₀` of pointed mapping spaces) and `HTT.A.2.7/kan-weak-equivalences` (Whitehead). Completeness by 1.2.1.19 and its dual, since `π_n` commutes with products and filtered colimits.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.17, 1.4.3.1, 1.4.3.4, 1.2.1.19, `HA.1.2.1.17/after`; `HTT.A.2.7/eilenberg-maclane`, `HTT.A.2.7/kan-weak-equivalences` (F2).

**`Sp(C)` is compactly generated** (HA Proposition 1.4.3.7, PDF p. 152). For C compactly generated, `Sp(C)` is compactly generated.

*Needs:* 1.4.4.4; 5.3.5.10 (L6); 5.5.1.9, 5.5.7.1 (L7); 5.3.4.5 (L6); `SSet.IsFullyFaithful` (L1.5).

**Homotopy groups detect equivalences** (HA Remark 1.4.3.8, PDF p. 153). The functors `π_n : Sp ⟶ N(Ab)` agree for `n ≥ 2` with the homotopy groups of `Ω^∞` composed with `S_* ⟶ N(Ab)`, and a map of spectra is an equivalence exactly when it induces isomorphisms on all `π_n`.

*Needs:* 1.4.3.6; `SSet.KanComplex.π` (Tau Ceti).

HA Proposition 1.4.3.9 (`Ω^∞ : Sp_{≥0} ⟶ S` preserves sifted colimits) is an L10 target (L10.9): its proof uses delooping in `S`.

**Colimits and compactness in stable ∞-categories** (HA Proposition 1.4.4.1, PDF p. 154). A stable ∞-category has small colimits exactly when it has small coproducts; an exact functor between such preserves small colimits exactly when it preserves small coproducts; and an object X is compact exactly when every map from X to a coproduct factors, up to homotopy, through a finite subcoproduct.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.22, 1.4.3.8, 1.1.3.4; 4.4.3.2, 4.2.3.1 (L5); 5.1.3.2 (L6); 5.3.4.5 (L6).

**Presentable stable ∞-categories** (HA Corollary 1.4.4.2, PDF pp. 155–156). A stable ∞-category is presentable exactly when it has small coproducts, `hC` is locally small, and for some regular κ it has a κ-compact generator (an X with `π₀ Map(X, Y) = ∗` only for Y zero).

*Needs:* 1.4.4.1, 1.1.3.3; 5.5.0.1, 5.5.1.1, 5.5.1.9, 5.5.2.10 (L7); 5.3.5.11 (L6); `HTT.5.4.1.7/after` (L7, locally small).

**Stabilizations of presentable ∞-categories** (HA Proposition 1.4.4.4, PDF pp. 156–157). For C, D presentable with D stable: `Sp(C)` is presentable; `Ω^∞ : Sp(C) ⟶ C` has a left adjoint `Σ^∞_+`; and an exact `G : D ⟶ Sp(C)` has a left adjoint exactly when `Ω^∞ ∘ G` does.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.25; 5.5.3.11, 5.5.3.18, 5.5.2.9 (L7); 4.4.2.9 (L5.10); 1.2.13.8 (L2).

**The universal property of `Σ^∞_+`** (HA Corollary 1.4.4.5, PDF p. 157). For C, D presentable with D stable, composition with `Σ^∞_+` is an equivalence `LFun(Sp(C), D) ⟶ LFun(C, D)` of colimit-preserving (left adjoint) functors.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.22, 1.4.4.4; 5.5.3.1 (L7, `Pr^L`); 5.5.2.9 (L7).

**The sphere spectrum** (`SSet.sphereSpectrum`, propose; `HA.1.4.4.5/after`, PDF p. 157). `𝕊 = Σ^∞(∗) ∈ Sp`, the image of the final object of `S` under `Σ^∞_+ : S ⟶ Sp`.

*Lean:* `SSet.sphereSpectrum` is the image of a final vertex of `SSet.spaces` under a chosen left adjoint of `SSet.spectra ⟶ SSet.pointedObjects S ⟶ S`, that is, of `Ω^∞` followed by forgetting the point (`Σ^∞_+`, 1.4.4.4); well defined up to equivalence. Propose.

*Needs:* 1.4.4.4, 1.4.3.1; `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**`Sp` is free on one object** (HA Corollary 1.4.4.6, PDF pp. 157–158). For D presentable stable, evaluation at 𝕊 is an equivalence `LFun(Sp, D) ⟶ D`.

*Needs:* 1.4.4.5, `HA.1.4.4.5/after`; 5.1.5.6 (L6).

**Exact reflective localizations** (HA Lemma 1.4.4.7, PDF p. 158). For C stable and `C' ⊆ C` a reflective localization with left adjoint L, L is left exact exactly when `C'` is stable.

*Needs:* 1.1.3.4, 1.1.4.1; 5.2.7.2 (L6).

**Fully faithful lifts to spectra** (HA Lemma 1.4.4.8, PDF pp. 158–159). For C stable, D with finite limits and `G : C ⟶ Sp(D)` exact with `Ω^∞ ∘ G` fully faithful, G is fully faithful.

*Needs:* 1.4.2.8, 1.1.1.9; `SSet.IsFullyFaithful` (L1.5).

**Presentable stable ∞-categories as localizations** (HA Proposition 1.4.4.9, PDF p. 159). For an ∞-category C the following are equivalent: C is presentable and stable; C is an accessible left exact reflective localization of a presentable stable ∞-category; C is an accessible left exact reflective localization of `Fun(E, Sp)` for some small E.

*Needs:* 1.4.4.4, 1.4.4.7, 1.4.4.8, 1.4.2.22, 1.4.2.9, 1.1.3.1; 5.5.1.1, 5.5.3.6 (L7).

**t-structures from colimit-closed subcategories** (HA Proposition 1.4.4.11, PDF pp. 160–163). For C presentable stable: a full subcategory `C' ⊆ C` that is presentable and closed under small colimits and extensions is `C_{≥0}` for a t-structure; and the smallest full subcategory containing a small set of objects and closed under extensions and small colimits is presentable.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HA.1.4.4.11/t-structure` (assertion (1)), `HA.1.4.4.11/cofinal` (cofinality of the compact approximations) and `HA.1.4.4.11/presentable` (assertion (2)), and this entry's own target `HA.1.4.4.11`, which is the conjunction of the two assertions.

*Proof route.* (1) is `HA.1.4.4.11/t-structure`. (2) is `HA.1.4.4.11/presentable`, Lurie's argument at the end of §1.4.4 (PDF pp. 161–163), whose cofinality step is `HA.1.4.4.11/cofinal`.

*Needs:* `HA.1.4.4.11/t-structure`, `HA.1.4.4.11/cofinal`, `HA.1.4.4.11/presentable` (below).

**Coreflective extension-closed subcategories are connective parts** (`HA.1.4.4.11/t-structure`, part 1 of 3 of t-structures from colimit-closed subcategories above; HA Proposition 1.4.4.11 (1), PDF p. 160). For C presentable stable, a full subcategory C′ that is presentable and closed under small colimits and extensions is `C_{≥0}` for a unique t-structure.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `C'_{/X} = C_{/X} ×_C C'` is presentable (5.5.3.12, with `C_{/X}` presentable by 5.5.3.10 and `C_{/X} ⟶ C` preserving colimits by 1.2.13.8), so it has a final object (5.5.2.4), and C′ is coreflective (5.2.7.8). Apply 1.2.1.16 to `C^op`, in which `C'^op` is a reflective localization closed under extensions: the t-structure it gives has `(C^op)_{≤−1} = C'^op`, that is `C_{≥1} = C'`, and shifting by one gives `C_{≥0} = C'`.

*Needs:* 1.2.1.15, 1.2.1.16; 5.5.2.4, 5.5.3.10, 5.5.3.12 (L7); 1.2.13.8 (L2.5); 5.2.7.8 (L6).

**Cofinality of the compact approximations** (`HA.1.4.4.11/cofinal`, part 2 of 3 of t-structures from colimit-closed subcategories above; HA Proposition 1.4.4.11, proof of (2), PDF pp. 162–163). With κ, `C'^κ`, C″ and D as in the proof of (2), and `f : X ⟶ Y` in D, the evaluation maps `(C'^κ[−1])_{/X} ⟵ D^κ_{/f} ⟶ (C'^κ)_{/Y}` are cofinal.

*Proof route.* Theorem A (4.1.3.1). For the first map the fibres are κ-filtered: extend a κ-small diagram by solving one lifting problem in `C_{/X}` against a trivial fibration, and factor a κ-compact colimit through a stage of a κ-filtered presentation of Y (5.3.1.20). The second map is similar, or follows because its fibres have κ-small colimits.

*Needs:* 4.1.3.1 (L5.4); 5.3.1.20, 5.3.4.5 (L6).

**Generated extension-closed subcategories are presentable** (`HA.1.4.4.11/presentable`, part 3 of 3 of t-structures from colimit-closed subcategories above; HA Proposition 1.4.4.11 (2), PDF pp. 160–163). For C presentable stable and a small set `{X_α}`, the smallest full subcategory containing every `X_α` and closed under extensions and small colimits is presentable.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. The colimit closure C″ of `C' ∩ C^κ` is κ-accessible. It contains C′ once it is closed under extensions, that is, once D is generated under colimits by `D^κ`; this follows from `HA.1.4.4.11/cofinal` with 5.3.5.8 and pointwise colimits (5.1.2.2).

*Needs:* `HA.1.4.4.11/cofinal`; 5.3.5.8, 5.1.2.2 (L6); 5.5.0.1 (L7).

**Accessible t-structures** (`SSet.TStructure.IsAccessible`; HA Definition 1.4.4.12, PDF p. 160). A t-structure on a presentable stable C is accessible when `C_{≥0}` is presentable.

*Lean:* `SSet.TStructure.IsAccessible t : Prop := SSet.IsPresentable (t.geq 0)`, for `[SSet.IsStable C]` with `SSet.IsPresentable C` as a hypothesis argument, and `t.geq 0` from 1.2.1.4.

*Needs:* 1.2.1.4; 5.5.0.1 (L7).

**Equivalent forms of accessibility** (HA Proposition 1.4.4.13, PDF p. 160). For a t-structure on a presentable stable C, the following are equivalent: `C_{≥0}` is presentable; `C_{≥0}` is accessible; `C_{≤0}` is presentable; `C_{≤0}` is accessible; `τ_{≤0} : C ⟶ C` is accessible; `τ_{≥0} : C ⟶ C` is accessible.

*Needs:* 1.4.4.12, 1.4.4.11, 1.2.1.16; 5.5.1.2, 5.5.4.5, 5.5.4.15, 5.5.4.16, 5.4.2.1 (L7).

## Layer L10: ∞-topoi

HTT §§6.1–6.2: the definition of an ∞-topos, the ∞-categorical Giraud axioms, descent, Giraud's theorem (6.1.0.6), Rezk's classifying-object characterization (6.1.6.8), left exact and topological localizations, Grothendieck topologies and sheaves on ∞-categories, effective epimorphisms and canonical topologies; also delooping in `S` (the case `X = S` of HTT 7.2.2.10–7.2.2.11) and HA Proposition 1.4.3.9, which uses it (L10.9). Groupoid objects, Čech nerves, effective groupoids and geometric realizations are L6.8's (`SSet.IsGroupoidObject`, `SSet.IsCechNerve`, `SSet.IsEffectiveGroupoid`, `SSet.IsGeometricRealization`); presheaves and the Yoneda embedding are L6's (`SSet.presheaf`, `SSet.yoneda`); presentability, local objects, strongly saturated classes and truncation are L7's (`SSet.IsPresentable`, `SSet.IsAccessibleFunctor`, `SSet.IsLocalObject`, `SSet.IsLocalEquivalence`, `SSet.IsStronglySaturated`, `SSet.IsOfSmallGeneration`, `SSet.IsTruncatedObject`, `SSet.IsTruncatedMorphism`, `SSet.IsMonomorphism`, `SSet.prL`).

Conventions for the layer:

- An ∞-topos is large: `X : SSet.{u + 1}`, since `P(C) = SSet.presheaf C` for `C : SSet.{u}` lives there (L6, *Size*). "Presentable" is `SSet.IsPresentable.{u}`, "small" means u-small, and every statement is universe-polymorphic in u.
- "Localization" in HTT §§6.1–6.2 is HTT's 5.2.7.2, the Conventions' *reflective localization* (`SSet.IsReflectiveLocalization`).
- *Left exact* is HTT's: G is left exact when `G^op` is right exact (HTT Remarks 5.3.2.2 and 5.3.2.10, the dual of 5.3.2.1 at κ = ω). The target is 5.3.2.10 (L6.6); this layer uses L6.6's `SSet.IsLeftExact`, with "preserves finite limits" as the characterization when the source has finite limits (the dual of 5.3.2.9). L7 (5.5.6.16, 5.5.6.28) already uses the word, so the definition belongs with 5.3.2.1 in L6.6.
- Grothendieck topologies on an ∞-category C are Mathlib's `GrothendieckTopology` on `hoFunctor.obj C`. This departs from HTT's sieves on the slices `C_{/C}` (6.2.2.1); HTT Remark 6.2.2.3 is the comparison target that justifies it (L10.8). Mathlib's sheafification of presheaves of sets on `hC` is then available for 6.2.2.16.
- The 1-categorical topos theory of 6.1.0.1–6.1.0.2 and 6.1.1.6 is stated with Mathlib's sites, sheaves and internal equivalence relations; Mathlib has no Giraud theorem.

Lurie cites two notions of L11 here. Remark 6.2.3.6 speaks of geometric morphisms (6.3.1.1), and Proposition 6.2.3.20 of the ∞-category `Fun^*` of left exact colimit-preserving functors (6.3.1.10). The entries below state both with the underlying condition (a left exact left adjoint; a full subcategory of `Fun` on left exact colimit-preserving functors), so no L10 target needs L11.

The items are written in the book's order. Forward needs:

- L10.1 needs L10.2, L10.3 and L10.5: the statement part `HTT.6.1.0.6/stmt` uses universal colimits (6.1.1.2), disjoint coproducts (`HTT.6.1.1.4/after`) and Cartesian transformations (6.1.3.1); Theorem 6.1.0.6 is the conjunction of its parts `1⇒2` (from 6.1.3.9 and 6.1.3.10, L10.3), `2⇒3` (6.1.3.19, L10.3) and `3⇒1` (6.1.5.3, L10.5).
- L10.1 needs L10.2: `HTT.6.1.0.1/presheaf-giraud` uses 6.1.1.6 (in `Type u` equivalence relations are effective), and 6.1.1.6 does not use 6.1.0.1. Later layers use only `HTT.6.1.0.1/stmt` and (A) ⇔ (B), so the parts on Giraud's axioms (`/presheaf-giraud` aside, which (B) ⇒ (A) uses: `/lex-giraud`, `/sheaves-giraud`, `/giraud-exact`, `/giraud-sheaves`) can be formalized last.

Inside L10.3, Proposition 6.1.3.10 uses Lemmas 6.1.3.12–6.1.3.15, stated after it. Inside L10.4, Proposition 6.1.4.2 uses Lemmas 6.1.4.3–6.1.4.8. Inside L10.8, Proposition 6.2.2.7 uses 6.2.2.9–6.2.2.15. None of these lemmas uses the statement that needs it. Formalization order: L10.2; L10.3 up to 6.1.3.9, then 6.1.3.12–6.1.3.17, then 6.1.3.10, 6.1.3.19, 6.1.3.20; L10.4 (lemmas first); L10.5; then L10.1's theorem; then L10.6–L10.10.

### L10.1 Topoi and ∞-topoi

**Giraud's theorem for ordinary topoi** (HTT Proposition 6.1.0.1, its statement part `HTT.6.1.0.1/stmt` and its parts `HTT.6.1.0.1/lex-localization`, `/lex-sheaves`, `/presheaf-giraud`, `/lex-giraud`, `/sheaves-giraud`, `/giraud-exact`, `/giraud-sheaves`, PDF pp. 546–547). For a category C with hom-sets in the universe u the following are equivalent:

- (A) C is equivalent to the category of sheaves of sets on a small site;
- (B) C is equivalent to a left exact localization of `C₀ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u` for a small category C₀: a reflective full subcategory whose reflector preserves finite limits (no accessibility is assumed; see `/lex-sheaves`);
- (C) Giraud's axioms: (i) C is presentable in the classical sense (A.1.1.2, `IsLocallyPresentable`); (ii) colimits in C are universal (stable under pullback); (iii) coproducts in C are disjoint; (iv) equivalence relations in C are effective.

The statement part defines the three conditions. The theorem is the conjunction of (A) ⇒ (B) (`/lex-localization`), (B) ⇒ (A) (`/lex-sheaves`), (A) ⇒ (C) (`/sheaves-giraud`, through `/presheaf-giraud` and `/lex-giraud`) and (C) ⇒ (A) (`/giraud-sheaves`, through `/giraud-exact`).

*Lean:* `/stmt`, for `C : Type u'` with `[Category.{u} C]` (propose all three names):

- (A) `CategoryTheory.IsSheafCategory C : Prop := ∃ (D : Type u) (_ : SmallCategory D) (J : GrothendieckTopology D), Nonempty (C ≌ Sheaf J (Type u))`;
- (B) `CategoryTheory.IsLeftExactPresheafLocalization C : Prop := ∃ (D : Type u) (_ : SmallCategory D) (i : C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (L : (Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) ⥤ C), Nonempty (L ⊣ i) ∧ Nonempty i.FullyFaithful ∧ PreservesFiniteLimits L`;
- (C) `CategoryTheory.SatisfiesGiraudAxioms C : Prop`, a structure with fields `isLocallyPresentable : IsLocallyPresentable.{u} C`; `isUniversalColimit : ∀ {J : Type u} [SmallCategory J] {F : J ⥤ C} (c : Cocone F), Nonempty (IsColimit c) → IsUniversalColimit c`; `coproductDisjoint : ∀ {ι : Type u} (X : ι → C), CoproductDisjoint X`; `isEffective : ∀ {R A : C} (p₁ p₂ : R ⟶ A), IsEquivalenceRelation p₁ p₂ → IsEffectiveEquivalenceRelation p₁ p₂` (all Mathlib notions).

The theorem: `List.TFAE [IsSheafCategory C, IsLeftExactPresheafLocalization C, SatisfiesGiraudAxioms C]`. Axiom (ii) includes the empty colimit, so initial objects are strict (`hasStrictInitial_of_isUniversal`).

**Checks.**

- `Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u` for small D satisfies (A) (every presheaf is a sheaf for `GrothendieckTopology.trivial D`) and (B) (L the identity); `Type u` is the case D = point.
- `AddCommGrpCat.{u}` satisfies (i), (iii) and (iv) but not (ii): its initial object is also final, so it is not strict.
- The poset `Fin 2` fails (iii): `1 ⊔ 1 = 1`, and the pullback of the two injections is 1, not initial.

*Proof route.* Lurie gives no proof and refers to SGA 4 (Exposé IV, §1, Théorème 1.2). The route is the classical one (SGA 4 IV.1; Mac Lane–Moerdijk, *Sheaves in Geometry and Logic*, ch. III and Appendix; Johnstone, *Sketches of an Elephant*, C2.2; Borceux, *Handbook of Categorical Algebra* vol. 3, ch. 3), split into the parts below.

*Needs:* the parts; `/stmt` needs A.1.1.2 (F1.1, `IsLocallyPresentable`) and Mathlib `GrothendieckTopology`, `Sheaf`, `IsUniversalColimit`, `CoproductDisjoint`, `IsEffectiveEquivalenceRelation`.

**Sheafification is a left exact localization** (`HTT.6.1.0.1/lex-localization`, (A) ⇒ (B)). For a small site (D, J), the inclusion of `Sheaf J (Type u)` into presheaves is fully faithful with a left adjoint, sheafification, that preserves finite limits; composing with `C ≌ Sheaf J (Type u)` gives (B) with C₀ = D.

*Lean:* `IsSheafCategory C → IsLeftExactPresheafLocalization C`.

*Proof route.* Mathlib: `sheafificationAdjunction J (Type u)`, `fullyFaithfulSheafToPresheaf J (Type u)` and the instance `PreservesFiniteLimits (presheafToSheaf J (Type u))`; compose the adjunction with the equivalence (`Adjunction.comp`, `Equivalence.toAdjunction`).

*Needs:* `/stmt`; Mathlib `Sites/Sheafification`, `Sites/LeftExact`.

**Left exact localizations of presheaves are sheaf categories** (`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.ofLeftExactReflection`; `HTT.6.1.0.1/lex-sheaves`, (B) ⇒ (A)). Let D be small, `i : C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u` fully faithful with a left adjoint L that preserves finite limits. Call a sieve S on d covering when L inverts its inclusion into `yoneda.obj d`. These sieves form a Grothendieck topology J on D, and a presheaf lies in the essential image of i exactly when it is a J-sheaf; so `C ≌ Sheaf J (Type u)`. In particular such a localization is accessible, which is HTT Remark 6.1.0.5's claim for set-valued presheaves.

*Lean:* `GrothendieckTopology.ofLeftExactReflection (adj : L ⊣ i) [i.Full] [i.Faithful] [PreservesFiniteLimits L] : GrothendieckTopology D` with `S ∈ _ d ↔ IsIso (L.map S.functorInclusion)`; the lemma `Presieve.IsSheaf (ofLeftExactReflection adj) P ↔ ∃ X, Nonempty (i.obj X ≅ P)`; and `IsLeftExactPresheafLocalization C → IsSheafCategory C`. Propose.

*Proof route.* Let W be the morphisms of presheaves that L inverts. W is `ObjectProperty.isLocal (· ∈ Set.range i.obj)` (Mathlib `ObjectProperty.isLocal_iff_isIso_map`), so with the unit (`isLocal_adj_unit_app`) a presheaf is in the essential image of i exactly when it is W-local. W has 2-out-of-3, is stable under pullback (L preserves pullbacks) and contains every colimit of members (L preserves colimits).

1. J is a topology. The maximal sieve covers. Stability: the inclusion of `S.pullback f` is the pullback of S's inclusion along `yoneda.map f`. Transitivity: let `S ∈ J d` and R a sieve with `R.pullback f` covering for every `f ∈ S`. Since colimits of presheaves are universal (`/presheaf-giraud`), `R ⊓ S ⟶ S` is the colimit, over the arrows `f : e ⟶ d` of S, of the inclusions `R.pullback f ⟶ yoneda.obj e`, so it lies in W; hence so does `R ⊓ S ⟶ yoneda.obj d`. The map `R ⊓ S ⟶ R` is a pullback of S's inclusion, hence in W, and 2-out-of-3 puts R's inclusion in W.
2. Local ⇒ sheaf: covering sieves' inclusions lie in W, and the sheaf condition for S is locality for its inclusion (`Presieve.isSheafFor_iff_bijective_shrinkFunctor_ι_comp`, or `isSheafFor_iff_yonedaSheafCondition`).
3. Sheaf ⇒ local. Let P be a J-sheaf and `w : A ⟶ B` in W. (a) If w is mono, then for each element `b : yoneda.obj d ⟶ B` the pullback of w along b is a sieve inverted by L, hence covering. So a map `A ⟶ P` gives a matching family on each such sieve, which glues uniquely; the glued elements are natural in b. So P is local for w (Mac Lane–Moerdijk V.3: a sheaf for the associated Lawvere–Tierney topology is local for the dense monos). (b) In general, factor `w = e ≫ m` with e epi and m mono (presheaf images). L preserves epis (left adjoint) and monos (left exact). `L.map m` is mono and, since `L.map w` is iso, split epi, so it is iso: `m ∈ W`, and `e ∈ W` by 2-out-of-3. The diagonal `δ : A ⟶ A ×_{Im} A` is mono and L inverts it (L preserves the kernel pair of e and inverts e), so P is local for δ by (a). Both projections retract δ, so every `g : A ⟶ P` coequalizes the kernel pair of e and factors uniquely through e (epis of presheaves are regular: Mathlib's `IsRegularEpiCategory` instance for functor categories). With (a) for m, P is local for w.
4. So the essential image of i is the J-sheaves, and C is equivalent to it (i fully faithful), hence to `Sheaf J (Type u)` (`sheafToPresheaf` is fully faithful).

*Needs:* `/stmt`, `/presheaf-giraud`; Mathlib `ObjectProperty.isLocal_iff_isIso_map`, `isLocal_adj_unit_app`, `Sieve.functorInclusion`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_iff_bijective_shrinkFunctor_ι_comp`, `IsRegularEpiCategory` for functor categories (`Functor/RegularEpi`).

**Presheaf categories satisfy Giraud's axioms** (`HTT.6.1.0.1/presheaf-giraud`). For a small category D, `Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u` satisfies (C). (i) is Mathlib. (ii)–(iv) hold in `Type u` and pass to presheaves objectwise, since limits and colimits of presheaves are computed objectwise.

*Lean:* `SatisfiesGiraudAxioms (Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)`, from the `Type u` lemmas `Types.isUniversalColimit` (every colimit cocone of a small diagram is universal) and `Types.coproductDisjoint`, with the objectwise transfer `isUniversalColimit_of_evaluation` (the analogue of Mathlib's `isVanKampenColimit_of_evaluation`), and the same for `CoproductDisjoint` and `IsEffectiveEquivalenceRelation`. Propose all four.

*Proof route.* In `Type u`, base change along `f : Y ⟶ colim F` preserves colimits, either elementwise or because base change in `Type u` has a right adjoint (dependent product). The injections of a sigma type are injective with pairwise disjoint ranges. Effectivity is 6.1.1.6. The van Kampen property holds only for special colimits (pushouts along monos, coproducts); universality is the weaker property that (ii) asks for.

*Needs:* `/stmt`; 6.1.1.6 (L10.2); Mathlib `IsLocallyPresentable` instance for presheaves (`Presentable/Presheaf`), `evaluationJointlyReflectsColimits`, `isVanKampenColimit_of_evaluation` (as the pattern).

**Giraud's axioms (ii)–(iv) pass to left exact localizations** (`HTT.6.1.0.1/lex-giraud`). Let P have small colimits and finite limits and satisfy (ii)–(iv), and let `i : E ⥤ P` be fully faithful with a left adjoint L that preserves finite limits. Then E satisfies (ii)–(iv).

*Lean:* under `(adj : L ⊣ i) [i.Full] [i.Faithful] [PreservesFiniteLimits L]`, three lemmas whose conclusions are the fields `isUniversalColimit`, `coproductDisjoint`, `isEffective` of `SatisfiesGiraudAxioms` for E. Propose.

*Proof route.* A colimit in E of F is L of the colimit in P of `F ⋙ i`, since `i ⋙ L ≅ 𝟭`; limits in E are computed in P (i is a right adjoint). (ii) is Mathlib's `IsUniversalColimit.map_reflective` with `IsUniversalColimit.of_iso`. (iii): a colimit cofan in E is L of the coproduct of the `i.obj X_j`; L preserves pullbacks, monos and initial objects, so the injections are mono and the pullback of two distinct ones is initial. (iv): i carries an equivalence relation `R ⇉ A` to one on `i.obj A` (the axioms are finite-limit conditions: `ReflexiveRelation.map` and its symmetric and transitive companions); its quotient `q : i.obj A ⟶ Q` in P has kernel pair `i.obj R`; then `L.map q`, composed with the counit, is a coequalizer of `R ⇉ A` (L preserves colimits) whose kernel pair is `L.obj (i.obj R) ≅ R` (L preserves pullbacks).

*Needs:* `/stmt`; Mathlib `IsUniversalColimit.map_reflective`, `IsUniversalColimit.of_iso`, `EffectiveEquivalenceRelation`.

**Sheaf categories satisfy Giraud's axioms** (`HTT.6.1.0.1/sheaves-giraud`, (A) ⇒ (C)). For a small site (D, J), `Sheaf J (Type u)` satisfies (C), and so does every category equivalent to it.

*Lean:* `SatisfiesGiraudAxioms (Sheaf J (Type u))`, `SatisfiesGiraudAxioms.of_equivalence (e : C ≌ C')`, and `IsSheafCategory C → SatisfiesGiraudAxioms C`. Propose.

*Proof route.* (ii)–(iv): `/lex-giraud` applied to `/lex-localization` and `/presheaf-giraud`. (i): J-sheaves are the presheaves local for the small class W of covering-sieve inclusions `(Sieve.shrinkFunctor S).ι` (`Presieve.isSheafFor_iff_bijective_shrinkFunctor_ι_comp`, `isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type`). Choose a regular κ with `HasCardinalLT (Arrow D) κ`. Representables are κ-presentable (`Presentable/Presheaf`), and so is each sieve, as a colimit of representables indexed by its category of elements (`isCardinalPresentable_of_isColimit`). Then Mathlib's `MorphismProperty.isLocallyPresentable_isLocal` applies, and `Equivalence.isLocallyPresentable` transports it. Invariance under equivalence: equivalences preserve and reflect limits, colimits, monos, initial objects and the three notions. Mathlib's instances `FinitaryExtensive`, `Balanced`, `IsRegularEpiCategory` on `Sheaf J (Type u)` are consistency checks.

*Needs:* `/lex-localization`, `/lex-giraud`, `/presheaf-giraud`; Mathlib `MorphismProperty.isLocallyPresentable_isLocal`, `isCardinalPresentable_of_isColimit`, `Equivalence.isLocallyPresentable`.

**Exactness of Giraud categories** (`HTT.6.1.0.1/giraud-exact`). Let C satisfy (C). Then C has finite limits and a strict initial object; every mono is regular, so C is balanced; every epi is effective, so `IsRegularEpiCategory C`; epis are stable under pullback, so C is `Regular`; and every small jointly epimorphic family `(X_a ⟶ Y)_a` is a universal effective epimorphic family.

*Lean:* `SatisfiesGiraudAxioms C →` `HasFiniteLimits C`, `HasStrictInitialObjects C`, `Balanced C`, `IsRegularEpiCategory C`, `Regular C`, and the family statement through `EffectiveEpiFamily` and pullbacks. Propose.

*Proof route.*

1. Finite limits: a locally presentable category is complete (Adámek–Rosický, ch. 1); supply it if Mathlib lacks it. Strict initial object: `hasStrictInitial_of_isUniversal`.
2. Monos are regular. For `m : A ⟶ B` mono, the relation on `B ⊔ B` given by the diagonal together with the two copies of A mapped by `(ι₁ m, ι₂ m)` and `(ι₂ m, ι₁ m)` is a monomorphism into `(B ⊔ B) ⨯ (B ⊔ B)` and an equivalence relation. Both facts are checked summand by summand, using that coproducts are universal and disjoint and that m is mono. By (iv) it is effective. Its quotient is `B ⊔_A B`, and the pullback of the two maps `B ⟶ B ⊔_A B` is A, so m is their equalizer. A mono and epi is then iso.
3. Epis are effective. For f epi, its kernel pair is an equivalence relation (`IsKernelPair.equivalenceRelation`), effective by (iv), with quotient q whose kernel pair is the same. Then `f = q ≫ m`, and m is mono: `q × q` is epi (a composite of base changes of the coequalizer q, universal by (ii)), and both maps `Q ×_Y Q ⟶ Q` agree after precomposing with it. So m is mono and epi, hence iso by 2.
4. Pullback-stability of (regular) epis is (ii) for the coequalizer diagram, giving `Regular C` with 1 and 3.
5. Families: `(X_a ⟶ Y)_a` is jointly epi exactly when `∐ X_a ⟶ Y` is epi. Then 3 and the universality of coproducts and coequalizers make the family effective epimorphic after any base change (Mathlib `EffectiveEpiFamily`, `Sieve.effectiveEpimorphic_family`).

*Needs:* `/stmt`; Mathlib `hasStrictInitial_of_isUniversal`, `IsKernelPair.equivalenceRelation`, `Regular`, `EffectiveEpiFamily`, `CoproductDisjoint`.

**Giraud categories are sheaf categories** (`HTT.6.1.0.1/giraud-sheaves`, (C) ⇒ (A)). Let C satisfy (C), and let `ι : D ⥤ C` be the inclusion of a small full subcategory whose objects separate maps (for example a small skeleton of the κ-presentable objects). With the topology induced on D by the canonical topology of C, C is equivalent to `Sheaf J (Type u)`.

*Lean:* `SatisfiesGiraudAxioms C → IsSheafCategory C`, with J := `ι.inducedTopology (canonicalTopology C)`, the equivalence `(canonicalTopology C).yoneda ⋙ (Functor.IsDenseSubsite.sheafEquiv ι J (canonicalTopology C) (Type u)).inverse : C ⥤ Sheaf J (Type u)`, and the lemma `mem_canonicalTopology_iff`: `S ∈ canonicalTopology C X ↔ ∀ {Y} (f : Y ⟶ X), (S.pullback f).EffectiveEpimorphic` (propose; from `finestTopology` and `Sieve.EffectiveEpimorphic.iff_forall_isSheafFor_yoneda`).

*Proof route.* Write K for `canonicalTopology C` and Φ for `K.yoneda : C ⥤ Sheaf K (Type u)`.

1. Generators: from `IsLocallyPresentable.{u} C` choose κ with `IsCardinalLocallyPresentable C κ`; the κ-presentable objects are essentially small and dense (`Presentable/Dense`), hence separating; take D a small skeleton of them.
2. Cover-density: for each X, the maps `ι.obj d ⟶ X` form a small jointly epimorphic family, so by `/giraud-exact` 5 and `mem_canonicalTopology_iff` their sieve (`Sieve.coverByImage ι X`) is K-covering: `ι.IsCoverDense K`. Mathlib then gives `ι.IsDenseSubsite J K` and the comparison equivalence `E : Sheaf J (Type u) ≌ Sheaf K (Type u)`, since `StructuredArrow X ι.op` is u-small. Through E, `Sheaf K (Type u)` has small colimits, epis are its locally surjective maps, and it is a balanced regular-epi category (Mathlib's instances on `Sheaf J (Type u)`).
3. Φ is fully faithful (`GrothendieckTopology.yonedaFullyFaithful`, K subcanonical) and preserves limits. It remains to show Φ essentially surjective.
4. Φ preserves small coproducts. The injections of `∐ X_i` form a covering family with initial pairwise pullbacks (iii), and the empty sieve covers the strict initial object, so every K-sheaf takes `∐ X_i` to `∏ F(X_i)` (Mathlib `Presieve.isSheafFor_sigmaDesc_iff`, `Sites/CoproductSheafCondition`).
5. Φ preserves quotients of equivalence relations. For an effective relation `R ⇉ X` with quotient q, the sieve of q covers (q is a universal effective epi, `/giraud-exact`), so `Φ R ⇉ Φ X ⟶ Φ Q` is a coequalizer (Tau Ceti `IsKernelPair.isColimitYonedaCofork`). Likewise Φ carries epis of C to epis of `Sheaf K`, since their sieves cover.
6. Subsheaves of `Φ Z` come from subobjects of Z. Let `G ⟶ Φ Z` be mono. Cover G by `Φ W ⟶ G` epi, with W a coproduct of objects `ι.obj d` over the elements of G (2 and 4). The composite `Φ W ⟶ Φ Z` is `Φ w`; factor `w = e ≫ n` (regular epi, then mono) in C (`Regular`); then `Φ e` is epi and `Φ n` mono (5, 3), and uniqueness of epi–mono factorizations gives `G ≅ Φ (image of w)` over `Φ Z`.
7. Essential surjectivity. For a K-sheaf F, take an epi `π : Φ X₀ ⟶ F` with X₀ a coproduct of objects `ι.obj d` over the elements of F (2, 4). Its kernel pair is a subsheaf of `Φ X₀ ⨯ Φ X₀ ≅ Φ (X₀ ⨯ X₀)`, so it is `Φ R'` for a subobject `R' ⟶ X₀ ⨯ X₀` (6). R' is an equivalence relation, since Φ is fully faithful and preserves finite limits, so it reflects the relation axioms. By (iv), R' is effective with quotient `q : X₀ ⟶ Q`. By 5, `Φ q` is a coequalizer of `Φ R' ⇉ Φ X₀`, and so is π (a regular epi, coequalizer of its kernel pair). Hence `F ≅ Φ Q`.
8. So Φ is an equivalence, and `C ≌ Sheaf K (Type u) ≌ Sheaf J (Type u)` (E.symm): C satisfies (A) with the small site (D, J).

**Giraud's theorem** (HTT Theorem 6.1.0.6, its statement part `HTT.6.1.0.6/stmt` and its parts `HTT.6.1.0.6/1⇒2`, `HTT.6.1.0.6/2⇒3`, `HTT.6.1.0.6/3⇒1`, PDF pp. 547–548). For an ∞-category X the following are equivalent:

### L10.2 Giraud's axioms in the ∞-categorical setting

**The codomain fibration and pullbacks** (`SSet.arrowTarget`; HTT Lemma 6.1.1.1, PDF p. 549). For an ∞-category X let `O_X = Fun(Δ[1], X)` and `p : O_X ⟶ X` evaluation at the vertex 1; p is a coCartesian fibration (2.4.7.12). An edge of `O_X`, that is a square `Δ[1] × Δ[1] ⟶ X`, is p-Cartesian exactly when the square is a pullback. Hence p is a Cartesian fibration exactly when X has pullbacks.

*Lean:* `SSet.arrowTarget X : (ihom Δ[1]).obj X ⟶ X`, evaluation at `1` (propose); the lemma as `(SSet.Edge.IsCartesian F (arrowTarget X)) ↔ SSet.IsPullback σ_F` and `CartesianFibration (arrowTarget X) ↔` every cospan has a pullback.

*Needs:* 2.4.7.12 (L3); 2.4.1.1 (L3.5, `SSet.Edge.IsCartesian`); 2.4.2.1 (L3.6); 2.1.3.4 (L2); `SSet.IsPullback` (4.4.2.1, L5.10).

**Universal colimits** (`SSet.HasUniversalColimits`; `HTT.6.1.1/intro`, HTT Definition 6.1.1.2, PDF pp. 548–550). The introduction of §6.1.1 recalls the classical notion: colimits in a category with pullbacks are universal when pulling back along any morphism preserves them. For a presentable ∞-category C and a morphism `f : T ⟶ S`, restricting `O_C ⟶ C` to f gives a Cartesian and coCartesian fibration over `Δ[1]` whose associated functors are composition with f, `C_{/T} ⟶ C_{/S}`, and its right adjoint, the pullback functor `f^* : C_{/S} ⟶ C_{/T}`. Colimits in C are universal when every such `f^*` preserves small colimits.

*Lean:* `SSet.HasUniversalColimits X hX` for a quasicategory X with `hX : IsPresentable X` as a hypothesis argument (so that `arrowTarget X` is a Cartesian fibration, by 6.1.1.1 and 5.5.2.4): `HasUniversalColimits X (hX : IsPresentable X) := ∀ f : Δ[1] ⟶ X, haveI : CartesianFibration (pullback.snd (arrowTarget X) f) := ‹6.1.1.1 + 5.5.2.4›; ∀ C D h₀ h₁ g, IsCategoricalEquivalence h₀ → IsCategoricalEquivalence h₁ → IsAssociated _ h₀ h₁ g → PreservesSmallColimits g` (5.2.1.1, L6.4; `IsAssociated` takes the Cartesian fibration instance, and h₀, h₁ are quantified), with `PreservesSmallColimits` for diagrams indexed by `K : SSet.{u}` (`SSet.PreservesColimit`). Propose. The 1-categorical notion of the introduction is Mathlib's `IsUniversalColimit`, used in 6.1.0.1.

**Checks.** `S` has universal colimits (6.1.3.14). The characterization by Cartesian transformations is 6.1.3.3.

*Needs:* 6.1.1.1; 5.2.1.1 (L6.4); 5.5.0.1, 5.5.2.4 (L7.5); `SSet.PreservesColimit` (L5.6).

**Universal colimits through classifying functors** (HTT Proposition 6.1.1.4, PDF p. 551). For an ∞-category X with finite limits, X is presentable with universal colimits exactly when the Cartesian fibration `O_X ⟶ X` is classified by a functor `X^op ⟶ Pr^L`: every slice `X_{/U}` is presentable and every pullback functor preserves small colimits.

*Lean:* the classifying map of `arrowTarget X` (`SSet.ClassifiesCartesianFibration`, 3.3.2.2) factors through `SSet.prL` exactly when `∃ hX : IsPresentable X, HasUniversalColimits X hX`.

*Proof route.* For the converse, X has a final object 1 and `X ≃ X_{/1}`.

*Needs:* 6.1.1.1, 6.1.1.2; 3.3.2.2 (L4.7); 5.5.3.1 (L7.5, `SSet.prL`); 5.5.3.10 (L7.5, slices); `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**Disjoint coproducts** (`SSet.HasDisjointCoproducts`; `HTT.6.1.1.4/after`, PDF pp. 551–552). For an ∞-category with finite coproducts, coproducts are disjoint when every pushout square with initial upper-left corner, `∅ ⟶ X`, `∅ ⟶ Y`, `X ⟶ X ⊔ Y ⟵ Y`, is also a pullback. The same prose recalls effective equivalence relations and effective epimorphisms of ordinary categories (Mathlib's `IsEffectiveEquivalenceRelation`); their ∞-categorical replacements are effective groupoids (6.1.2.14) and effective epimorphisms (6.2.3.5).

*Lean:* `SSet.HasDisjointCoproducts X := ∀ σ : Δ[1] ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ X, SSet.IsInitialVertex (squareVertex σ 0 0) → SSet.IsPushout σ → SSet.IsPullback σ`. Propose.

**Checks.** In `S` coproducts are disjoint (6.1.3.19 applied to `S`). In the nerve of the poset `{0 < 1}` they are not: `1 ⊔ 1 = 1`, and the pullback of `1 ⟶ 1 ⟵ 1` is 1, not initial.

*Needs:* `SSet.IsInitialVertex` (L1.5); `SSet.IsPushout`, `SSet.IsPullback` (4.4.2.1, L5.10).

**Sets** (HTT Fact 6.1.1.6, PDF p. 553). In `Type u` every equivalence relation is effective, and the effective epimorphisms are exactly the surjections.

*Lean:* `IsEffectiveEquivalenceRelation p₁ p₂` for every `IsEquivalenceRelation p₁ p₂` in `Type u`, and `EffectiveEpi f ↔ Function.Surjective f` for `f : X ⟶ Y` in `Type u`; supply whichever Mathlib lacks.

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.EquivalenceRelation`, `EffectiveEpi`, `Setoid`.

### L10.3 Descent

**Cartesian transformations** (`SSet.IsCartesianTransformation`; HTT Definition 6.1.3.1, PDF p. 562). For an ∞-category X and diagrams `p, q : K ⟶ X`, a natural transformation `α : p ⟶ q` (a map `K ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ X`) is Cartesian when, for every edge `φ : x ⟶ y` of K, the square `p(x) ⟶ p(y)` over `q(x) ⟶ q(y)` is a pullback.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsCartesianTransformation (α : K ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ X) := ∀ φ : K _⦋1⦌, SSet.IsPullback ((yonedaEquiv.symm φ ▷ Δ[1]) ≫ α)`, the edge φ in the first coordinate and the transformation in the second, so that the corner `(0, 0)` is `p(x)`. Propose.

**Checks.** The identity transformation of any diagram is Cartesian; every transformation of diagrams indexed by a discrete K is Cartesian.

*Needs:* `SSet.IsPullback` (L5.10); 1.2.7.2.

**Cartesian transformations over a cone** (HTT Lemma 6.1.3.2, PDF p. 562). For diagrams `p, q : K ⋄ Δ[0] ⟶ X` indexed by the fat right cone (4.2.1), a transformation whose restriction to each `{x} ⋄ Δ[0]` is Cartesian is Cartesian.

*Needs:* 6.1.3.1; 4.4.2.1 (L5.10); `SSet.fatJoin` (L5.5).

**Universal colimits through Cartesian transformations** (HTT Lemma 6.1.3.3, PDF p. 563). For a presentable ∞-category X the following are equivalent: (1) colimits in X are universal; (5) for every Cartesian transformation `ᾱ : p̄ ⟶ q̄` of diagrams `K^▷ ⟶ X`, if q̄ is a colimit diagram so is p̄. Conditions (2)–(4) are intermediate reformulations, through diagrams of slices and the fat join (4.2.1.2, 1.2.13.8), and are part of the target.

*Needs:* 6.1.1.1, 6.1.1.2, 6.1.3.1, 6.1.3.2; 3.1.2.1 (L4); 4.2.1.2 (L5.5); 1.2.13.8 (L2).

**Classes stable under pullback** (`SSet.IsStableUnderPullback`, `SSet.arrowsIn`, `SSet.cartesianArrowsIn`; HTT Notation 6.1.3.4, PDF p. 564). For an ∞-category X with pullbacks, a class S of morphisms is stable under pullback when every pullback of a member is a member. `O^S_X` is the full subcategory of `O_X` on S, and `O^{(S)}_X` the subcategory with the same objects whose morphisms are the pullback squares. Evaluation at 1 restricts to a Cartesian fibration `O^S_X ⟶ X` and to a right fibration `O^{(S)}_X ⟶ X` (2.4.2.5).

*Lean:* for S a predicate on edges of X: `SSet.IsStableUnderPullback S`; `SSet.arrowsIn S` (`SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory` of `Fun(Δ[1], X)`); `SSet.cartesianArrowsIn S` (an HTT 1.2.11 subcategory, L1.3). Propose. The fibration instances of `arrowsIn S` and `cartesianArrowsIn S` are not yet declared, since they need X to have pullbacks; they must be added with that hypothesis.

*Needs:* 6.1.1.1; 2.4.2.5 (L3.6); `HTT.1.2.11/intro`; `SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory`.

**Descent along a colimit diagram** (HTT Lemma 6.1.3.5, PDF p. 564). Let X be presentable with universal colimits, S stable under pullback, and `q̄ : K^▷ ⟶ X` a small colimit diagram. Equivalent: (1) the classifying map `X^op ⟶ Cat∞^` of `O^S_X ⟶ X`, composed with q̄, is a limit diagram; (2) the same for the classifying map `X^op ⟶ Ŝ` of `O^{(S)}_X ⟶ X`; (3) for every transformation `ᾱ : p̄ ⟶ q̄` of colimit diagrams whose restriction to K is Cartesian with components in S, ᾱ is Cartesian and its component at the cone point lies in S.

*Needs:* 6.1.3.3, 6.1.3.4; 3.3.3.1, 3.3.3.3 (L5); 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); 3.3.2.2 (L4.7).

**Maps into an initial object** (HTT Lemma 6.1.3.6, PDF p. 565). In a presentable ∞-category with universal colimits, an object admitting a morphism to an initial object is initial.

*Proof route.* The pullback functor along `X ⟶ ∅` preserves limits (a right adjoint) and colimits (universality), so it carries the object `id_∅`, both initial and final in `X_{/∅}`, to an object both initial and final; conclude with 1.2.13.8.

*Needs:* 6.1.1.2; 1.2.13.8 (L2); `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`.

**Local classes** (`SSet.IsLocalClass`; HTT Lemma 6.1.3.7, Definition 6.1.3.8, PDF pp. 565–566). Let X be presentable with universal colimits and S stable under pullback. Equivalent (6.1.3.7): (1) the classifying map `X^op ⟶ Cat∞^` of `O^S_X ⟶ X` carries colimits in X to limits; (2) the same for `O^{(S)}_X ⟶ X` and `Ŝ`; (3) S is stable under small coproducts (in `Fun(Δ[1], X)`), and for every pushout square in `O_X` with corners `f ⟶ g`, `f ⟶ f'`, `g ⟶ g'`, `f' ⟶ g'`, if the two edges out of f are Cartesian transformations and `f, f', g ∈ S`, then the two edges into `g'` are Cartesian and `g' ∈ S`. S is *local* when it is stable under pullback and these hold (6.1.3.8).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsLocalClass S` for X with `hX : IsPresentable X` and `HasUniversalColimits X hX` as hypothesis arguments: `IsStableUnderPullback S` and condition (3) (propose; the elementary form, with no classifying maps); (1) and (2) are the characterizations of 6.1.3.7.

**Checks.** The class of equivalences is local in any presentable X with universal colimits: it is stable under pullback and coproducts, a pushout of equivalences is an equivalence, and a square whose two parallel edges are equivalences is a pullback.

*Needs:* 6.1.3.4, 6.1.3.5, 6.1.3.6; 4.4.2.5, 4.4.2.6 (L5.10); 3.3.2.2 (L4.7).

**Descent** (HTT Theorem 6.1.3.9, PDF p. 566). For a presentable ∞-category X the following are equivalent: (1) colimits in X are universal, and in every pushout square of `O_X` as in 6.1.3.7 (3) whose edges out of the initial corner are Cartesian, the edges into the final corner are Cartesian; (2) colimits are universal and the class of all morphisms is local; (3) `O_X ⟶ X` is classified by a limit-preserving functor `X^op ⟶ Pr^L`; (4) condition (2) of 6.1.0.6 (`SSet.HasDescent X`).

*Needs:* 6.1.1.4, 6.1.3.3, 6.1.3.5, 6.1.3.7.

**∞-topoi satisfy descent** (HTT Proposition 6.1.3.10, PDF pp. 566–567; with 6.1.3.9 this is `HTT.6.1.0.6/1⇒2`). An ∞-topos has universal colimits, and satisfies the pushout condition (1) of 6.1.3.9.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: call X *good* when both hold; `S` is good (6.1.3.14); goodness passes to `Fun(K, X)` for small K (colimits and pullbacks are pointwise, 5.1.2.2), hence to `P(C)`; and to accessible left exact reflective localizations (6.1.3.15 for universality; the pushout condition by applying the localization to a colimit computed upstairs).

*Needs:* 6.1.0.4, 6.1.3.9, 6.1.3.14, 6.1.3.15; 5.1.2.2 (L6.1); 5.2.7.4 (L6.5).

**Pushouts of homotopy Cartesian squares of simplicial sets** (HTT Lemma 6.1.3.12, PDF p. 567). In the category of arrows of `SSet`, take a pushout square with corners φ, ψ, φ′, ψ′ in which the maps `p : φ ⟶ ψ` and `q : φ ⟶ φ′` are homotopy Cartesian and q is a cofibration. Then p′ and q′ are homotopy Cartesian, and a map `r : ψ′ ⟶ θ` is homotopy Cartesian as soon as `r ∘ p′` and `r ∘ q′` are.

*Proof route.* Replace the arrows by minimal Kan fibrations, where homotopy Cartesian means Cartesian.

*Needs:* 2.3.3.1 (L3.3, minimal fibrations); `HTT.A.2.7/kan-fibrations`, `HTT.A.2.7/model-structure` (F2.4).

**Overcategories of a simplicial model category** (HTT Lemma 6.1.3.13, PDF pp. 567–568). For a simplicial model category A and a fibrant-cofibrant Z, the map `N((A°)_{/Z}) ⟶ N(A°)_{/Z}` from the nerve of fibrant-cofibrant objects of `A_{/Z}` (induced model structure) is a categorical equivalence.

*Needs:* A.3.1.5 (F3.3); A.2.1.1 (F1.4); 2.2.2.7 (L2.8, `Hom^R` of a simplicial nerve); 1.1.5.14 (L1.5).

**Descent in `S`** (HTT Lemma 6.1.3.14, PDF pp. 568–569). Colimits in `S` are universal, and `S` satisfies the pushout condition (1) of 6.1.3.9.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Universality: for a Kan fibration `f : X ⟶ Y`, compare `S_{/X} ⟶ S_{/Y}` with the nerve of `f_! : SSet_{/X} ⟶ SSet_{/Y}` through 6.1.3.13; `f^*` is left Quillen because the Kan–Quillen model structure is right proper, so 5.2.4.6 gives the adjoints. The pushout condition: rectify to a strictly commuting square in `Kan` (4.2.4.4) and apply 6.1.3.12 with 4.2.4.1.

*Needs:* 6.1.3.12, 6.1.3.13; 5.2.4.6 (L6.4); 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4 (L5.7); A.2.4.1 (F1.5, proper model categories); `HTT.A.2.7/model-properties` (F2.4, Kan–Quillen is right proper); `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions`; 1.2.16.1.

**Universal colimits pass to left exact localizations** (HTT Lemma 6.1.3.15, PDF pp. 569–570). If X is presentable with universal colimits and `L : X ⟶ Y` is an accessible left exact reflective localization, colimits in Y are universal.

*Proof route.* Through characterization (5) of 6.1.3.3 (Lurie's text says "Lemma 6.1.3.2"): lift a Cartesian transformation along the right adjoint, take colimits in X, and push back with L.

*Needs:* 6.1.3.3; 5.2.7.4 (L6.5); `SSet.IsLeftExact`.

**Augmented simplicial objects with an extra degeneracy direction** (HTT Lemma 6.1.3.16, PDF pp. 571–572). Let `Δ_∞` be the category of finite linearly ordered sets J with morphisms `J ∪ {∞} ⟶ J′ ∪ {∞}` order-preserving and fixing ∞. An augmented simplicial object of an ∞-category X that extends to `N(Δ_∞)^op ⟶ X` is a colimit diagram.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.6.1.3.16/cofinality` (cofinal subposets of pairs) and `HTT.6.1.3.16/left-kan` (the left Kan extension step), and this entry's own target `HTT.6.1.3.16`, which chains them with 4.3.2.7.

*Lean:* `SimplexCategory.infty` (propose) as a Mathlib category with the functor from `AugmentedSimplexCategory`; the statement through `SSet.IsGeometricRealization`.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.3.16/cofinality`, `HTT.6.1.3.16/left-kan` (below); 6.1.2.2, 6.1.2.12 (L6.8); 4.3.2.7 (L5.9).

**Cofinal subposets of pairs** (`HTT.6.1.3.16/cofinality`, part 1 of 2 of the lemma on augmented simplicial objects with an extra degeneracy direction above; HTT Lemma 6.1.3.16, cofinality steps of the proof, PDF pp. 571–572). Let P be the category of pairs `(J, J₊)`, J finite linearly ordered and `J₊ ⊆ J` upward closed, with order-preserving maps respecting `J₊`, and let `P ⟶ Δ_∞` send `(J, J₊)` to `J − J₊`. The full subcategory where `J₊ = ∅` is `Δ₊`, and its intersection with `J ≠ ∅` is Δ. On opposites, the inclusion of Δ (the pairs with `J₊ = ∅` and `J ≠ ∅`) into the pairs with `J ≠ ∅` is cofinal, and so is the inclusion of the pairs with `J = J₊` into those with `J₊ ≠ ∅`. A constant diagram indexed by `N(Δ₊)^op`, or by a category with weakly contractible nerve, is a colimit diagram of its value.

*Proof route.* Theorem A (4.1.3.1): each relevant comma category has an explicit final object, `(J, ∅) ⟶ (J, J₊)` and `(J₊, J₊) ⟶ (J, J₊)` respectively; 4.4.4.10 for Δ.

*Needs:* 4.1.3.1 (L5.4); 4.4.4.10 (L5.10).

**The left Kan extension step** (`HTT.6.1.3.16/left-kan`, part 2 of 2 of the lemma on augmented simplicial objects with an extra degeneracy direction above; HTT Lemma 6.1.3.16, Kan extension step of the proof, PDF pp. 571–572). For `F : N(Δ_∞)^op ⟶ X` and `F'` its composite with `N(P)^op ⟶ N(Δ_∞)^op`, the restriction of `F'` to the pairs with `J ≠ ∅` is left Kan extended from the pairs with `J₊ ≠ ∅`.

*Proof route.* For `(J, ∅)`, the subcategory of maps `(J, ∅) ⟶ (J', J'₊)` with `J ≅ J' − J'₊` is cofinal (Theorem A, with an explicit final factorization), and the diagram on it is constant, indexed by `N(Δ₊)^op`.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.3.16/cofinality`; 4.1.3.1 (L5.4); 4.3.2.7 (L5.9); 4.4.4.10 (L5.10).

**Shifted simplicial objects** (HTT Lemma 6.1.3.17, PDF pp. 572–573). For a simplicial object U of X, let U′ be the augmented simplicial object `J ↦ U(J ⊔ {∞})`. Then U′ is a colimit diagram, and when U is a groupoid object the evident transformation from `U′|N(Δ)^op` to U is Cartesian.

*Needs:* 6.1.3.1, 6.1.3.16; `HTT.6.1.2.6/pullback`, 6.1.2.7 (L6.8, condition (4″)); 4.4.2.1 (L5.10).

**Descent implies the Giraud axioms** (HTT Proposition 6.1.3.19, PDF pp. 573–574; this is `HTT.6.1.0.6/2⇒3`). A presentable ∞-category satisfying the conditions of 6.1.3.9 satisfies the Giraud axioms (3) of 6.1.0.6.

*Proof route.* Disjointness from a pushout in `O_X` of `id_∅` with Cartesian edges (6.1.3.6). Effectiveness: compare a groupoid U, its colimit `Ū`, and the shift `U′` of 6.1.3.17; descent makes the transformation `U′ ⟶ Ū` Cartesian, and the resulting square with corners `U₁`, `U₀`, `U₀`, `Ū` (the two face maps `U₁ ⟶ U₀` and the map `U₀ ⟶ Ū` on both sides) is a pullback, so U is effective by 6.1.2.11.

*Needs:* 6.1.3.6, 6.1.3.9, 6.1.3.17; 6.1.2.7, 6.1.2.11, 6.1.2.14 (L6.8).

**Groupoid objects of `S` are effective** (HTT Corollary 6.1.3.20, PDF p. 574).

*Proof route.* 6.1.3.14 gives condition (1) of 6.1.3.9 for `S` (presentable by 5.5.1.8); apply 6.1.3.19.

*Needs:* 6.1.3.9, 6.1.3.14, 6.1.3.19; 5.5.1.8 (L7.5).

### L10.4 Free groupoids

**Left exactness at an object** (`SSet.IsLeftExactAt`; HTT Definition 6.1.4.1, PDF p. 574). For a functor `f : X ⟶ Y` between ∞-categories with finite limits and an object Z of X, f is left exact at Z when it carries every pullback square in X with final corner Z to a pullback square.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsLeftExactAt f Z := ∀ σ : Δ[1] ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ X, squareVertex σ 1 1 = Z → IsPullback σ → IsPullback (σ ≫ f)`. Propose.

**Checks.** A left exact functor is left exact at every object.

*Needs:* `SSet.IsPullback` (L5.10).

**Groupoid objects under functors left exact at `U₀`** (HTT Lemma 6.1.4.3, PDF p. 575). If `f : X ⟶ Y` (both with finite limits) is left exact at `U₀` and U is a groupoid object of X, then `f ∘ U` is a groupoid object of Y.

*Needs:* 6.1.4.1; 6.1.2.6, 6.1.2.7 (L6.8, condition (4″)).

**Simplicial and groupoid resolutions** (`SSet.IsGroupoidResolution`, `SSet.IsGeneratedGroupoidResolution`; `HTT.6.1.4.3/after`, PDF p. 575). In a presentable ∞-category X, a simplicial resolution is an augmented simplicial object that is a colimit of its underlying simplicial object (`SSet.IsGeometricRealization`); `Res(X) ⊆ X^{Δ₊}` is their full subcategory, and restriction `Res(X) ⟶ X^Δ` is a trivial fibration. A groupoid resolution is a simplicial resolution whose underlying simplicial object is a groupoid object. A map `U₊ ⟶ V₊` of resolutions exhibits V₊ as the groupoid resolution generated by U₊ when V₊ is a groupoid resolution and composition with it is a homotopy equivalence `Map(V₊, W₊) ⟶ Map(U₊, W₊)` for every groupoid resolution W₊.

*Lean:* `SSet.res X := fullEnhancedSubcategory ((ihom nerveAugmentedOp).obj X) fun v ↦ IsGeometricRealization (ihomVertexEquiv v)` (`augmentedSimplicialObjects X` is a type of maps, not a simplicial set), `SSet.IsGroupoidResolution`, and `SSet.IsGeneratedGroupoidResolution (g : Edge U₊ V₊)` through `Hom_{Res(X)}` (`SSet.morphismSpace`). Propose.

*Needs:* 6.1.2.2, 6.1.2.7, 6.1.2.12 (L6.8); 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); `HTT.1.2.2/morphism-space`.

**Generated groupoid resolutions exist** (HTT Remark 6.1.4.4, PDF p. 576). In a presentable X every simplicial resolution has a generated groupoid resolution; equivalently, `Gpd(X) ⊆ X^Δ` is a reflective localization.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.4.3/after`; 6.1.2.9 (L7.9, `Gpd(X)` strongly reflective), or Lurie's 6.1.2.6 with 5.5.4.18–5.5.4.19 (L7.6).

**The universal property against augmented groupoids** (HTT Lemma 6.1.4.5, PDF p. 576). If `U₊ ⟶ V₊` exhibits V₊ as the generated groupoid resolution, composition induces a homotopy equivalence `Map(V₊, W₊) ⟶ Map(U₊, W₊)` in `X^{Δ₊}` for every augmented simplicial object W₊ whose underlying simplicial object is a groupoid.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.4.3/after`.

**The generated groupoid keeps `U₋₁` and `U₀`** (HTT Lemma 6.1.4.6, PDF p. 576). If `U₊ ⟶ V₊` exhibits V₊ as the generated groupoid resolution, `U₋₁ ⟶ V₋₁` and `U₀ ⟶ V₀` are equivalences.

*Proof route.* Right Kan extension from `Δ₊^{≤0}` produces Čech nerves, which are groupoids (6.1.2.11); apply 6.1.4.5.

*Needs:* 6.1.4.5; 6.1.2.11 (L6.8); right Kan extension along `Δ₊^{≤0} ⊆ Δ₊` as a right adjoint to restriction (4.3.2.15, L5.9; the dual of 4.3.3.7, L6.9).

**Coequalizer diagrams resolve** (HTT Lemma 6.1.4.7, PDF p. 577). Let `I ⊆ Δ₊` have objects `∅, [0], [1]` and the injective maps, and `I₀ ⊆ I` the full subcategory on `[0], [1]`. A diagram `N(I)^op ⟶ X` is a coequalizer diagram when it is a colimit of its restriction to `N(I₀)^op`. In a presentable X, left Kan extension `i_!` along `I ⊆ Δ₊` carries coequalizer diagrams to simplicial resolutions.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.4.3/after`; 4.3.2.2, 4.3.3.7 (L5.9, L6.9).

**Left Kan extension from I keeps the augmentation** (HTT Lemma 6.1.4.8, PDF p. 577). For `U : N(I)^op ⟶ X`, the augmentations `(i_!U)₀ ⟶ (i_!U)₋₁` and `U₀ ⟶ U₋₁` are equivalent in `O_X`.

*Needs:* 6.1.4.7; 4.3.3.8 (L5.9).

**Colimit-preserving functors and kernel pairs of coequalizers** (HTT Proposition 6.1.4.2, PDF pp. 575–578). Let `f : X ⟶ Y` preserve small colimits, with X and Y presentable and every groupoid object of each effective. Given a coequalizer diagram `U₁ ⇉ U₀ ⟶ U₋₁` in X and the pullback square `U₀ ×_{U₋₁} U₀`, if f is left exact at `U₀`, then f carries that pullback square to a pullback square.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: resolve the coequalizer by `i_!` (6.1.4.7), take the generated groupoid resolution W (6.1.4.4), which is a Čech nerve by effectiveness and has the same square (6.1.4.6, 6.1.4.8); then `f ∘ W` is a groupoid resolution (6.1.4.3, f colimit-preserving), hence a Čech nerve in Y.

*Needs:* 6.1.4.1, 6.1.4.3, `HTT.6.1.4.3/after`, 6.1.4.4, 6.1.4.6, 6.1.4.7, 6.1.4.8; 6.1.2.11, 6.1.2.14 (L6.8).

### L10.5 Giraud's theorem

**Pullbacks of coproduct inclusions** (HTT Lemma 6.1.5.1, PDF p. 579). In a presentable ∞-category with universal colimits and disjoint coproducts, let `φᵢ : Zᵢ ⟶ Z` exhibit Z as a coproduct. A square with sides `φᵢ`, `φⱼ` and corner W is a pullback exactly when W is initial (for i ≠ j), and exactly when the edge `W ⟶ Zᵢ` is an equivalence (for i = j).

*Needs:* 6.1.1.2, `HTT.6.1.1.4/after`, 6.1.3.6.

**Left exactness from representables** (HTT Proposition 6.1.5.2, PDF pp. 580–582). Let C be a small ∞-category with finite limits and X satisfy the Giraud axioms. A colimit-preserving `F : P(C) ⟶ X` whose restriction `F ∘ j` along the Yoneda embedding is left exact is itself left exact.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.6.1.5.2/good-objects` (good objects and representables), `HTT.6.1.5.2/coproducts` (good objects are closed under coproducts) and `HTT.6.1.5.2/coequalizers` (good objects are closed under coequalizers), and this entry's own target `HTT.6.1.5.2`, which concludes by 4.4.3.3, generation by representables (5.1.5.8) and 4.4.2.5.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: F preserves final objects since j does (5.1.3.2); call Z good when F is left exact at Z (6.1.4.1); representables are good (`HTT.6.1.5.2/good-objects`), and good objects are closed under small coproducts (`HTT.6.1.5.2/coproducts`) and coequalizers (`HTT.6.1.5.2/coequalizers`), hence under all colimits (4.4.3.3), and `P(C)` is generated by representables (5.1.5.8).

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.5.2/good-objects`, `HTT.6.1.5.2/coproducts`, `HTT.6.1.5.2/coequalizers` (below); `HTT.6.1.0.6/stmt`; 5.1.5.8 (L6); 4.4.2.5, 4.4.3.3 (L5.10).

**Good objects and representables** (`HTT.6.1.5.2/good-objects`, part 1 of 3 of left exactness from representables above; HTT Proposition 6.1.5.2, first steps of the proof, PDF pp. 580–581). In the setting of 6.1.5.2, F preserves final objects.
