Call `α : Y ⟶ Z` good when F carries every pullback along α to a pullback, and Z good when every morphism into Z is good (F is left exact at Z, 6.1.4.1). Good morphisms compose. α is good as soon as F preserves the pullbacks of α along maps from representables, and Z is good as soon as every `j(y) ⟶ Z` is good. Every representable `j(z)` is good.

*Needs:* 6.1.4.1, `HTT.6.1.0.6/stmt`; 4.4.2.1 (L5.10); 5.1.3.2, 5.1.5.8 (L6); 6.1.3.10 (L10.3: colimits in `P(C)` are universal, so `F ∘ α^*` preserves colimits and it suffices to test on representables).

**Good objects are closed under coproducts** (`HTT.6.1.5.2/coproducts`, part 2 of 3 of left exactness from representables above; HTT Proposition 6.1.5.2, coproduct step of the proof, PDF pp. 581–582). A small coproduct of good objects of `P(C)` is good.

*Proof route.* A map `j(y) ⟶ ⨿ Z_i` factors through one summand (evaluation at y preserves colimits, 5.1.2.2), so it suffices that the coproduct inclusions are good; this is 6.1.5.1, F preserving initial objects.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.5.2/good-objects`; 6.1.5.1; 5.1.2.2 (L6); 6.1.3.10, 6.1.3.19 (L10.3: `P(C)` has universal colimits and disjoint coproducts, which 6.1.5.1 needs when applied in `P(C)`).

**Good objects are closed under coequalizers** (`HTT.6.1.5.2/coequalizers`, part 3 of 3 of left exactness from representables above; HTT Proposition 6.1.5.2, coequalizer step of the proof, PDF p. 582). If `Z_1 ⇉ Z_0 ⟶ Z_{−1}` is a coequalizer in `P(C)` with `Z_0` and `Z_1` good, then `Z_{−1}` is good.

*Proof route.* Maps from representables to `Z_{−1}` lift to `Z_0` (π₀ of evaluation preserves the coequalizer), which reduces to the pullback of `s : Z_0 ⟶ Z_{−1}` along itself; this is 6.1.4.2.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.5.2/good-objects`; 6.1.4.2; 5.1.2.2 (L6); 6.1.3.10, 6.1.3.19 (L10.3: groupoid objects of `P(C)` are effective, a hypothesis of 6.1.4.2 for `f = F : P(C) ⟶ X`).

**The Giraud axioms imply ∞-topos** (HTT Proposition 6.1.5.3, PDF p. 583; this is `HTT.6.1.0.6/3⇒1`). An ∞-category X satisfying the Giraud axioms is an accessible left exact reflective localization of `P(C)` for a small C with finite limits; in particular an ∞-topos.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: choose τ with X τ-accessible and `X^τ` closed under finite limits (5.4.7.4), a minimal model C of `X^τ` (2.3.3.1), so `X ≃ Ind_τ(C)`; the inclusion `Ind_τ(C) ⊆ P(C)` has a left adjoint L (the proof of 5.5.1.1), `L ∘ j` is the Yoneda embedding into `Ind_τ(C)` and preserves limits (5.1.3.2), so L is left exact by 6.1.5.2, and accessible since its target is presentable (5.5.1.2). Lurie's proof begins "let X be an ∞-topos"; read "satisfying the Giraud axioms".

*Needs:* 6.1.0.4, 6.1.5.2; 5.4.7.4, 5.5.1.1, 5.5.1.2 (L7); 5.1.3.2, 5.3.5.1 (L6); 2.3.3.1 (L3.3).

### L10.6 Classifying objects

**Classifying objects** (`SSet.Classifies`, `SSet.IsSubobjectClassifier`; HTT Definition 6.1.6.1, PDF p. 584). For an ∞-category X with pullbacks and S stable under pullback, a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` classifies S when it is a final object of `O^{(S)}_X`; then Y classifies S. A subobject classifier is an object classifying the monomorphisms.

*Lean:* `SSet.Classifies S f := SSet.IsTerminalVertex` of f in `SSet.cartesianArrowsIn S`; `SSet.IsSubobjectClassifier Y := ∃ f, f.tgt = Y ∧ Classifies SSet.IsMonomorphism f`. Propose.

**Checks.** In `S`, the discrete space with two points is a subobject classifier (HTT Example 6.1.6.2).

*Needs:* 6.1.3.4; `HTT.1.2.12/final`; 5.5.6.13 (L7.7, `SSet.IsMonomorphism`).

**Existence of classifying objects** (HTT Proposition 6.1.6.3, PDF p. 584). Let X be presentable with universal colimits and S stable under pullback. S has a classifying object exactly when S is local and, for every object X, the full subcategory of `X_{/X}` spanned by S is essentially small.

*Proof route.* S has a classifier exactly when the classifying map `X^op ⟶ Ŝ` of `O^{(S)}_X` is representable; apply the representability criterion 5.5.2.2 and 6.1.3.7.

*Needs:* 6.1.6.1, 6.1.3.7, 6.1.3.8; 5.5.2.2 (L7.5); 4.4.4.5 (L5.10, representable right fibrations); 5.4.1.3 (L7.2, `SSet.IsEssentiallySmall`).

**Relatively κ-compact morphisms** (`SSet.IsRelativelyCardinalPresentable`; HTT Definition 6.1.6.4, PDF p. 585). In a presentable ∞-category, `f : X ⟶ Y` is relatively κ-compact when every pullback of f along a morphism with κ-compact source has κ-compact source.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsRelativelyCardinalPresentable f κ (hX : HasCardinalFilteredColimits X κ)` for `[Fact κ.IsRegular]`: for every pullback square `σ : Δ[1] ⊗ Δ[1] ⟶ X` whose right edge is f, `IsCardinalPresentable (squareVertex σ 0 1) κ hX → IsCardinalPresentable (squareVertex σ 0 0) κ hX`, with `SSet.IsCardinalPresentable` (L6.6), which takes the κ-filtered-colimit hypothesis explicitly. Propose.

**Checks.** Equivalences are relatively κ-compact; a morphism between κ-compact objects is relatively κ-compact when κ-compact objects are closed under pullbacks (the last step of 6.1.6.6).

*Needs:* 5.3.4.5 (L6.6); `SSet.IsPullback`.

**κ-filtered colimits of relatively κ-compact morphisms** (HTT Lemma 6.1.6.5, PDF p. 585). If Y is a κ-filtered colimit of objects `Yα` and every pullback `fα` of `f : X ⟶ Y` to `Yα` is relatively κ-compact, so is f.

*Needs:* 6.1.6.4; 5.3.1.7 (L6.6); 4.4.2.1 (L5.10).

**Pushouts of relatively compact morphisms** (HTT Lemma 6.1.6.6, PDF pp. 586–587). Let X be presentable with universal colimits, `τ > κ` regular, X κ-accessible and `X^τ` closed under pullbacks. For a Cartesian transformation between pushout squares, viewed as a pushout square `f ⟶ g, f ⟶ f′, g ⟶ g′, f′ ⟶ g′` in `Fun(Δ[1], X)`, if f, g and f′ are relatively τ-compact then so is g′.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, writing the target square as a τ-filtered colimit of squares of τ-compact objects (the proof of 5.4.4.3) and reducing with 6.1.6.5 (the proof cites itself, "Lemma 6.1.6.6", for this step).

*Needs:* 6.1.6.4, 6.1.6.5; 5.3.4.15, 5.4.4.3, 5.5.2.3 (L7); 4.3.2.15 (L5.9).

**Classifiers for relatively κ-compact members of a local class** (HTT Proposition 6.1.6.7, PDF pp. 586–588). Let X be presentable with universal colimits and S local. For all sufficiently large regular κ, the class `S_κ` of relatively κ-compact members of S has a classifying object.

*Lean:* `∃ κ₀ κ₁, ∀ κ, Fact κ.IsRegular → Cardinal.PowLT κ₀ κ → κ₁ ≤ κ → ∃ f, Classifies (S ⊓ (IsRelativelyCardinalPresentable · κ)) f`, with `Cardinal.PowLT κ₀ κ` HTT's `κ₀ ≪ κ` (A.2.6.3, F1.6). The proof needs the κ-compact objects to be closed under pullbacks; 5.4.7.4 gives this when X is κ₀-accessible, `κ₀ ≪ κ` and `X^{κ₀}` is essentially κ-small (κ₁ bounds its size), not for every κ ≥ κ₀. "Sufficiently large" in 6.1.6.8 (2) and 6.4.1.5 (5) is read the same way; the converse of 6.1.6.8 only needs a cofinal class of κ.

*Needs:* 6.1.6.3, 6.1.6.4, 6.1.6.6, 6.1.3.7; 5.4.7.4, 5.4.7.7, 5.3.4.15 (L7); 4.2.3.4, 4.2.3.10 (L5.6); 5.1.2.2 (L6.1); A.1.1.1 (F1.1).

**Rezk's characterization** (HTT Theorem 6.1.6.8, PDF p. 588). A presentable ∞-category X is an ∞-topos exactly when colimits in X are universal and, for all sufficiently large regular κ, the class of relatively κ-compact morphisms has a classifying object.

*Proof route.* By 6.1.0.6 and 6.1.3.9, X is an ∞-topos exactly when the class of all morphisms is local; that gives the classifiers by 6.1.6.7, and conversely each `S_κ` is local by 6.1.6.3, and their union, all morphisms, is local by 6.1.3.7 (3).

*Needs:* 6.1.0.6, 6.1.3.7, 6.1.3.9, 6.1.6.3, 6.1.6.7.

### L10.7 Left exact and topological localizations

**Left exactness through pullback-stability** (HTT Proposition 6.2.1.1, PDF p. 589). For a reflective localization `L : X ⟶ Y` with X having finite limits, L is left exact exactly when the class of morphisms that L inverts is stable under pullback.

*Needs:* `SSet.IsReflectiveLocalization` (L6.5); 5.5.4.1, 5.5.4.2 (L7.6); `SSet.IsLeftExact`; `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**Pullback-stable closures of small generation** (HTT Proposition 6.2.1.2, PDF pp. 589–593). Let X be presentable with universal colimits, in which pullbacks commute with filtered colimits. For a small set S of morphisms, the smallest strongly saturated class containing S and stable under pullback is of small generation.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.6.2.1.2/closure` (a small closure `S′` of S), `HTT.6.2.1.2/localization-tower` (the `S′`-localization as a transfinite pushout tower) and `HTT.6.2.1.2/pullback-stable` (pullback stability of the class generated by `S′`), and this entry's own target `HTT.6.2.1.2`, which reads off small generation from `HTT.6.2.1.2/pullback-stable`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: a small closure `S′` of S inside `X^κ` under pushouts, pullbacks, diagonals and codiagonals (`HTT.6.2.1.2/closure`), a transfinite construction of the `S′`-localization (`HTT.6.2.1.2/localization-tower`), and pullback stability of the class `S′` generates (`HTT.6.2.1.2/pullback-stable`). Lurie notes that ∞-topoi satisfy the hypotheses by Example 7.3.4.7 (L11); that is a remark, not a step of the proof.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.2.1.2/closure`, `HTT.6.2.1.2/localization-tower`, `HTT.6.2.1.2/pullback-stable` (below); 5.5.4.7 (L7.6).

**A small closure of S** (`HTT.6.2.1.2/closure`, part 1 of 3 of pullback-stable closures of small generation above; HTT Proposition 6.2.1.2, first step of the proof, PDF pp. 589–590). Let X be presentable with universal colimits, in which pullbacks commute with filtered colimits, and let S be a small set of morphisms. Choose κ with X κ-accessible, `X^κ` closed under finite limits, and the sources and targets of S κ-compact. The smallest class S′ of morphisms of `X^κ` that contains S and is closed under pushouts and pullbacks in `X^κ` and under diagonals and codiagonals is essentially small, and it is contained in the smallest pullback-stable strongly saturated class containing S.

*Needs:* 5.4.7.4 (L7.4); 5.3.4.5 (L6.6).

**The S′-localization as a transfinite pushout tower** (`HTT.6.2.1.2/localization-tower`, part 2 of 3 of pullback-stable closures of small generation above; HTT Proposition 6.2.1.2, step (∗″) of the proof, PDF pp. 591, 593). With S′ as above, every object X admits a transfinite sequence `X = X_0 ⟶ X_1 ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X_κ`, continuous at limits, each step a pushout of a coproduct of morphisms of S′, with `X_κ` S′-local. It is therefore an S′-localization of X.

*Proof route.* Lurie's small object argument: attach along all pairs (u ∈ S′, `A ⟶ X`). Locality is checked by showing that `Map(B, X_κ) ⟶ Map(A, X_κ)` is n-connective for all n; the induction on n passes to codiagonals, which lie in S′, and the base case uses κ-compactness of A.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.2.1.2/closure`; 5.5.4.5, 5.5.4.15 (L7.6).

**Pullback stability of the generated class** (`HTT.6.2.1.2/pullback-stable`, part 3 of 3 of pullback-stable closures of small generation above; HTT Proposition 6.2.1.2, steps (∗), (∗′) and the conclusion of the proof, PDF pp. 590–593). The strongly saturated class generated by S′ is stable under pullback. Consequently it equals the smallest pullback-stable strongly saturated class containing S, which is therefore of small generation.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. (∗): pullbacks of S′-maps lie in the class, by κ-filtered colimits and universality. (∗′): the same holds for pushouts of S′-maps. For a general f in the class, factor its pullback as `X ×_Y Y' ⟶ X ×_{LY} Y' ⟶ Y'` and treat each factor by transfinite induction along `HTT.6.2.1.2/localization-tower`. At the successor steps of the first factor, reduce through κ-compact presentations to a pullback of a diagonal of `Y_k ⟶ Y_k ⨿_A B`, which lies in S′.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.2.1.2/closure`, `HTT.6.2.1.2/localization-tower`; 6.1.1.2; 5.5.4.5 (L7.6).

**Subobjects** (`SSet.Subobject`; HTT Proposition 6.2.1.3 and the prose before it, PDF pp. 593–594). For an ∞-category X and an object X, `Sub(X)` is the set of equivalence classes of monomorphisms into X, partially ordered by factorization; `τ_{≤−1}(X_{/X}) ≃ N(Sub(X))`. For X presentable, `Sub(X)` is small.

*Lean:* `SSet.Subobject X` as the quotient of `Σ c, {e : SSet.Edge c X // IsMonomorphism e}` (`SSet.Edge` is indexed by its endpoints) by equivalence of the corresponding vertices of `X_{/X}` (Tau Ceti `SSet.slice`), with its `PartialOrder`; the proposition as `Small.{u} (SSet.Subobject X)`. Propose.

**Checks.** In `S`, `Sub(∗)` has two elements, `∅` and `∗`.

*Needs:* 5.5.6.13 (L7.7); 5.5.3.10, 5.5.6.18 (L7).

**Topological localizations** (`SSet.IsTopological`, `SSet.IsTopologicalLocalization`; HTT Definition 6.2.1.4, PDF p. 594). For X presentable, a strongly saturated class S is topological when it is generated, as a strongly saturated class, by a subclass of monomorphisms, and is stable under pullback. A reflective localization is topological when the class of morphisms it inverts is.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsTopological S := (∃ S₀ ≤ S, (∀ f, S₀ f → IsMonomorphism f) ∧ stronglySaturatedClosure S₀ = S) ∧ IsStableUnderPullback S`; `SSet.IsTopologicalLocalization L := IsTopological (fun f ↦ SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence (image of f under L))`. Propose.

**Checks.** The identity of X is a topological localization. The sheaf inclusion `Shv(C) ⊆ P(C)` gives one (6.2.2.7).

*Needs:* 5.5.4.5, 5.5.4.7 (L7.6); 6.1.3.4; 5.5.6.13 (L7.7).

**Topological classes are generated by a small set of monomorphisms** (HTT Proposition 6.2.1.5, PDF pp. 594–595). If X is presentable with universal colimits and S is topological, a small set of monomorphisms in S generates S.

*Needs:* 6.2.1.3, 6.2.1.4; 6.1.1.2; 5.1.5.7 (L6.3); 5.5.4.7 (L7.6).

**Topological localizations are left exact, and accessible when colimits are universal** (HTT Corollary 6.2.1.6, PDF p. 595). For X presentable, every topological localization of X is left exact; if colimits in X are universal, it is also accessible. Lurie states accessibility for every presentable X; his only route to it is 6.2.1.5, which assumes universal colimits. Every use of this target is for `P(C)` or an ∞-topos, where colimits are universal.

*Proof route.* Left exactness from 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.1.4 (2) (the inverted class is stable under pullback). Accessibility from small generation (6.2.1.5) and 5.5.4.15.

*Needs:* 6.2.1.1, 6.2.1.4, 6.2.1.5; 5.5.4.15 (L7.6); 5.5.1.2 (L7.5).

### L10.8 Grothendieck topologies and sheaves

**Sieves and Grothendieck topologies** (`SSet.Sieve`, `SSet.GrothendieckTopology`; HTT Definition 6.2.2.1, PDF pp. 595–596). A sieve on an ∞-category C is a full subcategory `C⁽⁰⁾` such that the source of any morphism with target in `C⁽⁰⁾` is in `C⁽⁰⁾`; sieves pull back along functors. A sieve on an object C is a sieve on `C_{/C}`, and a morphism `f : D ⟶ C` pulls it back to a sieve on D. A Grothendieck topology assigns to every object a collection of covering sieves, containing the maximal sieve, stable under pullback, and local (a sieve whose pullbacks along the members of a covering sieve are covering is covering).

*Lean:* `SSet.Sieve C := {P : C _⦋0⦌ → Prop // ∀ ⦃c d : C _⦋0⦌⦄ (_ : Edge c d), P d → P c}`; `SSet.GrothendieckTopology C := CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology (hoFunctor.obj C)` for a quasicategory C (the layer convention: a departure from HTT's form, justified by 6.2.2.3). Propose.

**Checks.** For a category A and an object c, sieves on c (`SSet.Sieve` of `N(A)_{/c} ≅ N(A_{/c})`) correspond bijectively, preserving order and pullback, to Mathlib's `Sieve c`. `SSet.GrothendieckTopology (nerve A)` corresponds to Mathlib's `GrothendieckTopology A` along `hoFunctor.obj (nerve A) ≌ A`.

*Needs:* `HTT.1.2.11/intro`; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sites.Grothendieck`, `SSet.hoFunctor`; Tau Ceti `SSet.slice`.

**The trivial topology** (HTT Example 6.2.2.2, PDF p. 596). Every ∞-category carries the topology whose only covering sieves are the maximal ones.

*Lean:* Mathlib `GrothendieckTopology.trivial (hoFunctor.obj C)`.

**Checks.** Its sheaves are all presheaves (6.2.2.6).

*Needs:* 6.2.2.1.

**Topologies on C are topologies on hC** (HTT Remark 6.2.2.3, PDF p. 596). For an object C, the comparison `η : h(C_{/C}) ⟶ (hC)_{/C}` is in general not an equivalence, but it is surjective on morphism sets, so pulling back along η is a bijection from sieves on C in `hC` to sieves on `C_{/C}`. Hence HTT's Grothendieck topologies on C are exactly the Grothendieck topologies on `hC`.

*Lean:* `SSet.sieve_slice_equiv c : Nonempty (SSet.Sieve (slice c) ≃ CategoryTheory.Sieve (mk c : hoFunctor.obj C))`, for a quasicategory C. This is weaker than the remark, which says the bijection is pullback along η. To state that form, declare η, `SSet.sliceHoComparison c : hoFunctor.obj (slice c) ⥤ Over (mk c)` (propose), and identify the bijection with pullback of sieves along it. HTT's Grothendieck topologies on C themselves are not declared: the Conventions define a topology on C to be a Mathlib topology on `hC`, so the sieve comparison is the content of this target. Comparing HTT's axioms (stated with `SSet.Sieve` on slices) with Mathlib's `GrothendieckTopology` axioms on `hC` would first need a declaration of HTT's topologies; it is optional.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.1; Tau Ceti `SSet.slice`; Mathlib `SSet.hoFunctor`, `Over`.

**Sieves as subterminal presheaves** (HTT Lemma 6.2.2.4, PDF p. 597). For a small ∞-category C, sending a presheaf U to the full subcategory of objects C with `U(C)` nonempty is a bijection from equivalence classes of (−1)-truncated objects of `P(C)` to sieves on C.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.1; 5.1.0.1 (L6.1); 5.5.6.1 (L7.7).

**Sieves on an object as subobjects of a representable** (HTT Proposition 6.2.2.5, PDF p. 597). For C small and an object C, sending a monomorphism `i : U ⟶ j(C)` to the sieve of those `f : D ⟶ C` for which `j(f)` factors through i is a bijection `Sub(j(C)) ≅` sieves on C.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.4, 6.2.1.3; 5.1.6.12 (L6.3); `SSet.yoneda` (L6.1).

**Sheaves** (`SSet.IsSheaf`, `SSet.sheaf`; HTT Definition 6.2.2.6, PDF p. 597). For a small ∞-category C with a Grothendieck topology, let S be the monomorphisms `U ⟶ j(C)` corresponding (6.2.2.5) to covering sieves. A presheaf is a sheaf when it is S-local; `Shv(C) ⊆ P(C)` is the full subcategory of sheaves.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsSheaf J F := SSet.IsLocalObject (SSet.coveringMonos J) F` and `SSet.sheaf J := fullEnhancedSubcategory (IsSheaf J)` of `SSet.presheaf C`, with `SSet.coveringMonos J` the monomorphisms into representables whose sieve is J-covering. Propose.

**Checks.** For the trivial topology every presheaf is a sheaf. For C the nerve of a small category with a topology J, a 0-truncated presheaf is a sheaf exactly when its `π₀` is a Mathlib sheaf of sets for J.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.5; 5.5.4.1 (L7.6); `SSet.presheaf`, `SSet.yoneda` (L6.1).

**Sheaves form an ∞-topos** (HTT Proposition 6.2.2.7, PDF pp. 597, 600–601). `Shv(C) ⊆ P(C)` is a topological localization; in particular `Shv(C)` is an ∞-topos.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: it suffices that the localization is left exact (its inverted class is then stable under pullback by 6.2.1.1 and generated by the monomorphisms S). Iterate the left exact functor `F ↦ F†` of 6.2.2.9 transfinitely up to a regular κ for which every covering-sieve limit commutes with κ-filtered colimits; each stage is left exact (5.3.3.3, 6.2.2.11), each step is an S-equivalence (6.2.2.14), and the κ-th stage is a sheaf (6.2.2.15). The ∞-topos clause is 6.1.0.4 with 6.2.1.6.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.6, 6.2.2.9, 6.2.2.11, 6.2.2.13, 6.2.2.14, 6.2.2.15; 6.2.1.1, 6.2.1.4, 6.2.1.6; `HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if` (L6.6); 5.5.4.15 (L7.6); 6.1.0.4.

**The category of covering sieves** (`SSet.coveringSieves`; HTT Notation 6.2.2.8, PDF pp. 597–598). For an ordinary category with a topology, `Cov(C)` has objects the pairs `(C, covering sieve on C)` and morphisms `u : C ⟶ D` carrying the first sieve into the second. For an ∞-category C, `Cov(C) = C ×_{N(hC)} N(Cov(hC))`; the projection `ρ : Cov(C) ⟶ C` is a Cartesian fibration whose fibre over C is the nerve of the poset of covering sieves on C.

*Lean:* `SSet.coveringSieves J` as that pullback, with `ρ` and its `CartesianFibration` instance. Propose.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.3; 2.4.2.1 (L3.6); Mathlib `nerve`.

**The plus construction** (`SSet.plusSite`, `SSet.plusConstruction`; HTT Construction 6.2.2.9, PDF p. 598). `C⁺` is the full subcategory of `Fun(Δ[1], C) ×_{Fun({1}, C)} Cov(C)` on the pairs `(u : C′ ⟶ C, sieve)` with u in the sieve, with `e : C⁺ ⟶ C` (source) and `π : C⁺ ⟶ Cov(C)`. The functor `F ↦ F† = ρ_! π_* e^* F` on `P(C)` uses right Kan extension `π_*` and left Kan extension `ρ_!`.

*Lean:* `SSet.plusSite J` and `SSet.plusConstruction J : SSet.presheaf C ⟶ SSet.presheaf C`, through chosen Kan extension functors (L5.9, L6.9). Propose.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.8; 4.3.3.2, 4.3.3.7 (L5.9, L6.9); `SSet.presheaf`.

**The right Kan extension `π_*` as a limit over the sieve** (HTT Remark 6.2.2.10, PDF p. 598). π is a coCartesian fibration, so each fibre inclusion is cofinal and `(π_* F)(C, C⁽⁰⁾) ≃ lim_{C′ ∈ C⁽⁰⁾} F(C′ ⟶ C, C⁽⁰⁾)`.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.9; 4.1.1.1, 4.3.3.2 (L5); 2.4.2.1.

**`ρ_!` as a filtered colimit; `F†` is left exact** (HTT Remark 6.2.2.11, PDF p. 599). ρ is a Cartesian fibration, so `(ρ_! F)(C) ≃ colim F(C, C⁽⁰⁾)` over covering sieves ordered by reverse inclusion, a filtered poset; hence `ρ_!` is left exact (5.3.3.3), and so is `F ↦ F†`.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.9; 4.1.1.1 (L5); 5.3.1.7, `HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if` (L6.6).

**The map `F ⟶ F†`** (HTT Remark 6.2.2.13, PDF p. 599). The sections `s : C ⟶ Cov(C)`, `C ↦ (C, C_{/C})`, and `s⁺ : C ⟶ C⁺` give `s^* π_* ≃ s⁺^*` and a natural transformation from the identity of `P(C)` to `F ↦ F†`.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.10; `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**`F ⟶ F†` is invisible to sheaves** (HTT Lemma 6.2.2.14, PDF pp. 599–600). For F a presheaf and G a sheaf, composition with `F ⟶ F†` is a homotopy equivalence `Map(F†, G) ⟶ Map(F, G)`.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.6, 6.2.2.13; 4.3.2.2 (L5.9).

**Comparison through a covering sieve** (HTT Remark 6.2.2.15, PDF p. 600). For F a presheaf, a covering sieve `C⁽⁰⁾` on C, and `F₀(f : D ⟶ C) = lim_{E ∈ f^*C⁽⁰⁾} F(E)`, the transformations `F|C_{/C} ⟶ F₀ ⟶ F†|C_{/C}` compose to the map of 6.2.2.13, and the comparison map `lim_{D ∈ C⁽⁰⁾} F₀(D) ⟵ F₀(C)` it induces is a homotopy equivalence (cofinality).

*Needs:* 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.13; 4.1.1.1 (L5).

**Sheafification detects covering sieves** (HTT Lemma 6.2.2.16, PDF pp. 601–602). With `L : P(C) ⟶ Shv(C)` the sheafification, a monomorphism `U ⟶ j(C)` with sieve `C⁽⁰⁾` becomes an equivalence under L exactly when `C⁽⁰⁾` is covering.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `τ_{≤0}` commutes with L (5.5.6.28), which reduces the converse to sheafification of presheaves of sets on `hC`; use Mathlib's (`presheafToSheaf`, local surjectivity).

*Needs:* 6.2.2.6, 6.2.2.7; 5.5.6.28 (L7.7); Mathlib `presheafToSheaf`.

**Topologies and topological localizations of `P(C)`** (HTT Proposition 6.2.2.17, PDF pp. 602–603). For a small ∞-category C, `J ↦ Shv_J(C)` is a bijection from Grothendieck topologies on C to equivalence classes of topological localizations of `P(C)`.

*Lean:* injectivity (`sheaf J = sheaf J' → J = J'`, as full subcategories) and surjectivity onto the topological strongly saturated classes of `P(C)` (`SSet.IsTopological`).

*Needs:* 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.7, 6.2.2.16; 6.2.1.4; 6.2.2.5; 6.1.3.10 (colimits in `P(C)` are universal); 5.1.6.12 (L6.3); 5.5.4.7 (L7.6).

**Initial sheaves** (HTT Proposition 6.2.2.18, PDF pp. 603–604). Let `C₀` be the objects of C on which the empty sieve covers. A sheaf F is initial in `Shv(C)` exactly when `F(C)` is contractible for `C ∈ C₀` and empty otherwise.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.4, 6.2.2.7, 6.2.2.16; 5.5.6.16 (L7.7); `SSet.IsInitialVertex` (L1.5).

### L10.9 Semitopoi, effective epimorphisms and delooping in `S`

**Semitopoi** (`SSet.IsSemitopos`; HTT Definition 6.2.3.1, PDF p. 604). An ∞-category X is a semitopos when it is presentable, colimits in X are universal, and for every morphism `f : U ⟶ X` the underlying groupoid of the Čech nerve of f is effective.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsSemitopos X := ∃ hX : IsPresentable X, HasUniversalColimits X hX ∧ ∀ U₊, IsCechNerve U₊ → IsEffectiveGroupoid (U₊ restricted to N(Δ)^op)`. Propose.

**Checks.** `S` is a semitopos (6.1.3.14, 6.1.3.20); every ∞-topos is one (6.1.0.6; HTT Remark 6.2.3.2, not a target).

*Needs:* 6.1.1.2; 6.1.2.11, 6.1.2.14 (L6.8); 5.5.0.1 (L7.5).

**Colimits of Čech nerves are (−1)-truncations** (HTT Proposition 6.2.3.4, PDF pp. 604–605). In a semitopos, for `p : U ⟶ X` with Čech nerve U and V a colimit of its underlying simplicial object, the induced `V ⟶ X` is a (−1)-truncation of p in `X_{/X}`.

*Needs:* 6.2.3.1; 6.1.2.11 (L6.8); 5.5.6.1, 5.5.6.18 (L7.7); 1.2.13.8 (L2).

**Effective epimorphisms** (`SSet.IsEffectiveEpi`; HTT Corollary 6.2.3.5 and the definition after it, PDF p. 605). For a morphism `f : x ⟶ y` of a semitopos X, equivalent: the (−1)-truncation of f, as an object of the slice `X_{/y}` over the target of f, is final in `X_{/y}`; the Čech nerve of f is a simplicial resolution of y (a colimit diagram). f is an effective epimorphism when these hold.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsEffectiveEpi f` for an edge f of any quasicategory: some Čech nerve `U₊` of f (augmentation f, `SSet.IsCechNerve`) is a geometric realization (`SSet.IsGeometricRealization`). Propose; the condition is the second one, and makes sense in any ∞-category. The (−1)-truncation form, in a semitopos, is the characterization: `SSet.isEffectiveEpi_iff (hX : IsSemitopos X) f`, whose first part reads: for every vertex τ of `X_{/y}` and edge `e : f ⟶ τ` exhibiting τ as a (−1)-truncation (`Edge.IsLocalizationInto {Z | IsTruncatedObject (-1) Z} e`), τ is final (`IsTerminalVertex τ`). Here f as a vertex of `X_{/y}` is `SSet.Edge.toSliceVertex f` (propose, through `Δ[1] ≅ Δ[0] ⋆ Δ[0]`). Its second part is the definition with "some" replaced by "every" Čech nerve of f (`∀ U, U.app _ augmentationEdge = f.edge → IsCechNerve U → IsGeometricRealization U`); Čech nerves of f are unique up to equivalence, so the two agree. Lurie's further remark that effective epimorphisms correspond to effective groupoids has no target number.

**Checks.** Equivalences are effective epimorphisms (6.2.3.7). In `S`, `∅ ⟶ ∗` is not: its Čech nerve is constant at `∅`.

*Needs:* 6.2.3.4; 6.1.2.11, 6.1.2.12 (L6.8).

**Left exact left adjoints preserve effective epimorphisms** (HTT Remark 6.2.3.6, PDF p. 605). Lurie states it for the pullback functor `f^*` of a geometric morphism of ∞-topoi (6.3.1.1, L11); the target states the content: a left exact functor between ∞-topoi with a right adjoint carries effective epimorphisms to effective epimorphisms (left exact functors preserve Čech nerves, left adjoints preserve colimits).

*Needs:* 6.2.3.5; 5.2.3.5 (L6.4); `SSet.IsLeftExact`; 6.1.2.11 (L6.8).

**First properties** (HTT Proposition 6.2.3.7, PDF p. 606). In a semitopos: equivalences are effective epimorphisms; being one is invariant under homotopy; a left exact colimit-preserving functor between semitopoi preserves them.

*Needs:* 6.2.3.5, 6.2.3.1.

**Subobjects of a coproduct** (HTT Remark 6.2.3.9, PDF p. 606). For X presentable with universal colimits, the map `Sub(⊔ Xα) ⟶ ∏ Sub(Xα)` given by pullback is injective; when coproducts are disjoint it is bijective.

*Needs:* 6.2.1.3; 6.1.1.2, `HTT.6.1.1.4/after`; 6.1.5.1; 5.5.6.16 (L7.7).

**Effective epimorphisms through subobjects** (HTT Proposition 6.2.3.10, PDF pp. 606–607). In a semitopos, `f : U ⟶ X` is an effective epimorphism exactly when pullback `f^* : Sub(X) ⟶ Sub(U)` is injective.

*Needs:* 6.2.3.4, 6.2.3.5, 6.2.1.3; 5.5.6.16 (L7.7).

**Coproducts and composition** (HTT Corollaries 6.2.3.11–6.2.3.12, PDF pp. 607–608). In a semitopos, a coproduct of effective epimorphisms is one (6.2.3.11). For `h = g ∘ f`: if f and g are effective epimorphisms so is h, and if h is then so is g (6.2.3.12).

*Needs:* 6.2.3.9, 6.2.3.10.

**Colimit cocones are jointly effective** (HTT Lemma 6.2.3.13, PDF p. 608). In a semitopos, for a colimit diagram `p : K^▷ ⟶ X` with cone point ∞, the induced `⊔_{x ∈ K₀} p(x) ⟶ p(∞)` is an effective epimorphism.

*Needs:* 6.2.1.3, 6.2.3.9, 6.2.3.10 (by 6.2.3.9, injectivity of pullback on `Sub(p(∞))` along the coproduct map reduces to the pullbacks along the maps `p(x) ⟶ p(∞)`); 6.1.3.1, 6.1.3.3 (pulling two subobjects back along p gives Cartesian transformations into the colimit diagram p, whose sources are again colimit diagrams, so an equivalence over K is one at the cone point); 6.1.1.2.

**Local classes by descent along effective epimorphisms** (HTT Proposition 6.2.3.14, PDF pp. 608–609). In an ∞-topos X, a class S stable under pullback and coproducts is local exactly when it descends along effective epimorphisms: if a pullback of f along an effective epimorphism lies in S, so does f.

*Needs:* 6.1.3.5, 6.1.3.7, 6.1.3.8, 6.1.3.10, 6.2.3.13; 6.2.3.5.

**Pullback-stability and descent of effective epimorphisms** (HTT Proposition 6.2.3.15, PDF p. 609). In a semitopos, effective epimorphisms are stable under pullback; conversely, if the pullback of f along an effective epimorphism g is an effective epimorphism, so is f.

*Needs:* 6.2.3.5, 6.2.3.12; 6.1.1.2.

**Equivalences descend along effective epimorphisms** (HTT Lemma 6.2.3.16, PDF p. 610). In a semitopos, if the pullback of f along an effective epimorphism is an equivalence, then f is an equivalence.

*Needs:* 6.2.3.15; 6.1.2.11 (L6.8).

**Truncatedness descends along effective epimorphisms** (HTT Proposition 6.2.3.17, PDF pp. 610–611). In a semitopos, pullbacks of n-truncated morphisms are n-truncated; conversely, if the pullback of f along an effective epimorphism is n-truncated, so is f.

*Needs:* 6.2.3.15, 6.2.3.16; 5.5.6.8, 5.5.6.15, 5.5.6.16 (L7.7).

**Sieves generated by families** (HTT Lemma 6.2.3.18, PDF p. 611). For C small and morphisms `fα : Cα ⟶ C`, the monomorphism into `j(C)` corresponding to the sieve they generate is a (−1)-truncation of `⊔ j(Cα) ⟶ j(C)` in `P(C)_{/j(C)}`.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.5; 6.2.3.4.

**Factoring through sheaves** (HTT Lemma 6.2.3.19, PDF pp. 611–612). Let X be an ∞-topos, C small with a topology, and `f_* : X ⟶ P(C)` with a left exact left adjoint `f^*`. Then `f_*` factors through `Shv(C)` exactly when, for every family `Cα ⟶ C` generating a covering sieve, `⊔ f^*j(Cα) ⟶ f^*j(C)` is an effective epimorphism.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.6, 6.2.2.7 (L is left exact, so 6.2.3.6 applies to it), 6.2.3.4, 6.2.3.5 (factorization), 6.2.3.6, 6.2.3.12, 6.2.3.18; 6.2.3.10 (an effective epimorphism that is a monomorphism is an equivalence).

**The universal property of `Shv(C)`** (HTT Proposition 6.2.3.20, PDF pp. 612–613). Let X be an ∞-topos and C small with a topology. Let `Fun^*(A, X) ⊆ Fun(A, X)` be the full subcategory of left exact colimit-preserving functors (HTT Definition 6.3.1.10 names it; here it is just this full subcategory). Composition with sheafification and the Yoneda embedding, `Fun^*(Shv(C), X) ⟶ Fun^*(P(C), X) ⟶ Fun(C, X)`, is fully faithful. If C has finite limits, its essential image is the left exact `f : C ⟶ X` carrying every family generating a covering sieve to an effective epimorphism `⊔ f(Cα) ⟶ f(C)`.

*Needs:* 6.2.3.19; 6.1.5.2; 6.2.2.7 (composition with L preserves left exactness); 5.1.5.6 (L6.3); 5.5.4.20 (L7.6).

**Effective epimorphisms of spaces** (`HTT.6.2.3/effective-epi-spaces`; HTT's description of surjections of spaces after Fact 6.1.1.6, PDF p. 553, as a statement about Corollary 6.2.3.5). A morphism `f : U ⟶ X` of `S` is an effective epimorphism exactly when `π₀ U ⟶ π₀ X` is surjective. In particular a base point `∗ ⟶ X` is an effective epimorphism exactly when X is connected.

*Proof route.* HTT states the general form for ∞-topoi as 7.2.1.14 (L11); for `S` the results above suffice. If f is an effective epimorphism, so is its pullback `F_x ⟶ ∗` along each point x (6.2.3.15), so the fibre `F_x` is nonempty: the Čech nerve of `∅ ⟶ ∗` is constant at `∅`, and `N(Δ)^op` is weakly contractible, so its colimit is `∅` (4.4.4.10). Conversely, X is the colimit of the constant diagram at `∗` indexed by X (4.4.4.9, with the mapping spaces of `S` from 2.2.0.1), so `⊔_{x ∈ X₀} ∗ ⟶ X` is an effective epimorphism (6.2.3.13). The pullback of f along it is `⊔_x F_x ⟶ ⊔_x ∗`. Each `F_x ⟶ ∗` with `F_x` nonempty is one, since a point of `F_x` makes `∗ ⟶ F_x ⟶ ∗` the identity (6.2.3.7, 6.2.3.12), and a coproduct of effective epimorphisms is one (6.2.3.11). So f is an effective epimorphism by the descent half of 6.2.3.15.

*Needs:* 6.2.3.5, 6.2.3.7, 6.2.3.11, 6.2.3.12, 6.2.3.13, 6.2.3.15; 4.4.4.9, 4.4.4.10 (L5.10); 2.2.0.1 (L2).

**Delooping in `S`** (`HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces`; the case `X = S` of HTT Lemmas 7.2.2.10–7.2.2.11, PDF pp. 742–745). Forgetting the base point gives `Grp(S_*) ≃ Grp(S)`, and the Čech nerve of a base point `∗ ⟶ X` gives an equivalence from connected pointed spaces to `Grp(S)` under which Ω corresponds to evaluation at `[1]` (7.2.2.11 (1)); for `n ≥ 1` it carries the Eilenberg–MacLane objects `EM_n(S)` onto `Grp(EM_{n−1}(S))` (7.2.2.11 (2)). Addition beyond HTT 7.2.2.11, part of this target because HA 1.4.3.9 needs it: a connected pointed space X is n-connective exactly when its group object is levelwise (n−1)-connective, since the group object has `U_k ≃ (ΩX)^k` and `π_i ΩX ≅ π_{i+1} X`. HA 1.4.3.9 uses it.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as six targets: the five parts that follow this entry, `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/grp-pointed` (forgetting base points), `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/cech` (the Čech nerve of a base point), `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/equivalence` (delooping as an equivalence), `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/em` (Eilenberg–MacLane objects) and `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/connectivity` (the connectivity addition, which completes the statement), and this entry's own target `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces`, which collects them.

*Proof route.* Lurie's proof of 7.2.2.11 at `X = S`, with two inputs special to `S` in place of the ∞-topos results it cites: every groupoid object of `S` is effective (6.1.3.20, for Giraud's theorem 6.1.0.6), and a base point `∗ ⟶ X` is an effective epimorphism exactly when X is connected (`HTT.6.2.3/effective-epi-spaces`, for 7.2.1.14). Part (2) and the connectivity addition use the homotopy theory of Kan complexes (F2) in place of homotopy sheaves (6.2.3.17, 6.5.1.5, 6.5.1.16).

*Needs:* `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/grp-pointed`, `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/cech`, `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/equivalence`, `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/em`, `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/connectivity` (below).

**Group objects forget base points** (`HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/grp-pointed`, part 1 of 5 of delooping in `S` above; HTT Lemma 7.2.2.10 at `X = S`, PDF pp. 744–745). For an ∞-category with finite limits, here `S`, forgetting the base point gives an equivalence `Grp(S_*) ⟶ Grp(S)`.

*Proof route.* The level `U₀` of a group object is final, so its levels are canonically pointed; the forgetful functor `S_* = S_{∗/} ⟶ S` preserves and reflects the pullbacks of (4″) over the final object.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed` (L6.8).

**The Čech nerve of a base point** (`HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/cech`, part 2 of 5 of delooping in `S` above; the construction in HTT Lemma 7.2.2.11 at `X = S`, PDF pp. 745–746). For a connected pointed Kan complex X, the Čech nerve of `∗ ⟶ X` restricts to a group object `U_•` of `S` with `U_k ≃ (ΩX)^k`. This is functorial in X, and Ω corresponds to evaluation at `[1]`.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/grp-pointed`; 6.1.2.11 (L6.8).

**Delooping as an equivalence** (`HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/equivalence`, part 3 of 5 of delooping in `S` above; HTT Lemma 7.2.2.11 (1) at `X = S`, PDF p. 745). The functor of `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/cech` is an equivalence from connected pointed spaces to `Grp(S)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Every groupoid object of `S` is effective (6.1.3.20), so restriction identifies effective epimorphisms of `S` with groupoid objects of `S` (the correspondence after 6.2.3.5: Čech nerves are right Kan extensions from the augmentation, 6.1.2.11, and simplicial resolutions are left Kan extensions, 4.3.2.15). Group objects are the groupoid objects whose level `U₀` is final, and these correspond to the effective epimorphisms `∗ ⟶ X`. By `HTT.6.2.3/effective-epi-spaces` those are the base points of connected X.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/cech`; `HTT.6.2.3/effective-epi-spaces`, 6.2.3.5 (above); 6.1.3.20 (L10.3); 6.1.2.11, `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed` (L6.8); 4.3.2.15 (L5.9).

**Eilenberg–MacLane objects** (`HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/em`, part 4 of 5 of delooping in `S` above; HTT Lemma 7.2.2.11 (2) at `X = S`, PDF pp. 745–746). For `n ≥ 1` the equivalence of `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/equivalence` carries `EM_n(S)` onto `Grp(EM_{n−1}(S))`.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/equivalence`; `HTT.A.2.7/eilenberg-maclane` (F2.5).

**Connectivity of group objects** (`HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/connectivity`, part 5 of 5 of delooping in `S` above; the addition beyond HTT Lemma 7.2.2.11 in the entry above; compare observation (a) in its proof, PDF p. 746). A connected pointed space X is n-connective exactly when its group object is levelwise (n−1)-connective, since `U_k ≃ (ΩX)^k` and `π_i ΩX ≅ π_{i+1} X`. With the other parts this is the statement of the entry above.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/equivalence`, `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/em`; homotopy groups of Kan complexes (F2.2).

**`Ω^∞` on connective spectra preserves sifted colimits** (HA Proposition 1.4.3.9, PDF p. 153). The functor `Ω^∞ : Sp_{≥0} ⟶ S` preserves sifted colimits.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: reduce to `Ω : S_*^{≥n+1} ⟶ S_*^{≥n}`, identify `S_*^{≥1}` with group objects of `S` (HTT 7.2.2.10–7.2.2.11, supplied at `X = S` by `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces` above), and use that sifted colimits in `S` commute with finite products (HTT 5.5.8.11).

*Needs:* HA 1.4.3.6 (L9.6); `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/equivalence`, `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces/connectivity` (above), `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed` (L6.8); 5.5.8.1, 5.5.8.11 (L7); 4.4.2.9 (L5.10); 5.1.2.2 (L6).

### L10.10 Canonical topologies

**Canonical coverings** (`SSet.IsCanonicalCovering`; HTT Definition 6.2.4.1, PDF p. 613). Let X be a semitopos, C a small ∞-category with finite limits and `f : C ⟶ X` left exact. A sieve on an object C is a canonical covering relative to f when it contains a family `uα : Cα ⟶ C` for which `⊔ f(Cα) ⟶ f(C)` is an effective epimorphism.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsCanonicalCovering f (S : CategoryTheory.Sieve c)`, for a vertex c of C, a Mathlib sieve on c in `hoFunctor.obj C` (6.2.2.3), and f left exact into a semitopos: there are `ι : Type u` and edges `u i : C.Edge (c' i) c` whose classes lie in S such that the map to `f c` from a coproduct of the `f (c' i)`, induced by the `u i`, is `SSet.IsEffectiveEpi`. Propose.

*Needs:* 6.2.3.1, 6.2.3.5; 6.2.2.1.

**The canonical topology** (`SSet.canonicalTopology`; HTT Proposition 6.2.4.2, PDF p. 614). The canonical coverings relative to f form a Grothendieck topology on C.

*Lean:* `SSet.canonicalTopology f : SSet.GrothendieckTopology C`, whose covering sieves are the canonical coverings. Propose.

**Checks.** Maximal sieves are canonical coverings (identities are effective epimorphisms, 6.2.3.7). If `f(C)` is initial in X, the empty sieve on C is a canonical covering (the empty coproduct is initial).

*Needs:* 6.2.4.1; 6.2.3.11, 6.2.3.12, 6.2.3.15; 6.1.1.2.

**Objects sent to the initial object** (HTT Lemma 6.2.4.3, PDF p. 615). With the canonical topology, if `f(C)` is initial in X then `L j(C)` is initial in `Shv(C)`.

*Needs:* 6.2.4.2; 6.2.2.6.

**Sheaves for the canonical topology preserve coproducts** (HTT Lemma 6.2.4.4, PDF pp. 615–616). If moreover f is fully faithful and coproducts in X are disjoint, and morphisms `uα : Cα ⟶ C` exhibit `f(C)` as the coproduct of the `f(Cα)`, then every sheaf F for the canonical topology has `F(C) ≃ ∏ F(Cα)` through the `F(uα)`.

*Needs:* 6.2.4.3; 6.1.5.1; 6.1.3.10 (colimits in `P(C)` are universal); 6.2.2.7; 6.2.3.4, 6.2.3.5, 6.2.3.6, 6.2.3.16, 6.2.3.18; 6.2.2.5.

**A local surjectivity criterion** (HTT Lemma 6.2.4.5, PDF p. 616). In `Shv(C)`, a morphism `u : F₀ ⟶ F` is an effective epimorphism when every point of `π₀ F(C)` lifts locally: it restricts, along a family generating a covering sieve on C, to images of points of `π₀ F₀(Cα)`.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.5, 6.2.2.6, 6.2.2.7 (`Shv(C)` is an ∞-topos and L preserves colimits); 6.1.3.10; 6.2.3.4, 6.2.3.5, 6.2.3.12 (reduction to a monomorphism through the image); 5.1.5.8 (L6.3).

**Comparison with sheaves for the canonical topology** (HTT Proposition 6.2.4.6, PDF pp. 617–618). Let X be a semitopos, C small with finite limits, `F ⊣ G : P(C) ⇄ X` with `f = F ∘ j` left exact, and C carry the canonical topology relative to f. Then G factors through `Shv(C)`; and if f is fully faithful and its image generates X under colimits, G carries effective epimorphisms of X to effective epimorphisms of `Shv(C)`.

*Needs:* 6.2.4.2, 6.2.4.5; 6.2.3.12, 6.2.3.15, 6.2.3.18; 6.2.2.6.

## Layer L11: The ∞-category of ∞-topoi, n-topoi, homotopy theory in an ∞-topos

HTT §§6.3–6.5, with Proposition 5.5.7.6 (limits in `Pr^R_κ`), which waits for Lemma 6.3.3.7, and the statements of §§7.2.1 and 7.3.4 about arbitrary ∞-topoi that §§6.3–6.5 use (L11.4). Inputs: L10 (∞-topoi, descent, Grothendieck topologies, effective epimorphisms), L7 (presentability, `Pr^L`, `Pr^R`, truncation, strongly saturated classes), L6 (adjunctions, reflective localizations, presheaves, simplicial and groupoid objects).

Conventions used throughout:

- An ∞-topos is a large ∞-category, an `SSet.{u + 1}` (Universes convention). `Cat∞^` is `SSet.catInfty` one universe up (L4.1), and `LTop`, `RTop`, `Pr^R_κ` are HTT 1.2.11 subcategories of it (L1.3).
- "Left exact" for a functor between ∞-categories with finite limits means that it preserves finite limits; the Lean predicate is L6.6's `SSet.IsLeftExact`. "Colimit-preserving" means preserving small colimits.
- The L10 names used below are proposals: `SSet.IsInftyTopos` (HTT 6.1.0.4), `SSet.IsEffectiveEpi` (effective epimorphisms, §6.2.3), `SSet.sheaf J` for `Shv(C)` with J a Mathlib `GrothendieckTopology` on `hoFunctor.obj C` (6.2.2.6), and "colimits are universal" (6.1.1.2), "the class of S-morphisms is local" (6.1.3.8), "Cartesian transformation" (6.1.3.1) by their HTT numbers. L6 and L7 names are those of those layers (`SSet.presheaf`, `SSet.IsReflectiveLocalization`, `SSet.IsReflectiveSubcategory`, `SSet.IsGroupoidObject`, `SSet.IsCechNerve`, `SSet.IsEffectiveGroupoid`, `SSet.IsGeometricRealization`, `SSet.simplicialObjects`, `SSet.semisimplicialObjects`, `SSet.IsPresentable`, `SSet.prL`, `SSet.prR`, `SSet.prRCardinal`, `SSet.IsTruncatedObject`, `SSet.IsTruncatedMorphism`, `SSet.IsStronglySaturated`, `SSet.IsLocalObject`, `SSet.IsStronglyReflective`, `SSet.IsAccessibleSubcategory`, `SSet.IsCompactlyGenerated`), and `SSet.IsNCategory` is L3's.
- `P_{≤n−1}(C) ⊆ P(C)` is the full subcategory of (n − 1)-truncated presheaves, and `Shv_{≤n−1}(C) ⊆ Shv(C)` that of (n − 1)-truncated sheaves.

Departures from Lurie's text, each recorded in its entry:

- Jardine's local model structure (6.5.2.1) is stated with the combinatorial description of local weak equivalences (`Ex^∞` and simplicial spheres in place of geometric realization and topological spheres).
- Coherent spaces (6.5.4.4, 6.5.4.5) are stated with Mathlib's classes `CompactSpace`, `QuasiSeparatedSpace` and `PrespectralSpace`, which together are Lurie's definition; Mathlib's `SpectralSpace` adds `T0Space` and `QuasiSober` and is not used.
- §6.5.4 uses Mathlib's general topology (the Hilbert cube, finite spaces, coherent spaces) and nothing from AlgebraicTopology.
- Lurie's proofs of 6.5.1.12, 6.5.1.20 and 7.2.1.14 are circular: 6.5.1.12 and 6.5.1.20 apply 7.2.1.14, whose proof applies 7.2.1.13, whose proof applies 6.5.1.12, 6.5.1.16 and 6.5.1.20. The entries of 6.5.1.12 and 7.2.1.14 give a repair route that breaks the cycle.

The items are written in the book's order. Three of them need L11.4:

- L11.1 needs L11.4: the proofs of Lemma 6.3.3.4, Proposition 6.3.3.8 and Proposition 6.3.6.2 apply Example 7.3.4.7 (filtered colimits in an ∞-topos are left exact).
- L11.2 needs L11.4: the proof of Proposition 6.4.4.7, and through it part `2⇒4` of Theorem 6.4.1.5, applies Lemma 7.2.1.13. It also needs L11.3: the hypothesis of 7.2.1.13 there, that Y is (n + 1)-connective over `τ_{≤n} Y`, comes from 6.5.1.12.
- L11.3 needs L11.4: the proof of Proposition 6.5.2.8 applies Proposition 7.2.1.14, and so do Lurie's proofs of 6.5.1.12 and 6.5.1.20 (repaired below).

Inside L11.2, Theorem 6.4.1.5 is proved by later statements of the same item (6.4.1.6, 6.4.2.1, 6.4.3.4, 6.4.3.6, 6.4.4.6–6.4.4.9), and Proposition 6.4.3.6 applies Lemma 6.4.4.8; inside L11.1, Theorem 6.3.5.13 is proved by 6.3.5.14–6.3.5.28. Nothing in L11.4 uses L11.1, and L11.4 uses only Definition 6.4.1.1 from L11.2, so the formalization order is: Definition 6.4.1.1 and §7.3.4 (L11.4); L11.1; §6.5.1 through 6.5.1.19 with the repair lemma of 6.5.1.12; Proposition 7.2.1.14; Proposition 6.5.1.20; Lemma 7.2.1.13; the rest of L11.2 and L11.3.

### L11.1 The ∞-category of ∞-topoi

**Geometric morphisms** (`SSet.IsGeometricMorphism`; HTT Definition 6.3.1.1, PDF p. 618). For ∞-topoi X and Y, a functor `f_* : X ⟶ Y` is a geometric morphism when it has a left adjoint `f^*` that is left exact. Either adjoint determines the other up to contractible choice, and HTT often names a geometric morphism by its left adjoint.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsGeometricMorphism (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := ∃ g : Y ⟶ X, SSet.IsAdjunction g f ∧ SSet.IsLeftExact g` for quasicategories X, Y, with `SSet.IsAdjunction` (L10, 6.1.0.4) the adjunction in `SSet.QCat.bicategory` (`HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`); targets about ∞-topoi state `SSet.IsInftyTopos` as hypotheses.

**Checks.** Equivalences of ∞-topoi are geometric morphisms; a functor naturally equivalent to a geometric morphism is one; composites of geometric morphisms are geometric morphisms.

*Needs:* `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`; 6.1.0.4 (L10).

**`LTop` and `RTop`** (`SSet.lTop`, `SSet.rTop`; HTT Definition 6.3.1.5, PDF p. 619). The subcategories of `Cat∞^` whose objects are the ∞-topoi, with morphisms in `LTop` the left exact colimit-preserving functors and morphisms in `RTop` the geometric morphisms. They are canonically anti-equivalent (6.3.1.8).

*Lean:* `SSet.lTop` and `SSet.rTop`, the HTT 1.2.11 subcategories of `SSet.catInfty.{u + 1}` whose vertices are ∞-topoi and whose edges are, respectively, left exact functors preserving small colimits (`SSet.PreservesColimit` for all small diagrams) and `SSet.IsGeometricMorphism` functors.

*Needs:* 6.3.1.1; `HTT.1.2.11/intro`; `SSet.catInfty` (HTT 3.0.0.1, L4.1); 5.5.3.4 (L7, the model for the anti-equivalence).

**Topos fibrations** (`SSet.ToposFibration`; HTT Definition 6.3.1.6, Proposition 6.3.1.7, Corollary 6.3.1.8, PDF p. 619). A map `p : X ⟶ S` of simplicial sets is a topos fibration when it is both a Cartesian and a coCartesian fibration, every fibre `X_s` is an ∞-topos, and for every edge `s ⟶ s'` the covariant transport `X_s ⟶ X_{s'}` is left exact (6.3.1.6). A Cartesian fibration classified by `χ : S^op ⟶ Cat∞^` is a topos fibration exactly when χ factors through `RTop`, and a coCartesian fibration classified by `S ⟶ Cat∞^` is one exactly when the classifying map factors through `LTop` (6.3.1.7). Hence, for every simplicial set S, equivalence classes in `Fun(S, LTop)` and `Fun(S^op, RTop)` correspond, and `LTop ≃ RTop^op` in the homotopy category of ∞-categories (6.3.1.8).

*Lean:* `structure SSet.ToposFibration p : Prop extends CartesianFibration p` with fields `cocartesian : CocartesianFibration p` (L3.6's `CocartesianFibration` is a `def`, so it cannot be extended), `isInftyTopos_fibre : ∀ s, SSet.IsInftyTopos (fibre p s)` and `isLeftExact_transport`, left exactness of the covariant transport along every edge through a chosen `cocartesianTransport`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: 6.3.1.7 is the argument of 5.5.3.3, and 6.3.1.8 that of 5.5.3.4, with 2.4.2.1 for adjoint transports.

*Needs:* 6.3.1.5; 2.4.2.1 (L3); 5.5.3.3, 5.5.3.4 (L7); 6.1.0.4 (L10).

**Geometric morphisms preserve truncation** (HTT Proposition 6.3.1.9, PDF p. 620). For a geometric morphism `f_* : X ⟶ Y` with left adjoint `f^*`, both functors carry k-truncated objects and morphisms to k-truncated ones (k ≥ −2), and `f^* ∘ τ^Y_{≤k} ≃ τ^X_{≤k} ∘ f^*`.

*Needs:* 6.3.1.1; 5.5.6.1, 5.5.6.15–5.5.6.16, 5.5.6.28 (L7).

**`Fun_*` and `Fun^*`** (`SSet.funLowerStar`, `SSet.funUpperStar`; HTT Definition 6.3.1.10, PDF p. 620). For ∞-topoi X, Y, `Fun_*(X, Y) ⊆ Fun(X, Y)` is the full subcategory of geometric morphisms and `Fun^*(Y, X) ⊆ Fun(Y, X)` the full subcategory of their left adjoints, i.e. of left exact colimit-preserving functors.

*Lean:* `SSet.funLowerStar X Y := SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory {f | SSet.IsGeometricMorphism f}` in `(ihom X).obj Y`, and `SSet.funUpperStar Y X` the full subcategory of left exact functors preserving small colimits. Passing to adjoints gives `Fun_*(X, Y)^op ≃ Fun^*(Y, X)` (5.2.6.2, L6); state it.

*Needs:* 6.3.1.1; `HTT.1.2.11/intro`; 5.2.6.2 (L6).

**`Fun^*(Y, X)` is accessible** (HTT Proposition 6.3.1.13, PDF p. 620). For ∞-topoi X and Y, `Fun^*(Y, X)` is an accessible ∞-category.

*Proof route.* Lurie's (PDF pp. 620–621): choose κ with Y κ-accessible and `Y^κ` closed under finite limits (5.4.7.4), so `Y ≃ Ind_κ(C)` with `C ≃ Y^κ`. By 5.3.5.10 and 5.5.1.9, colimit-preserving functors `Y ⟶ X` are the `f : C ⟶ X` preserving κ-small colimits. Such an F is left exact exactly when `f = F ∘ j` is. Lurie cites 6.1.5.2 here, which is stated for `P(C)`; the step holds because every finite diagram in `Ind_κ(C)` is a κ-filtered colimit of diagrams in C (5.3.5.15), finite limits commute with κ-filtered colimits in `Ind_κ(C) ⊆ P(C)` (5.3.3.3, objectwise) and in X (7.3.4.7, L11.4), and j preserves finite limits (5.1.3.2). So `Fun^*(Y, X)` is the full subcategory of `Fun(C, X)` of functors preserving κ-small colimits and finite limits (5.2.6.2). It is accessible: `Fun(C, X)` is accessible (5.4.4.3), each condition is accessible (5.4.7.9), and there are boundedly many conditions (5.4.7.10).

*Needs:* 6.3.1.10; 5.1.3.2, 5.2.6.2, `HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if`, 5.3.5.10 (L6); 5.3.5.15, 5.4.2.1, 5.4.4.3, 5.4.7.4, 5.4.7.8–5.4.7.10, 5.5.1.9 (L7); 7.3.4.7 (L11.4, forward need).

**Products of ∞-topoi** (HTT Proposition 6.3.2.1, PDF p. 621). For a small family `{X_α}` of ∞-topoi, the product `X = ∏ X_α` is an ∞-topos, the projections `X ⟶ X_α` are left exact and colimit-preserving, and they exhibit X as a product of the family in `LTop`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, through the Giraud criterion 6.1.0.6 and 5.5.3.5 for presentability; products in `Cat∞^` are homotopy products (4.2.4.1).

*Needs:* 6.3.1.1, 6.3.1.5; 6.1.0.4, 6.1.0.6 (L10); 5.5.0.1, 5.5.3.5 (L7); 4.2.4.1 (L5).

**Pullbacks of ∞-topoi along left exact colimit-preserving functors** (HTT Proposition 6.3.2.2, PDF pp. 621–622). Let `X' ⟶ X`, `X' ⟶ Y'`, `p^* : X ⟶ Y`, `q^* : Y' ⟶ Y` form a categorical pullback square of ∞-categories (Terms), with X, Y, Y' ∞-topoi and `p^*`, `q^*` left exact and colimit-preserving. Then X' is an ∞-topos, and a functor `f^* : Z ⟶ X'` from an ∞-topos is left exact and colimit-preserving exactly when its composites with the two projections `X' ⟶ X` and `X' ⟶ Y'` are; in particular the projections are.

*Needs:* 6.3.1.5; 6.1.0.4, 6.1.0.6 (L10); 5.4.5.5, 5.5.3.12 (L7).

**`LTop` has small limits** (HTT Proposition 6.3.2.3, PDF p. 622). `LTop` admits small limits, and the inclusion `LTop ⊆ Cat∞^` preserves them.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: products (6.3.2.1) and pullbacks (6.3.2.2) generate small limits (4.4.2.6), computed in `Cat∞^` (4.2.4.1).

*Needs:* 6.3.2.1, 6.3.2.2; 4.2.4.1, 4.4.2.6 (L5).

**Filtered limits in `RTop`** (HTT Theorem 6.3.3.1, PDF p. 622). `RTop` admits limits of small filtered diagrams `C^op ⟶ RTop` (C a small filtered ∞-category), and the inclusion `RTop ⊆ Cat∞^` preserves them.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, modelled on 5.5.3.18: reduce to a topos fibration over `N(A)` for a filtered poset A (3.3.3.2, 5.3.1.18); the Cartesian sections form an ∞-topos (6.3.3.2, 6.3.3.3), the evaluations are geometric morphisms (6.3.3.5), and geometric morphisms into the limit are detected after evaluation (6.3.3.8).

*Needs:* 6.3.3.2, 6.3.3.3, 6.3.3.5, 6.3.3.8; 6.3.1.6–6.3.1.7; 3.3.3.2 (L5); 5.3.1.18 (L6); 5.5.3.17, 5.5.3.18 (L7).

**Sections of a topos fibration** (HTT Lemma 6.3.3.2, PDF p. 622). For a topos fibration `p : X ⟶ S` with S small, the ∞-category `Map_S(S, X)` of sections of p is an ∞-topos.

*Needs:* 6.3.1.6; 6.3.2.3 (hypothesis (a) of 5.4.7.11 for `C = LTop`: small limits, preserved by `LTop ⊆ Cat∞^`); 5.4.7.11 (L7); 6.1.0.6 (L10).

**Cartesian sections over a filtered poset** (HTT Proposition 6.3.3.3, PDF p. 623). For a small filtered poset A and a topos fibration `p : X ⟶ N(A)`, the full subcategory `C⁰` of Cartesian sections in `C = Map_{N(A)}(N(A), X)` is an accessible left exact localization of C.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the localization is built from right Kan extensions along the inclusions `N(A_{≥α}) ⊆ N(A)` (4.3.1.9–4.3.1.10, 4.3.2.15), and filteredness of A makes it left exact (4.4.4.10).

*Needs:* 6.3.3.2; 6.3.1.6; 2.4.1.1 (L3); 4.1.1.1, 4.3.1.9, 4.3.1.10, 4.3.2.15, 4.4.4.10 (L5); 5.2.7.2 (L6); 5.4.2.1 (L7).

**Intersections of accessible left exact localizations** (HTT Lemma 6.3.3.4, PDF p. 623). For an ∞-topos X and a small set `{L_α}` of accessible left exact localization functors `X ⟶ X`, the full subcategory `⋂_α L_α X` is an accessible left exact localization of X, hence an ∞-topos.

*Needs:* 5.2.7.2 (L6); 5.4.2.1, 5.5.4.15 (L7); 6.1.0.4, 6.2.1.1 (L10); 7.3.4.7 (L11.4, forward need).

**Evaluation of Cartesian sections is a geometric morphism** (HTT Proposition 6.3.3.5, PDF p. 624). For A a small filtered poset, `p : X ⟶ N(A)` a topos fibration, and `Y ⊆ Map_{N(A)}(N(A), X)` the Cartesian sections (the base of 6.3.3.3; Lurie prints `N(A)^op`, but his proof, through `A_{≥α}`, left Kan extensions from the least element α and 6.3.3.3, is over `N(A)`), every evaluation `Y ⟶ X_α` is a geometric morphism.

*Needs:* 6.3.3.3; 6.3.1.1, 6.3.1.6; 3.3.3.2, 4.1.3.1, 4.3.2.15 (L5); 4.3.2.17, 5.1.2.2 (L6).

**Cartesian sections over a colimit cone** (HTT Lemma 6.3.3.6, PDF p. 625). Let `p : X ⟶ S^▷` be a Cartesian fibration whose classifying functor `(S^▷)^op ⟶ Cat∞` is a limit diagram, and `s : S^▷ ⟶ X` a Cartesian section. Then s is a p-colimit diagram (relative colimit, L5.8).

*Needs:* 2.4.1.1, 2.4.4.2 (L3); 3.3.1.2 (L4); 3.3.3.1, 4.3.1.1 (L5).

**The identity of a limit of presentable ∞-categories as a colimit** (HTT Lemma 6.3.3.7, PDF p. 626). Let `p : X ⟶ S` be a presentable fibration (5.5.3.2), C the ∞-category of its Cartesian sections, `ψ(s)_* : C ⟶ X_s` evaluation at s and `ψ(s)^*` its left adjoint. There is a diagram `θ : S ⟶ Fun(C, C)` with `θ(s) ≃ ψ(s)^* ∘ ψ(s)_*` for every vertex s, of which `id_C` is a colimit in `Fun(C, C)`.

*Needs:* 6.3.3.6; 5.5.3.2, 5.5.3.18 (L7); 4.3.1.1, 4.3.1.9 (L5); 5.1.2.2 (L6).

**Limits in `Pr^R_κ`** (HTT Proposition 5.5.7.6, PDF p. 521). For κ regular, `Pr^R_κ` (`SSet.prRCardinal`, L7) admits small limits, and the inclusion `Pr^R_κ ⊆ Cat∞^` preserves them.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: limits are computed in `Pr^R` (5.5.3.18); 6.3.3.7 writes the identity of the limit as a colimit of composites `ψ(s)^* ψ(s)_*`, which shows that the limit is κ-compactly generated and that the projections preserve κ-filtered colimits (5.5.7.2).

*Needs:* 6.3.3.7; 5.5.3.18, 5.5.7.1, 5.5.7.2, 5.5.7.5 (L7).

**Geometric morphisms into a filtered limit** (HTT Proposition 6.3.3.8, PDF p. 627). With A, p and Y as in 6.3.3.3 (p over `N(A)`), a functor `π_* : Z ⟶ Y` from an ∞-topos is a geometric morphism as soon as every composite `Z ⟶ Y ⟶ X_α` is.

*Needs:* 6.3.3.7; 6.3.1.1; 6.1.0.4 (L10); 7.3.4.7 (L11.4, forward need).

**`S` is final in `RTop`** (HTT Proposition 6.3.4.1, PDF p. 628). For every ∞-topos X, `Fun^*(S, X)` (equivalently `Fun_*(X, S)`) is a contractible Kan complex; hence `S` is a final object of `RTop`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `S = Shv(Δ[0])` for the trivial topology, so 6.2.3.20 identifies `Fun^*(S, X)` with the left exact functors `Δ[0] ⟶ X`, i.e. the final objects of X, which form a contractible Kan complex (1.2.12.9).

*Needs:* 6.3.1.10; `HTT.1.2.12/final`, 1.2.12.9 (L2); 6.2.3.20 (L10).

**Freely forcing colimit diagrams** (HTT Lemma 6.3.4.2, PDF p. 628). For a small ∞-category C, κ regular and a small set of κ-small diagrams `f_α : K_α^▷ ⟶ C`, there is `F : C ⟶ D` with D small with κ-small colimits, each `F ∘ f_α` a colimit diagram, and, for every E with κ-small colimits, composition with F a fully faithful functor from κ-small-colimit-preserving functors `D ⟶ E` to `Fun(C, E)` with essential image the functors F' with every `F' ∘ f_α` a colimit diagram.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: D is the κ-compact objects of the localization of `P(C)` at the maps `colim (j ∘ f_α) ⟶ j(f_α(∞))` (5.5.4.20, 5.5.7.3), with 5.3.5.10–5.3.5.11 and 5.5.1.9.

*Needs:* 5.1.5.6, 5.3.4.5, 5.3.5.10, 5.3.5.11 (L6); 5.5.1.9, 5.5.4.20, 5.5.7.3 (L7).

**`Cat∞^lex`** (`SSet.catInftyLex`; HTT Definition 6.3.4.3, Lemma 6.3.4.4, PDF p. 629). `Cat∞^lex ⊆ Cat∞` is the subcategory of small ∞-categories with finite limits and left exact functors (6.3.4.3). It admits small colimits (6.3.4.4).

*Lean:* `SSet.catInftyLex`, the HTT 1.2.11 subcategory of `SSet.catInfty` whose vertices have finite limits and whose edges preserve finite limits.

*Proof route.* For 6.3.4.4, Lurie's dual of the construction of colimits in categories of κ-cocomplete ∞-categories: freely force the needed limit diagrams with (the dual of) 6.3.4.2.

*Needs:* 6.3.4.2; `HTT.1.2.11/intro`; 1.2.13.4.

**Geometric morphisms into `P(C)`** (HTT Lemma 6.3.4.5, PDF p. 630). For C small with finite limits and a geometric morphism `f_* : X ⟶ P(C)`, there are D small with finite limits and a left exact `f'' : C ⟶ D` such that `f_*` factors as a fully faithful geometric morphism `X ⟶ P(D)` followed by composition with f'', `P(D) ⟶ P(C)`.

*Needs:* 6.3.1.1; 5.1.5.6 (L6); 5.4.7.4 (L7); 6.1.5.2, 6.1.5.3 (L10).

**`RTop` has pullbacks and small limits** (HTT Proposition 6.3.4.6, Corollary 6.3.4.7, PDF pp. 631–632). `RTop` admits pullbacks (6.3.4.6), and hence small limits (6.3.4.7: with the final object 6.3.4.1 and filtered limits 6.3.3.1, by 4.2.3.11 and 4.4.2.4).

*Proof route.* For 6.3.4.6, Lurie's: present the three ∞-topoi as localizations of presheaf ∞-categories on ∞-categories with finite limits (6.3.4.5), take the pushout in `Cat∞^lex` (6.3.4.4), and localize (5.5.4.15, 6.2.1.2).

*Needs:* 6.3.4.4, 6.3.4.5, 6.3.4.1, 6.3.3.1; 5.1.5.6 (L6); 5.5.4.5, 5.5.4.7, 5.5.4.15 (L7); 6.1.5.2, 6.1.5.3, 6.2.1.2 (L10); 4.2.3.11, 4.4.2.4 (L5).

**Classifying ∞-topoi for diagrams of points** (HTT Proposition 6.3.4.9, PDF p. 632). For an ∞-topos X and a small ∞-category C there are an ∞-topos `Mor(C, X)` and a functor `e : C ⟶ Fun_*(Mor(C, X), X)` such that, for every ∞-topos Y, composition with e is an equivalence `Fun_*(Y, Mor(C, X)) ⟶ Fun(C, Fun_*(Y, X))`.

*Lean:* the statement is existence of the pair `(Mor(C, X), e)` with the universal property; no definition is needed beyond `SSet.funLowerStar`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: for `X = P(C')` take a presheaf ∞-category on a free finite-limit construction (6.3.4.2 with 5.1.5.6, 6.1.5.2), then localize for general X (6.1.5.3, 5.5.4.15, 6.2.1.2).

*Needs:* 6.3.4.2; 6.3.1.10; 5.1.5.6 (L6); 5.5.4.5, 5.5.4.7, 5.5.4.15 (L7); 6.1.3.4, 6.1.5.2, 6.1.5.3, 6.2.1.2 (L10).

**Slices of an ∞-topos; étale geometric morphisms** (`SSet.IsEtaleGeometricMorphism`; HTT Proposition 6.3.5.1 and the definition after it, the prose after Remark 6.3.5.2, Remark 6.3.5.3, PDF pp. 634–635). For an ∞-topos X and an object U: `X_{/U}` is an ∞-topos; the projection `π_! : X_{/U} ⟶ X` has a colimit-preserving right adjoint `π^* = U × −`, which therefore has a right adjoint `π_*`, a geometric morphism. A geometric morphism `f_* : X ⟶ Y` is *étale* when it factors as a categorical equivalence `X ⟶ Y_{/U}` followed by such a `π_*`; then `f^*` has a left adjoint `f_!` and preserves all small limits. Étale geometric morphisms contain the equivalences and are closed under composition; `RTop^ét ⊆ RTop` and `LTop^ét ⊆ LTop` are the subcategories with étale morphisms (a left adjoint `f^*` is étale when `f_*` is), and `RTop^ét ≃ (LTop^ét)^op`.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsEtaleGeometricMorphism (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop := ∃ (U : Y _⦋0⦌) (e : X ⟶ Y_{/U}), SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence e ∧ (f ≅ e ≫ π_*)` (isomorphism in `hFun`), with `π_*` a chosen right adjoint of `U × − : Y ⟶ Y_{/U}` (`SSet.slice`, Tau Ceti); `SSet.rTopEt`, `SSet.lTopEt` the corresponding subcategories.

**Checks.** `id : X ⟶ X` is étale (U final); for X = `S` and U a Kan complex, `S_{/U} ≃ Fun(U, S)` (straightening, L4) and `π^*` is the constant-diagram functor.

*Needs:* 6.3.1.1; 6.1.0.4, 6.1.0.6 (L10); 5.5.3.10 (L7); 4.4.2.9 (L5); 1.2.13.8 (L2).

**Classifying ∞-topoi for sections** (`SSet.IsClassifyingToposForSections`; HTT Definition 6.3.5.4, Proposition 6.3.5.5, PDF p. 636). Let `f^* : X ⟶ Y` be the left adjoint of a geometric morphism from Y to X, U an object of X and `α : 1_Y ⟶ f^* U`. Then α exhibits Y as a classifying ∞-topos for sections of U when, for every ∞-topos Z, the square formed by composition `Fun^*(Y, Z) ⟶ Fun^*(X, Z)`, evaluation at α into the pointed objects `Z_*` and evaluation at U into Z is a categorical pullback square (6.3.5.4). Such Y is unique up to equivalence. For U in X, with `π^* : X ⟶ X_{/U}` and α adjoint to `π_!(1_U) ≃ U`, α exhibits `X_{/U}` as the classifying ∞-topos for sections of U (6.3.5.5).

*Parts.* Proposition 6.3.5.5 is formalized as two targets: the part that follows this entry, `HTT.6.3.5.5/right-kan` (functors on the correspondence of `π_! ⊣ π^*`), and the target `HTT.6.3.5.5`, which shows that the restrictions `C ⟶ C' ⟶ C''` are trivial fibrations, u by `HTT.6.3.5.5/right-kan` and 4.3.2.15 and v because `M'' ⊆ M'` is a categorical equivalence (3.2.2.7), and with the retraction `r : M ⟶ X_{/U}` identifies `Fun^*(X_{/U}, Z)` with `Z_* ×_Z Fun^*(X, Z)`.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsClassifyingToposForSections (fstar : X ⟶ Y) (U) (α : Edge 1_Y (fstar U)) : Prop`, quantifying over ∞-topoi Z in the universe of X and Y: the square in `SSet.catInfty.{u + 1}` is an `SSet.IsPullback` (categorical pullback). `Z_*` is L6.8's pointed objects (`HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed`).

*Proof route.* Lurie's (6.3.5.5), through left Kan extensions along `X_{/U} ⟶ X` and 4.3.2.15, with 3.2.2.7 and 4.1.3.1; the characterization of the relevant functors on the correspondence is `HTT.6.3.5.5/right-kan`.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.3.5.5/right-kan` (below); 6.3.5.1, 6.3.1.10; `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed` (L6.8); 3.2.2.7 (L4); 4.1.3.1, 4.3.2.15 (L5); 5.2.1.1 (L6); `HTT.A.2.4.3/after` (F1, homotopy pullbacks).

**Functors on the correspondence of `π_! ⊣ π^*`** (`HTT.6.3.5.5/right-kan`, the only part of Proposition 6.3.5.5 in classifying ∞-topoi for sections above; HTT Proposition 6.3.5.5, step (∗) of the proof, PDF pp. 638–640). Let `M ⟶ Δ[1]` be the correspondence associated to `π_! : X_{/U} ⇄ X : π^*`, M′ ⊆ M the full subcategory on X and the object `1_U`, and Z an ∞-topos. A functor `F : M ⟶ Z` restricts on `X_{/U}` to a functor preserving small colimits and finite limits and carries the Cartesian edges over Δ[1] to equivalences if and only if its restriction to X preserves small colimits and finite limits, `F(1_U)` is final, and F is right Kan extended from M′.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. "Only if": write `F = F_0 ∘ r` and check that the squares `V ⟶ π^* V`, `1_U ⟶ π^* U` are pullbacks (1.2.13.8). "If": paste pullback squares, and on `X_{/U}` use the formula `V ↦ F(π_! V) ×_{F(U)} F(1_U)`, which preserves colimits by universality of colimits in Z (4.4.2.9).

*Needs:* 4.3.2.15, 4.1.3.1, 4.4.2.9 (L5); 1.2.13.8 (L2).

**Consequences of the universal property** (HTT Corollary 6.3.5.6, Remarks 6.3.5.7–6.3.5.8, Corollary 6.3.5.9, PDF pp. 636–637). For U in X and every ∞-topos Z, composition with `π^* : X ⟶ X_{/U}` is a left fibration `Fun^*(X_{/U}, Z) ⟶ Fun^*(X, Z)` whose fibre over `φ^*` is homotopy equivalent to `Map_Z(1_Z, φ^* U)` (6.3.5.6). Hence fibre sequences `Map_Z(1_Z, φ^* U) ⟶ Map_{LTop}(X_{/U}, Z) ⟶ Map_{LTop}(X, Z)`, and `Map_X(V, U) ≃ Map_{LTop_{X/}}(X_{/U}, X_{/V})` (6.3.5.7); for a geometric morphism with left adjoint `f^* : X ⟶ Y` and U in X, the square of `X ⟶ Y`, `X_{/U} ⟶ Y_{/f^*U}` is a pushout in `LTop` (6.3.5.8); in a commutative triangle in `LTop^op` with `g_*` étale, `f_*` is étale exactly when `h_*` is (6.3.5.9).

*Needs:* 6.3.5.5; 6.3.1.1; 2.0.0.3 (L2, left fibrations); 6.1.0.4 (L10).

**The ∞-topoi étale over X** (HTT Remark 6.3.5.10, PDF p. 637). The target projection `Fun(Δ[1], X) ⟶ X` is a Cartesian fibration whose transports `α^* : X_{/V} ⟶ X_{/U}` are étale, so it is classified by `X^op ⟶ LTop^ét`; the induced `χ : X^op ⟶ (LTop^ét)_{X/}` is fully faithful and essentially surjective, and identifies X with the full subcategory of `(LTop^op)_{/X}` on the ∞-topoi étale over X.

*Needs:* 6.3.5.7, 6.3.5.9; 2.4.2.1 (L3); `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`, `HTT.1.2.10/essentially-surjective`.

**Recognizing étale morphisms** (HTT Proposition 6.3.5.11, PDF p. 640). A geometric morphism with left adjoint `f^* : X ⟶ Y` is étale exactly when `f^*` has a left adjoint `f_!` (equivalently, by 5.5.2.9, `f^*` preserves small limits), `f_!` is conservative, and for every `X ⟶ Y` in X, Z in Y and `f_! Z ⟶ Y`, the square of `f_!(f^* X ×_{f^* Y} Z) ⟶ f_! Z` over `X ⟶ Y` is a pullback (the push-pull formula).

*Proof route.* Lurie's; the converse direction identifies Y with `X_{/f_! 1}` through 5.2.5.1 (adjunctions on slices).

*Needs:* 6.3.5.1; 6.3.1.1; 5.2.5.1 (L6); 5.5.2.9 (L7).

**`RTop^ét` has small colimits** (HTT Theorem 6.3.5.13, PDF p. 641). `RTop^ét` admits small colimits, and the inclusion `RTop^ét ⊆ RTop` preserves them.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.6.3.5.13/etale-colimit` (étale cocones), `HTT.6.3.5.13/coproducts` (coproducts of étale morphisms) and `HTT.6.3.5.13/coequalizers` (realizations of étale simplicial objects), and this entry's own target `HTT.6.3.5.13`, which combines coproducts and coequalizers through 4.4.3.2.

*Lean:* with `SSet.rTopEt : (catInfty.{u + 1}).Subcomplex` (∞-topoi, étale geometric morphisms), `HasSmallColimits.{u + 2, u} SSet.rTopEt` and `PreservesSmallColimits.{u + 2, u}` of `Subcomplex.homOfLE (rTopEt ≤ rTop)`; small means diagrams in `SSet.{u}`, and U does not enter.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: for diagrams of ∞-topoi étale over a fixed X it follows from 6.3.5.10 and 6.3.5.14, which gives étale cocones (`HTT.6.3.5.13/etale-colimit`); in general, coproducts (`HTT.6.3.5.13/coproducts`) and geometric realizations (`HTT.6.3.5.13/coequalizers`) suffice (4.4.3.2); for the latter, simplicial objects are replaced by groupoid objects (6.3.5.15), and these are glued as representable sheaves on `LTop^op` (6.3.5.21–6.3.5.28).

*Needs:* `HTT.6.3.5.13/etale-colimit`, `HTT.6.3.5.13/coproducts`, `HTT.6.3.5.13/coequalizers` (below); 6.1.2.12 (L6); 4.2.2.4, 4.3.3.2, 4.4.3.2 (L5); 6.1.3.17 (L10).

**Étale cocones** (`HTT.6.3.5.13/etale-colimit`, part 1 of 3 of the small colimits of `RTop^ét` above; HTT Theorem 6.3.5.13, step (∗) of the proof, PDF pp. 641–642). For a small diagram `p : K ⟶ LTop^op` and a geometric morphism from `colim p` to Y whose restriction to each `p(v)` is étale, the morphism `colim p ⟶ Y` is étale.

*Proof route.* By 6.3.5.10 the lifted diagram factors through `Y ⟶ LTop^op_{/Y}`, `V ↦ Y_{/V}`; with U a colimit in Y, 6.3.5.9 gives `colim p ≃ Y_{/U}`.

*Needs:* 6.3.5.9, 6.3.5.10.

**Coproducts of étale morphisms** (`HTT.6.3.5.13/coproducts`, part 2 of 3 of the small colimits of `RTop^ét` above; HTT Theorem 6.3.5.13, step (a) of the proof, PDF p. 642). `(LTop^ét)^op` has small coproducts, and the inclusion into `LTop^op` preserves them: the projections `∏ X_β ⟶ X_α` are étale.

*Proof route.* 6.3.5.11, with the object that is final in the α-th factor and initial in the others; then `HTT.6.3.5.13/etale-colimit`.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.3.5.13/etale-colimit`; 6.3.5.11.

**Realizations of étale simplicial objects** (`HTT.6.3.5.13/coequalizers`, part 3 of 3 of the small colimits of `RTop^ét` above; HTT Theorem 6.3.5.13, step (b) of the proof and the reduction after Lemma 6.3.5.15, PDF pp. 642–644). For a simplicial object `X_•` of `(LTop^ét)^op`, the leg `X_0 ⟶ |X_•|` of its realization in `LTop^op` is étale. Consequently `(LTop^ét)^op` has coequalizers, and the inclusion preserves them.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. A coequalizer diagram extends by left Kan extension to a simplicial object (4.3.2.7), so it suffices to treat simplicial objects. By 6.3.5.15 one may assume `X_•` is a groupoid object. Classify it by a Cartesian and coCartesian fibration `Z ⟶ N(Δ)^op` (3.3.3.1, 5.2.2.4), identify the realization with the Cartesian sections (6.3.2.3), and exhibit the pullback to `X_0` as a slice by a coCartesian lift of the shift `[n] ↦ [n] ⋆ [0]`.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.3.5.13/etale-colimit`; 6.3.5.9, 6.3.5.14, 6.3.5.15; 6.3.2.3; 3.3.3.1, 4.2.2.4, 4.3.2.7 (L5); 5.2.2.4 (L6); 6.1.3.17 (L10).

**Colimits of ∞-topoi étale over X** (HTT Proposition 6.3.5.14, PDF p. 641). For an ∞-topos X, the functor `χ : X ⟶ (LTop^op)_{/X}` of 6.3.5.10 preserves small colimits.

*Needs:* 6.3.5.10; 6.3.2.3; 6.1.3.9 (L10, descent); 1.2.13.8 (L2).

**Replacing simplicial objects by groupoid objects** (HTT Lemma 6.3.5.15, PDF p. 643). For a simplicial object `X_•` of `(LTop^ét)^op` there is a map of simplicial objects `X_• ⟶ X'_•` in `(LTop^ét)^op` that is an equivalence in degree 0, with `X'_•` a groupoid object of `LTop^op`, inducing an equivalence of geometric realizations in `LTop^op`.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as two targets: the part that follows this entry, `HTT.6.3.5.15/universal` (the leg `F_0 ⟶ |F_•|` is universal with small fibres), and this entry's own target `HTT.6.3.5.15`, which takes the Čech nerve of `F_0 ⟶ F`, whose terms are representable by ∞-topoi étale over `X_0` (6.3.5.25), so that it is the image of a groupoid object `X'_•` of `LTop^op`, étale by 6.3.5.9, and compares the realizations through effectivity of groupoids in `Shv(LTop^op)` (6.3.5.21).

*Needs:* `HTT.6.3.5.15/universal` (below); 6.3.5.9, 6.3.5.21, 6.3.5.25; `SSet.IsGroupoidObject` (6.1.2.7, L7); 6.1.2.11 (L6.8, Čech nerves).

**The leg `F_0 ⟶ |F_•|` is universal with small fibres** (`HTT.6.3.5.15/universal`, the only part of the replacement of simplicial objects by groupoid objects above; HTT Lemma 6.3.5.15, step (∗) of the proof, PDF pp. 651–653). Let `X_•` be a simplicial object of `(LTop^ét)^op`, `F_•` its image under the Yoneda embedding into `Shv(LTop^op)`, and F its realization. Then `F_0 ⟶ F` satisfies conditions (1) and (2) of 6.3.5.25.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: universality is 6.3.5.24. For small fibres, restrict to each ∞-topos Y (6.3.5.28 reduces to pointwise statements on `Fun(Y^op, Ŝ)`); the values have essentially small components (6.3.1.13) and the structure maps have essentially small fibres (6.3.5.7), so 6.3.5.27 applies.

*Needs:* 6.3.5.3, 6.3.5.7, 6.3.5.24, 6.3.5.27, 6.3.5.28 (its parts `HTT.6.3.5.28/left-exact` and `HTT.6.3.5.28/small-fibres`); 6.3.1.13.

**Sheaves on an ∞-topos with values in large spaces** (HTT Notation 6.3.5.16, Remarks 6.3.5.17–6.3.5.18, PDF pp. 644–645). For an ∞-topos X and an ∞-category C, `Shv_C(X) ⊆ Fun(X^op, C)` is the full subcategory of limit-preserving functors (HTT Notation 6.3.5.16, stated here). Let `Ŝ` be the ∞-category of spaces of a larger universe U (Universes convention: level `u + 2`, `Ŝ = SSet.spaces.{u + 2}`, the same for all of 6.3.5.17–6.3.5.28). Then the Yoneda embedding `X ≃ Shv_S(X)` (5.5.2.2); `Shv_Ŝ(X)` is an ∞-topos in U, and `Shv_S(X) ⊆ Shv_Ŝ(X)` preserves small colimits (6.3.5.17). For a geometric morphism with left adjoint `f^* : X ⟶ Y`, the induced functor `f̂^* : Shv_Ŝ(X) ⟶ Shv_Ŝ(Y)` (through `Shv_Ŝ ≃ Ind_κ̂`, 5.3.5.4) is the left adjoint of a geometric morphism in U (6.3.5.18).

*Lean (Notation 6.3.5.16):* `SSet.sheavesValuedOnTopos.{v, u} X C` (propose), for `X C : SSet.{v}`, the `SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory` of `Fun(Xᵒᵖ, C)` on the functors preserving limits of all diagrams indexed by `K : SSet.{u}` (the dual of `SSet.PreservesColimit`, L5.6); the small universe u is a separate parameter, given explicitly, so that lifting X does not make the limits large. The larger universe U of 6.3.5.17–6.3.5.28 is level `u + 2`, `Ŝ = SSet.spaces.{u + 2} : SSet.{u + 3}`, and for an ∞-topos `Y : SSet.{u + 1}`, `Shv_Ŝ(Y)` is `sheavesValuedOnTopos.{u + 3, u} (uliftFunctor.{u + 3}.obj Y) spaces.{u + 2}`.

*Lean (Remark 6.3.5.17):* (a) `IsInftyTopos.{u + 2}` of `Shv_Ŝ(X) : SSet.{u + 3}`; (b) `PreservesSmallColimits.{u + 3, u}` of the inclusion `uliftFunctor.{u + 3}.obj (sheavesValuedOnTopos.{u + 1, u} X spaces.{u}) ⟶ Shv_Ŝ(X)`.

*Lean (Remark 6.3.5.18):* κ is `Cardinal.univ.{u, u + 2}` (regular by `Cardinal.IsInaccessible.univ`), and `Shv_Ŝ(X) ≃ SSet.ind κ (uliftFunctor.{u + 2}.obj X)` in `SSet.{u + 3}`; for a geometric morphism with left adjoint `f^* : X ⟶ Y`, composition with `f^*`, `Shv_Ŝ(Y) ⟶ Shv_Ŝ(X)`, satisfies `SSet.IsGeometricMorphism` (at level `u + 3`).

*Needs:* 5.1.2.2, 5.1.5.6, 5.2.6.3, 5.3.5.4 (L6); 5.3.4.15, 5.3.5.15, 5.4.1.5, 5.5.2.2, 5.5.4.5, 5.5.4.7, 5.5.4.20 (L7); 6.1.3.4 (L10); 1.2.16.1; 6.3.1.1; 7.3.4.7 (L11.4, forward need, for 6.3.5.18).

**Sheaves on `LTop^op`** (HTT Notation 6.3.5.19, Example 6.3.5.20, Lemma 6.3.5.21, PDF p. 646). For `F : LTop ⟶ Ŝ` and an ∞-topos X, `F_X : X^op ⟶ Ŝ` is the composite `X^op ≃ LTop^ét_{X/} ⟶ LTop ⟶ Ŝ` (6.3.5.10); F is a sheaf when every `F_X` preserves small limits, and `Shv(LTop^op) ⊆ Fun(LTop, Ŝ)` is the full subcategory of sheaves; F is representable when `F ≃ e_X = Map_{LTop}(X, −)`, and every `e_X` is a sheaf by 6.3.5.14 (HTT Notation 6.3.5.19 and Example 6.3.5.20, stated here). Lemma 6.3.5.21: `Shv(LTop^op)` is an ∞-topos in U, and each restriction `F ↦ F_X`, `Shv(LTop^op) ⟶ Shv_Ŝ(X)`, preserves U-small colimits and finite limits.

*Parts.* Lemma 6.3.5.21 is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.6.3.5.21/topos-fibration` (the topos fibration of Ŝ-valued sheaves) and `HTT.6.3.5.21/sections` (sheaves on `LTop^op` as sections), and the target `HTT.6.3.5.21`, which applies 5.4.7.11 to the topos fibration and its sections.

*Lean (Notation 6.3.5.19):* for `F : uliftFunctor.{u + 3}.obj SSet.lTop ⟶ spaces.{u + 2}` (`LTop : SSet.{u + 2}` is U-small), `F_X : uliftFunctor.{u + 3}.obj (uliftFunctor.{u + 2}.obj Xᵒᵖ) ⟶ spaces.{u + 2}` is the `uliftFunctor.{u + 3}` image of the composite of a chosen equivalence `uliftFunctor.{u + 2}.obj Xᵒᵖ ⟶ LTop^ét_{X/}` (6.3.5.10) with the forgetful map to `SSet.lTop`, followed by F. `SSet.IsLTopSheaf F` says every `F_X` satisfies `PreservesSmallLimits.{u + 3, u}`, and `SSet.lTopSheaves : SSet.{u + 3}` is the full subcategory of `Fun(uliftFunctor.{u + 3}.obj SSet.lTop, Ŝ)` on sheaves. Propose.

*Lean (Lemma 6.3.5.21):* `IsInftyTopos.{u + 2} SSet.lTopSheaves`; each restriction `SSet.lTopSheaves ⟶ Shv_Ŝ(X)` satisfies `PreservesSmallColimits.{u + 3, u + 2}` (U-small colimits) and `PreservesFiniteLimits`.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.3.5.21/topos-fibration`, `HTT.6.3.5.21/sections` (below); 6.3.5.10, 6.3.5.14, 6.3.5.17; 6.3.2.3 (in the universe U: hypothesis (a) of 5.4.7.11 for `LTop`); 5.4.7.11 (L7).

**The topos fibration of Ŝ-valued sheaves** (`HTT.6.3.5.21/topos-fibration`, part 1 of 2 of Lemma 6.3.5.21 in sheaves on `LTop^op` above; HTT Lemma 6.3.5.21, first part of the proof, PDF pp. 646–647). Let `e : Fun^ét(Δ[1], LTop) ⟶ LTop` be evaluation at 0, a coCartesian fibration (6.3.5.8). There is a Cartesian fibration `p : K ⟶ LTop` whose objects are pairs `(X, F_X : LTop^ét_{X/} ⟶ Ŝ)` and whose Cartesian edges are characterized pointwise (3.2.2.13). Its full subcategory K⁰ on limit-preserving `F_X` is a topos fibration (6.3.1.6), with fibre `Shv_Ŝ(X)` over X and the pushforwards of 6.3.5.18.

*Needs:* 6.3.5.8, 6.3.5.17, 6.3.5.18, 6.3.5.19, 6.3.5.20; 6.3.1.6; 3.2.2.13 (L4).

**Sheaves on `LTop^op` as sections** (`HTT.6.3.5.21/sections`, part 2 of 2 of Lemma 6.3.5.21 in sheaves on `LTop^op` above; HTT Lemma 6.3.5.21, second part of the proof, PDF p. 647). The sections of K⁰ that carry étale morphisms to coCartesian edges (Lurie's equivalent conditions (a)–(d)) form a full subcategory `Y⁰` of `Fun(Fun^ét(Δ[1], LTop), Ŝ)`. Composition with the diagonal `LTop ⟶ Fun^ét(Δ[1], LTop)` is an equivalence `Y⁰ ≃ Shv(LTop^op)`.

*Proof route.* (a) ⇔ (b) ⇒ (c) ⇔ (d) by unwinding the definitions; (c) ⇒ (b) by two-out-of-three; then 4.3.2.15.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.3.5.21/topos-fibration`; 6.3.5.10, 6.3.5.14; 4.3.2.15 (L5).

**Universal morphisms of sheaves on `LTop^op`** (HTT Definition 6.3.5.22, Remarks 6.3.5.23 and 6.3.5.24, PDF p. 648). A morphism `α : F ⟶ G` in `Shv(LTop^op)` is universal when, for every geometric morphism with left adjoint `f^* : X ⟶ Y`, the square of `f̂^* F_X ⟶ f̂^* G_X` over `F_Y ⟶ G_Y` is a pullback in `Shv_Ŝ(Y)` (6.3.5.22). Universal morphisms are stable under pullback and composition and contain the equivalences (HTT Remark 6.3.5.23). If `p : K ⟶ Shv(LTop^op)` is a small diagram with colimit F and every edge of K maps to a universal morphism, so does every `p(v) ⟶ F` (6.3.5.24, by descent 6.1.3.9).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsUniversalMorphism α : Prop`, quantifying over geometric morphisms between ∞-topoi in `SSet.{u + 1}`, with the pullback squares in `sheavesValuedOnTopos.{u + 3, u} (uliftFunctor.{u + 3}.obj Y) spaces.{u + 2}` (6.3.5.16).

*Needs:* 6.3.5.18, 6.3.5.21; 6.1.3.9 (L10).

**Representability of universal morphisms** (HTT Lemma 6.3.5.25, PDF p. 648). For `α : F ⟶ G` in `Shv(LTop^op)` with G represented by an ∞-topos X, F is represented by an ∞-topos étale over X provided α is universal and, for every ∞-topos Y, the homotopy fibres of `F(Y) ⟶ G(Y)` are essentially small.

*Needs:* 6.3.5.7, 6.3.5.18, 6.3.5.21, 6.3.5.22, 6.3.5.24; 6.1.3.9 (L10); 5.5.2.2 (L7); 4.4.2.1 (L5.10, pasting the pullback squares).

**Smallness lemmas** (HTT Lemmas 6.3.5.27–6.3.5.28, PDF pp. 649–650). For κ uncountable regular and a simplicial object `X_•` of `S` whose spaces `X_n` have essentially κ-small components and whose structure maps have essentially κ-small homotopy fibres, the map `X_0 ⟶ |X_•|` has essentially κ-small homotopy fibres (6.3.5.27). For an ∞-topos X, the inclusion `Shv_Ŝ(X) ⊆ Fun(X^op, Ŝ)` has a left exact left adjoint L, which preserves pointwise essential smallness of values and of homotopy fibres of morphisms (6.3.5.28).

*Parts.* Lemma 6.3.5.28 is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.6.3.5.28/left-exact` (Ŝ-sheafification is left exact), `HTT.6.3.5.28/small-values` (it preserves small values) and `HTT.6.3.5.28/small-fibres` (it preserves small fibres), and the target `HTT.6.3.5.28`, which is their conjunction.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.3.5.28/left-exact`, `HTT.6.3.5.28/small-values`, `HTT.6.3.5.28/small-fibres` (below); 6.1.2.12 (L6); 6.1.3.6 (L10). Lurie cites 6.1.3.6 for "every Ŝ-valued sheaf on X is T-local" in 6.3.5.28 (2); that number appears to be a misprint, and the step holds because X is a κ-filtered colimit completion of `X^κ`, so a limit-preserving `X^op ⟶ Ŝ` is a right Kan extension of its restriction to `(X^κ)^op`.

**Ŝ-sheafification is left exact** (`HTT.6.3.5.28/left-exact`, part 1 of 3 of Lemma 6.3.5.28 in the smallness lemmas above; HTT Lemma 6.3.5.28 (1), PDF p. 650). For an ∞-topos X, the inclusion `Shv_Ŝ(X) ⊆ Fun(X^op, Ŝ)` has a left adjoint L, and L is left exact.

*Proof route.* Existence by 5.5.4.19; `L ∘ j ≃ j` for the Yoneda embedding j, which is left exact, so 6.1.5.2 applies.

*Needs:* 5.5.4.19 (L7); 6.1.5.2 (L10).
