**Sheafification preserves small values** (`HTT.6.3.5.28/small-values`, part 2 of 3 of Lemma 6.3.5.28 in the smallness lemmas above; HTT Lemma 6.3.5.28 (2), PDF p. 650). If every `F(X)` is essentially small, so is every `LF(X)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Replace F by its right Kan extension from `(X^κ)^op`, which L does not see. Identify such functors with Ŝ-valued sheaves on `P(X^κ)`, and use the left exact localization `Shv_Ŝ(P(X^κ)) ⟶ Shv_Ŝ(X)` of 6.3.5.17, which preserves the S-valued part. Lurie's citation of 6.1.3.6 for the T-locality of sheaves at this step appears to be a misprint (see the entry above); the step holds because X is a κ-filtered colimit completion of `X^κ`.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.3.5.28/left-exact`; 6.3.5.17; 4.3.2.15 (L5); 5.4.1.3 (L7).

**Sheafification preserves small fibres** (`HTT.6.3.5.28/small-fibres`, part 3 of 3 of Lemma 6.3.5.28 in the smallness lemmas above; HTT Lemma 6.3.5.28 (3), PDF pp. 650–651). If `α : F ⟶ G` has essentially small homotopy fibres pointwise, so does `Lα`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Fix `η ∈ LG(X)`. The U over X at which the fibres are small form a colimit-closed subcategory of `X_{/X}`, whose largest sieve is `X_{/X_0}` for a monomorphism `X_0 ⟶ X`. Left exactness of L forces `X_0 = X`. The fibre at X is `LF_0(X)` with `F_0 = F ×_G j(X)` small-valued, so `HTT.6.3.5.28/small-values` applies.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.3.5.28/left-exact`, `HTT.6.3.5.28/small-values`; 5.5.4.1, 5.5.4.7 (L7).

**Images and algebraic morphisms** (`SSet.geometricImage`, `SSet.IsAlgebraicGeometricMorphism`; HTT Definition 6.3.6.1, Proposition 6.3.6.2, PDF p. 653). For a geometric morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`, its image is the smallest full subcategory of X containing `f^* Y` and stable under small colimits and finite limits; f is algebraic when its image is all of X (6.3.6.1). The image Y' of `f : X ⟶ Z` is an ∞-topos, `Y' ⊆ X` is left exact and colimit-preserving, and f factors as `X ⟶ Y' ⟶ Z` with the second geometric morphism algebraic and the first, g, with `g^*` fully faithful (6.3.6.2).

*Lean:* `SSet.geometricImage f : Set (X _⦋0⦌)`, the intersection of all sets of objects containing the essential image of `f^*`, replete, and closed under small colimits and finite limits in X; `SSet.IsAlgebraicGeometricMorphism f := SSet.geometricImage f = Set.univ`.

*Needs:* 6.3.1.1; 5.1.5.7, 5.3.5.10, 5.3.5.11 (L6); 5.4.2.1, 5.4.4.3, 5.5.1.9 (L7); 6.1.0.6, 6.1.3.4 (L10); 7.3.4.7 (L11.4, forward need).

**Étale morphisms are algebraic** (HTT Proposition 6.3.6.4, PDF p. 654). Every étale geometric morphism is algebraic, and algebraic geometric morphisms are stable under filtered limits in `RTop`.

*Needs:* 6.3.6.1, 6.3.5.1; 6.3.3.1, 6.3.3.7 (filtered limits in `RTop` exist and are computed in `Cat∞^` as Cartesian sections, so 6.3.3.7 applies to them); 4.4.2.9 (L5).

### L11.2 n-topoi

**n-topoi** (`SSet.IsNTopos`; HTT Definition 6.4.1.1, PDF p. 657). For `0 ≤ n < ∞`, an ∞-category X is an n-topos when there are a small ∞-category C and an accessible left exact reflective localization `L : P_{≤n−1}(C) ⟶ X`. ∞-topoi are the case n = ∞ of 6.1.0.4 and are not this definition.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsNTopos (n : ℕ) (X : SSet.{u + 1}) [Quasicategory X] : Prop := ∃ (C : SSet.{u}) (_ : Quasicategory C) (L : P_{≤n−1}(C) ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ P_{≤n−1}(C)), SSet.IsAdjunction L g ∧ SSet.IsFullyFaithful g ∧ SSet.IsAccessibleFunctor.{u + 1, u} (L ≫ g) ∧ SSet.IsLeftExact L`, the shape of L10's 6.1.0.4. `P_{≤n−1}(C)` is the `SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory` of `SSet.presheaf C` on the objects with `SSet.IsTruncatedObject ((n : ℤ) − 1)`; the index is an integer, so for n = 0 these are the (−1)-truncated presheaves. Propose.

**Checks.** A 1-topos is the nerve of a Grothendieck topos (HTT Remark 6.4.1.3, through 6.1.0.1, L10); `τ_{≤n−1} S` is an n-topos.

*Needs:* `HTT.5.1.3/intro`, 5.2.7.2 (L6); 5.4.2.1, 5.5.6.1 (L7); 2.3.4.1 (L3).

**The characterization of n-topoi** (HTT Theorem 6.4.1.5 with its parts `HTT.6.4.1.5/stmt`, `HTT.6.4.1.5/1⇒2`, `HTT.6.4.1.5/2⇔3`, `HTT.6.4.1.5/2⇒4`, `HTT.6.4.1.5/4⇔5`, `HTT.6.4.1.5/4⇒6`, `HTT.6.4.1.5/6⇒1`, `HTT.6.4.1.5/n=0`, PDF p. 658). For X presentable and `0 ≤ n < ∞`, the following are equivalent (`/stmt` names the conditions):

1. X is equivalent to `Shv_{≤n−1}(C)` for a small n-category C with finite limits and a Grothendieck topology;
2. X is equivalent to `τ_{≤n−1} Y` for an ∞-topos Y;
3. X is an n-topos;
4. colimits in X are universal, X is equivalent to an n-category, and the (n − 2)-truncated morphisms of X form a local class;
5. colimits in X are universal, X is equivalent to an n-category, and for all sufficiently large regular κ some object classifies the (n − 2)-truncated relatively κ-compact morphisms;
6. the n-categorical Giraud axioms: X is equivalent to a presentable n-category, colimits are universal, coproducts are disjoint if n > 0, and every n-efficient groupoid object (6.4.3.1) is effective.

Each part is its own target: `n=0` is 6.4.2.1; for n > 0, `1⇒2` takes `Y = Shv(C)`; `2⇔3` is the presentation argument with the proof of 6.4.1.6; `2⇒4` is 6.4.4.6 (stated for n-topoi, so applied after `2⇔3`) with the `τ_{≤n−1}` case of 6.4.4.7; `4⇔5` is the proof of 6.1.6.8 (L10) repeated; `4⇒6` is 6.4.4.9; `6⇒1` is 6.4.3.6, whose hypothesis (iv), that the effective groupoids are exactly the n-efficient ones, follows from (6) with 6.4.3.4 (X is equivalent to an n-category, so effective groupoids are n-efficient). The theorem is the conjunction.

*Lean:* `List.TFAE` of the six conditions under the explicit hypothesis `(hX : SSet.IsPresentable X)` (a `def`, not a class), `(n : ℕ)`, each condition a separate `def` (the `/stmt` target) so that the parts can be stated as implications.

*Needs:* 6.4.1.1, 6.4.1.6, 6.4.2.1, 6.4.3.4 (for `6⇒1`), 6.4.3.6 (with its part `HTT.6.4.3.6/truncation-induction` for `6⇒1`), 6.4.4.6, 6.4.4.7, 6.4.4.9; 6.1.6.4, 6.1.6.8, 6.2.2.6 (L10); `SSet.IsGroupoidObject` (6.1.2.7, L7); 2.3.4.1 (L3); 5.5.0.1 (L7).

**Left exact localizations of n-topoi are topological** (HTT Proposition 6.4.1.6, PDF p. 658). For an n-topos X (0 ≤ n < ∞), every left exact reflective localization `L : X ⟶ Y` is topological (6.2.1.4).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: reduce to `X = P_{≤n−1}(C)` with C an n-category; the L-equivalences are generated by monomorphisms `U ⟶ j(C)`, through 6.2.2.17 and 5.5.6.15.

*Needs:* 6.4.1.1; 5.5.4.1, 5.5.4.5, 5.5.4.7, 5.5.6.13, 5.5.6.15 (L7); 6.2.1.4, 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.2, 6.2.2.17 (L10); 2.3.4.1 (L3).

**Locales** (HTT Definition 6.4.2.3, Example 6.4.2.4, PDF p. 661). A locale is a poset with all joins in which binary meets distribute over arbitrary joins (6.4.2.3); this is Mathlib's `Order.Frame` (the Heyting implication is determined by these conditions). The opens of a topological space form a locale, and locales and sober spaces are related by the adjunction `topToLocale ⊣ Locale.pt` (6.4.2.4).

*Lean:* Mathlib `Order.Frame` (state that a complete lattice satisfying `a ⊓ ⨆ b = ⨆ (a ⊓ b)` carries a unique compatible `Order.Frame`: Mathlib `Order.Frame.ofMinimalAxioms`); Mathlib `TopologicalSpace.Opens.instFrame`, `topToLocale`, `Locale.pt`, `Locale.adjunctionTopToLocalePT`.

*Needs:* Mathlib `Order.Frame`, `Mathlib.Topology.Order.Category.FrameAdjunction`.

**0-topoi are locales** (HTT Theorem 6.4.2.1, Proposition 6.4.2.5, Corollary 6.4.2.6, PDF pp. 660–662). For a presentable 0-category X, the following are equivalent: X ≃ `Shv_{≤−1}(C)` for a small 0-category C with finite limits and a Grothendieck topology; X ≃ `τ_{≤−1} Y` for an ∞-topos Y; X is a 0-topos; colimits in X are universal (6.4.2.1). A presentable 0-category is `N(U)` for a complete lattice U (2.3.4.3), and its colimits are universal exactly when U is a locale (6.4.2.5); so an ∞-category is a 0-topos exactly when it is equivalent to `N(U)` for a locale U (6.4.2.6).

*Lean:* 6.4.2.6 as `SSet.IsNTopos 0 X ↔ ∃ (U : Type u) (_ : Order.Frame U), Nonempty (X ≃ nerve U)` (categorical equivalence).

**Checks.** `N(Opens T)` is a 0-topos for every topological space T; the two-element lattice gives `τ_{≤−1} S`.

*Needs:* 6.4.1.1, 6.4.2.3; 2.3.4.1, 2.3.4.3 (L3); 5.2.7.2 (L6); 5.5.0.1 (L7); 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.2 (L10).

**n-efficient groupoids** (`SSet.IsNEfficient`; HTT Definition 6.4.3.1, Proposition 6.4.3.4, PDF p. 663). A groupoid object `U_•` of an ∞-category is n-efficient when `U_1 ⟶ U_0 × U_0` is (n − 2)-truncated (6.4.3.1). An ∞-category X is equivalent to an n-category exactly when every effective groupoid in X is n-efficient (6.4.3.4).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsNEfficient (n : ℕ) (U : SSet.simplicialObjects X) : Prop`, for a groupoid object U: for every object E, the map `Hom_X(E, U_1) ⟶ Hom_X(E, U_0) × Hom_X(E, U_0)` induced by the two face maps is `SSet.KanComplex.IsTruncatedMap ((n : ℤ) − 2)` (L7; the index is an integer, so n ≤ 1 gives (−2)- and (−1)-truncated maps). This needs no product in X (Lurie's 6.4.3.1 uses `U_0 × U_0` without assuming it exists); when the product exists it says that `U_1 ⟶ U_0 × U_0` is `SSet.IsTruncatedMorphism ((n : ℤ) − 2)`, a lemma.

*Needs:* `SSet.IsGroupoidObject` (6.1.2.7, L7); `SSet.IsEffectiveGroupoid` (6.1.2.14, L6); 5.5.6.12, 5.5.6.15 (L7); 2.3.4.1 (L3).

**Compact objects closed under subobjects** (HTT Lemma 6.4.3.5, PDF p. 663). For X presentable with universal colimits, there is a regular τ with X τ-accessible and the τ-compact objects closed under subobjects and finite limits.

*Needs:* 5.3.4.5 (L6); 5.3.4.15, 5.4.7.4, 5.5.0.1, 5.5.6.13 (L7); 4.4.5.12 (L5); 6.1.1.2 (L10).

**The n-categorical Giraud theorem** (HTT Proposition 6.4.3.6, PDF p. 664). For `0 < n < ∞` and X presentable with universal colimits, disjoint coproducts, and effective groupoids exactly the n-efficient ones, X ≃ `Shv_{≤n−1}(C)` for a small n-category C with finite limits and a Grothendieck topology.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.6.4.3.6/comparison` (the comparison adjunction), `HTT.6.4.3.6/coproducts` (its image is closed under coproducts) and `HTT.6.4.3.6/truncation-induction` (induction on truncation), and this entry's own target `HTT.6.4.3.6`, which states the theorem through the equivalence G of `HTT.6.4.3.6/truncation-induction`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, an induction modelled on Giraud's argument: 6.4.3.5 for the generating subcategory and 6.2.2.18 and 6.2.4.6 for the topology (`HTT.6.4.3.6/comparison`), 6.1.5.1 and 6.4.4.8 for coproducts (`HTT.6.4.3.6/coproducts`), and the induction itself (`HTT.6.4.3.6/truncation-induction`).

*Needs:* `HTT.6.4.3.6/comparison`, `HTT.6.4.3.6/coproducts`, `HTT.6.4.3.6/truncation-induction` (below).

**The comparison adjunction** (`HTT.6.4.3.6/comparison`, part 1 of 3 of the n-categorical Giraud theorem above; HTT Proposition 6.4.3.6, setup of the proof, PDF pp. 664–665). Under hypotheses (i)–(iv) of 6.4.3.6, X may be taken minimal. Choose κ with X κ-accessible and `C = X^κ` closed under subobjects and finite limits (6.4.3.5), with the canonical topology, and let `F : P(C) ⟶ X` be the colimit-preserving extension of `C ⊆ X` (5.1.5.6). Then F has a fully faithful right adjoint G, G factors through `Shv_{≤n−1}(C)`, and G preserves initial objects.

*Needs:* 6.4.3.4, 6.4.3.5 (later in this item); 5.1.5.6 (L6); 5.5.1.1 (L7); 6.1.3.6, 6.2.2.7, 6.2.2.18, 6.2.4.6 (L10).

**The image is closed under coproducts** (`HTT.6.4.3.6/coproducts`, part 2 of 3 of the n-categorical Giraud theorem above; HTT Proposition 6.4.3.6, coproduct step of the proof, PDF pp. 665–666). The essential image of G is closed under small coproducts in `Shv_{≤n−1}(C)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: disjointness (6.1.5.1) makes the comparison `⨿ G(U_α) ⟶ G(⨿ U_α)` a monomorphism (5.5.6.15). Surjectivity on `π_0` at each C ∈ C splits a map `C ⟶ ⨿ U_α` into summands `C_α ⊆ C` (6.4.4.8), glued by the canonical topology (6.2.4.4).

*Needs:* `HTT.6.4.3.6/comparison`; 6.4.4.8 (later in this item); 5.5.6.15 (L7); 6.1.5.1, 6.2.4.4 (L10).

**Induction on truncation** (`HTT.6.4.3.6/truncation-induction`, part 3 of 3 of the n-categorical Giraud theorem above; HTT Proposition 6.4.3.6, final induction of the proof, PDF p. 666). For `−2 ≤ k ≤ n − 1`: if `f : X ⟶ Y` is k-truncated in `Shv_{≤n−1}(C)` with Y in the essential image of G, then X is in the essential image. With `k = n − 1` and Y final, G is an equivalence.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: cover X by U in the image, show that the Čech groupoid lies in the image (the diagonal of f is (k−1)-truncated) and is n-efficient, hence effective in the image by (iv); the comparison `X ⟶ |U_•|` is a monomorphism and an effective epimorphism (6.2.4.6).

*Needs:* `HTT.6.4.3.6/comparison`, `HTT.6.4.3.6/coproducts`; 6.4.3.1 (later in this item); 5.5.6.15 (L7); 6.2.3.10, 6.2.3.12, 6.2.4.6 (L10).

**Coproducts of truncated morphisms** (HTT Lemma 6.4.4.4, PDF p. 668). In a presentable X with universal colimits and disjoint coproducts, n-truncated morphisms (n ≥ −2) are stable under small coproducts.

*Needs:* 5.5.6.15 (L7); 6.1.5.1 (L10).

**n-truncated descent** (HTT Notation 6.4.4.2, PDF p. 668; Theorem 6.4.4.5, PDF p. 669). Let X be presentable with universal colimits and disjoint coproducts. Let `O^n_X ⊆ Fun(Δ[1], X)` be the full subcategory on (n − 2)-truncated morphisms and `O^{(n)}_X ⊆ O^n_X` the subcategory with only Cartesian transformations as morphisms (HTT Notation 6.4.4.2, stated here). The following are equivalent:

1. for every pushout square in `O^n_X` whose two edges out of the initial corner are Cartesian transformations, the other two edges are Cartesian transformations;
2. the class of (n − 2)-truncated morphisms is local;
3. the Cartesian fibration `O^n_X ⟶ X` is classified by a limit-preserving functor `X^op ⟶ Cat∞^`;
4. the right fibration `O^{(n)}_X ⟶ X` is classified by a limit-preserving functor `X^op ⟶ Ŝ`;
5. for a natural transformation `ᾱ : p̄ ⟶ q̄` of colimit diagrams `K^▷ ⟶ X` (K small) whose restriction to K is Cartesian with (n − 2)-truncated components, `ᾱ` is Cartesian and its component at the cone point is (n − 2)-truncated.

*Lean (Notation 6.4.4.2):* `SSet.arrowsIn (SSet.IsTruncatedMorphism ((n : ℤ) − 2))` and `SSet.cartesianArrowsIn (SSet.IsTruncatedMorphism ((n : ℤ) − 2))` (6.1.3.4), for finite `n : ℕ∞`; for `n = ⊤` all morphisms are used. No new declaration.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the argument of 6.1.3.9 with the lemmas 6.1.3.3, 6.1.3.5, 6.1.3.7 and 6.4.4.4.

*Needs:* 6.4.4.4; 6.1.3.1, 6.1.3.3, 6.1.3.5, 6.1.3.7, 6.1.3.8, 6.1.3.9, 6.1.5.1 (L10); 5.5.6.15 (L7); 2.4.2.1 (L3); 2.0.0.3 (L2).

**Colimits in n-topoi are universal** (HTT Proposition 6.4.4.6, PDF p. 669). In an n-topos, `0 ≤ n ≤ ∞`, colimits are universal.

*Needs:* 6.4.1.1; 5.1.2.2, 5.2.7.5 (L6); 5.5.6.14, 5.5.6.28 (L7); 6.1.3.14, 6.1.3.15 (L10).

**Truncated morphisms in `τ_{≤n} Y` are local** (HTT Proposition 6.4.4.7, PDF p. 670). For an ∞-topos Y and `X = τ_{≤n} Y`, `0 ≤ n ≤ ∞`, the class of (n − 2)-truncated morphisms of X is local. The target also states the case `X = τ_{≤n−1} Y` for `1 ≤ n ≤ ∞`, which is the form 6.4.1.5 `2⇒4` needs (condition (2) of 6.4.1.5 has `τ_{≤n−1}`); Lurie's proof applies unchanged, with 7.2.1.13 used at n − 1 instead of n.

*Needs:* 6.4.4.4; 6.2.3.14, 6.2.3.17 (L10); 6.3.5.1 (L11.1, the slice `Y_{/τ_{≤n} Y}` is an ∞-topos); 5.5.6.14 (L7) and 6.5.1.12 (L11.3, forward need: Y is (n + 1)-connective as an object of `Y_{/τ_{≤n} Y}`, and n-connective over `τ_{≤n−1} Y`, which is the hypothesis of 7.2.1.13); 7.2.1.13 (L11.4, forward need).

**Maps from the initial object are monomorphisms** (HTT Lemma 6.4.4.8, PDF p. 670). In a presentable ∞-category with universal colimits, every morphism `∅ ⟶ X` from an initial object is a monomorphism.

*Needs:* 5.5.6.13 (L7); 6.1.3.6 (L10).

**n-categorical Giraud axioms from local truncated morphisms** (HTT Proposition 6.4.4.9, PDF p. 670). For `1 ≤ n ≤ ∞` and X a presentable n-category with universal colimits and local (n − 2)-truncated morphisms, X satisfies the n-categorical Giraud axioms of 6.4.1.5 (6).

*Needs:* 6.4.4.5, 6.4.4.8; 6.4.3.1; 6.1.3.6, 6.1.3.17 (L10); `SSet.IsGroupoidObject` (L6.8).

**Geometric morphisms of n-topoi** (`SSet.IsGeometricMorphism` for n-topoi, `SSet.rTopN`; HTT Definition 6.4.5.1, PDF p. 672). For n-topoi X, Y (`0 ≤ n ≤ ∞`), a geometric morphism is a functor `X ⟶ Y` with a left exact left adjoint; `Fun_*(X, Y) ⊆ Fun(X, Y)` is their full subcategory, and `Top^R_n ⊆ Cat∞^` the subcategory of n-topoi and geometric morphisms. For n = ∞ this is 6.3.1.1 and `RTop`.

*Lean:* L11.1's `SSet.IsGeometricMorphism`, used for n-topoi; `SSet.IsNToposInf (n : ℕ∞) X := (n = ⊤ → IsInftyTopos X) ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, n = m → IsNTopos m X` (propose; `SSet.IsNTopos` takes `n : ℕ`); `SSet.rTopN (n : ℕ∞)` on the X with `IsNToposInf n X`, with `SSet.rTopN ⊤ = SSet.rTop`.

*Needs:* `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`; `HTT.1.2.11/intro`; 6.3.1.1.

**Truncated objects of an n-topos** (HTT Proposition 6.4.5.4, PDF p. 672). For an n-topos X and `0 ≤ m ≤ n`, `τ_{≤m−1} X` is an m-topos.

*Needs:* 6.4.1.1, 6.4.1.5.

**Geometric morphisms into presheaves and sheaves** (HTT Lemmas 6.4.5.5–6.4.5.6, PDF pp. 672–673). For a small n-category C with finite limits and an ∞-topos Y, restriction to truncated objects is an equivalence `Fun_*(Y, P(C)) ⟶ Fun_*(τ_{≤n−1} Y, P_{≤n−1}(C))` (6.4.5.5); with a Grothendieck topology on C, likewise `Fun_*(Y, Shv(C)) ⟶ Fun_*(τ_{≤n−1} Y, Shv_{≤n−1}(C))` (6.4.5.6).

*Needs:* 6.4.5.1; 5.1.5.6, 5.2.6.2 (L6); 5.5.6.22 (L7); 6.1.5.2, 6.1.3.10, 6.2.2.6, 6.2.2.7 (L10, for 6.4.5.6: `Shv(C)` is a topological localization and colimits in `P(C)` are universal); 2.3.4.1 (L3).

**Localic reflection** (HTT Proposition 6.4.5.7, PDF p. 674). For `0 ≤ m ≤ n ≤ ∞` and an m-topos Y there are an n-topos X and a categorical equivalence `f_* : τ_{≤m−1} X ⟶ Y` such that for every n-topos Z composition with `f_*` is an equivalence `Fun_*(Z, X) ⟶ Fun_*(τ_{≤m−1} Z, Y)`.

*Needs:* 6.4.5.6; 6.4.1.5; 6.1.0.4 (L10).

**m-localic n-topoi** (`SSet.IsLocalic`; HTT Definition 6.4.5.8, PDF p. 674). For `0 ≤ m ≤ n ≤ ∞`, an n-topos X is m-localic when `Fun_*(Y, X) ⟶ Fun_*(τ_{≤m−1} Y, τ_{≤m−1} X)` is an equivalence for every n-topos Y. By 6.4.5.7, m-topoi correspond to m-localic n-topoi, and `τ_{≤m−1} : Top^R_n ⟶ Top^R_m` restricts to an equivalence on m-localic ones.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsLocalic (m n : ℕ∞) (X : SSet.{u + 1}) [Quasicategory X] : Prop`, for `m ≤ n` and `IsNToposInf n X` (6.4.5.1, L11.2): for every `Y : SSet.{u + 1}` with `IsNToposInf n Y`, the restriction map `Fun_*(Y, X) ⟶ Fun_*(τ_{≤m−1} Y, τ_{≤m−1} X)` is `SSet.IsCategoricalEquivalence`. For finite m the truncation index is the integer `(m : ℤ) − 1`, so m = 0 gives the (−1)-truncated objects; for `m = ⊤`, `τ_{≤m−1}` is the identity; in Lean `τ_{≤m−1}` is the helper `SSet.truncBelow m Y` (propose), the `SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory` of Y on the objects with `SSet.IsTruncatedObject ((m : ℤ) − 1)` for finite m, and all of Y for `m = ⊤`. The restriction map is induced by 6.3.1.9 (geometric morphisms preserve truncation).

*Needs:* 6.4.5.1, 6.4.5.7; 6.3.1.9.

**Topological localizations of n-localic ∞-topoi** (HTT Proposition 6.4.5.9, PDF p. 675). Every topological localization of an n-localic ∞-topos is n-localic.

*Needs:* 6.4.5.7, 6.4.5.8; 6.2.1.4 (L10).

### L11.3 Homotopy theory in an ∞-topos

**Brown–Joyal–Jardine sheaves** (HTT Remark 6.5.0.1, PDF p. 676). For a topological space X, the local model structure on simplicial presheaves on `Opens X` presents the hypercompletion `Shv(X)^∧`; `Shv(X)` itself is often better behaved (§6.5.4). Formalize it as the case `C = Opens X` of 6.5.2.14, with `HTT.6.5.4/intro`'s `Shv(X)`.

*Needs:* 6.5.2.14; `HTT.6.5.4/intro`.

**Sheaves of sets and cotensors** (`HTT.6.5.1/intro`, PDF p. 676). For an object X of an ∞-topos X, a *sheaf of sets on X* is a discrete (0-truncated) object of `X_{/X}`; these form the ordinary topos `Disc(X_{/X}) = h(τ_{≤0} X_{/X})`. X is cotensored over simplicial sets: for X in X and K a simplicial set there is `X^K` with `Map_X(Y, X^K) ≃ Map_H(K, Map_X(Y, X))` naturally in Y (5.5.2.6).

*Lean:* `SSet.cotensor K X`, a choice of object. Its representing property (`SSet.IsRepresentable`, L5.10, applied to `Map_H(K, Map_X(−, X))`) is not yet stateable, since no entry constructs that functor; it must be added when the functor exists.

*Needs:* 5.5.0.1, 5.5.2.6 (L7); 6.1.0.4 (L10).

**Homotopy sheaves** (`SSet.homotopySheaf`; HTT Definition 6.5.1.1, PDF p. 676). For `S^n = ∂Δ[n+1]` with a base point and X in an ∞-topos X, evaluation at the base point is `s : X^{S^n} ⟶ X`, an object of `X_{/X}`, and `π_n(X) := τ_{≤0}(s)`, a sheaf of sets on X, pointed by the constant map. For n ≥ 1 it is a group object of `Disc(X_{/X})` (abelian for n ≥ 2), from the pinch maps of spheres; `X^{K ∨ K'} ≃ X^K ×_X X^{K'}`. For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`, `π_n(f)` is `π_n` of f regarded as an object of `X_{/Y}`, an object of `Disc(X_{/X})`.

*Lean:* `SSet.homotopySheaf (n : ℕ) (f : Edge X Y)`, an object of the 0-truncated full subcategory of `X_{/X}`; the group structure is a separate target for n ≥ 1, stated through Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.GrpObj` objects of the Cartesian monoidal category `h(τ_{≤0} X_{/X})`.

**Checks.** For `X = S` and a pointed Kan complex `η : ∗ ⟶ X`, `η^* π_n(X)` is `π_n(X, η)` of F2.2 (HTT Remark 6.5.1.6). This is a pointed set for n = 0 and a group, compatibly with the group object structure, for n ≥ 1.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.5.1/intro`; 5.5.6.1 (L7); 6.1.0.4 (L10); F2.2.

**Truncation preserves finite products** (HTT Lemma 6.5.1.2, PDF p. 676). In an ∞-topos, `τ_{≤n} : X ⟶ X` preserves finite products.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: reduce through a left exact presentation (5.5.6.28) to `P(C)` and then to `S`, where it is the Kan-complex statement of `HTT.A.2.7/postnikov` (F2.5).

*Needs:* 5.2.7.2 (L6); 5.5.6.28 (L7); 6.1.0.4 (L10); `HTT.A.2.7/postnikov`; 1.2.16.1.

**Homotopy sheaves: recursion, base change, long exact sequence** (HTT Remarks 6.5.1.3–6.5.1.5, PDF pp. 677–678). For `f : X ⟶ Y`, `π_0(f) ≃ X ×_Y τ_{≤0}^{X/Y}(f)` with a canonical global section, and `π_n(f) ≃ π_{n−1}(δ_f)` for n > 0, `δ_f : X ⟶ X ×_Y X` the diagonal (6.5.1.3). For a geometric morphism with left adjoint `f^*` and `g : Y ⟶ Y'`, `f^* π_n(g) ≃ π_n(f^* g)` (6.5.1.4, by 5.5.6.28). For `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z` (f, then g) there is a long exact sequence of pointed objects of `Disc(X_{/X})`, `⋯ ⟶ f^*π_{n+1}(g) ⟶ π_n(f) ⟶ π_n(g ∘ f) ⟶ f^*π_n(g) ⟶ π_{n−1}(f) ⟶ ⋯`, with exactness at `π_0(f)` read through the action of `f^*π_1(g)` (6.5.1.5).

*Proof route.* 6.5.1.3 and 6.5.1.4 as Lurie. For 6.5.1.5, Lurie's reduction through a left exact presentation (6.5.1.4) to `P(C)` and pointwise to `S`, where the sequence is F2.2's long exact sequence; Lurie leaves the `π_0` action to the reader, and the formalization constructs it.

*Needs:* 6.5.1.1; 5.5.6.28 (L7); 5.2.7.2 (L6); 5.4.2.1 (L7); F2.2 (long exact sequences); 6.4.5.1.

**Homotopy sheaves of truncated morphisms** (HTT Proposition 6.5.1.7, PDF p. 678). If `f` is n-truncated then `π_k(f) ≃ ∗` for k > n; if moreover n ≥ 0 and `π_n(f) ≃ ∗`, f is (n − 1)-truncated.

*Needs:* 6.5.1.3; 5.5.6.1, 5.5.6.15 (L7).

**Homotopy sheaves of a truncation** (HTT Lemma 6.5.1.9, PDF p. 679). For an n-truncation `p : X ⟶ Y`, `π_k(X) ≃ p^* π_k(Y)` for all `k ≤ n`.

*Needs:* 6.5.1.4; 5.5.6.28 (L7); `HTT.A.2.7/postnikov/section`, `HTT.A.2.7/postnikov/tower`.

**n-connective morphisms and objects** (`SSet.IsConnectiveMorphism`, `SSet.IsConnectiveObject`, `SSet.IsConnectedObject`; HTT Definitions 6.5.1.10–6.5.1.11, PDF p. 679). For `0 ≤ n ≤ ∞`, a morphism f of an ∞-topos is n-connective when it is an effective epimorphism and `π_k(f) ≃ ∗` for `0 ≤ k < n`; every morphism is (−1)-connective; an object X is n-connective when `X ⟶ 1` is (6.5.1.10); X is connected when it is 1-connective, i.e. (by 6.5.1.12) `τ_{≤0} X` is final (6.5.1.11).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsConnectiveMorphism (n : WithBot ℕ∞) f : Prop`, true for `n = ⊥` (that is, −1), and otherwise `SSet.IsEffectiveEpi f ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, (k : ℕ∞) < n → SSet.IsTerminalVertex (homotopySheaf k f)` in `τ_{≤0} X_{/X}` (Definition 6.5.1.10 reads `π_k(f) = ∗` as final in `Disc(X_{/X})`); `SSet.IsConnectiveObject n X` through the map to a chosen final object; `SSet.IsConnectedObject X := SSet.IsConnectiveObject 1 X`.

**Checks.** In `S`, a map of Kan complexes is n-connective exactly when it is surjective on `π_0` and its homotopy fibres are (n − 1)-connected (F2.2); equivalences are ∞-connective (6.5.1.16 (2)).

*Needs:* 6.5.1.1; `SSet.IsEffectiveEpi` (6.2.3.5, L10); `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**Connectivity through truncation** (HTT Proposition 6.5.1.12, PDF p. 679). For n ≥ −1, an object X of an ∞-topos is n-connective exactly when `τ_{≤n−1} X` is final.

*Proof route.* Lurie's induction on n, through 6.2.3.4 (n = 0), 6.5.1.9, 6.5.1.7 and 6.2.3.16, except for one step: Lurie applies 7.2.1.14 to know that the truncation map `p : X ⟶ τ_{≤n−1} X` is an effective epimorphism, and 7.2.1.14 rests on this Proposition (layer intro). Replace that step by the repair lemma below, proved first:

- *Repair lemma.* For every object X of an ∞-topos and every k ≥ 0, `X ⟶ τ_{≤k} X` is an effective epimorphism. Present X as an accessible left exact localization `L : P(C) ⟶ X` with right adjoint G (6.1.0.4). Then `X ⟶ τ_{≤k} X` is L applied to `GX ⟶ τ_{≤k} GX` (5.5.6.28 and `L G ≃ id`); L preserves effective epimorphisms (it preserves Čech nerves and their colimits); in `P(C)` Čech nerves and colimits are computed pointwise (5.1.2.2), so effective epimorphisms are pointwise; truncation in `P(C)` is objectwise (5.5.6.28 applied to the evaluation functors, which preserve limits and colimits); and in `S` the map `K ⟶ τ_{≤k} K` is bijective on `π_0`, hence an effective epimorphism by 6.2.3.10, because a monomorphism of Kan complexes has empty or contractible homotopy fibres and so, up to equivalence, is the inclusion of a union of path components (`SSet.KanComplex.IsTruncatedMap`, L7).

*Needs:* 6.5.1.7, 6.5.1.9, 6.5.1.10; 6.2.3.4, 6.2.3.6 (the left exact L preserves effective epimorphisms, in the repair lemma), 6.2.3.10, 6.2.3.16 (L10); 5.5.6.28, `SSet.KanComplex.IsTruncatedMap` (L7); 5.1.2.2 (L6); 6.1.0.4 (L10).

**Products and maps of connective objects** (HTT Corollaries 6.5.1.13–6.5.1.14, PDF p. 680). n-connective objects are stable under finite products (6.5.1.13). A morphism `f : X ⟶ X'` is (n + 1)-connective exactly when composition with f is a homotopy equivalence `Map_{X/X'}(id_{X'}, Y) ⟶ Map_{X/X'}(f, Y)` for every n-truncated Y in `X_{/X'}` (6.5.1.14).

*Needs:* 6.5.1.2, 6.5.1.12; 5.5.6.1 (L7).

**Connective morphisms lift along left exact localizations** (HTT Remark 6.5.1.15, PDF p. 680). For a left exact localization `L : X ⟶ Y` of ∞-topoi and an n-connective `f` in Y, f is equivalent in `Fun(Δ[1], Y)` to `L f'` for an n-connective `f'` in X: factor `G f` as an n-connective map followed by an (n − 1)-truncated one (the relative truncation of `G f` in `X_{/G Y'}`, 5.5.6.18, whose first map is n-connective by 6.5.1.12 in the slice); then L of the (n − 1)-truncated map is n-connective (6.5.1.16) and (n − 1)-truncated, hence an equivalence: as an object of the slice over its target its (n − 1)-truncation is final (6.5.1.12) and is the object itself.

*Needs:* 6.5.1.10, 6.5.1.12, 6.5.1.16; 5.2.7.2 (L6); 5.5.6.18 (L7).

**Stability of n-connective morphisms** (HTT Proposition 6.5.1.16, PDF p. 680). In an ∞-topos: n-connective implies m-connective for m ≤ n, and n-connective for all finite n implies ∞-connective; equivalences are ∞-connective; connectivity is invariant under homotopy; left adjoints of geometric morphisms preserve n-connective morphisms; for `h ≃ g ∘ f` with f n-connective, g is n-connective exactly when h is; n-connective morphisms are stable under pullback, and the converse holds along an effective epimorphism.

*Needs:* 6.5.1.4, 6.5.1.5, 6.5.1.10, 6.5.1.12; 6.2.3.12, 6.2.3.15, 6.2.3.16 (L10); 5.5.6.28 (L7).

**Pushouts of connective morphisms** (HTT Corollary 6.5.1.17, PDF p. 682). In a pushout square in an ∞-topos, if `f'` is n-connective so is the opposite edge f.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: reduce through 6.5.1.15 and a presentation to `S`, where it is `HTT.A.2.7/connective-pushouts` (F2.5).

*Needs:* 6.5.1.12, 6.5.1.15, 6.5.1.16; `HTT.A.2.7/connective-pushouts`; 5.5.6.28 (L7).

**Connectivity of the diagonal** (HTT Proposition 6.5.1.18, PDF p. 682). For n ≥ 0, f is n-connective exactly when its diagonal `δ : X ⟶ X ×_Y X` is (n − 1)-connective and f is an effective epimorphism.

*Needs:* 6.5.1.3, 6.5.1.10.

**Connectivity in a slice** (HTT Proposition 6.5.1.19, PDF p. 682). For a 2-simplex σ of X exhibiting `f : Y ⟶ Z` over X, f is n-connective in X exactly when σ is n-connective in `X_{/X}`.

*Needs:* 6.5.1.10; 2.0.0.2 (L2).

**Sections of connective morphisms** (HTT Proposition 6.5.1.20, PDF p. 683). For n ≥ 0, `f : X ⟶ Y` and a section s of f, f is n-connective exactly when s is (n − 1)-connective.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, through 6.2.3.12, 6.2.3.16, 6.5.1.5 and 6.5.1.19, with 7.2.1.14 in the direction "f n-connective ⇒ s an effective epimorphism". Formalize after 7.2.1.14, whose repaired proof (L11.4) does not use this Proposition.

*Needs:* 6.5.1.5, 6.5.1.10, 6.5.1.19; 6.2.3.12, 6.2.3.16 (L10); 7.2.1.14 (L11.4, forward need); `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**Jardine's local model structure** (HTT Proposition 6.5.2.1, PDF p. 683). For a small category C with a Grothendieck topology (Mathlib `GrothendieckTopology`), the category `A = Fun(C^op, SSet)` of simplicial presheaves carries a left proper combinatorial simplicial model structure with cofibrations the injective cofibrations (objectwise monomorphisms) and weak equivalences the local equivalences. Departure (layer intro): `f : F ⟶ G` is a local equivalence when, for every object C, every n ≥ 0 and every commutative square from `∂Δ[n] ⟶ Δ[n]` to `Ex^∞ F(C) ⟶ Ex^∞ G(C)`, the morphisms `C_α ⟶ C` over which there is a diagonal `Δ[n] ⟶ Ex^∞ F(C_α)` making the upper triangle commute and the lower one commute up to homotopy relative to `∂Δ[n]` generate a covering sieve. Lurie states this with `|F(C)|` and topological spheres; the two agree by `HTT.A.2.7/realization`, which this target does not use.

*Proof route.* Through HTT Proposition A.2.6.15 (F1, Smith's recognition theorem), as Lurie indicates; Lurie's own text cites Jardine.

*Needs:* A.2.6.1, A.2.6.15, A.2.8.1, A.2.4.1 (F1); F2.3 (`Ex^∞`); Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sites`.

**Localizations relative to a Cartesian fibration** (HTT Lemmas 6.5.2.3–6.5.2.4, PDF pp. 684–685). Let `p : C ⟶ D` be a Cartesian fibration of ∞-categories and `C⁰ ⊆ C` full, closed under sources of p-Cartesian morphisms with target in `C⁰`. A morphism in a fibre `C_D` exhibiting a `C⁰_D`-localization is a `C⁰`-localization in C (6.5.2.3, `SSet.Edge.IsLocalizationInto`, L6.5); if every `C⁰_D ⊆ C_D` is reflective, so is `C⁰ ⊆ C` (6.5.2.4).

*Needs:* 5.2.7.6–5.2.7.9 (L6); 2.4.3.2, 2.4.4.7 (L3).

**Accessibility of truncated components** (HTT Lemma 6.5.2.5, PDF p. 685). For X presentable, C accessible and `α : F ⟶ G` a natural transformation of accessible functors `C ⟶ X`, the full subcategory of C on objects where `α(C)` is n-truncated is an accessible subcategory (5.4.7.8).

*Needs:* 5.4.6.6, 5.4.7.8, 5.5.6.1, 5.5.6.15 (L7).

**Truncated morphisms are strongly reflective** (HTT Lemma 6.5.2.6, PDF p. 685). For X presentable and `−2 ≤ n < ∞`, the n-truncated morphisms span a strongly reflective subcategory of `Fun(Δ[1], X)` (`HTT.5.5.4.16/after`, L7).

*Needs:* 6.5.2.4, 6.5.2.5; `HTT.5.5.4.16/after` (L7).

**n-connective morphisms are accessible and closed under colimits** (HTT Lemma 6.5.2.7, PDF p. 685). For an ∞-topos X and `0 ≤ n ≤ ∞`, the n-connective morphisms span an accessible subcategory of `Fun(Δ[1], X)` that is stable under colimits.

*Needs:* 6.5.2.3, 6.5.2.6; 6.5.1.10; 5.1.5.7 (L6); 5.4.6.6, 5.4.7.8, 5.4.7.10 (L7).

**∞-connective morphisms are strongly saturated** (HTT Proposition 6.5.2.8, PDF p. 686). In an ∞-topos, the ∞-connective morphisms form a strongly saturated class of small generation (5.5.4.5).

*Needs:* 6.5.2.7; 6.5.1.5, 6.5.1.12, 6.5.1.16, 6.5.1.17, 6.5.1.19; 5.5.4.5, 5.5.4.14 (L7); 7.2.1.14 (L11.4, forward need).

**Hypercomplete objects and ∞-topoi** (`SSet.IsHypercompleteObject`, `SSet.IsHypercomplete`, `SSet.hypercompletion`; `HTT.6.5.2.8/after`, PDF pp. 686–687). An object of an ∞-topos X is hypercomplete when it is local (`SSet.IsLocalObject`, 5.5.4.1) for the ∞-connective morphisms; `X^∧ ⊆ X` is their full subcategory. By 6.5.2.8 and 5.5.4.15 it is an accessible reflective localization; since ∞-connective morphisms are stable under pullback (6.5.1.16), it is left exact (6.2.1.1), hence an ∞-topos. X is hypercomplete when `X^∧ = X`, i.e. every ∞-connective morphism is an equivalence (the definition after Lemma 6.5.2.10, stated here).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsHypercompleteObject X := SSet.IsLocalObject {f | SSet.IsConnectiveMorphism ⊤ f} X`; `SSet.hypercompletion X` the full subcategory on hypercomplete objects; `SSet.IsHypercomplete X := ∀ f, SSet.IsConnectiveMorphism ⊤ f → SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence f`.

**Checks.** `S` is hypercomplete (Whitehead's theorem, F2.2); `P(C)` is hypercomplete (pointwise).

*Needs:* 6.5.2.8, 6.5.1.16; 5.5.4.1, 5.5.4.15 (L7); 6.2.1.1, 6.1.3.4 (L10).

**Truncated objects are hypercomplete; `X^∧` is hypercomplete** (HTT Lemmas 6.5.2.9–6.5.2.10, 6.5.2.12, PDF p. 687). For n < ∞, `τ_{≤n} X ⊆ X^∧` (6.5.2.9, by 6.5.1.14). If `L : X ⟶ X^∧` is the left adjoint and LX is ∞-connective in `X^∧`, then LX is final (6.5.2.10). The ∞-topos `X^∧` is hypercomplete (6.5.2.12).

*Needs:* `HTT.6.5.2.8/after`; 6.5.1.14; 5.5.6.28 (L7).

**Universal property of the hypercompletion** (HTT Proposition 6.5.2.13, PDF p. 687). For ∞-topoi X, Y with Y hypercomplete, composition with `X^∧ ⊆ X` is an isomorphism `Fun_*(Y, X^∧) ⟶ Fun_*(Y, X)`.

*Needs:* 6.5.2.12; 6.5.1.16 (4); 6.4.5.1.

**Jardine's model presents the hypercompletion** (HTT Proposition 6.5.2.14, PDF p. 688). For C a small category with a Grothendieck topology and A the local model structure of 6.5.2.1, the ∞-category `N(A°)` of fibrant-cofibrant objects is equivalent to `Shv(N(C))^∧`, a hypercomplete ∞-topos.

*Needs:* 6.5.2.1, `HTT.6.5.2.8/after`, 6.5.1.10 (the local equivalences between fibrant objects become the ∞-connective morphisms); 4.2.4.4 (L5); A.3.7.3, A.2.8.2 (F3, the injective model structure); 6.2.2.6 (L10).

**Cotopological localizations** (`SSet.IsCotopologicalLocalization`; HTT Proposition 6.5.2.16, Definition 6.5.2.17, Remark 6.5.2.18, Proposition 6.5.2.19, PDF pp. 689–690). For ∞-topoi X, Y and a left exact colimit-preserving `f^* : X ⟶ Y`, the following are equivalent: `f^*` reflects equivalences among monomorphisms; every u with `f^* u` an equivalence is ∞-connective (6.5.2.16). An accessible left exact localization of an ∞-topos is cotopological when its left adjoint satisfies these conditions (6.5.2.17). Then `f^*` also reflects effective epimorphisms (6.5.2.18, through the effective-epimorphism/monomorphism factorization and 6.2.3.12), and `X^∧` is the maximal cotopological localization of X. Every accessible left exact localization `X'' ⊆ X` factors as a topological localization `X' ⊆ X` followed by a cotopological localization `X'' ⊆ X'` (6.5.2.19).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsCotopologicalLocalization (L : X ⟶ Y)`: L an accessible left exact reflective localization of ∞-topoi with `∀ u, SSet.IsTruncatedMorphism (−1) u → SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence (L u) → SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence u`; the second condition of 6.5.2.16 is the `iff`.

*Needs:* 6.5.1.18; 6.2.3.12, 6.2.1.4, 6.1.3.4 (L10); 5.5.4.1 (L7); 5.2.7.2 (L6).

**Hypercoverings** (`SSet.IsHypercover`; HTT Definition 6.5.3.2, PDF p. 693). A simplicial object `U_•` of an ∞-topos X is a hypercovering when every `U_n ⟶ (cosk_{n−1} U_•)_n` is an effective epimorphism, where `cosk_{n−1}` is the right Kan extension of the restriction to `N(Δ_{≤n−1})^op`; it is effective when its colimit is a final object.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsHypercover (U : SSet.simplicialObjects X) : Prop := ∀ n, SSet.IsEffectiveEpi (unit of the right Kan extension of U restricted to (nerve (SimplexCategory.Truncated (n − 1))).op, at [n])` (for n = 0, `(cosk_{−1} U)_0` is the final object); `SSet.IsEffectiveHypercover U` adds that a colimit of U is final.

**Checks.** The Čech nerve of an effective epimorphism `U ⟶ 1` is a hypercovering (it is 0-coskeletal); a constant simplicial object at an ∞-connective object is one (6.5.3.5).

*Needs:* `SSet.simplicialObjects` (6.1.2.2, L6); right Kan extensions (L5.9); `SSet.IsEffectiveEpi` (L10); `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**Hypercoverings and hypercompletion** (HTT Lemmas 6.5.3.4–6.5.3.5, PDF p. 694). For `L : X ⟶ X^∧` the left adjoint, `U_•` is a hypercovering of X exactly when `L ∘ U_•` is one of `X^∧` (6.5.3.4, by 6.5.2.18). The constant simplicial object on an ∞-connective object is a hypercovering (6.5.3.5).

*Needs:* 6.5.3.2; 6.5.2.18; `HTT.6.5.2.8/after`.

**Coskeletal simplicial and semisimplicial objects** (`SSet.IsCoskeletal`; `HTT.6.5.3.7/after`, Lemma 6.5.3.8, PDF pp. 694–695). By cofinality of `N(Δ_s)^op ⊆ N(Δ)^op` (6.5.3.7, L5), colimits of a simplicial object and of its underlying semisimplicial object agree. A simplicial object is n-coskeletal when it is a right Kan extension of its restriction to `N(Δ_{≤n})^op`, and a semisimplicial object when it is one of its restriction to `N(Δ_{s,≤n})^op`, `Δ_{s,≤n} = Δ_s ×_Δ Δ_{≤n}` (`/after`). A simplicial object is n-coskeletal exactly when its semisimplicial object is (6.5.3.8).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsCoskeletal n U := SSet.IsRightKanExtension (fun v ↦ (nerveEquiv (opObjEquiv v.down)).len ≤ n) U`, the vertex predicate of the truncation `(nerve (SimplexCategory.Truncated n)).op` of `(nerve SimplexCategory).op` (L5.9's `SSet.IsRightKanExtension`, the dual of `SSet.IsLeftKanExtension`, takes a predicate on vertices), and likewise for `SSet.semisimplicialObjects` with the same predicate on `nerve SimplexCategory.inj` (L6.8's proposed wide subcategory).

*Needs:* 6.5.3.6 (L6, `SSet.semisimplicialObjects`), 6.5.3.7 (L5); 4.3.2.2 (L5); 4.1.1.1, 4.1.3.1 (L5).

**Coskeletal hypercoverings are effective** (HTT Lemma 6.5.3.9, PDF p. 695). In an ∞-topos, every n-coskeletal hypercovering is effective.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.6.5.3.9/diagonal` (the diagonal of the Čech bisimplicial object) and `HTT.6.5.3.9/retract` (U is a retract of the diagonal), and this entry's own target `HTT.6.5.3.9`, which runs the induction on n (for `n = 0`, U is a Čech nerve) and passes colimits between simplicial and semisimplicial objects by 6.5.3.7.

*Proof route.* Lurie's (after Dugger–Hollander–Isaksen): induction on n through semisimplicial objects and Kan extensions (6.5.3.7, 6.5.3.8, 4.3.2.7, 4.3.3.9), with 5.5.8.4 and descent; the inductive step is `HTT.6.5.3.9/diagonal` followed by `HTT.6.5.3.9/retract`.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.5.3.9/diagonal`, `HTT.6.5.3.9/retract` (below); 6.5.3.2; 6.5.3.7 (L5); 4.4.5.15 (L5); 6.1.2.2 (L6); 6.2.3.5, 6.2.3.12 (L10).

**The diagonal of the Čech bisimplicial object** (`HTT.6.5.3.9/diagonal`, part 1 of 2 of the effectivity of coskeletal hypercoverings above; HTT Lemma 6.5.3.9, first half of the inductive step of the proof, PDF pp. 695–696). Let U• be an n-coskeletal hypercovering in an ∞-topos, `n > 0`, with `V• = cosk_{n−1} U•` effective, and let `W⁺` be a Čech nerve of `U• ⟶ V•` in `X^Δ`. Every colimit of the diagonal simplicial object D• of `W = W⁺|N(Δ × Δ)^op` is a final object.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Each `U_m ⟶ V_m` is a finite composite of pullbacks of `U_n ⟶ V_n`, hence an effective epimorphism, so the columns of `W⁺` are colimit diagrams and `W⁺` is left Kan extended from W (4.3.3.9, 4.3.2.7). The augmentation column is V•, whose colimit is final, and the diagonal is cofinal (5.5.8.4).

*Needs:* 6.1.2.11 (L6.8); 4.3.2.7, 4.3.3.9 (L5); 5.5.8.4 (L7); 6.2.3.15 (L10).

**U is a retract of the diagonal** (`HTT.6.5.3.9/retract`, part 2 of 2 of the effectivity of coskeletal hypercoverings above; HTT Lemma 6.5.3.9, second half of the inductive step of the proof, PDF pp. 696–697). In the same situation, the semisimplicial object `U•^s` is a retract of `D•^s`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Both are n-coskeletal as semisimplicial objects (6.5.3.8), so it suffices to work on `Δ_{s,≤n}`. Over `V_{≤n−1}`, the n-th stage of `D^s` is an (n+1)-fold product of copies of that of `U^s`, the map between them is the diagonal, and a projection is a left inverse.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.5.3.9/diagonal`; 6.5.3.7, `HTT.6.5.3.7/after`, 6.5.3.8.

**Connectivity of realizations** (HTT Lemma 6.5.3.10, PDF p. 697). For a map `f_• : U_• ⟶ V_•` of simplicial objects in an ∞-topos with `f_k` an equivalence for all k ≤ n, the induced map of colimits `|U_•| ⟶ |V_•|` is n-connective.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, through a presentation and 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4; in `S` the input is `HTT.A.2.7/realization-connectivity` (F2).

*Needs:* 6.5.1.10, 6.5.1.12, 6.5.1.16; 4.2.4.1, 4.2.4.4 (L5); 5.5.6.28 (L7); A.2.8.2 (F3); `HTT.A.2.7/realization-connectivity`.

**Realizations of hypercoverings are ∞-connective** (HTT Lemma 6.5.3.11, PDF p. 698). For a hypercovering `U_•` of an ∞-topos X, the colimit `|U_•|` is ∞-connective.

*Needs:* 6.5.3.9, 6.5.3.10; 6.5.3.2.

**Hyperdescent** (HTT Theorem 6.5.3.12, Corollary 6.5.3.13, PDF p. 698). An ∞-topos X is hypercomplete exactly when, for every X in X, every hypercovering of `X_{/X}` is effective (6.5.3.12). For S the class of maps `|U_•| ⟶ X` with `U_•` a hypercovering of `X_{/X}` (X ranging over X), `X^∧ = S^{−1}X`: an object is hypercomplete exactly when it is S-local (6.5.3.13, Dugger–Hollander–Isaksen, Toën–Vezzosi).

*Needs:* 6.5.3.5, 6.5.3.11; `HTT.6.5.2.8/after`; 5.5.4.1 (L7).

**Sheaves on a topological space** (`SSet.sheafOnSpace`; `HTT.6.5.4/intro`, PDF p. 699). For a topological space X, `Shv(X) := Shv(N(Opens X))` for the topology whose covering sieves on U are the families with union U (Mathlib `Opens.grothendieckTopology X`); it is an ∞-topos (6.2.2.7), with hypercompletion `Shv(X)^∧`, which satisfies descent for all hypercoverings (6.5.3.12) where `Shv(X)` satisfies it for coverings. A continuous map `f : X ⟶ Y` gives the geometric morphism `f_* : Shv(X) ⟶ Shv(Y)`, composition with `f^{−1} : Opens Y ⟶ Opens X`.

*Lean:* `SSet.sheafOnSpace (X : TopCat.{u}) := SSet.sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X (transported along Mathlib's `nerveFunctorCompHoFunctorIso`, `hoFunctor.obj (nerve (Opens X)) ≅ Opens X`))` on `nerve (Opens X)`; `SSet.sheafOnSpace.map f` and the proof that it is a geometric morphism (its left adjoint is left Kan extension followed by sheafification, 6.2.2.9–6.2.2.16).

**Checks.** `Shv(∗) ≃ S`; `Shv(∅) ≃ Δ[0]`.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.2, 6.2.2.6, 6.2.2.7 (L10); `HTT.6.5.2.8/after`, 6.5.3.2, 6.5.3.12; Mathlib `Opens.grothendieckTopology`.

**Proper base change fails after hypercompletion** (HTT Counterexample 6.5.4.2, PDF p. 700). For Q the Hilbert cube, `X = Q × [0, 1]`, the proper projection `π : X ⟶ [0, 1]` and the inclusion `ψ : {0} ⟶ [0, 1]`, the base change map `ψ^* π_* ⟶ π'_* ψ'^*` is not an equivalence on hypercompleted sheaves: Lurie builds a sheaf F on X by adjoining, at stage i, paths between the previous sections over open sets `⋯ × Q_i × [0, 1/i)` shrinking towards `Q × {0}`; `F^∧` has a global section over `Q × {0}` (F is ∞-connective there) but none over any neighbourhood `Q × [0, 1/n)`. (For `Shv(−)` itself proper base change holds, 7.3.1.16 in L12.)

*Lean:* the statement is the existence of such a sheaf: an object F of `Shv(X)^∧` such that `Γ({0}, ψ^* π_* F)` is empty while `Γ(Q × {0}, ψ'^* F)` is not (in the hypercomplete ∞-topoi). Q is Mathlib's `ℕ → unitInterval` with the product topology.

*Proof route.* Lurie's is a sketch; the formalization must make the construction precise.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.5.4/intro`; `HTT.6.5.2.8/after`; 6.2.2.6 (L10); Mathlib `unitInterval`, product topology.

**A coherent space whose hypercomplete sheaves have a non-compact final object** (HTT Counterexample 6.5.4.5, PDF p. 702). Let `S = {x, y, z}` with opens generated by `{x, y}` and `{x, z}`, and `X = S^ℕ` with the product topology; X is coherent. The global sections functor `Γ : Shv(X)^∧ ⟶ S` does not preserve filtered colimits, so the final object of `Shv(X)^∧` is not compact: a sequence `F_0 ⟶ F_1 ⟶ ⋯` built as in 6.5.4.2 has a colimit in `Shv(X)^∧` with a global section, while no `F_n` has one.

*Lean:* `S` as a `Fin 3` with the generated topology, X as `ℕ → S` with the product topology; the coherence of X is a Mathlib-level lemma (`CompactSpace`, `QuasiSeparatedSpace`, `PrespectralSpace`); the claim is `¬ SSet.IsCardinalPresentable t ℵ₀ hC` for a final vertex t of `SSet.hypercompletion (SSet.sheafOnSpace X)`, with `Cardinal.fact_isRegular_aleph0` for `Fact ℵ₀.IsRegular` and hC the small filtered-colimit hypothesis, from presentability of the hypercompletion (`HTT.6.5.2.8/after`), as in L6.6's `IsCardinalPresentable X κ hC`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's is a sketch, like 6.5.4.2's; Lurie also asserts without proof that `Shv(X)^∧` has no compact objects besides the initial one, which is not part of this target.

*Needs:* 6.5.4.2; `HTT.6.5.4/intro`; 5.3.4.5 (L6); 5.5.4.7 (L7); 6.2.2.6 (L10).

### L11.4 General facts stated in chapter 7

**Truncated objects of a slice over a connective object** (HTT Lemma 7.2.1.13, PDF p. 740). For an ∞-topos X, n ≥ 0, an (n + 1)-connective object X and `f^* : X ⟶ X_{/X}` the right adjoint of the projection, `f^*` is fully faithful on n-truncated objects and restricts to an equivalence `τ_{≤n−1} X ⟶ τ_{≤n−1} X_{/X}`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: full faithfulness from 6.5.1.2; essential surjectivity through 6.5.1.16, 6.5.1.19, 6.5.1.20 and 5.5.6.28. Formalize after 6.5.1.20.

*Needs:* 6.5.1.2, 6.5.1.10, 6.5.1.16, 6.5.1.19, 6.5.1.20; 5.5.6.1, 5.5.6.28 (L7).

**Effective epimorphisms are detected on `τ_{≤0}`** (HTT Proposition 7.2.1.14, PDF p. 741). For an ∞-topos X, a morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` is an effective epimorphism exactly when `τ_{≤0} φ` is an effective epimorphism of the category `h(τ_{≤0} X)`. (That category is a Grothendieck topos by 6.4.1.5 with n = 1 and 6.4.1.3, so effective epimorphisms there are the epimorphisms; that identification is not part of this target.)

*Proof route.* The forward direction is Lurie's (Čech nerves and 6.2.3.10). Lurie's converse applies 7.2.1.13 in `X_{/τ_{≤0} X}`, which depends on 6.5.1.20, which applies this Proposition. Repair: first prove that, for every object X, pullback along `p : X ⟶ τ_{≤0} X` is a bijection `Sub(τ_{≤0} X) ⟶ Sub(X)`:

- p is an effective epimorphism (the repair lemma of 6.5.1.12), so by descent (6.1.3.9, with 6.2.3.17 for monomorphisms) `Sub(τ_{≤0} X)` is the set of subobjects V of X whose two pullbacks to `X ×_{τ_{≤0} X} X` agree;
- p is 1-connective: `π_0(p)` is `τ_{≤0}` of p in `X_{/τ_{≤0} X}`, which is `id_{τ_{≤0} X}` because truncation over a 0-truncated base is computed in X (5.5.6.14); so by 6.5.1.18 the diagonal `δ : X ⟶ X ×_{τ_{≤0} X} X` is an effective epimorphism, and since both pullbacks of V restrict along δ to V, they agree (6.2.3.10).

Then for the converse, factor φ as an effective epimorphism followed by a monomorphism `V ⟶ X`; the monomorphism is the pullback of a monomorphism `i : V' ⟶ τ_{≤0} X`, through which `τ_{≤0} φ` factors; an effective epimorphism that factors through a monomorphism forces the monomorphism to be an isomorphism (in any category), so i is an equivalence, and φ is an effective epimorphism. This uses only 6.5.1.10, 6.5.1.12 (repaired) and 6.5.1.18, so the cycle is broken.

*Needs:* 6.5.1.3, 6.5.1.12, 6.5.1.18; 6.2.3.4, 6.2.3.5 (L10, factorization through the colimit of the Čech nerve), 6.2.3.10, 6.2.3.17, 6.1.3.9, `HTT.6.1.1.4/after` (L10); 5.5.6.13, 5.5.6.14 (L7).

**Left exact filtered colimits** (`SSet.HasLeftExactFilteredColimits`; HTT Definition 7.3.4.2, PDF p. 787). For a presentable ∞-category C, filtered colimits in C are left exact when, for every small filtered ∞-category I, the colimit functor `Fun(I, C) ⟶ C` is left exact.

*Lean:* `SSet.HasLeftExactFilteredColimits C : Prop := ∀ (I : SSet.{u}) [SSet.IsFiltered I], SSet.IsLeftExact (SSet.colimFunctor I C)` (L6's `SSet.colimFunctor` and `SSet.IsFiltered`, 5.3.1.7), with the explicit hypothesis `(_hC : IsPresentable.{u, w} C)` (`SSet.IsPresentable` is a `def`, not a class).

*Needs:* 5.3.1.7 (L6); 5.5.0.1 (L7); 1.2.13.4.

**Examples: spaces, functor categories, localizations, n-topoi** (HTT Examples 7.3.4.4–7.3.4.7, PDF pp. 787–788). Filtered colimits are left exact in `S` (5.3.3.3) and in each `τ_{≤n} S` (7.3.4.4); in `Fun(X, C)` for any simplicial set X when they are in C (pointwise, 5.1.2.2; 7.3.4.5); in the essential image of an accessible left exact localization of such a C (7.3.4.6); hence in every n-topos, `0 ≤ n ≤ ∞` (7.3.4.7).

*Needs:* 7.3.4.2; `HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if`, 5.1.2.2 (L6); 5.2.7.2 (L6); 5.4.2.1, 5.5.0.1 (L7); 6.4.1.1 (L11.2); 6.1.0.4 (L10).

## Layer L12: Higher topos theory in topology

HTT chapter 7, with Proposition 6.3.6.6 and Corollary 6.3.6.7, which wait for the classification of gerbes (7.2.2.26). This is the one layer that uses the topology of spaces. Proposition 6.5.4.4 and Remark 6.5.4.7 are placed in L12.3, after Theorem 7.3.5.2, which proves 6.5.4.4; this makes L12.2 → L12.3 a forward need (7.2.1.17 uses 6.5.4.7). Its inputs are L10–L11, with the names of those layers: ∞-topoi (`SSet.IsInftyTopos`, 6.1.0.4), geometric morphisms (`SSet.IsGeometricMorphism`, 6.3.1.1), `SSet.rTop`, `Shv(X)` of a topological space (`SSet.sheafOnSpace`, `HTT.6.5.4/intro`), effective epimorphisms (`SSet.IsEffectiveEpi`), homotopy sheaves and connectivity (`SSet.homotopySheaf`, `SSet.IsConnectiveObject`, `SSet.IsConnectiveMorphism`, 6.5.1), hypercompleteness (`SSet.IsHypercomplete`, 6.5.2), points (`SSet.HasEnoughPoints`, 6.5.4.7), m-localic ∞-topoi (`SSet.IsLocalic`, 6.4.5.8), and the general facts 7.2.1.13–7.2.1.14 and 7.3.4.2–7.3.4.7 of L11.4, L7 (truncation, Postnikov towers, group objects), L5 (Kan extensions, with the names of L5.9), F3 (the projective model structure on simplicial presheaves) and Mathlib's general topology. Simplicial sets are compared with topological spaces only in L12.1, through Mathlib's realization `SSet.toTop` and singular complex `TopCat.toSSet`, and the comparison target `HTT.A.2.7/realization` (F2.4).

**Conventions of this layer.**

- A topological space is a type with Mathlib's `TopologicalSpace`, or an object of `TopCat.{u}`. Its locale of opens is Mathlib's `TopologicalSpace.Opens X`, and `U(X)` is that poset.
- *Paracompact* includes Hausdorff, as Lurie's proofs use (normality in 7.1.1.1, partitions of unity in 7.1.3.13): `[ParacompactSpace X] [T2Space X]`. Mathlib's `ParacompactSpace` has no separation axiom; with `T2Space` it gives `NormalSpace` (Mathlib `NormalSpace.of_paracompactSpace_r1Space`) and partitions of unity (`PartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`).
- *Locally compact* (HTT 7.3.1.7) is Mathlib's `LocallyCompactSpace`; *completely regular* (7.3.1.12, points closed) is Mathlib's `T35Space`; *proper* maps of spaces (7.3.1.14, universally closed) are Mathlib's `IsProperMap`; *coherent* spaces (compact opens closed under finite intersections and forming a basis) are `[CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [PrespectralSpace X]`, as in L11 (Mathlib's `SpectralSpace` adds T0 and sobriety, which Lurie does not assume); *Noetherian* spaces are `NoetherianSpace`; *irreducible* spaces are `IrreducibleSpace`. Each identification is a check of the entry that introduces the term.
- Paracompactness and partitions of unity come from Mathlib, not from AlgebraicTopology: that roadmap's Stage 5 (bundles, covers, products) supplies neither paracompactness nor dimension theory. Covering dimension is defined here (7.2.3.1).
- `X_*`, `Grp(X)`, `EM_n(X)` follow 7.2.2.1; `Disc(X)` is the ordinary topos `h(τ_{≤0} X)` of discrete objects; `1_X` is a final object.
- Geometric morphisms are written `p_* : X ⟶ Y` with left exact left adjoint `p^*`. "Unique up to equivalence" statements (the geometric morphism to `S`, 6.3.4.1) are used through a chosen representative; independence of the choice is part of each definition target that uses one.

**Forward needs inside the layer.** The items are written in the book's order. These entries need a later entry of the same subsection; none is circular:

- L12.1: Theorem 7.1.0.1 is proved after Proposition 7.1.5.1 (Lurie's deferred proof). Lemma 7.1.5.7 (in the entry of 7.1.5.1) uses `HTT.7.1.5.5/neighbourhood`, which uses only 7.1.5.2 and 7.1.1.1, so the order is 7.1.5.1–7.1.5.2, the part, then 7.1.5.7.
- L12.3: Theorem 7.3.1.16 uses Corollary 7.3.2.10 and Proposition 7.3.2.12 (closed embeddings give proper geometric morphisms) and Corollary 7.3.4.11 (global sections of a compact Hausdorff space are proper); Corollary 7.3.1.18 uses 7.3.2.10 and 7.3.2.12. Neither §7.3.2 nor §7.3.4 uses 7.3.1.16 or 7.3.1.18, so the order is §7.3.1 up to 7.3.1.14, then §§7.3.2–7.3.4, then 7.3.1.16 and 7.3.1.18.

Four results rest on classical topology or rigid geometry that no other roadmap supplies: the extension characterization of covering dimension in 7.2.3.7, the countable sum theorem in 7.3.6.5, Haver's theorem for (3) ⇒ (2) of 7.3.6.6, and the rigid-analytic spaces and Berkovich's dimension theorem in 7.3.6.10. L12.4 states these inputs as targets, so L12.2 and L12.3 need L12.4. These forward needs are not circular: from L12.1–L12.2, L12.4 uses only 7.1.1.1, 7.1.6.8, 7.2.1.8, 7.2.3.1 and 7.2.3.6, none of which needs L12.4.

### L12.1 Paracompact spaces

**Nonabelian cohomology of paracompact spaces** (HTT Theorem 7.1.0.1, PDF p. 708). Let X be a paracompact space, `p : X ⟶ ∗`, and K a Kan complex, regarded as an object of `S ≃ Shv(∗)`. Then there is a canonical bijection from `[X, |K|]`, the homotopy classes of continuous maps from X to the realization of K, to `π₀ (p_* p^* K)`, the components of the global sections of the constant sheaf with value K.

*Lean:* `[X, |K|]` is the quotient of `C(X, SSet.toTop.obj K)` by Mathlib's `ContinuousMap.Homotopic`; the target is `SSet.π₀` of a Kan model of `p_* p^* K` (global sections, L11).

**Checks.** For K = Δ[0] both sides are a point. For X a point, the bijection is `π₀ |K| ≅ π₀ K`, which is `HTT.A.2.7/realization` in degree 0.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: Proposition 7.1.5.1 for `Y = ∗` and F the constant presheaf with value K, through Corollary 7.1.4.4.

*Needs:* 7.1.5.1, 7.1.4.4; `HTT.A.2.7/realization`; Mathlib `SSet.toTop`, `ContinuousMap.Homotopic`.

**The basis of open Fσ subsets** (HTT Proposition 7.1.1.1, PDF p. 708). For a paracompact space X and an open U ⊆ X, these are equivalent: U is the cozero set `{f > 0}` of a continuous `f : X ⟶ [0, 1]`; U is the union of closed sets `K₀, K₁, …` with each `K_{n+1}` a neighbourhood of `K_n`; U is a countable union of closed sets. The family B of such U is a basis of the topology, closed under finite intersections, contains ∅ and X, and consists of paracompact subspaces. The paragraph after the statement adds that, for a basis closed under finite intersections, restriction `Shv(X) ⟶ Shv(B)` is an equivalence (through 0-localic ∞-topoi, 6.4.5); 7.1.4.4 uses it.

*Lean:* `TopologicalSpace.openFσ X : Set (Opens X)` (propose), the open sets satisfying the second condition; the three conditions as a `TFAE`.

**Checks.** In a metric space every open set is in B (Lurie's Remark 7.1.1.3). For `U ≠ X`, U is the cozero set of `x ↦ min(1, Metric.infDist x Uᶜ)`. For `U = X`, use the constant function 1, since Mathlib's `infDist x ∅` is 0.

*Needs:* Mathlib `ParacompactSpace`, `NormalSpace`, Urysohn's lemma (`exists_continuous_zero_one_of_isClosed`); for the paragraph after: 6.4.2.5–6.4.2.6, 6.4.5.8–6.4.5.9 (L11), 6.2.2.7 (L10).

**Spaces over X and their model structure** (HTT Proposition 7.1.2.1, PDF pp. 710–712). Let X be a space and B a set of open subsets of X (Lurie fixes a basis; the proof does not use that it is one). For `p : Y ⟶ X` and an open U, `Sing_X(Y, U)` is the simplicial set whose n-simplices are the maps `U × |Δ[n]| ⟶ Y` over X; it is a Kan complex, and `Sing_X(Y)` is the simplicial presheaf `U ↦ Sing_X(Y, U)`. There is a unique model structure on `Top_{/X}` whose weak equivalences (fibrations) are the maps `Y ⟶ Z` over X inducing homotopy equivalences (Kan fibrations) `Sing_X(Y, U) ⟶ Sing_X(Z, U)` for every U ∈ B. (Lurie writes the induced map the other way round, a typo.) It is a simplicial model category, with `Y ⊗ Δ[n] = Y × |Δ[n]|`.

*Parts.* This statement is formalized as five targets: the four parts that follow this entry, `HTT.7.1.2.1/sing` (spaces over X and their singular presheaves), `HTT.7.1.2.1/small-object` (the small object argument in `Top_{/X}`), `HTT.7.1.2.1/horn-cells` (relative horn complexes are weak equivalences) and `HTT.7.1.2.1/simplicial` (the simplicial structure), and this entry's own target `HTT.7.1.2.1`, which builds the model structure with `ModelCategory.mk'` (step 4 below) together with the `OverBasis` bridge and transport lemmas.

*Lean:* `TopCat.singOver (X : TopCat.{u}) : Over X ⥤ (Opens X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ SSet.{u}` (propose), with n-simplices `{f : C(U × SimplexCategory.toTop.obj ⦋n⦌, Y.left) // Y.hom ∘ f = Subtype.val ∘ Prod.fst}`, and the generating sets `TopCat.OverBasis.horns B` and `TopCat.OverBasis.boundaries B` described below are defined in the part `HTT.7.1.2.1/sing`. This target adds a `def` type synonym `TopCat.OverBasis (X : TopCat.{u}) (B : Set (Opens X)) := Over X` (propose) with `HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory` and `SimplicialModelCategory` (A.3.1.5) instances, the bridge `TopCat.OverBasis.equivalence X B : Over X ≌ OverBasis X B` and transport lemmas `OverBasis.fibrations_eq`, `.cofibrations_eq`, `.weakEquivalences_eq`, fibrations `(TopCat.OverBasis.horns B).rlp` and cofibrations `(TopCat.OverBasis.boundaries B).rlp.llp`, where the generating sets are `U × Λ_top ⟶ U × |Δ[n]|` (n ≥ 1) and `U × ∂_top ⟶ U × |Δ[n]|` for U ∈ B, Λ_top and ∂_top being the closed subsets `{t | ∃ j ≠ i, t j = 0}` and `{t | ∃ j, t j = 0}` of the topological simplex; theorems `fibration_iff` and `weakEquivalence_iff` stating Lurie's (F) and (W).

**Checks.** For X a point and B = {X}, the weak equivalences are the maps whose singular sets are weakly equivalent (Quillen's structure on `TopCat`). Every object is fibrant (`Sing_X(X, U)` is a point). Every space is small relative to the cell complexes, but ℵ₀ does not suffice: for X = ℝ, a section through one cell near each integer factors through no finite stage.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, with the cofibrantly generated argument written out (his I, the horns, and J, the boundaries).
1. Adjunction, the Kan property of `Sing_X(Y, U)`, fibrations `horns.rlp` and trivial fibrations `boundaries.rlp`: `HTT.7.1.2.1/sing`.
2. Small object argument (Mathlib `HasSmallObjectArgument`), relative to cell complexes only: `HTT.7.1.2.1/small-object`.
3. Relative horn-cell complexes are weak equivalences, through the class 𝒦 of closed embeddings with a deformation flow: `HTT.7.1.2.1/horn-cells`.
4. Build the structure with `ModelCategory.mk'`: two-out-of-three and retracts from `HTT.A.2.7/kan-weak-equivalences`; `boundaries.rlp = fibrations ⊓ W` from step 1; `horns.rlp.llp = cofibrations ⊓ W` from step 3 and the retract argument.
5. Simplicial clause: tensors, cotensors and SM7: `HTT.7.1.2.1/simplicial`.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.1.2.1/sing`, `HTT.7.1.2.1/small-object`, `HTT.7.1.2.1/horn-cells`, `HTT.7.1.2.1/simplicial` (below); A.2.1.1 (F1); A.3.1.5 (F3.3); `HTT.A.2.7/kan-weak-equivalences` (F2); Mathlib `Over`, `SSet.Subcomplex.MulticoequalizerDiagram`, `TopCat.continuous_iff_of_isColimit`, `HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory.mk'`.

**Spaces over X and their singular presheaves** (`HTT.7.1.2.1/sing`, part 1 of 4 of the model structure on spaces over X above; HTT Proposition 7.1.2.1, step 1 of the route above, PDF pp. 710–711). The functor `TopCat.singOver X : Over X ⥤ (Opens X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ SSet` with its functoriality, and the generating sets `U × Λ_top ⟶ U × |Δ[n]|` (horns) and `U × ∂_top ⟶ U × |Δ[n]|` (boundaries) for U ∈ B. Maps over X from `U × Λ_top` to Y correspond to maps `Λ[n, i] ⟶ Sing_X(Y, U)`, and likewise for `U × ∂_top`. Every `Sing_X(Y, U)` is a Kan complex. A map over X is a fibration (a trivial fibration) for every U ∈ B exactly when it has the right lifting property against the horn (boundary) generators.

*Lean:* `TopCat.singOver`, `TopCat.OverBasis.horns B` and `TopCat.OverBasis.boundaries B`, as in the entry above, are defined here.

*Proof route.* Paste over the finite closed cover by faces (Mathlib `horn.isColimit`, `LocallyFinite.continuous`); `U × Λ_top` is a retract of `U × |Δ[n]|` over X; `SSet.rlp_monomorphisms` and `HTT.A.2.7/model-structure` for the trivial fibrations.

*Needs:* `HTT.A.2.7/model-structure` (F2); Mathlib `SimplexCategory.toTop`, `SSet.horn.isColimit`, `SSet.rlp_monomorphisms`, `LocallyFinite.continuous`, `ContinuousMap.curry`.

**The small object argument in `Top_{/X}`** (`HTT.7.1.2.1/small-object`, part 2 of 4 of the model structure on spaces over X above; HTT Proposition 7.1.2.1, step 2 of the route above, PDF p. 711). For κ regular above the cardinality of every `U × |Δ[n]|`, the horn and boundary generators admit Mathlib's `HasSmallObjectArgument` in `Over X`. Smallness holds only relative to relative cell complexes: `Top_{/X}` is not presentable, so F1's A.1.2.5 does not apply.

*Proof route.* The generators are closed embeddings; closed embeddings in `TopCat` are stable under coproducts, pushouts and transfinite composition; a map from A into a relative cell complex factors through a stage as a map of sets, and is continuous into it (`TopCat.isClosed_iff_of_isColimit`).

*Needs:* A.1.2.2 (F1); Mathlib `MorphismProperty.IsCardinalForSmallObjectArgument`, `MorphismProperty.HasSmallObjectArgument`, `HasCardinalLT.isCardinalPresentable`, `Over.createsColimitsOfSize`, `TopCat.isClosed_iff_of_isColimit`.

**Relative horn complexes are weak equivalences** (`HTT.7.1.2.1/horn-cells`, part 3 of 4 of the model structure on spaces over X above; HTT Proposition 7.1.2.1, step 3 of the route above, PDF pp. 711–712). Let 𝒦 be the closed embeddings `k : Y ⟶ Z` over X that admit a continuous `λ : Z ⟶ [0, ∞)` with `λ⁻¹{0} = k(Y)` and a continuous flow `h : Z × [0, ∞) ⟶ Z` over X fixing `k(Y)`, with `h(z, 0) = z` and `h(z, λ z) ∈ k(Y)`. Then 𝒦 contains the horn generators, is closed under coproducts, pushouts, transfinite composition and retracts, and its members are homotopy equivalences over X, hence weak equivalences. Therefore `horns.rlp.llp ⊆ W`.

*Proof route.* The route of the entry above, which repairs Lurie's omission of continuity, "over X" and the fixing condition (replacing h by `h(z, min(t, λ z))` gives the last): radial projection from the point with coordinate −1 at i and 2/n elsewhere for the generators; `IsQuotientMap.continuous_lift_prod_left` for pushouts; concatenated flows for transfinite composites; `llp_rlp_of_hasSmallObjectArgument`.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.1.2.1/sing`, `HTT.7.1.2.1/small-object`; `HTT.A.2.7/kan-weak-equivalences` (F2); Mathlib `Topology.IsQuotientMap.continuous_lift_prod_left`, `MorphismProperty.llp_rlp_of_hasSmallObjectArgument`.

**The simplicial structure on `Top_{/X}`** (`HTT.7.1.2.1/simplicial`, part 4 of 4 of the model structure on spaces over X above; HTT Proposition 7.1.2.1, step 5 of the route above, PDF p. 712). With `Y ⊗ K = colim_{Δ[n] ⟶ K} Y × |Δ[n]|` and the fibrewise compact-open cotensor, `Over X` is a simplicial category, and the model structure satisfies SM7 (A.3.1.5) in cotensor form.

*Proof route.* SM7 reduces through `Sing_X(−, U)` to Mathlib `SSet.fibration_pullbackObjObjπ`, using `|Δ[m] × Δ[n]| ≅ |Δ[m]| × |Δ[n]|` (GeneralizedCohomology G2.1 `realizationProductKelleyComparison`, for finite simplicial sets).

*Needs:* `HTT.7.1.2.1/sing`; A.3.1.5 (F3.3); GeneralizedCohomology G2.1 `realizationProductKelleyComparison`; Mathlib `SSet.fibration_pullbackObjObjπ`.

**The adjunction `(|−|_X, Sing_X)`** (HTT Proposition 7.1.2.3, PDF p. 712). `Sing_X` has a left adjoint `|−|_X` from simplicial presheaves on B to `Top_{/X}`, and the pair is a simplicial Quillen adjunction for the model structure of 7.1.2.1 and the projective model structure (A.3.3).

*Needs:* 7.1.2.1, `HTT.7.1.2.1/simplicial` (the simplicial structure); `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions` (F1); A.2.8.2 (F3, the projective model structure).

**The presheaves `N_𝒰`** (HTT Definition 7.1.3.2, Proposition 7.1.3.7, Corollaries 7.1.3.8–7.1.3.9, PDF pp. 713–715). Let B be a basis of X closed under finite intersections (as throughout §7.1.3). For a linearly ordered set 𝒰 with a map `s : 𝒰 ⟶ B`, `N_𝒰` is the simplicial presheaf sending V ∈ B to the nerve of `{U ∈ 𝒰 : V ⊆ s(U)}`, a subobject of the constant presheaf `Δ^𝒰` (7.1.3.2). An order-preserving injection `𝒰 ⟶ 𝒰'` over B induces a projective cofibration `N_𝒰 ⟶ N_{𝒰'}` (7.1.3.7), so every `N_𝒰` is projectively cofibrant (7.1.3.8). If 𝒰 is a sieve with a linear order, `N_𝒰 ⟶ χ_𝒰` (the presheaf that is a point on 𝒰 and empty elsewhere) is a weak equivalence (7.1.3.9).

*Lean:* `TopCat.cechNerveLinear (s : 𝒰 → B) [LinearOrder 𝒰] : Bᵒᵖ ⥤ SSet` (propose), `V ↦ nerve {U // V ≤ s U}`.

**Checks.** For `𝒰 = ∅`, `N_𝒰 = ∅`; for `𝒰 = {U}`, `N_𝒰 ≅ χ_U` (Lurie's Examples 7.1.3.5–7.1.3.6).

*Proof route.* 7.1.3.7: add the nondegenerate simplices of `N(𝒰')` one at a time; each step is a pushout of `χ_U ⊗ ∂Δ[n] ⟶ χ_U ⊗ Δ[n]` with U the intersection of the corresponding opens.

*Needs:* A.2.8.1–A.2.8.2 (projective cofibrations, F1/F3); 6.2.2.1 (sieves, L10); Mathlib `CategoryTheory.nerve`.

**The sheaf criterion** (HTT Remark 7.1.3.11, Corollary 7.1.3.12, PDF p. 715). With `F(𝒰) = Map(N_𝒰, F)` (Lurie's Notation 7.1.3.10, not itself a target): `F({U}) = F(U)`, and `F(𝒰)` models the homotopy limit of F over the sieve generated by 𝒰 (7.1.3.11). A projectively fibrant `F : Bᵒᵖ ⟶ Kan` is a sheaf (lies in `Shv(B) ⊆ P(B)` under 5.1.1.1) exactly when, for every U ∈ B and every covering sieve 𝒰 of U, some linearly ordered `𝒰' ⟶ 𝒰` generating 𝒰 makes `F(U) ⟶ F(𝒰')` a weak homotopy equivalence (7.1.3.12).

*Needs:* 7.1.3.9; 6.2.2.1, 6.2.2.6 (L10); 5.1.1.1 (L6); A.2.8.2, `HTT.A.2.8.7/after` (F3); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

**`Sing_X(Y)` is a sheaf** (HTT Lemma 7.1.3.13, Proposition 7.1.3.14, PDF p. 715). For a paracompact open U, a covering 𝒰 ⊆ B of U and a linear order on 𝒰, the projection `|N_𝒰|_X ⟶ U` is a homotopy equivalence in `Top_{/X}`: a partition of unity subordinate to 𝒰 gives a section, and a straight-line homotopy (7.1.3.13). Hence, if B is closed under finite intersections and consists of paracompact sets, `Sing_X(Y)` is a sheaf for every `p : Y ⟶ X` (7.1.3.14).

*Needs:* 7.1.3.12; 7.1.2.3; Mathlib `PartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`.

**Replacement by subpresheaves of `Δ^V`** (HTT Lemma 7.1.4.1, PDF p. 716). For a poset B with least element ∅ and a simplicial presheaf F with `F(∅)` weakly contractible, there are a linearly ordered set V and a projectively cofibrant subpresheaf `F' ⊆ Δ^V` (constant presheaf), weakly equivalent to F, such that for each finite `V₀ ⊆ V` there is U ∈ B with `Δ^{V₀} ⊆ F'(U')` exactly when `U' ⊆ U`.

*Needs:* 4.2.3.15 (L5.6); A.2.8.2 (F3); A.2.1.1 (F1); `HTT.A.2.7/weak-equivalences`.

**Sheaves are recovered from spaces over X** (HTT Lemma 7.1.4.2, Theorem 7.1.4.3, Corollary 7.1.4.4, PDF pp. 718–721). Let X be paracompact and B the open Fσ subsets of X. For a projectively cofibrant sheaf F on B, the unit `F ⟶ Sing_X |F|_X` is a weak equivalence (7.1.4.2; Lurie's statement omits paracompactness, which the proof uses through 7.1.3.14 and a locally finite refinement). For every projectively cofibrant F the unit exhibits `Sing_X |F|_X` as a sheafification of F (7.1.4.3). Hence `Sing_X` induces an equivalence `N(Top°_{/X}) ⟶ Shv(X)` from the underlying ∞-category of the model structure of 7.1.2.1 (fibrant-cofibrant objects), and `N(Top°_{/X})` is an ∞-topos (7.1.4.4).

*Parts.* Lemma 7.1.4.2 is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.7.1.4.2/reduction` (reducing to local lifting problems) and `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift` (lifting by partitions of unity), and the target `HTT.7.1.4.2`, which combines them.

**Checks.** For X a point, B is `{∅, ∗}`, the model structure of 7.1.2.1 has the weak homotopy equivalences of spaces (detected by `TopCat.toSSet`) as weak equivalences, and 7.1.4.4 identifies its underlying ∞-category with `S`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. 7.1.4.2 reduces by 7.1.4.1 to subpresheaves of `Δ^V` and to local lifting problems (`HTT.7.1.4.2/reduction`), and compares `Sing |F|` with `Sing_X |F|_X` by partitions of unity (`HTT.7.1.4.2/lift`); 7.1.4.3 combines it with 7.1.3.14 and the derived adjunction of 7.1.2.3; 7.1.4.4 uses Shv(X) ≃ Shv(B) (the paragraph after 7.1.1.1).

*Needs:* `HTT.7.1.4.2/reduction`, `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift` (below); 7.1.1.1 (with the paragraph after it), 7.1.2.1, 7.1.2.3, 7.1.3.12, 7.1.3.14, 7.1.4.1; 5.2.7.2 (L6); 6.2.2.6 (L10), `HTT.6.5.4/intro` (L11); A.2.5.1 (F1), A.2.8.2 (F3); `HTT.A.2.7/realization`.

**Reducing to local lifting problems** (`HTT.7.1.4.2/reduction`, part 1 of 2 of Lemma 7.1.4.2 in the recovery of sheaves from spaces over X above; HTT Lemma 7.1.4.2, first half of the proof, PDF p. 718). For X paracompact and F a projectively cofibrant sheaf on B (the open Fσ sets), the unit `F ⟶ Sing_X |F|_X` is an equivalence provided the following holds. Take F a subsheaf of the constant presheaf `Δ^V` with `F(∅) = Δ^V` (7.1.4.1). For every inclusion `K' ⊆ K` of finite simplicial sets and every `g : K ⟶ (Sing_X |F|_X)(X)` with compatible data on K′, there is a cover U ⊆ B of X over which the relative lifting problem from `Sing |F|` is solved.

*Proof route.* Both functors preserve the relevant weak equivalences, which justifies the replacement (7.1.4.1). Replace X by any U ∈ B. Both `Sing |F|` and `Sing_X |F|_X` are sheaves (7.1.3.12, 7.1.3.14), so lifting may be done after refining to a cover.

*Needs:* 7.1.4.1, 7.1.3.12, 7.1.3.14, 7.1.2.3.

**Lifting by partitions of unity** (`HTT.7.1.4.2/lift`, part 2 of 2 of Lemma 7.1.4.2 in the recovery of sheaves from spaces over X above; HTT Lemma 7.1.4.2, second half of the proof, PDF pp. 719–720). For X paracompact and `g : X × |K| ⟶ |F|_X` over X with K finite, there are a locally finite cover `U = {U_x}` ⊆ B, a map `g' : K ⟶ (Sing |F|)(U)` given by convex combinations of maps `f_x : |K| ⟶ |Δ^{V_0}|` chosen by partitions of unity, and a straight-line homotopy between the images of g and g′ in `(Sing_X |F|_X)(U)`.

*Parts.* This part is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/cover` (the cover and the partition-of-unity maps), `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/map` (the convex-combination lift) and `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/homotopy` (the straight-line homotopy), and this entry's own target `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift`, which collects them.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the cover and the maps `f_x` are `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/cover`, the map g′ is `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/map`, and the homotopy is `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/homotopy`.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/cover`, `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/map`, `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/homotopy` (below); `HTT.7.1.4.2/reduction`.

**The cover and the partition-of-unity maps** (`HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/cover`, part 1 of 3 of lifting by partitions of unity above; in the proof of HTT Lemma 7.1.4.2, PDF p. 719). For X paracompact, K finite and `g : X × |K| ⟶ |F|_X` over X, there are a locally finite cover `U = {U_x}_{x ∈ X₀}` of X by members of B, linearly ordered, and, for each x, a finite set `V_0` and a map `f_x : |K| ⟶ |Δ^{V_0}|` from a partition of unity subordinate to a cover `{W_{x,v}}` of `|K|`, such that g carries `U_x × W_{x,v}` into the open set where the v-th coordinate is positive.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: compactness of `|K|` gives `V_0`, the neighbourhoods `U_x` and the covers `W_{x,v}`; paracompactness of X gives the locally finite refinement.

*Needs:* 7.1.1.1; Mathlib `PartitionOfUnity`, `ParacompactSpace`, `CompactSpace`.

**The convex-combination lift** (`HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/map`, part 2 of 3 of lifting by partitions of unity above; in the proof of HTT Lemma 7.1.4.2, PDF p. 719). Fix the data of `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/cover`. For every finite chain `x_0 < ⋯ < x_n` in X₀, the map `(Σ λ_i x_i, z) ↦ Σ λ_i f_{x_i}(z)` sends `|Δ^{\{x_0, …, x_n\}}| × |K|` into `|F(U_{x_0} ∩ ⋯ ∩ U_{x_n})|`. These maps are compatible and together form `g' : K ⟶ (Sing |F|)(U)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's, through condition (2) of 7.1.4.1.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/cover`; 7.1.4.1.

**The straight-line homotopy** (`HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/homotopy`, part 3 of 3 of lifting by partitions of unity above; in the proof of HTT Lemma 7.1.4.2, PDF pp. 719–720). The images of g and g′ in `(Sing_X |F|_X)(U)` are joined by a straight-line homotopy `K × Δ[1] ⟶ (Sing_X |F|_X)(U)`.

*Proof route.* Continuity has to be checked for the topology of `|F|_X`, which is not the subspace topology of `X × |Δ^V|` (7.1.1.1).

*Needs:* `HTT.7.1.4.2/lift/map`; 7.1.1.1.

**Base change for paracompact spaces** (HTT Proposition 7.1.5.1, Lemmas 7.1.5.2 and 7.1.5.7, PDF pp. 722–727). Let `p : X ⟶ Y` be a map of paracompact spaces, with `q : B_Y ⟶ B_X` inverse image on open Fσ sets and `q^*` left adjoint to restriction along q. For projectively cofibrant F on `B_Y`, the comparison `|q^* F|_X ⟶ |F|_Y ×_Y X`, a continuous bijection in general, is a weak equivalence in `Top_{/X}` (7.1.5.1). The proof runs through Lurie's subcomplexes `Map⁰_{Top/Y}(X, |F|_Y)` of maps whose partition-of-unity coordinates have locally finite supports subordinate to the given opens: for F built from a system of opens `U(V₀) ∈ B` as in 7.1.4.1, the inclusion of `Map⁰` into `Map_{Top/Y}(X, |F|_Y)` is a homotopy equivalence when X is paracompact (7.1.5.2), and restriction of `Map⁰` along a closed paracompact `X' ⊆ X` is a Kan fibration (7.1.5.7).

*Needs:* 7.1.1.1, 7.1.4.1, 7.1.4.2; 7.1.2.3; A.2.1.1, A.2.8.1 (F1), A.2.8.2 (F3); `HTT.A.2.5/quillen-adjunctions`; `HTT.7.1.5.5/neighbourhood` (below, a forward need, applied over the base Y to `Z ⊆ X × [0, 1]`) and 2.0.0.1 (L2) for 7.1.5.7; Mathlib `PartitionOfUnity`.

**Closed subsets** (HTT Corollaries 7.1.5.5–7.1.5.6, Proposition 7.1.5.8, PDF pp. 725–728). Let Y ⊆ X be closed in a paracompact space, `i : Y ⟶ X`, and F ∈ Shv(X). Every global section of `i^* F` lifts, up to a path, to a section of F on some open U ⊇ Y (7.1.5.5), and the colimit over open neighbourhoods `colim_{U ⊇ Y} F(U) ⟶ (i^* F)(Y)` (a filtered colimit in S) is a homotopy equivalence (7.1.5.6). If `X₀ ⊆ X₁ ⊆ ⋯` are closed subspaces exhausting X and X carries the colimit topology (U open when every `U ∩ X_i` is), then `Shv(X)` is the colimit of the `Shv(X_i)` in `RTop` (7.1.5.8).

*Parts.* Corollary 7.1.5.5 is formalized as two targets: the part that follows this entry, `HTT.7.1.5.5/neighbourhood` (extending sections off a closed set, which 7.1.5.6 also uses), and the target `HTT.7.1.5.5`, which reduces from F to that assertion through 7.1.5.1, 7.1.4.4 and 7.1.5.2.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.1.5.5/neighbourhood` (below, also for 7.1.5.6); 7.1.5.1, 7.1.5.2, 7.1.5.7; 7.1.4.1, 7.1.4.3, 7.1.4.4; `HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if` (L6.6); 6.5.1.10 (L11); 6.3.2.3 (L11, limits in `LTop`); for 7.1.5.8, Lurie's Remark 7.1.5.9 (with `X` the colimit of the `X_i`, `X × |Δ[n]|` is the colimit of the `X_i × |Δ[n]|`; Mathlib `ContinuousMap.curry` for the locally compact `|Δ[n]|`).

**Extending partition-of-unity sections off a closed set** (`HTT.7.1.5.5/neighbourhood`, the only part of Corollary 7.1.5.5 in closed subsets above; HTT Corollary 7.1.5.5, assertion (a) of the proof, PDF p. 726). Let S be paracompact, `F ⊆ Δ^V` on the open Fσ subsets of S as in 7.1.5.2, X ∈ `Top_{/S}` paracompact and Y ⊆ X closed. Every vertex of `Map⁰_{Top/S}(Y, |F|_S)` (7.1.5.2) is the restriction of a vertex of `Map⁰_{Top/S}(U, |F|_S)` for some paracompact open U ⊆ X containing Y. Corollary 7.1.5.5 uses the case S = X; Lemma 7.1.5.7 uses `X × [0, 1]` over S.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. Take locally finite open sets `U'_v` around the supports, extend each coordinate function `φ_v` to X with support in `U'_v`, and remove the locally finite closed set where the extensions leave F. Shrink to where `Σ φ'_v > 0` (open Fσ, hence paracompact by 7.1.1.1) and renormalize.

*Needs:* 7.1.5.2, 7.1.1.1; Mathlib `PartitionOfUnity`, Tietze or Urysohn extension.

**Pro-spaces and shape** (`SSet.proSpaces`, `SSet.shape`; HTT Definitions 7.1.6.1 and 7.1.6.3, Remark 7.1.6.5, PDF p. 732). `Pro(S)` is the opposite of the full subcategory of `Fun(S, S)` spanned by the accessible left exact functors (7.1.6.1). For an ∞-topos X with geometric morphism `q_* : X ⟶ S` (6.3.4.1) and left adjoint `q^*`, the shape `Sh(X) = q_* q^*` is an accessible left exact functor, an object of `Pro(S)` (7.1.6.3). A geometric morphism `p_* : Y ⟶ X` induces `Sh(Y) ⟶ Sh(X)` from the unit of `p^* ⊣ p_*`, making Sh a functor `hRTop ⟶ hPro(S)`; p is a *shape equivalence* when this map is an equivalence (7.1.6.5).

*Lean:* `SSet.proSpaces := (SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory (P := fun F ↦ IsAccessibleFunctor F ∧ SSet.IsLeftExact F) (Fun(S, S))).op`, with `S = SSet.spaces` and Fun computed one universe up (L6 Size convention); `SSet.shape X := q_* ∘ q^*` for a chosen `q_*`, and `SSet.IsShapeEquivalence p`. Propose.

**Checks.** `Sh(S)` is the identity functor (the final object of `Pro(S)`); for a small C with finite limits, a functor `C ⟶ S` is left exact exactly when it lies in `Ind(C^op)` (Lurie's Remark 7.1.6.2, through 5.3.5.4).

*Needs:* 5.4.2.1, `SSet.IsAccessibleFunctor` (L7); 6.1.0.4 (L10); 6.3.4.1, 6.3.1.1 (L11); `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`; `SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory`.

**Shape of paracompact spaces** (HTT Proposition 7.1.6.8, PDF p. 732). For a map `p : X ⟶ Y` of paracompact spaces, `p_* : Shv(X) ⟶ Shv(Y)` is a shape equivalence exactly when, for every Kan complex K, restriction `Map_Top(Y, |K|) ⟶ Map_Top(X, |K|)` is a homotopy equivalence; here `Map_Top(Z, |K|)` has n-simplices the maps `Z × |Δ[n]| ⟶ |K|`.

*Lean:* `Map_Top(Z, |K|) := TopCat.toSSet.obj (TopCat.of C(Z, SSet.toTop.obj K))` (compact-open topology; this is the right simplicial set because `|Δ[n]|` is locally compact). Propose.

*Proof route.* For paracompact Z, 7.1.4.4 and 7.1.5.1 identify `Sh(Shv(Z))(K)` with `Map_Top(Z, |K|)` in H, naturally in Z.

*Needs:* 7.1.4.4, 7.1.5.1, 7.1.6.5; Mathlib `ContinuousMap.curry` (compact-open topology).

**Trivial shape; local systems on a Pro-space** (HTT Definition 7.1.6.11, Warning 7.1.6.16, PDF pp. 733–734). An ∞-topos X has trivial shape when `Sh(X)` is equivalent to the identity of S (7.1.6.11); equivalently (Lurie's Remark 7.1.6.12, a characterization) `q^* : S ⟶ X` is fully faithful. For a Pro-space X̂, Lurie defines (prose before 7.1.6.13) the ∞-topos `S_{/X̂}` of local systems as the limit in `RTop` of `S_{/X}` over the filtered ∞-category of the left fibration classified by X̂ (through 4.2.2.4 and 6.3.3.1); its shape need not be X̂, and there is only a counit `Sh(S_{/X̂}) ⟶ X̂` (7.1.6.16).

*Lean:* `SSet.HasTrivialShape X : Prop`, for an ∞-topos X with a chosen `q_*`: HTT's definition, that the vertices `SSet.shape X` and the identity functor of `S` in `SSet.proSpaces` are equivalent (some edge between them is an `SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence`). The `iff` with "`q^*` is fully faithful" (HTT Remark 7.1.6.12) is a target. Propose. Warning 7.1.6.16 is formalized as the existence of the counit map, with a negative statement only if an example is supplied (Lurie gives none).

**Checks.** S has trivial shape; `Shv(X)` has trivial shape for X irreducible (7.3.6.11) and for X contractible paracompact (7.1.6.8 with Y a point).

*Needs:* 7.1.6.1, 7.1.6.3; 6.1.0.4 (L10); 6.3.3.1 (L11); 4.2.2.4 (L5); `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`.

### L12.2 Dimension theory

**Homotopy dimension** (`SSet.HasHomotopyDimLE`; HTT Definition 7.2.1.1, Remark 7.2.1.5, PDF pp. 735–736).
