For `n ≥ −1`, an ∞-topos X has homotopy dimension ≤ n when every n-connective object (6.5.1.10; every object is (−1)-connective) has a global section `1_X ⟶ U`; X has finite homotopy dimension when this holds for some `n ≥ 0` (7.2.1.1). A coproduct in `RTop` of ∞-topoi `X_α` has homotopy dimension ≤ n exactly when each `X_α` does (7.2.1.5).

*Lean:* `SSet.HasHomotopyDimLE (n : ℤ) (X : SSet) [Quasicategory X]` for `−1 ≤ n`: for a final vertex `t` and every vertex U with `SSet.IsConnectiveObject n U` (L11's index `WithBot ℕ∞`, with −1 as ⊥), `Nonempty (X.Edge t U)`; independence of t is part of the target. Results assume `SSet.IsInftyTopos X`. Propose.

**Checks.** X has homotopy dimension ≤ −1 exactly when it is equivalent to Δ[0] (Lurie's Example 7.2.1.2); `S` and every `P(C)` with C having a final object have homotopy dimension ≤ 0 (Example 7.2.1.3).

*Needs:* 6.1.0.4 (L10); 6.5.1.10 (L11); `HTT.1.2.12/final`; 6.3.2.1 (L11, coproducts in `RTop` are products of the underlying ∞-categories) for 7.2.1.5.

**Relative homotopy dimension** (`SSet.GeometricMorphism.HasHomotopyDimLE`; HTT Definition 7.2.1.6, Lemma 7.2.1.7, PDF p. 737). A geometric morphism `f_* : X ⟶ Y` has homotopy dimension ≤ n when, for every `k ≥ n`, `f_*` carries k-connective morphisms to (k − n)-connective morphisms (7.2.1.6). An ∞-topos has homotopy dimension ≤ n exactly when its geometric morphism to S does (7.2.1.7).

*Lean:* the predicate on f with `SSet.IsGeometricMorphism f`, through `SSet.IsConnectiveMorphism`; it depends only on the equivalence class of f. Propose.

*Needs:* 7.2.1.1; 6.5.1.10, 6.5.1.16, 6.5.1.18, 6.3.1.1 (L11); `HTT.1.2.12/final`.

**Local homotopy dimension; convergence and hypercompleteness** (`SSet.IsLocallyOfHomotopyDimLE`; HTT Definition 7.2.1.8, Proposition 7.2.1.10, Lemma 7.2.1.11, Corollary 7.2.1.12, PDF pp. 738–740). X is locally of homotopy dimension ≤ n when some family of objects `U_α` generating X under colimits has every `X_{/U_α}` of homotopy dimension ≤ n (7.2.1.8). Then Postnikov towers in X converge (7.2.1.10, in the sense of 5.5.6.23) and X is hypercomplete (7.2.1.12, Jardine). For any presentable X, evaluation at ∞ from the Postnikov towers `X_τ ⊆ Fun(N(ℤ^∞_{≥0})^op, X)` to X is a trivial fibration, so every object has a Postnikov tower (7.2.1.11).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsLocallyOfHomotopyDimLE n X := ∃ (ι : Type u) (U : ι → X _⦋0⦌), generates X under small colimits ∧ ∀ i, HasHomotopyDimLE n (X_{/U i})`. Propose.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: 7.2.1.10 checks the criterion of 5.5.6.26 via Remark 5.5.6.27, using 7.2.1.5 and 7.2.1.7 on `X_{/U}` for a coproduct U of the generators; 7.2.1.12 combines it with 7.2.1.11 and 6.5.1.14.

*Needs:* 7.2.1.1, 7.2.1.5, 7.2.1.7; 5.5.6.23–5.5.6.27, 5.5.6.18 (L7); 6.5.0.1, 6.5.1.10–6.5.1.11, 6.5.1.14, 6.5.2.8 (L11); 6.2.3.5, 6.2.3.12, 6.2.3.13 (L10); 6.3.5.1 (L11, slices); 5.2.2.5 (L6); 2.4.2.1, 3.1.0.2 for 7.2.1.11.

**Effective epimorphisms of spaces; enough points** (HTT Corollaries 7.2.1.15 and 7.2.1.17, PDF pp. 741–742). A map of Kan complexes is an effective epimorphism in S exactly when it is surjective on `π₀` (7.2.1.15). If `Shv(X)` is locally of homotopy dimension ≤ n for some n, the points `x^*` for x ∈ X detect equivalences, so `Shv(X)` has enough points (7.2.1.17).

**Checks.** `∅ ⟶ Δ[0]` is not an effective epimorphism; `Δ[0] ⟶ X` for X connected is one.

*Needs:* 7.2.1.13, 7.2.1.14 (L11.4); 6.2.3.10, 6.1.1.6 (L10); for 7.2.1.17: 7.2.1.12, `HTT.6.5.4/intro` (L11), 6.5.1.10, 6.5.1.18 (the induction through diagonals), and 6.5.4.7 (L12.3, a forward need).

**Eilenberg–MacLane objects** (`HTT.7.2.2.1/em`, HTT Definition 7.2.2.1, PDF p. 742). In an ∞-topos X and for `n ≥ 0`, a pointed object `1 ⟶ X` is an Eilenberg–MacLane object of degree n when X is n-truncated and n-connective; `EM_n(X) ⊆ X_*` is their full subcategory. The pointed objects and group objects of the same definition are the L6.8 target `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed` (`SSet.pointedObjects`, `SSet.IsGroupObject`, `SSet.grp`); the statement target HTT 7.2.2.1 consists of the two parts.

*Lean:* `SSet.emObjects n X := SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory (P := fun e ↦ IsTruncatedObject n (target e) ∧ IsConnectiveObject n (target e)) (SSet.pointedObjects X)`. Propose.

**Checks.** In S, for n ≥ 1, `EM_n(S)` consists of the pointed Kan complexes equivalent to F2.5's `K(A, n)` (A a group for n = 1, abelian for n ≥ 2). `EM_0(S)` consists of the pointed discrete spaces. `EM_n(X)` is closed under finite products, including the empty product `1 ⟶ 1` (Lurie's Remark 7.2.2.3).

*Needs:* `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed` (L6.8); 5.5.6.1 (L7); 6.5.1.10 (L11); 6.1.0.4 (L10).

**Group objects through products; zero objects** (HTT Proposition 7.2.2.4, Corollaries 7.2.2.5–7.2.2.6, Definition 7.2.2.7, PDF p. 743). A simplicial object `U_•` of an ∞-category is a group object exactly when `U₀` is final and, for every decomposition `[n] = S ∪ S'` with `S ∩ S' = {s}`, the restrictions exhibit `U_n` as a product of `U(S)` and `U(S')` (7.2.2.4). Finite-product-preserving functors preserve group objects (7.2.2.5), and for a full subcategory closed under finite products, group objects in it are those of the ambient ∞-category lying in it (7.2.2.6). A zero object is one that is both initial and final (7.2.2.7); this is the L9 definition `SSet.IsZeroObject` (HA 1.1.1.1), not a new declaration.

*Lean (7.2.2.7):* L9's `SSet.IsZeroObject` (HA 1.1.1.1); no new declaration.

*Needs:* `HTT.6.1.2.6/pullback` (L6.8); `HTT.7.2.2.1/pointed`; `HTT.1.2.12/final`; `SSet.IsZeroObject` (L9.1).

**Pointed objects and loop groups** (HTT Lemmas 7.2.2.8–7.2.2.11, PDF pp. 743–745). If X has a final object `1`, the inclusion `X_{1/} ⊆ X_*` is an equivalence (7.2.2.8); `X_*` has a zero object, and if X has one the forgetful functor `X_* ⟶ X` is an equivalence (7.2.2.9); forgetting points gives `Grp(X_*) ≃ Grp(X)` (7.2.2.10). In an ∞-topos and for `n ≥ 1`, the Čech nerve of the base point gives an equivalence from connected pointed objects to `Grp(X)`, and it carries `EM_n(X)` onto the group objects in `EM_{n−1}(X)` (7.2.2.11). The case X = S is L10.9's `HTT.7.2.2/delooping-spaces`.

*Needs:* 1.2.12.9 (L2), 2.4.7.12 (L3.9), 3.3.1.3 (L4) for 7.2.2.8; 1.2.13.8 (L2), 7.2.2.7 for 7.2.2.9; 7.2.2.5, 5.1.2.2 (L6) for 7.2.2.10; 6.1.2.11 and `/after` (L6.8), 6.1.0.6, 6.2.3.5 with the equivalence after it (effective epimorphisms ↔ effective groupoids), 6.2.3.16, 6.2.3.17 (L10), 6.5.1.5, 6.5.1.16, 7.2.1.14 (L11) for 7.2.2.11.

**Eilenberg–MacLane objects are classified by homotopy sheaves** (HTT Proposition 7.2.2.12, PDF p. 746). For an ∞-topos X, `π_n : X_* ⟶ N(Disc(X))` restricts to an equivalence from `EM_n(X)` to the nerve of the category of pointed objects of `Disc(X)` (n = 0), of group objects (n = 1), and of commutative group objects (n ≥ 2). Its inverse is written `A ↦ (1_X ⟶ K(A, n))` (prose after the proof).

*Lean:* `SSet.Disc X := hoFunctor.obj (SSet.fullEnhancedSubcategory (P := SSet.IsTruncatedObject 0) X)` with `CartesianMonoidalCategory (Disc X)` and `BraidedCategory (Disc X)` instances (propose; finite products in `Disc(X)`, which `CommGrp` needs); `SSet.eilenbergMacLane n A : X _⦋0⦌` for `A : CommGrp (Disc X)`, the object K(A, n): the target of a chosen inverse image `1_X ⟶ K(A, n)` of A in `EM_n(X)`; propose.

**Checks.** In S and for n ≥ 1, `K(A, n)` is F2.5's Eilenberg–MacLane complex (`HTT.A.2.7/eilenberg-maclane`). For n = 0 it is A regarded as a discrete space.

*Proof route.* Induction on n through 7.2.2.10–7.2.2.11, with `Grp(Grp(C)) ≃ Ab(C) ≃ Grp(Ab(C))` for an ordinary category C with finite products (Eckmann–Hilton).

*Needs:* 7.2.2.10, 7.2.2.11; 6.5.1.1 (L11).

**Cohomology and cohomological dimension** (`SSet.cohomology`, `SSet.HasCohomologicalDimLE`; HTT Definitions 7.2.2.14 and 7.2.2.18, PDF pp. 747–748). For an ∞-topos X, `n ≥ 0` and an abelian group object A of `Disc(X)`, `H^n(X; A) = π₀ Map_X(1_X, K(A, n))` (7.2.2.14). X has cohomological dimension ≤ n when `H^k(X; A)` vanishes for every `k > n` and every such A (7.2.2.18).

*Lean:* `SSet.cohomology n A := SSet.π₀ (Hom_X(1_X, eilenbergMacLane n A))` for `A : CommGrp (Disc X)` (L12, 7.2.2.12) and `HasCohomologicalDimLE n X := ∀ A, ∀ k > n, Subsingleton (cohomology k A)`. Propose. The group structure (Lurie's Remark 7.2.2.16) is a separate construction if a user needs it.

**Checks.** For X = `Shv(C)` on a small site, `H^n(X; A)` is the sheaf cohomology of A (Lurie's Remark 7.2.2.17; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`). This is a comparison target to add only if a user needs it.

*Needs:* 7.2.2.12; 6.1.0.4 (L10).

**Gerbes and their bands** (HTT Definition 7.2.2.20, Remarks 7.2.2.21 and 7.2.2.23, PDF pp. 748–749). An n-gerbe in an ∞-topos X is an object that is n-connective and n-truncated. For `n ≥ 2`, `π_n X` is an abelian group object of `Disc(X_{/X})` pulled back from a unique (up to isomorphism) A in `Disc(X)` (7.2.1.13); X is then *banded by A* (7.2.2.20). For n < 2 the band needs nonabelian coefficients and is not developed (7.2.2.21). With Lurie's Notation 7.2.2.22 (`Band(X)` and `Gerb_n(X) ⊆ Fun(Δ[1], X)`, the maps `X ⟶ S` that are n-gerbes in `X_{/S}` and pullback squares; not itself a target), the projection `Gerb_n(X) ⟶ X` is a right fibration and the band is a functor `Gerb_n(X) ⟶ N(Band(X))` (7.2.2.23).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsGerbe n X := IsConnectiveObject n X ∧ IsTruncatedObject n X` and `SSet.IsBandedBy`, an isomorphism of objects of `Disc(X_{/x})`. Propose. Compatibility of that isomorphism with the group structures is not yet stated, and must be added when the needed API exists.

*Needs:* 7.2.2.1, 7.2.2.12; 7.2.1.13 (L11.4); 6.5.1.10 (L11), 5.5.6.1; 2.4.7.12, 2.4.2.5 (L3), 6.1.1.1 (L10), 3.3.1.3 (L4) for 7.2.2.23.

**Classification of gerbes** (HTT Lemmas 7.2.2.24–7.2.2.25, Theorem 7.2.2.26, Corollary 7.2.2.27, PDF pp. 750–753). Let X be an ∞-topos, `n ≥ 2` and A an abelian group object of `Disc(X)`. Lurie states 7.2.2.24–7.2.2.26 for `n ≥ 1`, but `Gerb_n` and bands are defined only for `n ≥ 2` (Notation 7.2.2.22), and every use (6.3.6.6 and 7.2.2.27, hence 7.2.2.29) has `n ≥ 2`. For an n-gerbe X with an identification `φ` of its band with A and the Eilenberg–MacLane object `u : 1 ⟶ K(A, n)`, composition with u is a homotopy equivalence from the band-respecting maps `K(A, n) ⟶ X` to `Map(1, X)` (7.2.2.24); maps in `Gerb^A_n` from the trivial gerbe `K(A, n) × X ⟶ X` to any A-banded gerbe `Ỹ ⟶ Y` form `Map_X(X, Ỹ)` (7.2.2.25). The A-banded gerbes `Gerb^A_n(X) ⟶ X` (defined in the proof of 7.2.2.26) form a right fibration represented by `K(A, n + 1)` (7.2.2.26). For `n ≥ 2`, `H^{n+1}(X; A)` is in bijection with equivalence classes of n-gerbes banded by A (7.2.2.27).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: (u, φ) is final in `Gerb^A_n(X)`, which is local on X, reducing to trivial gerbes (7.2.2.25).

*Needs:* 7.2.2.12, 7.2.2.14, 7.2.2.20, 7.2.2.23; 2.1.1.3 (L2), 2.0.0.3; 4.4.4.5 (L5.10, representable right fibrations); 5.5.6.14 (L7); 6.5.1.5 (L11); A.2.1.1 (F1).

**Truncated objects over 1-truncated ones** (HTT Proposition 6.3.6.6, Corollary 6.3.6.7, PDF pp. 655–656). If `f^*` of a geometric morphism `f_* : X ⟶ Y` is fully faithful and essentially surjective on 1-truncated objects, it is essentially surjective on n-truncated objects for every n (6.3.6.6); if moreover X is n-localic (6.4.5.8), f is an equivalence (6.3.6.7).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: induction on n, slicing over `τ_{≤n−1} X` to reduce to an n-gerbe, which for `n ≥ 2` is banded by a discrete A (7.2.1.13) and is the fibre of `1 ⟶ K(A, n + 1)` (7.2.2.26).

*Needs:* 7.2.2.12, 7.2.2.26; 7.2.1.13 (L11.4); 6.3.1.1, 6.3.5.1, 6.4.5.8 (L11); 6.1.3.4 (L10); 5.5.6.1; `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`, `HTT.1.2.10/essentially-surjective`.

**Cohomological and homotopy dimension** (HTT Theorem 7.2.2.29, Corollary 7.2.2.30, PDF pp. 753–754). For `n ≥ 2`, X has cohomological dimension ≤ n exactly when every n-connective truncated object has a global section (7.2.2.29). Homotopy dimension ≤ n implies cohomological dimension ≤ n, and conversely for `n ≥ 2` if X has finite homotopy dimension (7.2.2.30). Without finite homotopy dimension the converse fails (Lurie's Warning 7.2.2.31, Wieland, not a target).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: descending induction on the truncation degree, killing the obstruction class of a k-gerbe by 7.2.2.27.

*Needs:* 7.2.2.18, 7.2.2.20, 7.2.2.27; 7.2.1.1, 7.2.1.7; 6.5.1.10–6.5.1.11 (L11); 5.5.6.1.

**Covering dimension** (`TopologicalSpace.HasCoveringDimLE`; HTT Definition 7.2.3.1, PDF p. 755). A paracompact space X has covering dimension ≤ n when every open cover has an open refinement in which any `n + 2` members with distinct indices have empty intersection.

*Lean:* `TopologicalSpace.HasCoveringDimLE (n : ℕ) (X)`: for every open cover `u : ι → Set X` there is an open cover `v : κ → Set X` refining it with `⋂ i ∈ s, v i = ∅` for every `s : Finset κ` of card `n + 2`. Stated for any space; results assume paracompact Hausdorff. Propose (not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti).

**Checks.** A discrete space has covering dimension ≤ 0 (refine by singletons); the empty space has covering dimension ≤ n for every n.

*Needs:* Mathlib `ParacompactSpace`.

**Covering dimension bounds homotopy dimension** (HTT Lemma 7.2.3.5, Theorem 7.2.3.6, Corollary 7.2.3.7, PDF pp. 756–758). Lemma 7.2.3.5 refines a cover `{U_α}` of a paracompact space, given covers of the (k+1)-fold intersections, to one whose (k+1)-fold intersections over distinct indices lie in members of the given covers. A paracompact X of covering dimension ≤ n has `Shv(X)` of homotopy dimension ≤ n (7.2.3.6). For paracompact X these are equivalent: covering dimension ≤ n; `Shv(X)` of homotopy dimension ≤ n; every map from a closed subset to `S^m`, `m ≥ n`, extends to X (7.2.3.7).

*Parts.* Corollary 7.2.3.7 is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.7.2.3.7/extension-sheaf` (the sheaf of extensions into a sphere) and `HTT.7.2.3.7/extension-connective` (that sheaf is n-connective), and the target `HTT.7.2.3.7`, which combines (1) ⇒ (2) (7.2.3.6), (2) ⇒ (3) (the two parts, with a global section of an n-connective sheaf from homotopy dimension ≤ n) and (3) ⇒ (1) (`HTT.7.2.3/sphere-extension`).

*Proof route.* 7.2.3.6: build maps `N_𝒰^{(i)} ⟶ F` skeleton by skeleton along refinements (7.2.3.5), ending with an n-dimensional nerve. 7.2.3.7: (1) ⇒ (2) is 7.2.3.6; (2) ⇒ (3) through the sheaf of extensions and 7.1.3.13 (`HTT.7.2.3.7/extension-sheaf`), using that `S^m` is an absolute neighbourhood retract and `π_k(S^m) = 0` for `k < m` (`HTT.7.2.3.7/extension-connective`); (3) ⇒ (1) is classical dimension theory (Lurie cites Engelking), the L12.4 target `HTT.7.2.3/sphere-extension`.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.2.3.7/extension-sheaf`, `HTT.7.2.3.7/extension-connective` (below); 7.2.3.1; 7.2.1.1; 7.1.3.2, 7.1.3.12–7.1.3.14, 7.1.1.1; 6.2.2.6 (L10), `HTT.6.5.4/intro`, 6.5.1.10 (L11); 1.1.5.5; `HTT.7.2.3/sphere-extension` (L12.4) for (3) ⇒ (1).

**The sheaf of extensions into a sphere** (`HTT.7.2.3.7/extension-sheaf`, part 1 of 2 of Corollary 7.2.3.7 in the bound of homotopy dimension by covering dimension above; HTT Corollary 7.2.3.7, (2) ⇒ (3), sheaf step, PDF pp. 758–759). Let X be paracompact, A ⊆ X closed and `f_0 : A ⟶ S^m`. The simplicial presheaf on open Fσ subsets whose n-simplices over U are the continuous maps `U × |Δ[n]| ⟶ S^m` restricting to `f_0` on `(U ∩ A) × |Δ[n]|` is Kan-valued and a sheaf.

*Proof route.* As in 7.1.3.14: for a cover 𝒰 of U, the value on 𝒰 is the maps `|N_𝒰|_X ⟶ S^m` relative to `π⁻¹(A)`, and `|N_𝒰|_X ⟶ U` is a fibrewise homotopy equivalence (7.1.3.13).

*Needs:* 7.1.3.13, 7.1.3.14, 7.1.1.1; 6.2.2.6 (L10).

**The sheaf of extensions is n-connective** (`HTT.7.2.3.7/extension-connective`, part 2 of 2 of Corollary 7.2.3.7 in the bound of homotopy dimension by covering dimension above; HTT Corollary 7.2.3.7, (2) ⇒ (3), connectivity step, PDF p. 759). For `m ≥ n`, the sheaf of `HTT.7.2.3.7/extension-sheaf` is n-connective: every `∂Δ[k] ⟶ F(U)` with `k ≤ n` extends to `Δ[k]` locally on U.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. At a point x, `S^{k−1} ⟶ S^m` is null-homotopic (`k − 1 < m`), relative to A. Glue to a map on the closed set `(S^{k−1} × U) ∪ (D^k × (A ∪ {x}))` and extend it to an open neighbourhood by `HTT.7.2.3/spheres` (a); the neighbourhood contains `D^k × U_x` by compactness of `D^k`.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.2.3.7/extension-sheaf`; `HTT.7.2.3/spheres`, `HTT.7.2.3/sphere-extension` (L12.4); 6.5.1.10, `HTT.6.5.4/intro` (L11).

**Heyting spaces and Heyting dimension** (`TopologicalSpace.HeytingSpace`, `TopologicalSpace.HasHeytingDimLE`; HTT §7.2.4 (`HTT.7.2.4/intro`), Remark 7.2.4.3, Proposition 7.2.4.5, PDF pp. 759–761). A Heyting space has a basis of compact opens, finite intersections of compact opens compact (so X is compact), and, for compact opens U, V, the interior of `U ∪ (X − V)` compact. For X Noetherian, the irreducible closed subsets are well-founded under strict inclusion, and the Krull dimension of X is the supremum of their ordinal ranks (`/intro`). For U compact open, U and `X − U` are Heyting spaces; `X − U` is a *cocompact closed* subset (7.2.4.3). Heyting dimension ≤ α (an ordinal) is defined recursively: the boundary of every compact open has Heyting dimension < α, and dimension < 0 means empty. It is inherited by compact opens and their complements, and a finite union of compact opens, or of cocompact closed subsets, of dimension ≤ α has dimension ≤ α (7.2.4.5).

*Lean:* `class TopologicalSpace.HeytingSpace X extends PrespectralSpace X, QuasiSeparatedSpace X, CompactSpace X` with the interior condition; `HasHeytingDimLE (α : Ordinal) X` by well-founded recursion on α; Krull dimension through `WellFounded.rank` on irreducible closed subsets. Propose.

**Checks.** A Noetherian space is a Heyting space (Lurie's Remark 7.2.4.2). A T0 Heyting space has dimension ≤ 0 exactly when it is Hausdorff. Lurie's Remark 7.2.4.4 states this without T0, and then it fails: the indiscrete two-point space is Noetherian, has Heyting dimension 0 and is not Hausdorff. The two-point Sierpiński space has Heyting dimension 1.

*Needs:* Mathlib `PrespectralSpace`, `QuasiSeparatedSpace`, `IsIrreducible`, `WellFounded.rank`.

**Krull and Heyting dimension agree** (HTT Proposition 7.2.4.7, PDF p. 761). For a Noetherian space, Krull dimension equals Heyting dimension (as ordinals).

**Checks.** For n : ℕ, Krull dimension ≤ n in the ordinal sense is Mathlib's `topologicalKrullDim X ≤ n` (a well-founded rank is finite exactly when chain lengths are bounded); Mathlib's value is ⊤ when ranks are infinite.

*Needs:* 7.2.4.5, `HTT.7.2.4/intro`; Mathlib `NoetherianSpace`, `topologicalKrullDim`.

**Strongly connective sheaves** (HTT Definition 7.2.4.8, Remark 7.2.4.11, Lemmas 7.2.4.12–7.2.4.13, Theorem 7.2.4.14, PDF pp. 762–763). On a compact open V of a Heyting space X, a sheaf F is strongly k-connective when every `∂Δ[m] ⟶ F(U)`, U ⊆ V compact open, extends to `Δ[m]` on an open cover of `U − K` for some cocompact closed K whose closure has Heyting dimension `< m − k` (7.2.4.8). A strongly k-connective sheaf is k-connective, and if X has Heyting dimension ≤ n, every k-connective sheaf is strongly (k − n)-connective (7.2.4.11). The extension property of 7.2.4.8 holds for any inclusion `A ⊆ B` of finite simplicial sets with B of dimension ≤ m, with the same bound `m − k` (7.2.4.12; Lurie prints `m − 1 − k`, which is false, see the Checks); fibres of `F^{Δ[m]} ⟶ F^{∂Δ[m]}` over a section are strongly (k − m)-connective (7.2.4.13). On a Heyting space X of dimension ≤ n, for F a sheaf on a compact open W, the following are equivalent (7.2.4.14): (1) for compact opens `U ⊆ V ⊆ W` and a commutative square formed by `ζ : ∂Δ[m] ⟶ F(V)` and `η : Δ[m] ⟶ F(U)`, there are a cocompact closed `K ⊆ V − U` whose closure in X has Heyting dimension `< m − k` and an extension `η' : Δ[m] ⟶ F(V − K)` of ζ whose image in `F(U)` is homotopic to η relative to `∂Δ[m]`; (2) for a compact open `V ⊆ W` and `ζ : ∂Δ[m] ⟶ F(V)`, there are a cocompact closed `K ⊆ V` whose closure in X has Heyting dimension `< m − k` and an extension `Δ[m] ⟶ F(V − K)` of ζ; (3) F is strongly k-connective. ((1) ⇒ (2) takes U = ∅.)

*Parts.* Theorem 7.2.4.14 is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.7.2.4.14/fibre-reduction` (reduction to vertices) and `HTT.7.2.4.14/induction` (lifting points by induction on connectivity), which together give (3) ⇒ (1), and the target `HTT.7.2.4.14`, which adds the direct implications (1) ⇒ (2) ⇒ (3).

*Lean:* `IsStronglyConnective k F` for F ∈ Shv(V), a Kan-valued sheaf on all opens of V (Lurie's `F : U(V)^op ⟶ Kan` of 7.2.4.12). The definition quantifies over compact opens `U ⊆ V` and open covers of `U − K`; the conditions of 7.2.4.14 also evaluate F on the non-compact opens `V − K`. In Lean F is a presheaf `(Opens V)ᵒᵖ ⥤ SSet` and "cocompact closed K" is a closed `K ⊆ U` with `U − K` compact; the integer bounds are read through `HasHeytingDimLT (j : ℤ) K`: K empty when `j ≤ 0`, and `HasHeytingDimLE (j − 1)` otherwise; the Kan and sheaf conditions on F are not yet part of the definition: they are hypotheses of the results, and must be added to the definition when the needed API exists. Propose.

**Checks.** Lurie prints the bound of 7.2.4.12 as `m − 1 − k`, and that bound fails. Let X be the Sierpiński space (Heyting dimension 1), F its initial sheaf (a point on ∅, empty on nonempty opens) and k = −2. F is strongly (−2)-connective: for m = 0 take K = U, and for m ≥ 1 a map `∂Δ[m] ⟶ F(U)` forces U = ∅, where K = ∅ works. For `∅ ⊆ Δ[0]` and U = X, a cover of `X − K` by opens carrying sections of F forces K = X, whose dimension is not < 1. Induction on the simplices of B outside A, applying 7.2.4.8 on each member of the cover, gives `m − k`: the closures of the new sets K are cocompact closed by the interior condition on Heyting spaces, and their finite union has dimension `< m − k` by 7.2.4.5. This is the bound that 7.2.4.13 uses, for `∂(Δ[m] × Δ[n]) ⊆ Δ[m] × Δ[n]`, of dimension m + n.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.2.4.14/fibre-reduction`, `HTT.7.2.4.14/induction` (below); 7.2.4.3, 7.2.4.5 (for 7.2.4.12), `HTT.7.2.4/intro`; 6.5.1.10 (L11, for 7.2.4.11); 6.2.2.6 (L10); A.2.8.1–A.2.8.2 (F1/F3) and the after-part of A.2.4.3 (F1) for 7.2.4.14.

**Reduction to vertices** (`HTT.7.2.4.14/fibre-reduction`, part 1 of 2 of Theorem 7.2.4.14 in strongly connective sheaves above; HTT Theorem 7.2.4.14, first step of (3) ⇒ (1), PDF p. 764). If (3) ⇒ (1) of 7.2.4.14 holds for `m = 0` and every k, it holds for every m. The pullback of `F^{Δ[m]} ⟶ F^{∂Δ[m]}` along ζ is a homotopy pullback in the projective structure, hence a sheaf, and it is strongly (k − m)-connective (7.2.4.13).

*Needs:* 7.2.4.13; A.2.8.1–A.2.8.2 (F1/F3).

**Lifting points by induction on connectivity** (`HTT.7.2.4.14/induction`, part 2 of 2 of Theorem 7.2.4.14 in strongly connective sheaves above; HTT Theorem 7.2.4.14, inductive step of (3) ⇒ (1), PDF pp. 764–765). Let X be a Heyting space of dimension ≤ n, V a compact open set and F strongly k-connective on V. For a compact open U ⊆ V and η ∈ F(U), there are a cocompact closed `K ⊆ V − U` whose closure in X has Heyting dimension `< −k`, and `η' ∈ F(V − K)` whose restriction to U lies in the component of η.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the base case is `k = −n − 1`, with `K = V − U`. Otherwise cover by finitely many `V_α` with points `ψ_α` and induct on their number: apply the inductive hypothesis to the strongly (k−1)-connective path sheaf on `U ∩ V_α`, and glue along the homotopy pullback for `V' ∪ U`, removing the boundary of K.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.2.4.14/fibre-reduction`; 7.2.4.3, 7.2.4.8.

**Grothendieck vanishing** (HTT Corollaries 7.2.4.15–7.2.4.17 and 7.2.4.20, PDF pp. 765–766). For a map `π : X ⟶ Y` of finite-dimensional Heyting spaces carrying cocompact closed sets of dimension ≤ n into cocompact closed sets of dimension ≤ n, `π_*` preserves strongly k-connective sheaves (7.2.4.15). On a Heyting space of finite dimension, a strongly k-connective F has `F(X)` k-connective (7.2.4.16). On a Heyting space of dimension ≤ n, every n-connective sheaf has `π₀ F(X) ⟶ π₀ F(U)` surjective for compact open U, so `Shv(X)` has homotopy dimension ≤ n (7.2.4.17). A Noetherian space of Krull dimension ≤ n has `Shv(X)` of cohomological dimension ≤ n (7.2.4.20, Grothendieck's vanishing theorem).

**Checks.** A finite discrete space has cohomological dimension 0.

*Proof route.* Lurie's. 7.2.4.16 is 7.2.4.15 for Y a point, with the first half of 7.2.4.11. For 7.2.4.17, an n-connective sheaf is strongly 0-connective (7.2.4.11), and condition (1) of 7.2.4.14 with m = 0, where K must be empty, gives the surjectivity. Lurie cites condition (2), which gives only a section over X.

*Needs:* 7.2.4.11, 7.2.4.14; 7.2.4.7; 7.2.2.18, 7.2.2.30; 7.2.1.1; 6.5.1.10, `HTT.6.5.4/intro` (L11); Mathlib `topologicalKrullDim`.

### L12.3 The proper base change theorem

**Left adjointable squares** (`CategoryTheory.TwoSquare.IsLeftAdjointable`, `SSet.IsLeftAdjointableSquare`; HTT §7.3.1 (`HTT.7.3.1/intro`), Definitions 7.3.1.1–7.3.1.2, Remark 7.3.1.3, PDF pp. 768–769). For a square of categories `q'_* : C' ⟶ D'`, `p'_* : C' ⟶ C`, `p_* : D' ⟶ D`, `q_* : C ⟶ D` with an isomorphism `η : p_* q'_* ≅ q_* p'_*`, and left adjoints `q^*`, `q'^*`, the push-pull transformation `γ : q^* p_* ⟶ p'_* q'^*` is the mate of η (`/intro`); the square is left adjointable when γ is an isomorphism (7.3.1.1). A square of ∞-categories commuting up to a specified equivalence is left adjointable when its square of homotopy categories is (7.3.1.2). When the square comes from a map `P : M' ⟶ M` of Cartesian fibrations over `Δ[1]` carrying Cartesian edges to Cartesian edges, and the left adjoints exist, γ at an object is an equivalence exactly when P carries the corresponding coCartesian edge to a coCartesian edge (7.3.1.3).

*Lean:* for 7.3.1.1, Mathlib's `TwoSquare` and `mateEquiv`: for `η : q'_* ⋙ p_* ≅ p'_* ⋙ q_*`, `adj : q^* ⊣ q_*` and `adj' : q'^* ⊣ q'_*`, `IsLeftAdjointable η adj adj' := IsIso ((mateEquiv adj' adj).symm η.hom : p_* ⋙ q^* ⟶ q'^* ⋙ p'_*)` (η is a square of right adjoints, so the push–pull map is its inverse mate, with the adjunctions in that order); for 7.3.1.2, the same predicate on the image of the square under `SSet.hoFunctor`, the adjunctions being those induced from `Bicategory.Adjunction`s in `SSet.QCat.bicategory` (`HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`). Propose.

**Checks.** A square of identity functors is left adjointable; for the nerve of a square of ordinary categories, 7.3.1.2 agrees with 7.3.1.1.

*Needs:* `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`; 1.2.7.2; 2.3.1.3, 2.4.1.1 with its after-part, 2.4.2.1 (L3) and A.2.1.1 (F1) for 7.3.1.3; Mathlib `TwoSquare`, `mateEquiv`, `SSet.hoFunctor`.

**Proper geometric morphisms** (`SSet.IsProperGeometricMorphism`; HTT Definition 7.3.1.4, Remark 7.3.1.5, Proposition 7.3.1.6, PDF pp. 769–770). `p_* : X ⟶ Y` is proper when, for every Cartesian rectangle of ∞-topoi `X'' ⟶ X' ⟶ X` over `Y'' ⟶ Y' ⟶ Y`, the left square is left adjointable (7.3.1.4). A proper `p_*` commutes with filtered colimits, by applying the definition to `X ⟶ Fun(J, X) ⟶ X` for J small and filtered (7.3.1.5; Lurie asserts without proof that this rectangle is Cartesian in `RTop` and states the converse only informally, so the target is the forward statement with that Cartesian claim as an explicit lemma). Equivalences are proper, properness is invariant under equivalence of geometric morphisms, and stable under pullback and composition (7.3.1.6).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsProperGeometricMorphism p h` for p with `h : SSet.IsGeometricMorphism p` (an explicit argument), quantifying over pullback squares in `SSet.rTop` (6.3.4.6, L11) in the universe of X and Y. Propose.

*Needs:* 7.3.1.2; 6.3.1.1, 6.3.4.6 (L11); 6.1.0.4 (L10); 5.1.2.2 (L6) and 7.3.4.7 (L11.4, filtered colimits in an ∞-topos are left exact, so `δ_!` is left exact; Lurie cites 5.3.3.3, which covers `S`) for 7.3.1.5.

**Products of spaces and of ∞-topoi** (HTT Definition 7.3.1.7, Proposition 7.3.1.11, PDF p. 771). A space is locally compact when every neighbourhood of a point contains a compact set that is a neighbourhood of the point (7.3.1.7, Mathlib's `LocallyCompactSpace`). For X locally compact and any Y, `Shv(X × Y)` is the product of `Shv(X)` and `Shv(Y)` in `RTop` (7.3.1.11).

*Lean (7.3.1.7):* Mathlib `LocallyCompactSpace X`; no new definition. Mathlib asks every neighbourhood of a point to contain a compact neighbourhood of it, with no separation axiom, as HTT's definition does.

**Checks.** For Hausdorff X, 7.3.1.7 is the usual local compactness (Lurie's Example 7.3.1.8); a space with a basis of compact opens is locally compact (Example 7.3.1.9).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: 0-localic ∞-topoi form a localization of `RTop` (6.4.5), so it suffices that `U(X × Y)` is the coproduct of the frames `U(X)` and `U(Y)`, which uses local compactness of X.

*Needs:* 6.4.2.3, 6.4.5.8–6.4.5.9 (L11); 5.2.7.2 (L6); Mathlib `LocallyCompactSpace`, `Locale`.

**Proper maps of spaces and the proper base change theorem** (HTT Definitions 7.3.1.12, 7.3.1.14, Theorem 7.3.1.16, Corollary 7.3.1.18, PDF pp. 772–774). A space is completely regular when points are closed and points are separated from closed sets by functions to `[0, 1]` (7.3.1.12, Mathlib `T35Space`); a map is proper when it is universally closed (7.3.1.14, Mathlib `IsProperMap`, by `isProperMap_iff_universally_closed`). If `p : X ⟶ Y` is proper and X completely regular, `p_* : Shv(X) ⟶ Shv(Y)` is proper (7.3.1.16). For a pullback square of locally compact Hausdorff spaces with p proper, the square of `Shv` is left adjointable: the nonabelian proper base change theorem (7.3.1.18).

*Lean (7.3.1.12):* Mathlib `T35Space X` (T0 plus `CompletelyRegularSpace`, hence T1); no new definition. The equivalence with HTT's wording (points closed, separation by maps to `[0, 1]`) is a lemma.

*Lean (7.3.1.14):* Mathlib `IsProperMap p`; no new definition. `isProperMap_iff_universally_closed` gives continuity plus closedness of every `p × id_Z`; HTT asks every base change `X ×_Y Y' ⟶ Y'` to be closed. They agree because the base change is `p × id_{Y'}` restricted over the graph of `Y' ⟶ Y`, and a closed map restricted to a full preimage is closed; that equivalence is a lemma of this target.

*Lean (7.3.1.16):* `SSet.isProperGeometricMorphism_sheafOnSpace_map (p : X ⟶ Y) (hp : IsProperMap p) [T35Space X] : ∃ h : IsGeometricMorphism (sheafOnSpace.map p), IsProperGeometricMorphism (sheafOnSpace.map p) h`. `SSet.IsProperGeometricMorphism` takes the proof that the map is a geometric morphism as an argument, so the statement asserts both.

**Checks.** Agreement of 7.3.1.12 with `T35Space` (T0 with complete regularity implies points closed); agreement of 7.3.1.14 with `IsProperMap` for continuous maps (Mathlib tests closedness after products only; base change along `Y' ⟶ Y` restricts the product case to the graph).

*Proof route.* Lurie's. 7.3.1.16: embed X in a compact Hausdorff space X̄ (Mathlib `isEmbedding_stoneCechUnit` for `T35Space`), factor p as `X ⟶ X̄ × Y ⟶ Y`; the first map is a closed embedding (7.3.2.10, 7.3.2.12), the second a pullback of `Γ : Shv(X̄) ⟶ S` (7.3.1.11), proper by 7.3.4.11; conclude with 7.3.1.6. 7.3.1.18: with X̄ the one-point compactification (Mathlib `OnePoint`), 7.3.1.11 twice and 7.3.2.10, 7.3.2.12 show the square of ∞-topoi is a pullback, and 7.3.1.16 applies.

*Needs:* 7.3.1.4, 7.3.1.6, 7.3.1.11; 7.3.2.10, 7.3.2.12, 7.3.4.11 (forward, see the layer introduction); Mathlib `T35Space`, `IsProperMap`, `StoneCech`, `OnePoint`.

**Closed subtopoi** (HTT Lemmas 7.3.2.1–7.3.2.2, Proposition 7.3.2.3 and the definition after it (`HTT.7.3.2.3/after`), Lemmas 7.3.2.4–7.3.2.5, Definition 7.3.2.6, PDF pp. 776–778). In an ∞-topos, initial objects are (−1)-truncated (7.3.2.1) and every map out of an initial object is a monomorphism (7.3.2.2). For an object U, the strongly saturated class `S_U` generated by `∅ ⟶ V` for V admitting a map to U is topological (7.3.2.3, `SSet.IsTopological` of L10); its members are the *equivalences away from U* (`/after`). For U, X these are equivalent: X is `S_U`-local; `Map(Ũ, X)` is contractible for every `Ũ ⟶ U`; some `g : U ⟶ X` makes U a product of U and X (7.3.2.4). Such X are *trivial on U*, and they span a topological localization `X^{/U}`, an ∞-topos (prose after 7.3.2.4). For `g : U ⟶ V`, `X^{/V} ⊆ X^{/U}`, with equality if g is an effective epimorphism (7.3.2.5). For U ∈ `Sub(1_X)`, `X^{/U}` is the closed subtopos complementary to U, and a geometric morphism is a closed immersion when it is an equivalence onto some `X^{/U}` (7.3.2.6).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsEquivalenceAwayFrom U f` (membership in the strongly saturated closure, L7 `SSet.stronglySaturatedClosure`), `SSet.closedComplement U := fullEnhancedSubcategory (IsLocalObject (IsEquivalenceAwayFrom U))`, `SSet.IsClosedImmersion π`, where "equivalence onto `X^{/U}`" is read as a strict factorization `e ≫ ι = π` with e a categorical equivalence. Propose.

**Checks.** `X^{/∅} = X`, and `X^{/1_X}` is the trivial ∞-topos.

*Needs:* 6.1.3.6 (L10); 5.5.6.13; 5.5.4.5, 5.5.4.15 (L7); 6.2.1.4, 6.2.2.7 (L10); 6.3.3.4 (L11); 6.2.3.16 (L10) for 7.3.2.5; 6.4.5.1 (L11).

**Subterminal objects of a closed subtopos** (HTT Proposition 7.3.2.7, Corollaries 7.3.2.8–7.3.2.10, PDF pp. 778–779). The closed immersion `X^{/U} ⟶ X` identifies `Sub(1_{X^{/U}})` with `{V ∈ Sub(1_X) : U ⊆ V}` (7.3.2.7); `S_U ⊆ S_V` exactly when `U ⊆ V` (7.3.2.8). For a 0-localic X with locale 𝒰, `X^{/U}` is 0-localic with locale `{V : U ⊆ V}` (7.3.2.9). For U ⊆ X open in a space, `Shv(X − U) ⟶ Shv(X)` is a closed immersion with image `Shv(X)^{/U}` (7.3.2.10).

*Needs:* 7.3.2.4–7.3.2.6; 6.4.2.3, 6.4.5.8–6.4.5.9 (L11); 5.2.7.2.

**Closed immersions are proper** (HTT Lemma 7.3.2.11, Proposition 7.3.2.12, Corollary 7.3.2.13, PDF pp. 779–781). Geometric morphisms `X ⟶ Y^{/U}` are the geometric morphisms `X ⟶ Y` whose pullback sends U to an initial object (7.3.2.11). For `π_* : X ⟶ Y` and U ∈ `Sub(1_Y)`, the square with `X^{/π^* U} ⟶ Y^{/U}` over `π_*` is a pullback in `RTop` and is left adjointable (7.3.2.12); so closed immersions are proper and stable under pullback (7.3.2.13).

*Needs:* 7.3.2.4, 7.3.1.1; 4.2.4.1 (L5); `HTT.4.4.5/intro` (L5); 5.5.4.5, 5.5.4.7 (L7); 6.4.5.1 (L11); `HTT.1.2.7/adjunction`.

**Sheaves with values in an ∞-category** (`SSet.sheavesValued`; HTT Definition 7.3.3.1, PDF p. 781). For a space X and an ∞-category C, a C-valued presheaf is a functor `N(U(X))^op ⟶ C`; it is a sheaf when, for every open U and covering sieve of U, the restricted cone is a limit diagram. `P(X; C)` and `Shv(X; C) ⊆ P(X; C)`; `Shv(X; S)` is `Shv(X)` (Lurie's Remark 7.3.3.3); with `C = SSet.spaces` this is a check against L11's `SSet.sheafOnSpace X`.

*Lean:* `SSet.sheavesValued X C := fullEnhancedSubcategory (P := IsSheafValued) (Fun((nerve (Opens X)).op, C))`, sieves from Mathlib `Opens.grothendieckTopology X` (transported along Mathlib's `nerveFunctorCompHoFunctorIso`, `hoFunctor.obj (nerve (Opens X)) ≅ Opens X`). Propose.

*Needs:* 6.2.2.1–6.2.2.2 (L10), `HTT.6.5.4/intro` (L11); 1.2.13.5 (L2); Mathlib `Opens.grothendieckTopology`.

**Products with ∞-topoi of sheaves** (HTT Lemmas 7.3.3.4–7.3.3.5, 7.3.3.7–7.3.3.8, Theorem 7.3.3.9, PDF pp. 782–785). A functor `F : C × D ⟶ E` between ∞-categories with finite limits is left exact exactly when its restrictions with one variable final are left exact and `F(C, D)` is the product of `F(1, D)` and `F(C, 1)`, and also exactly when its restrictions with one variable final are left exact and F is a right Kan extension of its restriction to `C × D⁰ ∐_{C⁰ × D⁰} C⁰ × D` (7.3.3.4). For small C, D with finite limits, `P(C × D)` is the product of `P(C)` and `P(D)` in `RTop` (7.3.3.5). With Lurie's tensor `X ⊗ S` of an ∞-topos with S (Notation 7.3.3.6, not itself a target), for g corepresented by X the functor `X ⊗_C −` is left adjoint to the induced `P(C; X) ⟶ P(C)` (7.3.3.7), and for C with finite limits and a final object `P(C; X)` is the product of `P(C)` and X in `RTop` (7.3.3.8). For a space X and an ∞-topos X, `Shv(X; X)` is an ∞-topos, the product of `Shv(X)` and X in `RTop` through global sections and `π_*` (7.3.3.9).

*Needs:* 4.1.3.1, 4.3.2.2, 5.5.2.3 for 7.3.3.4; 1.2.12.9, 4.3.2.15, 5.2.6.2, 5.2.6.4, 6.2.3.20 for 7.3.3.5; 5.1.5.6, 5.5.2.9 for 7.3.3.7; 6.1.5.3 (L10), 6.3.4.1 (L11) for 7.3.3.8; 4.4.2.1, 6.2.2.7, 6.3.3.4 for 7.3.3.9.

**K-sheaves on locally compact spaces** (`SSet.kSheaves`; HTT Definition 7.3.4.1, Lemma 7.3.4.8, Theorem 7.3.4.9, Corollary 7.3.4.10, PDF pp. 786–791). For X locally compact Hausdorff, `K(X)` is the poset of compact subsets, `K ⋐ K'` when some open lies between them; a presheaf `F : N(K(X))^op ⟶ C` is a K-sheaf when `F(∅)` is final, `F(K ∪ K') ⟶ F(K), F(K'), F(K ∩ K')` is a pullback, and `F(K)` is the colimit of F over `{K' : K ⋐ K'}` (7.3.4.1). Let C be presentable with left exact filtered colimits (7.3.4.2, L11.4). A K-sheaf is right Kan extended from compact sets lying in members of any open cover (7.3.4.8). A presheaf on `K(X) ∪ U(X)` is right Kan extended from a K-sheaf exactly when it is left Kan extended from a sheaf (7.3.4.9), so `Shv(X; C) ≃ Shv_K(X; C)` by restriction (7.3.4.10, stated by Lurie for locally compact X; the Hausdorff hypothesis of 7.3.4.9 is needed).

*Parts.* Theorem 7.3.4.9 is formalized as five targets: the four parts that follow this entry, `HTT.7.3.4.9/1⇒2-left-kan` (from K-sheaves, left Kan extension), `HTT.7.3.4.9/1⇒2-sheaf` (from K-sheaves, the sheaf condition), `HTT.7.3.4.9/2⇒1-k-sheaf` (from sheaves, the K-sheaf conditions) and `HTT.7.3.4.9/2⇒1-right-kan` (from sheaves, right Kan extension), and the target `HTT.7.3.4.9`, which combines the two directions.

*Lean:* `SSet.IsKSheaf F` for `F : (nerve {K : Set X // IsCompact K}).op ⟶ C`, `SSet.kSheaves X C`. Propose.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.3.4.9/1⇒2-left-kan`, `HTT.7.3.4.9/1⇒2-sheaf`, `HTT.7.3.4.9/2⇒1-k-sheaf`, `HTT.7.3.4.9/2⇒1-right-kan` (below); 7.3.1.7, 7.3.3.1; 7.3.4.2 (L11.4); 4.1.3.1, 4.2.3.4, 4.3.2.2, 4.3.2.8 (L5); 5.1.2.2, 5.3.1.7 (L6); 5.5.0.1 (L7); 6.2.2.1–6.2.2.6 (L10); Mathlib `IsCompact`, `LocallyCompactSpace`.

**From K-sheaves: left Kan extension** (`HTT.7.3.4.9/1⇒2-left-kan`, part 1 of 4 of Theorem 7.3.4.9 in K-sheaves on locally compact spaces above; HTT Theorem 7.3.4.9, (1) ⇒ (2), first claim, PDF p. 789). Let X be locally compact Hausdorff, C presentable with left exact filtered colimits, and F a presheaf on `K(X) ∪ U(X)`. If `F_K` is a K-sheaf and F is right Kan extended from `F_K`, then F is left Kan extended from `F_U`.

*Proof route.* At a compact K, the poset of compact `K'` with `K ⋐ K'` and the poset of opens containing K are both cofinal (filtered, being closed under finite unions); combine with the colimit condition of K-sheaves.

*Needs:* 7.3.4.1; 4.1.3.1 (L5.4); 4.3.2.2 (L5).

**From K-sheaves: the sheaf condition** (`HTT.7.3.4.9/1⇒2-sheaf`, part 2 of 4 of Theorem 7.3.4.9 in K-sheaves on locally compact spaces above; HTT Theorem 7.3.4.9, (1) ⇒ (2), second claim, PDF pp. 789–790). Under (1), `F_U` is a sheaf.

*Proof route.* For a covering sieve 𝒲 on U, `N(𝒲) ⊆ N(𝒲 ∪ K_𝒲(X))` is cofinal. This reduces to `F | (K_𝒲(X) ∪ {U})^op` being right Kan extended from `K_𝒲(X)`, which follows from 7.3.4.8 and transitivity (4.3.2.8).

*Needs:* `HTT.7.3.4.9/1⇒2-left-kan`; 7.3.4.8; 4.1.3.1, 4.3.2.8 (L5); 6.2.2.6 (L10).

**From sheaves: the K-sheaf conditions** (`HTT.7.3.4.9/2⇒1-k-sheaf`, part 3 of 4 of Theorem 7.3.4.9 in K-sheaves on locally compact spaces above; HTT Theorem 7.3.4.9, (2) ⇒ (1), first claim, PDF pp. 790–791). If `F_U` is a sheaf and F is left Kan extended from `F_U`, then `F_K` is a K-sheaf: `F(∅)` is final, the squares for `K ∪ K'`, K, K′ and `K ∩ K'` are pullbacks, and `F(K)` is the colimit over `K ⋐ K'`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the pullback square is a filtered colimit of the squares of opens `U ⊇ K`, `U' ⊇ K'` (left exact filtered colimits, 5.1.2.2, and a cofinality argument). For the colimit condition, F on `U(X) ∪ K_{K⋐}(X) ∪ {K}` is left Kan extended (4.3.2.8), and `K_{K⋐}(X)^op` is cofinal.

*Needs:* 7.3.4.1, 7.3.4.2 (L11.4); 5.1.2.2 (L6); 4.1.3.1, 4.3.2.8 (L5).

**From sheaves: right Kan extension** (`HTT.7.3.4.9/2⇒1-right-kan`, part 4 of 4 of Theorem 7.3.4.9 in K-sheaves on locally compact spaces above; HTT Theorem 7.3.4.9, (2) ⇒ (1), second claim, PDF p. 791). Under (2), F is right Kan extended from `F_K`.

*Proof route.* At an open U, the sieve of `V ⋐ U` covers U, and both `{V : Y ⊆ V ⋐ U}` and `{K : Y ⊆ K ⊆ U}` are filtered, so the two inclusions are cofinal (4.1.3.1).

*Needs:* 4.1.3.1 (L5.4); 6.2.2.6 (L10).

**Global sections of compact Hausdorff spaces** (HTT Corollaries 7.3.4.11–7.3.4.12, PDF pp. 792–795). For X compact Hausdorff, `Γ : Shv(X) ⟶ S` is a proper geometric morphism (7.3.4.11) and preserves filtered colimits (7.3.4.12).

*Parts.* Corollary 7.3.4.11 is formalized as four targets: the three parts that follow this entry, `HTT.7.3.4.11/sheaf-correspondence` (sheaf correspondences of a geometric morphism), `HTT.7.3.4.11/cartesian` (Cartesian lifts of KU-sheaves) and `HTT.7.3.4.11/cocartesian` (coCartesian lifts of KU-sheaves), and the target `HTT.7.3.4.11`, which identifies the base change of Γ and checks adjointability.

*Proof route.* 7.3.4.11, Lurie's: by 7.3.3.9, the base change of Γ along `Y' ⟶ S` is global sections `Shv(X; Y') ⟶ Y'`, so it suffices that for every geometric morphism `f_* : Y'' ⟶ Y'` the square formed by these global sections and by composition with `f_*`, `Shv(X; Y'') ⟶ Shv(X; Y')`, is left adjointable. This is checked on the correspondences of `HTT.7.3.4.11/sheaf-correspondence`. The restrictions `φ_U : M_{𝒦U} ⟶ M_U` and `φ_𝒦 : M_{𝒦U} ⟶ M_𝒦` are fibrewise equivalences (7.3.4.10) that preserve Cartesian, respectively coCartesian, edges (`HTT.7.3.4.11/cartesian`, `HTT.7.3.4.11/cocartesian`), hence categorical equivalences (2.4.4.4). So `M_U ⟶ Δ[1]` is also a coCartesian fibration and `Γ_U` preserves Cartesian and coCartesian edges; conclude with 7.3.1.3. 7.3.4.12 is Lurie's, through 7.3.4.9–7.3.4.10 and the observation of 7.3.1.5. Both apply K-sheaves with values in an ∞-topos, whose filtered colimits are left exact (7.3.4.4–7.3.4.7, L11.4).

*Needs:* `HTT.7.3.4.11/sheaf-correspondence`, `HTT.7.3.4.11/cartesian`, `HTT.7.3.4.11/cocartesian` (below); 7.3.1.3, 7.3.1.4, 7.3.1.5, 7.3.3.9, 7.3.4.9, 7.3.4.10; 7.3.4.4–7.3.4.7 (L11.4); 2.4.4.4 (L3); 5.1.2.2, 5.2.1.1 (L6).

**Sheaf correspondences of a geometric morphism** (`HTT.7.3.4.11/sheaf-correspondence`, part 1 of 3 of Corollary 7.3.4.11 in global sections of compact Hausdorff spaces above; in the proof of HTT Corollary 7.3.4.11, PDF pp. 792–793). Let `f_* : Y'' ⟶ Y'` be a geometric morphism of ∞-topoi with left adjoint `f^*`, and `M ⟶ Δ[1]` a correspondence from Y′ to Y″ associated to `f_*`; it is both a Cartesian and a coCartesian fibration. For a simplicial set K let `M^K = Fun(K, M) ×_{Fun(K, Δ[1])} Δ[1]`, a correspondence from `Fun(K, Y')` to `Fun(K, Y'')`, Cartesian and coCartesian over Δ[1], associated to composition with `f_*` and with `f^*`. For X compact Hausdorff:

- the full subcategory `M_U ⊆ M^{N(U(X))^op}` on the sheaves with values in Y′ or Y″ is a Cartesian fibration over Δ[1], and its inclusion preserves Cartesian edges;
- the full subcategory `M_𝒦 ⊆ M^{N(K(X))^op}` on the K-sheaves (7.3.4.1) is a coCartesian fibration over Δ[1], and its inclusion preserves coCartesian edges.

*Proof route.* Composition with `f_*` preserves sheaves, since `f_*` preserves limits; composition with `f^*` preserves K-sheaves, since `f^*` preserves finite limits and filtered colimits. A full subcategory closed under the transport functor inherits the (co)Cartesian lifts (3.1.2.1).

*Needs:* 7.3.3.9, 7.3.4.1; 3.1.2.1 (L4.2); 5.2.1.3 (L6.4); 6.2.2.6 (L10.8).

**Cartesian lifts of KU-sheaves** (`HTT.7.3.4.11/cartesian`, part 2 of 3 of Corollary 7.3.4.11 in global sections of compact Hausdorff spaces above; in the proof of HTT Corollary 7.3.4.11, PDF pp. 793–794). In the setting of `HTT.7.3.4.11/sheaf-correspondence`, let `M_{𝒦U} ⊆ M^{N(K(X) ∪ U(X))^op}` be the full subcategory on the presheaves of 7.3.4.9 with values in Y′ or Y″ that are left Kan extended from a sheaf, equivalently right Kan extended from a K-sheaf. Then `M_{𝒦U} ⟶ Δ[1]` is a Cartesian fibration, and restriction `φ_U : M_{𝒦U} ⟶ M_U` preserves Cartesian edges.

*Proof route.* Lurie's.

1. For F over the vertex 1, take a Cartesian lift `α : F' ⟶ F` in the ambient correspondence (3.1.2.1). `F'|U(X)` is a sheaf, but F′ need not be left Kan extended from it.
2. Let `β : F'' ⟶ F'` come from the left Kan extension F″ of `F'|U(X)` (4.3.2.15); it restricts to the identity on `U(X)`.
3. Choose a 2-simplex σ with edges β, α and their composite γ. γ is Cartesian: the comparison map of slices is a right fibration, so it suffices that its fibres are contractible (dual of 2.1.3.4). This follows from three trivial fibrations, coming from right anodyne horn inclusions (2.1.2.5), from α being Cartesian, and from the adjunction between left Kan extension and restriction (since `r(β)` is an equivalence).
4. `φ_U(γ)` is a Cartesian edge composed with an equivalence (2.4.1.7).

*Needs:* `HTT.7.3.4.11/sheaf-correspondence`; 7.3.4.9; 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); 2.4.1.1, 2.4.1.7 (L3.5); 3.1.2.1 (L4.2); 2.1.2.5 (L2.3); 2.1.3.4 (L2.4).

**coCartesian lifts of KU-sheaves** (`HTT.7.3.4.11/cocartesian`, part 3 of 3 of Corollary 7.3.4.11 in global sections of compact Hausdorff spaces above; in the proof of HTT Corollary 7.3.4.11, PDF p. 793). In the setting of `HTT.7.3.4.11/sheaf-correspondence`, with `M_{𝒦U}` the full subcategory of KU-sheaves described in `HTT.7.3.4.11/cartesian`, `M_{𝒦U} ⟶ Δ[1]` is a coCartesian fibration, and restriction `φ_𝒦 : M_{𝒦U} ⟶ M_𝒦` preserves coCartesian edges.

*Proof route.* The argument of `HTT.7.3.4.11/cartesian` with the roles exchanged: take coCartesian lifts for composition with `f^*`, and correct them by right Kan extension from `K(X)` (4.3.2.15). Lurie leaves this case to the reader; it is not a formal dual of `HTT.7.3.4.11/cartesian`, since K-sheaves are not the opposite of sheaves, so it is written out.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.3.4.11/sheaf-correspondence`; 7.3.4.9; 4.3.2.15 (L5.9); 2.4.1.1, 2.4.1.7 (L3.5); 3.1.2.1 (L4.2); 2.1.2.5 (L2.3); 2.1.3.4 (L2.4).

**Coherent spaces** (HTT Lemma 7.3.5.1, Theorem 7.3.5.2, Corollaries 7.3.5.3–7.3.5.4, PDF pp. 795–798). For a coherent space X and C with small limits, restriction `Shv(X; C) ⟶ Fun(N(U₀(X))^op, C)` to compact opens is fully faithful, with image the functors with `F(∅)` final and pullbacks for `U ∩ V`, `U`, `V`, `U ∪ V` (7.3.5.2, through the Kan-extension Lemma 7.3.5.1). Global sections of a coherent space are proper (7.3.5.3) and preserve filtered colimits (7.3.5.4).

*Parts.* Theorem 7.3.5.2 is formalized as three targets: the two parts that follow this entry, `HTT.7.3.5.2/restriction` (sheaves restrict to coherent data) and `HTT.7.3.5.2/gluing` (coherent data glue to sheaves), and the target `HTT.7.3.5.2`, which identifies the image of the restriction through 4.3.2.15.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.3.5.2/restriction`, `HTT.7.3.5.2/gluing` (below); 7.3.4.8 (pattern), 7.3.4.10, 7.3.4.11; 7.3.1.4; 4.1.3.1, 4.3.2.8, 4.3.2.15 (L5); 5.5.4.7 (L7); 6.2.2.1–6.2.2.6 (L10); Mathlib `CompactSpace`, `QuasiSeparatedSpace`, `PrespectralSpace`.

**Sheaves restrict to coherent data** (`HTT.7.3.5.2/restriction`, part 1 of 2 of Theorem 7.3.5.2 in coherent spaces above; HTT Theorem 7.3.5.2, the inclusion of sheaves into D, PDF pp. 796–797). For a coherent space X and C with small limits, a C-valued sheaf F on X is right Kan extended from its restriction `F_0` to compact opens, `F_0(∅)` is final, and `F_0` makes `F_0(U ∪ V)` the pullback of `F_0(U) ⟶ F_0(U ∩ V) ⟵ F_0(V)`.

*Proof route.* Theorem A for the inclusions of compact opens into the sieves they generate, which cover since X is coherent; the empty sieve covers ∅.

*Needs:* 7.3.3.1; 4.1.3.1 (L5.4); 6.2.2.6 (L10); Mathlib `PrespectralSpace`.

**Coherent data glue to sheaves** (`HTT.7.3.5.2/gluing`, part 2 of 2 of Theorem 7.3.5.2 in coherent spaces above; HTT Theorem 7.3.5.2, the inclusion of D into sheaves, PDF pp. 797–798). If F is right Kan extended from `F_0`, and `F_0` satisfies (1) and (2), then F is a sheaf.

*Proof route.* For a covering sieve on U, reduce by transitivity (4.3.2.8) to the compact opens inside the sieve, which is Lemma 7.3.5.1.

*Needs:* 7.3.5.1; 4.3.2.8 (L5); 6.2.2.6 (L10).

**Shv(X) of a coherent space is compactly generated** (HTT Proposition 6.5.4.4, PDF p. 701; stated in §6.5.4, placed here because its proof is Theorem 7.3.5.2). For a coherent topological space X (compact opens closed under finite intersections, including X itself, and forming a basis), `Shv(X)` is compactly generated.

*Lean:* hypotheses `[CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [PrespectralSpace X]` (Mathlib), which together are Lurie's coherence; conclusion `SSet.IsCompactlyGenerated (SSet.sheafOnSpace X)` (5.5.7.1, L7).

*Proof route.* Lurie's: `Shv(X)` is equivalent to the ∞-category `Shv_c(X)` of presheaves on compact opens carrying ∅ to a final object and the squares `U ∩ V, U, V, U ∪ V` to pullbacks; this is Theorem 7.3.5.2, which is why the target sits in L12.3 after §7.3.5. Then `Shv_c(X)` is an accessible localization of `P(N(U_c(X)))` (5.5.4.17–5.5.4.19) closed under filtered colimits (5.3.3.3), so compact objects localize to compact objects (5.3.5.12).

*Needs:* `HTT.6.5.4/intro` (L11.3); 7.3.5.2; `HTT.5.3.3.3/only-if` (L6); 5.3.5.12, 5.5.4.17–5.5.4.19, 5.5.7.1 (L7).

**Points** (`SSet.IsPoint`, `SSet.HasEnoughPoints`; HTT Remark 6.5.4.7, PDF p. 703). A point of an ∞-topos X is a geometric morphism `p_* : S ⟶ X`, where `S` is the final object of `RTop` (6.3.4.1); its left adjoint `p^*` is the stalk functor, and `p_*` is determined by `p^*` up to equivalence; X has enough points when a morphism f with every stalk `p^* f` an equivalence is an equivalence. An ∞-topos with enough points is hypercomplete: stalks of an ∞-connective morphism are ∞-connective (6.5.1.16 (4)), hence equivalences in `S` by Whitehead's theorem (F2.2). Lurie concludes that `Shv(X)` for the coherent X of 6.5.4.5 does not have enough points (so Deligne's completeness theorem fails for ∞-topoi); that conclusion also needs 6.5.4.4 (through Theorem 7.3.5.2), which precedes this entry in L12.3.

*Lean:* `SSet.HasEnoughPoints X : Prop := ∀ f, (∀ p, SSet.IsGeometricMorphism p → SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence (p^* f)) → SSet.Edge.IsEquivalence f`, with p ranging over geometric morphisms `SSet.spaces ⟶ X` and `p^*` a chosen left adjoint.

*Needs:* 6.3.4.1; 6.5.1.16; `HTT.6.5.2.8/after`; 6.4.5.1; F2.2 (Whitehead); `HTT.6.5.4/intro`; 6.5.4.4 (above), 6.5.4.5 (L11.3).

**Cell-like morphisms** (`SSet.IsCellLike`; HTT Definition 7.3.6.1, Remark 7.3.6.3, Proposition 7.3.6.4, Corollary 7.3.6.5, PDF pp. 798–800). A geometric morphism `p_*` is cell-like when it is proper and `p^*` is fully faithful (7.3.6.1); then the unit `id ⟶ p_* p^*` is an equivalence and p is a shape equivalence (7.3.6.3). For p proper and Y with enough points, p is cell-like exactly when every fibre `X' = X ×_Y S` over a point has trivial shape (7.3.6.4). For a map of paracompact spaces with `p_*` proper and Y of finite covering dimension, `p_*` is cell-like exactly when every fibre `X_y` has trivial shape (7.3.6.5).

*Lean:* `SSet.IsCellLike p h := IsProperGeometricMorphism p h ∧ IsFullyFaithful h.choose` for `h : IsGeometricMorphism p` (an explicit argument, as for `SSet.IsProperGeometricMorphism`, 7.3.1.4), where `h.choose` is the left adjoint of p that h provides (that is, `p^*`). Lurie's text (PDF p. 798) says "right adjoint `p^*`"; the left adjoint `p^*` is meant, as Remark 7.3.6.3 shows. Propose.

*Proof route.* 7.3.6.5: Lurie combines 7.3.6.4 with 7.2.1.17; the hypothesis of 7.2.1.17 needs `Shv(Y)` locally of finite homotopy dimension, which comes from 7.2.3.6 on the open Fσ subsets of Y (paracompact, 7.1.1.1) once their covering dimension is bounded by that of Y (`HTT.7.2.3/countable-sum`, L12.4). 7.3.6.4 quantifies over all points of `Shv(Y)`. Since `Shv(Y)` is 0-localic, a point is a point of the locale `U(Y)` (6.4.5.6), that is, an irreducible closed subset, which is a single point y because Y is Hausdorff (as in Lurie's proof of 7.3.6.10). The fibre over y is `Shv(X_y)` by 7.3.2.10 and 7.3.2.12.

*Needs:* 7.3.1.4, 7.1.1.1, 7.1.6.5, 7.1.6.11; 7.2.1.17, 7.2.3.1, 7.2.3.6 (L12.2); `HTT.7.2.3/countable-sum` (L12.4); 7.3.2.10, 7.3.2.12; 6.4.5.6 (L11); 6.5.4.7 (L12.3); `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`.

**Cell-like maps of ANRs** (HTT Proposition 7.3.6.6, PDF p. 800). For a proper map `p : X ⟶ Y` of locally compact absolute neighbourhood retracts (metrizable spaces that are neighbourhood retracts of every metric space they embed in as closed subsets), these are equivalent: `p_*` is cell-like; `X ×_Y U ⟶ U` is a homotopy equivalence for every open U ⊆ Y; every fibre has trivial shape.

*Lean:* `TopologicalSpace.IsANR X` (`HTT.7.3.6/anr`, L12.4).

*Proof route.* (1) ⇒ (2): restrictions to opens are cell-like, hence shape equivalences (7.3.6.3), hence homotopy equivalences (7.1.6.8 and `HTT.7.3.6/anr-cw-type`). The restriction over an open U is a pullback in `RTop` (6.3.5.8, slices), so it is proper (7.3.1.6) and its pullback functor is fully faithful. (2) ⇒ (1): through 7.1.4.4 and 7.1.5.1. (1) ⇒ (3): the "only if" half of the proof of 7.3.6.4, which does not use enough points (Lurie writes "the proof of Proposition 7.3.6.6"). (3) ⇒ (2) is classical (Lurie cites Haver): `HTT.7.3.6/haver` (L12.4), applied as described there.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.3.6/anr`, `HTT.7.3.6/anr-cw-type`, `HTT.7.3.6/haver` (L12.4); 7.1.4.4, 7.1.5.1, 7.1.6.8, 7.3.6.3, 7.3.6.4; 6.3.5.8 (L11), 7.3.1.6; 7.3.1.7, 7.3.1.16 (`p_*` proper; ANRs are metrizable, hence completely regular); 7.3.2.10, 7.3.2.12 (the fibre over y is `Shv(X_y)`, for (1) ⇒ (3)).

**Homotopy dimension under cell-like maps** (HTT Proposition 7.3.6.9, PDF p. 801). If `p_* : X ⟶ Y` is cell-like and X has homotopy dimension ≤ n, so does Y.

*Needs:* 7.3.6.1, 7.2.1.1; 6.5.1.16 (L11); `HTT.1.2.10/fully-faithful`.

**Irreducible spaces have trivial shape** (HTT Lemma 7.3.6.11, PDF p. 802). For an irreducible space X, `Shv(X)` has trivial shape.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: the left Kan extension along `U ↦ (∅ if U = ∅, else ∗)` is a left adjoint to `π_*` with invertible unit, since nonempty opens form a filtered poset (irreducibility), whose nerve is weakly contractible.

*Needs:* 7.1.6.11; 4.3.2.2 (L5); 5.3.1.7 (L6); 6.2.2.1 (L10); Mathlib `IrreducibleSpace`.

**The Zariski–Riemann space over the Berkovich space** (HTT Proposition 7.3.6.10, PDF p. 802). For K complete with respect to a non-Archimedean absolute value, A an affinoid K-algebra and X its rigid space, the natural map `p : X_ZR ⟶ X_B` from the Zariski–Riemann space to the Berkovich space induces a cell-like `p_* : Shv(X_ZR) ⟶ Shv(X_B)`.

*Proof route.* Lurie's: factor p through the graph into a closed immersion (7.3.2.10, 7.3.2.12; Lurie writes 7.3.2.9) and a pullback of global sections of the coherent space `X_ZR` (7.3.1.11, which applies because `X_B` is compact Hausdorff, hence locally compact; 7.3.5.3); `X_B` is paracompact of finite covering dimension (Berkovich), so `Shv(X_B)` has enough points (7.2.1.17, as in 7.3.6.5), and the fibres are coherent irreducible spaces (7.3.6.4, 6.4.5.6, 7.3.6.11).

*Needs:* 7.3.1.11, 7.3.2.10, 7.3.2.12, 7.3.5.3, 7.3.6.4, 7.3.6.11, 7.2.1.17; 6.4.5.6 (L11); `HTT.7.3.6/zariski-riemann`, `HTT.7.3.6/berkovich-dimension`, `HTT.7.2.3/countable-sum` (L12.4), 7.2.3.6.

### L12.4 Classical inputs

Foundational targets for the classical topology and rigid geometry that L12 uses and no roadmap supplies: dimension theory for 7.2.3.7, 7.3.6.5 and 7.3.6.10, absolute neighbourhood retracts for 7.3.6.6, and the Zariski–Riemann and Berkovich spaces for 7.3.6.10. Each target contains exactly what those proofs use. *Paracompact* includes Hausdorff, as in the conventions of this layer. `S^m` is Mathlib's `Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (m + 1))) 1`. A cover has *order ≤ n* when no `n + 2` members with distinct indices have a common point.

**Covering dimension by finite covers** (`HTT.7.2.3/finite-covers`; the first sentence of HTT Remark 7.2.3.2, PDF p. 755; Dowker's theorem). Let X be paracompact and `n ≥ 0`. Then X has covering dimension ≤ n (7.2.3.1) exactly when every finite open cover `{U_1, …, U_k}` has an open shrinking `{V_j ⊆ U_j}` of order ≤ n that still covers X. The right-hand side is the Čech–Lebesgue dimension of normal spaces, which the classical theorems below are stated for.

*Lean:* propose `TopologicalSpace.HasFiniteCoverDimLE (n : ℕ) (X)`: for every `k` and every open cover `u : Fin k → Set X` there is an open cover `v : Fin k → Set X` with `v j ⊆ u j` and `⋂ j ∈ s, v j = ∅` for every `s : Finset (Fin k)` with `s.card = n + 2`. The theorem is `TopologicalSpace.hasCoveringDimLE_iff_hasFiniteCoverDimLE [ParacompactSpace X] [T2Space X]` (propose).

**Checks.** For compact X the implication from finite covers is immediate (pass to a finite subcover). `Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1` satisfies `HasFiniteCoverDimLE 1` but not `HasFiniteCoverDimLE 0`: the cover by `[0, 2/3)` and `(1/3, 1]` has no disjoint open shrinking, since the interval is connected.

*Proof route.* Engelking, *Dimension Theory* (1978), Ch. 3 (Dowker's theorem on locally finite covers).
1. From HTT's dimension to finite covers: given a refinement `{V_α}` of order ≤ n of `{U_j}`, choose `φ` with `V_α ⊆ U_{φ(α)}` and put `V'_j = ⋃_{φ(α) = j} V_α`. Points in `n + 2` of the `V'_j` with distinct j lie in `n + 2` of the `V_α` with distinct α, so `{V'_j}` has order ≤ n.
2. Conversely, paracompactness refines an arbitrary open cover to a locally finite open cover with the same index set (Mathlib `precise_refinement`).
3. Dowker's theorem: in a normal space all of whose finite open covers have shrinkings of order ≤ n, every locally finite open cover has an open shrinking of order ≤ n. Together with step 2 this gives the refinement that 7.2.3.1 asks for.

*Needs:* 7.2.3.1; Mathlib `ParacompactSpace`, `precise_refinement`, `NormalSpace.of_paracompactSpace_r1Space`.

**Spheres as neighbourhood extensors** (`HTT.7.2.3/spheres`; not an HTT statement; used in the proof of HTT Corollary 7.2.3.7, (2) ⇒ (3)). (a) For a normal space Z, a closed C ⊆ Z and a continuous `f : C ⟶ S^m`, some open `W ⊇ C` carries a continuous `g : W ⟶ S^m` extending f. (b) For `j < m`, every continuous map `S^j ⟶ S^m` is homotopic to a constant map. Lurie's proof calls (a) "`S^m` is an absolute neighbourhood retract". In fact it applies (a) to `Z = U × D^k` with U an open Fσ subset of a paracompact space, which is paracompact (7.1.1.1; Mathlib's instance for a product with a compact space) and so normal, but not metrizable in general. So what is used is (a), the neighbourhood extension property for normal spaces, and not the metric ANR property of `HTT.7.3.6/anr`.

*Lean:* propose (a) `EuclideanSpace.exists_extension_sphere_of_isClosed [NormalSpace Z] (hC : IsClosed C) (f : C(C, S^m)) : ∃ W : Set Z, IsOpen W ∧ C ⊆ W ∧ ∃ g : C(W, S^m), ∀ x : C, g ⟨x, _⟩ = f x`; (b) `EuclideanSpace.nullhomotopic_sphere_of_lt (h : j < m) (f : C(S^j, S^m)) : f.Nullhomotopic` (Mathlib `ContinuousMap.Nullhomotopic`).

**Checks.** (b) fails for `j = m`: the identity of `S^m` is not null-homotopic (for `m = 0`, `S^0` is disconnected). (a) cannot take `W = Z`: the identity of `S^m = ∂D^{m+1}` does not extend over the disc `D^{m+1}` (Brouwer).

*Proof route.* (a) Extend f coordinatewise to `F : Z ⟶ ℝ^{m+1}` by Tietze (Mathlib `ContinuousMap.exists_restrict_eq` with `Pi.instTietzeExtension` and `Real.instTietzeExtension`, transported to `EuclideanSpace` by `TietzeExtension.of_homeo`); put `W = F⁻¹(ℝ^{m+1} ∖ {0})` and `g = F/‖F‖`. (b) Cellular approximation (AlgebraicTopology Stage 4) homotopes f into the j-skeleton of the CW structure on `S^m` with one 0-cell and one m-cell, which is a point.

*Needs:* Mathlib `TietzeExtension`, `NormalSpace`, `ContinuousMap.Nullhomotopic`; AlgebraicTopology Stage 4 (CW structure on spheres, cellular approximation).

**Covering dimension by extension into spheres** (`HTT.7.2.3/sphere-extension`; the implication (3) ⇒ (1) of HTT Corollary 7.2.3.7, PDF p. 758, which Lurie cites from Engelking; Alexandroff–Hurewicz). Let X be paracompact and `n ≥ 0`. If every continuous map from a closed subset of X to `S^n` extends to X, then X has covering dimension ≤ n. The converse is also classical. 7.2.3.7 does not need it, since it gets (1) ⇒ (3) as (1) ⇒ (2) ⇒ (3). Condition (3) of 7.2.3.7 with `m = n` gives the hypothesis.

*Lean:* propose `TopologicalSpace.hasCoveringDimLE_of_forall_extend_sphere [ParacompactSpace X] [T2Space X] (h : ∀ A : Set X, IsClosed A → ∀ f : C(A, S^n), ∃ g : C(X, S^n), ∀ a : A, g a = f a) : HasCoveringDimLE n X`.

**Checks.** A discrete space satisfies the hypothesis for `n = 0` (extend arbitrarily) and has covering dimension ≤ 0 (7.2.3.1, Checks). For `X = [0, 1]` and `n = 0` the hypothesis fails at `A = {0, 1}` with `f(0) ≠ f(1)` (connectedness), as it must, since `[0, 1]` does not have covering dimension ≤ 0.

*Proof route.* Engelking, *Dimension Theory* (1978), §3.2 (the theorem on partitions, Hemmingsen's characterization, and the characterization by mappings into spheres); Hurewicz–Wallman, *Dimension Theory*, Ch. VI, for separable metric spaces. X is normal.
1. Partitions. Let `(A_i, B_i)`, `i ≤ n + 1`, be pairs of disjoint closed sets. Urysohn functions `f_i : X ⟶ [−1, 1]`, equal to −1 on `A_i` and 1 on `B_i`, give `f : X ⟶ [−1, 1]^{n+1}`. The closed set `A = f⁻¹(∂[−1, 1]^{n+1})` contains every `A_i` and `B_i`. Since `∂[−1, 1]^{n+1} ≅ S^n` radially, `f|A` extends to `g : X ⟶ ∂[−1, 1]^{n+1}`. Then `L_i = g_i⁻¹(0)` separates `A_i` from `B_i`, and `⋂ L_i = ∅` because 0 is not on the boundary.
2. Shrinkings of `(n+2)`-element covers. Given an open cover `{U_1, …, U_{n+2}}`, take a closed shrinking `{F_i}` and apply step 1 to the pairs `(X ∖ U_i, F_i)`, `i ≤ n + 1`. This gives `X ∖ L_i = P_i ⊔ Q_i` with `P_i ⊇ X ∖ U_i` and `Q_i ⊇ F_i` open. Then `V_i = Q_i` (`i ≤ n + 1`) and `V_{n+2} = U_{n+2} ∩ ⋃_i P_i` form an open shrinking with empty total intersection: a point outside every `Q_i` lies in `F_{n+2}`, and, since `⋂ L_i = ∅`, it lies in some `P_i`.
3. All finite covers (Hemmingsen). Given a finite open cover and `n + 2` of its members, apply step 2 to those members, with the last one enlarged by the union of the members outside the chosen `n + 2`. Then intersect the new last member with the old one. This keeps a cover and kills that `(n+2)`-fold intersection without reviving earlier ones. Finitely many steps give `HasFiniteCoverDimLE n X`.
4. `HTT.7.2.3/finite-covers` converts this to covering dimension ≤ n.

*Needs:* 7.2.3.1, `HTT.7.2.3/finite-covers`; Mathlib Urysohn's lemma (`exists_continuous_zero_one_of_isClosed`), the shrinking lemma (`exists_iUnion_eq_closure_subset`).

**Open Fσ subsets do not raise covering dimension** (`HTT.7.2.3/countable-sum`; the closed subset and countable sum theorems; used in the proofs of HTT Corollary 7.3.6.5 and Proposition 7.3.6.10). Let Y be paracompact of covering dimension ≤ n and U ⊆ Y an open Fσ subset (7.1.1.1). Then U has covering dimension ≤ n. Then, for Y of covering dimension ≤ n, the ∞-topos `Shv(Y)` is locally of homotopy dimension ≤ n: `Shv(Y)_{/χ_U} ≃ Shv(U)` for U in the basis of open Fσ subsets, and 7.2.3.6 applies to U. 7.2.1.17 needs exactly this.

*Lean:* propose `TopologicalSpace.HasFiniteCoverDimLE.of_iUnion_isClosed [NormalSpace X] (F : ℕ → Set X) (hF : ∀ i, IsClosed (F i)) (hX : ⋃ i, F i = Set.univ) (h : ∀ i, HasFiniteCoverDimLE n (F i)) : HasFiniteCoverDimLE n X` (the countable sum theorem), `TopologicalSpace.HasFiniteCoverDimLE.of_isClosed` (closed subspaces of normal spaces), and the consequence `TopologicalSpace.HasCoveringDimLE.of_isOpen_iUnion_isClosed [ParacompactSpace Y] [T2Space Y]` for `U` open with `U = ⋃ i, K i`, `K i` closed.

**Checks.** `ℚ ⊆ ℝ` is a countable union of points, so it has covering dimension ≤ 0. `ℝ = ⋃_k [−k, k]` has covering dimension ≤ 1.

*Proof route.* Engelking, *Dimension Theory* (1978), §3.1 (the countable sum theorem 3.1.8 and the subspace theorem); §1.5 for separable metric spaces.
1. Closed subspaces: for F closed in a normal X, a finite open cover of F extends to a finite open cover of X by adding `X ∖ F`. A shrinking of order ≤ n of it restricts to one of the given cover.
2. Countable sum: let `X = ⋃ F_i` be normal with each `F_i` closed of dimension ≤ n, and `{U_j}_{j < k}` a finite open cover. Build open covers `{U^i_j}_{j < k}`, starting with `U^0_j = U_j`, with the closure of `U^i_j` inside `U^{i−1}_j` and the closures of order ≤ n on `F_i`. A shrinking of order ≤ n of the trace on `F_i` exists by hypothesis, and normality enlarges it to such a cover of X. The closed sets `C_j = ⋂_i closure(U^i_j)` cover X: a point lies in `U^i_j` for one j and infinitely many i, and the closures decrease. They have order ≤ n on every `F_i`, so on X.
3. Swelling: normality enlarges the finite closed cover `{C_j}`, `C_j ⊆ U_j`, to an open cover `{V_j}` with `C_j ⊆ V_j ⊆ U_j` and the same order.
4. For U open Fσ in Y: U is paracompact (7.1.1.1), hence normal. `U = ⋃ K_i` with `K_i` closed in Y, hence closed in U. By `HTT.7.2.3/finite-covers` and step 1 each `K_i` has finite-cover dimension ≤ n. Steps 2–3 give the same for U, and `HTT.7.2.3/finite-covers` for U concludes.

*Needs:* 7.2.3.1, 7.1.1.1, `HTT.7.2.3/finite-covers`; Mathlib `NormalSpace`, the shrinking lemma; for the consequence on `Shv(Y)`: 7.2.1.8, 7.2.3.6 (L12.2); `HTT.6.5.4/intro` (L11).

**Absolute neighbourhood retracts** (`TopologicalSpace.IsANR`, `HTT.7.3.6/anr`; HTT §7.3.6, opening paragraph, PDF p. 798). A space X is an absolute neighbourhood retract (ANR) when it is metrizable and, for every closed embedding `e : X ⟶ M` into a metric space, some open `U ⊇ e(X)` retracts onto `e(X)`. Prove also that an open subset of an ANR is an ANR. 7.3.6.6 applies its hypotheses to `U` and `X ×_Y U` for open `U ⊆ Y`.

*Lean:* `TopologicalSpace.IsANR (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop := MetrizableSpace X ∧ ∀ (M : Type u) [MetricSpace M] (e : X → M), IsClosedEmbedding e → ∃ U : Set M, IsOpen U ∧ Set.range e ⊆ U ∧ ∃ r : C(U, X), ∀ x, r ⟨e x, _⟩ = x`, with M in X's universe (the Kuratowski–Wojdysławski embedding of the proof lands there). `TopologicalSpace.IsANR.of_isOpen` for open subtypes. Propose. Mathlib has neither (its `TietzeExtension` file leaves absolute retracts as a TODO).

**Checks.** `ℝ^n` and `S^n` are ANRs. For `S^n`, apply `HTT.7.2.3/spheres` (a) to the embedding, since metric spaces are normal, and compose with a retraction after shrinking the neighbourhood. The topologist's sine curve is compact metrizable and not an ANR: it is not locally connected, while ANRs are locally contractible.

*Proof route.* Dugundji, *An extension of Tietze's theorem*, Pacific J. Math. 1 (1951); Hanner, *Some theorems on absolute neighborhood retracts*, Ark. Mat. 1 (1951).
1. Kuratowski–Wojdysławski: a metrizable X embeds as a closed subset of a convex subset of a normed space.
2. Dugundji's extension theorem (convex subsets of normed spaces are extensors for metric pairs), with step 1, shows that a metrizable X is an ANR exactly when every map from a closed subset of a metric space to X extends to an open neighbourhood.
3. That extension property passes to an open `V ⊆ X`: extend into X, then restrict to the preimage of V.

*Needs:* Mathlib `MetrizableSpace`, `IsClosedEmbedding`, `IsOpen.locallyCompactSpace` (local compactness of open subsets, for 7.3.6.6).

**ANRs have the homotopy type of CW complexes** (`HTT.7.3.6/anr-cw-type`; Milnor; used in the proof of HTT Proposition 7.3.6.6, (1) ⇒ (2), and in the proof and the application of `HTT.7.3.6/haver`). Every ANR is homotopy equivalent to a Hausdorff CW complex. Consequently, a map `f : X' ⟶ Y'` of ANRs is a homotopy equivalence when, for every Kan complex K, precomposition with f is a bijection from homotopy classes of maps `Y' ⟶ |K|` to those of maps `X' ⟶ |K|`. This holds when `Map_Top(Y', |K|) ⟶ Map_Top(X', |K|)` is a homotopy equivalence, which is what 7.1.6.8 provides. Two controlled forms are used by `HTT.7.3.6/haver`. For every open cover γ of an ANR Z, there is an open cover β of Z such that any two maps into Z whose values at each point lie in a common member of β are joined by a homotopy whose tracks lie in members of γ; and there are a simplicial complex Q and maps `c : Z ⟶ |Q|`, `s : |Q| ⟶ Z` with `s ∘ c` joined to `id_Z` by such a homotopy (Hanner). When Z is separable, Q can be taken locally finite.

*Lean:* propose `TopologicalSpace.IsANR.exists_homotopyEquiv_cwComplex (h : IsANR X) : ∃ (Z : Type u) (_ : TopologicalSpace Z) (_ : T2Space Z) (_ : Topology.CWComplex (Set.univ : Set Z)), Nonempty (X ≃ₕ Z)` (Mathlib `ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv`, with AlgebraicTopology's convention for CW type), and the consequence `TopologicalSpace.IsANR.nonempty_homotopyEquiv_of_bijective` stated with `ContinuousMap.Homotopic` classes and `SSet.toTop` of Kan complexes. The controlled forms are `TopologicalSpace.IsANR.exists_homotopic_of_near` and `TopologicalSpace.IsANR.exists_controlled_domination` (propose).

**Checks.** `S^n` (one 0-cell and one n-cell) and open subsets of `ℝ^n`. The Warsaw circle is weakly contractible but not contractible, so it has no CW homotopy type (Whitehead) and is not an ANR.

*Proof route.* Milnor, *On spaces having the homotopy type of a CW-complex*, Trans. AMS 90 (1959), §3; Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Appendix (Proposition A.11, domination).
1. By step 1 of `HTT.7.3.6/anr`, X is a retract of an open subset W of a convex subset of a normed space.
2. W is dominated by a CW complex. A locally finite partition of unity subordinate to an open cover of W whose stars (the union of the members meeting a given member) lie in convex open subsets of W maps W to the realization of the nerve. Affine maps on simplices map the nerve back to W. The composite on W is homotopic to the identity by straight-line homotopies. So the retract X is dominated by a CW complex. If the retraction `r : W ⟶ X` maps each of these convex sets into a member of a given open cover γ of X, the homotopies become γ-small after composing with r. The same straight lines followed by r join any two maps into X whose values at each point lie in one of these convex sets. If X is separable, the cover can be taken star-finite, since a Lindelöf regular space is strongly paracompact, and then the nerve is locally finite.
3. A space dominated by a CW complex has the homotopy type of one (mapping telescope).
4. Consequence: a space Z of CW type is homotopy equivalent to `|Sing Z|`, since the counit is a weak homotopy equivalence and Whitehead applies. Surjectivity at `K = Sing X'` gives g with `g ∘ f ≃ id`. Injectivity at `K = Sing Y'`, applied to `f ∘ g` and `id`, gives `f ∘ g ≃ id`.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.3.6/anr`; star-finite refinements of open covers of Lindelöf regular spaces (Engelking, *General Topology*, Ch. 5), for the separable controlled form; Mathlib `PartitionOfUnity`, `EMetric.instParacompactSpace`, `ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv`, `Topology.CWComplex`; AlgebraicTopology Stage 4 (realizations of simplicial complexes as CW complexes) and Stage 8 (Whitehead's theorem for spaces of CW type, item 5; the comparison of `π_n(Sing Z)` with `π_n(Z)`); `HTT.A.2.7/realization`.

**Cell-like maps of ANRs are homotopy equivalences** (`HTT.7.3.6/haver`; Haver's theorem; the implication (3) ⇒ (2) of HTT Proposition 7.3.6.6, PDF p. 800, which Lurie cites). Let `p : X ⟶ Y` be a proper surjective map of locally compact ANRs whose fibres are cell-like in Borsuk's sense: every continuous map from a fibre to an ANR is homotopic to a constant map. Then p is a homotopy equivalence (in fact a fine homotopy equivalence).

To apply it in 7.3.6.6, fix an open `U ⊆ Y`. U and `X ×_Y U` are locally compact ANRs (`HTT.7.3.6/anr`), and the restriction is proper and surjective with the same fibres. Lurie's condition (3), that `Shv(X_y)` has trivial shape, gives Borsuk's condition. The fibre is compact metrizable, hence paracompact, so 7.1.6.8 with target a point makes `|K| ⟶ Map_Top(X_y, |K|)` a homotopy equivalence for every Kan complex K. Taking `K = ∅` shows that `X_y` is nonempty, so p is surjective. Comparing `π₀` shows that every map `X_y ⟶ |K|` is homotopic to a constant map. By `HTT.7.3.6/anr-cw-type` an ANR P is homotopy equivalent to some `|K|` (`K = Sing P`), so every map `X_y ⟶ P` is homotopic to a constant map.

*Lean:* propose `TopologicalSpace.IsANR.exists_homotopyEquiv_of_cellLike (hX : IsANR X) (hY : IsANR Y) [LocallyCompactSpace X] [LocallyCompactSpace Y] (hp : IsProperMap p) (hs : Function.Surjective p) (hc : ∀ y (P : Type u) [TopologicalSpace P], IsANR P → ∀ g : C(p ⁻¹' {y}, P), g.Nullhomotopic) : ∃ q : C(Y, X), (p.comp q).Homotopic (.id Y) ∧ (q.comp p).Homotopic (.id X)`.

**Checks.** The projection `Y × [0, 1] ⟶ Y` (fibres intervals) is a homotopy equivalence. The map from `S^1` to a point has a fibre that is not cell-like (the identity of `S^1` is not null-homotopic), and it is not a homotopy equivalence.

*Proof route.* Haver, *Mappings between ANRs that are fine homotopy equivalences*, Pacific J. Math. 58 (1975), which proves it for closed maps between separable ANRs whose fibres have property UV^∞. For an open cover α of Y, two maps into Y are α-near when their values at each point lie in a common member of α, and α-homotopic when they are joined by a homotopy whose tracks lie in members of α. Maps into X are compared after composing with p, and `p⁻¹(α)` is the cover of X by the preimages.
0. Reductions. A proper map to a locally compact Hausdorff space is closed. ANRs are locally connected, so X and Y are disjoint unions of clopen components, and a connected locally compact metrizable space is σ-compact, hence separable. For a component `Y_j`, `p⁻¹(Y_j)` is σ-compact because p is proper, so `p⁻¹(Y_j) ⟶ Y_j` is a closed surjection between separable ANRs, and it suffices to treat it. Separability makes the polyhedra of steps 4–5 locally finite (`HTT.7.3.6/anr-cw-type`).
1. Cell-like fibres are UV^∞. For a fibre F and open `U ⊇ F`, U is an ANR (`HTT.7.3.6/anr`), so the inclusion `F ⟶ U` is null-homotopic, say through `H : F × [0, 1] ⟶ U` ending at a point c. On the closed subset `A = (U × {0}) ∪ (F × [0, 1]) ∪ (U × {1})` of `U × [0, 1]`, define the map by the inclusion at time 0, by H on `F × [0, 1]` and by c at time 1. Since U is an ANR, it extends to an open neighbourhood W of A. Since F is compact (p is proper), W contains `V × [0, 1]` for an open `V ⊇ F` (tube lemma). So `V ⟶ U` is null-homotopic.
2. UV^∞ star refinements (Haver, Lemma 2). Every open cover 𝒰 of the paracompact Y has a locally finite open refinement 𝒱 with two properties: each star `st(V, 𝒱)` lies in some `U ∈ 𝒰`; and every map `∂B^m ⟶ p⁻¹(st(V, 𝒱))` extends to `B^m ⟶ p⁻¹(U)`. This uses step 1, closedness of p (so `p⁻¹` of a small neighbourhood of y lies in a given neighbourhood of `p⁻¹(y)`), and star refinements of covers of a metric space.
3. Controlled lifting (Haver, Lemma 3, after Smale). Let K be a locally finite simplicial complex, J a subcomplex, `φ : |K| ⟶ Y`, and `ψ' : |J| ⟶ X` with `p ∘ ψ' = φ|J`. For every open cover α of Y there is `ψ : |K| ⟶ X` extending ψ' with `p ∘ ψ` α-near φ. Choose covers `α_0 = α, α_1, …`, each `α_{i+1}` a UV^∞ star refinement of `α_i` (step 2). For a simplex σ of K let `D(σ)` be the largest dimension of a simplex of K containing σ, finite because K is locally finite. By Haver's Lemma 1 there is a subdivision K' of K, restricting to one of J, such that φ maps the closed star of each vertex w of K' into a member of `α_{ℓ(w)}`, where `ℓ(w) = 2D(σ)` for the simplex σ of K containing w in its interior. Define ψ on the simplices of K' outside J by induction on dimension. A vertex w goes to a point of `p⁻¹(φ(w))`. For a k-simplex τ, let L be the least `ℓ(w)` over its vertices, so `L ≥ 2k`. By induction, `p ∘ ψ` and φ map each proper face of τ into one member of `α_{L−2k+2}`, and φ maps τ into a member of `α_L`, which lies in a member W of `α_{L−2k+2}`. So `p ∘ ψ` maps `∂τ` into `p⁻¹(st(W, α_{L−2k+2}))`, and step 2 extends ψ over τ into `p⁻¹(U)` for a member U of `α_{L−2k+1}` containing that star. This continues the induction, and at level 0 it says that `p ∘ ψ` is α-near φ. ψ is continuous because `|K|` carries the weak topology.
4. The inverse. Fix a star⁵ refinement α₁ of α, a star refinement α₂ of α₁, and an open refinement β of α₂ such that β-near maps into Y are α₂-homotopic (`HTT.7.3.6/anr-cw-type`, controlled forms). By the same target there are a locally finite polyhedron Q and maps `c : Y ⟶ Q`, `s : Q ⟶ Y` with `s ∘ c` α₂-homotopic to `id_Y`. Step 3 with `J = ∅` and the cover β lifts s to `v : Q ⟶ X` with `p ∘ v` β-near s. Put `g = v ∘ c`. Then `p ∘ g` is β-near, hence α₂-homotopic to, `s ∘ c`, so a homotopy h with α₁-small tracks runs from `h_0 = id_Y` to `h_1 = p ∘ g`.
5. The other composite. The same target gives a locally finite polyhedron P, maps `b : X ⟶ P` and `r : P ⟶ X`, and a homotopy W from `r ∘ b` to `id_X` such that `p ∘ W` and `p ∘ g ∘ p ∘ W` have α₁-small tracks. Triangulate `P × [0, 1]` as a locally finite complex with `P × {0, 1}` a subcomplex, and apply step 3 with the cover α₁, relative to `P × {0, 1}`, with ψ' equal to r at 0 and `g ∘ p ∘ r` at 1, over `(x, t) ↦ h_t(p(r(x)))`. The ends match because `h_0 = id_Y` and `h_1 = p ∘ g`. This gives a homotopy G from r to `g ∘ p ∘ r`. Then W reversed, `(x, t) ↦ G(b(x), t)`, and `g ∘ p ∘ W` join `id_X` to `g ∘ p`. Their images under p have tracks in members of `star³(α₁)`, which refines α. So `g ∘ p` is homotopic to `id_X`, and p is a (fine) homotopy equivalence.

*Needs:* `HTT.7.3.6/anr`, `HTT.7.3.6/anr-cw-type` (its controlled forms: near maps are cover-homotopic, and controlled domination by locally finite polyhedra); locally finite simplicial complexes, their subdivisions, and triangulations of `P × [0, 1]` (AlgebraicTopology Stage 4); Mathlib `IsProperMap`, `IsProperMap.isClosedMap`, `ParacompactSpace`, `LocallyCompactSpace`, `generalized_tube_lemma`, `ContinuousMap.Homotopic`, `ContinuousMap.Nullhomotopic`. The application in 7.3.6.6 also uses 7.1.6.8.

**The Zariski–Riemann space and its map to the Berkovich spectrum** (`HTT.7.3.6/zariski-riemann`; HTT §7.3.6 before Proposition 7.3.6.10, (ZR1)–(ZR3) and (B1)–(B2), PDF pp. 801–802). Let K be complete for a nontrivial non-Archimedean absolute value with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, and A a K-affinoid algebra (Tau Ceti `TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra K A`, with the topology and complete residue norm of AdicSpacesPartII R0.9). The Zariski–Riemann space is `X_ZR = Spa(A, A°)`: the continuous valuations bounded by 1 on power-bounded elements. This is the concrete description (ZR3) with the bound on `A°` made explicit. The Berkovich space is `X_B = M(A)`, the Gel'fand spectrum of A as a Banach ring (AdicSpacesPartIII *gelfand-spectrum-banach-ring*, `Huber.GelfandSpectrum`, which proves `M(A)` compact Hausdorff). Equivalent norms have the same bounded seminorms, so `M(A)` does not depend on the choice of norm. Prove:
- every `v ∈ X_ZR` has a unique rank-one generization, and normalizing it at ϖ gives a point `p(v) ∈ M(A)`. The map `p : X_ZR ⟶ X_B` is continuous;
- every `x ∈ M(A)` defines a rank-one point `s(x) ∈ X_ZR` with `p(s(x)) = x`, and the fibre `p⁻¹(x)` is the closure of `{s(x)}`. In particular it is irreducible, with generic point `s(x)`.

7.3.6.10 also uses that `X_ZR` is coherent (for 7.3.5.3). Tau Ceti main supplies this: the `SpectralSpace (spa Aplus)` instance for Huber rings (Wedhorn, Theorem 7.35). The sheaf-theoretic descriptions (ZR1) and (B1) are not used.
